\item finite typed preparation, intervention-outcome, and terminal-Read
      alphabets, together with finite exposed quantum port spaces and a finite
      physical CP frame spanning every exposed Hermitian Choi-coordinate space;
\item all admitted multitime probabilities on those frames, affine under
      randomization, additive under coarse graining, normalized on complete
      instruments and causal testers, and compatible on common prefixes;
\item a finite typed generated ledger
      $\widetilde{\mathscr R}_{X,x}$, partial deterministic updates $u_a$ for
      primitive branches, and a finite self-adjoint family of actual
      record-dependent response coordinates $\mathscr D_{X,x}$ containing the
      constant function, branch-domain indicators, terminal Reads, control
      predicates, and a spanning set of the record-dependent primitive CP
      response coordinates;
\item a distinguished deterministic Store step or Store instrument whenever a
      Store port is used later, but no Stinespring environment, scheduler,
      score collision, dwell law, or reset is included;
\item the requirement that the unique tensors reconstructed from the table pass
      the finite positivity and causal-prefix tests of
      \Cref{thm:comb-tomography}.
\end{enumerate}
No predictive state space, positive comb representative, hidden memory,
common dilation, formal adjoint, coherent fringe, flat depth, autonomous
renewal, regulator gap, domain semantic, or conjecture-specific coefficient is
part of the datum.
\end{definition}

\begin{assessment}[Exact meaning of minimal assumptions]
The entrance is assumption-minimal relative to tomographically complete finite
operational process data and the actual finite Read interface.  It is
informationally rich and is not claimed to follow from a few microscopic
Hamiltonian constants.  The theorem reconstructs every finite structural
object compatible with those data without adding a target-shaped algebra,
record, metric, arithmetic coefficient, or physical scheduler.  When a deeper
finite realization is considered, the operational table selects its minimal
active and Read-visible quotients but cannot select unread spectator fibres or
a preferred maximal dilation.
\end{assessment}

\begin{definition}[Generated operational record machine]
\label{def:protected-operational-record}
For a boundary type $x$, let $\widetilde{\mathscr R}_{X,x}$ be the finite set
of ledger values generated by the protocol.  For a primitive branch
$a:x\to y$, let
\[
 u_a:\operatorname{Dom}(u_a)\subseteq\widetilde{\mathscr R}_{X,x}
 \longrightarrow\widetilde{\mathscr R}_{X,y}
\]
be its deterministic ledger update.  The finite self-adjoint family
$\mathscr D_{X,x}\subset C(\widetilde{\mathscr R}_{X,x})$ contains exactly
the declared one-step scalar response coordinates needed to reconstruct every
record-conditioned primitive operation.  It may contain point indicators only
when the corresponding point Reads are physically admitted.
\end{definition}

For an admissible word $w=a_m\cdots a_1:x\to y$, write
$u_w=u_{a_m}\circ\cdots\circ u_{a_1}$ on its natural domain, and extend
$d\circ u_w$ by zero outside that domain.

\begin{definition}[Future equivalence and minimal readable record]
\label{def:minimal-readable-record}
For $r,s\in\widetilde{\mathscr R}_{X,x}$, write $r\sim_{X,x}s$ when
\[
 \boxed{d(u_w(r))=d(u_w(s))}
\]
for every admitted typed word $w:x\to y$ and every
$d\in\mathscr D_{X,y}$, including equality of all word-domain indicators.
Define
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathscr R_{X,x}^{\min}
 :=\widetilde{\mathscr R}_{X,x}/\!\sim_{X,x},
 \qquad
 q_{X,x}:\widetilde{\mathscr R}_{X,x}\twoheadrightarrow
 \mathscr R_{X,x}^{\min}.}
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Canonical minimal-readable-record theorem]
\label{thm:minimal-record}
The family $\mathscr R_X^{\min}$ is the unique coarsest typed classical record
through which every admitted record-conditioned future factors.  More
precisely:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(M\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item $\sim_{X,x}$ is an equivalence relation and a typed right congruence;
\item every primitive update descends uniquely to a partial deterministic map
      $u_a^{\min}$ satisfying $u_a^{\min}q_{X,x}=q_{X,y}u_a$;
\item every pulled-back future coordinate $d\circ u_w$ factors uniquely through
      $q_{X,x}$;
\item if $g_x:\widetilde{\mathscr R}_{X,x}\twoheadrightarrow S_x$ is any
      typed quotient through which all updates and all coordinates in
      $\mathscr D_{X,x}$ factor, then there is a unique surjection
      $h_x:S_x\twoheadrightarrow\mathscr R_{X,x}^{\min}$ with
      $q_{X,x}=h_xg_x$;
\item the construction is invariant under operational record-machine
      isomorphism and is idempotent.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Reflexivity, symmetry, and transitivity follow from equality of all future
signatures.  If $r\sim s$ and $a$ is admitted at both records, then for every
continuation $w$ and Read $d$,
\[
 d(u_w(u_a(r)))=d(u_{wa}(r))=d(u_{wa}(s))=d(u_w(u_a(s))),
\]
so $u_a(r)\sim u_a(s)$; branch-domain indicators ensure simultaneous
admissibility.  This proves the right-congruence property and makes the
quotient update well defined.  The definition of $\sim$ proves factorization
of every future coordinate, and surjectivity of $q$ gives uniqueness.

For the universal property, if $g_x(r)=g_x(s)$, then every immediate coordinate
agrees because it factors through $g_x$.  Induction on word length, using
that the updates descend through $g$, shows equality of every future
coordinate, so $r\sim s$.  Hence each $g$-fibre lies inside one $q$-fibre,
which defines the unique map $h_x$ with $q_x=h_xg_x$.  Operational
isomorphisms preserve the complete signature family, and applying the same
construction to the quotient separates all distinct quotient classes, proving
canonicity and idempotence.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Smallest readable classical algebra]
\label{def:minimal-read-algebra}
Let
\[
 \mathfrak R_{X,x}^{\min}
 :=q_{X,x}^*C(\mathscr R_{X,x}^{\min})
 \subseteq C(\widetilde{\mathscr R}_{X,x}).
\]
Equivalently, let $\mathfrak B_{X,x}$ be the unital $C^*$-algebra generated by
all functions $d\circ u_w$.  
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Minimal Read-algebra characterization]
\label{thm:minimal-read-algebra}
For every type $x$,
\[
 \boxed{\mathfrak R_{X,x}^{\min}=\mathfrak B_{X,x}.}
\]
It is the smallest unital classical $C^*$-subalgebra containing the actual
response coordinates and invariant under every primitive pullback
$f\mapsto f\circ u_a$.  Its Gelfand spectrum is canonically
$\mathscr R_{X,x}^{\min}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Every generator $d\circ u_w$ is constant on future-equivalence classes, hence
belongs to $q_x^*C(\mathscr R_x^{\min})$.  Conversely, distinct quotient
classes are separated by some pulled-back future coordinate.  A unital
self-adjoint subalgebra of functions on a finite set which separates points is
the whole function algebra: its joint level-set projections are obtained by
finite Lagrange interpolation.  This proves equality.  Pulling back a generator
along $u_a$ produces the generator associated with the concatenated word, so
the algebra is update invariant.  Any other update-invariant algebra
containing the immediate response coordinates contains all their iterated
pullbacks and hence contains $\mathfrak B_{X,x}$.
\end{proof}

\begin{construction}[Terminating partition refinement]
\label{con:partition-refinement}
Let $\Pi_x^{(0)}$ group ledger values with equal immediate coordinates in
$\mathscr D_{X,x}$ and equal primitive branch-domain indicators.  Given
$\Pi^{(k)}$, place $r,s$ in the same block of $\Pi_x^{(k+1)}$ exactly when they
are in the same block of $\Pi_x^{(0)}$ and, for every primitive $a:x\to y$,
either $a$ is unavailable at both records or $u_a(r),u_a(s)$ lie in the same
block of $\Pi_y^{(k)}$.
\end{construction}

\begin{theorem}[Termination, exactness, and record margin]
\label{thm:minimal-record-audit}
Let $n_{\rm rec}=\sum_x|\widetilde{\mathscr R}_{X,x}|$.  Then:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(P\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item $\Pi_x^{(k)}$ identifies exactly the records not separated by a future
      word of length at most $k$;
\item the refinement stabilizes after at most $n_{\rm rec}-1$ strict rounds;
\item the stable partition is $\mathscr R_{X,x}^{\min}$;
\item choosing the finitely many response coordinates encountered before
      stabilization gives signature vectors $v(r)$ with
      \[
       \boxed{r\sim s\iff\Delta_{\rm rec}(r,s)
       :=\|v(r)-v(s)\|_2^2=0;}
      \]
\item if at least two classes occur, the minimum nonzero signature distance
      $\delta_{{\rm rec},X}$ is positive and gives robust recovery whenever
      every estimated signature is within $\varepsilon$ and
      $4\varepsilon<\delta_{{\rm rec},X}$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The first assertion is induction on $k$: a future of length $k+1$ is either an
immediate Read or a primitive branch followed by a future of length at most
$k$.  Each strict refinement increases the total number of blocks, which is at
most $n_{\rm rec}$, proving termination.  At stabilization, equality is
preserved by every primitive update and every immediate coordinate, hence by
every word; conversely future-equivalent records survive every finite round.
This proves the first three claims.  The stabilized finite coordinate family
separates exactly the stable blocks, proving the residual criterion.  Finiteness
makes the least nonzero distance positive.  The triangle and reverse-triangle
inequalities separate same-class distances, at most $2\varepsilon$, from
different-class distances, at least
$\delta_{{\rm rec},X}-2\varepsilon$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Unread refinements and the correct bundle decomposition]
\label{thm:record-refinement-bundle}
Let $\pi:\widetilde{\mathscr R}'\twoheadrightarrow
\widetilde{\mathscr R}$ intertwine all updates and suppose every admitted
response upstairs is exactly a pullback of a response downstairs.  Then
$\mathscr R'^{\min}\cong\mathscr R^{\min}$ canonically.  For the quotient
$q:\widetilde{\mathscr R}\twoheadrightarrow\mathscr R^{\min}$ and fibres
$F_\rho=q^{-1}(\rho)$,
\[
 \boxed{
 C(\widetilde{\mathscr R})
 \cong\bigoplus_{\rho\in\mathscr R^{\min}}C(F_\rho),
 \qquad
 q^*C(\mathscr R^{\min})
 =\bigoplus_\rho\C\one_{F_\rho}.}
\]
A base-preserving tensor factorization
$C(\widetilde{\mathscr R})\cong C(\mathscr R^{\min})\otimes C(D)$ exists if
and only if $|F_\rho|=|D|$ for every $\rho$; even then it is noncanonical
without a fibre trivialization, and compatibility with updates imposes a
further dynamical condition.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Intertwining gives
$(d\circ\pi)(u'_w(r'))=d(u_w(\pi(r')))$, so two fine records have the same
complete future signature exactly when their images do.  This gives the
canonical bijection of minima.  Restriction to the disjoint fibres gives the
direct-sum decomposition, and pullback functions are exactly the fibrewise
constant ones.  In a base-preserving tensor split, the corner over $\rho$ is
both $C(F_\rho)$ and $C(D)$, so their finite spectra have equal cardinality.
Conversely, equal cardinalities plus chosen bijections $F_\rho\cong D$ give a
split.  The chosen bijections are not determined by the operational table,
and an update intertwines the split only when it respects them.
\end{proof}

\begin{countertheorem}[$C^*$-quotients cannot merge surviving classical records]
\label{cth:record-cstar-merge}
Let $p,q$ be orthogonal projections and let $\pi$ be a $*$-homomorphism.  If
$\pi(p)=\pi(q)$, then $\pi(p)=\pi(q)=0$.  Consequently classical record
minimization cannot be delegated to a two-sided $C^*$-ideal quotient after
nonzero point projections and their writers have been generated.
\end{countertheorem}

\begin{proof}
Since $pq=0$,
$0=\pi(pq)=\pi(p)\pi(q)=\pi(p)^2$.  A projection with square zero is zero.
Thus a $C^*$-quotient may delete a classical point ideal but cannot identify
two nonzero orthogonal points.  The future-equivalence quotient must therefore
be performed on the classical record machine before its writer
$C^*$-envelope is formed.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Minimal operational record completion]
\label{def:operationally-complete-renewal}
Let
\[
 \mathfrak R_X^{\min}:=\bigoplus_x C(\mathscr R_{X,x}^{\min}).
\]
For a quotient record class $\rho$ and primitive branch $a$, write
\[
 W^{\rm rec}_{a,\rho}:=|u_a^{\min}(\rho)\rangle\langle\rho|.
\]
The minimal operational completion is
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathfrak O_X^{\min,\rm op}
 :=\operatorname{MinRec}_X(\mathfrak O_X)
 =\bigl(\mathfrak O_X,\mathfrak R_X^{\min}\bigr).}
\]
If a support-minimal core branch has Kraus operators $K_{a,\rho,j}$, its
record-completed Kraus operators are
\[
 \widetilde K_{a,\rho,j}
 =W^{\rm rec}_{a,\rho}\otimes K_{a,\rho,j}.
\]
An optional full-provenance completion retains the generated ledger itself,
but is canonical only relative to the stronger declared point-Read policy.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Operational-record completion theorem]
\label{thm:operational-record-completion}
The minimal completion is canonical and has the following properties.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(O\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item every completed branch is CP and trace-nonincreasing, and every completed
      instrument is normalized;
\item discarding the record recovers every original record-forgetting word map
      and intervention probability;
\item sequential and parallel composition, coarse graining, deterministic
      discard, and label-preserving operational morphisms are preserved;
\item unread record refinements yield canonically isomorphic minimal
      completions;
\item compatible cutoff morphisms induce compatible maps of minimal records
      whenever they preserve the complete old future signature;
\item if every generated ledger point has an actual terminal point Read, then
      the minimal record is the full generated ledger and no operational fact
      is erased.
\end{enumerate}
No target-domain coefficient or semantic predicate enters the construction.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
For a completed branch,
\[
 \sum_j\widetilde K_{a,\rho,j}^*\widetilde K_{a,\rho,j}
 =P_\rho\otimes\sum_jK_{a,\rho,j}^*K_{a,\rho,j}
 \preceq P_\rho\otimes I.
\]
Summing over a complete instrument gives the identity in every record block.
Record discard removes the deterministic writer, and induction on word length
recovers every core word and scalar probability.  Writer multiplication is
composition of the deterministic quotient updates; parallel writers tensor
and coarse graining sums the CP branches.  Functoriality and unread-refinement
invariance follow from \Cref{thm:minimal-record,thm:record-refinement-bundle}.
A cutoff map descends precisely when old future-equivalent records remain
future equivalent after restriction.  Finally, point Reads separate every pair
of generated ledger values, making all equivalence classes singletons.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[Operational facts, not target-domain semantics]
\label{fire:record-semantic-firewall}
The minimal or full provenance record may store only facts independently
written by the protocol: preparation, intervention, outcome, chronology,
route, boundary, interface, regulator, and declared environment outcomes.  It
does not directly store primality, $\Lambda(n)$, $\mu(n)$, a metric, a gauge
group, a particle species, a Yukawa matrix, a chain equivalence, a complexity
answer, or the truth of a conjecture.
\end{firewall}

% =============================================================================
\section{Hankel reconstruction and the table-native executable algebra}
\label{sec:hankel-core}
% =============================================================================

For each boundary type $x$ and minimal readable record $\rho$, let
$\mathsf P_{x,\rho}$ and $\mathsf F_{x,\rho}$ be the admitted finite pasts and
futures meeting at $(x,\rho)$, and write
$\mathbb p_{x,\rho}(f,p)=\Pr(f\circ p)$.

\begin{definition}[Record-conditioned intervention Hankel operator]
\label{def:intervention-hankel}
Define
\[
 \mathsf H_{x,\rho}
 =[\mathbb p_{x,\rho}(f,p)]_{f,p},
 \qquad
 h_p(f)=\mathbb p_{x,\rho}(f,p),
 \qquad
 M_{x,\rho}=\Span_\R\{h_p\}.
\]
Its dimension is the typed Hankel rank $d_{x,\rho}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Canonical typed Hankel realization]
\label{thm:typed-hankel-realization}
For every primitive letter
$a:(x,\rho)\to(y,u_a^{\min}(\rho))$ there is a unique linear map
\[
 A_a:M_{x,\rho}\longrightarrow M_{y,u_a^{\min}(\rho)},
 \qquad A_ah_p=h_{a\circ p}.
\]
Every future defines $\lambda_f(m)=m(f)$, and
\[
 \boxed{\mathbb p(f,p)=\lambda_f(h_p),
 \qquad \lambda_fA_a=\lambda_{f\circ a}.}
\]
The realization is reachable and future separated in every minimal record
sector.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
If $\sum_jc_jh_{p_j}=0$, then for every target future $f$,
$\sum_jc_jh_{a\circ p_j}(f)=\sum_jc_j\mathbb p(f\circ a,p_j)=0$.
Thus appending $a$ respects all column relations and defines a unique map.
Evaluation gives the displayed identities.  Reachability holds by definition,
and a nonzero response function is detected by some future.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Hankel-rank minimality]
\label{thm:hankel-minimality}
For any linear realization $N_{x,\rho}$, let $N^{\rm reach}$ be its reachable
span and $N^{\rm unobs}$ the reachable vectors annihilated by every future.
Then
\[
 \boxed{N^{\rm reach}_{x,\rho}/N^{\rm unobs}_{x,\rho}
 \cong M_{x,\rho},
 \qquad \dim N_{x,\rho}\ge d_{x,\rho}.}
\]
Equality holds exactly for reachable future-separated realizations, and any
two minimal realizations are related by a unique record-preserving similarity
intertwining all primitive transitions and future effects.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
On the reachable span define $(Qn)(f)=\mu_f(n)$.  It maps the state of a past
$p$ to $h_p$, hence is onto, and its kernel is exactly the future-unobservable
subspace.  The first-isomorphism theorem gives the quotient and dimension
claims.  Mapping the state of each past in one minimal realization to the state
of the same past in another is well defined by equality of all future
probabilities, injective by future separation, onto by reachability, and
uniquely intertwines the generators.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Operational predictive cone]
For finite $d_{x,\rho}$ put
\[
 M_{x,\rho}^+
 :=\{m:m(f)\ge0\text{ for every positive admitted future }f\}.
\]
Let $u_{x,\rho}$ be deterministic discard.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Ordered predictive realization]
\label{thm:ordered-memory}
Each $M_{x,\rho}^+$ is closed, pointed, and generating; physical past columns
belong to it; every $A_a$ is positive; and every complete instrument
$\{a_o\}$ satisfies
\[
 \boxed{u\!\left(\sum_oA_{a_o}m\right)=u(m).}
\]
Thus order and normalization descend from the table rather than from a hidden
state-space model.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The cone is an intersection of closed half-spaces.  If both $m$ and $-m$ are
positive, every future vanishes on $m$, so $m=0$.  Physical columns span the
response space, making the cone generating.  Positivity of $A_a$ follows from
$(A_am)(f)=m(f\circ a)$, and instrument normalization holds on physical
columns by the operational axioms and hence on their span.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Record-conditioned predictive minimality]
\label{thm:conditional-core-minimality}
At finite cutoff the intrinsic linear predictive core is
\[
 \boxed{
 M_X^{\min,\rm op}
 =\bigoplus_{x,\rho\in\mathscr R_X^{\min}}
 |x,\rho\rangle\otimes M_{x,\rho}.}
\]
It preserves all intervention probabilities and every minimal Read.  An
optional full-provenance realization is the direct sum over the finer ledger,
but unread fibre contrasts are not part of the intrinsic minimum.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Take the direct sum of the Hankel quotients.  Every probability factors through
them by \Cref{thm:typed-hankel-realization}.  Distinct minimal record classes
are separated by an admitted future and therefore cannot be identified.
Unread refinements collapse by \Cref{thm:record-refinement-bundle}.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Table-native executable predictive algebra]
\label{def:executable-predictive-algebra}
Let $\mathfrak P_X^+$ be the finite typed forward path algebra generated by the
primitive executable letters and object units.  Its canonical response
representation sends a word to its action on the spaces $M_{x,\rho}$.  Define
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal B_X^{\rm pred}
 :=\rho_X^+(\mathfrak P_X^+)
 \cong\mathfrak P_X^+/\Ker\rho_X^+.}
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Realization-free executable algebra]
\label{thm:executable-predictive-algebra}
The scalar operational table determines $\mathcal B_X^{\rm pred}$ directly.
For a forward polynomial $q=\sum_wc_ww$,
\[
 \boxed{\rho_X^+(q)=0
 \iff
 \sum_wc_w\Pr(f\circ w\circ p)=0}
\]
for every compatible past $p$ and future $f$.  Every reachable,
future-separated linear realization of the same table is uniquely similar to
this response realization.  No Kraus map, Stinespring environment, Hilbert
metric, or formal reverse is used.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
A forward polynomial vanishes on the response spaces exactly when it sends
every past column to the zero response function, which is equivalent to the
displayed scalar identities against all futures.  The universal similarity is
the uniqueness part of \Cref{thm:hankel-minimality}, extended multiplicatively
from the primitive transitions.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Exact finite/infinite linear-predictive alternative]
\label{thm:predictive-alternative}
Let $H_n$ be an exhaustive increasing family of finite typed Hankel panels and
put $d_n=\rank H_n$.  The total infinite Hankel rank satisfies
\[
 \boxed{d_\infty=\sup_n d_n.}
\]
If $d_\infty=d<\infty$, the nondecreasing integer ranks stabilize at $d$ and
the complete process has a unique reachable future-separated linear predictor
of dimension $d$.  If $d_\infty=\infty$, no finite-dimensional linear
predictor represents all admitted histories.  No finite panel alone proves
that later innovations will never occur.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Every finite submatrix of the infinite Hankel table is contained in some
exhaustive panel, so its rank is at most $\sup_nd_n$; conversely each $H_n$ is
a finite submatrix, proving equality.  A bounded nondecreasing integer sequence
is eventually constant.  Once a basis of $d$ response columns has appeared,
every later column lies in their span and the canonical response construction
gives the global $d$-dimensional realization.  Infinite rank contradicts the
rank bound of every finite-dimensional realization.  For the last statement,
tensor any fixed finite-horizon process with a classical process which is
constant through that horizon and first emits an arbitrary number of
future-distinguishable states afterward.  This leaves the observed panel
unchanged while making the later rank arbitrarily large.
\end{proof}

% =============================================================================
\section{Finite comb tomography and the canonical minimal CP class}
\label{sec:comb-reconstruction}
% =============================================================================

At slot $k$, let
$E_k=\operatorname{Herm}(H_{2k-1}\otimes H_{2k-2})$.

\begin{lemma}[Physical CP branches span every Choi-coordinate space]
\label{lem:CP-frame-span}
The real span of
$\{M\succeq0:\Tr_{2k-1}M\preceq I\}$ is all of $E_k$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Write any Hermitian $X=X_+-X_-$ with $X_\pm\succeq0$ and scale each nonzero
part so its output partial trace is at most the identity.  Undoing the scales
expresses $X$ as a real linear combination of physical CP branches.
\end{proof}

Choose physical bases $M_{k,\alpha}$ and Hilbert--Schmidt duals
$D_{k,\alpha}$, and define
\[
 R^{(N)}
 =\sum_{\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_N}
 \mathfrak p_N(M_{1,\alpha_1},\ldots,M_{N,\alpha_N})
 D_{N,\alpha_N}\otimes\cdots\otimes D_{1,\alpha_1}.
\]

\begin{theorem}[Finite process-comb tomography]
\label{thm:comb-tomography}
The probability table determines a unique frame-independent Hermitian tensor
$R^{(N)}$ representing every multilinear intervention probability.  It is a
deterministic finite quantum process exactly when
\[
 \boxed{R^{(N)}\succeq0,
 \qquad
 \Tr_{2k-1}R^{(k)}=I_{2k-2}\otimes R^{(k-1)},
 \qquad R^{(0)}=1.}
\]
The positive causal prefix combs are therefore derived consistency outputs;
they are not separate entrance objects.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Tensor products of the selected frames form a basis, so the dual-frame formula
is the unique Riesz representative.  A second frame represents the same
multilinear functional and hence gives the same tensor.  Positivity and the
recursive trace identities are necessary by the Choi theorem and deterministic
causal normalization.  Conversely, minimal purifications of the positive
prefixes can be linked sequentially by purification uniqueness, giving a
completely positive normalized process with Choi tensor $R^{(N)}$.  Uniqueness
of tomography identifies it with the supplied table.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Canonical square-root prefix purification]
For each positive prefix put
\[
 E_k:=\supp R^{(k)},
 \qquad A_k:=\overline{E_k},
 \qquad
 |\Psi_k\rangle:=\operatorname{vec}\bigl((R^{(k)})^{1/2}\bigr)
 \in P_k\otimes A_k.
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Canonical comb-to-memory dilation]
\label{thm:canonical-comb-dilation}
There are finite memories $A_k\cong\overline{\supp R^{(k)}}$, $A_0=\C$, and
isometries
\[
 \boxed{
 V_k:H_{2k-2}\otimes A_{k-1}
 \longrightarrow H_{2k-1}\otimes A_k}
\]
whose sequential link, followed by tracing $A_N$, is $R^{(N)}$.  Every other
support-minimal sequential realization is related by unique memory unitaries
\[
 \boxed{V_k'=(I\otimes U_k)V_k(I\otimes U_{k-1}^*),}
\]
intertwining the minimal record representation.  Consequently all reduced
primitive maps, formal Hilbert--Schmidt reverses, mixed words, process ideals,
contextual ideals, regular traces, word Grams, and flat depths obtained from a
support-minimal representative are canonically isomorphic.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The causal prefix identity makes
$|I\rangle\!\rangle\otimes|\Psi_{k-1}\rangle$ and $|\Psi_k\rangle$
purifications of the same reduced positive operator.  Minimal purification
uniqueness supplies $V_k$; induction is the vectorized Choi-link law.  Applying
the same uniqueness theorem to two minimal sequential realizations gives the
unitaries $U_k$.  Conjugation by $U_k$ transports every Schr\"odinger branch,
and the induced conjugation on Hilbert--Schmidt operator space is unitary, so
it also transports the formal adjoints.  Kernels, contextual matrix
coefficients, regular traces, and word Grams are therefore preserved.
\end{proof}

\begin{countertheorem}[Arbitrary positive factorizations are not interchangeable]
\label{cth:nonminimal-factorization}
The same scalar operational process can have a one-dimensional support-minimal
history algebra and a nonminimal positive realization whose ambient
Hilbert--Schmidt-adjoint algebra is noncommutative.  Hence arbitrary unreduced
positive factorizations cannot define the structural Grand Tensor.
\end{countertheorem}

\begin{proof}
Take the trivial process for which every declared word has probability one.
Its minimal predictive and minimal CP realizations are one dimensional.  On
$M_2(\C)$, realize the same table by the reset channel
$T(X)=\Tr(X)P_0$ with source $P_0$ and terminal trace.  Then
$T=|P_0)(I|$ and $T_{\rm HS}^*=|I)(P_0|$.  On
$\Span\{P_0,I\}$ these two rank-one operators generate all of $M_2(\C)$;
on the off-diagonal complement they vanish and the unit acts scalarly.
Thus $C^*(I,T,T_{\rm HS}^*)\cong M_2(\C)\oplus\C$, although the complete
unmarked table is the trivial one.  The extra algebra is manufactured by the
ambient adjoint moving between reachable and spectator directions.  Support
reduction before adjoint closure is therefore necessary.
\end{proof}

\begin{countertheorem}[Scalar data do not select a $C^*$-adjoint]
\label{cth:metric-adjoint-no-go}
Let $A=\diag(\alpha,\beta)$ with $0<\alpha<\beta<1$.  With the standard metric,
$C^*(A,A^*)\cong\C^2$.  For
$G_t=\begin{psmallmatrix}1&t\\t&1\end{psmallmatrix}$, $0<t<1$, the
$G_t$-adjoint $A^{\dagger_t}=G_t^{-1}AG_t$ generates with $A$ the full
$M_2(\C)$.  Therefore a scalar Hankel realization does not by itself determine
its formal adjoint.
\end{countertheorem}

\begin{proof}
The standard adjoint equals $A$, so the algebra is diagonal.  Since $A$ has
distinct eigenvalues, its spectral projections $E_{11},E_{22}$ are polynomials
in $A$.  The matrix $G_t$ does not commute with $A$, and direct multiplication
shows that both off-diagonal entries of $A^{\dagger_t}$ are nonzero.  Hence
$E_{11}A^{\dagger_t}E_{22}$ and $E_{22}A^{\dagger_t}E_{11}$ are nonzero
multiples of $E_{12}$ and $E_{21}$; together with the diagonal units they
generate $M_2(\C)$.
\end{proof}

\begin{assessment}[Predictive and Stinespring minimality are distinct]
$\mathcal B_X^{\rm pred}$ is the smallest forward executable algebra needed
for scalar prediction.  The support-minimal CP history class is the canonical
positive completion which also supplies mathematical adjoints.  They need not
have the same dimension.  A direct operator-system $C^*$-envelope can bypass
sequential factorization only after a complete ancillary matrix order and
formal-adjoint panel has been supplied or derived; scalar probabilities alone
do not contain that additional structure.
\end{assessment}

% =============================================================================
\section{The support-minimal process-history algebra}
\label{sec:process-history-algebra}
% =============================================================================

Use the canonical support-minimal record-conditioned CP class of
\Cref{thm:canonical-comb-dilation}.  For each typed boundary object $\xi$, put
$\mathscr X_\xi=\mathcal B(A_\xi)$ with normalized Hilbert--Schmidt product and
$\mathscr X_X=\bigoplus_\xi\mathscr X_\xi$.  For a primitive branch
$a:\xi\to\eta$, let $T_a$ be its reduced Schr\"odinger CP superoperator and
put $\rho_X(a)=P_\eta T_aP_\xi$.  Adjoin a formal reverse $a^\sharp$ represented
by $\rho_X(a)^*_{\rm HS}$; this is a mathematical adjoint, not an asserted
executable reverse channel.

\begin{theorem}[Canonical process-history representation]
\label{thm:process-representation}
Let $\mathfrak F_X^{\min,\rm op}$ be the free finite-object path $*$-algebra on
the minimal core--record alphabet.  Then
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal A_X^{\rm proc}
 :=\mathfrak F_X^{\min,\rm op}/\Ker\rho_X
 \cong C^*(\rho_X(a):a\in\Sigma_X^{\min,\rm op})}
\]
is a finite-dimensional $C^*$-algebra.  It is independent of physical CP
frames, Kraus coordinates, square-root purification coordinates, and the
chosen support-minimal representative.  This independence does not extend to
arbitrary unreduced positive factorizations.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Typed concatenation is sent to block composition, object units to orthogonal
projections, and sharpening to Hilbert--space adjoint, so $\rho_X$ is a
$*$-homomorphism and its kernel is a two-sided $*$-ideal.  Its finite-dimensional
image is a $C^*$-algebra.  The support-minimal unitary covariance in
\Cref{thm:canonical-comb-dilation} conjugates the complete word representation
and therefore gives the unique generator-fixing $*$-isomorphism.  The final
qualification is \Cref{cth:nonminimal-factorization}.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Derived common finite CP completion]
\label{thm:common-CP-completion}
Every finite family of finite-dimensional CP trace-nonincreasing maps admits a
simultaneous finite controlled-unitary completion.  Every finite CP
decomposition of one Store channel has one common Stinespring--Naimark
dilation with orthogonal outcome projections, and every finite word family has
compatible path-labelled dilations under increasing word depth.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
A Stinespring contraction $V:H\to K$ has the Julia unitary
\[
 \begin{pmatrix}V&(I-VV^*)^{1/2}\\(I-V^*V)^{1/2}&-V^*\end{pmatrix}
 :H\oplus K\to K\oplus H.
\]
Taking finite direct sums gives simultaneous control.  For a decomposition
$\Psi_j\le_{\rm CP}\Phi$, the finite CP Radon--Nikodym theorem gives effects
$F_j$ in one minimal environment; adjoining
$F_0=I-\sum_jF_j$ and applying Naimark dilation gives orthogonal outcome
projections.  Tensoring fresh minimal environments along each finite word and
taking the finite direct sum yields path-labelled dilations; minimal
Stinespring uniqueness gives compatible source-cyclic compression.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Canonical source-ideal decomposition]
\label{thm:central-source-decomposition}
For any declared source packet $\mathcal S\subseteq\mathcal A_X^{\rm proc}$,
there is a unique central projection $z_{\mathcal S}$ such that
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal I(\mathcal S)=z_{\mathcal S}\mathcal A_X^{\rm proc},
 \qquad
 \mathcal A_X^{\rm proc}
 =z_{\mathcal S}\mathcal A_X^{\rm proc}
 \oplus(1-z_{\mathcal S})\mathcal A_X^{\rm proc}.}
\]
Residual histories are therefore retained as canonical central ideals rather
than assumed absent or manually routed.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
A finite-dimensional $C^*$-algebra is a direct sum of simple matrix blocks,
and every two-sided ideal is the direct sum of a unique subset of those blocks.
The sum of their central units is $z_{\mathcal S}$.
\end{proof}

% =============================================================================
\section{Contextual future separation and record survival}
\label{sec:predictive-history-quotient}
% =============================================================================

\begin{definition}[Complete contextual history-null ideal]
\label{def:history-null-ideal}
For the process algebra define
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal N_X^{\rm fut}
 :=\{q:R_j(uqv)=R_j(uq^*v)=0
 \text{ for every admitted }R_j\text{ and all }u,v\in\mathcal A_X^{\rm proc}\}.}
\]
All minimal readable-record coordinates are included among the $R_j$; optional
full-provenance point Reads are included only when physically declared.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Operational contextual nullity is a two-sided $*$-ideal]
\label{lem:contextual-null-ideal}
$\mathcal N_X^{\rm fut}$ is a two-sided $*$-ideal, and
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal A_X^{\rm hist}
 :=\mathcal A_X^{\rm proc}/\mathcal N_X^{\rm fut}}
\]
is a finite-dimensional contextually future-separated $C^*$-algebra.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
If $q$ is null and $c,d\in\mathcal A_X^{\rm proc}$, then
$R_j(u(cqd)v)=R_j((uc)q(dv))=0$ in every context.  The second family in the
definition makes the space $*$-stable.  A finite-dimensional $*$-ideal is
closed.  A nonzero quotient class fails at least one defining null test and is
therefore future visible.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Universal contextual history envelope]
\label{thm:contextual-envelope-universal}
$\mathcal A_X^{\rm hist}$ is the minimal context-preserving, contextually
future-separated $C^*$-history envelope.  Precisely, if
$\pi:\mathcal A_X^{\rm proc}\twoheadrightarrow B$ is a $C^*$-quotient through
which every contextual Read factors, then $\Ker\pi\subseteq\mathcal N_X^{\rm fut}$
and there is a canonical surjection
$B\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal A_X^{\rm hist}$.  If $B$ is itself contextually
future separated, this map is a $*$-isomorphism.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Every element of $\Ker\pi$ is zero in every factored context, so it belongs to
$\mathcal N_X^{\rm fut}$.  The quotient universal property gives the
surjection $A/\Ker\pi\to A/\mathcal N_X^{\rm fut}$.  If the kernel of that
surjection were nonzero, it would define a nonzero class in $B$ annihilated by
all factored contexts, contradicting contextual separation.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[A finite separating Read panel exists]
\label{lem:finite-read-panel}
At most $\dim\mathcal A_X^{\rm proc}$ scalar contextual coordinates have common
kernel $\mathcal N_X^{\rm fut}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Starting from the whole finite-dimensional algebra, whenever the intersection
of the selected kernels is larger than $\mathcal N_X^{\rm fut}$, choose one
vector outside the radical and one contextual coordinate which detects it.
The intersection dimension strictly decreases, so the procedure terminates.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Record-survival theorem]
\label{thm:record-survival}
In $\mathcal A_X^{\rm hist}$:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(S\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item distinct minimal readable-record classes remain distinct;
\item every nonzero minimal record projection survives;
\item every deterministic writer attached to a nonzero branch survives;
\item every optional provenance point whose Read is physically declared also
      survives;
\item unread fibre contrasts removed by $\operatorname{MinRec}$ never enter the
      intrinsic history algebra.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Distinct minimal classes are separated by an admitted future coordinate, so
their projection difference is not contextually null.  A nonzero writer is
detected by a preparation on which its branch has nonzero probability followed
by the Read of its target class.  The same argument applies to physically
protected provenance points.  The final statement is the definition and
universal property of the minimal record, together with
\Cref{cth:record-cstar-merge}.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[Order of the two minimizations]
Classical future-equivalence minimization must precede writer completion.
Afterward, the contextual $C^*$-ideal removes entire algebraic directions
invisible in all two-sided word contexts; it cannot merge surviving classical
points.  Minimal record, minimal linear predictor, and minimal contextual
$C^*$-history envelope are three distinct constructions.
\end{firewall}

% =============================================================================
\section{Intrinsic normalization and the finite structural Grand Tensor}
\label{sec:full-grand-tensor}
% =============================================================================

For a finite-dimensional unital $C^*$-algebra $\mathcal A$, let $L_a(b)=ab$.

\begin{definition}[Normalized regular trace]
\label{def:regular-trace}
Define
\[
 \tau_{\rm reg}^{\mathcal A}(a)=\Tr_\C(L_a),
 \qquad
 \widehat\tau_{\rm reg}^{\mathcal A}(a)
 =\frac{\tau_{\rm reg}^{\mathcal A}(a)}{\dim_\C\mathcal A}.
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Canonical faithful trace]
\label{thm:regular-trace}
The normalized regular trace is a faithful tracial state preserved by every
$*$-isomorphism.  If
$\mathcal A\cong\bigoplus_\lambda M_{n_\lambda}(\C)$, then
\[
 \boxed{
 \tau_{\rm reg}^{\mathcal A}(a)
 =\sum_\lambda n_\lambda\Tr(a_\lambda),
 \qquad
 \dim_\C\mathcal A=\sum_\lambda n_\lambda^2.}
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
$L_{ab}=L_aL_b$, so cyclicity of the ordinary trace gives traciality.  On
$M_n(\C)$, left multiplication is $a\otimes I_n$, with trace $n\Tr(a)$.
The displayed formula gives positivity and faithfulness on $a^*a$.
Normalization follows from $L_1=I$, and isomorphism invariance follows because
left multiplication is conjugated by the isomorphism.
\end{proof}

Let $\mathcal W^{\min,\rm op}_{X,\le r}$ have basis the composable mixed
minimal core--record words of length at most $r$, and put
$W_{X,r}e_w=[w]\in\mathcal A_X^{\rm hist}$.

\begin{definition}[Structural minimal operational Renewal Grand Tensor]
\label{def:grand-tensor}
Define
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathbb K^{\min,\rm op}_{X,r}(v,w)
 :=\widehat\tau_{\rm reg}^{\mathcal A_X^{\rm hist}}([v]^*[w]).}
\]
The canonical minimal operational Grand Tensor is
\[
 \boxed{
 \boldsymbol{\mathbb T}^{\min,\rm op}_{\Grand,X}
 :=\left(\mathcal A_X^{\rm hist},
 \{\mathbb K^{\min,\rm op}_{X,r}\}_{r\ge0},
 \mathfrak R_X^{\min}\right).}
\]
If every generated record value has a physical point Read, then
$\mathfrak R_X^{\min}=C(\widetilde{\mathscr R}_X)$ and this object is also
denoted
$\boldsymbol{\mathbb T}^{\min,op}_{\Grand,X}$.  Otherwise the optional
full-provenance tensor
$\boldsymbol{\mathbb T}^{\rm full,prot}_{\Grand,X}$ is canonical only relative
to that stronger Read policy.
\end{definition}

\begin{remark}[Structural shadow of the revised Grand Tensor]
The object in \Cref{def:grand-tensor} is the tensor denoted
$\boldsymbol{\mathbb T}_{\Grand,X}^{\rm old}$ in
\Cref{sec:relational-completion}.  It remains the canonical answer to the
finite structural reconstruction problem for the original Store cylinder.
The revised Renewal Grand Tensor is obtained by applying this same construction
to the conservative relational process $\mathsf P_X^{\rm rel}$ and retaining
the paired cutoff-polarization data.  Consequently no formula below must be
rewritten merely to preserve the old structural shadow; the superscript
``rel'' is required only when the persistent relation packet is being used.
\end{remark}

\begin{theorem}[Automatic finite operational-history saturation]
\label{thm:automatic-history-saturation}
At every finite cutoff there is a least $r_X$ such that
\[
 \boxed{\rank\mathbb K_{X,r_X}=\rank\mathbb K_{X,r_X+1}.}
\]
At this depth the word span is the whole $\mathcal A_X^{\rm hist}$, and the
panel through depth $r_X+1$ reconstructs the object units, minimal record
algebra, multiplication, involution, conditional predictive core algebras, and
every represented mixed history.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Faithfulness of the regular trace makes the Gram kernel exactly the word
relation space.  The nested word spans stabilize in the finite-dimensional
algebra.  At the first rank equality two consecutive spans have equal
dimension and are equal.  Left multiplication by every generator preserves
the stabilized span; since it contains the units, it contains every generated
word.  The one-step extension records each generator's left multiplication on
a spanning basis, and reversed words reconstruct the involution.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Canonical minimal finite-emergence theorem]
\label{thm:grand-emergence}
Every bare finite intervention--renewal datum satisfying the finite consistency
tests determines a canonical minimal structural Renewal Grand Tensor with the
following exact properties.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(E\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item the combs are reconstructed from the probability table rather than
      supplied;
\item the generated ledger is reduced to the unique minimal future-readable
      record, while every actual point Read is preserved;
\item the table-native executable algebra and the minimal linear predictor are
      realization free;
\item the positive comb determines a canonical square-root support-minimal CP
      class, unique up to record-intertwining memory unitaries;
\item the support-minimal process algebra, contextual future quotient, central
      source atlas, and intrinsic regular trace are canonical;
\item the complete word hierarchy is positive, finite flat, and reconstructs
      the represented monoidal $*$-algebra;
\item unread record refinements do not enlarge the minimal tensor, whereas a
      larger readable provenance tensor decomposes as the finite bundle of
      \Cref{thm:record-refinement-bundle};
\item arbitrary unreduced positive factorizations and arbitrary Hilbert metrics
      do not define the structural $C^*$-history algebra;
\item a faithful physical future metric preserves word relations and the
      monoidal algebra, but quantitative conditioning remains metric dependent;
\item direct fringes, infinite-horizon finite memory, autonomous physical
      renewal, and regulator-uniform gaps are separate certificates.
\end{enumerate}
Thus finite structural emergence is unconditional relative to complete finite
operational data and the actual Read interface, not relative to an arbitrary
hidden ledger or a few microscopic constants.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Comb reconstruction is \Cref{thm:comb-tomography}; record minimality and
completion are
\Cref{thm:minimal-record,thm:minimal-read-algebra,thm:operational-record-completion}.
The executable and linear predictive statements are
\Cref{thm:typed-hankel-realization,thm:hankel-minimality,thm:executable-predictive-algebra}.
The minimal CP class is \Cref{thm:canonical-comb-dilation}; the necessity of
support reduction and the metric boundary are
\Cref{cth:nonminimal-factorization,cth:metric-adjoint-no-go}.
The process and contextual algebras are
\Cref{thm:process-representation,thm:contextual-envelope-universal,thm:central-source-decomposition}.
Regular-trace positivity and flatness are
\Cref{thm:regular-trace,thm:automatic-history-saturation}.  Record refinements
are \Cref{thm:record-refinement-bundle}, and physical-metric invariance is
\Cref{thm:metric-independence}.  The final limitations are established in the
cutoff, infinite-horizon, coherence, and autonomous-renewal theorems below.
\end{proof}

\begin{countertheorem}[Degree-one data do not reconstruct multiplication]
\label{cth:pairwise-not-monoidal-new}
There are two finite unital $C^*$-algebra structures on one Hilbert
source-transfer datum with identical degree-one and pairwise source moments,
while one is commutative and the other simple noncommutative.
\end{countertheorem}

\begin{proof}
Take $\mathcal A_1=\C^4$ and $\mathcal A_2=M_2(\C)$ with normalized traces.
Their GNS spaces both have dimension four.  Choose a unitary carrying unit to
unit and transport the second multiplication to the first Hilbert space.  With
source map the identity and transfer $T=I/2$, every pairwise transfer moment is
$2^{-n}I$ in both structures, while the center dimensions are four and one.
\end{proof}


\begin{theorem}[Word-level monoidal transport residual]
\label{thm:GT-monoidal-transport}
Let $\mathcal A$ and $\mathcal B$ be finite source-generated unital
$C^*$-algebras with faithful traces, and let $r_*$ be a common flat word depth.
Choose word bases $(w_\alpha)$ and $(\widetilde w_\alpha)$ through that depth,
and let $U:L^2(\mathcal A)\to L^2(\mathcal B)$ be a unitary carrying the
primitive degree-one source vectors to their proposed images.  Form the
residual synthesis whose columns are
\[
 U1-1,
 \qquad U(w_\alpha^*)-U(w_\alpha)^*,
 \qquad U(w_\alpha w_\beta)-U(w_\alpha)U(w_\beta),
\]
and put
\[
 \boxed{\mathbb I_{\rm mon}(U)=\mathscr R_U^*\mathscr R_U\succeq0.}
 \tag{GT.1}
\]
Then $\mathbb I_{\rm mon}(U)=0$ if and only if $U$ is the $L^2$ extension of a
trace-preserving unital $*$-isomorphism
$\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$.  For composable unital linear maps,
\[
 \boxed{
 R_{VU}(a,b)=V R_U(a,b)+R_V(Ua,Ub),
 \qquad R_U(a,b)=U(ab)-U(a)U(b).}
 \tag{GT.2}
\]
Thus a terminal product defect is the transported sum of the local product
writers.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
If the residual vanishes, $U$ preserves the unit, involution, and products of a
spanning word basis.  Bilinearity and the flat-depth reconstruction extend
these identities to the complete generated algebra, and unitarity preserves
the faithful trace inner product.  The converse is immediate.  The chain rule
is obtained by adding and subtracting $V(Ua) V(Ub)$.
\end{proof}

\begin{countertheorem}[Flat linear holonomy need not be monoidal]
\label{cth:GT-flat-linear-not-monoidal}
There is a two-edge cycle of Hilbert-unitary source transports whose total
linear holonomy is the identity while both edgewise monoidal residuals are
nonzero.
\end{countertheorem}

\begin{proof}
Take $\mathcal A=\C^3$ with its normalized trace.  On the mean-zero real plane
choose a rotation $R$ through an angle which is not induced by a coordinate
permutation, and let $R$ fix the constant vector.  Then $R$ is unitary on
$L^2(\mathcal A)$ but is not an algebra automorphism.  The cycle transports
$R$ and $R^{-1}$ have product $I$, whereas
$\mathbb I_{\rm mon}(R)$ and $\mathbb I_{\rm mon}(R^{-1})$ are positive.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Positive-congruence invariance of the finite algebra]
\label{thm:metric-independence}
Let $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_0$ be the regular inner product and let
$\mathfrak g_X$ be any faithful physical future form.  There is a unique
$G_X\succ0$ such that
\[
 \mathfrak g_X(a,b)=\langle a,G_Xb\rangle_0,
 \qquad
 \mathbb K^G_{X,r}=W_{X,r}^*G_XW_{X,r}.
\]
If $g_-I\preceq G_X\preceq g_+I$, then
\[
 \boxed{g_-\mathbb K_{X,r}\preceq\mathbb K^G_{X,r}
 \preceq g_+\mathbb K_{X,r}.}
\]
Every faithful physical metric has the same word relations, ranks, flat depth,
unit, involution, multiplication, and history algebra.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Finite-dimensional Riesz representation gives $G_X\succ0$.  Conjugating the
operator bounds by $W_{X,r}$ gives the Gram bounds.  A coefficient vector has
zero physical quadratic form exactly when its synthesized word is zero,
because $G_X$ is positive definite.  Hence the Gram kernels, ranks, and all
relation-based reconstructions agree.
\end{proof}

\section{The degree-one Store shadow and source calculus}
\label{sec:degree-one-source}
% =============================================================================

\begin{theorem}[Predictive completely positive Radon--Nikodym envelope]
\label{thm:RN-envelope}
Let $V:\mathcal H\to\mathcal K\otimes\mathcal E$ be a minimal Stinespring
isometry for a finite UCP map
$\Phi:\mathcal B(\mathcal K)\to\mathcal B(\mathcal H)$.  For
$F\in\mathcal B(\mathcal E)$ define
$\Theta_V(F)(A)=V^*(A\otimes F)V$.  Then
\[
 \boxed{
 \{F:0\preceq F\preceq I\}
 \xrightarrow{\ F\mapsto\Theta_V(F)\ }
 \{\Psi:0\le_{\rm CP}\Psi\le_{\rm CP}\Phi\}}
\]
is an affine order isomorphism.  Finite POVMs correspond bijectively to finite
CP decompositions of $\Phi$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Positive contractions give dominated CP maps directly.  Conversely, the
finite CP Radon--Nikodym theorem gives a positive contraction in the commutant
of the represented system algebra.  For the representation
$A\mapsto A\otimes I_\mathcal E$, the commutant is
$I_\mathcal K\otimes\mathcal B(\mathcal E)$.  Minimality makes the derivative
unique: if $\Theta_V(F)=0$, matrix coefficients between the spanning vectors
$(A\otimes I)V\xi$ force $F=0$.  Summing coordinates proves the POVM claim.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Minimal-realization naturality]
\label{thm:minimal-naturality}
If a physical automorphism satisfies
$U_g^*\Phi(A)U_g=\Phi(Z_g^*AZ_g)$, there is a unique unitary $W_g$ on the
minimal environment such that
\[
 \boxed{(Z_g\otimes W_g)V=VU_g,}
 \qquad
 g\cdot\Theta_V(F)=\Theta_V(W_gFW_g^*).
\]
Projective multipliers obey
$W_gW_h=a(g,h)b(g,h)^{-1}W_{gh}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The isometries $VU_g$ and $(Z_g\otimes I)V$ are minimal dilations of the same
map, so minimal Stinespring uniqueness gives $W_g$.  Successive application
gives the cocycle law, and direct substitution gives the coordinate action.
\end{proof}

\begin{construction}[Degree-one latent source]
\label{con:degree-one-source}
Choose a minimal Stinespring realization of the marked Store channel $\Phi_X$.
For primitive Store-dominated basis ports let $F_{\alpha j,X}$ be their unique
Radon--Nikodym derivatives and put
\[
 \mathcal U_X^{(1)}=\Span_\C\{F_{\alpha j,X}\}_{\alpha,j}.
\]
Let $B_{\alpha,X}$ synthesize these derivatives and
$B_X=\bigoplus_\alpha B_{\alpha,X}$.  A chosen faithful physical future form
has source map $C_X$ and Riesz operator $G_X=C_X^*C_X$ after its null space is
shorted.  The calibrated degree-one pairwise shadow is
\[
 \boxed{\GTX:=B_X^*G_XB_X.}
\]
Its intrinsic regular version is obtained by taking the regular metric.
\end{construction}

\begin{corollary}[Block Cauchy--Schwarz inequality]
\label{cor:block-CS}
For $p\in\mathcal P_{\alpha,X}$ and $q\in\mathcal P_{\beta,X}$,
\[
 \abs{\ip{p}{\mathbb T_{\alpha\beta,X}^{\BR}q}}^2
 \le
 \ip{p}{\mathbb T_{\alpha\alpha,X}^{\BR}p}
 \ip{q}{\mathbb T_{\beta\beta,X}^{\BR}q}.
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Apply Cauchy--Schwarz to $C_XB_{\alpha,X}p$ and
$C_XB_{\beta,X}q$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Exact source Schur residual]
\label{thm:source-Schur}
Let $S_1:E_1\to\mathcal H$ and $S_2:E_2\to\mathcal H$ be finite source maps,
and put
\[
 A=S_1^*S_1,\qquad B=S_1^*S_2,\qquad D=S_2^*S_2.
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathbb G_{2\mid1}:=D-B^*A^\dagger B
 =S_2^*(I-P_1)S_2\succeq0,}
 \qquad P_1=S_1A^\dagger S_1^*,
\]
with
\[
 \mathbb G_{2\mid1}=0\iff\Ran S_2\subseteq\Ran S_1,
\]
and
\[
 \rank\begin{pmatrix}A&B\\B^*&D\end{pmatrix}-\rank A
 =\rank\mathbb G_{2\mid1}.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The Moore--Penrose formula gives the orthogonal projection
$P_1=S_1(S_1^*S_1)^\dagger S_1^*$.  Hence
$B^*A^\dagger B=S_2^*P_1S_2$.  Positivity, the range criterion, and the rank
increment follow from the orthogonal residual $(I-P_1)S_2$.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Joint-source universality, shorting, and score export}
\label{sec:joint-source-universality}

The preceding one-sided Schur residual becomes a complete comparison theorem
when two typed word families are operationally visible in one covered history
experiment.  This is stronger than reconstructing the two marginal sectors
separately.

\begin{definition}[Jointly visible typed source families]
\label{def:jointly-visible-sources}
Let $S_a:E_a\to\mathcal H$ $(a=1,2)$ be finite source syntheses in one
faithful operational history carrier.  They are \emph{jointly visible} when
the admitted word or differentiated-score panel contains every mixed pairing
$\langle S_2y,S_1x\rangle$.  Put
\[
 G_a=S_a^*S_a,
 \qquad C_{21}=S_2^*S_1,
 \qquad
 \mathbb G_{12}=
 \begin{pmatrix}G_1&C_{21}^*\\ C_{21}&G_2\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Separate visibility of $G_1$ and $G_2$ is not joint visibility.
\end{definition}

\begin{countertheorem}[Marginal canonicality does not determine relative orientation]
\label{cth:marginals-no-relative-orientation}
For fixed $G_1,G_2\succeq0$, the positive completions are precisely
\[
 \boxed{C_{21}=G_2^{1/2}KG_1^{1/2},\qquad \|K\|\le1,}
\]
where $K$ acts between the faithful source supports.  Thus two independently
canonical marginal sectors leave a full contraction ball of relative
orientations.
\end{countertheorem}

\begin{proof}
On the faithful supports, positivity of $\mathbb G_{12}$ is equivalent by the
Schur complement to
$G_1-C_{21}^*G_2^{-1}C_{21}\succeq0$.  Hence
$K=G_2^{-1/2}C_{21}G_1^{-1/2}$ is a contraction.  Conversely the factorization
with a contraction makes
$\begin{psmallmatrix}I&K^*\\K&I\end{psmallmatrix}\succeq0$ and therefore
makes the block Gram positive.  Moore--Penrose inverses give the same argument
on nonfaithful supports.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Canonical joint-source universality]
\label{thm:joint-source-universality}
For jointly visible source families, $\mathbb G_{12}$ is a canonical positive
operational coordinate.  The quotient
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal H_{12}^{\min}
 :=(E_1\oplus E_2)/\Ker\mathbb G_{12}}
\]
with inner product
$\langle[u],[v]\rangle=\langle u,\mathbb G_{12}v\rangle$ and synthesis
$S_{12}^{\min}u=[u]$ is source minimal and satisfies
\[
 \boxed{(S_{12}^{\min})^*S_{12}^{\min}=\mathbb G_{12},\qquad
 \dim\mathcal H_{12}^{\min}=\rank\mathbb G_{12}.}
\]
Every other source-minimal common realization with the same four Gram blocks
is related to it by a unique unitary fixing both source families.  The
construction is invariant under support-minimal Stinespring gauge and under
unread record refinements.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Positivity makes the displayed quotient inner product well defined and
positive definite.  The images of the two coefficient summands span the
quotient, so the realization is source minimal and its Gram is the prescribed
block.  If $T_1,T_2$ are another minimal realization, define
$U[S_1x+S_2y]=T_1x+T_2y$.  Equality of the complete block Gram makes this map
well defined and isometric; source minimality makes it onto.  It is unique
because the two source ranges span.  Support-minimal coordinate changes and
unread record refinements preserve every mixed operational pairing, so they
induce the same source-fixing unitary by this uniqueness.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Mutual range tests, normalized transport, and universal short]
\label{thm:joint-source-short}
Let $\Pi_a$ project onto $\Ran S_a$.  The two Schur residuals are
\[
 \boxed{R_{1\mid2}=G_1-C_{21}^*G_2^\dagger C_{21}
 =S_1^*(I-\Pi_2)S_1\succeq0,}
\]
\[
 \boxed{R_{2\mid1}=G_2-C_{21}G_1^\dagger C_{21}^*
 =S_2^*(I-\Pi_1)S_2\succeq0.}
\]
They vanish exactly on the corresponding range inclusions and both vanish
exactly when the source ranges coincide.  The normalized cross transport
\[
 \boxed{K_{21}=G_2^{\dagger/2}C_{21}G_1^{\dagger/2}}
\]
is a contraction; its singular values are the cosines of the principal angles
between the two source ranges.  Moreover the Anderson--Trapp short of
$\mathbb G_{12}$ to $E_1$ is
\[
 \boxed{
 \operatorname{Short}_{E_1}(\mathbb G_{12})
 =\begin{pmatrix}R_{1\mid2}&0\\0&0\end{pmatrix},}
\]
equivalently
\[
 \langle x,R_{1\mid2}x\rangle
 =\inf_{y\in E_2}\langle(x,y),\mathbb G_{12}(x,y)\rangle.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The projection formulas are the Moore--Penrose identities used in
\Cref{thm:source-Schur}.  Whitening gives
$K_{21}=V_2^*V_1$ for the isometric source embeddings
$V_a=S_aG_a^{\dagger/2}$, so it is contractive and has the stated principal
angle interpretation.  Minimizing
$\|S_1x+S_2y\|^2$ over $y$ subtracts the orthogonal projection of $S_1x$ onto
$\Ran S_2$ and yields $\|(I-\Pi_2)S_1x\|^2$, proving the short formula.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Corrected Douglas factor]
\label{thm:corrected-Douglas-factor}
If $R_{1\mid2}=0$, then the unique reduced factor
\[
 \boxed{D_{2\leftarrow1}=G_2^\dagger C_{21}}
\]
satisfies
\[
 \boxed{S_1=S_2D_{2\leftarrow1},\qquad
 D_{2\leftarrow1}^*G_2D_{2\leftarrow1}=G_1.}
\]
Thus it is an isometry for the two canonical source Gram norms.  It need not be
a contraction in arbitrary Euclidean coefficient norms.  The stronger order
\[
 S_1S_1^*\preceq S_2S_2^*
\]
is equivalent to the existence of a factor $S_1=S_2D$ with $\|D\|\le1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Zero residual gives $S_1=\Pi_2S_1=S_2G_2^\dagger S_2^*S_1$, proving the
factorization and uniqueness on $\supp G_2$.  Taking Grams gives the metric
isometry.  The final equivalence is the finite Douglas lemma: factorization by
a contraction implies the operator order; conversely polar reduction on the
range of $S_2$ constructs the contraction.  For example $S_2=1$, $S_1=2$ has
zero residual but reduced factor $2$, showing why range inclusion alone is not
an Euclidean contraction statement.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Simultaneous nuisance short]
\label{thm:simultaneous-nuisance-short}
Let $A:E\to\mathcal H$, $S:E\to\mathcal H$, and $N:F\to\mathcal H$ be
completed, Euler, and common nuisance syntheses with joint Gram blocks
\[
 M=A^*A,\quad \mathbb E=S^*S,\quad B=A^*S,
 \quad G_N=N^*N,\quad C_M=N^*A,\quad C_E=N^*S.
\]
With $P_N=NG_N^\dagger N^*$, put
$\widehat A=(I-P_N)A$ and $\widehat S=(I-P_N)S$.  Then
\[
 \boxed{\widehat M=M-C_M^*G_N^\dagger C_M,}
\]
\[
 \boxed{\widehat{\mathbb E}=\mathbb E-C_E^*G_N^\dagger C_E,}
\]
\[
 \boxed{\widehat B=B-C_M^*G_N^\dagger C_E.}
\]
The block
$\begin{psmallmatrix}\widehat M&\widehat B\\
\widehat B^*&\widehat{\mathbb E}\end{psmallmatrix}$ is positive and is the
short of the three-family Gram to the completed--Euler coefficient space.
Shorting the two marginals separately while leaving $B$ unchanged is generally
incorrect.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The formulas follow by expanding
$A^*(I-P_N)A$, $S^*(I-P_N)S$, and
$A^*(I-P_N)S$.  Their block is the Gram of the two shorted syntheses and is
therefore positive.  The variational characterization of the short follows by
minimizing the joint norm over the nuisance coefficient.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Operational score export and unread-refinement law]
\label{thm:operational-score-export}
Let $p_{\theta,\phi}$ be one finite positive record distribution in which
$\theta$ and $\phi$ deform two declared source families.  At the reference
point put
\[
 s_1=\partial_\theta\log p_{\theta,\phi}|_0,
 \qquad
 s_2=\partial_\phi\log p_{\theta,\phi}|_0.
\]
Then the joint Fisher block
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathbb I_{12}=
 \begin{pmatrix}
 \mathbb E[s_1s_1^*]&\mathbb E[s_1s_2^*]\\
 \mathbb E[s_2s_1^*]&\mathbb E[s_2s_2^*]
 \end{pmatrix}\succeq0}
\]
is the joint source Gram of the score syntheses.  If a fine record is
coarse-grained to a record $R_c$, then
\[
 s_c=\mathbb E[s_f\mid R_c],
 \qquad
 \boxed{
 \mathbb I_f=\mathbb I_c+
 \mathbb E[(s_f-s_c)(s_f-s_c)^*].}
\]
Thus genuinely unread refinements contribute zero joint innovation, while an
informative refinement adds a positive block.  Projecting both source scores
orthogonally away from a nuisance score family gives exactly the simultaneous
short of \Cref{thm:simultaneous-nuisance-short}.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Score centering follows from differentiating normalization.  The displayed
matrix is the Gram of the two score vectors in $L^2(p_0)$.  Differentiating the
coarse probability, which is the sum of the fine probabilities in a fibre,
gives the conditional-expectation identity.  Orthogonal decomposition into a
conditional expectation and a centred fibre contrast gives the covariance
Pythagoras formula.  Linear least-squares projection onto nuisance scores is the
Moore--Penrose Schur short.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Strict joint-source cutoff functor]
\label{thm:joint-source-cutoff-functor}
For $X\le Y$, let $j_{a,Y/X}:E_{a,X}\to E_{a,Y}$ be typed source isometries.
If all four blocks compress,
\[
 \boxed{j_{a,Y/X}^*G_{ab,Y}j_{b,Y/X}=G_{ab,X},
 \qquad a,b\in\{1,2\},}
\]
then there is a unique isometry
\[
 \boxed{\iota_{Y/X}:\mathcal H_{12,X}^{\min}
 \longrightarrow\mathcal H_{12,Y}^{\min}}
\]
satisfying
$\iota_{Y/X}S_{a,X}=S_{a,Y}j_{a,Y/X}$.  These maps compose strictly.  The
normalized transports obey compressed naturality
\[
 \sigma_{2,Y/X}^*K_{21,Y}\sigma_{1,Y/X}=K_{21,X}.
\]
They obey the stronger intertwining relation exactly when
\[
 \boxed{
 \Delta_{21,Y/X}^{\rm new}
 =\|(I-\sigma_{2,Y/X}\sigma_{2,Y/X}^*)
 K_{21,Y}\sigma_{1,Y/X}\|_{\HS}^2=0.}
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Define the cutoff map on Gram-quotient generators by
$[x_1,x_2]\mapsto[j_1x_1,j_2x_2]$.  Compression of the complete block Gram
makes it well defined and isometric; source minimality gives uniqueness.
Agreement on the source generators proves strict composition.  Whitening and
compression give the normalized cross-transport identity.  Decomposing
$K_{21,Y}\sigma_1$ into the old source-$2$ range and its orthogonal complement
shows that the displayed defect is precisely the obstruction to full
intertwining.
\end{proof}



% =============================================================================
\subsection{Cross-record source kernels, source-sufficient records, and transport separation}
\label{sec:source-kernel-record-transport}
% =============================================================================

Let $(\Omega,\nu)$ be one finite physical history law and let
$S_\omega:E\to\mathcal K$ be the pointwise profile of a complete typed source.

\begin{definition}[Complete weighted cross-record source kernel]
\label{def:GT-cross-record-kernel}
The complete source kernel is the positive block matrix
\[
 \boxed{
 (\mathbb K_{\mathcal S})_{\omega\eta}
 =\sqrt{\nu_\omega\nu_\eta}\,S_\omega^*S_\eta.}
 \tag{SK.1}
\]
Its diagonal blocks are the recordwise source energies; its off-diagonal
blocks retain the relative orientation between histories.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Source-minimal kernel realization and uniqueness]
\label{thm:GT-source-kernel-realization}
Every positive block kernel $\mathbb K=[K_{\omega\eta}]\succeq0$ on a faithful
finite law has a realization of the form \textup{(SK.1)}.  The least possible
carrier dimension is $\rank\mathbb K$, and any two source-minimal realizations
are related by one global unitary acting simultaneously on every profile.
The kernel does not determine the probabilities $\nu_\omega$: rescaling
$S_\omega$ by $\sqrt{\nu_\omega/\nu_\omega'}$ leaves $\mathbb K$ unchanged.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Realize $\mathbb K$ by its Gram quotient and divide the $\omega$-th block
synthesis by $\sqrt{\nu_\omega}$.  Gram minimality gives the rank and the
usual source-fixing unitary.  The displayed rescaling proves the final
independence statement.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Exact conditional-source variance and coarsest sufficient record]
\label{thm:GT-source-record-variance}
Let $\mathcal P$ be a partition of $\Omega$.  For $B\in\mathcal P$ put
\[
 \nu_B=\sum_{\omega\in B}\nu_\omega,
 \qquad
 \overline S_B=\nu_B^{-1}\sum_{\omega\in B}\nu_\omega S_\omega.
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{
 G_{\mathcal S}
 =\sum_{B\in\mathcal P}\nu_B\overline S_B^*\overline S_B
 +\mathbb I_{\mathcal S\mid\mathcal P},}
 \tag{SK.2}
\]
where
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathbb I_{\mathcal S\mid\mathcal P}
 =\frac12\sum_{B\in\mathcal P}\frac1{\nu_B}
 \sum_{\omega,\eta\in B}\nu_\omega\nu_\eta
 (S_\omega-S_\eta)^*(S_\omega-S_\eta)\succeq0.}
 \tag{SK.3}
\]
The unique coarsest source-sufficient record identifies exactly those
$\omega,\eta$ for which
$(S_\omega-S_\eta)^*(S_\omega-S_\eta)=0$.  Its innovation rank is the minimum
orthogonal source dimension omitted by the proposed record.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Expand the weighted variance inside each fibre.  Equality of two profiles is
equivalent to vanishing of their positive discrepancy operator.  Finiteness
and the universal property of the joint level-set partition give the coarsest
record statement.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Zero-innovation overlap is pure gauge]
\label{thm:GT-source-overlap-flatness}
Let a connected graph of equal-rank source profiles be realized in one common
carrier.  Whiten the supported profiles and write the normalized overlap on an
edge as $W_{j\leftarrow i}=V_j^*V_i$.  If every edge has zero source-range
innovation in both directions, then all source ranges coincide, every
$W_{j\leftarrow i}$ is unitary, and there are vertex unitaries $Q_i$ such that
\[
 \boxed{W_{j\leftarrow i}=Q_j^*Q_i,
 \qquad W(C)=I\quad\text{for every cycle }C.}
 \tag{SK.4}
\]
Hence nontrivial physical holonomy cannot be inferred from a globally glued
zero-innovation source atlas.  It requires an independent action, unit,
kinetic, return, or intervention transport, or a measured direct-versus-staged
mismatch.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Zero innovation in both directions makes the two whitened isometries have the
same range.  Choose one common isometry $V$ and write $V_i=VQ_i$; then
$V_j^*V_i=Q_j^*Q_i$, whose cycle products telescope.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[Incidence is not dynamics]
\label{fire:GT-incidence-not-dynamics}
The complete source kernel determines linear incidence and record sufficiency.
It does not determine a semigroup, connection, conductance, writer law, or
physical-time generator.  Those objects require their own same-history panel.
In particular a nonflat physical connection may coexist with a trivial
source-overlap atlas.
\end{firewall}

\subsection{Source-core comparison, semigroup transport, and common-action routers}
\label{sec:source-core-comparison}

The finite joint-source calculus above compares source ranges.  The following
package compares an ambient generator with a proposed source compression.  It
is domain independent and applies equally to finite loaded sectors, unbounded
continuum generators, and cutoff families.

\begin{theorem}[Exact source-core Pythagorean comparison]
\label{thm:source-core-Pythagoras}
Let $E,H$ be Hilbert spaces, let $V:E\to H$ be an isometry, and put
$P=VV^*$.  Let $A$ and $N$ be closed densely defined operators on $E$ and $H$
with
\[
 V\mathcal D(A)\subseteq\mathcal D(N).
\]
On $\mathcal D(A)$ define
\[
 R:=NV-VA,
 \qquad
 L:=(I-P)NV,
 \qquad
 C:=V^*NV-A.
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{R=L+VC,\qquad \Ran L\perp\Ran(VC),}
\]
and for all $x,y\in\mathcal D(A)$,
\[
 \boxed{
 \langle Rx,Ry\rangle_H
 =\langle Lx,Ly\rangle_H+\langle Cx,Cy\rangle_E.}
\]
Equivalently, on the graph Hilbert space $\mathcal D(A)_A$,
\[
 \boxed{R^*R=L^*L+C^*C}
\]
as a bounded quadratic-form identity.  In particular,
\[
 \boxed{
 \|NVx-VAx\|^2
 =\|(I-P)NVx\|^2+\|V^*NVx-Ax\|^2.}
\]
Thus zero leakage and zero compression mismatch are equivalent to
\[
 \boxed{NV=VA\quad\text{on }\mathcal D(A).}
\]
If $\mathcal C\subseteq\mathcal D(A)$ is an $A$-core, it is enough that both
defects vanish on $\mathcal C$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Since $P=VV^*$,
\[
 NV-VA=(I-P)NV+P NV-VA=L+V(V^*NV-A)=L+VC.
\]
The first summand lies in $(\Ran V)^\perp$ and the second in $\Ran V$, proving
orthogonality and the inner-product identity.  The map
$NV:\mathcal D(A)_A\to H$ is closed: if $x_n\to x$ in graph norm and
$NVx_n\to y$, then $Vx_n\to Vx$ and closedness of $N$ gives $Vx\in\mathcal
D(N)$ and $NVx=y$.  The closed graph theorem therefore makes $NV$, and hence
$L,C,R$, bounded on the graph Hilbert space.  The quadratic-form identity
follows by polarization.

If the defects vanish on an $A$-core and $x\in\mathcal D(A)$, choose
$x_n\in\mathcal C$ with $x_n\to x$ and $Ax_n\to Ax$.  Then
$NVx_n=VAx_n\to VAx$.  Closedness of $N$ yields $NVx=VAx$.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Norm discipline]
The Pythagorean identity is exact pointwise, in Hilbert--Schmidt norm, and in
any weighted trace-source norm.  For operator norm one has the sharp general
bounds
\[
 \max\{\|L\|,\|C\|\}\le\|R\|
 \le\sqrt{\|L\|^2+\|C\|^2};
\]
an operator-norm equality with the sum of squares need not hold.
\end{remark}

\begin{theorem}[Generator, resolvent, and semigroup intertwining]
\label{thm:source-core-semigroup}
In the setting of \Cref{thm:source-core-Pythagoras}, suppose $A$ and $N$
generate strongly continuous semigroups $S(t)$ and $T(t)$.  Then
\[
 \boxed{NV=VA\text{ on }\mathcal D(A)
 \iff T(t)V=VS(t)\text{ for every }t\ge0.}
\]
For $z\in\rho(N)\cap\rho(A)$ the exact defect identity is
\[
 \boxed{
 (z-N)^{-1}V-V(z-A)^{-1}
 =(z-N)^{-1}R(z-A)^{-1}.}
\]
If $R:\mathcal D(A)_A\to H$ is graph bounded, then for
$x\in\mathcal D(A)$,
\[
 \boxed{
 T(t)Vx-VS(t)x
 =\int_0^tT(t-s)R S(s)x\,\dd s.}
\]
Consequently, if
$\|T(t)\|\le M_Ne^{\omega_Nt}$ and
$\|S(t)\|_{\mathcal D(A)_A\to\mathcal D(A)_A}
 \le M_Ae^{\omega_At}$, then
\[
 \boxed{
 \|T(t)V-VS(t)\|_{\mathcal D(A)_A\to H}
 \le M_NM_A\Phi_t(\omega_N,\omega_A)
      \sqrt{\Delta_{\rm leak}+\Delta_{\rm comp}},}
\]
where
\[
 \Phi_t(\omega_N,\omega_A)
 :=\int_0^te^{\omega_N(t-s)+\omega_As}\,\dd s,
\]
$\Delta_{\rm leak}=\|L\|^2$, and
$\Delta_{\rm comp}=\|C\|^2$ in graph norm.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
If $NV=VA$, then for sufficiently large $\operatorname{Re}z$,
$(z-N)V=V(z-A)$ on $\mathcal D(A)$; inversion gives
$(z-N)^{-1}V=V(z-A)^{-1}$.  Equality of Laplace transforms gives the
semigroup intertwining.  Conversely, differentiating at $t=0$ on
$\mathcal D(A)$ gives the generator relation.

For a nonzero defect, multiply
$(z-N)V-V(z-A)=-R$ by the two resolvents to obtain the displayed resolvent
identity.  Differentiating
$T(t-s)VS(s)x$ in $s$ gives
$-T(t-s)RS(s)x$; integration from $0$ to $t$ gives Duhamel's formula.  The
norm estimate follows from the semigroup bounds and
\Cref{thm:source-core-Pythagoras}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Quantitative history-Gram transport]
\label{cor:source-core-Gram-transport}
Let $S_0:K\to\mathcal D(A)_A$ be bounded and, on a finite time window, put
\[
 B_N(t)=T(t)VS_0,
 \qquad
 B_A(t)=VS(t)S_0.
\]
If $\eta_t=\|B_N(t)-B_A(t)\|$, then
\[
 \boxed{
 \|B_N(t)^*B_N(t)-B_A(t)^*B_A(t)\|
 \le(\|B_N(t)\|+\|B_A(t)\|)\eta_t.}
\]
Moreover the two mutual source Schur residuals are bounded by
$\eta_t^2I$.  Hence, for a cutoff family with uniform graph and semigroup
bounds and
\[
 \Delta_{{\rm leak},X}+\Delta_{{\rm comp},X}\longrightarrow0,
\]
every finite time-window, Krylov, or atomic Hankel Gram obeys
\[
 \boxed{G_{A,X}\preceq G_{N,X}+o(1)I,}
\]
and the mutual source innovations are $o(1)$ at the quadratic defect rate.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Write $B_N=B_A+E$.  Then
$B_N^*B_N-B_A^*B_A=B_A^*E+E^*B_A+E^*E$, which gives the norm estimate in its
symmetric form.  The component of either source orthogonal to the other source
range is the orthogonal projection of $E$, and therefore has norm at most
$\eta_t$; \Cref{thm:source-Schur} gives the Schur bounds.  Apply
\Cref{thm:source-core-semigroup} uniformly and integrate or stack finitely many
times to obtain the cutoff statement.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Common-action Hessian, Schur residual, and Ward router]
\label{thm:common-action-router}
Let $\mathscr A$ be a $C^2$ nonnegative functional of two Hilbert variables
$(\theta,\phi)$ and suppose at a reference point it has a positive Hessian
\[
 H=
 \begin{pmatrix}
 G_\Gamma&C\\ C^*&G_E
 \end{pmatrix}\succeq0.
\]
Equivalently, for the square-root source maps
$B_\Gamma=H^{1/2}|_{X_\Gamma}$ and
$B_E=H^{1/2}|_{X_E}$,
\[
 G_\Gamma=B_\Gamma^*B_\Gamma,
 \qquad C=B_\Gamma^*B_E,
 \qquad G_E=B_E^*B_E.
\]
Assume $\Ran B_\Gamma$ is closed and define
\[
 K=G_\Gamma^\dagger C,
 \qquad
 \mathsf S_E=G_E-C^*G_\Gamma^\dagger C.
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathsf S_E=B_E^*(I-P_\Gamma)B_E\succeq0,}
\]
\[
 \boxed{
 \langle y,\mathsf S_Ey\rangle
 =\inf_x\left\langle\binom{x}{y},H\binom{x}{y}\right\rangle,}
\]
and
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathsf S_E=0
 \iff B_E=B_\Gamma K
 \iff G_E=K^*G_\Gamma K.}
\]
If a source-native infinitesimal symmetry has graph direction
$\mathcal R_Wy=(-Wy,y)$ and the Ward identity gives
$H\mathcal R_W=0$, then
\[
 \boxed{C=G_\Gamma W,
 \qquad G_E=W^*G_\Gamma W,
 \qquad K=W,
 \qquad\mathsf S_E=0.}
\]
Thus the mixed block and router are derivatives of one action rather than an
independently loaded comparison.

If instead
$0\preceq\mathcal R_W^*H\mathcal R_W\preceq\varepsilon^2I$, then
\[
 \boxed{0\preceq\mathsf S_E\preceq\varepsilon^2I.}
\]
If additionally $G_\Gamma\succeq m^2I$ on its support, then
\[
 \boxed{
 \|K-W\|\le \frac{\sqrt{\|H\|}}{m^2}\,\varepsilon.}
\]
In the source-fixing case $W=I$, this gives
$K=I+O(\varepsilon)$ and
$G_E\preceq G_\Gamma+O(\varepsilon)I$ under uniform upper metric bounds.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Let $P_\Gamma$ project onto $\Ran B_\Gamma$.  Moore--Penrose calculus gives
$B_\Gamma G_\Gamma^\dagger B_\Gamma^*=P_\Gamma$, hence
\[
 C^*G_\Gamma^\dagger C
 =B_E^*P_\Gamma B_E.
\]
This proves the source form of the Schur residual.  Minimizing
$\|B_\Gamma x+B_Ey\|^2$ over $x$ subtracts the orthogonal projection of
$B_Ey$ onto $\Ran B_\Gamma$, proving the variational identity and the exact
range criterion.

If $H\mathcal R_W=0$, its two block rows are
$-G_\Gamma W+C=0$ and $-C^*W+G_E=0$, giving the Ward formulas.  For the
approximate statement, the variational formula implies
$\mathsf S_E\preceq\mathcal R_W^*H\mathcal R_W$.  Also
$\|H\mathcal R_W\|^2\le\|H\|\,\|H^{1/2}\mathcal R_W\|^2
\le\|H\|\varepsilon^2$.  The first block row gives
$G_\Gamma(K-W)=C-G_\Gamma W$, and inversion on the supported range yields the
router estimate.  Expanding $K^*G_\Gamma K$ about $W$ gives the final Gram
bound.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[What common action does not supply]
A zero Schur residual gives an intrinsic source-metric isometry, not equality
of arbitrary coefficient-space Euclidean metrics.  Domination by a specified
marginal requires either a source-fixing Ward symmetry, protected anchor and
metric normalization, or a separately proved metric contraction.  Likewise,
the abstract theorem does not construct a domain's action, source core, or
uniform closed-range margin.
\end{firewall}



% =============================================================================
\subsection{Physical secants, protected influence, and effective actions}
\label{sec:physical-secants-effective-actions}
% =============================================================================

The preceding common-action theorem starts from a differentiated positive
functional.  In applications, however, the first physical data may consist only
of finitely many neighbouring laws or deterministic response values.  The
following results separate finite secant geometry, a physical tangent, and a
dynamical action.  This order prevents an arbitrarily chosen interpolation or
positive operator from being promoted to a source-native action.

\begin{definition}[Hellinger source bank]
\label{def:GT-Hellinger-bank}
Let $\Omega$ be finite and let $p_0,p_1,\ldots,p_m$ be full-support
probability laws on $\Omega$.  Put
\[
 \mathfrak h(p):=2\sqrt p\in\ell^2(\Omega),
 \qquad v_a:=\mathfrak h(p_a)-\mathfrak h(p_0),
\]
where the square root is taken coordinatewise.  The Hellinger source synthesis
is
\[
 V_{\rm Hel}:\C^m\longrightarrow\ell^2(\Omega),
 \qquad V_{\rm Hel}c=\sum_{a=1}^mc_av_a,
\]
and its finite secant Gram is
\[
 \boxed{G_{\rm Hel}:=V_{\rm Hel}^*V_{\rm Hel}\succeq0.}
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Finite secant geometry, nuisance shorting, and Fisher limit]
\label{thm:GT-Hellinger-Fisher}
The construction in \Cref{def:GT-Hellinger-bank} has the following properties.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.8em]
\item For any two full-support laws,
      \[
       \boxed{
       \|\mathfrak h(p)-\mathfrak h(q)\|_2^2
       =8\left(1-\sum_{\omega\in\Omega}\sqrt{p(\omega)q(\omega)}\right).}
      \]
\item If $V_{\rm Hel}=[N\ S]$ is split into nuisance and retained secants, then
      the efficient retained Gram is exactly
      \[
       \boxed{
       G_{S\mid N}^{\rm Hel}
       =S^*(I-P_N)S
       =G_{SS}-G_{SN}G_{NN}^{\dagger}G_{NS}\succeq0,}
      \]
      where $P_N=N(N^*N)^\dagger N^*$.
\item Let $\theta\mapsto p_\theta$ be an independently physical $C^1$ family
      with $p_0=p_{\theta=0}$ and score
      $s_j=\partial_{\theta_j}\log p_\theta|_0$.  Then
      \[
       \boxed{
       \partial_{\theta_j}\mathfrak h(p_\theta)|_0
       =\sqrt{p_0}\,s_j,}
      \qquad
       \boxed{
       \left\langle\partial_i\mathfrak h,
       \partial_j\mathfrak h\right\rangle
       =\mathbb E_{p_0}[s_i\overline{s_j}].}
      \]
\item For a physical $C^2$ family $p_{\alpha,\beta}$ with nuisance score bank
      $N$ and retained score bank $S$, the profiled relative entropy
      \[
       \mathcal I_{\rm prof}(\beta)
       :=\inf_\alpha D(p_{\alpha,\beta}\Vert p_{0,0})
      \]
      has Hessian
      \[
       \boxed{
       D^2\mathcal I_{\rm prof}(0)
       =S^*(I-P_N)S.}
      \]
\end{enumerate}
Thus an actual shrinking family converts the canonical finite secant geometry
into the efficient Fisher action, while a finite secant by itself does not
select a tangent or generator.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The first identity is the direct expansion
\[
 4\sum_\omega(\sqrt{p(\omega)}-\sqrt{q(\omega)})^2
 =8-8\sum_\omega\sqrt{p(\omega)q(\omega)}.
\]
The second assertion is the orthogonal projection formula and the
Moore--Penrose identity for the Anderson--Trapp short.  Differentiating
$2\sqrt{p_\theta}$ gives
$\partial_j(2\sqrt p)=p^{-1/2}\partial_jp=\sqrt p\,s_j$, which proves the
third assertion.  Finally,
\[
 D(p_{\alpha,\beta}\Vert p_{0,0})
 =\frac12\left\|N\alpha+S\beta\right\|_{L^2(p_0)}^2
  +o(\|\alpha\|^2+\|\beta\|^2).
\]
Minimizing the quadratic term over $\alpha$ subtracts the orthogonal
projection onto $\Ran N$ and gives the displayed Schur short.
\end{proof}

\begin{countertheorem}[Finite endpoint laws do not determine a physical tangent]
\label{cth:GT-secant-no-tangent}
Two full-support $C^1$ paths can have the same initial and terminal laws and
different derivatives at the initial point.  Consequently no tangent, score,
or dynamical action is determined by two endpoint laws alone.
\end{countertheorem}

\begin{proof}
On the two-point space take $p_0=(1/2,1/2)$ and
$p_1=(1/2+\delta,1/2-\delta)$ with $0<\delta<1/4$.  The linear path
$p_t=p_0+t(p_1-p_0)$ and, for sufficiently small nonzero $\eta$, the path
\[
 q_t=p_t+\eta t(1-t)(1,-1)
\]
remain full support and have the same endpoints.  Their initial derivatives
differ by $\eta(1,-1)$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Protected-observable Riesz theorem]
\label{thm:GT-protected-Riesz}
Let $L\succeq0$ act on a finite-dimensional Hilbert space $H$, and let
$E:K\to H$ satisfy $\Ran E\subseteq\Ran L$.  Define
\[
 \boxed{\mathcal R_E(L):=E^*L^\dagger E\succeq0.}
