\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{
 \|E^*v\|^2
 \le \|\mathcal R_E(L)\|\,\langle v,Lv\rangle
 \qquad(v\perp\Ker L),}
\]
and the constant is optimal.  If $c$ is a unit eigenvector of
$\mathcal R_E(L)$ with eigenvalue $\lambda>0$, then
\[
 z=\lambda^{-1}L^\dagger Ec
\]
satisfies
\[
 \boxed{E^*z=c,\qquad \langle z,Lz\rangle=\lambda^{-1}.}
\]
Thus an unbounded influence sequence is equivalent to a unit protected output
whose action tends to zero.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Since $E=L^{1/2}L^{\dagger/2}E$,
\[
 \|E^*v\|^2
 =\|(L^{\dagger/2}E)^*L^{1/2}v\|^2
 \le\|E^*L^\dagger E\|\,\langle v,Lv\rangle.
\]
Taking $v=L^\dagger Ec$ for a top eigenvector gives equality after scaling.
The displayed identities for $z$ follow from
$E^*L^\dagger Ec=\lambda c$ and
$LL^\dagger E=E$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Exact tail elimination and influence preservation]
\label{thm:GT-effective-action}
Let $H=H_P\oplus H_Q$ and let
\[
 L=\begin{pmatrix}A&B\\B^*&C\end{pmatrix}\succeq0,
 \qquad C\succeq\gamma I\quad(\gamma>0).
\]
Define the effective head action
\[
 \boxed{S_P(L):=A-BC^{-1}B^*\succeq0.}
\]
Then for $p\in H_P$ and $q\in H_Q$,
\[
 \boxed{
 \left\langle\binom pq,L\binom pq\right\rangle
 =\langle p,S_P(L)p\rangle
 +\left\langle q+C^{-1}B^*p,
 C(q+C^{-1}B^*p)\right\rangle.}
\]
Consequently,
\[
 \inf_q\left\langle\binom pq,L\binom pq\right\rangle
 =\langle p,S_P(L)p\rangle,
\]
\[
 \boxed{
 \Ker L
 =\left\{\binom{p}{-C^{-1}B^*p}:p\in\Ker S_P(L)\right\}.}
\]
If $E:K\to H_P$ and $\Ran E\subseteq\Ran S_P(L)$, then, after embedding
$E$ into $H_P\oplus H_Q$,
\[
 \boxed{E^*L^\dagger E=E^*S_P(L)^\dagger E.}
\]
Thus every protected influence and every mixed influence innovation is exactly
preserved by physical tail elimination.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Expanding the square gives
\[
 \langle q,Cq\rangle+2\Re\langle p,Bq\rangle
 =\langle q+C^{-1}B^*p,C(q+C^{-1}B^*p)\rangle
  -\langle p,BC^{-1}B^*p\rangle,
\]
which proves the first assertions.  The kernel formula follows because both
nonnegative terms must vanish.  For a head source $Ec$, the minimum-energy
solution of $Lx=Ec$ has tail component $-C^{-1}B^*p$ and head equation
$S_P(L)p=Ec$.  Hence the minimum-energy representative is obtained by applying
$S_P(L)^\dagger$ on the head, and taking its source pairing gives the final
identity.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Certified approximate corrector]
\label{cor:GT-effective-corrector}
In the setting of \Cref{thm:GT-effective-action}, let $K:H_P\to H_Q$ be any
proposed tail corrector and put
\[
 \rho_K:=CK-B^*,
\]
\[
 \widetilde S_K
 :=A-BK-K^*B^*+K^*CK.
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{\widetilde S_K=S_P(L)+\rho_K^*C^{-1}\rho_K.}
\]
If $\widetilde S_K\succeq\delta I$ and $\|\rho_K\|\le\varepsilon$, then
\[
 \boxed{S_P(L)\succeq
 \left(\delta-\frac{\varepsilon^2}{\gamma}\right)I.}
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Write $K=C^{-1}B^*+C^{-1}\rho_K$ and expand.  The cross terms cancel, leaving
the exact positive error.  Since $C^{-1}\preceq\gamma^{-1}I$, the lower bound
follows.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Boundary-complete head--detail packet]
\label{def:GT-boundary-complete-packet}
Let $\mathcal H$ be a retained head, $\mathcal T$ a detail carrier, and
$\mathcal B$ a physical boundary space.  Let
\[
 L=\begin{pmatrix}A&B\\B^*&C\end{pmatrix}\succeq0
 \quad\text{on }\mathcal H\oplus\mathcal T,
 \qquad
 \mathcal D=(D_H\;D_T):\mathcal H\oplus\mathcal T\to\mathcal B,
 \tag{BC.1}
\]
with $C\succ0$ on the declared detail support.  Put
\[
 S=A-BC^{-1}B^*,\qquad
 E=D_H-D_TC^{-1}B^*,\qquad
 K=D_TC^{-1}D_T^*\succeq0.
 \tag{BC.2}
\]
The complete action is $G=L+\mathcal D^*\mathcal D$.  Its
boundary-complete head short is the positive form $G_{/\mathcal T}$ defined by
\[
 \langle x,G_{/\mathcal T}x\rangle
 =\inf_{y\in\mathcal T}\langle x\oplus y,G(x\oplus y)\rangle.
 \tag{BC.3}
\]
A kernel of $C$ is first retained in the exceptional screen and the definition
is applied on its supported complement.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Exact boundary-complete Schur formula]
\label{thm:GT-boundary-complete-short}
For the packet of \Cref{def:GT-boundary-complete-packet},
\[
 \boxed{G_{/\mathcal T}=S+E^*(I+K)^{-1}E.}
 \tag{BC.4}
\]
The minimizing detail correction is
\[
 \boxed{
 y_*(x)=-C^{-1}B^*x
 -(C+D_T^*D_T)^{-1}D_T^*Ex.}
 \tag{BC.5}
\]
The first term is the interior harmonic corrector; the second is the additional
boundary-relaxation corrector.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Write $y=-C^{-1}B^*x+u$.  Completion of the interior square gives
\[
 \langle x\oplus y,L(x\oplus y)\rangle
 =\langle x,Sx\rangle+\langle u,Cu\rangle,
\]
while the boundary value is $Ex+D_Tu$.  The remaining minimization is
\[
 \inf_u\bigl(\langle u,Cu\rangle+\|Ex+D_Tu\|^2\bigr).
\]
Its normal equation gives \textup{(BC.5)}.  Substitution yields
\[
 E^*\!
 \left[I-D_T(C+D_T^*D_T)^{-1}D_T^*\right]E.
\]
The Woodbury identity identifies the bracket with
$(I+D_TC^{-1}D_T^*)^{-1}=(I+K)^{-1}$, proving \textup{(BC.4)}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Boundary-relaxation dispersion]
\label{cor:GT-boundary-relaxation-dispersion}
Shorting the interior first and then evaluating the boundary only on the frozen
harmonic lift gives $G_{\rm naive}=S+E^*E$.  The exact discrepancy is
\[
 \boxed{
 G_{\rm naive}-G_{/\mathcal T}
 =E^*K(I+K)^{-1}E\succeq0.}
 \tag{BC.6}
\]
It vanishes exactly when $K^{1/2}E=0$.  If $C\succeq\gamma I$ and
$\|D_T\|\le d$, then
\[
 \boxed{
 S+\frac{1}{1+d^2/\gamma}E^*E
 \preceq G_{/\mathcal T}\preceq S+E^*E.}
 \tag{BC.7}
\]
In particular, every interior floor $S\succeq gI$ survives the
boundary-complete elimination unchanged.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Use $I-(I+K)^{-1}=K(I+K)^{-1}$.  The two positive factors commute by
functional calculus, proving \textup{(BC.6)} and its zero condition.  The
bounds on $C$ and $D_T$ give $0\preceq K\preceq(d^2/\gamma)I$; applying the
order-reversing function $x\mapsto(1+x)^{-1}$ and taking the congruence by $E$
gives \textup{(BC.7)}.
\end{proof}

\begin{countertheorem}[Short-then-attach has no uniform multiplicative control]
\label{cth:GT-boundary-short-order}
There is no universal constant bounding $G_{\rm naive}$ by a multiple of the
boundary-complete short.  In the scalar packet
$A=B=0$, $C=1$, $D_H=1$, $D_T=t$, one has
\[
 \boxed{G_{\rm naive}=1,\qquad G_{/\mathcal T}=(1+t^2)^{-1}.}
\]
Thus the ratio is unbounded.
\end{countertheorem}

\begin{proof}
Here $S=0$, $E=1$, and $K=t^2$; apply
\Cref{thm:GT-boundary-complete-short}.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Assembly before shorting and router dispersion]
\label{thm:GT-assembly-before-short}
For $i=1,\ldots,m$, let
\[
 G_i=\begin{pmatrix}A_i&B_i\\B_i^*&D_i\end{pmatrix}\succeq0,
 \qquad A_i\succ0,
\]
and put
\[
 K_i=A_i^{-1}B_i,
 \quad S_i=D_i-B_i^*A_i^{-1}B_i,
\]
\[
 A=\sum_iA_i,
 \quad B=\sum_iB_i,
 \quad K=A^{-1}B,
 \quad S=\sum_iD_i-B^*A^{-1}B.
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{
 S=\sum_iS_i+
 \sum_i(K_i-K)^*A_i(K_i-K).}
\]
Equivalently,
\[
 \boxed{
 \sum_iB_i^*A_i^{-1}B_i-B^*A^{-1}B
 =\sum_i(K_i-K)^*A_i(K_i-K)\succeq0.}
\]
Hence shorting after coherent assembly retains a positive router-dispersion
coordinate which is lost by separately shorting the local packets.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Since $B_i=A_iK_i$ and $B=AK$, expand
\[
 \sum_i(K_i-K)^*A_i(K_i-K)
 =\sum_iK_i^*A_iK_i-K^*AK,
\]
because the two cross sums equal $K^*AK$.  Substitute
$K_i^*A_iK_i=B_i^*A_i^{-1}B_i$ and
$K^*AK=B^*A^{-1}B$.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Protected-angle localizer]
\label{def:GT-protected-angle-localizer}
Let $P$ be an independently fixed predictor projection, put $Q=I-P$, and let
$t_0=Qt$, $p_0=Qp$.  For $0\le\eta\le1$, define
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathbb L_\eta(t,p\mid P)
 =\begin{pmatrix}
   \eta\|t_0\|^2&-\langle t_0,p_0\rangle\\
   -\langle p_0,t_0\rangle&\eta\|p_0\|^2
  \end{pmatrix}.}
 \tag{PA.1}
\]
If either residual vanishes, set the protected angle to zero; otherwise put
\[
 \rho(t,p\mid P)
 =\frac{|\langle t_0,p_0\rangle|}{\|t_0\|\,\|p_0\|}.
 \tag{PA.2}
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Exact protected-angle criterion]
\label{thm:GT-protected-angle}
For every packet of \Cref{def:GT-protected-angle-localizer},
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathbb L_\eta(t,p\mid P)\succeq0
 \iff \rho(t,p\mid P)\le\eta.}
 \tag{PA.3}
\]
If a readout has the exact form
$f=\mathfrak p+\langle t_0,p_0\rangle$ and
$|\mathfrak p|\le a$, then positivity of the localizer implies
\[
 \boxed{|f|\le a+\eta\|t_0\|\,\|p_0\|.}
 \tag{PA.4}
\]
A negative eigenvector of $\mathbb L_\eta$ is an explicit violating linear
combination of the residual total and phase sources.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The diagonal entries are nonnegative and the determinant is
$\eta^2\|t_0\|^2\|p_0\|^2-|\langle t_0,p_0\rangle|^2$.  Positivity of a
$2\times2$ Hermitian matrix is therefore equivalent to \textup{(PA.3)}.
Equation \textup{(PA.4)} follows by the triangle inequality.
\end{proof}

\begin{countertheorem}[Protected angle is not monotone under predictor enlargement]
\label{cth:GT-angle-predictor-nonmonotone}
Adding a predictor direction can either increase or decrease the residual
protected angle.  Consequently the predictor bank must be fixed by the
physical cylinder before the terminal readout is inspected.
\end{countertheorem}

\begin{proof}
In $\R^2$, take $t=e_1$, $p=e_2$.  With $P=0$ the angle is zero, whereas
projection onto $\Span(e_1-e_2)$ leaves both residuals equal to
$(e_1+e_2)/2$ and the angle becomes one.  In $\R^3$, take
$t=e_1+e_3$, $p=e_2+e_3$.  The initial angle is $1/2$, whereas projecting onto
$\Span(e_3)$ leaves the orthogonal vectors $e_1,e_2$ and the angle becomes
zero.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[Secants, tangents, and actions]
\label{fire:GT-secant-tangent-action}
A finite Hellinger Gram is a canonical comparison of actual laws.  A Fisher
matrix additionally requires a physical shrinking family.  A dynamical or
field action further requires a physical process, residual map, transfer, or
pressure whose derivative or Hessian is being used.  None of these stronger
objects may be manufactured by choosing an interpolation or by selecting a
positive operator with the desired kernel.
\end{firewall}

% =============================================================================

% =============================================================================
\subsection{Signed coherence, source-word Hodge decomposition, and inertia certificates}
\label{sec:signed-coherence-inertia}
% =============================================================================

\begin{definition}[Canonical coherent/counterflow split]
\label{def:GT-coherent-counterflow}
Let $\mu$ be a finite real signed measure, let
$T=|\mu|(X)$ and $S=\mu(X)$, and assume $T>0$.  Define
\[
 \mu_{\rm coh}=\frac ST|\mu|,
 \qquad
 \mu_{\rm cf}=\mu-\mu_{\rm coh},
 \qquad
 \kappa_{\rm cf}=\frac{T^2-S^2}{2T}.
 \tag{SC.1}
\]
If $\kappa_{\rm cf}>0$, let $P^\pm$ be the normalized Jordan parts of
$\mu_{\rm cf}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Orthogonal signed-coherence decomposition]
\label{thm:GT-coherent-counterflow}
The split \textup{(SC.1)} is the orthogonal projection of
$d\mu/d|\mu|$ onto the constant functions in $L^2(|\mu|)$.  It satisfies
\[
 \boxed{\mu_{\rm cf}=\kappa_{\rm cf}(P^+-P^-),}
 \qquad
 \boxed{
 \left\|\frac{d\mu}{d|\mu|}-\frac ST\right\|_{L^2(|\mu|)}^2
 =2\kappa_{\rm cf}.}
 \tag{SC.2}
\]
For every real observable $f$, with
$f^0=T^{-1}\int f\,d|\mu|$ and
$f^\pm=\int f\,dP^\pm$,
\[
 \boxed{
 \int f\,d\mu=Sf^0+\kappa_{\rm cf}(f^+-f^-).}
 \tag{SC.3}
\]
Thus total variation, coherent resultant, and counterflow are retained as
separate physical coordinates.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The sign density has squared norm $T$ and mean $S/T$.  Orthogonal projection
onto constants gives $\mu_{\rm coh}$.  The residual has total mass zero; direct
Jordan decomposition gives equal positive and negative masses
$(T^2-S^2)/(2T)$.  Pairing with $f$ proves \textup{(SC.3)}.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Six-term source-word--transport--Hodge identity]
\label{thm:GT-source-word-Hodge}
Let $W_r$ be the actual degree-$r$ source-word synthesis.  Let
$P_r^{\rm alg}$ project onto the word carrier predicted by a proposed
lower-grade compiler, let $P_R$ be conditional expectation onto an actual
physical record, and let $P_{\rm tr}$ project the record-visible source onto an
independently loaded transport-source carrier.  On the transported component,
let $d_U$ be the physical covariant derivative, $L_U=d_U^*d_U$, and let
$\beta_U$ be the physical boundary-flux Read.  Then the complete word Gram has
the exact decomposition
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathbb K_r
 =\mathbb I_{\rm alg}^{(r)}
 +\mathbb I_{\rm hid}^{(r)}
 +\mathbb I_{\rm tr}^{(r)}
 +G_{\rm dem}^{(r)}
 +G_{\rm open}^{(r)}
 +G_{\rm cyc}^{(r)}.}
 \tag{SC.4}
\]
The terms are respectively the missing word source, the source hidden inside
record fibres, the record-visible source absent from the transport carrier,
the minimum covariant demand action, the minimum open-boundary current, and
the internal boundary-free cycle current.  A finite domination constant by
the physical action exists exactly when the kernel of the last three terms is
contained in the kernel of the first three; the sharp constant is the largest
generalized eigenvalue of this pair.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Apply three successive orthogonal projections to $W_r$: first onto the proposed
word carrier, then onto the physical record, and then onto the transport
carrier.  On the last range, the covariant Hodge projection
$d_UL_U^\dagger d_U^*$ separates the minimum demand current from
$\ker d_U^*$; the Moore--Penrose short by $\beta_U$ separates the minimum open
current from the boundary-free cycle current.  Taking Grams gives
\textup{(SC.4)}.  The domination statement is the finite generalized Riesz
criterion.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Mean return connection and local coherence loss]
\label{thm:GT-return-coherence-loss}
Let a hidden excursion on an oriented edge carry a random isometry $U_e$ and
let $C_e=\mathbb E(U_e\mid e)$.  Then, for endpoint vectors $x_i,x_j$,
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathbb E\|x_j-U_ex_i\|^2
 =\|x_j-C_ex_i\|^2
 +\langle x_i,(I-C_e^*C_e)x_i\rangle.}
 \tag{SC.5}
\]
Moreover
\[
 \boxed{I-C_e^*C_e
 =\mathbb E[(U_e-C_e)^*(U_e-C_e)]\succeq0.}
 \tag{SC.6}
\]
The first term is deterministic connection mismatch and the second is local
coherence loss.  In the scalar phase case the latter is
$(1-|c_e|^2)|x_i|^2$; cycle products of the deterministic phases retain the
projectively flat or nonflat holonomy.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Expand the square and use $\mathbb E U_e=C_e$ and $U_e^*U_e=I$.  The variance
identity follows by expanding the right side of \textup{(SC.6)}.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Rank--trace certificate for an indefinite compression]
\label{thm:GT-rank-trace-indefinite}
Let $P,Q$ be Hermitian matrices with $P\succeq0$, $\rank P\le r$, and
$n_+(Q)\le b$.  For every $c>0$,
\[
 \boxed{
 \|P+Q\|_{\rm F}^2
 \ge c\Tr P-\frac{c^2}{4}r+2c\Tr Q-c^2b.}
 \tag{SC.7}
\]
In particular,
\[
 \boxed{r\ge2\Tr P+4\Tr Q-4b-\|P+Q\|_{\rm F}^2.}
 \tag{SC.8}
\]
The inertia and this bound are invariant under invertible congruence, but they
do not determine the protected cross orientation.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Write $Q=Q_+-Q_-$, use von Neumann's trace inequality to bound
$\Tr(PQ_-)$ by the ordered eigenvalue pairing, apply
$x^2\ge cx-c^2/4$ to the rank-$r$ positive eigenvalues, and
$q^2\ge2cq-c^2$ to the at most $b$ positive eigenvalues of $Q$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Signed Feshbach inertia]
\label{thm:GT-signed-Haynsworth}
Let
\[
 H=\begin{pmatrix}A&B\\B^*&D\end{pmatrix}=H^*,
 \qquad \Ran B^*\subseteq\Ran D.
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{
 \operatorname{In}(H)
 =\operatorname{In}(A-BD^\dagger B^*)+
   \operatorname{In}(D),}
 \tag{SC.9}
\]
where $\operatorname{In}$ denotes the positive, negative, and null indices.
Thus nuisance or tail elimination preserves the complete signed index only
when the mixed block is assembled before the short.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The congruence by
$\begin{psmallmatrix}I&-BD^\dagger\\0&I\end{psmallmatrix}$
block-diagonalizes $H$ under the range condition.  Sylvester inertia is
invariant under invertible congruence.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[Action and inertia do not select orientation]
\label{fire:GT-action-inertia-not-selection}
A positive holonomy or resistance action prices a nonflat component only after
source incidence has been proved.  It does not choose a value without an
independent Euler, continuity, stationarity, boundary, or intervention law,
and it vanishes on flat coherent modes.  Likewise inertia and trace moments
bound populations or threshold indices but do not determine a canonical
residual subspace or a signed cross phase.  Coercive, inertial, and causal
certificates are retained in parallel.
\end{firewall}

\subsection{Augmentation, character sectors, and open currents}
\label{sec:augmentation-character-current}
% =============================================================================

\begin{theorem}[Mean-ergodic fixed/coboundary decomposition]
\label{thm:GT-fixed-coboundary}
Let $T$ be a contraction on a Hilbert space $H$, and let $P_0$ be the
orthogonal projection onto $\Ker(I-T)$.  Then
\[
 \boxed{H=\Ker(I-T)\oplus\overline{\Ran(I-T)},}
\]
and the Ces\`aro means
$M_N(T)=N^{-1}\sum_{n=0}^{N-1}T^n$ converge strongly to $P_0$.  For every
finite source synthesis $Z:K\to H$,
\[
 \boxed{
 Z^*P_0Z
 =\lim_{N\to\infty}Z^*M_N(T)^*M_N(T)Z,}
\]
\[
 \boxed{
 \Tr(Z^*P_0Z)
 =\inf_G\|Z-(I-T)G\|_{\HS}^2.}
\]
If $A:E\to H$ obeys $T^*A=A$, then
\[
 \boxed{A^*Z=A^*P_0Z,}
\]
and
\[
 \boxed{
 (A^*Z)^*(A^*A)^\dagger(A^*Z)
 \preceq Z^*P_0Z.}
\]
Thus a retained source couples to a fixed accepted source only through its
zero-mode component; an exact coboundary has zero router even when no
nontrivial point character exists.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
For a contraction, $\Ker(I-T)=\Ker(I-T^*)$, and
$\overline{\Ran(I-T)}=\Ker(I-T^*)^\perp$.  The mean ergodic theorem gives the
strong limit.  The squared distance from $Z$ to
$\overline{\Ran(I-T)}$ is the squared norm of $P_0Z$, which proves the
variational identity.  The columns of $A$ lie in $\Ker(I-T^*)=\Ker(I-T)$, so
$A^*=A^*P_0$.  Finally
$A(A^*A)^\dagger A^*$ is the projection $P_A$ onto $\Ran A$, and
$P_A\preceq P_0$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Character projection commutes with invariant shorting]
\label{thm:GT-character-short}
Let a finite abelian group $G$ act unitarily on $H$.  Let $L\succeq0$ commute
with this action and let the nuisance range $\Ran N$ be $G$-invariant.  For
$\chi\in\widehat G$, put
\[
 P_\chi=\frac1{|G|}\sum_{g\in G}\overline{\chi(g)}U(g).
\]
Then $L^\dagger$, $P_{\Ran N}$, and the nuisance-shorted action commute with
every $P_\chi$.  Consequently every action-dressed or nuisance-shorted mixed
Gram is block diagonal by character.  In particular, if $A$ is a
trivial-character source and $Z$ is a nontrivial-character source, then
\[
 \boxed{A^*L^\dagger Z=0}
\]
whenever the two source ranges lie in $\Ran L$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Functional calculus for the commuting pair $(L,U(g))$ gives commutation of
$L^\dagger$ with every $P_\chi$.  Invariance of $\Ran N$ makes its orthogonal
projection commute with the action.  Distinct character subspaces are
orthogonal and remain so after applying every commuting positive operator.
\end{proof}

\begin{countertheorem}[A noninvariant nuisance can manufacture cross-character coupling]
\label{cth:GT-character-nuisance}
Character orthogonality need not survive shorting by a noninvariant nuisance
range.
\end{countertheorem}

\begin{proof}
On $\C^2$ let $U=\diag(1,-1)$, let $s_+=e_1$, $s_-=e_2$, and short by
$n=(e_1+e_2)/\sqrt2$.  Although $\langle s_+,s_-\rangle=0$,
\[
 \left\langle(I-P_n)s_+,(I-P_n)s_-\right\rangle=-\frac12.
\]
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Open path boundary]
\label{def:GT-open-path-boundary}
For edge currents $j=(j_0,\ldots,j_{N-1})$ on the oriented path
$0\to1\to\cdots\to N$, define
\[
 (\partial_Nj)_0=-j_0,
 \qquad
 (\partial_Nj)_k=j_{k-1}-j_k\ (1\le k<N),
 \qquad
 (\partial_Nj)_N=j_{N-1}.
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Exact open-path Thomson and Wasserstein compiler]
\label{thm:GT-open-current}
Let $s=(s_0,\ldots,s_N)$ and let
$A=\diag(a_0,\ldots,a_{N-1})$ with $a_k>0$.  The equation
$\partial_Nj=s$ is solvable exactly when $\sum_{k=0}^Ns_k=0$, and on that
branch the current is unique:
\[
 \boxed{j_k=-\sum_{r=0}^ks_r.}
\]
Writing $L_N=\partial_NA^{-1}\partial_N^*$, one has
\[
 \boxed{
 \inf_{\partial_Nj=s}\langle j,Aj\rangle
 =\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}a_k\left|\sum_{r=0}^ks_r\right|^2
 =\langle s,L_N^\dagger s\rangle.}
\]
For real $s$ and unit edge lengths,
\[
 \boxed{
 \sum_{k=0}^{N-1}\left|\sum_{r=0}^ks_r\right|
 =\sup_{|\phi_{k+1}-\phi_k|\le1}\sum_{k=0}^N\phi_ks_k,}
\]
the discrete $W_1$ transport cost between the positive and negative parts of
$s$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Summing the boundary equation gives the necessary zero-mass condition.
Solving successively from the left endpoint gives the displayed current and
proves uniqueness.  The variational identity is the finite Thomson principle:
the Lagrange multiplier equation gives
$j=A^{-1}\partial_N^*L_N^\dagger s$.  Direct substitution gives the cumulative
sum formula.  For the last identity, summation by parts gives
\[
 \sum_{k=0}^N\phi_ks_k
 =-\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}(\phi_{k+1}-\phi_k)j_k,
\]
and the supremum is attained by choosing each increment with sign opposite to
$j_k$.
\end{proof}

\begin{countertheorem}[Artificial periodic closure can erase an open-boundary cost]
\label{cth:GT-periodicization}
For the source $s=-\delta_0+\delta_N$ with unit edge weights, the open-path
energy is $N$.  If one adjoins an artificial closing edge of unit weight, the
minimum cycle energy is $N/(N+1)$.  Hence periodic closure can reduce a
physical boundary cost by the unbounded factor $N+1$.
\end{countertheorem}

\begin{proof}
On the path the unique current equals one on all $N$ edges.  On the cycle the
two routes from $0$ to $N$ have resistances $N$ and $1$ in parallel, whose
effective resistance is $N/(N+1)$.
\end{proof}


\begin{theorem}[Exact common-core loading transfer]
\label{thm:core-loading-transfer}
Let $D_X\succeq0$ on $\mathcal U_X^{(1)}$ and
$E_{\alpha,X}\succeq0$ on $\mathcal P_{\alpha,X}$.  If
\[
 G_X\succeq g_XD_X,
 \qquad
 B_{\alpha,X}^*D_XB_{\alpha,X}\succeq b_{\alpha,X}E_{\alpha,X},
\]
then
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathbb T_{\alpha\alpha,X}^{\BR}
 \succeq g_Xb_{\alpha,X}E_{\alpha,X}.}
\]
Moreover,
\[
 \Ker B_{\alpha,X}\subseteq\Ker\mathbb T_{\alpha\alpha,X}^{\BR},
 \qquad
 0\preceq\mathbb T_{\alpha\alpha,X}^{\BR}
 \preceq\norm{G_X}_{\op}B_{\alpha,X}^*B_{\alpha,X}.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Conjugate the first lower bound by $B_{\alpha,X}$ and apply the second.  The
upper bound follows from $G_X\preceq\norm{G_X}_{\op}I$; the kernel inclusion
is immediate.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[Cross-sector coherence does not repair a missing loading]
A strong common-core estimate transfers to a sector only through a
sector-specific loading estimate.  Off-diagonal blocks cannot make a diagonal
quadratic form positive on a vector annihilated by its own loading map.
\end{firewall}

\begin{definition}[Prefix-exact cutoff morphism]
\label{def:prefix-exact-cutoff}
For $X\le Y$, a prefix-exact cutoff morphism consists of isometries
$J_{XY,k}$ between every old physical prefix Choi space such that
\[
 \boxed{R_X^{(k)}=J_{XY,k}^*R_Y^{(k)}J_{XY,k}}
\]
for every old prefix, together with exact compression of old physical CP-frame
branches, discards, and Reads, and a compatible injection of the minimal record
algebras.  Pure horizon extension is the special case $J_{XY,k}=I$ on old
prefixes.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Canonical cutoff support, absorbing histories, and quotient transport]
\label{thm:cutoff-compatibility}
Let $X\le Y$ be prefix exact.  Put
$E_{X,k}=\supp R_X^{(k)}$ and $A_{X,k}=\overline{E_{X,k}}$.  Then:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(C\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item there is a unique support isometry
      \[
       \boxed{
       W_{XY,k}(R_X^{(k)})^{1/2}
       =(R_Y^{(k)})^{1/2}J_{XY,k},}
      \]
      and for $X\le Y\le Z$ these maps are strictly transitive;
\item with $C_{XY,k}=\overline{W_{XY,k}}$, the canonical sequential
      isometries satisfy
      \[
       \boxed{
       (j_{XY,k}^{\rm out}\otimes C_{XY,k})V_{X,k}
       =V_{Y,k}(j_{XY,k}^{\rm in}\otimes C_{XY,k-1});}
      \]
      conversely these intertwinings imply prefix exactness;
\item on Hilbert--Schmidt memory space define
      $\Gamma_{XY,\xi}(a)=C_{XY,\xi}aC_{XY,\xi}^*$ and
      $\Pi_{XY,\xi}=\Gamma_{XY,\xi}\Gamma_{XY,\xi}^*$.  Inserting
      $\Pi_{XY}$ after every old letter gives an absorbing representation
      satisfying, for every old $*$-word $w:\xi\to\eta$,
      \[
       \boxed{
       \widehat\rho_{Y\mid X}(w)
       =\Gamma_{XY,\eta}\rho_X(w)\Gamma_{XY,\xi}^*.}
      \]
      Hence the absorbing corner is canonically $*$-isomorphic to
      $\mathcal A_X^{\rm proc}$;
\item the support-completed algebras
      \[
       \widetilde{\mathcal A}_X^{\rm cut}
       :=C^*(\Gamma_{ZX}\mathcal A_Z^{\rm proc}\Gamma_{ZX}^*:Z\le X)
      \]
      form a strict directed system under $b\mapsto\Gamma_{XY}b\Gamma_{XY}^*$;
\item the absorbing projections can be omitted for the full refined letters
      exactly when every primitive inflow defect
      \[
       \boxed{
       \Delta_{XY}^{\rm in}(a)
       :=\|(I-\Pi_{XY,\xi})
       T_{Y,j(a)}^{*_{\rm HS}}\Pi_{XY,\eta}\|_{\HS}^2}
      \]
      vanishes and the full refined letters satisfy one finite flat presentation
      of the old process algebra.  Under these conditions the resulting
      full-letter map is injective;
\item let $\mathscr C_X\subseteq(\mathcal A_X^{\rm proc})^*$ be the span of
      all old contextual functionals.  For an injective raw cutoff map
      $\alpha$, a map of contextual quotients exists exactly when
      $\alpha^*\mathscr C_Y\subseteq\mathscr C_X$ and is injective exactly when
      equality holds.  If $F_{Y\mid X}$ is a row map of restricted new
      contextual coordinates and $P_X^{\rm ctx}$ projects onto
      $\mathscr C_X$, the positive innovation Gram
      \[
       \boxed{
       \mathbb G_{Y\mid X}^{\rm ctx}
       =F_{Y\mid X}(I-P_X^{\rm ctx})F_{Y\mid X}^*}
      \]
      vanishes exactly when the separated quotient commutes with cutoff descent;
\item for every injective separated-history map there is a unique positive
      invertible central density $h_{XY}\in Z(\mathcal A_X^{\rm hist})$ such
      that
      \[
       \boxed{
       \widehat\tau_Y(\iota_{XY}(a))
       =\widehat\tau_X(h_{XY}a),
       \qquad
       (I_{XY}^{(r)})^*\mathbb K_{Y,r}I_{XY}^{(r)}
       =\mathbb K_{X,r}^{h_{XY}}.}
      \]
      Exact regular-trace isometry is the special case $h_{XY}=I$;
\item an independently verified isometric physical future metric gives exact
      physical Gram compression.
\end{enumerate}
Thus prefix-exact finite processes always have a strict absorbing-corner
history functor.  Uncornered full-letter nesting, contextual-quotient nesting,
and trace isometry are stronger properties with separate finite certificates.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Put $K=(R_Y^{(k)})^{1/2}J_{XY,k}$.  Prefix exactness gives
$K^*K=R_X^{(k)}$.  The polar decomposition therefore has the unique form
$K=W_{XY,k}(R_X^{(k)})^{1/2}$ with initial space $E_{X,k}$, proving
\textup{(C1)}.  For three cutoffs, both $W_{XZ,k}$ and
$W_{YZ,k}W_{XY,k}$ have the same product with $(R_X^{(k)})^{1/2}$, whose
range is $E_{X,k}$, proving strict transitivity.

Vectorization of the polar identity identifies the compressed $Y$ square-root
purification with the $X$ purification followed by $C_{XY,k}$.  Minimal
purification uniqueness gives the sequential intertwining in \textup{(C2)}.
Conversely, linking those intertwining isometries and tracing the final memory
compresses every prefix comb exactly.

The branch intertwinings give
$T_{Y,j(a)}\Gamma_{XY,\xi}=\Gamma_{XY,\eta}T_{X,a}$; taking Hilbert--Schmidt
adjoints gives the corresponding absorbing identity for formal reverses.
Induction on word length, using $\Gamma^*\Gamma=I$, proves the word formula in
\textup{(C3)} and equality of the representation kernels.  The quotient
universal property gives the $*$-isomorphism.  Strict transitivity of
$\Gamma$ carries each predecessor corner at $X$ to the corresponding
predecessor corner at $Y$, proving \textup{(C4)}.

Forward invariance is already supplied by prefix exactness.  The inflow defect
vanishes exactly when the old source and target ranges also co-reduce the
refined adjoint, equivalently when
$\Pi_\eta T_Y=T_Y\Pi_\xi$.  Then intermediate absorbing projections commute
through every letter and can be removed.  A homomorphism from the old quotient
exists exactly when a finite flat rewriting list for its relation ideal
vanishes on the full refined letters.  Its reducing old corner remains a
faithful copy, so the descended map is injective.  This proves \textup{(C5)}.

The contextual ideal is $\mathscr C_X^\perp$.  Therefore
$\alpha^{-1}(\mathcal N_Y^{\rm fut})
=(\alpha^*\mathscr C_Y)^\perp$.  Ideal descent is equivalent to
$\alpha^*\mathscr C_Y\subseteq\mathscr C_X$, and equality is equivalent to
reflection and injectivity.  The innovation Gram is the Gram of the component
of the restricted new contexts orthogonal to the old span, so it vanishes
exactly on equality.  This proves \textup{(C6)}.

The pullback of the target normalized regular trace is a faithful trace on the
finite source algebra.  On each simple central block it is a positive scalar
multiple of the source regular trace; collecting those scalars gives the
unique positive central density and the word-Gram identity.  A physical
isometry intertwines word synthesis directly, proving the final item.
\end{proof}

\section{Optional Store--score interferometric realization}
\label{sec:canonical-history-compiler}
% =============================================================================

The following packet is retained because it gives a concrete coherent
realization of selected histories and is used in later spacetime loadings.  It
is no longer an assumption for \Cref{thm:grand-emergence}.

\begin{assumption}[Optional coherent Store--score realization packet]
\label{ass:minimal-store-score-entrance}
Conditional on a selected protected record sector, suppose:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(C\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item a finite Store carrier has a Hermitian involution $Z_{\rm c}$ and raw
      Hermitian generator $L$;
\item one fresh coherent score sign $\C^2_\epsilon$ has its sign involution,
      coherent swap, scalar phase control, and one resolved sign Read;
\item the pointer--score pulse supplies
      $\exp(-i\theta Z_\epsilon\otimes Z_{\rm c})$ through finite pulse
      repetition, with physical inverse pulses or an equivalent sign reversal;
\item the selected reversible target block has the stated local controls and
      contains a nontrivial projection seen by the score path.
\end{enumerate}
No common unitary extension, complete environment-label list, absence of
residual ideals, or predetermined irreversible-path coherence is assumed.
Those structures are respectively derived by
\Cref{thm:common-CP-completion,lem:contextual-null-ideal,thm:central-source-decomposition}
or supplied as measured realization panels.
\end{assumption}

Write the retained action register as
\[
 \mathcal R_{\rm act}\cong\C^2_\epsilon\otimes\mathcal R_{\rm sh},
 \qquad
 |\Omega_{\rm act}\rangle=|+\rangle_\epsilon\otimes|\Omega_{\rm sh}\rangle.
\]

\begin{theorem}[The sourced score pulse derives local control and exact controlled-$Z$]
\label{thm:canonical-score-control}
Under \Cref{ass:minimal-store-score-entrance}, every
$\exp(-i\theta Z_\epsilon\otimes Z_{\rm c})$ is physical, local phases follow
by branch kickback, and
\[
 \boxed{
 \operatorname{CZ}_{\epsilon,{\rm c}}
 =e^{-i\pi/4}e^{i\pi Z_\epsilon/4}e^{i\pi Z_{\rm c}/4}
  e^{-i\pi Z_\epsilon Z_{\rm c}/4}.}
\]
If the nonzero Store support decomposes into distinct anticommuting frequencies
$L=\sum_j\mu_jJ_j$, the dynamical Lie algebra generated by $L$ and
$-iZ_{\rm c}$ contains $\bigoplus_j\mathfrak{su}(2)_j$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Commuting repetitions of a sufficiently small sourced pulse add their angles.
Preparing either factor in an eigenbranch gives the local phase on the other,
and evaluation on the four joint eigenvalues proves the controlled-$Z$
identity.  On the $j$th frequency block,
$-\frac14\operatorname{ad}_L^2(-iZ_{\rm c})=\mu_j^2(-iZ_{\rm c})$.
Lagrange interpolation in the distinct $\mu_j^2$ isolates each block; its
commutator with $L$ gives a second Pauli axis and one more commutator gives the
third.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[A fresh score sign gives a deterministic two-clock entangler]
\label{lem:score-bus-entangler}
For two Store clocks $A,B$, prepare a fresh score sign $Q$ in $|+\rangle$,
apply $\operatorname{CZ}_{Q,A}\operatorname{CZ}_{Q,B}$, and resolve
\[
 |y_m\rangle=\frac{|0\rangle+im|1\rangle}{\sqrt2}.
\]
The induced Kraus operator is
\[
 K_m=\frac12(I-imZ_AZ_B)
 =\frac1{\sqrt2}e^{-im\pi Z_AZ_B/4},
\]
so each result has probability $1/2$.  With the available branch correction,
both outcomes implement
\[
 \boxed{E_{AB}=e^{-i\pi Z_AZ_B/4}.}
\]
The marginal score distribution is target independent.  If the outcome is
retained as a protected mark, however, the conditional output remains a
unitary branch and is not a target reset.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Contract
$2^{-1/2}(|0\rangle\otimes\psi+|1\rangle\otimes Z_AZ_B\psi)$ with
$\langle y_m|$.  Since $(Z_AZ_B)^2=I$, $K_m^*K_m=I/2$.  The two unitary
factors are inverse and the branch correction identifies them.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Canonical full-matrix target control]
\label{cor:canonical-full-matrix-control}
Local clock control and $E_{AB}$ generate $\mathfrak{su}(4)$ on two clocks.
More generally, a resolved simple full-matrix target carrying the analogous
local and entangling controls has its full connected unitary group.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Conjugating a local Pauli by $E_{AB}$ produces a two-body axis.  Commutators
with the six local Pauli axes generate all nine two-body axes, which together
with the local six form a basis of $\mathfrak{su}(4)$.  The simple-block case
is the same Lie-ideal argument.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Canonical controlled-history compiler]
\label{thm:canonical-history-compiler}
Let $M_d(\C)$ be a resolved reversible target and let $P$ be a nontrivial
projection seen by the score path.  Then the joint Lie algebra contains
\[
 iZ_\epsilon\otimes\mathfrak{su}(d),
 \qquad
 ip_1^\epsilon\otimes\mathfrak{su}(d),
 \qquad p_1^\epsilon=\frac12(I-Z_\epsilon).
\]
Every reversible primitive unitary therefore has an exact one-sided controlled
lift, and controlled reversible letters multiply to controlled words.  A
finite irreversible alphabet has the derived mathematical completion of
\Cref{thm:common-CP-completion}; its path and control labels remain explicit.
A laboratory comparison that erases two such path labels coherently is an
additional realization panel, not part of structural emergence.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The traceless part of $P$ is nonzero.  The smallest Lie ideal of the simple
algebra $\mathfrak{su}(d)$ containing it is all of $\mathfrak{su}(d)$.
Commutators with local target axes therefore produce
$iZ_\epsilon\otimes\mathfrak{su}(d)$; combining this with
$iI\otimes\mathfrak{su}(d)$ gives the one-sided projector algebra.
Exponentiation and a path-local central phase produce every controlled
unitary.  The irreversible completion is
\Cref{thm:common-CP-completion}; it does not erase its derived labels.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Exact canonical writer]
\label{thm:canonical-writer}
Let $P=P^*=P^2$, $Q=I-P$, and suppose $I-2P$ belongs to the reversible target
group.  Put
\[
 \boxed{U_P=I_{\rm w}\otimes Q+X_{\rm w}\otimes P.}
\]
Then $U_P^*=U_P$, $U_P^2=I$, it writes the projection nondestructively, and
\[
 \boxed{
 U_P(Z_{\rm w}\otimes I)U_P^*
 =Z_{\rm w}\otimes(I-2P).}
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Use $PQ=0$, $P+Q=I$, $X_{\rm w}^2=I$, and
$X_{\rm w}Z_{\rm w}X_{\rm w}=-Z_{\rm w}$.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Two phase settings reconstruct a measured ordered kernel]
\label{cor:canonical-two-phase-history}
If a physical score path prepares the calibrated amplitudes
$\frac12(A+zB)$ for $z\in\{1,i\}$, with known marginal Grams, then
\[
 \boxed{
 A^*B=\frac12\bigl[(G_1-D)-i(G_i-D)\bigr],}
 \qquad
 D=A^*A+B^*B,
 \quad G_z=(A+zB)^*(A+zB).
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Expand the two Grams and solve the resulting real-linear equations for $A^*B$.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Positive two-history block factorization]
\label{lem:coherence-factorization}
For $A,B\succeq0$,
\[
 \begin{pmatrix}A&X\\X^*&B\end{pmatrix}\succeq0
 \iff
 \boxed{X=A^{1/2}CB^{1/2}}
\]
for a contraction $C$ between the support spaces.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
On the supports, the Schur complement gives
$A-XB^{-1}X^*\succeq0$, so
$C=A^{-1/2}XB^{-1/2}$ is a contraction.  Conversely,
\[
 \begin{pmatrix}A&X\\X^*&B\end{pmatrix}
 =\begin{pmatrix}A^{1/2}&0\\0&B^{1/2}\end{pmatrix}
  \begin{pmatrix}I&C\\C^*&I\end{pmatrix}
  \begin{pmatrix}A^{1/2}&0\\0&B^{1/2}\end{pmatrix},
\]
and the middle block is positive exactly when $\norm C\le1$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Complete parameterization of physical two-history coherence]
\label{thm:coherence-parameterization}
For two CP histories with Choi operators $J_0,J_1$, every positive controlled
completion has off-diagonal Choi block
\[
 \boxed{X=J_0^{1/2}CJ_1^{1/2},\qquad\norm C\le1,}
\]
and every such contraction gives a positive completion.  The diagonal
histories determine the supports and magnitude bounds, but not $C$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Apply \Cref{lem:coherence-factorization} to the controlled block Choi matrix.
\end{proof}

\begin{countertheorem}[Diagonal histories do not identify a fringe]
\label{cth:coherence-no-go}
No rule derived only from two diagonal CP branches identifies the physical
off-diagonal coherence of every realization.
\end{countertheorem}

\begin{proof}
For one-dimensional input and output, take both diagonal Choi operators equal
to one.  Every $c\in\C$ with $|c|\le1$ makes
$\begin{psmallmatrix}1&c\\\bar c&1\end{psmallmatrix}$ positive.  Thus
$c=0$, $c=1$, and $c=e^{i\theta}$ have the same diagonal process data and
different fringes.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[Exact scope of the Store--score compiler]
\label{fire:canonical-compiler-scope}
The Store--score packet gives a concrete controlled realization of selected
reversible words and, when calibrated fringes are actually measured, their
physical ordered kernels.  It is not needed for the existence, positivity,
flatness, or monoidal reconstruction of the structural Grand Tensor.  A
measured contraction panel may be inserted; it must not be inferred from the
diagonal histories.  Protected path labels remain protected until a causal
future-nullity theorem permits their discard.
\end{firewall}

\section{Source-native renewal, scheduler identifiability, and the primitive lift}
\label{sec:autonomous-store-renewal}
% =============================================================================

The structural tensor requires no reset.  A recurrent physical realization is
a stronger statement and must distinguish an unmarked coarse channel from a
resolved event instrument.

\begin{countertheorem}[An unmarked process does not identify a scheduler instrument]
\label{cth:store-scheduler-no-go}
Let a hidden finite instrument $\{\Phi_a\}_{a\in\mathscr A}$ have coarse
channel $\Phi=\sum_a\Phi_a$.  After the outcomes $a$ are discarded, complete
multitime process tomography with arbitrary visible interventions depends only
on $\Phi$, not on the decomposition.  In particular, one and the same exact
reset channel admits hidden renewal boundaries with any geometric hazard
$\lambda\in[0,1]$.
\end{countertheorem}

\begin{proof}
For visible interventions $\mathcal I_0,\ldots,\mathcal I_k$, summing the
hidden outcomes gives
\[
 \sum_{a_1,\ldots,a_k}
 \mathcal I_k\Phi_{a_k}\mathcal I_{k-1}\cdots
 \Phi_{a_1}\mathcal I_0
 =\mathcal I_k\Phi\mathcal I_{k-1}\cdots\Phi\mathcal I_0
\]
by multilinearity.  Hence every hidden CP refinement of $\Phi$ has the same
unmarked process tensor.  For the reset
$\mathcal R_*(\rho)=\Tr(\rho)\omega$, put
$\mathcal B_{\lambda,*}=\lambda\mathcal R_*$ and
$\mathcal C_{\lambda,*}=(1-\lambda)\mathcal R_*$.  Their sum is always
$\mathcal R_*$, while the hidden first-return maps are
$\lambda(1-\lambda)^{n-1}\mathcal R_*$.  Thus the same unmarked table realizes
immediate, rare, or absent hidden renewal.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Passive marked renewal interface]
A passive renewal mark is a finite outcome alphabet
$\{\varnothing\}\sqcup\mathscr M$ written at each primitive tick, where
$\varnothing$ means no completed boundary and $m\in\mathscr M$ means that a
boundary completed with mark $m$.  Reading or discarding the mark does not
trigger or modify the event, and discarding it recovers the original coarse
process.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Marked first-return reconstruction]
\label{thm:marked-first-return}
Complete branch-conditioned tomography of a passive marked interface uniquely
reconstructs, for every $n\ge1$ and $m\in\mathscr M$, the first-return CP map
\[
 \boxed{\mathcal F_{n,m,*}
 :=\Phi_{m,*}\Phi_{\varnothing,*}^{\,n-1}}
\]
when the primitive marked instrument is stationary, and more generally the CP
map associated with the resolved word $\varnothing^{n-1}m$.  The no-return
word through horizon $N$ gives a survivor map $\mathcal S_{N,*}$.  These maps
form a valid first-return instrument exactly when their Choi operators are
positive and
\[
 \boxed{
 \sum_{n=1}^{N}\sum_m\mathcal F_{n,m,*}^{*}(I)
 +\mathcal S_{N,*}^{*}(I)=I.}
\]
If $\mathcal U_n$ is the unrestricted boundary-to-boundary map of length $n$
and $\mathcal F_n=\sum_m\mathcal F_{n,m}$, then
\[
 \boxed{\mathcal U_n=\sum_{k=1}^{n}\mathcal U_{n-k}\circ\mathcal F_k,
 \qquad
 \mathcal F_n=\mathcal U_n-
 \sum_{k=1}^{n-1}\mathcal U_{n-k}\circ\mathcal F_k.}
\]
Equivalently, for formal series,
$\mathcal U(z)=I+\mathcal U(z)\mathcal F(z)$ and
$\mathcal F(z)=I-\mathcal U(z)^{-1}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
A resolved word is an admitted branch of the marked process tensor, so
branch-conditioned tomography gives its unique Choi map.  The resolved words
$\varnothing^{n-1}m$ and $\varnothing^N$ partition the finite sample space
according to the first marked return or survival, which gives positivity and
the normalization identity.  Every unrestricted path of length $n$ has a
unique first return at some $k\le n$ followed by an unrestricted path of length
$n-k$.  Composition of the corresponding CP maps and summation over $k$ gives
the renewal equation; rearrangement gives the recursion, and formal series
multiplication gives the resolvent identities.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Norm-convergent boundary-cycle channel and return pencil]
\label{thm:marked-cycle-channel}
In the setting of \Cref{thm:marked-first-return}, put
$\mathcal F_{n,*}=\sum_m\mathcal F_{n,m,*}$.  Assume that the survivor effects
satisfy
\[
 \boxed{\|\mathcal S_{N,*}^{*}(I)\|\le Ce^{-\alpha N}}
\]
for some $C,\alpha>0$.  Then the partial first-return sums converge in induced
trace norm to a completely positive trace-preserving boundary-to-boundary
channel
\[
 \boxed{\mathcal R_*:=\sum_{n\ge1}\mathcal F_{n,*}.}
\]
Moreover the marked cycle pencil
\[
 \boxed{\mathcal R_*(z):=\sum_{n\ge1}z^n\mathcal F_{n,*}}
\]
is norm analytic for $|z|<e^{\alpha}$, and its derivatives at $z=1$ reconstruct
all finite return-duration moments allowed by the same exponential window.
The channel has at least one stationary boundary state.  Its Heisenberg dual is
a contraction in every stationary GNS representation.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Let $R_{N,*}=\sum_{n=1}^{N}\mathcal F_{n,*}$.  The first-return
normalization in \Cref{thm:marked-first-return} gives, for every positive trace
class input $\rho$,
\[
 \Tr\bigl[(R_{M,*}-R_{N,*})(\rho)\bigr]
 \le \Tr\bigl[\rho\,\mathcal S_{N,*}^{*}(I)\bigr]
 \le Ce^{-\alpha N}\Tr\rho
 \qquad(M>N).
\]
For a positive map the induced trace norm is attained on positive inputs, so
$(R_{N,*})$ is Cauchy in that norm.  Its limit is CP, and the survivor effect
tends to zero, so the finite normalization identity passes to
$\mathcal R_*^{*}(I)=I$.  The same estimate with $|z|^n$ proves normal
convergence of the pencil on compact subsets of $|z|<e^{\alpha}$; termwise
differentiation gives the moment formulas.  The finite-dimensional state space
is compact and convex, hence the dual channel has a fixed state.  Kadison's
inequality for the unital Heisenberg dual and stationarity give the GNS
contraction.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[The minimal repair after scheduler nonidentifiability]
For occurrence alone, one passive boundary bit is the minimal separating
datum.  To reconstruct a two-score mechanism, the time-local alphabet
$\{\varnothing,+,-\}$ is sufficient: one boundary bit and one score bit
conditional on a boundary.  The mark does not assume fairness, independence,
reset, or a gap; those are finite branch-level tests.  Without such an exposed
mark or an independently physical environment POVM, an internal scheduler is
not identifiable from the coarse channel.
\end{firewall}


% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
\subsection{Minimal upstream weight forcing and the pre-writer identifiability boundary}
\label{sec:upstream-weight-forcing}
% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

The exact renewal table fixes the concrete coefficients $1/5$ and $1/3$.
A stronger upstream claim would derive those numbers from a smaller physical
principle.  The relevant reduction is representation theoretic: after the
internal entry labels and completion labels have been verified to be regular,
only one cross-fibre scalar remains in each active phase.

\begin{definition}[One-neutral/$n$-writer phase source]
\label{def:one-neutral-writer-source}
Let one nonwriting atom be fixed and let $\mathfrak S_n$ permute $n$ writing
atoms.  Write a full-support source as
\[
 p(a,u)=\bigl(a,(1-a)u_1,\ldots,(1-a)u_n\bigr),
 \qquad u\in\Delta_n,
\]
and put
\[
 \omega_n=\frac1{\sqrt{n(n+1)}}(n,-1,\ldots,-1),
 \qquad
 J_n(a)=a-\frac{1-a}{n}.
\]
The first coordinate is the nonwriting mass and $u$ is the conditional
writing-label distribution.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Invariant-axis decomposition and the unique cross-fibre Ward coordinate]
\label{thm:phase-invariant-axis}
The centered coefficient space has the orthogonal decomposition
\[
 \boxed{
 \one_{n+1}^{\perp}
 =\R\omega_n\oplus
 \bigl(\{0\}\oplus\one_n^{\perp}\bigr).}
\]
Moreover
\[
 \boxed{
 \begin{aligned}
 &(n+1)\left\|p(a,u)-\frac1{n+1}\one_{n+1}\right\|_2^2\\
 &\qquad
 =nJ_n(a)^2
 +(n+1)(1-a)^2
 \left\|u-\frac1n\one_n\right\|_2^2.
 \end{aligned}}
\]
The line $\R\omega_n$ is the complete $\mathfrak S_n$-fixed subspace of
$\one_{n+1}^{\perp}$.  Consequently, once the writing-label source is
internally regular, every invariant centered linear observable is a scalar
multiple of $J_n$, and
\[
 \boxed{
 p\left(a,\frac1n\one_n\right)=\frac1{n+1}\one_{n+1}
 \iff J_n(a)=0
 \iff a=\frac1{n+1}.}
\]
Quantitatively,
\[
 \boxed{
 \left|a-\frac1{n+1}\right|=\frac n{n+1}|J_n(a)|.}
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Every vector fixed by the writing-label permutations has one nonwriting
coordinate and one common writing coordinate.  Imposing zero total sum leaves
precisely the line $\R\omega_n$.  The orthogonal complement inside the
centered space is $\{0\}\oplus\one_n^\perp$, whose dimension is $n-1$.
Splitting the writing coordinates into their mean and centered parts gives
\[
 p(a,u)-\frac1{n+1}\one_{n+1}
 =\langle\omega_n,p(a,u)\rangle\omega_n
  +\bigl(0,(1-a)(u-n^{-1}\one_n)\bigr),
\]
where
\[
 \langle\omega_n,p(a,u)\rangle
 =\frac{(n+1)a-1}{\sqrt{n(n+1)}}.
\]
Taking squared norms and multiplying by $n+1$ proves the displayed identity.
The fixed-space assertion proves uniqueness of the invariant centered
coordinate, and solving $J_n(a)=0$ gives the final statements.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Rank-minimal forcing of the concrete renewal weights]
\label{cor:minimal-renewal-Ward-currents}
For the hub phase, one neutral atom and four regular entry labels leave the
single current
\[
 \boxed{J_H=a-\frac{1-a}{4}.}
\]
For the private phase, one survivor atom and two fair completion labels leave
\[
 \boxed{J_P=s-\frac{1-s}{2}.}
\]
Thus
\[
 \boxed{J_H=J_P=0
 \iff a=\frac15,\qquad s=\frac13.}
\]
One scalar Ward coordinate per phase is therefore necessary and sufficient;
a complete five-atom or three-atom transition kernel is stronger than needed
for numerical weight forcing.
\end{corollary}

\begin{definition}[Fresh terminal-atom instrument]
\label{def:fresh-terminal-atom}
Let $A=\{1,\ldots,m\}$ be an unobserved pre-writer atom set with full-support
source $p$.  A hidden sampler is either a stochastic kernel $K$ satisfying
$K\one=\one$, $K^{\mathsf T}p=p$, or a Markov semigroup $e^{tQ}$ satisfying
$Q\one=0$, $Q^{\mathsf T}p=0$.  At every opportunity a fresh atom is prepared
with law $p$, the sampler acts, a visible branch map $\Phi_{\omega,i}$ depending
only on the terminal atom is applied, and the atom is discarded.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Complete multitime invisibility of a fresh stationary sampler]
\label{thm:fresh-opportunity-invisibility}
In \Cref{def:fresh-terminal-atom}, put
\[
 \overline\Phi_\omega=\sum_{i=1}^mp_i\Phi_{\omega,i}.
\]
Every resolved downstream word, every adaptive visible intervention family,
and every terminal Read are obtained by composing the averaged branches
$\overline\Phi_\omega$.  They are independent of the hidden sampler and its
admitted duration.  Hence the complete downstream table determines none of
\[
 \boxed{
 K,\quad Q,\quad\text{balance},\quad\text{circulation},\quad
 \text{components},\quad\text{rooted-tree weights},\quad\text{or a gap}.}
\]
In particular, arbitrarily long post-writer chronology does not reconstruct a
pre-writer second time slice.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Stationarity leaves the terminal hidden atom with law $p$ after every hidden
duration.  Summing the unobserved atom therefore gives
$\overline\Phi_\omega$.  The next opportunity begins with a fresh copy, so no
hidden coordinate propagates between visible cycles.  Induction on the
resolved visible word gives a composition solely of the averaged branches and
the visible interventions.  Since stationary samplers with the same $p$ may
have different values of every listed dynamical quantity, none is identifiable
from that table.
\end{proof}

\begin{countertheorem}[One isolated continuous delay does not identify a hidden generator]
\label{cth:fixed-delay-hidden-generator}
For every $t>0$ there are distinct balanced irreducible three-state Markov
generators $Q^{(0)}\ne Q^{(1)}$ such that
\[
 \boxed{e^{tQ^{(0)}}=e^{tQ^{(1)}}.}
\]
Thus even an atom-resolved panel at one isolated continuous delay need not
recover circulation or a generator logarithm.
\end{countertheorem}

\begin{proof}
Let $C$ be the cyclic permutation of three atoms and put
$Q_{a,b}=a(C-I)+b(C^2-I)$.  Its two nonzero eigenvalues are
$-3(a+b)/2\pm i\sqrt3(a-b)/2$.  With
$s_*=4\pi/(\sqrt3t)$, choose
$Q^{(0)}=Q_{s_*/2,s_*/2}$ and $Q^{(1)}=Q_{s_*,0}$.  The latter eigenvalues
differ from the former by $\pm2\pi i/t$, while both generators are circulant
and share the Fourier eigenbasis.  Exponentiation at time $t$ therefore gives
the same matrix.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[One delayed binary Read evaluates the minimal Ward current]
\label{thm:delayed-binary-Ward}
Assume, independently, that one nonwriting atom is joined to each of the $n$
writing atoms by the same positive exchange rate $r$, while arbitrary
writing-to-writing dynamics preserves the writing orbit.  If
$h_n(t)$ is the nonwriting probability, then
\[
 \boxed{
 h_n'(t)=r\bigl(1-(n+1)h_n(t)\bigr),
 \qquad
 h_n(t)=\frac1{n+1}
 +\left(a-\frac1{n+1}\right)e^{-(n+1)rt}.}
\]
The outward cross-fibre current is
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal J_{n,r}=-h_n'(0)
 =r\bigl((n+1)a-1\bigr)=rnJ_n(a).}
\]
For every $t_*>0$,
\[
 \boxed{
 h_n(t_*)=h_n(0)
 \iff \mathcal J_{n,r}=0
 \iff a=\frac1{n+1}.}
\]
Thus, on a verified exchange branch, one binary nonwriting-versus-writing Read
at two pre-writer times per phase forces the concrete weights without
atom-resolved transition tomography or rate calibration.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The forward equation aggregates the $n$ incoming rates to
$r(1-h_n)$ and the $n$ outgoing rates to $nrh_n$, giving the scalar ODE.
Its solution proves the current and fixed-delay identities.  Internal
writing-orbit transitions cancel under aggregation.
\end{proof}

\begin{assessment}[Exact primitive-weight boundary]
\label{assess:primitive-weight-boundary}
The current completed-private and synchronized-opportunity interfaces expose
the return law, completion mark, fresh endpoint, retained private fingerprint,
and terminal accepted/no-response record.  They do not expose the same hidden
five-atom or three-atom source at two pre-writer times, nor an independently
physical derivative realizing $J_H$ and $J_P$.  By
\Cref{thm:fresh-opportunity-invisibility}, the existing fresh terminal table
cannot supply that missing dynamics.  Therefore $1/5$ and $1/3$ are exact
measured source coefficients in the selected packet.  Their derivation from a
smaller exchange or Ward principle is conditional on two additional scalar
physical ports; merely naming $5a-1$ and $3s-1$ as currents would restate the
desired equations rather than prove them.
\end{assessment}


% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
\subsection{The canonical primitive floor: returned feedback and sealed provenance}
\label{sec:pre-renewal-primitive-floor}
% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

A finite microscopic realization may contain more coordinates than the
minimal renewal predictor.  The relevant question is not whether such
coordinates can be written down, but which part of them can leave the visible
renewal, evolve, and later return to a declared active future.  The following
construction is invariant under hidden changes of basis and separates that
returned part from permanently sealed provenance.

\begin{definition}[Finite pre-renewal lift]
\label{def:finite-pre-renewal-lift}
Let $\mathcal L$ be a finite visible carrier and $\mathcal E$ a finite hidden
carrier.  A finite lift of a visible transfer is
\[
 \widetilde T=
 \begin{pmatrix}A&B\\ C&D\end{pmatrix}
 \quad\text{on }\mathcal L\oplus\mathcal E,
\]
where $Jx=(x,0)$ and $P(x,e)=x$.  Put
\[
 X_n=P\widetilde T^nJ,
 \qquad
 K_n=BD^nC\quad(n\ge0).
\]
Define the hidden source-reachable space, its future-sealed subspace, and the
returned-feedback quotient by
\[
 \mathcal R_{\rm hid}
 :=\Span\{D^nCx:n\ge0,\ x\in\mathcal L\},
\]
\[
 \mathcal N_{\rm seal}
 :=\{e\in\mathcal R_{\rm hid}:BD^ne=0\text{ for every }n\ge0\},
 \qquad
 \mathcal F_{\rm fb}:=\mathcal R_{\rm hid}/\mathcal N_{\rm seal}.
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Canonical pre-renewal decomposition]
\label{thm:canonical-pre-renewal-decomposition}
The spaces in \Cref{def:finite-pre-renewal-lift} satisfy:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.8em]
\item $\mathcal R_{\rm hid}$ and $\mathcal N_{\rm seal}$ are $D$-invariant;
\item $C,D,B$ descend to maps
      \[
       \overline C:\mathcal L\to\mathcal F_{\rm fb},\qquad
       \overline D:\mathcal F_{\rm fb}\to\mathcal F_{\rm fb},\qquad
       \overline B:\mathcal F_{\rm fb}\to\mathcal L;
      \]
\item the descended realization is reachable and observable:
      \[
       \Span\{\overline D^n\overline C\mathcal L:n\ge0\}
       =\mathcal F_{\rm fb},
      \]
      and
      \[
       \overline B\overline D^n\bar e=0\ \forall n
       \Longrightarrow \bar e=0;
      \]
\item there is a canonical exact sequence
      \[
       \boxed{
       0\longrightarrow\mathcal N_{\rm seal}
       \longrightarrow\mathcal R_{\rm hid}
       \longrightarrow\mathcal F_{\rm fb}
       \longrightarrow0;}
      \]
\item if $d_{\rm fb}=\dim\mathcal F_{\rm fb}$, then for all
      $p,q\ge d_{\rm fb}$ the block Hankel operator
      \[
       \mathsf H^{\rm fb}_{p,q}
       =[BD^{i+j}C]_{0\le i<p,\ 0\le j<q}
      \]
      has rank $d_{\rm fb}$.
\end{enumerate}
The quotient is the unique minimal reachable--observable realization of the
returned kernels $(K_n)_{n\ge0}$, up to a unique similarity intertwining
$\overline B,\overline C,\overline D$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The space $\mathcal R_{\rm hid}$ is $D$-invariant by construction.  If
$e\in\mathcal N_{\rm seal}$, then
$BD^n(De)=BD^{n+1}e=0$ for every $n$, so the sealed subspace is invariant.
Taking $n=0$ shows that $B$ annihilates $\mathcal N_{\rm seal}$; hence all
three maps descend.  Reachability is inherited from the definition of
$\mathcal R_{\rm hid}$, and the defining condition of
$\mathcal N_{\rm seal}$ gives observability of the quotient.

Let $\mathcal C_q$ synthesize the columns
$\overline D^j\overline C\mathcal L$, $0\le j<q$, and let $\mathcal O_p$
collect the rows $\overline B\overline D^i$, $0\le i<p$.  Then
\[
 \mathsf H^{\rm fb}_{p,q}=\mathcal O_p\mathcal C_q.
\]
Reachability makes $\mathcal C_q$ onto after at most $d_{\rm fb}$ strict rank
increases; observability makes $\mathcal O_p$ injective after at most
$d_{\rm fb}$ strict kernel decreases.  The rank formula follows.  Any other
realization factors the same Hankel family through its state space and
therefore has dimension at least $d_{\rm fb}$.  Equality gives the standard
reachable--observable similarity, which is unique because the reachable
columns span.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Visible recovery and exact no-return criterion]
\label{thm:pre-renewal-visible-recovery}
The visible compressed powers determine every returned kernel recursively:
\[
 \boxed{A=X_1,}
\]
\[
 \boxed{
 K_n=X_{n+2}-AX_{n+1}
     -\sum_{j=1}^{n}K_{n-j}X_j
 \qquad(n\ge0).}
\]
Equivalently,
\[
 \sum_{n\ge0}X_nz^n
 =[I-zA-z^2B(I-zD)^{-1}C]^{-1}.
\]
For a prescribed visible transfer $T_0$,
\[
 \boxed{
 X_n=T_0^n\ \forall n\ge0
 \iff
 A=T_0\text{ and }K_n=0\ \forall n\ge0.}
\]
In finite hidden dimension it is enough to test
$0\le n<\dim\mathcal E$.  Hence an exact finite lift of the complete visible
renewal cannot contain a hidden direction which leaves the visible carrier and
later returns with additional active predictive information.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Block multiplication gives
\[
 X_{n+1}=AX_n+\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}K_{n-1-j}X_j,
 \qquad X_0=I.
\]
The displayed recursion is obtained by solving the equation for $X_{n+2}$ for
its $K_nX_0$ term.  Summing the convolution gives the resolvent identity.
If $X_n=T_0^n$, then $A=T_0$ at $n=1$.  The recursion gives $K_0=0$ from
$n=0$, and induction gives $K_n=0$ because all earlier returned kernels have
already vanished.  The converse is immediate.  Cayley--Hamilton for $D$
reduces the infinite zero list to the first $\dim\mathcal E$ powers.
\end{proof}

The aggregate criterion can conceal cancellations in a signed linear model.
The complete resolved word table removes that ambiguity.

\begin{theorem}[Resolved-word Schur inversion]
\label{thm:resolved-excursion-inversion}
Let a finite resolved alphabet $\Sigma$ have branch lifts
\[
 \widetilde T_a=
 \begin{pmatrix}A_a&B_a\\ C_a&D_a\end{pmatrix},
 \qquad a\in\Sigma.
\]
For noncommuting formal variables $(z_a)_{a\in\Sigma}$ put
\[
 \mathbf A(z)=\sum_aA_az_a,\quad
 \mathbf B(z)=\sum_aB_az_a,\quad
 \mathbf C(z)=\sum_aC_az_a,\quad
 \mathbf D(z)=\sum_aD_az_a,
\]
\[
 \mathbf X(z)=P(I-\sum_a\widetilde T_az_a)^{-1}J.
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathbf X(z)^{-1}
 =I-\mathbf A(z)-\mathbf E(z),}
\]
where
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathbf E(z)
 =\mathbf B(z)(I-\mathbf D(z))^{-1}\mathbf C(z).}
\]
The coefficient of $z_bz_uz_a$ in $\mathbf E$ is exactly the irreducible
hidden excursion
\[
 \boxed{E_{b,u,a}=B_bD_uC_a.}
\]
Consequently the complete resolved word table reconstructs every hidden
excursion.  If
\[
 P\widetilde T_wJ=T_w\qquad\text{for every resolved word }w,
\]
then
\[
 \boxed{A_a=T_a,\qquad B_bD_uC_a=0\quad\forall a,b,u.}
\]
If the excursion maps are positive or completely positive, aggregate
exactness already implies the same branchwise conclusion, because a sum of
positive maps can vanish only when every summand vanishes.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Formal block inversion gives the Schur complement
\[
 P(I-\widetilde{\mathbf T})^{-1}J
 =\bigl[I-\mathbf A
 -\mathbf B(I-\mathbf D)^{-1}\mathbf C\bigr]^{-1},
\]
which proves the first two formulas.  Expanding
$(I-\mathbf D)^{-1}=\sum_uD_uz_u$ gives the coefficient formula.  The
length-one resolved coefficients give $A_a=T_a$.  Equality of the complete
resolved series gives
$\mathbf X(z)=(I-\sum_aT_az_a)^{-1}$, hence $\mathbf E(z)=0$ and every
coefficient vanishes.  In the positive case, evaluate the aggregate returned
kernel on positive inputs and effects: it is a sum of nonnegative scalars, so
zero forces every positive summand to vanish.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Normal form of every exact source-reachable lift]
\label{cor:exact-lift-normal-form}
Let the hidden sector be source reachable from the visible renewal.  If the
complete resolved table is exact, then, after restricting to that reachable
sector,
\[
 \boxed{
 \widetilde T_a=
 \begin{pmatrix}T_a&0\\ C_a&D_a\end{pmatrix}.}
\]
Thus every exact finite source-reachable lift is a one-way provenance
extension: it may be written by renewal, but it cannot route back into any
later active branch of the declared alphabet.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The source-reachable hidden space is spanned by the vectors $D_uC_ax$.
\Cref{thm:resolved-excursion-inversion} gives
$B_bD_uC_a=0$ for every $b,u,a$, so every $B_b$ vanishes on that span.
\end{proof}

\begin{countertheorem}[No canonical finest primitive]
\label{cth:no-finest-primitive}
No unrestricted operational table selects a finest finite microscopic lift.
For any realization and any finite auxiliary system, tensoring an unread
spectator on which every declared letter acts trace preservingly leaves all
visible probabilities and all declared Reads unchanged.  The spectator
algebra, dimension, and symmetry may be chosen arbitrarily.
\end{countertheorem}

\begin{proof}
For every visible branch $\Phi_*$ and trace-preserving spectator branch
$\Psi_*$,
\[
 \Tr_{\rm sp}[(\Phi_*\otimes\Psi_*)(X)]
 =\Phi_*(\Tr_{\rm sp}X).
\]
Iteration gives equality of all visible multitime tables.  Nonisomorphic
spectator choices therefore define inequivalent lifts of the same process.
\end{proof}

% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
\subsection{Read-minimal one-way provenance}
\label{sec:read-minimal-provenance}
% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

The lower-triangular normal form is not itself a physical record.  It becomes
operational only after a passive Read family is declared.  The correct
quotient is obtained from centered responses, because a future word may write
new provenance as well as propagate provenance already present at the cut.

\begin{definition}[Finite sealed provenance extension]
\label{def:sealed-provenance-extension}
Let
\[
 \widetilde T_a=
 \begin{pmatrix}T_a&0\\ C_a&D_a\end{pmatrix}
\]
act on $\mathcal L\oplus\mathcal E$, with zero initial hidden coordinate, and
let $R_\lambda:\mathcal E\to\mathcal Y_\lambda$ be passive terminal Reads.
For a word $w$, write
\[
 \widetilde T_w=
 \begin{pmatrix}T_w&0\\ H_w&D_w\end{pmatrix},
 \qquad
 Y_{\lambda,w}=R_\lambda H_w.
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Sealed-provenance cocycle and centered response]
\label{thm:sealed-provenance-cocycle}
For all words $v,w$,
\[
 \boxed{H_{vw}=H_vT_w+D_vH_w,\qquad D_{vw}=D_vD_w.}
\]
Consequently the table-native centered response
\[
 \boxed{
 K_{\lambda;v,w}
 :=Y_{\lambda,vw}-Y_{\lambda,v}T_w}
\]
is exactly
\[
 \boxed{K_{\lambda;v,w}=R_\lambda D_vH_w.}
\]
It measures the future of provenance already present after $w$ and removes
provenance newly written during $v$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The cocycle is the lower-left block of
$\widetilde T_v\widetilde T_w$.  Applying $R_\lambda$ and subtracting
$Y_{\lambda,v}T_w$ gives the centered identity.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Source-minimal passive provenance carrier]
\label{def:passive-provenance-quotient}
Put
\[
 \mathcal R_{\rm prov}
 :=\Span\{H_wx:w\in\Sigma^*,\ x\in\mathcal L\},
\]
\[
 \mathcal N_{\rm prov}
 :=\{e\in\mathcal R_{\rm prov}:
 R_\lambda D_ve=0\text{ for all }\lambda,v\},
 \qquad
 \mathcal P_{\rm prov}:=\mathcal R_{\rm prov}/\mathcal N_{\rm prov}.
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Canonical sealed-provenance quotient]
\label{thm:sealed-provenance-quotient}
The spaces $\mathcal R_{\rm prov}$ and $\mathcal N_{\rm prov}$ are invariant
under every $D_a$.  The writers, hidden letters, and Reads descend to a
source-reachable and Read-observable realization on
$\mathcal P_{\rm prov}$, and
\[
 \boxed{
 0\longrightarrow\mathcal N_{\rm prov}
 \longrightarrow\mathcal R_{\rm prov}
 \longrightarrow\mathcal P_{\rm prov}
 \longrightarrow0.}
\]
Every centered response factors through this quotient.  Two finite sealed
extensions with the same visible maps and the same complete passive Read table
have uniquely similar source-reachable, Read-observable quotients, with the
similarity intertwining every writer, hidden letter, and Read.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
For a reachable generator the cocycle gives
$D_aH_w=H_{aw}-H_aT_w$, so $\mathcal R_{\rm prov}$ is invariant.  If
$e\in\mathcal N_{\rm prov}$, then
$R_\lambda D_vD_ae=R_\lambda D_{va}e=0$, proving invariance of the null
space.  The quotient maps are therefore well defined.  Reachability is by
construction, and vanishing of all descended future Reads places a
representative in $\mathcal N_{\rm prov}$, proving observability.

For uniqueness, map a reachable combination
$\sum_w\overline H_w^{(1)}x_w$ to
$\sum_w\overline H_w^{(2)}x_w$.  Equality of all centered coefficients makes
this map well defined; observability makes it injective, and reachability makes
it onto.  The cocycle proves the hidden-letter intertwining, while the source
and Read intertwinings are immediate.  Reachable generators also prove
uniqueness.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Provenance-Hankel minimality]
\label{thm:provenance-hankel-minimality}
Let
\[
 \mathsf H^{\rm prov}_{p,q}[(\lambda,v),w]
 :=K_{\lambda;v,w}
 =\overline R_\lambda\overline D_v\overline H_w,
\]
where $|v|\le p$ and $|w|\le q$.  If
$d_{\rm prov}=\dim\mathcal P_{\rm prov}$, then
\[
 \boxed{
 \rank\mathsf H^{\rm prov}_{p,q}=d_{\rm prov}
 \qquad(p,q\ge d_{\rm prov}).}
\]
This rank is the minimum possible dimension of any finite source-reachable,
Read-observable sealed realization of the same passive table.  The quotient
and all descended letters are reconstructed from one saturated finite panel by
\[
 \boxed{
 \overline D_a[H_wx]=[H_{aw}x]-[H_aT_wx],
 \qquad
 \overline C_ax=[H_ax].}
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Factor the panel as $\mathcal O_p\mathcal C_q$, where $\mathcal C_q$ collects
the source columns $\overline H_w$ and $\mathcal O_p$ collects the future rows
$\overline R_\lambda\overline D_v$.  Source reachability makes
$\mathcal C_q$ onto after at most $d_{\rm prov}$ strict dimension increases;
Read observability makes $\mathcal O_p$ injective after at most
$d_{\rm prov}$ strict kernel decreases.  The rank formula and minimality
follow.  The displayed shift formula is the cocycle solved for
$\overline D_a\overline H_w$ and respects all Hankel column relations.
\end{proof}


% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
\subsubsection{Geometric-dwell inversion of a signed provenance panel}
\label{sec:provenance-dwell-inversion}
% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

The centered provenance Hankel theorem identifies the minimal carrier once the
complete passive Read table is given.  For the concrete geometric private
dwell, the whole centered propagation can in fact be reconstructed from one
completion-aggregated signed panel.

\begin{definition}[Completion-aggregated centered provenance transfer]
\label{def:completion-aggregate-provenance}
Let $D_0:W\to W$ be a centered private-provenance contraction.  Let
$s\in[0,1)$ be the private-survival probability and put $c=1-s$.  One mandatory
private update occurs before completion and is followed by $k\ge0$ additional
updates with probability $cs^k$.  Define
\[
 \boxed{
 A_s:=\sum_{k\ge0}cs^kD_0^{k+1}.}
\]
For the concrete renewal, $s=1/3$ and $c=2/3$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Exact linear-fractional inversion of geometric dwell]
\label{thm:completion-aggregate-inversion}
For every contraction $D_0$ and $0\le s<1$,
\[
 \boxed{A_s=cD_0(I-sD_0)^{-1}.}
\]
The transform is injective and its exact operator inverse is
\[
 \boxed{
 D_0=A_s(cI+sA_s)^{-1}
     =(cI+sA_s)^{-1}A_s.}
\]
Moreover
\[
 \boxed{\Ker A_s=\Ker D_0,
 \qquad \rank A_s=\rank D_0.}
\]
Thus one signed entry--completion transfer, even after summing over every
private dwell length, reconstructs the complete centered channel and its
instantaneous provenance-Hankel dimension.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The geometric series converges in norm and gives the first identity.  Since
$A_s$ is a rational function of $D_0$, the two commute, and
\[
 cI+sA_s
 =c\bigl[I+sD_0(I-sD_0)^{-1}\bigr]
 =c(I-sD_0)^{-1}.
\]
This operator is invertible and multiplication gives the inverse formula.
Finally $A_s$ is $D_0$ followed by an invertible commuting factor, proving the
kernel and rank identities.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Stable aggregate reconstruction]
\label{thm:completion-aggregate-stability}
If $D_0,\widetilde D_0$ are contractions with aggregate transfers
$A_s,\widetilde A_s$, then
\[
 \boxed{
 \|D_0-\widetilde D_0\|
 \le L_s\|A_s-\widetilde A_s\|,}
\]
where
\[
 \boxed{
 L_s=\frac{1+s}{1-s}
 +\frac{s(1+s)^2}{(1-s)^2}.}
\]
For $s=1/3$, one may take $L_{1/3}=10/3$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Put $R_A=cI+sA_s$.  The inverse formula gives
$R_A^{-1}=c^{-1}(I-sD_0)$ and hence
$\|R_A^{-1}\|\le(1+s)/c$.  Also $\|A_s\|\le1$.  Apply
\[
 D_0-\widetilde D_0
 =(A_s-\widetilde A_s)R_A^{-1}
 +\widetilde A_s(R_A^{-1}-R_{\widetilde A}^{-1})
\]
and the inverse-difference identity
$R_A^{-1}-R_{\widetilde A}^{-1}
 =R_{\widetilde A}^{-1}s(\widetilde A_s-A_s)R_A^{-1}$.
The displayed constant follows after inserting $c=1-s$.
\end{proof}

\begin{countertheorem}[The old-private fingerprint does not determine the entry-provenance channel]
\label{cth:private-fingerprint-no-provenance-channel}
Fix the complete active renewal packet, the fresh endpoint, and the retained
old-private binary source with its prescribed Gram.  For every finite
contraction $D_0$ on an additional centered provenance space, there is a
one-way extension which propagates that space by $D_0$ during the private
phase, routes no provenance coordinate into the active future, and leaves all
currently declared renewal probabilities, endpoint data, and old-private
Grams unchanged.  Hence the existing marginals impose no condition on $D_0$.
\end{countertheorem}

\begin{proof}
Tensor the selected realization with a centered provenance factor, write that
factor at private entry, apply $D_0$ at each private survivor step, and discard
it before every currently declared Read.  Partial trace over the new factor
commutes with every visible branch, while lower-triangular wiring prevents any
return to the active future.  Therefore every existing visible table and the
independent old-private Gram remain unchanged for arbitrary $D_0$.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[$S_4$-covariant tetrahedral specialization]
\label{cor:covariant-provenance-inversion}
If the centered four-entry provenance carries the standard $S_4$ triplet and
$D_0=\rho I$ on that triplet, then
\[
 \boxed{
 A_s=\alpha_s(\rho)I,
 \qquad
 \alpha_s(\rho)=\frac{(1-s)\rho}{1-s\rho},
 \qquad
 \rho=\frac{\alpha_s}{1-s+s\alpha_s}.}
\]
For $s=1/3$, $\rho=3\alpha/(2+\alpha)$.  A terminal Gram $A_s^*A_s$ alone is
insufficient because it loses the sign of $\alpha$; a signed cross transfer or
an equivalent mixed Gram retaining relative orientation is necessary.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Restrict \Cref{thm:completion-aggregate-inversion} to the irreducible triplet,
where Schur's lemma makes the channel scalar, and solve the resulting
linear-fractional equation.  The final statement follows because
$\alpha$ and $-\alpha$ have the same quadratic Gram.
\end{proof}


\begin{theorem}[Active, ledger, and provenance innovation]
\label{thm:provenance-innovation-decomposition}
Let $A,L,S$ be saturated signature maps on one past coefficient space,
representing respectively the active predictor, the protected renewal ledger,
and a finer passive provenance Read.  Assume the ledger refines the active
predictor, so $\Ker L\subseteq\Ker A$.  Put
$P_A=A^\dagger A$ and $P_L=L^\dagger L$.  Then
\[
 \boxed{
 S(I-P_A)S^*
 =S(P_L-P_A)S^*+S(I-P_L)S^*.}
\]
Both summands are positive.  The first is historical information already
contained in the protected ledger but absent from the current active phase;
the second is genuinely new provenance beyond the ledger.  Moreover,
\[
 \boxed{
 \rank\begin{pmatrix}A\\S\end{pmatrix}-\rank A
 =\rank\bigl(S(I-P_A)S^*\bigr).}
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The kernel inclusion gives $P_A\preceq P_L$.  The projections $P_L-P_A$ and
$I-P_L$ are orthogonal and sum to $I-P_A$, proving the decomposition.
The rank increment is the rank of $S$ restricted to $\Ker A$, equivalently the
rank of the Gram $S(I-P_A)S^*$.
\end{proof}

\begin{assessment}[Canonical meaning of the microscopic primitive]
\label{assess:canonical-microscopic-floor}
At finite cutoff, the strongest basis-free object below the renewal table is
therefore the following layered floor:
\[
 \boxed{
 \begin{gathered}
 \text{minimal visible renewal quotient}
 \; + \; \text{Read-minimal sealed provenance}\\
 {}+\;\text{minimal returned-feedback quotient}
 \end{gathered}}
\]
Exact renewal makes the last summand zero.  The middle summand exists only
relative to actual passive Reads and may be a deterministic history copy, a
fresh but state-independent mark, or genuinely new provenance as decided by
\Cref{thm:provenance-innovation-decomposition}.  No theorem selects an
unread maximal substrate.
\end{assessment}

\begin{definition}[Concrete completed-private Store packet]
\label{def:completed-private-packet}
The concrete renewal source has two hub classes and a private region with the
following source-native properties.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(C\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item after a completed-private return, the number $D$ of direct hub-edge
      returns before the next private entry satisfies
      $\Pr(D=d)=\frac45(\frac15)^d$, $d\ge0$;
\item conditional on private entry, the private duration $L$ satisfies
      $\Pr(L=2+n)=\frac23(\frac13)^n$, $n\ge0$;
\item the strong Markov property makes $D$ and $L$ independent, and a completed
      private excursion writes a passive completion record;
\item the endpoint amplitude factors through
      $|+\rangle=(|0\rangle+|1\rangle)/\sqrt2$, while the retained old private
      record is represented by unit vectors $|r_0\rangle,|r_1\rangle$ with
      $\langle r_0,r_1\rangle=1/5$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Exact completed-private renewal law]
\label{thm:completed-private-renewal}
For successive completed-private records, the interarrival time $W=D+L$ has
\[
 \boxed{
 F_W(z):=\mathbb E[z^W]
 =\frac{8z^2}{(5-z)(3-z)},
 \qquad
 \mathbb EW=\frac{11}{4},
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Var}W=\frac{17}{16}.}
\]
For $n\ge2$,
\[
 \boxed{\Pr(W=n)=4\bigl(3^{1-n}-5^{1-n}\bigr),}
\]
and for $N\ge1$,
\[
 \boxed{\Pr(W>N)=6\,3^{-N}-5\,5^{-N}\le6\,3^{-N}.}
\]
Thus every interarrival is finite almost surely and, if $N_t$ is the number of
completed-private records by raw time $t$,
\[
 \boxed{\frac{N_t}{t}\longrightarrow\frac4{11}}
 \qquad\text{almost surely.}
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The probability generating functions are
$F_D(z)=4/(5-z)$ and $F_L(z)=2z^2/(3-z)$.  Independence gives their product.
Differentiating at one yields the first two moments.  Partial fractions give
the displayed mass function, and summing the two geometric tails gives
$6\,3^{-N}-5\,5^{-N}$.  Hence the iid interarrivals have finite mean and are
almost surely finite.  The strong law gives
$k^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^kW_j\to11/4$; inversion of the renewal epochs gives
$N_t/t\to4/11$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Fresh predictive endpoint with retained private information]
\label{thm:fresh-endpoint-retained-record}
After the stable endpoint Read, the completed-private reset channel has the
form
\[
 \boxed{
 \Phi_{\rm hub}(\rho)
 =\frac{I_2}{2}\otimes
 \left(\rho_{00}|r_0\rangle\langle r_0|
       +\rho_{11}|r_1\rangle\langle r_1|\right).}
\]
The new hub mark is independent of the accessible old private record, but that
private record is not erased.  Its optimal equal-prior discrimination
probability is
\[
 \boxed{P_{\rm succ}^{\rm opt}
 =\frac12\left(1+\sqrt{1-|\langle r_0,r_1\rangle|^2}\right)
 =\frac{5+2\sqrt6}{10}.}
\]
Thus predictive renewal of the active hub and microscopic destruction of all
old records are inequivalent.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The equal endpoint amplitude and the sharp endpoint conditional expectation
prepare $I_2/2$ independently of the old diagonal hub value, while the old
weights remain in the private-record ensemble, giving the channel.  For two
pure states with equal priors, the Helstrom success probability is
$\frac12(1+\frac12\||r_0\rangle\langle r_0|-|r_1\rangle\langle r_1|\|_1)$,
and the trace distance is
$\sqrt{1-|\langle r_0,r_1\rangle|^2}=2\sqrt6/5$.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Private-provenance fingerprint and reset factorization]
\label{cor:private-provenance-fingerprint}
The retained private source has Gram
\[
 \boxed{
 G_{\rm priv}
 =\begin{pmatrix}1&1/5\\[0.15em]1/5&1\end{pmatrix},}
\]
with eigenvalues $6/5$ and $4/5$.  Its centered contrast
$(r_0-r_1)/\sqrt2$ has squared norm $4/5$.  The completed-reset source factors
as
\[
 \boxed{G_{\rm reset}=\frac12I_{\rm end}\otimes G_{\rm priv}.}
\]
Thus the fresh endpoint and the old private provenance are independent source
factors at the completed cut.  The private overlap $1/5$ is a calibrated
comparison target for any proposed endpoint defect, but it does not determine
that defect from marginal data alone.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The Gram follows from $\|r_0\|=\|r_1\|=1$ and
$\langle r_0,r_1\rangle=1/5$.  Diagonalization gives the two eigenvalues and
the contrast norm.  The source vectors after reset are
$2^{-1/2}|h\rangle\otimes r_x$, so their inner products factor as
$\frac12\delta_{hk}\langle r_x,r_y\rangle$.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Locked synchronized opportunity instrument]
\label{def:locked-opportunity-instrument}
At each completed-private opportunity, let
$\mathscr J=E(K_4)\times\{+,-\}\times\{c,\ell\}$, $|\mathscr J|=24$, and let
\[
 A_j=K_e\otimes\Pi_\sigma\otimes P_r,
 \qquad
 \sum_{j\in\mathscr J}A_j^*A_j=I,
 \qquad
 \sum_{j\in\mathscr J}A_j=\sqrt2\,I.
\]
The $A_j$ are assumed linearly independent.  The order sign writes the binary
pointer, so no second independent mark is present.  With
\[
 \boxed{\vartheta=\frac{576851}{417942208512},}
\]
the resolved opportunity Kraus operators are
\[
 \boxed{L_\varnothing=\sqrt{1-\vartheta}\,I,
 \qquad L_j=\sqrt\vartheta\,A_j.}
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Locked record count, Choi rank, and minimal Naimark record]
\label{thm:locked-opportunity-instrument}
The concrete opportunity instrument has exactly twenty-four nonzero accepted
records and one no-response record.  Its accepted and total coarse Choi ranks
are both twenty-four.  Let $B$ synthesize the accepted Choi vectors and put
\[
