 c=2^{-1/2}(1,\ldots,1)^{\mathsf T}\in\C^{24},
 \qquad
 M_\vartheta=\vartheta I_{24}+(1-\vartheta)cc^*.
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{J_{\rm opp}=BM_\vartheta B^*,
 \qquad M_\vartheta\succ0.}
\]
On the minimal twenty-four-dimensional Stinespring environment, the unique
outcome POVM is
\[
 \boxed{
 F_\varnothing=(1-\vartheta)M_\vartheta^{-1/2}cc^*
 M_\vartheta^{-1/2},
 \qquad
 F_j=\vartheta M_\vartheta^{-1/2}|e_j\rangle\langle e_j|
 M_\vartheta^{-1/2}.}
\]
It is not projection valued.  Its minimal sharp Naimark dilation has
twenty-five cells and one-dimensional excess, with normalized synthesis-null
vector
\[
 \boxed{
 n_{25}
 =\frac{1}{\sqrt{24-22\vartheta}}
 \left(\sqrt{2\vartheta},
       -\sqrt{1-\vartheta},\ldots,-\sqrt{1-\vartheta}\right)^{\mathsf T}.}
\]
A thirty-seven-cell record would require a second independent binary mark on
twelve lepton branches and is not the locked concrete Store record.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Order--pointer locking leaves the labels $(e,\sigma,c)$ and
$(e,\sigma,\ell,\mu(\sigma))$, hence $6\cdot2\cdot2=24$ accepted records.
Linear independence gives accepted Choi rank twenty-four.  Since
$Bc=|I\rangle\!\rangle$, the no-response Choi vector lies in the accepted
span, and summing the branch Choi operators gives $BM_\vartheta B^*$.
Positivity follows from $\vartheta>0$, so the total rank remains twenty-four.

For a full-column-rank factor $W=BM_\vartheta^{1/2}$, the unique environment
effect representing a branch Choi operator $J_\omega$ is
$F_\omega=W^\dagger J_\omega(W^\dagger)^*$, which gives the displayed
formulas and their sum $I$.  There are twenty-five nonzero effects on a
24-dimensional space, so they cannot be orthogonal nonzero projections.  The
rank-one frame vectors
$f_\varnothing=\sqrt{1-\vartheta}M_\vartheta^{-1/2}c$ and
$f_j=\sqrt\vartheta M_\vartheta^{-1/2}e_j$ form a Parseval frame.  Direct
substitution shows that the displayed $n_{25}$ is orthogonal to every row of
the synthesis map; rank twenty-four makes its kernel exactly this line.
Splitting twelve locked lepton cells by a genuinely independent point-readable
mark would add twelve further classical contrasts, which are absent under the
locking relation.
\end{proof}


\begin{corollary}[Contrast spectrum and the sharp-record boundary]
\label{cor:locked-opportunity-contrast-spectrum}
With $P_c=cc^*/\|c\|^2$ and $\|c\|^2=12$, the opportunity coefficient metric is
\[
 \boxed{
 M_\vartheta
 =\vartheta(I-P_c)+(12-11\vartheta)P_c.}
\]
Hence every accepted coefficient contrast orthogonal to the uniform direction
has exact squared source norm $\vartheta$.  For the minimal-environment Parseval
vectors
$f_j=\sqrt\vartheta M_\vartheta^{-1/2}e_j$,
\[
 \boxed{
 \langle f_j,f_k\rangle
 =-\frac{1-\vartheta}{2(12-11\vartheta)}
 \quad(j\ne k).}
\]
In particular, the accepted effects do not define twenty-four orthogonal
minimal-environment sectors.  The twenty-five-cell Naimark completion is a
sharp classical outcome record; its projection algebra is abelian and does not
by itself constitute six dynamical edge qubits.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The first formula is the spectral decomposition of the rank-one update
$\vartheta I+(1-\vartheta)cc^*$.  Its inverse is
$\vartheta^{-1}(I-P_c)+(12-11\vartheta)^{-1}P_c$.  Since every coordinate of
$P_c$ equals $1/24$, substitution in
$\langle f_j,f_k\rangle=\vartheta\langle e_j,M_\vartheta^{-1}e_k\rangle$
gives the displayed off-diagonal value.  A sharp Naimark record is generated
by commuting outcome projections, so no anticommuting endpoint axes follow
from record sharpness alone.
\end{proof}


\begin{theorem}[Exact normalized sign of the locked opportunity instrument]
\label{thm:SMST-exact-locked-sign}
Let the accepted branches have the locked factorization
\[
 A_{e,\sigma,r}=K_e\otimes\Pi_\sigma\otimes P_r,
 \qquad
 \sum_{e,\sigma,r}A_{e,\sigma,r}^*A_{e,\sigma,r}=I,
\]
where $\Pi_+,\Pi_-$ are orthogonal and sum to the identity.  Put
\[
 Q_\sigma=I\otimes\Pi_\sigma\otimes I,
 \qquad
 Z_{\rm ph}=Q_+-Q_-.
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{
 \sum_{e,r}A_{e,\sigma,r}^*A_{e,\sigma,r}=Q_\sigma.}
\]
For the opportunity Kraus operators
$L_{e,\sigma,r}=\sqrt\vartheta A_{e,\sigma,r}$, the two physical sign effects
are
\[
 \boxed{
 E_\sigma^{\rm phys}=\vartheta Q_\sigma,
 \qquad
 h_{\rm phys}=\vartheta I,
 \qquad
 d_{\rm phys}=\vartheta Z_{\rm ph}.}
\]
Consequently the normalized binary contrast is exactly
\[
 \boxed{
 h_{\rm phys}^{-1/2}d_{\rm phys}h_{\rm phys}^{-1/2}=Z_{\rm ph},
 \qquad Z_{\rm ph}^2=I.}
\]
After conditioning on acceptance, the sign Read is the sharp projective Read
$(Q_+,Q_-)$.  In the minimal twenty-four-dimensional Stinespring environment,
if $P_\pm$ denote the two twelve-label coordinate projections and
$S=P_+-P_-$, the aggregated sign effects satisfy
\[
 F_\pm^{\rm env}
 =\vartheta M_\vartheta^{-1/2}P_\pm M_\vartheta^{-1/2},
\]
\[
 \boxed{
 h_{\rm env}^{-1/2}
 (F_+^{\rm env}-F_-^{\rm env})
 h_{\rm env}^{-1/2}=S,}
 \qquad h_{\rm env}=\vartheta M_\vartheta^{-1},
\]
and
\[
 \boxed{
 \frac{\vartheta}{12-11\vartheta}I
 \preceq h_{\rm env}\preceq I.}
\]
Thus the nonorthogonality of the minimal outcome frame changes the total
accepted-likelihood metric but not the normalized sign.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Every branch of sign $\sigma$ is supported in the $Q_\sigma$ corner.
Multiplying the total normalization on both sides by $Q_\sigma$ gives the first
identity.  Multiplication by $\vartheta$ gives the physical effects, and their
sum and difference give $h_{\rm phys}$ and $d_{\rm phys}$.

For the environment statement, sum the rank-one effects of
\Cref{thm:locked-opportunity-instrument} over the twelve labels of each sign.
Since $P_++P_-=I$,
\[
 h_{\rm env}=\vartheta M_\vartheta^{-1},
 \qquad
 F_+^{\rm env}-F_-^{\rm env}
 =\vartheta M_\vartheta^{-1/2}SM_\vartheta^{-1/2}.
\]
Conjugation by $h_{\rm env}^{-1/2}=\vartheta^{-1/2}M_\vartheta^{1/2}$ gives
$S$.  Finally
\[
 M_\vartheta
 =\vartheta(I-P_c)+(12-11\vartheta)P_c
\]
by \Cref{cor:locked-opportunity-contrast-spectrum}; inversion gives the stated
likelihood window.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Fixed positive sign-information rate]
\label{cor:SMST-sign-information-rate}
Let an accepted sign experiment have Fisher form $\mathbb I_{\rm acc}$, and
suppose acceptance occurs independently of the tangent parameter with
probability $\vartheta$.  Then the opportunity and raw-time Fisher forms are
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathbb I_{\rm opp}=\vartheta\mathbb I_{\rm acc},
 \qquad
 \mathbb I_{\rm time}=\frac4{11}\vartheta\mathbb I_{\rm acc}.}
\]
Thus the rarity of the synchronized response changes the information rate but
cannot collapse a positive accepted-sign frame.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The rejected branch has parameter-independent likelihood and therefore zero
score.  On an accepted branch the full score is the accepted conditional
score, while its probability is multiplied by $\vartheta$; Fisher information
is therefore multiplied by $\vartheta$.  The completed-private opportunities
occur at asymptotic raw-time rate $4/11$ by
\Cref{thm:completed-private-renewal}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[The acceptance bit is the unique state-independent likelihood coordinate]
\label{cor:acceptance-likelihood}
Suppose the same Kraus directions are exponentially reweighted by real scores
$s_\varnothing,s_j$ and normalized by one scalar partition function on a
nonempty open interval.  Then all accepted scores are equal.  Modulo a common
additive constant and parameter rescaling, the unique nonconstant score is
$s(\varnothing)=0$, $s(j)=1$.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The partition operator is
$(1-\vartheta)e^{qs_\varnothing}I+
\vartheta\sum_je^{qs_j}A_j^*A_j$.  It is scalar for an interval of $q$.
Differentiating repeatedly at one point and using linear independence of the
accepted effects forces all coefficients $e^{qs_j}$, hence all $s_j$, to be
equal.  The converse is immediate from $\sum_jA_j^*A_j=I$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Exact accepted-response renewal and source-native coarse gap]
\label{thm:accepted-response-renewal}
Assume a fresh copy of \Cref{def:locked-opportunity-instrument} is applied at
every completed-private opportunity.  Accepted marks are iid
Bernoulli$(\vartheta)$ and independent of the inter-opportunity durations.
If $T$ is the raw time between accepted responses, then
\[
 \boxed{
 F_T(z)
 =\frac{\vartheta F_W(z)}{1-(1-\vartheta)F_W(z)}
 =\frac{8\vartheta z^2}{15-8z+(8\vartheta-7)z^2},}
\]
\[
 \boxed{\mathbb ET=\frac{11}{4\vartheta},
 \qquad
 p_{\rm resp}=\frac4{11}\vartheta
 =\frac{52441}{104485552128}.}
\]
The survivor generating function is
\[
 \boxed{
 \sum_{n\ge0}\Pr(T>n)z^n
 =\frac{15+7z}{15-8z+(8\vartheta-7)z^2}.}
\]
If an accepted response applies an idempotent conditional expectation
$\mathcal R$, while rejection applies the identity, then at opportunity count
$N$ and raw time $n$ respectively,
\[
 \boxed{
 \Phi_{\rm opp}^N
 =\mathcal R+(1-\vartheta)^N(I-\mathcal R),
 \qquad
 \mathcal T_n
 =\mathcal R+\Pr(T>n)(I-\mathcal R).}
\]
Thus the selected Store has an exact autonomous coarse renewal and a positive
fixed-source response-tail exponent.  Regulator-uniformity still requires
uniform cutoff bounds on the opportunity law and $\vartheta_X$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The scalar accepted effect $\vartheta I$ makes the acceptance probability
$\vartheta$ after every resolved past; using a fresh opportunity environment
makes the marks iid and independent of $W$.  The number of opportunities until
acceptance is geometric, so the generating function is the geometric random
sum of iid $W$'s.  Differentiation at one gives the mean and renewal-rate
multiplication gives $p_{\rm resp}$.  The survivor transform is
$(1-F_T(z))/(1-z)$ and simplifies to the displayed rational function.  Since
$\mathcal R^2=\mathcal R$, a trajectory on which at least one acceptance has
occurred contributes $\mathcal R$, while a survivor contributes the identity.
Conditioning on these two events gives both channel formulas.
\end{proof}


% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
\subsubsection{Renewal pressure and the exact accepted-response continuum}
\label{sec:renewal-pressure-phase}
% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

The accepted-response process carries more than a positive tail exponent.  Once
its duration and accepted-count writers are retained, its normalization defines
an intrinsic renewal pressure and fixes the affine action unit.  The fast
active-phase contrast can then be shorted explicitly rather than treated as an
unknown regulator memory.

\begin{theorem}[Accepted-response renewal pressure]
\label{thm:accepted-response-pressure}
Let $T_\vartheta$ be the accepted-response interarrival time of
\Cref{thm:accepted-response-renewal}, let one protected tick have physical
duration $h>0$, and assign unit reward to one accepted response.  The
operator-valued tilted first-return effect is
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathsf H_{\vartheta,h}(q,r)
 =e^{-q}F_{T_\vartheta}(e^{-hr})I.}
\]
Hence there is a unique analytic pressure $\mathcal P_{\vartheta,h}$ near the
origin satisfying
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathsf H_{\vartheta,h}
 \bigl(q,\mathcal P_{\vartheta,h}(q)\bigr)=I.}
\]
Put
\[
 A_\vartheta(q)=7+8\vartheta(e^{-q}-1).
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{
 e^{-h\mathcal P_{\vartheta,h}(q)}
 =\frac{-8+\sqrt{64+60A_\vartheta(q)}}{2A_\vartheta(q)},}
\]
with the continuous value at a removable zero of $A_\vartheta$, and
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal P_{\vartheta,h}'(0)
 =-\frac{4\vartheta}{11h},
 \qquad
 -h\,\mathbb ET_\vartheta\,
 \mathcal P_{\vartheta,h}'(0)=1.}
\]
If $h\downarrow0$ and $\vartheta_h/h\to a\in(0,\infty)$, then locally
uniformly for $q$ near zero,
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal P_{\vartheta_h,h}(q)
 \longrightarrow \frac{4a}{11}(e^{-q}-1).}
\]
Thus the concrete accepted-response count supplies a source-independent
partition anchor and converges to the Poisson pressure with intensity
$4a/11$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
At each completed-private opportunity the total accepted effect is
$\vartheta I$.  Independence of the fresh opportunity environment and the
completed-private duration therefore makes the effect of first acceptance at
raw time $n$ equal to $\Pr(T_\vartheta=n)I$.  Summing the tilted effects gives
the first formula, so the scalar pressure equation normalizes the instrument
for every boundary input.

Substitution of the rational generating function in
\Cref{thm:accepted-response-renewal} gives, with
$z=e^{-h\mathcal P_{\vartheta,h}(q)}$,
\[
 A_\vartheta(q)z^2+8z-15=0.
\]
The displayed root is the unique branch with $z(0)=1$.  Differentiating
$e^{-q}F_{T_\vartheta}(e^{-h\mathcal P(q)})=1$ at zero and using
$F_{T_\vartheta}'(1)=\mathbb ET_\vartheta=11/(4\vartheta)$ gives the pressure
derivative and the anchor identity.

If $\vartheta_h/h\to a$, then for $p$ in a fixed compact neighborhood of zero,
\[
 F_{T_{\vartheta_h}}(e^{-hp})
 \longrightarrow
 \frac{4a/11}{4a/11+p}
\]
locally uniformly.  The limiting pressure equation is
$e^{-q}\lambda/(\lambda+p)=1$, with $\lambda=4a/11$, whose unique local root
is $p=\lambda(e^{-q}-1)$.  Uniform implicit-function stability gives the
claimed convergence.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Exact shorting of the intrinsic renewal phase]
\label{thm:accepted-phase-feedback}
Let $\mathcal R$ be an orthogonal state-preserving conditional expectation on
a payload GNS space.  Rejection applies the identity and acceptance applies
$\mathcal R$.  With
\[
 Q_0=\begin{pmatrix}1/5&4/5\\0&1/3\end{pmatrix},
 \qquad
 \mathsf C_0=\begin{pmatrix}0&0\\2/3&0\end{pmatrix},
 \qquad M_0=Q_0+\mathsf C_0,
\]
the exact phase--payload tick transfer is
\[
 \mathbb M_\vartheta
 =M_0\otimes I-\vartheta\mathsf C_0\otimes(I-\mathcal R).
\]
Relative to the stationary phase line and its normalized contrast, its blocks
are
\[
 \boxed{
 A_\vartheta=I-\frac{4\vartheta}{11}(I-\mathcal R),}
\]
\[
 \boxed{
 B_\vartheta=\frac{24\vartheta}{11\sqrt{30}}(I-\mathcal R),
 \qquad
 C_\vartheta=-\frac{20\vartheta}{11\sqrt{30}}(I-\mathcal R),}
\]
\[
 \boxed{
 D_\vartheta=-\frac7{15}I+\frac{4\vartheta}{11}(I-\mathcal R).}
\]
The returned kernels through the fast phase are
\[
 \boxed{
 B_\vartheta D_\vartheta^kC_\vartheta
 =-\frac{16\vartheta^2}{121}
 \left(-\frac7{15}+\frac{4\vartheta}{11}\right)^k
 (I-\mathcal R),}
\]
and satisfy
\[
 \boxed{
 \sum_{k\ge0}\|B_\vartheta D_\vartheta^kC_\vartheta\|
 \le\frac{30}{121}\vartheta^2.}
\]
For the pressure-derived model step
\[
 W_{\vartheta,h}
 =\mathcal R+e^{-4\vartheta/11}(I-\mathcal R),
\]
one has
\[
 \boxed{
 \|A_\vartheta-W_{\vartheta,h}\|
 \le\frac8{121}\vartheta^2.}
\]
Consequently, if $\vartheta_h/h$ remains bounded,
\[
 \frac{\|A_{\vartheta_h}-W_{\vartheta_h,h}\|}{h}\to0,
 \qquad
 \frac1h\sum_{k\ge0}
 \|B_{\vartheta_h}D_{\vartheta_h}^kC_{\vartheta_h}\|\to0.
\]
If $\vartheta_h/h\to a$, the stationary-head compression converges uniformly
on compact physical-time intervals to
\[
 \boxed{
 e^{(4a/11)t(\mathcal R-I)}.}
\]
Thus the primitive temporal renewal backbone lies on a memoryless,
non-Zeno positive continuum branch; any surviving returned kernel is produced
by a genuinely loaded interacting regulator.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
In the stationary inner product of $M_0$, the constant vector and the normalized
contrast $\varphi=(-6,5)/\sqrt{30}$ form an orthonormal basis and
$M_0\varphi=-(7/15)\varphi$.  Direct evaluation of the four matrix coefficients
of $\mathsf C_0$ gives
\[
 \left\langle\one,\mathsf C_0\one\right\rangle=\frac4{11},
 \quad
 \left\langle\one,\mathsf C_0\varphi\right\rangle
 =-\frac{24}{11\sqrt{30}},
\]
\[
 \left\langle\varphi,\mathsf C_0\one\right\rangle
 =\frac{20}{11\sqrt{30}},
 \quad
 \left\langle\varphi,\mathsf C_0\varphi\right\rangle=-\frac4{11}.
\]
Substitution yields the displayed blocks.  Since $I-\mathcal R$ is a
projection, it commutes with all four blocks and the returned-kernel formula is
scalar.  The ratio has modulus at most $7/15$, so summing the geometric series
gives the stated bound.

On $\Ran\mathcal R$ the direct and model steps are both the identity; on
$\Ker\mathcal R$ their multipliers are $1-x$ and $e^{-x}$ with
$x=4\vartheta/11$.  Taylor's theorem gives
$0\le e^{-x}-(1-x)\le x^2/2$.  The two normalized limits follow from
$\vartheta_h=O(h)$.  The finite-time feedback estimate in
\Cref{thm:universal-feedback-memory} then gives compact-time agreement with the
powers of $W_{\vartheta_h,h}$, whose scalar transient multiplier converges to
$e^{-(4a/11)t}$.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[The count anchor is not the complete physical action]
The accepted count calibrates one affine action unit.  A gravitational,
matter, gauge, potential, counterterm, or boundary reward generally fluctuates
within an accepted cycle and therefore has a nonzero count-shorted covariance.
The complete action must be reconstructed from its own protected vector reward
on the resolved cycle record, as in \Cref{thm:reward-pressure-reconstruction}.
\end{firewall}

\begin{countertheorem}[A coarse pinching does not identify the fine score basis]
\label{cth:coarse-score-basis}
Let $P_\pm=(I\pm Z)/2$.  The L\"uders instrument
$\rho\mapsto P_\pm\rho P_\pm$ and the fair phase instrument
$\rho\mapsto\frac12U_\pm\rho U_\pm^*$,
$U_\pm=e^{\mp i\pi Z/4}$, have the same coarse channel
$\frac12(\rho+Z\rho Z)$ but different resolved outcome laws.  Hence the
coarse collision does not identify a physical score bit or its environment
basis.
\end{countertheorem}

\begin{proof}
Summing the L\"uders branches gives dephasing.  Expanding
$U_\pm=2^{-1/2}(I\mp iZ)$ and summing cancels the cross terms and gives the
same channel.  On an input supported in $P_+$, the L\"uders law is $(1,0)$,
whereas each phase outcome has probability $1/2$.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Renewal-native closure and the downstream loading boundary}
\label{sec:renewal-native-closure}

The completed-private renewal mechanism does not require the later edge,
charge, portal, or Standard-Model interpretation of the synchronized response.
Those labels may be loaded on top of the same renewal process, but they cannot
be used as hidden premises for renewal itself.

\begin{theorem}[Semantic stripping of the renewal packet]
\label{thm:renewal-semantic-stripping}
Let $\mathfrak P_X^{\rm ren}$ consist only of the shared-edge continuation,
completed-private boundary, active phase, fresh endpoint, and protected private
provenance histories.  Any extension by charge, $K_4$, edge-orbit, portal, or
matter labels which leaves all renewal-native probabilities unchanged is a
conservative domain loading.  Consequently failure or nonuniqueness of such a
loading cannot invalidate the renewal process reconstructed from
$\mathfrak P_X^{\rm ren}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Restriction of the enlarged operational table to the renewal-native alphabet
is the original table, so the minimal record, Hankel quotient, branch maps, and
first-return law on that alphabet are unchanged by the uniqueness theorems of
Part~I.  Conversely one may tensor any renewal realization with inequivalent
finite charge or portal systems on which the renewal letters act trivially;
all renewal-native probabilities remain equal.  Hence the additional semantics
are neither necessary nor determined by the renewal packet.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Exact minimal two-state active renewal]
\label{thm:two-state-active-renewal}
In the ordered active phase basis $(H,P)$, the no-boundary transfer and
completion effect are
\[
 Q_0=\begin{pmatrix}1/5&4/5\\0&1/3\end{pmatrix},
 \qquad
 r_0=\begin{pmatrix}0\\2/3\end{pmatrix},
 \qquad
 \alpha=(1,0).
\]
Completion resets the active phase to $H$ and writes an independent fair
endpoint $h\in\{0,1\}$.  The recurrent transition is
\[
 \boxed{M_0=Q_0+r_0\alpha
 =\begin{pmatrix}1/5&4/5\\2/3&1/3\end{pmatrix}.}
\]
The first-return transform and survivor law are
\[
 \boxed{F_W(z)=z\alpha(I-zQ_0)^{-1}r_0
 =\frac{8z^2}{(5-z)(3-z)},}
\]
\[
 \boxed{\Pr(W>N)=6\,3^{-N}-5\,5^{-N}.}
\]
The active linear predictive dimension is exactly two.  The recurrent chain is
reversible with
\[
 \boxed{\pi=(5/11,6/11),\qquad
 \operatorname{spec}M_0=\{1,-7/15\},}
\]
so
\[
 \boxed{
 \|M_0^n-\Pi_\pi\|_{L^2(\pi)\to L^2(\pi)}=(7/15)^n,\qquad
 \operatorname{cond}(\diag\pi)=6/5.}
\]
For any two phase laws,
\[
 \boxed{\|\mu M_0^n-\nu M_0^n\|_{\rm TV}
 =(7/15)^n\|\mu-\nu\|_{\rm TV}.}
\]
The stationary completed-boundary flux is $4/11$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The rows of $Q_0$ are the no-boundary probabilities of staying at the hub,
entering the private phase, and remaining private.  The missing private mass
$2/3$ is the completed boundary and the reset row is $\alpha$.  The standard
phase-type first-return formula gives the displayed rational transform; partial
fractions give the survivor law.  Since $W\ge2$, the first survivor values are
$s_0=s_1=1$ and $s_2=7/15$, so
$\det\begin{psmallmatrix}s_0&s_1\\s_1&s_2\end{psmallmatrix}=-8/15\ne0$.
The Hankel rank is therefore at least two, while the displayed phase
realization gives rank at most two.

Solving $\pi M_0=\pi$ gives $\pi=(5/11,6/11)$; detailed balance is
$(5/11)(4/5)=(6/11)(2/3)$.  The second eigenvalue is the trace minus one,
$-7/15$.  A reversible two-state chain acts by this scalar on the mean-zero
line, giving the $L^2$ and total-variation identities.  The stationary event
flux is $\pi_P(2/3)=4/11$, and the metric condition number is
$(6/11)/(5/11)=6/5$.
\end{proof}


% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
\subsection{Protected ticks and the positive physical-time lift}
\label{sec:renewal-physical-time-lift}
% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

The recurrent matrix $M_0$ is the exact transfer per protected primitive tick.
It is not itself a deterministic positive-time step of a continuous-time
Markov chain.  Physical time must therefore be introduced at the scheduler
level rather than by taking a matrix logarithm of the tick transfer.

\begin{countertheorem}[Non-embeddability of the discrete recurrent step]
\label{cth:discrete-renewal-nonembeddable}
There are no $\tau>0$ and real two-state Markov generator $L$ such that
\[
 \boxed{M_0=e^{\tau L}.}
\]
Indeed every positive-time two-state Markov transition has a strictly positive
second eigenvalue, while $M_0$ has second eigenvalue $-7/15$.
\end{countertheorem}

\begin{proof}
Every two-state Markov generator has the form
\[
 L=\begin{pmatrix}-\alpha&\alpha\\ \beta&-\beta\end{pmatrix},
 \qquad \alpha,\beta\ge0.
\]
Its eigenvalues are $0$ and $-(\alpha+\beta)$, so $e^{\tau L}$ has eigenvalues
$1$ and $e^{-(\alpha+\beta)\tau}>0$.  This contradicts
$\spec M_0=\{1,-7/15\}$.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Poisson-uniformized renewal instrument]
\label{def:renewal-uniformization}
Let protected discrete opportunities occur at the jump times of a Poisson
process of rate $\lambda>0$, and apply one fresh copy of the resolved renewal
instrument at each opportunity.  The coarse continuous-time generator is
\[
 \boxed{L_0=\lambda(M_0-I).}
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Canonical positive continuous-time lift]
\label{thm:renewal-uniformization}
The generator of \Cref{def:renewal-uniformization} is
\[
 \boxed{
 L_0=\begin{pmatrix}
 -4\lambda/5&4\lambda/5\\[0.15em]
 2\lambda/3&-2\lambda/3
 \end{pmatrix}.}
\]
It has stationary law $\pi=(5/11,6/11)$ and semigroup
\[
 \boxed{
 e^{tL_0}=\Pi_\pi+e^{-gt}(I-\Pi_\pi),
 \qquad g=\frac{22\lambda}{15}.}
\]
Thus the exact physical relaxation rate of the uniformized process is
$22\lambda/15$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Subtracting the identity from $M_0$ gives the displayed generator with rates
$4\lambda/5$ and $2\lambda/3$.  Their detailed-balance stationary law is
$(5/11,6/11)$, and the mean-zero eigenvalue is the negative sum of the two
rates.  Spectral decomposition gives the semigroup.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Continuous completion time and physical event intensity]
\label{thm:renewal-continuous-completion}
Starting immediately after a completion, the physical time $\mathcal T$ to the
next completion satisfies
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal T\ \stackrel d=
 \operatorname{Exp}(4\lambda/5)
 +\operatorname{Exp}(2\lambda/3),}
\]
with independent summands.  Equivalently,
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathbb E[e^{-s\mathcal T}]
 =F_W\!\left(\frac{\lambda}{\lambda+s}\right)
 =\frac{8\lambda^2}{(4\lambda+5s)(2\lambda+3s)}.}
\]
Consequently
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathbb E\mathcal T=\frac{11}{4\lambda},
 \qquad j_{\rm phys}=\frac{4\lambda}{11}.}
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Poisson thinning makes the first $H\to P$ event exponential of rate
$4\lambda/5$ and, after entry, makes the first completion event exponential of
rate $2\lambda/3$.  Strong-Markov freshness gives independence.  Alternatively,
conditional on $W=k$, the elapsed physical time is an Erlang sum of $k$
rate-$\lambda$ exponentials, which gives the substituted generating function.
The mean and intensity follow immediately.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Uniformization gauge and the protected-clock boundary]
\label{thm:renewal-uniformization-gauge}
For a fixed continuous generator
\[
 L_{\alpha,\beta}=
 \begin{pmatrix}-\alpha&\alpha\\ \beta&-\beta\end{pmatrix},
\]
every rate $\Lambda\ge\max\{\alpha,\beta\}$ gives a stochastic kernel
\[
 K^{(\Lambda)}=I+\Lambda^{-1}L_{\alpha,\beta}
\]
whose Poisson uniformization has the same semigroup $e^{tL_{\alpha,\beta}}$.
Hence discrete self-loop probabilities are invariants only when the primitive
opportunity clock is itself protected and readable.  Below an unprotected
clock, the intrinsic data are the continuous rates up to physical time scale,
not a preferred uniformization.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The stated lower bound on $\Lambda$ makes $K^{(\Lambda)}$ stochastic, and
$\Lambda(K^{(\Lambda)}-I)=L_{\alpha,\beta}$.  Distinct $\Lambda$ therefore
produce different tick kernels but the same continuous semigroup.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[The tick transfer and the continuum clock are distinct layers]
The logarithm of $M_0$ is not a real Markov generator.  Blocking an even
number of ticks removes the sign obstruction but does not supply a shrinking
physical step or prevent a Zeno limit.  The protected-tick theorem and the
positive continuous-time lift must therefore be stated separately.
\end{firewall}


% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
\subsection{Intrinsic reset boundary and positive phase selection}
\label{sec:intrinsic-renewal-boundary}
% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

\begin{theorem}[Atomic-reset characterization]
\label{thm:atomic-reset-characterization}
Let $R:V\to W$ be a nonzero positive branch between finite ordered spaces with
generating cones.  The following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.8em]
\item every normalized positive input on which the branch occurs has the same
      normalized output;
\item there are a nonzero positive functional $\ell$ and one normalized
      $\omega\in W_+$ such that
      \[
       \boxed{R(x)=\ell(x)\omega;}
      \]
\item $\rank R=1$.
\end{enumerate}
For a completely positive matrix-algebra branch,
$R(X)=\Tr(EX)\omega$ for a unique positive input effect $E$ after fixing
$\Tr\omega=1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
If every positive input is mapped into one output ray, linearity and generation
of $V$ by its cone put the full range of $R$ in that ray.  Since $R\ne0$, the
rank is one, and $\ell=u_W\circ R$ gives the atomic form.  Conversely the
atomic form is manifestly decoupling and rank one.  A nonzero positive rank-one
map has a positive factorization after a simultaneous sign choice.  On a
matrix algebra, positive functionals are exactly $X\mapsto\Tr(EX)$, and the
resulting Choi operator $E^{\mathsf T}\otimes\omega$ is positive.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[The completed-private mark is the first predictive reset]
\label{thm:completed-boundary-decoupling}
Let $R_h=\frac12r_0\alpha$, $h\in\{0,1\}$, be the two endpoint-resolved
completion branches of the concrete renewal packet.  Then:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.8em]
\item each $R_h$ is a nonzero atomic reset with normalized output $\alpha$;
\item $R_0=R_1=R/2$, so the completed endpoint is a fresh fair mark;
\item every pure survivor $Q_0^n$, $n\ge1$, has rank two;
\item every first-completion word $Q_0^{n-1}R_h$, $n\ge2$, is nonzero and rank
      one with normalized output $\alpha$.
\end{enumerate}
Consequently the first completed-private mark is exactly the first
source-decoupling event relative to the passive event/no-event interface; no
earlier survivor prefix erases the active phase.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The completion formula gives
$R_h\mu=\frac12(\mu r_0)\alpha$, proving the first two claims.  Since
$\det Q_0=1/15$, every survivor power is invertible.  Finally,
$Q_0^{n-1}R_h=\frac12(Q_0^{n-1}r_0)\alpha$ is nonzero rank one for
$n\ge2$.
\end{proof}

The scalar first-return law does not by itself select the orientation or the
absence of pre-completion backtracking.

\begin{theorem}[Complete positive two-state quotient family]
\label{thm:positive-renewal-quotient-family}
Let
\[
 Q=\begin{pmatrix}a&1-a\\ c&d\end{pmatrix},
 \qquad
 r=\begin{pmatrix}0\\1-c-d\end{pmatrix}
\]
be an anchored positive two-state no-completion transfer, with completion
impossible at the first tick.  Its first-return transform equals
\[
 \frac{8z^2}{(5-z)(3-z)}
\]
exactly for
\[
 \boxed{\frac15\le a\le\frac13,}
\]
with
\[
 \boxed{
 d(a)=\frac8{15}-a,
 \qquad
 c(a)=\frac{(5a-1)(1-3a)}{15(1-a)},
 \qquad
 r_P(a)=\frac8{15(1-a)}.}
\]
Every member is reachable and future separated and has
\[
 \spec Q(a)=\left\{\frac15,\frac13\right\}.
\]
The recurrent reset chain has nontrivial eigenvalue $-7/15$ and stationary
completion flux $4/11$ for every $a$ in the interval.  The serial primitives
$c(a)=0$ are exactly the two endpoints.

More generally, any finite positive first-return model whose minimal ordered
predictive quotient has a proper generating cone and positive mass functional
has a two-dimensional quotient of this form.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Direct inversion gives
\[
 F_Q(z)=
 \frac{z^2(1-a)(1-c-d)}
 {1-(a+d)z+(ad-(1-a)c)z^2}.
\]
Comparison with
$(8/15)z^2/[1-(8/15)z+(1/15)z^2]$ yields
$a+d=8/15$, $(1-a)(1-c-d)=8/15$, and
$ad-(1-a)c=1/15$.  Solving gives the displayed formulas.  Nonnegativity of
$c$ is equivalent to $(5a-1)(1-3a)\ge0$, hence to the stated interval; the
other positivity conditions then follow.  The trace and determinant of $Q(a)$
are $8/15$ and $1/15$.  A two-state stochastic reset chain has second
eigenvalue trace minus one, hence $-7/15$, and direct solution of the stationary
law gives flux $4/11$.

The target first-return sequence has scalar Hankel rank two because its
rational denominator has degree two and its leading $2\times2$ Hankel minor is
nonzero.  A minimal positive quotient therefore has dimension two.  Its
initial source lies on an extreme ray because the nonzero completion
functional vanishes on it at the first tick.  A proper cone in two dimensions
is simplicial; normalizing its two extreme rays gives the anchored form above.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Resolved phase and back-transition selection]
\label{cor:resolved-phase-selection}
Within \Cref{thm:positive-renewal-quotient-family}, the probability of reading
$H$ after the first no-completion tick is $a$, and the pre-completion
transition probability $P\to H$ is $c(a)$.  The concrete resolved renewal
selects
\[
 \boxed{a=\frac15,\qquad c=0,}
\]
and therefore uniquely recovers $Q_0$ and $r_0$.  If seriality is independently
known, the two scalar orientations are separated by $2/15$; without a
back-transition certificate there is no positive isolation margin from the
interior family.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The two claims are the upper-left and lower-left entries of $Q(a)$.  Substituting
$a=1/5$ gives $d=1/3$, $c=0$, and $r_P=2/3$.  The equation $c(a)=0$ has only
the two endpoint solutions $a=1/5,1/3$, while interior values approach either
endpoint continuously.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Exact active no-routing]
\label{thm:active-private-no-routing}
Let $J_X^{\rm priv}$ synthesize contrasts in the retained old private record and
let $C_X^{\rm act}$ collect all later active recurrent Reads.  For the concrete
renewal source,
\[
 \boxed{C_X^{\rm act}J_X^{\rm priv}=0,
 \qquad
 (J_X^{\rm priv})^*(C_X^{\rm act})^*C_X^{\rm act}J_X^{\rm priv}=0.}
\]
Thus old private information may survive in the full provenance tensor but adds
no active recurrent predictive coordinate.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
After the completed-private cut, every active future factors through the fresh
hub phase and endpoint and acts as the identity on, or discards, the old private
factor.  Hence every pure private contrast lies in the kernel of every later
active Read.  The Gram identity is the squared norm of this composite map.
\end{proof}

% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
\subsection{Coherent endpoint extensions and their intrinsic defect}
\label{sec:endpoint-coherence-defect}
% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

The fresh endpoint theorem is diagonal: it fixes the endpoint probabilities
and their independence from the old active/private label.  A physical
operation may nevertheless retain or destroy endpoint superpositions.  Once a
classical endpoint population is nondemolished, the remaining ambiguity has a
canonical contraction coordinate.

\begin{theorem}[Canonical endpoint-coherence defect]
\label{thm:endpoint-coherence-defect}
Let $E\cong\C^2$ and let a finite channel have a minimal Stinespring isometry
whose Heisenberg action fixes $Z_E\otimes I$.  Then, after one output
identification,
\[
 \boxed{V=P_0\otimes V_0+P_1\otimes V_1}
\]
for isometries $V_0,V_1$.  Put
\[
 \boxed{C_{\rm end}=V_0^*V_1,\qquad
 \mathbb D_{\rm end}=I-C_{\rm end}^*C_{\rm end}\succeq0.}
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{
 V_1=V_0C_{\rm end}+L_{\rm end},
 \qquad
 V_0^*L_{\rm end}=0,
 \qquad
 L_{\rm end}^*L_{\rm end}=\mathbb D_{\rm end}.}
\]
The minimal joint carrier of the two endpoint sheets is canonically
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal H\oplus\Ran\mathbb D_{\rm end}^{1/2},}
\]
with source isometries
\[
 J_0x=(x,0),
 \qquad
 J_1x=(C_{\rm end}x,\mathbb D_{\rm end}^{1/2}x).
\]
Its excess dimension is $\rank\mathbb D_{\rm end}$.  The endpoint is fully
nondemolished exactly when $C_{\rm end}=I$; it is completely dephased exactly
when $C_{\rm end}=0$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Fixing the two spectral projections of $Z_E$ puts them in the multiplicative
domain, forcing the controlled Stinespring form.  The overlap of the two
isometries is a contraction.  Orthogonal projection of $V_1$ onto
$\Ran V_0$ gives $V_0C_{\rm end}$; the orthogonal remainder is
$L_{\rm end}=(I-V_0V_0^*)V_1$, and direct multiplication gives
$L_{\rm end}^*L_{\rm end}=I-C_{\rm end}^*C_{\rm end}$.  The displayed
canonical pair has the same Gram
$\begin{psmallmatrix}I&C_{\rm end}\\C_{\rm end}^*&I\end{psmallmatrix}$.
Any other minimal pair with this Gram is related by the unique source-fixing
unitary.  The endpoint identities follow from the overlap extremes.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Symmetry localization of endpoint memory]
\label{cor:endpoint-defect-symmetry}
If one physical group action naturalizes both endpoint sheets, then
$C_{\rm end}$ commutes with the payload representation.  For
\[
 \mathcal H=\bigoplus_\pi V_\pi\otimes M_\pi,
\]
one has
\[
 \boxed{
 C_{\rm end}=\bigoplus_\pi I_{V_\pi}\otimes C_\pi,}
\]
so every coherent defect lies in multiplicity spaces.  On an irreducible
payload, $C_{\rm end}=cI$ and the complete transverse endpoint response is one
complex visibility $c$.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Naturality gives
$(R_g\otimes W_g)V_h=V_hU_g$ for both $h$.  Taking the cross product of the
two equations gives $U_g^*C_{\rm end}U_g=C_{\rm end}$.  The commutant
decomposition and the irreducible specialization are Schur's lemma.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Intrinsic record selected by an endpoint defect]
\label{thm:endpoint-defect-record}
Let
\[
 \mathbb D_{\rm end}=\sum_{a=1}^{q}\delta_aP_a
\]
be the decomposition into distinct positive eigenvalues.  The finest sharp
record invariant under every unitary commuting with
$\mathbb D_{\rm end}$ is the spectral PVM $(P_1,\ldots,P_q)$.  No basis inside
a degenerate eigenspace is intrinsic.  In particular, if
$\mathbb D_{\rm end}=\delta I$ on a nontrivial irreducible sector, the defect
contains no nontrivial basis-free classical point record.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
A projection invariant under the full commutant unitary group of a
self-adjoint operator must belong to the center of its commutant, which is the
algebra generated by the distinct spectral projections.  Its projections are
therefore sums of the $P_a$.  Degenerate eigenspaces carry full unitary groups,
which fix no finer rank decomposition.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[The old private overlap does not determine endpoint coherence]
\label{fire:endpoint-private-nonidentifiability}
The calibrated private overlap $1/5$ in
\Cref{cor:private-provenance-fingerprint} does not force
$C_{\rm end}=1/5$.  For every contraction $C$ one may tensor the completed
reset with the canonical pair
$(x,0)$ and $(Cx,(I-C^*C)^{1/2}x)$ and discard the auxiliary output.  The old
renewal probabilities, the fresh endpoint marginal, and the private Gram are
unchanged while the endpoint coherence is $C$.  Identification of the endpoint
defect with old private provenance, a half-edge source, or any other candidate
therefore requires their mixed source Gram and the mutual Schur residuals of
\Cref{thm:joint-source-short}.
\end{firewall}

\begin{definition}[Downstream synchronized Store-loading residual]
\label{def:primitive-phase-residual}
On top of the exact renewal-native process, and only when the downstream synchronized edge/order/charge loading is claimed, define:
\begin{align*}
 \Delta_{\rm exh,X}&=\|(I-P_{BC/CB})C_{\rm odd}\|_{\HS}^2,\\
 \Delta_{\rm lock,X}&=\sum_{\sigma,m}
 \|E_{\sigma,m}-\delta_{m,\mu(\sigma)}\Pi_\sigma\|_{\HS}^2,\\
 \Delta_{\rm mult,X}&=\sum_\lambda\sigma_2(H_{\lambda,X})^2,\\
 \Delta_{\rm rev,X}&=\|G_{\rm fwd,X}-G_{\rm rev,X}\|_{\HS}^2,\\
 \Delta_{\rm edge,X}&=\sum_{g,e}
 \|U_gE_eU_g^*-E_{g\cdot e}\|_{\HS}^2,\\
 \Delta_{\rm cov,X}&=\sum_{g,e}
 \|Z_gA_eU_g^*-A_{g\cdot e}\|_{\HS}^2,\\
 \Delta_{\rm ad,X}&=|b_X|^2,
\end{align*}
where the terms respectively test odd-word exhaustion, order--pointer locking,
multiplicity-one typed ports, normalized reversal, stopped $S_4$ edge
regeneration, charge-quartet amplitude covariance, and causal adaptedness.
Let $\Delta_{\rm writ,X}$ be the sum of squared deterministic-writer,
normalization, and exposed-point-Read relation residuals, and put
\[
 \boxed{
 \Delta_{\rm phase,X}
 :=\Delta_{\rm exh,X}+\Delta_{\rm lock,X}+\Delta_{\rm mult,X}
 +\Delta_{\rm rev,X}+\Delta_{\rm edge,X}+\Delta_{\rm cov,X}
 +\Delta_{\rm ad,X}+\Delta_{\rm writ,X}.}
\]
Let $\gamma_{\rm odd,X}$ be the least nonzero singular value of a finite
contextual Read panel detecting the signed-return odd sector.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Finite domain-enriched synchronized-interface theorem]
\label{thm:primitive-phase-selection}
Assume the renewal-native packet of
\Cref{thm:two-state-active-renewal,thm:active-private-no-routing}.  Independently
assume that the downstream edge, order, charge, and portal ports used by the
synchronized Store--Read claim are physically exposed or jointly reconstructed,
that their typed supports are nonzero, and that their declared primitive word
panel is saturated.  Then
\[
 \boxed{\gamma_{\rm odd,X}>0,
 \qquad \Delta_{\rm phase,X}=0}
\]
if and only if this additional domain-enriched packet is operationally
isomorphic to the locked twenty-five-cell synchronized Store phase, up to
minimal Stinespring coordinate changes, simultaneous exchange of the two
determinant-sign names, and irrelevant rank-one Kraus phases.  A positive term
is a concrete first-failure witness.  If a tested coordinate is not physically
exposed, the corresponding Read or environment POVM is the minimal additional
datum required to decide that term.  This theorem is not an assumption of, or
a missing step in, autonomous renewal itself.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The renewal-native theorems provide the completed-private boundary, active
phase carrier, fresh endpoint, and active no-routing, but none of the extra
edge, charge, order, or portal relations is inferred from those data.  On the
independently exposed enriched packet, a positive odd margin makes the
signed-return class nonzero in the future-separated quotient.  Zero exhaustion
residual places it in the $BC/CB$ word span.  Vanishing second singular values
and nonzero first singular values make each typed intertwiner space one
dimensional.  The stopped $S_4$ covariance and charge-amplitude covariance then
transport one nonzero rank-one branch through the full six-edge orbit with
fixed support.  Reversal fixes the common normalized boundary scale.  Locking
identifies the pointer with the order sign, adaptedness removes the unique
edge--endpoint correlation coefficient, and the writer residual fixes the
exposed classical record and total accepted effect.  A rank-one Choi operator
with fixed support and effect fixes its CP branch; Kraus phase is invisible.
These statements reconstruct the selected instrument and its only intrinsic
finite label symmetry.

Conversely, the locked synchronized instrument has the stated saturated odd
word, rank-one typed supports, reversal, covariance, adaptedness, writers, and
locking identities.  Hence every residual vanishes and its retained odd Read
has positive separation margin.  Minimal Stinespring uniqueness gives the
claimed operational isomorphism.
\end{proof}

\begin{assessment}[Where structural and renewal emergence end]
The finite structural Grand Tensor and the renewal-native two-state process are
now separate closed theorems.  The completed-private boundary, exact return law,
active predictor, fresh endpoint, stationary metric, mixing factor, and active
no-routing do not require the $K_4$/SM synchronized response.  If the locked
$25$-cell edge/order/charge table is itself operationally exposed, that loaded
subhierarchy is reconstructed unconditionally from its table.  Deriving it from
an austere source is the downstream finite loading test
$\gamma_{\rm odd,X}>0$, $\Delta_{\rm phase,X}=0$.  Horizontal finite-Dirac
first derivatives and typed matter occurrence remain later Standard-Model
source exports.
\end{assessment}

\subsection{Optional anticommuting score--dwell realization}
% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

The following exact packet is retained as an alternative physical realization.
It is not required by the finite structural theorem and is not inferred from
the source-native completed-private scheduler above.

Let $Q\cong\C^2$ be a fresh score sign, let $Z=Z^*=Z^{-1}$ act on one Store
carrier, and put
\[
 |+\rangle=\frac{|0\rangle+|1\rangle}{\sqrt2},
 \qquad
 |y_m\rangle=\frac{|0\rangle+im|1\rangle}{\sqrt2}.
\]

\begin{lemma}[One fresh score sign gives a fair dephasing collision]
\label{lem:one-clock-score-collision}
Prepare $Q$ in $|+\rangle$, apply controlled-$Z$, and resolve $Q$ in the
$y_m$ basis.  The target Kraus operators are
\[
 \boxed{K_m=\frac12(I-imZ)=\frac1{\sqrt2}e^{-im\pi Z/4},
 \qquad K_m^*K_m=\frac12I.}
\]
Forgetting the score gives
\[
 \boxed{\mathcal D_Z(X)=\frac12(X+ZXZ).}
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Contract
$2^{-1/2}(|0\rangle\otimes\psi+|1\rangle\otimes Z\psi)$ with
$\langle y_m|$ and use $Z^2=I$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Anticommuting Store-block decomposition]
\label{thm:store-block-decomposition}
If $L=L^*$ and $ZL=-LZ$, then on $(\Ker L)^\perp$ there are distinct
$\mu_j>0$ and multiplicity spaces $M_j$ such that
\[
 \boxed{
 H_{\rm nz}\cong\bigoplus_j(\C^2\otimes M_j),
 \quad Z=\bigoplus_j(\sigma_z\otimes I),
 \quad L=\bigoplus_j(\mu_j\sigma_x\otimes I),}
\]
and
\[
 \boxed{\{Z,L\}'=\bigoplus_j(I_2\otimes\mathcal B(M_j)).}
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
In the $Z$ eigenspace decomposition,
$L=\begin{psmallmatrix}0&A^*\\A&0\end{psmallmatrix}$.  Singular-value
decomposition of $A$ gives the Pauli blocks.  Commutation first with $Z$ and
then with $L$ gives the displayed commutant.
\end{proof}

For a dwell law $\nu$, put
\[
 \mathcal U_\nu(X)=\int e^{-itL}Xe^{itL}\,\nu(\dd t),
 \qquad
 \phi_\nu(\omega)=\int\cos(\omega t)\,\nu(\dd t),
 \qquad
 \mathcal R_\nu=\mathcal D_Z\mathcal U_\nu\mathcal D_Z,
\]
and
$\Omega_L=\{\mu_j+\mu_k\}_{j,k}\cup
\{|\mu_j-\mu_k|:j\ne k\}$.

\begin{theorem}[Exact score--dwell spectrum and retained algebra]
\label{thm:score-dwell-spectrum}
For a $Z$-even block from frequency $k$ to $j$, write
$X_{jk}=\diag(A_{jk},B_{jk})$,
$M_{jk}=(A_{jk}+B_{jk})/2$, and
$D_{jk}=(A_{jk}-B_{jk})/2$.  Then
\[
 \boxed{
 M_{jk}\mapsto\phi_\nu(\mu_j-\mu_k)M_{jk},
 \qquad
 D_{jk}\mapsto\phi_\nu(\mu_j+\mu_k)D_{jk}.}
\]
All $Z$-odd operators are killed.  If
$\rho_\nu=\max_{\omega\in\Omega_L}|\phi_\nu(\omega)|<1$, the fixed algebra is
$\{Z,L\}'$, and for the Hilbert--Schmidt expectation $\mathcal E_L$ onto this
algebra,
\[
 \boxed{\|\mathcal R_\nu^n-\mathcal E_L\|_{2\to2}=\rho_\nu^n.}
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
On the $j$th Pauli block,
$e^{-itL}=\begin{psmallmatrix}c_j&-is_j\\-is_j&c_j\end{psmallmatrix}$.
Conjugation followed by $\mathcal D_Z$ gives
$A'=c_jc_kA+s_js_kB$ and $B'=s_js_kA+c_jc_kB$.  Their sum and difference have
the displayed cosine frequencies.  Averaging gives the spectrum; the unit
multipliers are exactly the commutant blocks, and orthogonal diagonalization
gives the norm identity.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Exponential dwell and a uniform cutoff gap]
\label{cor:uniform-store-gap}
For $\nu_\lambda(\dd t)=\lambda e^{-\lambda t}\one_{t\ge0}\dd t$,
\[
 \phi_{\nu_\lambda}(\omega)=\frac{\lambda^2}{\lambda^2+\omega^2}.
\]
If across cutoffs the least positive frequency obeys $\delta_X\ge\delta_0>0$
and $\lambda_X\le\lambda_1$, then
\[
 \boxed{
 \|\mathcal R_X^n-\mathcal E_{L_X}\|_{2\to2}
 \le(1-\gamma_0)^n,
 \qquad
 \gamma_0=\frac{\delta_0^2}{\lambda_1^2+\delta_0^2}.}
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Direct integration gives the multiplier.  It decreases with positive
frequency and increases with $\lambda$, so the uniform bounds give the stated
maximum.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Fresh one-way transient-record sink]
\label{def:fresh-record-sink}
Let $\mathfrak F_X$ forget only a fresh score--dwell factor and act identically
on the core and minimal or physically protected record.  It is a one-way sink
when the factor is prepared independently, interacts only in the current
cycle, and no later admitted operation has an input wire from it.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Causal transient sink gives exact record nullity]
\label{thm:record-sink-nullity}
Under \Cref{def:fresh-record-sink}, every later admitted map factors uniquely
as $C_f=\overline C_f\mathfrak F_X$.  Hence for any synthesis
$J_{\rm rec}$ of pure transient contrasts,
\[
 \boxed{\mathbb G_{{\rm rec},X}
 =J_{\rm rec}^*C_X^*C_XJ_{\rm rec}=0.}
\]
Minimal readable or physically protected record projections and writers are
untouched.  Literal destruction of an inaccessible hidden copy is not implied.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The one-way wiring makes record forgetting the first operation in every later
circuit, giving the factorization.  Since
$\Ran J_{\rm rec}\subseteq\Ker\mathfrak F_X$, the composite future map and its
Gram vanish.  A hidden inaccessible copy gives the same operational table and
is therefore not excluded.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Generator-native score--dwell renewal certificate]
\label{thm:generator-native-renewal}
Suppose the actual uncontrolled process, at every declared renewal boundary,
samples $\nu_X$, autonomously applies one fresh collision of
\Cref{lem:one-clock-score-collision}, and sends only the score--dwell record to
the sink of \Cref{def:fresh-record-sink}.  Then the branches have probability
$1/2$, the retained algebra is $\{Z_X,L_X\}'$, the hidden contraction factor is
\[
 \rho_X=\max_{\omega\in\Omega_{L_X}}|\phi_{\nu_X}(\omega)|,
\]
and the transient leakage Gram is zero.  If
$\sup_X\rho_X\le1-\gamma_0<1$, the packet is regulator-uniform.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The branch effects are \Cref{lem:one-clock-score-collision}; the retained
algebra and contraction are \Cref{thm:score-dwell-spectrum}; and transient
nullity is \Cref{thm:record-sink-nullity}.  Taking the supremum gives the
uniform statement.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[Scope of the optional score--dwell packet]
The collision theorem is conditional on its actual autonomous occurrence.
Control availability alone is insufficient by
\Cref{cth:store-scheduler-no-go}.  The concrete completed-private and accepted
response processes above already provide a different source-native coarse
renewal inside the selected Store interface; neither mechanism identifies a
fine phase-score basis from its coarse channel.
\end{firewall}

\subsection{Exact horizon transport and the regulator trichotomy}
\label{sec:renewal-regulator-trichotomy}

\begin{theorem}[Projective horizon transport and infinite marked path state]
\label{thm:renewal-horizon-transport}
Let $\{T_a:a\in\{hh,hp,pp,b_0,b_1\}\}$ be the resolved branch matrices of the
fixed two-state renewal instrument, with $\sum_aT_a=M_0$.  For a phase law
$\alpha$ and a resolved word $w=a_1\cdots a_n$, put
\[
 p_\alpha[w]=\alpha T_{a_1}\cdots T_{a_n}\one.
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{\sum_ap_\alpha[wa]=p_\alpha[w],\qquad
 \sum_{|w|=n}p_\alpha[w]=1.}
\]
The finite-horizon tables are therefore the cylinder restrictions of one unique
infinite marked path law.  Their minimal active predictors all identify the
same two phase response functions, and the horizon maps are strict identities
on those states and on every old endpoint writer.  The compatible cylinder
states define a canonical state on the commutative AF path algebra; after
quotienting by measure-zero support it is faithful.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The first identity follows from $\sum_aT_a=M_0$ and $M_0\one=\one$; induction
gives the second.  Finite cylinder consistency gives the unique path law.  The
rank-two theorem and the persistence of the two phase response columns make the
minimal predictor maps identity maps.  Compatible finite probability states
extend uniquely to the inductive-limit cylinder algebra, and restriction to the
topological support removes its null ideal.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Spectator and independent-cell regulators]
\label{thm:renewal-spectator-product}
If $\Phi_*$ is any local renewal branch and $\Psi_*$ any trace-preserving
spectator map, then
\[
 \boxed{\Tr_K[(\Phi_*\otimes\Psi_*)(X)]
 =\Phi_*(\Tr_KX).}
\]
Thus arbitrary unresolved spectators preserve every old multitime probability,
word relation, and endpoint writer, even for initially correlated states.
For $m$ independent labelled renewal cells the active transfer is
$M_0^{\otimes m}$, its product stationary state has finite-volume $L^2$ mixing
factor $(7/15)^n$ independent of $m$, and the full point-labelled predictive
rank is exactly $2^m$.  The countable product defines a faithful quasilocal
infinite process with the same local contraction, but no finite faithful global
carrier.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The partial-trace identity is checked on elementary tensors and extended by
linearity.  Tensor-product spectra give the finite-volume mixing factor.  A
one-cell response panel of rank two tensorizes to a panel of rank $2^m$, while
the phase configuration itself gives a realization of that dimension.  The
finite product states and local maps are projectively compatible and therefore
define the quasilocal limit.  Unboundedly many point-readable phase
configurations preclude a finite faithful global representation.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Interacting-regulator feedback memory]
\label{thm:interacting-feedback-memory}
Let an enlarged finite transfer, relative to the old local carrier and a new
external carrier, be
\[
 \widetilde T=\begin{pmatrix}A&B\\C&D\end{pmatrix}.
\]
The exact returned memory kernel is
\[
 \boxed{K_k=BD^kC\qquad(k\ge0),}
\]
and the old-support compression $X_n=P\widetilde T^nJ$ satisfies
\[
 \boxed{X_{n+1}=AX_n+\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}K_{n-1-j}X_j,\qquad X_0=I.}
\]
Equivalently,
\[
 \boxed{\sum_{n\ge0}X_nz^n
 =[I-zA-z^2B(I-zD)^{-1}C]^{-1}.}
\]
The old raw-time process remains exactly the original Markov process iff
\[
 \boxed{A=M_0,\qquad BD^kC=0\quad(0\le k<\dim\mathcal E).}
\]
For sufficiently large block sizes the feedback Hankel matrix
$[BD^{i+j}C]_{i,j}$ has rank
\[
 \boxed{d_{\rm fb}
 =\dim\frac{\Span\{D^kC\mathcal L:k\ge0\}}
 {\Span\{D^kC\mathcal L:k\ge0\}\cap\bigcap_{k\ge0}\Ker(BD^k)},}
\]
which is the minimal number of additional linear recurrent coordinates induced
by the regulator.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Block multiplication separates paths which remain local from paths which enter
the external carrier, propagate there for $k$ steps, and return, giving the
convolution equation.  Summing it gives the Schur-complement resolvent.  Equality
with $M_0^n$ for all $n$ forces $A=M_0$ at first order and every return kernel
to vanish; Cayley--Hamilton reduces the infinite list to the displayed finite
one.  The block-Hankel rank theorem for a finite linear system identifies the
rank with the reachable external subspace modulo the future-unobservable
subspace, and minimal-realization theory gives the final interpretation.
\end{proof}

\begin{assessment}[Exact regulator boundary]
Time horizon, trace-preserving spectators, and independent quasilocal replication
are exact regulators of the renewal process.  A physical regulator which couples
new states back into the old cell changes the process unless its feedback kernel
vanishes.  Small one-step coupling is not by itself sufficient: long-lived
external modes can produce order-one integrated feedback.  Such interacting
extensions require their actual branch blocks or a separately proved influence
bound.
\end{assessment}

\begin{assessment}[Exact finite and infinite boundary]
The minimal record, finite comb, table-native predictor, support-minimal CP
class, contextual history algebra, regular word hierarchy, finite flatness,
and cutoff support functor are exact at every finite cutoff.  An AF structural
limit follows under prefix exactness.  A compatible physical state, bounded
Hilbert action, finite linear memory, finite recurrent CP memory, finite full
record carrier, finite-dimensional limit algebra, uniform gap, and primitive
phase selection are separate properties with the explicit certificates above.
None is included merely by calling the finite tensor ``emergent.''
\end{assessment}

\section{Flat reconstruction and strong theorem transport}
\label{sec:flat-word}
% =============================================================================

\begin{definition}[Finite source-generated history realization]
A finite source-generated history realization is a tuple
$(\mathcal A,\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle,\mathcal E,\sharp,S)$ consisting of a
finite unital $*$-algebra, a faithful Hilbert inner product, a finite label
space with conjugate-linear involution, and a linear source map satisfying
$S(x^\sharp)=S(x)^*$.  The unit and $S(\mathcal E)$ generate $\mathcal A$.
\end{definition}

For $r\ge0$ put
$\mathcal W_{\le r}=\bigoplus_{k=0}^r\mathcal E^{\otimes k}$ and define
\[
 W_r\Omega=\one,
 \qquad
 W_r(x_1\otimes\cdots\otimes x_k)=S(x_1)\cdots S(x_k),
 \qquad
 \mathbb K_r=W_r^*W_r.
\]

\begin{lemma}[Flatness exhausts the generated algebra]
\label{lem:flat-exhausts-new}
If $\rank\mathbb K_r=\rank\mathbb K_{r+1}$, then
$\Ran W_r=\Ran W_{r+1}=\mathcal A$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
The ranges are nested, and equality of their dimensions gives equality.  Left
multiplication of a word of length at most $r$ by one source generator produces
a word of length at most $r+1$, so the common range is invariant under every
generator.  It contains the unit and therefore every generated word.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Flat monoidal moment reconstruction]
\label{thm:flat-monoidal-reconstruction}
Let
$(\mathcal A_i,\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_i,\mathcal E,\sharp,S_i)$,
$i=1,2$, be two finite source-generated history realizations.  Suppose for
some $r\ge1$ that
\[
 \mathbb K_{1,r+1}=\mathbb K_{2,r+1},
 \qquad
 \rank\mathbb K_{i,r}=\rank\mathbb K_{i,r+1}.
\]
Then there is a unique unital $*$-isomorphism and Hilbert-space unitary
\[
 U:\mathcal A_1\longrightarrow\mathcal A_2
\]
satisfying $UW_{1,r+1}=W_{2,r+1}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Define $U_0(W_{1,r+1}\xi)=W_{2,r+1}\xi$.  Equality of the Grams gives equality
of null spaces and output inner products, so the map is well defined and
isometric.  By \Cref{lem:flat-exhausts-new}, both ranges are the full algebras,
hence $U_0$ is unitary and the empty word gives $U\one=\one$.

For a source letter $x$ and a word $w$ of length at most $r$,
\[
 U(S_1(x)W_{1,r}w)=W_{2,r+1}(xw)=S_2(x)UW_{1,r}w.
\]
Depth-$r$ words span, so $U$ intertwines left multiplication by every source
generator and therefore preserves all products.  Word reversal and sharpening
give $U(a^*)=U(a)^*$.  Uniqueness follows because the saturated words span.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Two- and three-point reconstruction]
Let $a_1,\ldots,a_d$ be a basis of a finite unital $*$-algebra with faithful
inner product.  Put
\[
 G_{i\ell}=\ip{a_i}{a_\ell},\quad
 M_{i;jk}=\ip{a_i}{a_ja_k},\quad
 J_{ij}=\ip{a_i}{a_j^*},\quad
 u_i=\ip{a_i}{\one}.
\]
Then $G,M,J,u$ determine multiplication, involution, and unit.  If
$a_ja_k=\sum_\ell c_{jk}^\ell a_\ell$,
$a_j^*=\sum_\ell d_j^\ell a_\ell$, and
$\one=\sum_\ell e^\ell a_\ell$, then
\[
 \boxed{c_{jk}=G^{-1}M_{\cdot;jk},\qquad
 d_j=G^{-1}J_{\cdot j},\qquad e=G^{-1}u.}
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Take inner products of each expansion with every basis vector.  The resulting
linear systems have invertible coefficient matrix $G$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Finite inserted-panel certificate]
\label{thm:inserted-panel-certificate}
Under the hypotheses of \Cref{thm:flat-monoidal-reconstruction}, let $T_i$ be
linear transfers and $R_i$ unitary actions of finite groups related by an
isomorphism $\phi:G_1\to G_2$.  If
\[
 W_{1,r}^*T_1W_{1,r}=W_{2,r}^*T_2W_{2,r}
\]
and
\[
 W_{1,r}^*R_1(g)W_{1,r}
 =W_{2,r}^*R_2(\phi(g))W_{2,r}
\]
for all $g$, then the reconstructed unitary satisfies
$UT_1=T_2U$ and $UR_1(g)=R_2(\phi(g))U$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
For saturated word vectors $a=W_{1,r}\xi$ and $b=W_{1,r}\eta$, equality of
the transfer panels gives
\[
 \ip{Ua}{T_2Ub}=\ip{a}{T_1b}=\ip{Ua}{UT_1b}.
\]
Since the vectors span, $T_2U=UT_1$.  The symmetry identity is identical.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Strong-duality transport]
\label{thm:strong-transport}
A monoidal unitary intertwining transfer and symmetry transports exactly:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.8em]
\item polynomial and continuous functional calculi of normal transfers;
\item spectra, singular values, kernels, gaps, and pseudodeterminants;
\item source moments, Hankel ranks, sector leakage Grams, and Schur residuals;
\item spectral determinants;
\item every finite noncommutative word identity and every norm or order
      inequality formulated from the preserved structures.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Transfer intertwining gives polynomial identities by induction and continuous
functional calculus by uniform approximation.  Unitary equivalence preserves
spectra, singular values, kernels, and determinants.  Source-history syntheses
and their Grams are conjugated by the same unitary.  Moore--Penrose inverses and
orthogonal projections are preserved by unitary conjugation, so Schur and
leakage constructions are preserved.  The monoidal $*$-isomorphism proves
every finite word statement by substitution.
\end{proof}

\begin{principle}[Minimum preserved signature]
An isomorphism transports every identity built from the operations it
intertwines, and transports norm or order inequalities only when it is also
isometric or order preserving.  No conclusion involving an omitted operation
follows from the comparison alone.
\end{principle}

\begin{proof}
Induct on the construction of a finite term from the preserved operations.
The negative statement follows from
\Cref{cth:pairwise-not-monoidal-new}: multiplication can vary while degree-one
pairwise structure is fixed.  Analogous rescaling, nonunitary similarity, and
generator-change examples vary positive cones, determinant metrics, and word
cost while preserving weaker signatures.
\end{proof}

% =============================================================================

% =============================================================================
\section{Part I-B: Global-process descent and analytic regulator limits}
\label{sec:directed-limit-emergence}
% =============================================================================

The finite Grand Tensor is canonical at one operational cutoff.  A regulator
limit requires additional structure, but the cutoff arrows need not be placed
at the entrance.  The correct upstream datum is one globally consistent
cylinder process whose finite restrictions generate the entire cutoff family.
This section derives the strict raw system from that datum, distinguishes exact
from summably correctable compatibility, makes renormalization part of the
limit object, and treats changing domains through quadratic-form convergence.
Every failed descent or convergence condition is paired with a finite vector,
Gram, observable, or subsequence witness.

\subsection{Global operational cylinder processes and automatic descent}
\label{sec:global-cylinder-descent}

\begin{definition}[Global operational cylinder process]
\label{def:global-operational-cylinder}
Let $X_1\le X_2\le\cdots$ be a countably cofinal family of finite protocol
cutoffs.  The alphabets, exposed CP frames, generated ledgers, terminal Reads,
and source-coordinate spaces at $X_m$ are identified with designated old
subobjects at every $X_n\ge X_m$.  A \emph{global operational cylinder process}
is a normalized positive family
\[
 \mathfrak p_\infty(w,r,f)
\]
defined for every finite admitted intervention word $w$, readable record event
$r$, and compatible terminal future $f$, such that restriction, coarse
graning, deterministic discard, sequential composition, and parallel
composition agree on every common finite cylinder.  Its restriction to $X_n$
is denoted $\mathfrak p_n$.
\end{definition}

For $m\le n$, let $J_{n/m,k}$ be the canonical inclusion of the old $k$-prefix
Choi-coordinate space into the $X_n$ prefix space.  Let $F_{m}^{\rm rec}$ be a
row map spanning the finite future signatures of the old generated ledger, let
$H_m$ be the old record-conditioned Hankel matrix, and let
$\mathscr C_m\subseteq(\mathcal A_m^{\rm proc})^*$ be the span of all old
contextual functionals.  Later restricted rows are denoted respectively by
$F_{n\mid m}^{\rm rec}$, $H_{n\mid m}$, and
$\alpha_{n/m}^*\mathscr C_n$.

\begin{definition}[Cutoff innovation Grams]
\label{def:cutoff-innovation-Grams}
Let $P_m^{\rm rec}$ project onto the row span of $F_m^{\rm rec}$ and let
$P_m^{\rm ctx}$ project onto $\mathscr C_m$ in any fixed faithful finite
coordinate metric.  Define
\[
 \mathbb I_{n\mid m}^{\rm rec}
 :=F_{n\mid m}^{\rm rec}(I-P_m^{\rm rec})
   (F_{n\mid m}^{\rm rec})^*,
\]
\[
 \mathbb I_{n\mid m}^{\rm pred}
 :=P_{\Ker H_m}H_{n\mid m}^*H_{n\mid m}P_{\Ker H_m},
\]
and
\[
 \mathbb I_{n\mid m}^{\rm ctx}
 :=F_{n\mid m}^{\rm ctx}(I-P_m^{\rm ctx})
   (F_{n\mid m}^{\rm ctx})^*,
\]
where $F_{n\mid m}^{\rm ctx}$ is any row map for the restricted new contextual
coordinates.  These positive operators are independent of the chosen spanning
rows up to congruence and record, respectively, new readable distinctions,
new predictive columns, and revival of old contextually null histories.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Global cylinder reconstruction and exact cutoff alternative]
\label{thm:global-cylinder-descent}
A global operational cylinder process has the following canonical finite and
directed consequences.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(G\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item Each restriction $\mathfrak p_n$ reconstructs the finite structural Grand
      Tensor $\boldsymbol{\mathbb T}_{\Grand,X_n}$, and every old causal prefix
      satisfies
      \[
       \boxed{R_m^{(k)}=J_{n/m,k}^*R_n^{(k)}J_{n/m,k}.}
      \]
\item The square-root supports admit unique polar isometries
      \[
       W_{n/m,k}(R_m^{(k)})^{1/2}
       =(R_n^{(k)})^{1/2}J_{n/m,k},
      \]
      which compose strictly.  Hence the support-completed process algebras form
      the raw directed system of \Cref{thm:cutoff-compatibility} without an
      independently assumed prefix-exact family.
\item Restriction of future signatures gives a canonical surjection from the
      refined minimal record onto the old minimal record and therefore a unital
      injection of their function algebras.  Equality with the record defined by
      all later futures holds exactly when
      $\mathbb I_{n\mid m}^{\rm rec}=0$ for every $n\ge m$.  If it fails, a
      singular vector yields two old ledger values and one finite later future
      separating them.
\item The refined predictor restricts canonically onto the old predictor.  Its
      rank gain is
      \[
       \boxed{
       \rank H_{n\mid m}-\rank H_m
       =\rank\mathbb I_{n\mid m}^{\rm pred}.}
      \]
      A nonzero singular vector is an old linear combination of pasts invisible
      to every $X_m$ future but visible to one finite later future.
\item The separated history quotient descends from $m$ to $n$ exactly when
      $\mathbb I_{n\mid m}^{\rm ctx}=0$.  Otherwise a singular vector constructs
      $q\in\mathcal N_m^{\rm fut}$ and a finite later context detecting
      $\alpha_{n/m}(q)$.  The tail ideal
      \[
       \mathcal N_m^{\infty}
       :=\left(\Span_{n\ge m}\alpha_{n/m}^*\mathscr C_n\right)^\perp
      \]
      always gives a strict directed quotient, and for each fixed $m$ it is
      already determined at some finite later cutoff.
\item For jointly declared source families there are orthogonal innovations
      $\eta_{a,n/m}$ such that
      \[
       S_{a,n}j_{a,n/m}
       =I_{n/m}S_{a,m}+\eta_{a,n/m},
       \qquad
       \eta_{a,n/m}\perp I_{n/m}\mathcal H_m,
      \]
      and therefore
      \[
       \boxed{
       j_{a,n/m}^*G_{ab,n}j_{b,n/m}
       =G_{ab,m}+\eta_{a,n/m}^*\eta_{b,n/m}.}
      \]
      Exact joint-source compression is precisely the zero-innovation branch.
\item The finite closed-tester functionals are exact restrictions of one state
      on the algebraic cylinder order-unit limit.  When the support-completed
      embeddings are unital and the physical mass of every old corner is one,
      this state extends to the AF or quasilocal $C^*$-limit.
\end{enumerate}
Conversely, an exactly compatible family of all finite cylinder tables extends
uniquely to a global operational cylinder process.  Failure of compatibility
is witnessed by one finite tester whose probability differs on two purported
restrictions.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Restriction of the global multilinear functional to the finite CP frames gives
$\mathfrak p_n$.  Uniqueness of dual-frame tomography implies that the Riesz
representative of an old prefix is the compression of the later representative,
which proves \textup{(G1)}.  The polar decomposition of
$(R_n^{(k)})^{1/2}J_{n/m,k}$ has initial modulus $(R_m^{(k)})^{1/2}$; uniqueness
on its support gives the displayed isometry and strict composition, proving
\textup{(G2)}.

A refined record class has a well-defined old future signature, so restriction
induces a surjection of finite record spectra and the contravariant injection of
function algebras.  The component of the later signature row orthogonal to the
old span is exactly the Gram in
\Cref{def:cutoff-innovation-Grams}.  It vanishes precisely when no old class is
split; otherwise a right singular vector supplies the two records and a row
coordinate supplies the separating future.  Since the old ledger is finite,
the descending sequence of equivalence relations stabilizes after finitely
many strict refinements.  This proves \textup{(G3)}.

Restriction of response functions maps the refined Hankel column space onto the
old one.  Its kernel consists of old past combinations annihilated by $H_m$ but
not necessarily by the later row family.  The Gram of the later action on this
kernel is $\mathbb I_{n\mid m}^{\rm pred}$, and the rank-nullity theorem gives
\textup{(G4)}.  The contextual ideal is the annihilator of the contextual row
span.  Hence
\[
 \alpha_{n/m}^{-1}(\mathcal N_n^{\rm fut})
 =(\alpha_{n/m}^*\mathscr C_n)^\perp.
\]
Equality with $\mathcal N_m^{\rm fut}=\mathscr C_m^\perp$ is equivalent to
vanishing of the orthogonal row innovation.  Taking the span over all later
cutoffs gives the tail ideal; finite dimensionality again gives finite
stabilization.  This proves \textup{(G5)}.

For sources, decompose $S_{a,n}j_{a,n/m}$ into its orthogonal projection onto
the old carrier and its complement.  Global consistency identifies the old
component with $I_{n/m}S_{a,m}$.  Taking pairwise inner products yields the
mixed-block Pythagoras formula in \textup{(G6)}.  Finally, consistent finite
closed-tester functionals define a positive normalized functional on the
algebraic cylinder union; boundedness in the order-unit norm gives its unique
completion.  This proves \textup{(G7)}.  The converse is the usual extension of
a compatible cylinder premeasure: define the global value by any finite cutoff
containing the cylinder; compatibility makes it well defined and positivity,
normalization, and composition pass from that cutoff.  If compatibility fails,
the difference of the two finite functionals is nonzero and is separated by a
finite frame tester.
\end{proof}

\begin{assessment}[Logical effect of the global-process entrance]
The raw AF or quasilocal carrier and its cylinder state are no longer assumed
through a prefabricated directed family.  Local record, predictor, contextual,
and source minima need not be literally constant under refinement; they either
descend strictly or return the positive innovation which explains the change.
This is the strongest universal statement compatible with delayed readable
bits, late contextual Reads, and informative score refinements.
\end{assessment}

\subsection{Exact AF, quasilocal, source, and finite-memory modules}

\begin{definition}[Directed operational Grand-Tensor system]
\label{def:directed-GT-system}
Let $(\mathcal D,\le)$ be a countable directed set.  A \emph{directed
operational Grand-Tensor system} consists of finite structural tensors
$\boldsymbol{\mathbb T}_{\Grand,X}$, $X\in\mathcal D$, together with the
support-completed unital $*$-monomorphisms
\[
 \iota_{Y/X}:\mathcal A_X^{\rm cut}\longrightarrow
 \mathcal A_Y^{\rm cut},\qquad X\le Y,
\]
obtained from prefix-exact operational morphisms, such that
\[
 \iota_{Z/Y}\iota_{Y/X}=\iota_{Z/X},\qquad
 \iota_{X/X}=\id.
\]
It is \emph{contextually strict} when the contextual innovation Grams vanish,
so the maps descend to the separated history algebras.  A finite collection of
typed source families is \emph{jointly strict} when all marginal and mixed
source Gram blocks compress under the corresponding coefficient embeddings.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[AF structural limit and compatible physical states]
\label{thm:AF-limit-state}
Let $X_1\le X_2\le\cdots$ be a cofinal prefix-exact cutoff family with the
support-completed injections of \Cref{thm:cutoff-compatibility}.  Then the raw
support-completed history algebras have a canonical AF $C^*$-inductive limit
$\mathcal A_\infty^{\rm cut}$.  If every contextual innovation Gram in
\Cref{thm:cutoff-compatibility} vanishes, the separated history algebras also
form an AF inductive system.

If states $\omega_n$ satisfy
$\omega_{n+1}\circ\iota_{n,n+1}=\omega_n$, there is a unique state
$\omega_\infty$ on the inductive limit.  Its GNS representation is bounded and
obeys $\|\pi_{\omega_\infty}(a)\|\le\|a\|$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
An inductive limit of finite-dimensional $C^*$-algebras is AF.  The contextual
quotients form a covariant system exactly when the innovation criterion gives
ideal descent and reflection.  Define $\omega_\infty$ on the algebraic union by
$\omega_\infty(\iota_{n,\infty}(a))=\omega_n(a)$; compatibility makes this
well defined, positivity and normalization pass to the norm completion, and
uniqueness follows from density.  The standard GNS estimate
$\|\pi(a)[b]\|^2=\omega(b^*a^*ab)\le\|a\|^2\omega(b^*b)$ gives boundedness.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Projective compactness of finite-stage states]
\label{thm:projective-state-compactness}
Let
$\mathcal A_1\xrightarrow{}\mathcal A_2\xrightarrow{}\cdots$
be an injective sequence of finite-dimensional unital $C^*$-algebras.  For
each $n$, let $\omega_n$ be an arbitrary state on $\mathcal A_n$.  There are a
subsequence $n_j$ and compatible states $\omega_m^\infty$ on every fixed stage
such that
\[
 \omega_{n_j}(\iota_{n_j/m}(a))\longrightarrow\omega_m^\infty(a)
 \qquad(a\in\mathcal A_m),
\]
and
\[
 \omega_\ell^\infty(\iota_{\ell/m}a)=\omega_m^\infty(a)
 \qquad(m\le\ell).
\]
Consequently the subsequence determines a state on the AF inductive limit.  If
the original states are exactly compatible, the limit is unique and no
subsequence is required.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The state space of each finite-dimensional $\mathcal A_m$ is compact.  Choose a
subsequence whose restrictions to $\mathcal A_1$ converge, then a further
subsequence whose restrictions to $\mathcal A_2$ converge, and continue.  The
diagonal subsequence converges on every fixed stage.  Positivity and
normalization pass to the limit.  For $m\le\ell$, strict composition gives
\[
 \omega_{n_j}(\iota_{n_j/\ell}\iota_{\ell/m}a)
 =\omega_{n_j}(\iota_{n_j/m}a),
\]
so the limits are compatible.  Apply \Cref{thm:AF-limit-state}.  Under exact
compatibility every later restriction already equals the earlier state,
proving uniqueness.
\end{proof}



\begin{theorem}[Joint-source inductive-limit universality]
\label{thm:joint-source-inductive-limit}
Let $a=1,\ldots,m$ label finitely many jointly strict source families.  At
cutoff $X$, let
\[
 S_{a,X}:E_{a,X}\longrightarrow\mathcal H_X^{\min},
 \qquad G_{a,X}=S_{a,X}^*S_{a,X},
\]
be their canonical joint source realization, and suppose every mixed block
compresses under coefficient isometries $j_{a,Y/X}$:
\[
 j_{a,Y/X}^*S_{a,Y}^*S_{b,Y}j_{b,Y/X}
 =S_{a,X}^*S_{b,X}
 \qquad(a,b=1,\ldots,m).
\]
Give the faithful Gram-source quotient
\[
 \mathcal E_{a,X}^{G}:=E_{a,X}/\Ker G_{a,X}
\]
the inner product
$\langle[x],[y]\rangle_G=\langle x,G_{a,X}y\rangle$, and let
$V_{a,X}[x]=S_{a,X}x$ be its canonical isometric synthesis.  Then:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(J\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item the coefficient maps induce strict source-support isometries
      $\sigma_{a,Y/X}[x]=[j_{a,Y/X}x]$;
\item there are unique common-carrier isometries
      \[
       \iota^{\rm src}_{Y/X}:\mathcal H_X^{\min}\to\mathcal H_Y^{\min},
       \qquad
       \iota^{\rm src}_{Y/X}V_{a,X}=V_{a,Y}\sigma_{a,Y/X},
      \]
      and they compose strictly;
\item the Hilbert direct limits
      $\mathcal E_{a,\infty}^{G}$ and $\mathcal H_\infty^{\min}$ carry unique
      compatible isometries
      $V_{a,\infty}:\mathcal E_{a,\infty}^{G}\to
      \mathcal H_\infty^{\min}$ reproducing every finite marginal and mixed
      Gram by compression;
\item for two families, the normalized cross transports define one limit
      contraction $K_{21,\infty}$ exactly when the new-direction defects
      \[
       \Delta^{\rm new}_{21,Y/X}
       =\bigl\|(I-\sigma_{2,Y/X}\sigma_{2,Y/X}^*)
       K_{21,Y}\sigma_{1,Y/X}\bigr\|_{\HS}^2
      \]
      vanish on every cutoff arrow.
\end{enumerate}
Thus complete mixed-block functoriality excludes cutoff-dependent relative
rotations; separate marginal canonicality does not.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Marginal compression gives
\[
 \langle j_{a,Y/X}x,G_{a,Y}j_{a,Y/X}y\rangle
 =\langle x,G_{a,X}y\rangle.
\]
It therefore sends $\Ker G_{a,X}$ into $\Ker G_{a,Y}$ and induces the source
isometry $\sigma_{a,Y/X}$.  On the joint coefficient direct sum, put
$J_{Y/X}=\bigoplus_aj_{a,Y/X}$.  Compression of every mixed block is exactly
$J_{Y/X}^*\mathbb G_YJ_{Y/X}=\mathbb G_X$.  Hence
$[u]_X\mapsto[J_{Y/X}u]_Y$ is well defined and isometric on the joint Gram
quotients.  Its action on the source summands gives the displayed
intertwining; those summands span the source-minimal carrier, proving
uniqueness.  Strict composition follows because both composites agree on every
source generator.

The source-support and common-carrier isometries are strict directed systems,
so their algebraic direct limits carry well-defined inner products and their
completions are Hilbert direct limits.  The finite isometries $V_{a,X}$
intertwine the arrows and therefore define $V_{a,\infty}$.  Inner products of
finite-stage source vectors are exactly the finite mixed Gram entries, proving
the compression claim.

For two families, whitening gives the compressed transport identity of
\Cref{thm:joint-source-cutoff-functor}.  Decompose
$K_{21,Y}\sigma_{1,Y/X}$ into the old source-$2$ range and its orthogonal
complement.  The old component is
$\sigma_{2,Y/X}K_{21,X}$ and the displayed defect is the squared norm of the
new component.  It vanishes exactly when the transports intertwine.  The
resulting compatible contractions define a contraction on the algebraic
source-support direct limit and hence on its Hilbert completion.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Canonical causal efficient-score record]
\label{cor:causal-efficient-score-record}
For a finite causal path process with finitely many declared score coordinates,
apply the minimal-readable-record construction to the current scores and to all
future score-cylinder probabilities.  The resulting quotient is the unique
coarsest causal score-sufficient record: every score factors through it, its
quotient transition is well defined, and every other causal score-sufficient
record maps onto it.  Under a cutoff refinement preserving all old score
futures, these minimal score records form a strict quotient system.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The selected coordinates are a finite instance of the response family in
\Cref{thm:minimal-record}.  Its right-congruence property is exactly strong
lumpability of the quotient transition, and its universal property gives the
unique factor map from every other sufficient record.  Preservation of the old
future signatures is the cutoff descent criterion in
\Cref{thm:operational-record-completion}.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Quasilocal Grand-Tensor net]
\label{def:quasilocal-GT-net}
Let $\mathfrak L$ be a countable directed family of finite regions.  A
\emph{quasilocal Grand-Tensor net} is a family of finite-dimensional unital
$C^*$-algebras $\mathcal A_\Lambda$, $\Lambda\in\mathfrak L$, with isotonic
unital embeddings, such that disjoint region algebras commute.  Its
quasilocal algebra is
\[
 \mathcal A_{\rm ql}:=
 \overline{\bigcup_{\Lambda\in\mathfrak L}\mathcal A_\Lambda}^{\|\cdot\|}.
\]
A family of local states or local UCP maps is compatible when its restrictions
agree under every inclusion.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Quasilocal completion, states, and local dynamics]
\label{thm:quasilocal-completion}
Every quasilocal Grand-Tensor net has a unique $C^*$-inductive-limit algebra
with the stated local embeddings.  Every compatible family of local states
extends uniquely to a state on $\mathcal A_{\rm ql}$.  Every compatible family
of unital completely positive contractions
