$\partial\log q_\theta^B(b)|_0=\mathbb E[s\mid R_B=b]$.  Taking the covariance
gives the Fisher formula.  Coordinate restriction gives the stated blocks.
The final qualification follows because marginal quadratic forms are
unchanged under independent unitary rotations of the source ranges, whereas
the mixed blocks are not.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Symmetry localization of a tetrahedral provenance source]
\label{cor:S4-provenance-isotypic}
Let an $S_4$-covariant connected carrier have standard isotypic component
$M_{31}\otimes[31]$.  Every equivariant tetrahedral provenance synthesis has
the form $p\otimes I_{[31]}$ and its projector is
\[
 \boxed{
 \Pi_{\rm prov}
 =\frac{|p\rangle\langle p|}{\|p\|^2}\otimes I_{[31]}.}
\]
It changes only the standard isotypic block and removes at most one standard
multiplicity direction.  Every connected witness in the trivial, $[22]$,
$[211]$, or sign isotype is automatically provenance independent.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Schur's lemma identifies the equivariant homomorphism space from $[31]$ to
$M_{31}\otimes[31]$ with $M_{31}$.  The projector formula follows by taking
the Gram of $p\otimes I$.  Orthogonality of inequivalent isotypic components
proves the last statement.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Primitive pair carrier and four-cell Hoeffding exhaustion]
\label{thm:primitive-Hoeffding-support}
For two independent primitive renewal cells, after both one-cell score spaces
are shorted, the complete connected tangent is
\[
 \boxed{\mathscr I_{\rm conn}^{(2)}
 \cong\mathscr I_{\rm br}\otimes\mathscr I_{\rm br},}
\]
with dimension $9$, physical Gram $G_0\otimes G_0$, and frame window
\[
 \boxed{
 \left(\frac{176}{225}\right)^2I
 \preceq G_0\otimes G_0\preceq I.}
\]

For four primitive cells let $E_i$ be conditional expectation onto constants in
factor $i$, $Q_i=I-E_i$, and
\[
 P_A=\bigotimes_{i\in A}Q_i\bigotimes_{i\notin A}E_i
 \qquad(A\subseteq\{1,2,3,4\}).
\]
These projections are mutually orthogonal and sum to the identity.  Their
ranges satisfy
\[
 \Ran P_A\cong\mathscr I_{\rm br}^{\otimes|A|}.
\]
After constants and all one-cell sectors are removed, the complete interaction
tangent is
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathscr I_{\rm int}^{(4)}=\bigoplus_{|A|\ge2}\Ran P_A,}
\]
with support-order dimensions
\[
 \boxed{
 \begin{array}{c|ccc}
 |A|&2&3&4\\ \hline
 \dim&54&108&81.
 \end{array}}
\]
Hence the complete interaction dimension is $243$, and pairwise locality is
exactly the vanishing of all $|A|\ge3$ components.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
For two factors, the finite product-space Hoeffding decomposition is the
orthogonal sum of the first one-cell space, the second one-cell space, and
their tensor product.  The connected residual is therefore the tensor square
of the three-dimensional score bank.  Independence tensorizes the Gram and its
spectrum.

For four factors, $E_i,Q_i$ are complementary orthogonal projections.  The
tensor products obtained by choosing one of them in each factor are mutually
orthogonal and sum to $\bigotimes_i(E_i+Q_i)=I$.  The range of $P_A$ is
row-centred precisely in the coordinates of $A$, hence is the indicated tensor
power.  Counting subsets gives $\binom42 3^2=54$, $\binom43 3^3=108$, and
$3^4=81$.  Orthogonality proves the final characterization.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[$S_4$ prototype reduction of the complete support audit]
\label{thm:S4-support-prototype}
Let a four-cell differentiated score synthesis be exactly $S_4$-covariant.
For the support-resolved connected Grams
$\mathbb C_A=F^*P_AF$ one has
\[
 \boxed{\rho_g^*\mathbb C_{gA}\rho_g=\mathbb C_A.}
\]
Consequently all six pair panels are unitarily conjugate, all four triple
panels are unitarily conjugate, and the four-body panel is a single invariant
object.  The complete interaction is pairwise exactly when one prototype
triple Gram and the four-body Gram vanish.  On that branch, one nonzero
prototype pair Gram forces all six pairs and hence the graph $K_4$; one zero
prototype pair Gram forces every pair panel to vanish.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Covariance gives $\mathcal U_gF=F\rho_g$ and
$\mathcal U_gP_A\mathcal U_g^*=P_{gA}$, whence the displayed congruence.
The group is transitive on subsets of each fixed cardinality.  Positivity and
the orthogonal Hoeffding sum make vanishing an orbitwise property.  On the
pairwise branch the maximal nonzero supports have cardinality two, and
transitivity on unordered pairs gives the final dichotomy.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[Support exhaustion does not force a physical interaction]
The spaces in \Cref{thm:primitive-Hoeffding-support} are the complete available
primitive carriers.  The actual differentiated table may project to zero in
all of them.  Interaction occurrence is the positivity of the measured
shorted Gram, not the existence of a potential coefficient space.
\end{firewall}


% =============================================================================
\subsection{Operational source fusion, occurrence innovations, and effective all-support actions}
\label{sec:graded-fusion-effective-actions}
% =============================================================================

The support decomposition above identifies which primitive slots participate
in an interaction.  A stronger statement is needed before a degree-$t$ source
or action may be treated as a tensor power of degree one: the actual
multi-occurrence carrier, its fusion, its associator, and its differentiated
transfer must all be reconstructed from complete mixed panels.  This
subsection supplies that graded layer and separates product-connected
correlations from genuinely nonmonoidal occurrence directions.

\begin{definition}[Finite graded source packet]
\label{def:GT-graded-source}
For $t\ge1$, let $S_t:E_t\to H_t$ be source-minimal syntheses with
$G_t=S_t^*S_t$.  For $r,s\ge1$, let
$m_{r,s}:E_r\otimes E_s\to E_{r+s}$ be a declared coefficient-level occurrence
map.  Its metric fusion defect is
\[
 \boxed{
 \Delta_{r,s}^{\rm met}
 :=\left\|m_{r,s}^*G_{r+s}m_{r,s}-G_r\otimes G_s\right\|_{\HS}^2.}
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Canonical source fusion and occurrence innovation]
\label{thm:GT-source-fusion}
If $\Delta_{r,s}^{\rm met}=0$, there is a unique isometry
\[
 \Gamma_{r,s}:H_r\otimes H_s\longrightarrow H_{r+s}
\]
satisfying
\[
 \boxed{
 \Gamma_{r,s}(S_rx\otimes S_sy)
 =S_{r+s}m_{r,s}(x\otimes y).}
\]
The positive occurrence innovation is
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathbb I_{r,s}^{\rm fus}
 :=S_{r+s}^*(I-\Gamma_{r,s}\Gamma_{r,s}^*)S_{r+s}\succeq0.}
\]
It vanishes exactly when $\Gamma_{r,s}$ is unitary, and
\[
 \boxed{
 \rank\mathbb I_{r,s}^{\rm fus}
 =\dim H_{r+s}-\dim(H_r\otimes H_s).}
\]
Thus a positive fusion innovation is a genuinely new multi-occurrence source,
not a coordinate mismatch inside a tensor product carrier.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The metric identity makes the displayed assignment isometric on the algebraic
span of product source vectors; source minimality makes that span dense and
finite dimensional, so it extends uniquely.  The innovation is the Gram of
the component of the degree-$(r+s)$ source orthogonal to the product range.
Its kernel and rank statements follow from orthogonal projection and source
minimality.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Fusion associator residual]
\label{def:GT-fusion-associator}
When the relevant fusion isometries exist, define
\[
 \mathfrak A_{r,s,t}
 :=\Gamma_{r+s,t}(\Gamma_{r,s}\otimes I)
 -\Gamma_{r,s+t}(I\otimes\Gamma_{s,t}),
\]
\[
 \boxed{\mathbb A_{r,s,t}^{\rm fus}:=
 \mathfrak A_{r,s,t}^*\mathfrak A_{r,s,t}\succeq0.}
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Associativity and all-degree product-system reconstruction]
\label{thm:GT-fusion-associativity}
Assume the coefficient occurrence maps are associative, all metric fusion
defects vanish, all associator residuals vanish, and
$\mathbb I_{n,1}^{\rm fus}=0$ for every $n\ge1$.  Then there are unique
unitaries
\[
 U_t:H_1^{\otimes t}\longrightarrow H_t
\]
with $U_1=I$ and
\[
 \boxed{U_{t+1}=\Gamma_{t,1}(U_t\otimes I),}
\]
which satisfy
\[
 \boxed{\Gamma_{r,s}(U_r\otimes U_s)=U_{r+s}.}
\]
Thus the complete graded carrier is reconstructed from one source carrier, one
associative occurrence law, and the complete mixed occurrence Grams.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Vanishing successive fusion innovations makes each $\Gamma_{n,1}$ onto, so the
recursive maps are unitary.  Vanishing associators implies independence of
parenthesization.  Induction on $r+s$ gives the displayed coherence relation,
and source minimality gives uniqueness.
\end{proof}

\begin{countertheorem}[Exact one- and two-occurrence data do not determine degree three]
\label{cth:GT-two-not-three}
The degree-one and degree-two carriers, sources, fusion, and transfers may be
exact tensor products while the degree-three carrier contains an arbitrary
additional orthogonal source sector.  Consequently a first triple-occurrence
panel or an equivalent associator/innovation certificate is logically
independent of all one- and two-occurrence data.
\end{countertheorem}

\begin{proof}
Take $H_2=H_1^{\otimes2}$ with the canonical fusion and choose
$H_3=H_1^{\otimes3}\oplus K$ for any nonzero finite $K$.  Let every degree at
most two have the prescribed product data and let the degree-three source have
an additional component spanning $K$.  No lower-degree Gram changes, while
$\mathbb I_{2,1}^{\rm fus}$ has positive rank.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Dynamic fusion Pythagoras]
\label{thm:GT-dynamic-fusion}
Let $T_t$ be actual degree-$t$ transfers and suppose $\Gamma_{r,s}$ is an
isometric source fusion.  Put
\[
 R_{r,s}^{\rm dyn}
 :=T_{r+s}\Gamma_{r,s}-\Gamma_{r,s}(T_r\otimes T_s),
\]
\[
 L_{r,s}^{\rm dyn}
 :=(I-\Gamma_{r,s}\Gamma_{r,s}^*)T_{r+s}\Gamma_{r,s},
\]
\[
 C_{r,s}^{\rm dyn}
 :=\Gamma_{r,s}^*T_{r+s}\Gamma_{r,s}-T_r\otimes T_s.
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{
 (R_{r,s}^{\rm dyn})^*R_{r,s}^{\rm dyn}
 =(L_{r,s}^{\rm dyn})^*L_{r,s}^{\rm dyn}
 +(C_{r,s}^{\rm dyn})^*C_{r,s}^{\rm dyn}.}
\]
Hence dynamic nonmonoidality splits orthogonally into leakage toward the new
occurrence sector and a mismatch of the action compressed to the product
carrier.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Decompose $T_{r+s}\Gamma_{r,s}$ into its orthogonal components in
$\Ran\Gamma_{r,s}$ and its complement.  The product-range component equals
$\Gamma_{r,s}(T_r\otimes T_s+C_{r,s}^{\rm dyn})$, and the complement is
$L_{r,s}^{\rm dyn}$.  Orthogonality gives the identity.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Exact Hoeffding proper-subset short]
\label{thm:GT-Hoeffding-short}
Let $H_1=\C\Omega\oplus H_1^0$, with
$P=|\Omega\rangle\langle\Omega|$ and $Q=I-P$.  For
$S\subseteq[t]$, put
\[
 \Pi_S=\bigotimes_{i=1}^t
 \begin{cases}Q,&i\in S,\\P,&i\notin S.\end{cases}
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{H_1^{\otimes t}=\bigoplus_{S\subseteq[t]}^\perp\Ran\Pi_S,}
\]
and the orthogonal complement of the sum of all proper-support grades is
\[
 \boxed{(H_1^0)^{\otimes t}=\Ran Q^{\otimes t}.}
\]
Consequently the simultaneous short of any product-carrier source
$Z_t:E_t\to H_1^{\otimes t}$ by every proper-support source is
\[
 \boxed{\mathbb U_t(Z_t)=Z_t^*Q^{\otimes t}Z_t.}
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Expand $(P+Q)^{\otimes t}$.  The resulting projections are mutually
orthogonal and sum to the identity.  The only grade not contained in the sum
of proper supports is the all-$Q$ grade.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Product-connected and nonmonoidal occurrence sectors]
\label{thm:GT-complete-connected-sector}
Let $U_t:H_1^{\otimes t}\to H_t$ be an isometric product fusion.  After every
proper-subset product source has been shorted, the complete all-support
projection in the actual degree-$t$ carrier is
\[
 \boxed{
 C_t^{\rm full}
 =U_tQ^{\otimes t}U_t^*+(I-U_tU_t^*).}
\]
For every actual source $Z_t:E_t\to H_t$,
\[
 \boxed{
 Z_t^*C_t^{\rm full}Z_t
 =Z_t^*U_tQ^{\otimes t}U_t^*Z_t
 +Z_t^*(I-U_tU_t^*)Z_t.}
\]
The first term is the product-connected neutral tensor; the second is the
nonmonoidal occurrence innovation.  They are orthogonal and must not be
identified.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The product-connected subspace is contained in $\Ran U_t$, whereas the
occurrence innovation is its orthogonal complement.  The two projections are
orthogonal, and their sum is exactly the complement of the transported
proper-subset product grades.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[M\"obius-connected generator]
\label{def:GT-Mobius-generator}
Let $L_B$ be actual generators indexed by subsets $B\subseteq A$, transported
to the $A$-carrier by the declared vacuum-face embeddings.  Define
\[
 \boxed{
 K_A:=\sum_{B\subseteq A}(-1)^{|A|-|B|}L_B^{\uparrow A}.}
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[M\"obius inversion and face-connectedness]
\label{thm:GT-Mobius-inversion}
One has
\[
 \boxed{
 L_A=\sum_{\varnothing\ne B\subseteq A}K_B^{\uparrow A}.}
\]
If the subset actions are face consistent, then for every proper face
$C\subsetneq A$,
\[
 \boxed{(J_C^A)^*K_AJ_C^A=0.}
\]
Thus $K_A$ is the unique signed interaction which disappears whenever any
required slot is frozen to its vacuum face.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The first identity is Boolean M\"obius inversion.  Compressing to a proper
face replaces each $L_B^{\uparrow A}$ by $L_{B\cap C}^{\uparrow C}$.  For each
fixed $D\subseteq C$, the coefficients of $L_D^{\uparrow C}$ sum to
$(1-1)^{|A\setminus C|}=0$.
\end{proof}

\begin{countertheorem}[A positive graded action may have a negative connected interaction]
\label{cth:GT-negative-connected-generator}
Positivity of every $L_B$ does not imply positivity of $K_A$.
\end{countertheorem}

\begin{proof}
Let $Q_i$ be the excitation projection at site $i$ and put
\[
 L_1=Q_1,\qquad L_2=Q_2,
\]
\[
 L_{12}=Q_1\otimes I+I\otimes Q_2-Q_1\otimes Q_2\succeq0.
\]
Then
$K_{12}=-Q_1\otimes Q_2\preceq0$.
\end{proof}

\begin{assessment}[Where positivity belongs]
The M\"obius interaction is a signed cumulant coordinate.  The positive
coercive object is the complete action restricted to the all-residual sector,
then shorted by every actual occurrence direction.  A signed connected
interaction is admissible precisely when it is relatively controlled by that
source-native positive action.
\end{assessment}

\begin{theorem}[Occurrence Feshbach action and effective source]
\label{thm:GT-occurrence-Feshbach}
Let the all-support carrier split as a product-connected head and a
nonmonoidal occurrence sector,
$H=H_{\rm prod}\oplus H_{\rm occ}$, and let
\[
 L=\begin{pmatrix}A&B\\B^*&C\end{pmatrix}\succeq0,
 \qquad C\succeq\gamma I.
\]
The occurrence-shorted action is
\[
 \boxed{S_{\rm eff}=A-BC^{-1}B^*\succeq0.}
\]
For an actual source $z=(z_{\rm prod},z_{\rm occ})$, the source seen by the
effective product action is
\[
 \boxed{z_{\rm eff}=z_{\rm prod}-BC^{-1}z_{\rm occ}.}
\]
More generally, for $\lambda>0$, put
\[
 S_\lambda=A+\lambda I-B(C+\lambda I)^{-1}B^*,
\]
\[
 z_{{\rm eff},\lambda}
 =z_{\rm prod}-B(C+\lambda I)^{-1}z_{\rm occ}.
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{
 \begin{aligned}
 \langle z,(L+\lambda I)^{-1}z\rangle
 ={}&\langle z_{{\rm eff},\lambda},
 S_\lambda^{-1}z_{{\rm eff},\lambda}\rangle\\
 &+\langle z_{\rm occ},(C+\lambda I)^{-1}z_{\rm occ}\rangle.
 \end{aligned}}
\]
Thus occurrence sources alter both the effective action and the effective
retained source.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The action formula is the Schur complement of the positive occurrence block.
Solving the block resolvent equation first in the occurrence component gives
\[
 y=(C+\lambda I)^{-1}(z_{\rm occ}-B^*x),
\]
and substitution gives
$S_\lambda x=z_{{\rm eff},\lambda}$.  Inserting the solution into the
quadratic pairing yields the displayed identity.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Relative connected-load coercivity]
\label{thm:GT-connected-load}
Suppose on the product all-residual sector
\[
 S_{\rm eff}=L_0+V-R_{\rm occ},
 \qquad R_{\rm occ}=BC^{-1}B^*\succeq0,
\]
where $L_0\succeq\gamma I$.  If
\[
 |\langle f,Vf\rangle|+\langle f,R_{\rm occ}f\rangle
 \le\alpha\langle f,L_0f\rangle
 \qquad(\alpha<1),
\]
then
\[
 \boxed{S_{\rm eff}\succeq(1-\alpha)L_0
 \succeq(1-\alpha)\gamma I.}
\]
Hence signed connected interactions and occurrence relaxation are jointly
harmless whenever their total relative load is subcritical.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
For every $f$,
\[
 \langle f,S_{\rm eff}f\rangle
 \ge\langle f,L_0f\rangle
 -|\langle f,Vf\rangle|
 -\langle f,R_{\rm occ}f\rangle,
\]
and the assumed bound gives the conclusion.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Physical subset secants and the all-support tangent]
\label{thm:GT-subset-secants}
Let $(p_B)_{B\subseteq A}$ be an actual full-support intervention cube and put
\[
 c_B:=\sum_{C\subseteq B}(-1)^{|B|-|C|}\mathfrak h(p_C).
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{\mathfrak h(p_B)=\sum_{C\subseteq B}c_C.}
\]
If one intervention slot is operationally inert on the entire cube, every
$c_B$ containing that slot vanishes.  For independent occurrences, the
all-slot secant is the tensor product of the one-slot secants.  In general it
has the orthogonal decomposition
\[
 \boxed{c_A=c_A^{\rm prod}+c_A^{\rm occ},}
\]
where $c_A^{\rm prod}$ lies in the product fusion range and
$c_A^{\rm occ}$ is the occurrence innovation.  If the cube is obtained from
an independently physical $C^{|A|}$ family and its side lengths tend to zero,
then
\[
 \boxed{
 \frac{c_A}{\prod_{i\in A}h_i}
 \longrightarrow 2\,\partial_A\sqrt{p_\theta}\big|_{\theta=0}.}
\]
After simultaneous proper-support and nuisance shorting, the Gram of this
limit is the canonical positive all-support Fisher action.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The first identity is Boolean M\"obius inversion.  Inertness pairs terms with
opposite signs.  Tensor factorization of the Hellinger embedding proves the
independent-occurrence statement, and orthogonal projection onto the product
fusion range gives the Pythagorean split.  Repeated use of the fundamental
theorem of calculus gives
\[
 c_A=2\int_0^{h_{i_1}}\cdots\int_0^{h_{i_t}}
 \partial_A\sqrt{p_\theta}\,
 d\theta_{i_t}\cdots d\theta_{i_1},
\]
which proves the tangent limit.  Orthogonal shorting yields the unique positive
efficient Gram.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Positive second quantization and character neutralization]
\label{thm:GT-positive-unitary-tensor-dichotomy}
Let $T$ be a self-adjoint positive contraction, let
$F=\Ker(I-T)$, and assume
$\|T|_{F^\perp}\|\le q<1$.  Then for every $t\ge1$,
\[
 \boxed{\Ker(I-T^{\otimes t})=F^{\otimes t},}
\]
\[
 \boxed{
 I-T^{\otimes t}\succeq(1-q)(I-P_F^{\otimes t}).}
\]
In contrast, if a finite-order unitary has character decomposition
$H=\bigoplus_\chi H_\chi$, then
\[
 \boxed{
 \Ker(I-U^{\otimes t})
 =\bigoplus_{\chi_1\cdots\chi_t=1}
 H_{\chi_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes H_{\chi_t}.}
\]
Thus a positive one-particle gap creates no new neutral fixed tensors, whereas
unitary characters can neutralize at higher tensor degree.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Diagonalize the positive contraction.  Every tensor eigenvalue is a product of
one-particle eigenvalues; it equals one exactly when every factor lies in
$F$, and otherwise it is at most $q$.  For the unitary action, tensor
characters multiply, so the invariant sector is exactly the product-one sum.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[Degree-one data are not a graded action]
\label{fire:GT-degree-one-not-graded}
A one-occurrence source, transfer, or gap does not determine the higher
occurrence carrier, its fusion, its associator, its occurrence innovation, or
its connected action.  Those objects require complete mixed multi-occurrence
panels.  Likewise a signed M\"obius interaction or log-cumulant is not itself
a positive action; coercivity belongs to the proper-support- and
occurrence-shorted positive form reconstructed from an actual physical family.
\end{firewall}


\subsection{Renewal-boundary complete observability, fluctuation--dissipation,
and compact Lyapunov control}
\label{sec:renewal-boundary-coercivity}

The preceding metric and innovation theorems are static.  A regenerative
continuum requires a dynamically typed boundary panel, a physical duration for
one boundary step, and a distinction between dissipation inside the selected
source head and energy merely leaving that head.  The following construction
uses only current-boundary, outgoing-boundary, common-action, and protected-soft
source maps already represented in the Grand Tensor.

\begin{definition}[Current/outgoing renewal-boundary panel]
\label{def:renewal-boundary-panel}
Let $S_X:E_X\to\mathcal H_X$ synthesize the selected current-boundary source
and let $Y_X:E_X\to\mathcal H_X$ synthesize the same coefficient family at the
next completed boundary.  Assume
\[
 G_X:=S_X^*S_X\succ0,
 \qquad C_X:=S_X^*Y_X,
 \qquad H_{2,X}:=Y_X^*Y_X.
\]
Put
\[
 V_X=S_XG_X^{-1/2},\qquad P_X=V_XV_X^*,
\]
\[
 \widehat K_X=G_X^{-1/2}C_XG_X^{-1/2},
 \qquad
 B_X=G_X^{-1/2}H_{2,X}G_X^{-1/2},
\]
and
\[
 \boxed{\Lambda_X:=B_X-\widehat K_X^*\widehat K_X.}
\]
The physical duration of one completed dense boundary step is denoted
$\tau_X>0$.  In the pressure-adapted spacetime branch,
\[
 \boxed{\tau_X=h_{{\rm P},X}\mathcal N_X=c_*\ell_{0,X}.}
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Outgoing-energy Pythagoras and the Ward--graph identity]
\label{thm:renewal-boundary-Ward-graph}
For the panel of \Cref{def:renewal-boundary-panel},
\[
 \boxed{\Lambda_X=L_X^*L_X\succeq0,
 \qquad L_X=(I-P_X)Y_XG_X^{-1/2},}
\]
and
\[
 \boxed{B_X=\widehat K_X^*\widehat K_X+\Lambda_X.}
\]
Consequently
\[
 \boxed{
 I-\widehat K_X^*\widehat K_X
 =(I-B_X)+\Lambda_X.}
\]
Thus compressed predictor dissipation is the sum of genuine outgoing
source-vector dissipation and source-head leakage.

For any coefficient-space model step $W_X:E_X\to E_X$, define
\[
 \mathfrak W_X(W_X)
 :=H_{2,X}-C_X^*W_X-W_X^*C_X+W_X^*G_XW_X.
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{\mathfrak W_X(W_X)
 =(Y_X-S_XW_X)^*(Y_X-S_XW_X)\succeq0,}
\]
and, with
$\widehat W_X=G_X^{1/2}W_XG_X^{-1/2}$,
\[
 \boxed{
 G_X^{-1/2}\mathfrak W_X(W_X)G_X^{-1/2}
 =\Lambda_X+
 (\widehat K_X-\widehat W_X)^*
 (\widehat K_X-\widehat W_X).}
\]
Hence
\[
 \mathfrak W_X(W_X)=0
 \iff Y_X=S_XW_X
 \iff \Lambda_X=0\ \text{and}\ \widehat K_X=\widehat W_X.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Because $V_X$ is an isometry,
\[
 Y_XG_X^{-1/2}
 =P_XY_XG_X^{-1/2}+(I-P_X)Y_XG_X^{-1/2}
 =V_X\widehat K_X+L_X
\]
is an orthogonal decomposition.  Taking Grams gives the first identities.
The Ward--graph formula is the direct expansion of
$(Y_X-S_XW_X)^*(Y_X-S_XW_X)$.  Completing the square with
$K_X=G_X^{-1}C_X$ gives
\[
 \mathfrak W_X(W_X)
 =H_{2,X}-C_X^*G_X^{-1}C_X
 +(K_X-W_X)^*G_X(K_X-W_X),
\]
and whitening gives the displayed decomposition.  Both summands are positive,
so zero of the sum is equivalent to zero of each summand.
\end{proof}


\begin{theorem}[Noise-shorted renewal-boundary Ward identity]
\label{thm:renewal-noise-shorted-Ward}
Suppose the outgoing boundary source has the canonical decomposition
$Y_X=M_X+N_X$, where $M_X$ is predictable from the pre-boundary information
and $N_X$ is a fresh martingale source satisfying
\[
 S_X^*N_X=0,\qquad M_X^*N_X=0.
\]
For every model step $W_X$,
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathfrak W_X^{\rm raw}(W_X)
 =\mathfrak W_X^{\rm mean}(W_X)+N_X^*N_X,}
\]
where
\[
 \mathfrak W_X^{\rm mean}(W_X)=(M_X-S_XW_X)^*(M_X-S_XW_X).
\]
The simultaneous Schur short of the full $(S_X,Y_X,N_X)$ Gram away from
$N_X$ produces exactly the current/mean Gram and hence
$\mathfrak W_X^{\rm sh}=\mathfrak W_X^{\rm mean}$.  In particular, if
\[
 N_X^*N_X=\tau_XG_X^{\rm noise}+o(\tau_X)
\]
and
\[
 \|G_X^{-1/2}(M_X-S_XW_X)\|=o(\tau_X),
\]
then
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathfrak W_X^{\rm raw}(W_X)
 =\tau_XG_X^{\rm noise}+o(\tau_X),
 \qquad
 G_X^{-1/2}\mathfrak W_X^{\rm sh}(W_X)G_X^{-1/2}
 =o(\tau_X^2).}
\]
Thus the Brownian fluctuation scale is compatible with the deterministic dense
Ward scale once the declared noise source is shorted.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Apply \Cref{thm:renewal-mean-noise-short} at cutoff $X$.  The asymptotic
statements are obtained by substituting the two assumed norm estimates into
the exact positive decomposition.
\end{proof}

\begin{assessment}[Predictor innovation is not automatically physical dissipation]
The Schur form
$G_X-C_X^*G_X^{-1}C_X$ tests unpredictability from the selected current head.
If $H_{2,X}=G_X$, it is also the exact stationary innovation form.  Without
that equal-marginal identity, however, a large predictor innovation may be
entirely produced by $\Lambda_X$: the physical transfer can be isometric while
its compression to an incomplete source head is zero.  Physical dissipation is
therefore read from $I-B_X$, while $\Lambda_X$ is retained as a separate missing
source direction.
\end{assessment}

\begin{theorem}[Finite regenerative complete observability]
\label{thm:renewal-complete-observability}
Let $R$ be a contraction on a finite source space, let
$J:E\to\mathcal Y$ be a physically admitted observation or energy synthesis,
and put $Q=J^*J$.  For $m\ge1$, define
\[
 \mathcal O_m=\sum_{j=0}^{m-1}R^{*j}QR^j,
 \qquad
 \mathcal D_m=Q-R^{*m}QR^m.
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{\mathcal O_m-R^*\mathcal O_mR=\mathcal D_m.}
\]
Suppose that, for one faithful source metric $G\succ0$,
\[
 \boxed{aG\preceq\mathcal O_m\preceq bG,
 \qquad \mathcal D_m\succeq\delta\mathcal O_m}
\]
with $a,b,\delta>0$.  Then
\[
 \boxed{
 \|R^n\|_{G\to G}
 \le\sqrt{b/a}\,(1-\delta)^{n/2},}
\]
and
\[
 \boxed{
 \sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\|JR^kx\|^2
 \le\delta^{-1}\langle x,\mathcal O_mx\rangle.}
\]
The same finite panel therefore supplies a source-frame floor, a cycle
Poincar\'e inequality, exponential contraction, finite total observed energy,
and exclusion of an invisible fixed direction.  When $Q$ is the shorted
common-action or Hodge form and already dominates $G$, one may take $m=1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The first identity is the telescoping difference of the two finite sums.  The
endpoint inequality gives
$R^*\mathcal O_mR\preceq(1-\delta)\mathcal O_m$, hence iteration and the two
metric comparisons give the contraction estimate.  Since $Q\preceq\mathcal
O_m$,
\[
 \delta\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}
 \langle R^kx,\mathcal O_mR^kx\rangle
 \le
 \sum_{k=0}^{N-1}
 \langle R^kx,(\mathcal O_m-R^*\mathcal O_mR)R^kx\rangle
 \le\langle x,\mathcal O_mx\rangle.
\]
Dropping $\mathcal O_m-Q\succeq0$ and sending $N\to\infty$ proves the energy
bound.
\end{proof}


\begin{theorem}[Canonical Lyapunov metric for a stable one-way provenance quotient]
\label{thm:one-way-provenance-Lyapunov}
Let
\[
 R_X=\begin{pmatrix}A_X&0\\ C_X&D_X\end{pmatrix}
 \quad\text{on }H_X^{\rm act}\oplus H_X^{\rm prov}
\]
be the transfer on an active source plus a Read-minimal local provenance
quotient after every protected history-copy direction has been removed.
Assume that, uniformly in $X$,
\[
 \|A_X^n\|\le M_Aa^n,
 \qquad
 \|D_X^n\|\le M_Dd^n,
 \qquad
 \|C_X\|\le c,
\]
where $M_A,M_D\ge1$, $0\le a,d<1$, and $c<\infty$.  Choose
$q=\max\{a,d\}<r<1$ and put
\[
 \boxed{
 M_R=\max\left\{1,
 M_A+M_D+\frac{M_AM_Dc}{r-q}\right\}.}
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{\|R_X^n\|\le M_Rr^n\qquad(n\ge0)}
\]
uniformly in $X$.  The word-Gram series
\[
 \boxed{H_X^{\rm Lyap}:=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}R_X^{*n}R_X^n}
\]
converges in norm, is the unique bounded positive solution of
\[
 \boxed{H_X^{\rm Lyap}-R_X^*H_X^{\rm Lyap}R_X=I,}
\]
and satisfies
\[
 \boxed{
 I\preceq H_X^{\rm Lyap}
 \preceq\frac{M_R^2}{1-r^2}I,}
\]
\[
 \boxed{
 R_X^*H_X^{\rm Lyap}R_X
 \preceq(1-\gamma_*)H_X^{\rm Lyap},
 \qquad
 \gamma_*:=\frac{1-r^2}{M_R^2}>0.}
\]
Moreover, the finite word-Gram truncations
\[
 H_{X,N}^{\rm Lyap}=\sum_{n=0}^{N}R_X^{*n}R_X^n
\]
obey
\[
 \boxed{
 \|H_X^{\rm Lyap}-H_{X,N}^{\rm Lyap}\|
 \le\frac{M_R^2r^{2N+2}}{1-r^2}.}
\]
Thus exact no-feedback, uniform stability of the two diagonal transfers, and a
bounded one-way writer give a canonical uniformly conditioned coercive metric;
no smallness assumption on $C_X$ is required.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Block multiplication gives
\[
 R_X^n=
 \begin{pmatrix}
 A_X^n&0\\
 \displaystyle\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}D_X^{n-1-j}C_XA_X^j&D_X^n
 \end{pmatrix}.
\]
The lower-left block has norm at most
\[
 M_AM_Dc\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}d^{n-1-j}a^j
 \le M_AM_Dc\,nq^{n-1}.
\]
Since
$n(q/r)^{n-1}\le\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}(q/r)^k\le r/(r-q)$,
one has $nq^{n-1}\le r^n/(r-q)$.  Summing the three nonzero block norms gives
the stated power estimate.

The power estimate makes the defining series norm convergent and gives the
upper metric bound; its zeroth term gives the lower bound.  Shifting the series
yields
\[
 R_X^*H_X^{\rm Lyap}R_X=H_X^{\rm Lyap}-I.
\]
If two bounded solutions existed, their difference $K_X$ would satisfy
$K_X=R_X^{*n}K_XR_X^n$ for every $n$, and the uniform power decay would force
$K_X=0$.  Since
$H_X^{\rm Lyap}\preceq M_R^2(1-r^2)^{-1}I$, one has
$I\succeq\gamma_*H_X^{\rm Lyap}$, which proves the coercive estimate.  Summing
the geometric tail gives the truncation bound.  Every matrix coefficient of a
truncation is a finite sum of represented word-Gram coefficients.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Physical-time rate and dense-cycle comparison]
\label{thm:renewal-physical-rate}
Let the current/outgoing panel be realized by an ambient contraction $T_X$,
so $Y_X=T_XS_X$.  Put
\[
 \varepsilon_X(W_X)
 :=\left\|
 G_X^{-1/2}\mathfrak W_X(W_X)G_X^{-1/2}
 \right\|^{1/2}.
\]
If
\[
 W_X^*G_XW_X\preceq e^{-2\lambda\tau_X}G_X,
\]
then
\[
 \boxed{
 \|T_XV_X\|\le e^{-\lambda\tau_X}+\varepsilon_X(W_X),
 \qquad
 \|\widehat K_X\|
 \le e^{-\lambda\tau_X}+\varepsilon_X(W_X).}
\]
For every $0<\lambda'<\lambda$, the target rate $\lambda'$ survives whenever
\[
 \boxed{
 \varepsilon_X(W_X)
 \le e^{-\lambda'\tau_X}-e^{-\lambda\tau_X}.}
\]
Moreover, for $n\ge1$,
\[
 \boxed{
 \|T_X^nV_X-V_X\widehat W_X^n\|
 \le n\,\varepsilon_X(W_X).}
\]
Consequently
$\varepsilon_X(W_X)=o(\tau_X)$, equivalently
$\|G_X^{-1/2}\mathfrak W_X(W_X)G_X^{-1/2}\|=o(\tau_X^2)$,
is sufficient for agreement of the ambient and action-model dynamics on every
compact physical-time interval.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The normalized Ward--graph Gram is the squared norm of
$T_XV_X-V_X\widehat W_X$.  The triangle inequality and the assumed action
contraction give the first two estimates and the target-rate budget.  The
identity
\[
 T_X^nV_X-V_X\widehat W_X^n
 =\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}
 T_X^{n-1-j}(T_XV_X-V_X\widehat W_X)\widehat W_X^j
\]
gives the last estimate because both transfers are contractive.  For
$n\le T/\tau_X+1$, the stated little-$o$ condition makes the right-hand side
vanish uniformly.
\end{proof}

\begin{countertheorem}[Fixed per-cycle contraction gives a Zeno limit]
\label{cth:renewal-Zeno}
Let $\tau_X\downarrow0$ and let $K_X$ act nontrivially on a transient source
sector.  If $\|K_X\|\le q<1$ uniformly, then for every $t>0$,
\[
 \|K_X^{\lfloor t/\tau_X\rfloor}\|
 \le q^{\lfloor t/\tau_X\rfloor}\longrightarrow0.
\]
The limiting family is the identity at $t=0$ and the equilibrium projection
for every $t>0$, and is therefore not a nontrivial strongly continuous
continuum evolution.  A finite dense physical rate requires a deficit of order
$\tau_X$, for example
$\|K_X\|\le e^{-\lambda\tau_X}$.
\end{countertheorem}

\begin{proof}
The displayed bound is immediate.  If the transient sector is nonzero, the
pointwise limiting family jumps at the origin, which contradicts strong
continuity.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Unique stationary states and cutoff transport from cycle mixing]
\label{thm:renewal-state-transport}
Let $\mathcal R_X:\mathcal A_X\to\mathcal A_X$ be unital positive
boundary-cycle maps on finite unital $C^*$-algebras.  On self-adjoint
functionals of zero mass put
\[
 q_{\rm st}(\mathcal R_X)
 :=\sup_{\ell(\one)=0,\ \ell=\ell^*}
 \frac{\|\ell\circ\mathcal R_X\|}{\|\ell\|}.
\]
If $q_X:=q_{\rm st}(\mathcal R_X)<1$, then $\mathcal R_X$ has a unique
stationary state $\omega_X$.  For a unital cutoff embedding
$\iota_{Y/X}:\mathcal A_X\to\mathcal A_Y$, exact intertwining
\[
 \mathcal R_Y\iota_{Y/X}=\iota_{Y/X}\mathcal R_X
\]
implies
\[
 \boxed{\omega_Y\circ\iota_{Y/X}=\omega_X.}
\]
More generally, with
\[
 \delta_{Y/X}
 :=\|\mathcal R_Y\iota_{Y/X}-\iota_{Y/X}\mathcal R_X\|,
\]
one has
\[
 \boxed{
 \|\omega_Y\circ\iota_{Y/X}-\omega_X\|
 \le\frac{\delta_{Y/X}}{1-q_X}.}
\]
Along a cofinal chain, summability of
$\delta_{X^+/X}/(1-q_X)$ gives a canonical limiting state.  In the dense
branch $q_X\le e^{-\lambda\tau_X}$, the sharp one-step scale is
$\delta_{X^+/X}=o(\tau_X)$, and
$\sum_X\delta_{X^+/X}/\tau_X<\infty$ gives full-sequence compatibility.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Existence follows from compactness and Ces\`aro averaging.  If $\omega$ and
$\eta$ are stationary, then
$\|\omega-\eta\|\le q_X\|\omega-\eta\|$, proving uniqueness.  Exact
intertwining makes the restriction of $\omega_Y$ stationary for
$\mathcal R_X$, hence equal to $\omega_X$.  For the approximate statement, put
$\eta=\omega_Y\circ\iota_{Y/X}$.  Then
$\|\eta\circ\mathcal R_X-\eta\|\le\delta_{Y/X}$ and
\[
 \|\eta-\omega_X\|
 \le\sum_{n\ge0}
 \|(\eta-\eta\circ\mathcal R_X)\circ\mathcal R_X^n\|
 \le\delta_{Y/X}\sum_{n\ge0}q_X^n.
\]
The chain statement is telescoping.  Finally
$1-e^{-\lambda\tau_X}=\lambda\tau_X+O(\tau_X^2)$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Renewal fluctuation--dissipation and covariance noncollapse]
\label{thm:renewal-fluctuation-dissipation}
Let $H=H^*\succ0$, let $K$ satisfy
$K^*HK\preceq q^2H$ with $q<1$, and let $Q\succeq0$ obey
\[
 \boxed{
 d_-(H-K^*HK)\preceq Q\preceq d_+(H-K^*HK)}
\]
for $0<d_-\le d_+<\infty$.  Then
\[
 \Sigma:=\sum_{n\ge0}K^{*n}QK^n
\]
is the unique positive solution of
\[
 \boxed{\Sigma-K^*\Sigma K=Q,}
\]
and
\[
 \boxed{d_-H\preceq\Sigma\preceq d_+H.}
\]
If $mI\preceq H\preceq MI$, the stationary source covariance has the uniform
window
\[
 \boxed{d_-mI\preceq\Sigma\preceq d_+MI.}
\]
In particular, every compatible centered unit source has variance at least
$d_-m$ and therefore remains nontrivial in any compatible limit.

For stationary consecutive-boundary sources with joint Gram
\[
 \begin{pmatrix}H&C\\C^*&H\end{pmatrix}\succeq0,
 \qquad K=H^{-1}C,
 \qquad Q=H-C^*H^{-1}C,
\]
one has the exact identities
\[
 \boxed{Q=H-K^*HK,\qquad\Sigma=H.}
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The $H$-contraction makes the series norm convergent.  Termwise subtraction
gives the Lyapunov equation, and a difference of two bounded solutions equals
$K^{*n}DK^n$ for every $n$, hence is zero.  The telescope
\[
 \sum_{n=0}^{N}K^{*n}(H-K^*HK)K^n
 =H-K^{*(N+1)}HK^{N+1}
\]
converges to $H$.  Conjugating the relative innovation inequalities by $K^n$
and summing gives the two-sided covariance bound.  The equal-marginal case is
direct substitution with $d_-=d_+=1$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Compact renewal Lyapunov drift and state tightness]
\label{thm:renewal-Lyapunov-tightness}
Let $\omega_X$ be stationary for a unital positive cycle map $\mathcal R_X$.
Suppose $V_X\succeq0$ satisfies
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal R_X(V_X)
 \preceq e^{-\kappa\tau_X}V_X+b\tau_X\one}
\]
with $\kappa,b>0$ independent of $X$.  Then
\[
 \boxed{
 \omega_X(V_X)
 \le\frac{b\tau_X}{1-e^{-\kappa\tau_X}}
 \le\frac{be^{\kappa\tau_{\max}}}{\kappa}.}
\]
If finite-rank screens $P_{X,R}$ satisfy
\[
 V_X\succeq\psi(R)(I-P_{X,R}),
 \qquad \psi(R)\longrightarrow\infty,
\]
then
\[
 \boxed{
 \omega_X(I-P_{X,R})
 \le\frac{be^{\kappa\tau_{\max}}}{\kappa\psi(R)}.}
\]
If a declared self-adjoint field obeys
$|F_X|^p\preceq aV_X+c\one$, its spectral laws are uniformly tight.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Apply the stationary state to the drift inequality and rearrange.  The bound
$1-e^{-x}\ge xe^{-x}$ gives the displayed uniform estimate.  Applying the
state to the screen domination gives the tail bound, and the field moment
estimate followed by Markov's inequality gives spectral tightness.
\end{proof}


\begin{countertheorem}[Growing protected chronology has no uniform transient gap]
\label{cth:growing-ledger-gap}
Let $S_N$ be the nilpotent history-copy shift on $\C^N$,
\[
 S_Ne_j=e_{j+1}\quad(1\le j<N),
 \qquad S_Ne_N=0.
\]
Let $G_N\succ0$ satisfy
$\operatorname{cond}(G_N)\le\kappa<\infty$, and suppose
$\|S_N\|_{G_N\to G_N}\le q_N$.  Then
\[
 \boxed{q_N^{N-1}\ge\kappa^{-1/2},}
\]
and therefore
\[
 \boxed{\liminf_{N\to\infty}q_N\ge1.}
\]
Thus no uniformly conditioned physical metric gives a growing point-readable
history-copy shift a noncollapsing transient contraction gap.
\end{countertheorem}

\begin{proof}
Since $S_N^{N-1}e_1=e_N$,
\[
 q_N^{N-1}
 \ge\frac{\|e_N\|_{G_N}}{\|e_1\|_{G_N}}.
\]
If $m_N,M_N$ are the extreme eigenvalues of $G_N$, the last ratio is at least
$\sqrt{m_N/M_N}=\operatorname{cond}(G_N)^{-1/2}\ge\kappa^{-1/2}$.
Taking $(N-1)$st roots proves the limit statement.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Protected-ledger short is necessary for uniform coercivity]
\label{cor:protected-ledger-short}
A point-readable chronology or deterministic history-copy provenance chain
must remain in the structural record algebra but be declared protected and
shorted before a uniform Poincar\'e or Hodge estimate is imposed.  Otherwise a
uniform transient gap forces the physical metric condition number to diverge.
The proper coercive carrier is the active centered source plus the Read-minimal
local provenance quotient, modulo the protected ledger and all other declared
soft directions.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The growing protected record contains arbitrarily long finite shift chains.
Apply \Cref{cth:growing-ledger-gap} to their restrictions.  Shorting the
protected history-copy range removes exactly the directions on which the
obstruction acts.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Protected-soft Hodge short and the common compact screen]
\label{thm:renewal-shorted-Hodge}
Let $D_X:E_X\to\mathcal Y_X$ be a physical differential or action synthesis,
let $Z_X:F_X\to\mathcal Y_X$ synthesize the declared gauge, harmonic,
Goldstone, fixed, or other protected soft coordinates, and put
\[
 P_{Z_X}=Z_X(Z_X^*Z_X)^\dagger Z_X^*,
 \qquad
 \boxed{S_X^{\rm sh}=D_X^*(I-P_{Z_X})D_X.}
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{
 \langle x,S_X^{\rm sh}x\rangle
 =\inf_y\|D_Xx+Z_Xy\|^2
 =\|(I-P_{Z_X})D_Xx\|^2.}
\]
Relative to a faithful source metric $G_X\succ0$, the optimal physical
Poincar\'e constant is
\[
 \boxed{
 \lambda_X^{\rm phys}
 =\sigma_{\min}^2\bigl((I-P_{Z_X})D_XG_X^{-1/2}\bigr).}
\]
If, on one fixed compact region,
\[
 S_X^{\rm sh}\succeq c(I+L_X)^s-C_0I
\]
with $c,s>0$ and compact-resolvent anchors $L_X$ whose fixed spectral screens
have uniformly bounded rank, then every family with
$\langle x_X,S_X^{\rm sh}x_X\rangle\le E$ satisfies
\[
 \boxed{
 \|(I-P_{X,R})x_X\|^2
 \le\frac{E+C_0\sup_X\|x_X\|^2}{c(1+R)^s}.}
\]
The same shorted action can therefore supply both the continuum Poincar\'e
floor and the compact screen used for strong local field convergence.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The Moore--Penrose expression is the orthogonal projection onto
$\Ran Z_X$.  Minimizing $\|D_Xx+Z_Xy\|^2$ subtracts the projection of $D_Xx$
onto that range, proving the short and singular-value formulas.  On the
spectral complement of $P_{X,R}$ one has
$(I+L_X)^s\succeq(1+R)^sI$.  Apply the form domination and rearrange.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Regenerative complete-observability--Lyapunov packet]
\label{def:renewal-regenerative-packet}
A directed renewal Grand-Tensor family has the regenerative
complete-observability--Lyapunov packet when the following data are represented
by finite mixed panels and satisfy regulator-uniform margins.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(R\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item A passive marked boundary reconstructs the cycle maps of
      \Cref{thm:marked-cycle-channel}, with physical duration $\tau_X$ and either
      exact cutoff intertwining or a summable normalized channel defect.
\item The current/outgoing source panel of
      \Cref{def:renewal-boundary-panel} is source saturating and
      $mI\preceq G_X\preceq MI$.
\item Every order-$\tau_X$ fresh fluctuation used by the physical limit is
      represented by a joint noise source and simultaneously shorted as in
      \Cref{thm:renewal-noise-shorted-Ward}; the predictable mean remains in the
      retained current/outgoing panel.
\item A shorted common-action model $W_X$ has a positive physical rate.  When
      protected vector rewards occur, its affine first variation and complete
      mixed action metric are reconstructed by the renewal-pressure jet.  The
      normalized predictable-mean Ward residual has dense scaling
      $o(\tau_X^2)$ on every fixed compact screen; on a rare fixed-kick branch
      the event intensity and kick deficit are used instead.
\item The innovation form satisfies the relative
      fluctuation--dissipation inequalities of
      \Cref{thm:renewal-fluctuation-dissipation}; a retained stochastic source
      has a tight predictable bracket or a convergent rare-event intensity.
\item The protected-soft action satisfies
      \Cref{thm:renewal-shorted-Hodge}, and one compact Lyapunov drift of
      \Cref{thm:renewal-Lyapunov-tightness} uses the same or a dominating energy.
      The compact screen may instead be discharged by the protected spatial
      atlas and pressure-flow packet of
      \Cref{thm:operational-Sobolev-Weyl,cor:renewal-spatial-positive-screen}.
      On a stable Read-minimal one-way provenance quotient,
      \Cref{thm:one-way-provenance-Lyapunov} supplies the uniformly conditioned
      coercive metric directly from finite word Grams.
\item The selected physical locality is controlled by a first-order weighted
      influence estimate, a second-order Davies graph-form estimate, or the
      pressure-flow/coordinate-atlas route.  Controlled feedback may replace
      strict one-step locality; on a Hodge-dominated loaded sector it must reduce
      to declared finite low modes plus the compact tail of
      \Cref{cor:finite-resolution-memory}.
\end{enumerate}
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Renewal-native reduction of the physical-continuum entrance]
\label{thm:renewal-regenerative-continuum}
Let a countably cofinal directed Grand-Tensor family satisfy
\Cref{def:renewal-regenerative-packet}.  Then:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.8em]
\item the finite cycle maps have unique stationary states which are exactly or
      summably compatible and therefore define one state on the inductive-limit
      algebra;
\item the stationary source covariances are uniformly equivalent to the
      physical reference metrics, have bounded pseudoinverses, and give a
      positive limiting variance on every compatible centered source direction;
\item every declared field controlled by the compact Lyapunov energy is
      spectrally tight, and the same shorted Hodge energy gives uniformly
      exhausted finite-rank screens;
\item after the declared martingale source is shorted, the actual predictable
      dense cycle and the common-action model agree on compact physical-time
      windows and retain a noncollapsing rate; any retained stochastic source
      converges through its bracket, while the rare branch is governed by its
      event intensity and fixed kick rather than by an event logarithm;
\item the declared ballistic, diffusive, or pressure-flow locality estimate
      passes to the limit on the common local domain; Hodge-dominated loaded
      feedback decomposes into declared finite low-mode fields, a local
      high-energy correction, and a vanishing compact tail.
\end{enumerate}
Consequently the compatible-state, source-metric, nontriviality, tightness,
compact-screen, and coercivity clauses of
\Cref{thm:universal-physical-continuum} are outputs of one regenerative packet.
The convergence and semantic identification of the declared renormalized
observables, and every domain-specific variational or boundary residual, remain
separate.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Item~\textup{(i)} is \Cref{thm:renewal-state-transport}.  Item~\textup{(ii)}
is \Cref{thm:renewal-fluctuation-dissipation}.  Item~\textup{(iii)} follows
from
\Cref{thm:renewal-Lyapunov-tightness,thm:renewal-shorted-Hodge,cor:renewal-spatial-positive-screen}.
The Ward--graph square completion, canonical noise short, reward-pressure
reconstruction, and physical-time comparison in
\Cref{thm:renewal-boundary-Ward-graph,thm:renewal-noise-shorted-Ward,thm:reward-pressure-reconstruction,thm:renewal-physical-rate,thm:accepted-phase-feedback}
give item~\textup{(iv)}.  The intrinsic hypergraph, weighted influence, Davies,
pressure-flow, and Hodge-feedback theorems of the surrounding subsections give
item~\textup{(v)}.  The
last statement is obtained by matching these conclusions with the corresponding
profile clauses in \Cref{thm:universal-physical-continuum}.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Finite-type energy-to-amplitude and inverse closure]
\label{thm:renewal-finite-type-closure}
Let a predeclared finite type map
$\vartheta_X:\mathscr E_X\to\mathfrak T$ classify local current/outgoing,
source-frame, and face panels by protected operational labels.  Assume every
type has physical mass
\[
 \omega_{\alpha,X}
 :=\sum_{\vartheta_X(e)=\alpha}\mu_{e,X}\ge\omega_*>0.
\]
Let $\Xi_{e,X}\succeq0$ be normalized Ward--graph matrices, and suppose that
for every $e$ of type $\alpha$,
\[
 \|\Xi_{e,X}-U_{e,X}\Xi_{\alpha,X}U_{e,X}^*\|
 \le\varepsilon_{\Xi,X}.
\]
If
\[
 \mathcal E_{2,X}^2
 :=\sum_e\mu_{e,X}\|\Xi_{e,X}\|
\]
is bounded, then
\[
 \boxed{
 \sup_e\|\Xi_{e,X}\|
 \le\frac{\mathcal E_{2,X}^2}{\omega_*}
 +2\varepsilon_{\Xi,X}.}
\]
Hence the local amplitudes $d_{e,X}=\|\Xi_{e,X}\|^{1/2}$ satisfy, for every
finite $p\ge2$,
\[
 \boxed{
 \|d_X\|_{L^p}
 \le\|d_X\|_{L^\infty}^{1-2/p}
       \|d_X\|_{L^2}^{2/p}.}
\]

Let in addition the protected-horizontal Hodge--Dirac operator $\mathbb D_X$
satisfy
\[
 \mathbb D_X^2\succeq\sigma_*^2I,
\]
and, for every real one-Lipschitz $\phi$,
\[
 \|e^{\mu\phi}\mathbb D_Xe^{-\mu\phi}-\mathbb D_X\|
 \le b_*<\sigma_*.
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{
 \|P_x\mathbb D_X^{-1}P_y\|
 \le\frac{e^{-\mu d_X(x,y)}}{\sigma_*-b_*}.}
\]
If the forward and backward exponential volume sums are uniformly finite, the
inverse has a two-sided weighted Schur bound and therefore supplies every
finite $L^p$ Hodge conorm.  On this finite-type branch, integrated quadratic
renewal energy replaces an independent local innovation cap, and one weighted
inverse packet replaces separate exponent-by-exponent Hodge estimates.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
For a type $\alpha$,
\[
 \mathcal E_{2,X}^2
 \ge\omega_{\alpha,X}
 (\|\Xi_{\alpha,X}\|-\varepsilon_{\Xi,X}),
\]
which bounds the prototype; a second triangle inequality bounds every local
matrix.  The $L^p$ estimate is interpolation of the finite weighted sum.
For the inverse estimate, conjugation gives
$\mathbb D_{X,\phi}=\mathbb D_X+E_{X,\phi}$ with
$\|\mathbb D_X^{-1}E_{X,\phi}\|<1$.  The Neumann series yields
$\|\mathbb D_{X,\phi}^{-1}\|\le(\sigma_*-b_*)^{-1}$.  Taking
$\phi(z)=d_X(z,y)$ gives the pointwise exponential bound, and row and column
summation gives the Schur estimate.  The Schur test and interpolation give all
finite $L^p$ bounds.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[Dense, rare, ballistic, and diffusive branches]
A dense weak cycle is governed by a defect of order $\tau_X$ and by an Euler or
form limit; a rare fixed reset is governed by its physical event intensity and
must not be logarithmized on its kernel.  Likewise, an exponentially weighted
one-step norm is natural for first-order or ballistic propagation, but it may
diverge under second-order heat scaling.  The latter branch is controlled by a
Davies graph-form estimate.  A gap alone does not imply locality, and locality
alone does not imply a noncollapsing gap.
\end{firewall}


\subsection{Intrinsic operational interaction hypergraphs and canonical collars}
\label{sec:intrinsic-operational-locality}

A locality filtration may be measured, but it should not be inserted when the
complete connected response panels are already available.  The primitive
object is generally a hypergraph rather than a graph: irreducible higher-body
responses can survive even when every pairwise connected panel vanishes.

\begin{definition}[Connected operational support Gram]
\label{def:connected-operational-support}
Let $I_X$ index primitive source atoms or protected localization writers.  For
a finite $A\subseteq I_X$, let $F_{A,X}$ collect every declared connected
mixed word, ordered cumulant, commutator, score Hessian, or transfer derivative
whose primitive support is $A$.  Let $P_{A,X}^{\rm nuis}$ project onto the
joint span of proper-partition products, declared mediators, lower-order
responses, and nuisance coordinates.  Define
\[
 \widehat F_{A,X}=(I-P_{A,X}^{\rm nuis})F_{A,X},
 \qquad
 \boxed{\mathbb C_{A,X}=\widehat F_{A,X}^*\widehat F_{A,X}\succeq0.}
\]
A support $A$ is retained exactly when $\mathbb C_{A,X}\ne0$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Canonical interaction hypergraph and minimal graph]
\label{thm:intrinsic-interaction-hypergraph}
Let
\[
 \mathfrak S_X=\{A\subseteq I_X:\mathbb C_{A,X}\ne0\}.
\]
The maximal members
\[
 \boxed{\mathscr H_X^{\min}=\max_{\subseteq}\mathfrak S_X}
\]
form the unique edge-minimal hypergraph whose genuine nonzero hyperedges cover
every retained connected response.  Its two-section graph is
\[
 i\sim_Xj
 \iff
 \exists A\in\mathscr H_X^{\min}\text{ with }i,j\in A.
\]
It is the unique edge-minimal clique-support graph of the operational
hypergraph and is invariant under support-minimal coordinate changes, source
unitaries, response-frame changes, and genuinely unread record refinements.
Every nonzero singular vector of $\mathbb C_{A,X}$ synthesizes an explicit
connected history on the support $A$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Simultaneous nuisance shorting is an orthogonal projection in the common
operational carrier, so $\mathbb C_{A,X}$ vanishes exactly when every declared
response on $A$ is explained by the nuisance and proper-partition span.  Any
hypergraph supporting all retained responses must contain a hyperedge covering
each maximal nonzero support.  The family of maximal supports itself has that
property and contains no redundant edge, proving uniqueness.  Taking the
two-section is the least graph in which every hyperedge is a clique.  All
listed coordinate changes are unitary or congruence changes of the same
shorted source ranges and therefore preserve zero versus nonzero support.  A
right singular vector of the shorted row map gives the asserted history.
\end{proof}

\begin{countertheorem}[Pairwise panels do not determine interaction support]
\label{cth:pairwise-no-hypergraph}
For
\[
 p_\theta(x_1,x_2,x_3)
 =\frac18(1+\theta x_1x_2x_3),
 \qquad x_i\in\{\pm1\},
\]
every one- and two-variable marginal is independent of $\theta$, whereas
$\mathbb E_\theta[x_1x_2x_3]=\theta$.  Thus every pairwise connected panel may
vanish while a three-body hyperedge survives.
\end{countertheorem}

\begin{proof}
Summing over any omitted sign cancels the cubic term, so every proper marginal
is uniform.  Multiplication by $x_1x_2x_3$ and summation leaves $\theta$.
\end{proof}


\begin{corollary}[Four-cell support exhaustion and one-orbit audit]
\label{cor:four-cell-support-orbit-audit}
For the four-cell primitive score carrier, the general support Grams of
\Cref{def:connected-operational-support} may be chosen as the Hoeffding Grams of
\Cref{thm:primitive-Hoeffding-support}.  Hence every connected differentiated
response decomposes orthogonally into pair, triple, and four-body innovations.
If the complete panel is $S_4$-covariant, its interaction support is decided by
one pair, one triple, and one four-body prototype.  The operational hypergraph
is exactly the pairwise $K_4$ branch when
\[
 \boxed{\mathbb C_{\{1,2\}}\ne0,
 \qquad \mathbb C_{\{1,2,3\}}=0,
 \qquad \mathbb C_{\{1,2,3,4\}}=0.}
\]
A nonzero higher-order prototype is an explicit obstruction to a purely graph
local continuum model.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The Hoeffding projections are simultaneous nuisance shorts by all proper
subsets, so they are instances of the connected support construction.
\Cref{thm:S4-support-prototype} transports zero and nonzero Grams through each
support orbit.  Maximal-support reduction in
\Cref{thm:intrinsic-interaction-hypergraph} then gives the stated hypergraph.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Visibility and explanation innovations]
\label{thm:interaction-refinement-innovations}
Under a strict refinement which adds response rows but preserves the old
nuisance span,
\[
 j_{n/m}^*\mathbb C_{A,n}j_{n/m}
 =\mathbb C_{A,m}+\mathbb I_{A,n/m}^{\rm vis},
 \qquad
 \mathbb I_{A,n/m}^{\rm vis}\succeq0.
\]
If instead the refinement enlarges the nuisance or mediator projection from
$P_0$ to $P_1\succeq P_0$ while retaining the same raw response, then
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathbb C_0
 =\mathbb C_1+F^*(P_1-P_0)F.}
\]
Hence refinement may reveal a new interaction or explain an old one.  Old
hyperedges persist only under arrows which are strict for both visibility and
nuisance structure.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The first identity is the Pythagorean decomposition of the refined response
row into the embedded old row span and its orthogonal complement.  The second
follows from
$F^*(I-P_0)F=F^*(I-P_1)F+F^*(P_1-P_0)F$, using
$P_0\preceq P_1$.  Both increments are positive Grams.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Forced and possible locality]
\label{def:locality-modulus}
When only part of the mixed panel has been measured, let $\mathfrak C_X$ be the
compact set of positive connected-panel completions satisfying all measured
linear and positivity constraints.  A support is \emph{forced} when it is
nonzero in every completion and \emph{possible} when it is nonzero in at least
one completion.  Their maximal supports define the forced and possible
hypergraphs and their two-section graphs.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Incomplete-panel locality modulus]
\label{thm:locality-modulus}
The forced graph is contained in every operationally admissible interaction
graph and the possible graph contains every such graph.  If they coincide, the
interaction graph is identified.  Otherwise the pair, together with the
induced upper and lower graph-distance functions, is the canonical locality
modulus; selecting an intermediate graph is additional structure.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The assertions are the definitions of universal and existential nonvanishing
over the compact feasible set.  Maximal-support reduction and the two-section
construction preserve inclusion.  Equality makes every feasible completion
have the same zero pattern, while inequality exhibits two feasible panels with
different adjacency.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Protected localization atlas and operational collars]
\label{def:operational-collars}
Suppose a protected commutative localization algebra supplies mutually
orthogonal projections
\[
 I=\sum_{i\in I_X}Q_{i,X}.
\]
For $A\subseteq I_X$, let $N_R(A)$ be its radius-$R$ neighborhood in the
operational two-section graph and define
\[
 \boxed{P_{A,R}=\sum_{i\in N_R(A)}Q_{i,X}.}
\]
For an effective transfer $T$, put
\[
 \ell_{A,R}(T)=\|(I-P_{A,R+1})TP_{A,R}\|.
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Canonical propagation and operational light cone]
\label{thm:operational-light-cone}
If every primitive corner $Q_jTQ_i$ is included as a non-nuisance response row,
then the operational two-section graph is the smallest graph supporting the
primitive transfer.  If $\|T\|\le1$, then
\[
 \boxed{
 \|(I-P_{A,k})T^kP_A\|
 \le\sum_{r=0}^{k-1}\ell_{A,r}(T).}
\]
In particular, zero collar residuals give exact finite propagation.

More generally, put
\[
 C(T)_{ji}=\|Q_jTQ_i\|.
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{\|Q_jT^kQ_i\|\le(C(T)^k)_{ji}.}
\]
For a bounded generator $L$,
\[
 \boxed{\|Q_je^{tL}Q_i\|\le(e^{|t|C(L)})_{ji}.}
\]
If
\[
 \kappa_\mu(L)
 :=\sup_i\sum_j e^{\mu d(i,j)}C(L)_{ji}<\infty,
\]
then
\[
 \boxed{
 \|Q_Be^{tL}Q_A\|
 \le e^{-\mu d(A,B)+|t|\kappa_\mu(L)}.}
\]
These are operational propagation estimates; identification of $d$ with a
physical spatial metric remains a domain theorem.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The smallest support graph contains precisely the nonzero primitive corners.
Insert $I=P_{A,r+1}+(I-P_{A,r+1})$ after each application of $T$ and telescope;
contractivity bounds every propagated earlier error by its originating collar
residual.  Expanding $Q_jT^kQ_i$ over intermediate atoms and applying the
triangle inequality gives the matrix path sum.  The exponential series gives
the generator estimate.  Conjugating the nonnegative influence matrix by the
weight $e^{\mu d(\cdot,A)}$ bounds its weighted column norm by
$\kappa_\mu(L)$; summing the exponential series and removing the weight yields
the final inequality.
\end{proof}


% =============================================================================
\subsection{Protected spatial atlases, pressure-flow duality, and compact screens}
\label{sec:renewal-spatial-atlas}
% =============================================================================

The interaction hypergraph identifies which localization atoms are connected,
but connectedness and one-cell coercivity do not exclude a macroscopic neck.
The regulator-uniform spatial statement is therefore formulated in the
physical vertex masses and edge-current capacities reconstructed from the
loaded tensor.

\begin{definition}[Physical endpoint coequalizer and efficient capacities]
\label{def:physical-endpoint-coequalizer}
At cutoff $X$, let $V_{c,X}$ be the finite point-readable endpoint set of a
local cell $c$, and let every physically resolved face match supply a partial
bijection between the corresponding face endpoint sets.  The physical endpoint
set is the finite coequalizer
\[
 \boxed{
 V_X^{\rm end}
 :=\left(\bigsqcup_cV_{c,X}\right)\Big/\!\sim_X,}
\]
where $\sim_X$ is the equivalence relation generated by those face matches.
The quotient is accepted only if no local cell is collapsed and every protected
face, orientation, and vertex-link incidence relation passes its finite Read
test.

Let $S_{E,X}:\C^{E_X}\to\mathcal H_X$ synthesize the resolved oriented edge
current after passage to the endpoint quotient, and let $N_X$ synthesize all
one-cell, protected-record, mediator, and provenance nuisance directions on the
same covered history carrier.  With $P_{N,X}$ the orthogonal projection onto
$\Ran N_X$, define
\[
 \boxed{
 H_{E,X}^{\rm eff}
 :=S_{E,X}^*(I-P_{N,X})S_{E,X}\succeq0,}
 \qquad
 \boxed{
 u_{e,X}:=h_X\langle e,H_{E,X}^{\rm eff}e\rangle.}
\]
The numbers $u_{e,X}$ are the provenance-safe physical edge capacities.  A
zero value is retained as a missing-current witness; it is not replaced by a
raw record frequency or an unshorted marginal norm.
\end{definition}

\begin{proposition}[Finite reconstruction and nuisance invariance]
\label{prop:endpoint-capacity-reconstruction}
The endpoint coequalizer, all collapse/incidence witnesses, and every capacity
$u_{e,X}$ are reconstructed from finite cylinder rows.  Replacing the raw edge
source by $S_{E,X}+N_XL$ for an arbitrary nuisance-valued map $L$ leaves
$H_{E,X}^{\rm eff}$ and all capacities unchanged.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
The coequalizer is obtained by the terminating union--find algorithm on the
finite endpoint ledger.  A cell collapse is an explicit equivalence chain;
face over-incidence, orientation failure, or a disconnected/incorrect vertex
link is checked on the finite quotient.  The efficient capacity matrix is the
Schur short of the joint edge--nuisance Gram.  Since
$(I-P_{N,X})N_X=0$,
\[
 (S_{E,X}+N_XL)^*(I-P_{N,X})(S_{E,X}+N_XL)
 =H_{E,X}^{\rm eff},
\]
which proves nuisance invariance.
\end{proof}



\begin{theorem}[Functorial endpoint coequalizers and the induced hierarchy]
\label{thm:endpoint-refinement-coequalizer}
Let consecutive cutoff cell ledgers carry a resolved parent map
$p_n:\mathscr C_{n+1}\to\mathscr C_n$ and local endpoint refinement maps
$\rho_{c,n}$.  The local refinement descends to the physical endpoint
coequalizers if and only if every fine generating face match $x\sim_{n+1}y$
satisfies
\[
 \boxed{q_n\widetilde\rho_n(x)=q_n\widetilde\rho_n(y).}
\]
On that branch there is a unique quotient map
\[
 \boxed{\pi_n:V_{n+1}^{\rm end}\to V_n^{\rm end},
 \qquad \pi_nq_{n+1}=q_n\widetilde\rho_n,}
\]
and these maps compose strictly whenever the protected refinement records do.
At a terminal cutoff $N$, the fibres of $\pi_{N/n}$ form a canonical nested
parent/child hierarchy.  Endpoint masses descend by pushforward, and a failed
compatibility is witnessed by one fine matched pair whose parent images belong
to distinct coarse endpoint classes.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The displayed equality is exactly the universal property required for
$\widetilde\rho_n$ to be constant on the equivalence classes defining the fine
coequalizer.  It therefore yields a unique descended map, and uniqueness makes
composition strict.  Fibres of composable quotient maps are nested and hence
form the hierarchy.  Pushforward is the unique additive mass descent, and a
violated generating relation is the stated finite witness.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Physically weighted operational graph]
\label{def:weighted-operational-graph}
Let $G_X=(V_X,E_X)$ be the two-section graph of a protected localization atlas.
Assign vertex masses $m_{v,X}>0$, symmetric edge conductances
$c_{uv,X}>0$, and physical cell scale $h_X>0$.  Put
\[
 \mu_X(A)=\sum_{v\in A}m_{v,X},
 \qquad
 \mathsf V_X=\mu_X(V_X),
\]
\[
 \mathcal E_X^{\rm sp}(f)
 =\sum_{\{u,v\}\in E_X}c_{uv,X}|f(u)-f(v)|^2,
\]
and let $\Delta_X^{\rm sp}$ be the self-adjoint operator in
$L^2(V_X,\mu_X)$ associated with this form.  For an oriented antisymmetric
edge current $j$, define
\[
 (\operatorname{div}_{\mu_X}j)(v)
 =m_{v,X}^{-1}\sum_uj_{vu},
 \qquad
 \Gamma_X(j)=\max_{e\in E_X}\frac{|j_e|}{h_Xc_{e,X}}.
\]
\end{definition}

For $0<\mu_X(A)\le\mathsf V_X/2$, set $a=\mu_X(A)$ and define the canonical
centered dimension-three pressure demand
\[
 \boxed{
 \sigma_{A,X}
 =a^{-1/3}\one_A
 -\frac{a^{2/3}}{\mathsf V_X-a}\one_{A^c}.}
\]
Let $\Gamma_{A,X}^*$ be the minimum congestion among currents satisfying
$\operatorname{div}_{\mu_X}j=\sigma_{A,X}$, and put
\[
 \Gamma_{{\rm press},X}=\sup_A\Gamma_{A,X}^*,
 \qquad
 I_X=\inf_A
 \frac{h_Xc_X(\partial A)}{\mu_X(A)^{2/3}}.
\]

\begin{theorem}[Exact pressure-flow characterization of spatial isoperimetry]
\label{thm:pressure-flow-isoperimetry}
For every finite connected weighted operational graph,
\[
 \boxed{\Gamma_{{\rm press},X}=I_X^{-1},}
\]
with $1/0=+\infty$.  Equivalently, the three-dimensional cut inequality
\[
 \boxed{
 h_Xc_X(\partial A)
 \ge I_*\min\{\mu_X(A),\mu_X(A^c)\}^{2/3}}
\]
holds uniformly in $X$ if and only if every canonical pressure demand has a
physical edge-current realization with congestion at most $I_*^{-1}$.
Among all minimum-congestion solutions there is a unique minimizer of
\[
 \sum_{e}\frac{|j_e|^2}{h_Xc_{e,X}},
\]
and this canonical current is invariant under every weighted graph
automorphism preserving $A$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The divergence amount $b_A(v)=m_{v,X}\sigma_{A,X}(v)$ is centered and has
positive mass $a^{2/3}$ on $A$.  Moreover, for every $B\subseteq V_X$,
\[
 \left|\sum_{v\in B}b_A(v)\right|
 \le\min\{\mu_X(B),\mu_X(B^c)\}^{2/3}.
\]
Indeed the positive part on $B$ is at most
$a^{-1/3}\min\{a,\mu_X(B)\}\le\mu_X(B)^{2/3}$, and centeredness gives the
complementary bound.

If $j$ realizes the demand, summing its divergence over $A$ gives
\[
 a^{2/3}\le\Gamma_X(j)h_Xc_X(\partial A),
\]
so $\Gamma_{{\rm press},X}\ge I_X^{-1}$.  Conversely, give every edge
capacity $u_e=h_Xc_{e,X}/I_X$.  The preceding cut bound for $b_A$ is exactly
the cut condition for an undirected capacitated transshipment.  Replacing each
edge by two directed arcs and adjoining a source to positive-demand vertices
and a sink to negative-demand vertices, the max-flow/min-cut theorem produces
a current with $|j_e|\le u_e$.  Hence
$\Gamma_{A,X}^*\le I_X^{-1}$ for every $A$.

The feasible minimum-congestion set is compact and convex.  The displayed
quadratic functional is strictly convex because all capacities are positive,
so it has a unique minimizer.  Every weighted automorphism preserving $A$
preserves the feasible set and the functional, and therefore fixes that
minimizer.
\end{proof}


\begin{definition}[Pointwise and linear hierarchy-router constants]
\label{def:hierarchy-router-constants}
For a hierarchy block $Q$ with child-constant centered demand space
$\mathscr D_Q$, collar incidence $B_Q$, capacities $u_e$, and norms
\[
 \|g\|_{Q,3}=\max_i\frac{|g(Q_i)|}{\mu(Q_i)^{2/3}},
 \qquad
 \|j\|_{Q,\infty}=\max_e\frac{|j_e|}{u_e},
\]
define
\[
 C_Q^{\rm nl}
 =\sup_{g\ne0}
 \frac{\inf_{B_Qj=g}\|j\|_{Q,\infty}}{\|g\|_{Q,3}},
\]
and
\[
 C_Q^{\rm lin}
 =\inf_{\substack{\mathcal R\text{ linear}\\B_Q\mathcal R=I}}
 \sup_{g\ne0}\frac{\|\mathcal Rg\|_{Q,\infty}}{\|g\|_{Q,3}}.
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Linear pressure-router correction and finite compiler]
\label{thm:hierarchy-linear-router-distinction}
For every finite hierarchy block,
\[
 \boxed{C_Q^{\rm nl}\le C_Q^{\rm lin}
 \le(\dim\mathscr D_Q)C_Q^{\rm nl}.}
\]
The first constant is the max-flow/min-cut pointwise optimum; the second is the
best one linear router required by a multiscale telescoping construction.  Both
are finite linear programmes: $C_Q^{\rm nl}$ is obtained from the extreme cuts,
while $C_Q^{\rm lin}$ is obtained by imposing the congestion inequalities on
the finitely many extreme points of the unit-demand polytope.

For $k$ equal-mass children with complete collar $K_k$, common child mass $m$,
and equal edge capacity $u$,
\[
 \boxed{
 C_{K_k}^{\rm nl}=\frac{m^{2/3}}{u\lceil k/2\rceil},
 \qquad
 C_{K_k}^{\rm lin}=\frac{2m^{2/3}}{ku}.}
\]
The constants agree for even $k$ and differ strictly for odd $k$.  In
particular the physical tetrahedral branch retains the exact value
\[
 \boxed{C_{K_4}^{\rm lin}=\frac{m^{2/3}}{2u}.}
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The first inequality is immediate.  For the second, choose an Auerbach basis
$g_1,\ldots,g_d$ for the finite demand norm and, for each $g_i$, a current
within $C_Q^{\rm nl}$ of the optimum.  Extending linearly and using
$\sum_i|a_i|\le d\|\sum_ia_ig_i\|_{Q,3}$ gives the factor $d$.
Finite-dimensional polyhedrality gives both linear programmes.

For $K_k$, a cut with $r$ children has capacity $r(k-r)u$ and the extremal
normalized demand sends the same sign through the smaller side.  Maximizing
the cut ratio gives the pointwise formula.  Symmetry forces the optimal linear
right inverse to be $k^{-1}B^*$; its largest edge current under the demand norm
is $2m^{2/3}/(ku)$.  Substitution gives the parity distinction and the
$K_4$ value.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Electrical-router spectral bound]
\label{thm:hierarchy-electrical-router}
Let $U_Q=\operatorname{diag}(u_e)$ and
$L_Q=B_QU_QB_Q^*$.  On the centered demand space the electrical router
\[
 \boxed{\mathcal R_Q^{\rm el}=U_QB_Q^*L_Q^\dagger}
\]
is an exact linear right inverse and satisfies
\[
 \boxed{
 C_Q^{\rm lin}
 \le\frac{\sqrt2}{\lambda_2(\mu(Q)^{-2/3}L_Q)}.}
\]
For four equal-mass children of mass $m$ with all six capacities
$u_{ij}\ge u_-$,
\[
 \boxed{
 \lambda_2(\mu(Q)^{-2/3}L_Q)
 \ge\frac{4u_-}{(4m)^{2/3}}.}
\]
Thus $u_-\ge c_0m^{2/3}$ gives a uniform linear-router bound.  A collapsing
normalized Fiedler vector is the explicit obstruction when the floor fails.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The identity $B_QU_QB_Q^*L_Q^\dagger=I$ holds on the centered range.  Cauchy--
Schwarz in the weighted edge norm and the spectral inverse bound give the
router estimate.  On $K_4$, $B_QB_Q^*=4P_0$, so
$L_Q\succeq4u_-P_0$; normalizing by the parent mass $(4m)^{2/3}$ gives the
last inequality.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Finite global spatial compiler and exact obstruction]
\label{thm:global-spatial-compiler}
Assume the physical endpoint and efficient-capacity packet of
\Cref{def:physical-endpoint-coequalizer}.  Give the quotient vertices their
physical masses and let
\[
 I_X:=\min_{0<\mu_X(A)\le\mu_X(V_X)/2}
       \frac{u_X(\partial A)}{\mu_X(A)^{2/3}},
 \qquad
 \Gamma_X:=I_X^{-1}.
\]
Then the following assertions are finite and canonical.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(G\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item The coequalizer and all valid endpoint, face, orientation, and link
      relations terminate after finitely many comparisons.
\item $I_X$ and $\Gamma_X$ are computed exactly by finite cut enumeration or,
      equivalently, by the pressure transshipment linear programme of
      \Cref{thm:pressure-flow-isoperimetry} together with its dual.
\item If $\inf_XI_X>0$, the Sobolev, Poincar\'e, low-energy counting, and
      compact-screen conclusions of
      \Cref{thm:operational-Sobolev-Weyl} hold without a separately assumed
      spatial coercivity constant.
\item If $I_{X_j}\to0$, there are cuts $A_j$ and potentials $\phi_j$, both
      functions of the actual endpoint record, such that
      \[
       \sum_{e}u_{e,X_j}|\dd\phi_j(e)|=1,
       \qquad
       \boxed{
       \left|\sum_v b_{A_j,X_j}(v)\phi_j(v)\right|
       =\Gamma_{X_j}\longrightarrow\infty,}
      \]
      where $b_{A,X}=m_X\sigma_{A,X}$ is the canonical centered pressure
      demand.  This is the normalized macroscopic-neck obstruction.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The first statement is
\Cref{prop:endpoint-capacity-reconstruction}.  Finiteness of the quotient gives
finitely many cuts and a finite transshipment programme.  The exact
max-flow/min-cut identity in
\Cref{thm:pressure-flow-isoperimetry} gives $\Gamma_X=I_X^{-1}$ and the stated
positive-branch consequences.  Linear-programme duality gives
\[
 \Gamma_X
 =\sup_{\phi\notin\R\one}
 \frac{|\sum_vb_{A,X}(v)\phi(v)|}
      {\sum_eu_{e,X}|\dd\phi(e)|}
\]
after maximizing over the canonical demands.  Choose a maximizing cut and
dual potential and normalize the denominator to one.  Along a sequence with
$I_X\to0$, the dual pairing is $I_X^{-1}\to\infty$.
\end{proof}

\begin{countertheorem}[Local renewal and tetrahedral cells do not force a global atlas]
\label{cth:local-renewal-no-global-atlas}
There are two globally consistent conservative extensions of the same complete
local renewal and internal-cell cylinder law, with the same $N^3$ endpoint
atoms, masses $m_v=N^{-3}$, physical scale $h_N=N^{-1}$, and local capacity
normalization, such that
\[
 \boxed{\inf_N I_N^{+}>0,}
 \qquad
 \boxed{I_N^{-}\longrightarrow0.}
\]
Thus no theorem using only the marginal one-cell renewal law and finite
internal tetrahedral panels can force the positive global spatial branch.
\end{countertheorem}

\begin{proof}
Tensor the fixed local cylinder process with an independently point-readable
global endpoint ledger.  For the positive extension take the cubic box
$[N]^3$ with nearest-neighbor edges and capacity $u_e=N^{-2}$; the Cartesian
cut theorem gives $I_N^+\ge1/16$.  For the negative extension take a path on
$N^3$ vertices with the same masses and capacities.  The first half of the
path has mass tending to $1/2$ and exactly one boundary edge, so
\[
 I_N^-
 \le\frac{N^{-2}}
 {\bigl(\lfloor N^3/2\rfloor/N^3\bigr)^{2/3}}
 \longrightarrow0.
\]
Discarding the independent endpoint ledger recovers every local cylinder
probability and every local Grand-Tensor panel in both extensions.
\end{proof}


\begin{theorem}[Operational Sobolev, Poincar\'e, and Weyl bounds]
\label{thm:operational-Sobolev-Weyl}
Assume, uniformly in $X$,
\[
 \mathsf V_X\le V_*,
 \qquad
 \sum_uc_{uv,X}\le D_*h_X^{-2}m_{v,X},
\]
and the cut inequality of \Cref{thm:pressure-flow-isoperimetry} with
$I_*>0$.  Then every mean-zero $f$ satisfies
\[
 \boxed{
 \|f\|_{L^6(\mu_X)}^2
 \le C_{\rm S}\mathcal E_X^{\rm sp}(f),
 \qquad
 C_{\rm S}=\frac{128D_*}{I_*^2},}
\]
\[
 \boxed{
 \|f\|_{L^2(\mu_X)}^2
 \le C_{\rm P}\mathcal E_X^{\rm sp}(f),
 \qquad
 C_{\rm P}=\frac{128D_*V_*^{2/3}}{I_*^2}.}
\]
Consequently
\[
 \boxed{
 \lambda_1(\Delta_X^{\rm sp})
 \ge\frac{I_*^2}{128D_*V_*^{2/3}}>0.}
\]
If
$N_X(R)=\rank\one_{[0,R]}(\Delta_X^{\rm sp})$, then
\[
 \boxed{
 N_X(R)
 \le1+4e^{3/2}V_*(C_{\rm S}R)^{3/2}.}
\]
Finally, for $P_{X,R}=\one_{[0,R]}(\Delta_X^{\rm sp})$,
\[
 \boxed{
 \|(I-P_{X,R})f\|_{L^2(\mu_X)}^2
 \le R^{-1}\mathcal E_X^{\rm sp}(f).}
\]
Thus one regulator-uniform pressure-flow margin supplies both the physical
Poincar\'e floor and uniformly exhausted finite-rank compact screens.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
For nonnegative $g$, discrete coarea gives
\[
 \int_0^\infty c_X(\partial\{g>t\})\,\dd t
 =\sum_{\{u,v\}}c_{uv,X}|g(u)-g(v)|.
\]
If $g$ is supported on a set of mass at most $\mathsf V_X/2$, layer cake,
Minkowski, and the cut inequality yield
\[
 \|g\|_{3/2}
 \le\frac{h_X}{I_*}
 \sum_{\{u,v\}}c_{uv,X}|g(u)-g(v)|.
\]
Apply this to $g=f^4$.  The inequality
$|a^4-b^4|\le4(a^3+b^3)|a-b|$, Cauchy--Schwarz, and the degree bound give
\[
 \|f\|_6^4
 \le\frac{4\sqrt{2D_*}}{I_*}
 \mathcal E_X^{\rm sp}(f)^{1/2}\|f\|_6^3
\]
for a nonnegative $f$ of half-volume support.  Applying the result to the
positive and negative parts of a median-zero function gives the constant
$32D_*/I_*^2$; shifting a mean-zero function by a weighted median costs at
most a factor four and gives the stated $C_{\rm S}$.  H\"older's inequality
then gives the Poincar\'e estimate and Rayleigh--Ritz gives the gap.

Interpolation between $L^1$ and $L^6$ yields the Nash inequality
\[
 \|f\|_2^{10/3}
 \le C_{\rm S}\mathcal E_X^{\rm sp}(f)\|f\|_1^{4/3}
\]
on the mean-zero sector.  Applied to $e^{-t\Delta_X^{\rm sp}}f$, it gives
\[
 \|e^{-t\Delta_X^{\rm sp}}P_{0,X}\|_{1\to\infty}
 \le4\left(\frac{3C_{\rm S}}{2t}\right)^{3/2}.
\]
Integrating the diagonal heat kernel bounds the mean-zero heat trace by the
same expression times $V_*$.  The inequality
$N_X(R)-1\le e^{tR}\operatorname{Tr}(e^{-t\Delta_X^{\rm sp}}P_{0,X})$ with
$t=3/(2R)$ gives the counting law.  The final estimate is the spectral
inequality
$\Delta_X^{\rm sp}\succeq R(I-P_{X,R})$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Protected coordinate integration and Cartesian filling]
\label{thm:protected-coordinate-integration}
Let $K_X$ be a finite connected oriented regulator $2$-complex and let
\[
 \vartheta_X:C_1(K_X;\Z)\longrightarrow\Z^3
\]
be an antisymmetric protected directional-increment cochain.  There is a
protected coordinate writer
$X_X:V_X\to\Z^3$, unique after fixing one endpoint value, with
\[
 \boxed{\vartheta_X(e)=X_X(t(e))-X_X(s(e))}
\]
if and only if:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(C\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item the oriented increment sum vanishes on every protected face;
\item its period vanishes on one integral basis of $H_1(K_X;\Z)$.
\end{enumerate}
If, in addition, the coordinate map is injective, has one anchored origin, and
for every nonterminal coordinate in each of the three directions the
corresponding unit-successor branch occurs with the deterministic endpoint
writer, then
\[
 \boxed{
 X_X(V_X)=\{1,\ldots,n_{1,X}\}\times
          \{1,\ldots,n_{2,X}\}\times
          \{1,\ldots,n_{3,X}\}.}
\]
The successor writers commute on their common domains, and their point
projections generate the complete protected endpoint algebra.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Fix a base endpoint and define $X_X(v)$ by summing $\vartheta_X$ along any
path from the base to $v$.  Two such paths differ by a cycle.  Face closure
removes boundaries and the period conditions remove the remaining homology
class, so the value is path independent.  The converse follows by telescoping.
Uniqueness after anchoring is immediate.

Starting from the origin, repeated unit-successor branches reach every triple
in the displayed box.  Deterministic writing places each reached endpoint at
the corresponding coordinate; injectivity prevents collisions.  Conversely,
terminality prevents points outside the box.  Two successor orders write the
same coordinate triple and therefore the same endpoint, proving commutation.
The point writers separate every coordinate triple, so they generate the full
finite endpoint algebra.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Coordinate and atlas discharge of the cut margin]
\label{thm:coordinate-atlas-isoperimetry}
Assume the Cartesian branch of
\Cref{thm:protected-coordinate-integration}.  Put
$N_X=n_{1,X}n_{2,X}n_{3,X}$ and suppose
\[
 n_{i,X}\ge\kappa N_X^{1/3},
 \qquad
 m_{v,X}\le m_+h_X^3,
 \qquad
 c_{e,X}\ge c_-h_X
\]
for every unit-coordinate edge, with cutoff-independent
$\kappa,m_+,c_->0$.  Define
\[
 C_\kappa=\max\{1,2^{-1/3}\kappa^{-1}\},
 \qquad
 \delta_\kappa=(16C_\kappa^2)^{-1}.
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{
 I_X\ge I_{\rm ax}
 :=\frac{c_-\delta_\kappa}{m_+^{2/3}}>0.}
\]

More generally, suppose $V_X$ is partitioned into finitely many protected
chart cores $V_{\alpha,X}$, each having cut constant at least $I_0$, with
\[
 \mu_X(V_{\alpha,X})\ge v_*,
 \qquad
 \mathsf V_X\le V_*.
\]
Assume their protected nerve is connected and that, for one
$0<\eta<1/2$, deleting endpoint subsets of masses at most
$\eta\mu_X(V_{\alpha,X})$ and
$\eta\mu_X(V_{\beta,X})$ from either end of any nerve interface leaves
capacity at least $J_*>0$.  Then
\[
 \boxed{
 I_X\ge I_{\rm atlas}
 :=\min\left\{
 I_0\left(\frac{2\eta v_*}{V_*}\right)^{2/3},
 J_*\left(\frac2{V_*}\right)^{2/3}
 \right\}>0.}
\]
Thus exact local coordinate charts do not require one global chart, but their
interfaces must have a deletion-resistant capacity floor.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
For a finite subset $A$ of a three-dimensional box, let $\pi_iA$ be the
projection obtained by deleting the $i$th coordinate.  Repeated
Cauchy--Schwarz gives the discrete Loomis--Whitney inequality
\[
 |A|^2\le|\pi_1A|\,|\pi_2A|\,|\pi_3A|.
\]
If $0<|A|\le N_X/2$, write $M_i(A)$ for the number of coordinate fibers in
direction $i$ meeting both $A$ and $A^c$.  Since the number of full fibers is
at most $|A|/n_{i,X}$, the Loomis--Whitney inequality and the shape bound imply
that some
$M_i(A)\ge\delta_\kappa|A|^{2/3}$; otherwise expanding
$\prod_i(\delta_\kappa+|A|^{1/3}/n_{i,X})$ gives a number strictly below one.
Every mixed fiber contains a distinct unit edge crossing the cut.  Choosing
the side of smaller cardinality and using
$\mu_X(A)\le m_+h_X^3|A|$ gives the stated $I_{\rm ax}$.

For the atlas statement, replace $A$ by its complement so that
$a=\mu_X(A)\le V_*/2$.  If one chart contains at least an $\eta$ fraction of
both $A$ and $A^c$, its local cut supplies the first displayed constant.  If
no chart is split in this way, every chart is predominantly inside or outside
$A$.  Since both types occur and the nerve is connected, two adjacent charts
have opposite majority.  Removing their minority endpoint sets leaves only
cut-crossing interface edges, whose capacity is at least $J_*$.  This gives
the second constant.  Taking the minimum proves the result.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Renewal-native spatial positive screen]
\label{cor:renewal-spatial-positive-screen}
Suppose the physical endpoint, edge-current, mass, conductance, and scale
writers pass either the coordinate or robust-atlas branch of
\Cref{thm:coordinate-atlas-isoperimetry}, and the weighted degree and volume
margins of \Cref{thm:operational-Sobolev-Weyl} hold.  Then the spatial source
has a regulator-uniform Poincar\'e floor and dimension-three low-energy
counting.  Its spectral projections give the compact screens in
\Cref{thm:renewal-shorted-Hodge,thm:SMST-positive-screen}; no separate spatial
compactness hypothesis is required on this branch.
\end{corollary}

\begin{firewall}[Local rank three does not imply global spatial coercivity]
A three-dimensional one-cell source, nondegenerate tetrahedra, and graph
connectedness do not exclude two macroscopic chambers joined by one weak edge.
Such a dumbbell preserves every local frame margin while $I_X\to0$ and
$\Gamma_{{\rm press},X}\to\infty$.  The coordinate-period, successor,
shape, or robust-interface tests above are therefore load bearing.
\end{firewall}

\subsection{Concrete renewal profile and the tetrahedral loading boundary}
\label{sec:concrete-renewal-profile}

The universal profiles can be evaluated completely on the autonomous
four-cell renewal regulator.  The resulting theorem separates a canonical
three-dimensional contrast frame from an interaction graph and from a loaded
edge connection.

\begin{theorem}[Concrete renewal continuum profile]
\label{thm:concrete-renewal-continuum-profile}
Let
\[
