 M_0=\begin{pmatrix}1/5&4/5\\2/3&1/3\end{pmatrix},
 \qquad
 \pi=(5/11,6/11),
\]
and let $\varphi$ be the normalized centered indicator of the private phase.
Then
\[
 M_0\varphi=-\frac7{15}\varphi,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Var}_\pi(\mathbf1_{\{P\}})=\frac{30}{121}.
\]
For $m$ independent cells, the Walsh functions
$\varphi_S=\prod_{i\in S}\varphi_i$ form an orthonormal basis and
\[
 M_0^{\otimes m}\varphi_S
 =\left(-\frac7{15}\right)^{|S|}\varphi_S.
\]
Consequently the mean-zero contraction is $7/15$ and the positive response
form has the volume-independent gap $176/225$.

For four cells, let
\[
 u_0=\frac12(1,1,1,1)^\mathsf T,
 \qquad W_0=u_0^\perp.
\]
The centered source synthesis
$\mathsf S_4c=\sum_ic_i\varphi_i$ restricts to an isometry on $W_0$.
The vectors
\[
 n_i=\frac2{\sqrt3}\left(e_i-\frac14\mathbf1_4\right)
\]
form a regular tetrahedron,
\[
 \langle n_i,n_j\rangle=
 \begin{cases}1,&i=j,\\-1/3,&i\ne j,\end{cases}
\]
and the six contrasts $d_{ij}=e_i-e_j$ obey
\[
 \boxed{\sum_{i<j}d_{ij}d_{ij}^*=4I_{W_0}.}
\]
Nevertheless every properly connected mixed panel across distinct independent
cells vanishes.  The autonomous interaction hypergraph is therefore the
disjoint union of its one-cell supports, not $K_4$.

The countable independent product has a unique faithful quasilocal state,
exact on-site locality, exact Markov memory, and the same positive gap.  Its
local finite screens are exact, but its global resolvent is noncompact: the
orthonormal one-site modes $\varphi_i$ escape every fixed finite collar while
retaining the same energy.  Finally, for
\[
 N_m=\sum_i\mathbf1_{\{P_i\}},\qquad
 \rho_m=N_m/m,\qquad
 F_m=m^{-1/2}\sum_i(\mathbf1_{\{P_i\}}-6/11),
\]
$N_m$ is nontight, $\rho_m\to6/11$ in $L^2$, and $F_m$ is uniformly tight
with variance $30/121$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The eigenvalue and variance follow by direct diagonalization of $M_0$ and the
stationary law.  Tensor products diagonalize on the Walsh basis, proving the
uniform contraction and gap.  Independence gives
$\langle\varphi_i,\varphi_j\rangle=\delta_{ij}$, hence
$\mathsf S_4^*\mathsf S_4=I_4$ and the restriction to $W_0$ is isometric.
Direct inner-product calculation gives the tetrahedral Gram, while the standard
complete-graph Laplacian identity gives
$\sum_{i<j}(e_i-e_j)(e_i-e_j)^*=4P_{W_0}$.

Every mixed moment across a nontrivial partition factors under the product
state, so its connected cumulant and every simultaneously shorted connected
row vanish.  The quasilocal and Markov claims follow from tensor-product
compatibility.  The one-site modes are orthonormal, weakly null, and have equal
form energy, which excludes compactness.  The three field statements follow
from the law of large numbers, the variance identity
$\operatorname{Var}(\rho_m)=30/(121m)$, and the uniform second moment of
$F_m$.
\end{proof}


\begin{theorem}[Resolved score bank, tetrahedral triplets, and stochastic limits]
\label{thm:concrete-renewal-score-profile}
For one primitive cell the physical branch score
$\xi=(\eta,\zeta,\epsilon)^{\mathsf T}$ has Gram
\[
 \boxed{G_0=\diag\!\left(\frac{176}{225},1,1\right),}
\]
is a martingale-difference source, and has zero moving-current predictor after
the realized branch is transferred to the protected ledger.  Thus its local
Schur innovation is exactly $G_0$.

For four independent cells, each of the three score coordinates gives an
$S_4$-covariant tetrahedral triplet on
$W_0=\one_4^\perp$.  The three triplets are mutually orthogonal, and their joint
Gram is
\[
 \boxed{I_{W_0}\otimes G_0.}
\]
The complete primitive tetrahedral score bank therefore has rank nine and
uniform frame floor $176/225$.  If
$d=\partial^*|_{W_0}:W_0\to C_1(K_4)$, then
\[
 \boxed{
 (d\otimes I)^*(I\otimes G_0)(d\otimes I)
 =4I_{W_0}\otimes G_0,}
\]
so the local fibre-frame floor relative to the Euclidean coefficient metric is
$704/225$; the only full-vertex kernel is the protected uniform triplet.

The dense integrated score field converges to Brownian motion with covariance
$G_0$, and the integrated active phase has diffusion coefficient $4/11$.  If
accepted responses are independently thinned with probability $\vartheta_X$
and raw step $\tau_X$, then on the scaling
\[
 \frac4{11}\frac{\vartheta_X}{\tau_X}\longrightarrow\lambda\in(0,\infty)
\]
the accepted endpoint-sign process converges to a symmetric compound-Poisson
process of intensity $\lambda$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The one-cell assertions are \Cref{thm:primitive-score-bank} and
\Cref{cor:primitive-score-continuum}.  Independence makes each four-cell source
synthesis an isometry on the coefficient space, and restriction to $W_0$
produces the standard triplet.  Orthogonality of the three one-cell score
coordinates tensorizes, giving $I_{W_0}\otimes G_0$.

The complete-graph incidence identity
$\partial\partial^*=4P_{W_0}$ gives $d^*d=4I_{W_0}$ and hence the displayed
weighted form identity.  The Brownian and active-phase limits are
\Cref{cor:primitive-score-continuum}.  For the rare branch, let $W_1,W_2,\ldots$
be the iid completed-boundary inter-opportunity durations and let
$G_\vartheta$ be geometric on $\{1,2,\ldots\}$ with success probability
$\vartheta$, independent of the $W_j$.  The accepted-response interarrival is
$T_\vartheta=\sum_{j=1}^{G_\vartheta}W_j$.  With
$p_\vartheta=(4/11)\vartheta$ and $s\ge0$,
\[
 \mathbb E e^{-sp_\vartheta T_\vartheta}
 =\frac{\vartheta F_W(e^{-sp_\vartheta})}
        {1-(1-\vartheta)F_W(e^{-sp_\vartheta})}.
\]
Since $F_W(e^{-u})=1-(11/4)u+O(u^2)$ at the origin, the last expression tends
to $(1+s)^{-1}$.  Hence $p_\vartheta T_\vartheta\Rightarrow\operatorname{Exp}(1)$.
Successive accepted interarrivals are independent regenerative copies, so their
partial sums converge jointly to the jump epochs of a rate-one Poisson process;
the associated counting paths converge in the Skorokhod topology because the
limiting epochs are almost surely distinct.  The physical scaling
$p_{\vartheta_X}/\tau_X\to\lambda$ gives the deterministic time change to
intensity $\lambda$.  Independent fair endpoint signs then give the symmetric
compound-Poisson marking.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[Local tetrahedral coercivity is not spatial ellipticity]
The identity in \Cref{thm:concrete-renewal-score-profile} controls the internal
four-vertex fibre at one physical cell.  It neither supplies connected panels
between physical cells nor gives a compact global resolvent.  Spatial
ellipticity requires the connected edge action and covariant graph estimate
below.
\end{firewall}

\begin{theorem}[Locked opportunity contrast geometry and incidence criterion]
\label{thm:locked-incidence-profile}
For the locked opportunity instrument of
\Cref{thm:locked-opportunity-instrument}, let
$c=2^{-1/2}(1,\ldots,1)^\mathsf T\in\C^{24}$ and
$P_c=cc^*/\|c\|^2$.  Then
\[
 \boxed{
 M_\vartheta
 =\vartheta(I-P_c)+(12-11\vartheta)P_c.}
\]
All accepted coefficient contrasts have exact metric $\vartheta I$.  The
minimal Stinespring outcome frame is globally nonorthogonal; for distinct
accepted labels
\[
 \boxed{
 \langle f_j,f_k\rangle
 =-\frac{1-\vartheta}{2(12-11\vartheta)}.}
\]
The minimal sharp Naimark record is an abelian outcome algebra and therefore
does not by itself supply anticommuting edge axes.

Suppose, in addition, that an oriented edge branch contains a nonzero shortened
cross-support operator
$B_e=P_{e,L}B_eP_{e,R}$ with equal-rank endpoint supports and
\[
 B_e^*B_e=\kappa_eP_{e,R},
 \qquad
 B_eB_e^*=\kappa_eP_{e,L},
 \qquad
 B_{\bar e}=z_eB_e^*,\quad |z_e|=1.
\]
Then $V_e=\kappa_e^{-1/2}B_e$ canonically generates the Pauli triple
\[
 X_e=V_e+V_e^*,\qquad
 Y_e=i(V_e-V_e^*),\qquad
 Z_e=P_{e,R}-P_{e,L},
\]
with
\[
 \boxed{-\frac i2[X_e,Y_e]=Z_e.}
\]
If the protected locked sign equals $\pm Z_e$, the endpoint axes required by a
shared-edge incidence packet are therefore derived from one odd route.

Six such marginal Pauli packets form six simultaneous edge clocks only when
their cross-edge commutator residual
\[
 \Delta_{\rm par}
 =\sum_{e<f}\sum_{a,b=1}^3\|[\sigma_{e,a},\sigma_{f,b}]\|_{\HS}^2
\]
vanishes; local marginal Grams alone do not decide this.  On the locked
$S_4$-covariant branch, the full oriented-edge source has
\[
 Q^*Q=\alpha P_{\rm cut}+\beta P_{\rm cyc},
 \qquad \alpha,\beta>0.
\]
Only the endpoint component $T=Q\partial^*$ can be compared with a tangential
vector source; the positive cycle triplet remains loop provenance.

For any finite family of $S_4$-covariant endpoint triplets
$S_a:W_0\to\mathcal H$, write
$S_a^*S_b=g_{ab}I_{W_0}$ and $\mathbf g=[g_{ab}]$.  Then
\[
 \boxed{\rank S_{\rm joint}=3\rank\mathbf g.}
\]
All triplets are one physical source exactly when $\rank\mathbf g=1$ and every
marginal is nonzero.  Relative to one anchor $0$, this is equivalent to
\[
 g_{aa}-\frac{|g_{0a}|^2}{g_{00}}=0,
 \qquad
 g_{ab}=\overline{\lambda_a}\lambda_bg_{00},
 \qquad
 \lambda_a=g_{0a}/g_{00}.
\]
Equality as normalized physical currents additionally requires the calibrated
amplitudes $\lambda_a=1$.  The response probability $\vartheta$ does not fix
that absolute generator scale.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Since $\|c\|^2=12$, spectral decomposition of the rank-one update gives the
formula for $M_\vartheta$.  Its inverse is
$\vartheta^{-1}(I-P_c)+(12-11\vartheta)^{-1}P_c$; substituting in
$f_j=\sqrt\vartheta M_\vartheta^{-1/2}e_j$ gives the off-diagonal inner
product.  The Naimark projections commute, proving the record boundary.

The two effect identities make $V_e$ a unitary partial isometry between the
endpoint supports.  Matrix multiplication in the decomposition
$P_{e,R}\oplus P_{e,L}$ gives the Pauli relations and the commutator formula.
Commuting full matrix factors multiply to an injective tensor-product
representation; conversely identical local Pauli Grams may be realized either
in a direct sum or in a tensor product, so the cross-edge word test is
necessary.  The cut--cycle decomposition follows from the inequivalent
irreducible $S_4$ triplets and Schur's lemma; $\partial$ annihilates the cycle
space.  Finally the joint Gram is $\mathbf g\otimes I_{W_0}$, proving the rank
formula.  Equality in the scalar Cauchy--Schwarz inequalities gives
$S_a=\lambda_aS_0$ and the displayed diamond identities.  Rescaling a
generator while inversely rescaling its protected dwell leaves the same
unitary, so normalized branch probabilities cannot determine the absolute
current scale.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[Source frame, interaction graph, and physical geometry]
The tetrahedral renewal contrast is an exact rank-three source frame.  The
locked opportunity packet is an exact six-edge source after its loading
residuals pass.  Neither statement alone supplies an inter-cell transport
operator, a simplicial connection, a physical metric, or the normal current of
the hypersurface-deformation algebra.  Those require the connected-panel,
parallelization, source-diamond, calibration, and domain certificates displayed
above and in the loaded spacetime section.
\end{firewall}



% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
\subsection{An interacting renewal--interchange regulator and its nonlinear cell profile}
\label{sec:renewal-interchange-regulator}
% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

The independent-cell profile above has a uniform local gap but no connected
inter-cell response.  The following reversible enlargement supplies a genuine
interaction graph without sacrificing the renewal stationary metric.  It also
provides a fully explicit regulator on which the abstract coercive and memory
profiles can be evaluated.

\begin{definition}[Graph interchange--renewal generator]
\label{def:renewal-interchange-generator}
Let $G=(V,E)$ be a finite undirected graph.  On
$\Omega_V=\{H,P\}^V$, let $M_i$ act as $M_0$ on coordinate $i$ and as the
identity elsewhere.  For $\{i,j\}\in E$, let $S_{ij}$ exchange the two phase
coordinates.  Given $\lambda>0$ and $\kappa_{ij}\ge0$, define
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal L_G
 =\lambda\sum_{i\in V}(M_i-I)
 +\sum_{\{i,j\}\in E}\kappa_{ij}(S_{ij}-I).}
\]
Let $\mu_G=\pi^{\otimes V}$ and let $\varphi$ be the normalized centered
private-phase indicator.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Exact stationarity, interaction occurrence, and uniform gap]
\label{thm:renewal-interchange-gap}
The operator $\mathcal L_G$ is a reversible Markov generator on
$L^2(\mu_G)$.  Its Dirichlet form is
\[
 \boxed{
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathcal E_G(f)
 &:=-\langle f,\mathcal L_Gf\rangle_{\mu_G}\\
 &=\lambda\sum_i\langle f,(I-M_i)f\rangle_{\mu_G}
 +\frac12\sum_{\{i,j\}\in E}\kappa_{ij}
   \|f-S_{ij}f\|_{L^2(\mu_G)}^2.
 \end{aligned}}
\]
For every finite graph and every nonnegative interchange-rate family,
\[
 \boxed{
 \operatorname{gap}(-\mathcal L_G)=\frac{22\lambda}{15}.}
\]
The constant is independent of $|V|$, the graph geometry, and the edge rates.
Moreover, for every exposed edge $e=\{i,j\}$,
$S_{ij}-I$ has operator distance at least one from the span of all one-site
operators.  Hence its differentiated transfer survives simultaneous one-cell
shorting and defines a genuine operational edge.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The one-site kernel is reversible for $\pi$, and the product state is invariant
under swaps.  This proves reversibility and the displayed Dirichlet form.
On the Walsh basis $\varphi_A=\prod_{i\in A}\varphi_i$,
\[
 \lambda\sum_i(I-M_i)\varphi_A
 =\frac{22\lambda}{15}|A|\varphi_A.
\]
The swap contribution is nonnegative, so every mean-zero function has energy
at least $(22\lambda/15)\|f\|^2$.  The symmetric first-chaos vector
$\sum_i\varphi_i$ is fixed by every swap and is an eigenvector with precisely
that eigenvalue, proving sharpness.  Finally, with
$e_1=\varphi\otimes\one$ and $e_2=\one\otimes\varphi$,
\[
 \langle e_2,(S_{ij}-I)e_1\rangle=1,
\]
whereas this matrix coefficient vanishes for every
$A\otimes I+I\otimes B$.  The distance and connected-score conclusion follow.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Exact first-chaos reaction--diffusion closure]
\label{thm:renewal-interchange-first-chaos}
For $c:V\to\C$, put
\[
 \Phi_c=\sum_{i\in V}c_i\varphi_i,
 \qquad
 (\Delta_\kappa c)_i
 =\sum_{j:\{i,j\}\in E}\kappa_{ij}(c_j-c_i).
\]
Then the first-chaos space is invariant and
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal L_G\Phi_c
 =\Phi_{\Delta_\kappa c-gc},
 \qquad g=\frac{22\lambda}{15},}
\]
with
\[
 \boxed{
 -\langle\Phi_c,\mathcal L_G\Phi_c\rangle
 =g\sum_i|c_i|^2
 +\sum_{\{i,j\}\in E}\kappa_{ij}|c_i-c_j|^2.}
\]
Thus local renewal supplies the mass and interchange supplies the graph-gradient
energy.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The local generator sends each $\varphi_i$ to $-g\varphi_i$.  A swap across
$\{i,j\}$ sends the coefficient pair $(c_i,c_j)$ to $(c_j,c_i)$, producing
$(c_j-c_i)\varphi_i+(c_i-c_j)\varphi_j$.  Summing the edges gives the first
identity, and the graph-Laplacian quadratic-form identity gives the second.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Stationary massive Ornstein--Uhlenbeck limit]
\label{thm:renewal-interchange-OU}
Let $V_N=(\Z/N\Z)^3$, give every nearest-neighbor swap rate $\kappa N^2$,
and start the process from $\mu_N=\pi^{\otimes V_N}$.  For smooth
$f$ on $\Torus^3$, define
\[
 Y_t^N(f)=N^{-3/2}\sum_{x\in V_N}f(x/N)\varphi_x(\eta_t).
\]
Then, for every $T<\infty$,
\[
 \boxed{
 (Y_t^N)_{0\le t\le T}
 \Longrightarrow (Y_t)_{0\le t\le T}}
\]
in $D([0,T],\mathscr D'(\Torus^3))$, where $Y$ is the stationary generalized
Ornstein--Uhlenbeck field determined by
\[
 \boxed{
 \dd Y_t=(\kappa\Delta-g)Y_t\,\dd t
 +\sqrt{2g}\,\dd W_t^{(0)}
 +\sqrt{2\kappa}\,\nabla\!\cdot\dd\mathbf W_t^{(1)}.}
\]
Equivalently, every Fourier mode satisfies
\[
 \boxed{
 \dd\widehat Y_t(k)
 =-\bigl(g+4\pi^2\kappa|k|^2\bigr)\widehat Y_t(k)\,\dd t
 +\sqrt{2\bigl(g+4\pi^2\kappa|k|^2\bigr)}\,\dd B_t(k).}
\]
The limiting martingale bracket is exactly twice the continuum coercive form.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The first-chaos identity gives the exact Dynkin martingale
\[
 M_t^N(f)=Y_t^N(f)-Y_0^N(f)
 -\int_0^tY_s^N((\kappa\Delta_N-g)f)\,\dd s.
\]
A local phase flip contributes the bracket
$2g\langle f,h\rangle_N$ plus a centered remainder of variance $O(N^{-3})$.
An edge exchange contributes
$2\kappa\langle\nabla_Nf,\nabla_Nh\rangle_N$ plus a centered finite-range
remainder with the same variance order.  Stationarity makes their time
integrals converge uniformly in probability to
\[
 2t\left[g\int fh+\kappa\int\nabla f\cdot\nabla h\right].
\]
All jumps vanish, the discrete drift converges to $(\kappa\Delta-g)f$, and the
initial fields converge by the product-state central limit theorem to spatial
white noise.  The martingale functional central limit theorem and the Mitoma
criterion give tightness and identify the unique distribution-valued linear
martingale problem.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Actual short-cylinder and local-update audit of the cubic regulator]
\label{thm:renewal-interchange-actual-audit}
Let $V_N=(\Z/N\Z)^3$, $h_N=N^{-1}$, and let the one-direction modulated
interchange generator be the one of
\Cref{def:modulated-renewal-interchange}.  Put
\[
 a=\frac{4\lambda}{5},\qquad b=\frac{2\lambda}{3},
 \qquad \pi_H=\frac5{11},\qquad\pi_P=\frac6{11}.
\]
Then every actual compiler output supplied by this regulator is explicit.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(A\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item The endpoint translations $T_jx=x+e_j$ commute, satisfy $T_j^N=I$,
      and act transitively.  With $T_4=(T_1T_2T_3)^{-1}$,
      $T_1T_2T_3T_4=I$.  For masses $m_x=h_N^3$ and continuum-normalized
      conductances $c_e=\kappa h_N$,
      \[
       \boxed{I_N\ge\kappa/16.}
      \]
\item The private-phase count
      $K_N(\eta)=\sum_x\one_{\{\eta_x=P\}}$ is an exactly lumpable Markov
      coordinate.  Its quotient generator is
      \[
       \boxed{
       \begin{aligned}
       (\mathcal L_NF)(k)={}&a(N^3-k)[F(k+1)-F(k)]\\
       &+bk[F(k-1)-F(k)],
       \end{aligned}}
      \]
      and its stationary law is
      \[
       \boxed{
       \Pr(K_N=k)=\binom{N^3}{k}
       \left(\frac6{11}\right)^k
       \left(\frac5{11}\right)^{N^3-k}.}
      \]
\item With the extensive product action
      \[
       \boxed{
       \mathcal A_N(\eta)=-\sum_x\log\pi_{\eta_x},}
      \]
      every primitive phase flip and every unmodulated or positive modulated
      swap obeys
      \[
       \boxed{
       \log\frac{q_N(\eta,\eta')}{q_N(\eta',\eta)}
       +\mathcal A_N(\eta')-\mathcal A_N(\eta)=0.}
      \]
      Hence the local inverse-action regression has
      $\beta_*=1$ and zero prototype residual.
\item If every local phase Read is determining, the minimal future-separated
      field record is the full configuration space and has cardinality
      $2^{N^3}$.  A fixed finite bank of orbit-summed local pattern counts
      cannot represent this point-readable field.
\item On the nonlinear branch, the operator
      $\varphi_{x+2e_1}(I-S_{x,x+e_1})$ sends one-site Walsh functions to
      two-site monomials and, under primitive closure, generates products on
      $\{0,2e_1,\ldots,2ne_1\}$ for every $n$.  No cutoff-independent finite
      pattern radius is closed under the complete local field dynamics.
\item In the count quotient the Gibbs representation has reference weight
      $w_N(k)=\binom{N^3}{k}$ and action
      \[
       \mathcal A_N(k)
       =-(N^3-k)\log(5/11)-k\log(6/11).
      \]
      Although the bare action is minimized at $k=N^3$,
      $K_N/N^3\to6/11$, and the reference-complexity term is
      \[
       \boxed{H_N=N^3\log2.}
      \]
      Exact detailed balance therefore selects the corresponding free energy,
      not the minimum of an independently specified Einstein action.
\end{enumerate}
Consequently the regulator has an unconditional massive stochastic
reaction--diffusion/Ornstein--Uhlenbeck continuum, but this table does not
supply a Lorentzian coframe, Palatini reward, or Einstein stationarity law.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The endpoint relations are the translation relations of the finite abelian
group.  The Cartesian cut estimate of
\Cref{thm:coordinate-atlas-isoperimetry}, with equal side lengths and the stated
mass/conductance scaling, gives the first lower bound.  Swaps preserve $K_N$;
there are $N^3-k$ available $H\to P$ flips and $k$ available $P\to H$ flips,
which proves the quotient generator and its binomial reversible law.

For a flip,
$a/b=6/5=\pi_P/\pi_H$, while the action increment is $\log(5/6)$; the two
logarithms cancel.  A swap preserves the product action.  In the modulated
branch the environment site $x+2e_1$ is unchanged by swapping the two edge
endpoints, so the forward and reverse rates are equal.  This proves the local
detailed-balance identity.

Point Reads separate any two distinct configurations, giving the
$2^{N^3}$ minimal record.  For the growth statement, applying the modulated
edge operator to $\varphi_0$ produces a nonzero multiple of
$\varphi_{2e_1}(\varphi_0-\varphi_{e_1})$; translating and iterating the
degree-raising term inductively produces a nonzero monomial containing
$\prod_{j=0}^{n}\varphi_{2je_1}$.  Finally the binomial law is exactly
$w_N(k)e^{-\mathcal A_N(k)}$, and
$\sum_kw_N(k)=2^{N^3}$ while $w_N(N^3)=1$.  The law of large numbers gives the
stated density and completes the audit.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[The explicit interchange continuum is not the locked Einstein update]
\label{fire:renewal-interchange-not-Einstein}
The renewal--interchange generator is a separately specified interacting
regulator.  Its exact local rates, reversible product action, and massive OU
limit cannot be substituted for the missing accepted spacetime-field operation
of the locked opportunity packet.  Such a substitution requires a
source-preserving same-history identification of the accepted initial field,
resolved update/reverse label, terminal field, and common Einstein-action
increment.
\end{firewall}

\begin{definition}[One-direction nonlinear modulation]
\label{def:modulated-renewal-interchange}
On $V_N=(\Z/N\Z)^3$, retain the local renewal and all nearest-neighbor swaps
of rate $\kappa N^2$.  On each positive $e_1$ edge
$\{x,x+e_1\}$ multiply the swap rate by
\[
 1+\theta\varphi_{x+2e_1},
 \qquad |\theta|q_\varphi<1,
 \qquad q_\varphi:=\|\varphi\|_\infty=\frac6{\sqrt{30}}.
\]
Write $H_N^\theta=-\mathcal L_N^\theta$ and decompose the centered Hilbert
space into first and higher Walsh chaos:
\[
 H_N^\theta=
 \begin{pmatrix}
 A_N&B_N^{\theta *}\\ B_N^\theta&C_N^\theta
 \end{pmatrix}.
\]
Define the first-chaos short, cell corrector, and memory kernel by
\[
 \boxed{
 S_N^\theta=A_N-B_N^{\theta *}(C_N^\theta)^{-1}B_N^\theta,}
\]
\[
 \boxed{
 \Gamma_N^\theta=-(C_N^\theta)^{-1}B_N^\theta,
 \qquad
 K_N^\theta(t)=B_N^{\theta *}e^{-tC_N^\theta}B_N^\theta.}
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Exact Schur cell, coercivity, and Mori--Zwanzig memory]
\label{thm:modulated-renewal-Schur-Mori}
For every admissible $\theta$:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.8em]
\item $C_N^\theta\succeq2gI$ and
      \[
       \boxed{
       \langle x,S_N^\theta x\rangle
       =\inf_y\langle x+y,H_N^\theta(x+y)\rangle,}
      \]
      with unique minimizer $y=\Gamma_N^\theta x$;
\item the mass remains exactly $g$, while the shorted $e_1$ diffusivity is at
      least $\kappa(1-|\theta|q_\varphi)$ and the transverse diffusivities are
      at least $\kappa$;
\item the exact projected covariance
      $U_N^\theta(t)=P_1e^{-tH_N^\theta}P_1$ obeys
      \[
       \boxed{
       \frac{\dd}{\dd t}U_N^\theta(t)
       =-A_NU_N^\theta(t)
       +\int_0^tK_N^\theta(t-s)U_N^\theta(s)\,\dd s;}
      \]
\item for $z>0$,
      \[
       \boxed{
       \widehat U_N^\theta(z)
       =\bigl[zI+A_N
       -B_N^{\theta *}(zI+C_N^\theta)^{-1}B_N^\theta\bigr]^{-1}.}
      \]
\end{enumerate}
Exact first-chaos Markov closure occurs if and only if $B_N^\theta=0$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The local renewal number operator gives $H_N^\theta\succeq g\mathcal N$,
so the higher-chaos block has floor $2g$.  Completing the block square proves
the variational short and corrector.  Comparison of the positive modulated
edge rates with $(1-|\theta|q_\varphi)\kappa N^2$ gives the diffusivity floor;
constants are fixed by every swap, so the mass is unchanged.  Solving the
higher-chaos component of $e^{-tH_N^\theta}x$ by variation of constants gives
the Volterra equation and its Laplace transform.  Finally
$U_N'(0)=-A_N$ but
$U_N''(0)=A_N^2+B_N^{\theta *}B_N^\theta$, which equals the second derivative
of a semigroup with generator $A_N$ precisely when the coupling vanishes.
\end{proof}

The small-modulation continuum profile can be expressed by canonical
exclusion-cell energies.  Let $L_2$ be the infinite two-particle relative
exclusion Laplacian on
$(\Z^3\setminus\{0\})/(r\sim-r)$, put
\[
 \mathbf v=\delta_{[e_1]}-\delta_{[2e_1]},
 \qquad
 \psi=L_2^\dagger\mathbf v,
 \qquad
 r=\langle\mathbf v,L_2^\dagger\mathbf v\rangle>0.
\]
Let $L_3,L_4$ be the three- and four-particle relative exclusion Laplacians.
The degree-raising block of the modulation produces
$\mathbf g_3=\mathcal C_{32}\psi$ and then
$\mathbf g_4=\mathcal C_{43}L_3^\dagger\mathbf g_3$.  Put
\[
 \Psi_3=L_3^\dagger\mathbf g_3,
 \qquad
 r_3=\langle\mathbf g_3,L_3^\dagger\mathbf g_3\rangle,
\]
\[
 j_3=\langle\Psi_3,J_3\Psi_3\rangle,
 \qquad
 k_3=\langle J_3\Psi_3,L_3^\dagger J_3\Psi_3\rangle,
\]
\[
 r_{23}=\langle\mathcal C_{23}\Psi_3,
 L_2^\dagger\mathcal C_{23}\Psi_3\rangle,
 \qquad
 r_4=\langle\mathbf g_4,L_4^\dagger\mathbf g_4\rangle,
\]
where $J_3$ is the positive degree-preserving skew subgraph operator and
$\mathcal C_{23}=\mathcal C_{32}^*$ in the energy pairing.  These constants
are finite and nonnegative; moreover
\[
 \frac1{12}\le r\le1,
 \qquad 0\le j_3\le r_3,
 \qquad 0\le k_3\le j_3,
 \qquad 0\le r_{23}\le q_\varphi^2r_3.
\]
The one-site skewness is
\[
 \boxed{\mu_3=\mathbb E_\pi[\varphi^3]=-\frac1{\sqrt{30}}.}
\]

\begin{theorem}[Universal continuum cell profile through sixth order]
\label{thm:renewal-sixth-order-cell-profile}
For a fixed Fourier mode $k$, let
\[
 m_k^\theta(z)=d_k^\theta+
 \int_{[2g,\infty)}\frac{\lambda}{\lambda+z}\,\dd\nu_k^\theta(\lambda)
\]
be any continuum subsequential Stieltjes profile of the first-chaos cell.
Define
\[
 D_k^{[2]}=\kappa r(2\pi k_1)^2,
\]
\[
 D_k^{[3]}=-\kappa\mu_3r^2(2\pi k_1)^2,
\]
\[
 D_k^{[4]}=\kappa(\mu_3^2r^3+r_3)(2\pi k_1)^2,
\]
\[
 D_k^{[5]}=-\kappa\mu_3
 (\mu_3^2r^4+2rr_3+j_3)(2\pi k_1)^2,
\]
and
\[
 \boxed{
 \begin{aligned}
 D_k^{[6]}=\kappa(&\mu_3^4r^5+3\mu_3^2r^2r_3
 +2\mu_3^2rj_3+\mu_3^2k_3\\
 &+r_{23}+r_4)(2\pi k_1)^2.
 \end{aligned}}
\]
Put
\[
 P_k^{[6]}(\theta)=\sum_{j=2}^{6}\theta^jD_k^{[j]},
 \qquad
 E_k^{[7]}(\theta)
 =\frac{q_\varphi^5|\theta|^7}{1-|\theta|q_\varphi}D_k^{[2]}.
\]
Then, for every $z\ge0$,
\[
 \boxed{|m_k^\theta(z)-P_k^{[6]}(\theta)|
 \le E_k^{[7]}(\theta),}
\]
\[
 \boxed{|d_k^\theta-P_k^{[6]}(\theta)|
 \le E_k^{[7]}(\theta),
 \qquad
 0\le\nu_k^\theta([2g,\infty))\le2E_k^{[7]}(\theta).}
\]
Therefore every finite-frequency memory mass is $O_k(|\theta|^7)$, and every
continuum two-point law is Markovian through sixth order.  The effective
diffusivity in the modulated direction is
\[
 \boxed{
 \begin{aligned}
 \kappa_{1,\rm eff}^{[6]}(\theta)=\kappa\Bigl[&1-r\theta^2
 +\mu_3r^2\theta^3-(\mu_3^2r^3+r_3)\theta^4\\
 &+\mu_3(\mu_3^2r^4+2rr_3+j_3)\theta^5\\
 &-(\mu_3^4r^5+3\mu_3^2r^2r_3+2\mu_3^2rj_3
   +\mu_3^2k_3+r_{23}+r_4)\theta^6\Bigr].
 \end{aligned}}
\]
The mass remains $g$ and the two transverse diffusivities remain $\kappa$
through this order.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
At $\theta=0$ the higher block preserves Walsh degree, and the first/higher
coupling is degree two.  The normalized resolvent expansion
\[
 (I+\theta T_N)^{-1}
 =\sum_{j=0}^{4}(-\theta T_N)^j
 +(-\theta T_N)^5(I+\theta T_N)^{-1}
\]
has $\|T_N\|\le q_\varphi$.  Inserting the Walsh-degree projections turns the
first five terms into finite Motzkin path families.  The two-particle dipole,
three-particle dipole sheet, repeated skew, pair-return, and first
four-particle sources have finite $H_{-1}$ and $H_{-2}$ Green energies on their
transient relative exclusion graphs.  Periodic variational convergence makes
each coefficient independent of $z$ and gives exactly the displayed
$D_k^{[2]},\ldots,D_k^{[6]}$.  The remainder has absolute value at most
$E_k^{[7]}$.  Letting $z\to\infty$ isolates the instantaneous mass, while
subtracting the values at $z=0$ and $z=\infty$ bounds the finite-frequency
measure.  Subtracting the response polynomial from the bare Fourier rate gives
the diffusivity formula.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[All-order exponential localization in Walsh degree]
\label{thm:renewal-chaos-localization}
Let $\mathcal N$ be the Walsh number operator and let
$T_N(z)$ be the normalized higher-chaos modulation insertion.  For every
$\alpha\ge0$,
\[
 \boxed{
 \|e^{\alpha(\mathcal N-2)}T_N(z)e^{-\alpha(\mathcal N-2)}\|
 \le q_\varphi(1+2\sinh\alpha).}
\]
If
\[
 |\theta|q_\varphi(1+2\sinh\alpha)<1,
\]
then the exact resummed cell corrector satisfies
\[
 \boxed{
 \sum_{r\ge R}\|P_{r,N}\Gamma_N^\theta x_{k,N}\|_2^2
 \le C_{\theta,\alpha}e^{-2\alpha(R-2)}}
\]
uniformly in the cutoff.  Thus large chaos degree is exponentially controlled
throughout the strict positivity interval; the remaining nonperturbative
obstruction is spatial $H_{-2}$ localization of arbitrarily long returns
inside each fixed degree.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The normalized insertion changes Walsh degree by at most one.  Conjugation by
$e^{\alpha\mathcal N}$ therefore multiplies its diagonal, raising, and lowering
blocks by $1,e^\alpha,e^{-\alpha}$, and the positive form bound gives the
stated weighted norm.  The strict inequality makes the weighted Neumann series
for $(I+\theta T_N(z))^{-1}$ converge uniformly.  Applying it to the degree-two
source and removing the weight gives the exponential tail.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Parity-corrected collision Hodge decomposition]
\label{thm:collision-parity-Hodge}
Let $G=(V,E)$ be a finite connected collision-support graph.  On its edge
coefficient space define the odd and even incidence maps
\[
 \partial_-e_{ij}=e_j-e_i,
 \qquad
 \partial_+e_{ij}=e_i+e_j.
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{\C^E=\Ran\partial_-^*\oplus\Ker\partial_-,
 \qquad
 \C^E=\Ran\partial_+^*\oplus\Ker\partial_+.}
\]
The odd collision dipole uses $\partial_-$, while the transverse-constant
threshold channel uses $\partial_+$.  If
$\mathbf b_G=\sum_{e\in E}e$ is the coefficient of a spatially constant
reflecting state, then
\[
 \boxed{\mathbf b_G=\frac12\partial_+^*\one_V,}
\]
so its image in the even cycle quotient $\Ker\partial_+$ is zero.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The two orthogonal decompositions are the standard identity
$\C^E=\Ran D^*\oplus\Ker D$ applied to the two incidence matrices.  Pair
interchange changes the sign of an odd transverse function and fixes an even
one, which identifies the corresponding incidence actions.  Finally every
edge has two endpoints, so the coefficient of each edge in
$\partial_+^*\one_V$ is two.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[All-degree hard-core corrector profile]
\label{thm:renewal-hard-core-all-degree}
Fix $\delta>0$ and a Fourier test mode of the explicit three-dimensional
modulated renewal--interchange regulator.  For every finite Walsh-degree
ceiling $R$ and every
\[
 |\theta|q_\varphi\le1-\delta,
\]
the exact hard-core cell corrector has a representation
\[
 P_{r,N}\Gamma_N^\theta f
 =\frac{d_{N,k}}{N}\,\mathcal U_{r,N}^{(k)}
   \psi_{r,N}^{\theta,k},
 \qquad 2\le r\le R,
\]
with
\[
 \boxed{
 \sup_N\sum_{r=2}^{R}
 \left(
  \|\psi_{r,N}^{\theta,k}\|_2^2
  +\mathcal E_{r,N}(\psi_{r,N}^{\theta,k})
 \right)<\infty.}
\]
Consequently
\[
 \boxed{
 \sum_{r=2}^{R}\|P_{r,N}\Gamma_N^\theta f\|_2^2
 =O_{R,f,\theta,\delta}(N^{-2}).}
\]
Together with \Cref{thm:renewal-chaos-localization}, this gives
\[
 \boxed{\|\Gamma_N^\theta f\|_2\longrightarrow0}
\]
for every fixed strict coupling $|\theta|q_\varphi<1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
At $\theta=0$, degree $r$ is the $r$-particle exclusion sheet with massive
operator $grI+\kappa N^2\mathsf L_{r,N}$.  One modulation insertion changes
Walsh degree by at most one and creates a neutral first-difference source on a
codimension-three collision sheet.  The three-dimensional Green estimate
therefore maps the source into a uniformly bounded relative $H_{-2}$ and
Dirichlet potential.

It remains to include all intersecting hard-core collision channels.  Induct
on the connected collision-support graph.  After all proper connected
subclusters have been inverted, a failure of the mixed-scale inverse would,
by the finite Feshbach alternative, reconstruct a zero-energy reflecting bulk
state.  Positivity of the exclusion Dirichlet form makes that state spatially
constant on the connected configuration graph.  Its odd boundary trace is
zero, and by \Cref{thm:collision-parity-Hodge} its even trace is the unsigned
star $\mathbf b_G\in\Ran\partial_+^*$, which belongs to the already inverted
proper-subcluster cut sector.  It therefore has zero image in the new quotient,
a contradiction.  This closes every connected cluster; disconnected supports
factor over their connected components.  There are finitely many supports
below a fixed ceiling, giving the displayed uniform profile.

The fluctuation source carries the external factor $d_{N,k}/N$, which gives
the $N^{-2}$ squared-norm estimate.  First send $N\to\infty$ at fixed $R$.
The high-degree energy tail of \Cref{thm:renewal-chaos-localization} is
uniformly exponentially small and, since $C_N^0\succeq gR$ above degree $R$,
also controls the high-degree $L^2$ norm.  Sending $R\to\infty$ proves complete
corrector disappearance.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Orbit-orthogonal bracket concentration]
\label{lem:renewal-orbit-bracket}
Let $f_N$ be a centered rooted Walsh polynomial of degree at most $R$ on the
product stationary state of $N^3$ sites and put
\[
 \operatorname{Av}_Nf_N=N^{-3}\sum_x\tau_xf_N.
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{
 \operatorname{Var}(\operatorname{Av}_Nf_N)
 \le\frac{R}{N^3}\|f_N\|_2^2.}
\]
The same estimate, multiplied by $T^2$, controls the supremum of the time
integral on a stationary interval $[0,T]$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Expand $f_N$ in orthogonal Walsh monomials and group supports into translation
orbits.  Distinct orbits are orthogonal.  For one orbit, the number of rooted
representatives times the stabilizer size equals the support cardinality,
which is at most $R$.  Parseval gives the stated factor $R/N^3$.  For the time
integral use
$\sup_{t\le T}|\int_0^tg_s\,\dd s|^2\le T\int_0^T|g_s|^2\,\dd s$ and
stationarity.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Full fixed-coupling generalized OU branch]
\label{thm:renewal-fixed-coupling-OU}
Assume the deterministic signed continuum packet for the explicit modulated
renewal--interchange regulator, convergence of its shorted first-chaos forms,
stationary Gaussian initial convergence, and the jump Lindeberg condition.
Then for every fixed
\[
 \boxed{|\theta|q_\varphi<1}
\]
the complete hard-core fluctuation field converges to the generalized
Ornstein--Uhlenbeck field whose drift is the limiting shorted generator
$S_\infty$ and whose covariance is
\[
 \boxed{Q(f,h)=2\langle f,S_\infty h\rangle.}
\]
All finite particle collision clusters and every Walsh degree are included.
No additional fixed-degree collision nonresonance or numerical screen
certificate remains for this regulator.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Corrector disappearance is
\Cref{thm:renewal-hard-core-all-degree}.  At every fixed degree ceiling,
\Cref{lem:renewal-orbit-bracket} and the uniform relative $L^2$ and Dirichlet
bounds make the corrected predictable bracket self-average at volume rate.
The exponential degree tail removes the ceiling by a double limit.  The
expected corrected bracket equals twice the Schur-short action by the exact
corrector Pythagoras in \Cref{thm:modulated-renewal-Schur-Mori}.  The
martingale functional central limit theorem, the assumed Lindeberg condition,
and convergence of the shorted drift identify the unique generalized OU
martingale problem.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[Scope of the all-degree theorem]
The all-degree theorem closes the stochastic analysis of the explicitly
specified modulated renewal--interchange regulator.  It does not infer a
connected interaction, the modulated rate, or its physical source from the
fresh one-cell Store table.  Occurrence of that regulator and convergence of
its deterministic shorted forms remain physical connected-panel and cutoff
certificates.
\end{firewall}


\subsection{Connected information actions, operational holonomy, and tetrahedral coercivity}
\label{sec:connected-action-holonomy}

The efficient connected Gram determines more than adjacency.  Its Hessian
separates canonical transport from a genuinely additional edge source and,
on the zero-innovation branch, reconstructs an operational connection whose
cycle products are finite curvature witnesses.

\begin{theorem}[Connected edge-action Pythagoras]
\label{thm:connected-edge-action-Pythagoras}
Let a physically loaded connected Hessian on endpoint coefficient spaces have
block form
\[
 \mathbb H_e=
 \begin{pmatrix}A_e&-C_e\\-C_e^*&B_e\end{pmatrix}\succeq0,
 \qquad A_e\succ0,\quad B_e\succ0.
\]
Define
\[
 U_{x\leftarrow y,e}=A_e^{-1}C_e,
 \qquad
 R_{y\mid x,e}=B_e-C_e^*A_e^{-1}C_e\succeq0.
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{
 \left\langle\binom{x}{y},\mathbb H_e\binom{x}{y}\right\rangle
 =\|x-U_{x\leftarrow y,e}y\|_{A_e}^2
  +\langle y,R_{y\mid x,e}y\rangle.}
\]
The excess connected source dimension is $\rank R_{y\mid x,e}$.  The residual
vanishes exactly when
\[
 U_{x\leftarrow y,e}^*A_eU_{x\leftarrow y,e}=B_e;
\]
for equal endpoint dimensions the router is then a metric unitary.  A positive
residual is retained as an additional physical edge source.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Complete the square in the positive block quadratic form.  Positivity gives the
Schur residual.  Whitening by $A_e^{1/2},B_e^{1/2}$ shows that
$A_e^{-1/2}C_eB_e^{-1/2}$ is a contraction, and its defect rank equals the
rank of the Schur residual.  The zero-residual identity follows by taking the
$A_e$-Gram of the reduced router.
\end{proof}


\begin{theorem}[Resistance reconstruction and coframe calibration]
\label{thm:action-resistance-coframe}
Let $H\succeq0$ be a connected action Hessian on a centered finite point
space $W=\one^\perp$, so $\Ker H=\Span\{\one\}$.  Define the resistance
matrix
\[
 \mathscr R_{ij}=(e_i-e_j)^*H^\dagger(e_i-e_j),
 \qquad
 P_0=I-|I|^{-1}\one\one^*.
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{
 H^\dagger=-\frac12P_0\mathscr RP_0,
 \qquad
 H=\left(-\frac12P_0\mathscr RP_0\right)^\dagger.}
\]
Thus the complete resistance geometry reconstructs the positive action,
including all conductances and its support graph.

Let $A,C:W\to\mathcal Y$ synthesize, respectively, the action source and an
independently physical transport or coframe source in one carrier, with
\[
 H=A^*A\succ0,
 \qquad G=C^*C\succ0,
 \qquad X=A^*C.
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{
 R_{C\mid A}:=G-X^*H^{-1}X=C^*(I-P_A)C\succeq0,
 \qquad P_A=AH^{-1}A^*.}
\]
It vanishes exactly when the two source ranges coincide; on that branch the
unique router is $T_{C/A}=H^{-1}X$ and
$G=T_{C/A}^*HT_{C/A}$.  If a common physical symmetry acts irreducibly on
$W$ with scalar commutant and both sources are equivariant, then
\[
 \boxed{R_{C\mid A}=0\Longrightarrow C=cA,
 \qquad G=|c|^2H.}
\]
Consequently the coframe resistance metric is $|c|^{-1}$ times the action
resistance metric.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
For a centered symmetric matrix $K=H^\dagger$, the resistance matrix satisfies
$\mathscr R_{ij}=K_{ii}+K_{jj}-2K_{ij}$.  Double centering removes the two
diagonal rank-one terms and gives $P_0\mathscr RP_0=-2K$, proving the
reconstruction.  For the source comparison,
$P_A$ is the projection onto $\Ran A$ and
\[
 C=AH^{-1}X+(I-P_A)C
\]
is an orthogonal decomposition.  Taking Grams gives the Schur residual and its
range criterion.  Zero residual yields $C=AT_{C/A}$.  Equivariance then makes
$T_{C/A}$ commute with the irreducible coefficient action, so Schur's lemma
makes it scalar.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[Positive resistance geometry is not Lorentzian geometry]
A vanishing action--coframe residual calibrates two positive source metrics.
It does not supply a normal/tangential splitting, Lorentzian signature, causal
cone, or hypersurface-deformation algebra.  Those remain independently loaded
signed, symplectic, or common-action structures.
\end{firewall}


\begin{theorem}[Operational connection, holonomy, and tree observability]
\label{thm:operational-holonomy-coercivity}
Assume the zero-edge-innovation branch on a finite connected graph, and write
$U_e$ for the metric-unitary routers.  Under vertex gauge transformations
$U_e\mapsto Q_yU_eQ_x^*$, path transport is covariant and closed-path holonomy
is conjugated.  Hence
\[
 \operatorname{spec}U_c,
 \qquad \sigma_j(I-U_c),
 \qquad (I-U_c)^*(I-U_c)
\]
are gauge-invariant finite coordinates.  For a spanning tree $T$, there is a
tree gauge in which every tree router is the identity and each non-tree router
is the holonomy of its fundamental cycle.  The connection is flat exactly
when all these finitely many holonomies are the identity.

Let
\[
 q_U(f)=\sum_{e:x\to y}\kappa_e\|f_y-U_ef_x\|^2
\]
with each unoriented edge counted once.  Put
\[
 C_T=\sum_{x\in V}\sum_{e\in p_x}\kappa_e^{-1},
 \qquad
 d_T^{\rm nt}=\max_x\sum_{\substack{e\notin T\\e\ni x}}\kappa_e,
\]
and let $\mathcal H_Tv=(\sqrt{\kappa_e}(I-H_e)v)_{e\notin T}$,
$K_T=\Ker\mathcal H_T$, and
$\sigma_T^2=\lambda_{\min}^+(\mathcal H_T^*\mathcal H_T)$.  Then
\[
 \boxed{
 \dist(f,\mathscr P_U)^2
 \le C_{\rm TH}q_U(f),
 \qquad
 C_{\rm TH}=2C_T+
 \frac{6|V|(1+d_T^{\rm nt}C_T)}{\sigma_T^2},}
\]
where $\mathscr P_U$ is the space of global parallel sections.  Therefore
$\lambda_U^+\ge C_{\rm TH}^{-1}$.  Uniform tree geometry and a positive
holonomy-observability margin give a regulator-uniform curved Hodge floor.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Gauge by parallel transport along the rooted tree.  If $a_x=f_x-f_o$, weighted
Cauchy--Schwarz along the unique tree path gives
$\sum_x\|a_x\|^2\le C_Tq_U(f)$.  On a non-tree edge,
\[
 f_y-H_ef_x=(I-H_e)f_o+a_y-H_ea_x.
\]
Squaring, summing, and using $d_T^{\rm nt}$ gives
\[
 \|\mathcal H_Tf_o\|^2
 \le3(1+d_T^{\rm nt}C_T)q_U(f).
\]
The definition of $\sigma_T$ controls the component of $f_o$ orthogonal to
$K_T$.  The constant tree-gauge field with value $P_{K_T}f_o$ is parallel.
Combining the root estimate with the tree deviations gives the displayed
constant.  The gauge and flatness statements follow by telescopic cancellation
of vertex gauges and the fundamental-cycle basis.
\end{proof}

Let $F$ be a finite whitened fibre carrying a unitary representation
$\rho:S_4\to\U(F)$.  Put
$e_0=(1,2)$, $k=(34)$, $s=(12)$, $r=(123)$, and
$R=\rho(r^{-1})$.

\begin{theorem}[One-orbit tetrahedral connection and curvature]
\label{thm:tetrahedral-prototype-connection}
An $S_4$-covariant unitary connection on the directed edges of $K_4$ is
uniquely determined by the prototype $U=U_{12}$.  It exists exactly when
\[
 [U,\rho(k)]=0,
\]
and orientation reversal holds exactly when
\[
 \rho(s)U\rho(s)^*=U^*.
\]
The prototype triangle holonomy is
\[
 \boxed{H_{123}=(RU)^3,}
\]
and every other oriented triangle holonomy is conjugate to $H_{123}$ or its
adjoint.  Hence one triangle decides exact flatness.

For a near-identity prototype $U_h=e^{-hA}$ satisfying the infinitesimal
stabilizer and reversal relations, one has
\[
 H_{123}(h)=I+O(h^2)
 \iff
 A+RAR^{-1}+R^2AR^{-2}=0.
\]
On this area-scaled branch,
\[
 \boxed{
 H_{123}(h)=I+\frac{h^2}{2}[A,RAR^{-1}]+O(h^3).}
\]
A nonzero dense connection is impossible on a trivial fibre and, under the
full untwisted real orthogonal $S_4$ action, on the bare standard tetrahedral
fibre $W_0$.  It therefore requires an internal multiplicity, a projective or
orientation twist, weaker router symmetry, or an independently loaded
connection source.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Transitivity on ordered edges gives
$U_{g1,g2}=\rho(g)U\rho(g)^*$.  Independence of the choice of $g$ is exactly
commutation with the ordered-edge stabilizer $\{1,k\}$.  The transposition $s$
reverses the prototype edge, giving the adjoint condition.  Transport of the
prototype by $r,r^{-1}$ gives
$U_{23}=R^{-1}UR$ and $U_{31}=RUR^{-1}$, whence
$U_{31}U_{23}U_{12}=(RU)^3$.

Moving the three order-three symmetry factors to the left yields
\[
 (Re^{-hA})^3
 =e^{-hRAR^{-1}}e^{-hR^2AR^{-2}}e^{-hA}.
\]
Its linear term is minus the orbit sum.  When that sum vanishes, the ordered
second-order term reduces to $\frac12[A,RAR^{-1}]$.  On a trivial fibre the
reversal law makes a near-identity unitary self-adjoint and hence the identity.
For the real standard fibre write $A=[a]_\times$.  Orthogonal conjugation
obeys
$Q[a]_\times Q^{-1}=\det(Q)[Qa]_\times$.  The stabilizer $(34)$ and reversal
$(12)$ are odd permutations, so their infinitesimal conditions become
$\rho(34)a=-a$ and $\rho(12)a=a$; their common solution is
$\R(e_3-e_4)$.  The order-three element is orientation preserving.  For
$a=e_3-e_4$ its orbit sum is
$e_1+e_2+e_3-3e_4\ne0$, so the area-cancellation condition forces $a=0$ and
hence $A=0$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Prototype triangle controls the complete tetrahedral gap]
\label{thm:tetrahedral-prototype-gap}
Assume the pairwise $S_4$ branch of \Cref{thm:S4-support-prototype}.  Let the
common fibre metric satisfy $mI\preceq G\preceq MI$, let
$\delta=\|I-H_{123}\|$, and suppose each actual edge Hessian differs from its
ideal router form by a self-adjoint block of norm at most $\varepsilon$.  After
a star-tree gauge, every field with $\sum_{i=1}^4f_i=0$ satisfies
\[
 \boxed{
 q_{\rm act}(f)
 \ge(4m-2M\delta-6\varepsilon)\|f\|^2.}
\]
Thus one prototype edge and one prototype triangle give a positive local Hodge
floor whenever
\[
 \boxed{4m>2M\delta+6\varepsilon.}
\]
If $\delta=O(h^2)$ and $\varepsilon=o(1)$, the gap converges to the flat value
$4m$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
In the star-tree gauge the three tree routers are the identity.  Every non-tree
router is a triangle holonomy and hence differs from the identity by at most
$\delta$.  The flat complete-graph identity gives
\[
 \sum_{i<j}\|f_j-f_i\|_G^2=4\sum_i\|f_i\|_G^2
 \ge4m\|f\|^2
\]
under the zero-sum condition.  Only three non-tree edges differ from the flat
form; their total quadratic error is at most $2M\delta\|f\|^2$.  The six edge
Hessian errors contribute at most $6\varepsilon\|f\|^2$.  Subtracting proves
the estimate.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Prototype action to physical-time Ward closure]
\label{cor:prototype-Ward-closure}
Let $L_X$ be the operator reconstructed from the connected prototype action and
$W_X=(I+\tau_XL_X)^{-1}$.  After the primitive martingale source is shorted, let
$K_X$ be the actual predictable mean step.  If
\[
 \|K_X-W_X\|=o(\tau_X),
\]
the noise-shorted Ward Gram is $o(\tau_X^2)$ and, uniformly for
$0\le n\tau_X\le T$,
\[
 \|K_X^n-W_X^n\|\le n\|K_X-W_X\|\longrightarrow0.
\]
If the connected forms converge in Mosco sense, then
\[
 \boxed{K_X^{\lfloor t/\tau_X\rfloor}\longrightarrow e^{-tL_\infty}}
\]
strongly on compact time intervals, and every uniform prototype coercive floor
passes to the limit.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The shorted Ward Gram is the Gram of $K_X-W_X$.  The telescoping identity for
$K_X^n-W_X^n$ and contractivity give the finite-time estimate.
\Cref{thm:GT-Mosco} gives convergence of the minimizing movements to the
limiting semigroup, and the Mosco lower bound passes the uniform coercive
estimate to the limit.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[What the one-orbit theorem leaves physical]
The one-orbit reduction does not assert that the microscopic process lies on
the pairwise branch, that the edge Schur innovation vanishes, or that the
required internal fibre or twist occurs.  It reduces the complete local audit
to one pair, one triple, one four-body support Gram, one edge Hessian, one
triangle holonomy, and one predictable mean-step residual.
\end{firewall}

\subsection{Predeclared filtration locality and finite feedback modules}
\label{sec:universal-locality-feedback}

\begin{definition}[Source-filtration locality residual]
Let $P_0\le P_1\le\cdots$ be a predeclared increasing family of source
projections and let $T$ be a contraction.  Define
\[
 \boxed{\ell_n(T)=\|(I-P_{n+1})TP_n\|.}
\]
The filtration is exact one-step local when every $\ell_n(T)$ vanishes.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Finite propagation from source-locality residuals]
\label{thm:source-locality-propagation}
For every $k\ge1$,
\[
 \boxed{\|(I-P_{n+k})T^kP_n\|
 \le\sum_{j=0}^{k-1}\ell_{n+j}(T).}
\]
Hence exact one-step locality gives
$T^kP_n\mathcal H\subseteq P_{n+k}\mathcal H$.  Uniformly summable or decaying
residuals give the corresponding quasilocal approximation bound.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
For a unit vector $v\in P_n\mathcal H$, put $v_j=T^jv$ and
$e_j=(I-P_{n+j})v_j$.  Since $T$ is contractive,
\[
 \|e_{j+1}\|
 \le\|(I-P_{n+j+1})TP_{n+j}v_j\|+\|Te_j\|
 \le\ell_{n+j}(T)+\|e_j\|.
\]
Induction from $e_0=0$ gives the sum.  Taking the supremum proves the operator
bound.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Universal feedback-memory theorem]
\label{thm:universal-feedback-memory}
Let $T_0$ be an old finite transfer and let an enlarged transfer be
\[
 \widetilde T=\begin{pmatrix}A&B\\ C&D\end{pmatrix}
\]
relative to the old carrier and an external carrier.  If
$X_n=P\widetilde T^nJ$, then
\[
 \boxed{K_k=BD^kC,\qquad
 X_{n+1}=AX_n+\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}K_{n-1-j}X_j,\quad X_0=I,}
\]
and
\[
 \boxed{\sum_{n\ge0}X_nz^n
 =[I-zA-z^2B(I-zD)^{-1}C]^{-1}.}
\]
Moreover,
\[
 \boxed{X_n=T_0^n\ \forall n
 \iff A=T_0\text{ and }BD^kC=0\ \forall k\ge0.}
\]
In finite external dimension it is enough to test
$0\le k<\dim\mathcal E$.  The stabilized block-Hankel rank of
$[BD^{i+j}C]_{i,j}$ is the minimal added linear feedback memory.  More
precisely, it is the dimension of the canonical quotient
\[
 \frac{\Span\{D^kC\mathcal L:k\ge0\}}
 {\Span\{D^kC\mathcal L:k\ge0\}
  \cap\bigcap_{k\ge0}\Ker(BD^k)},
\]
which is the unique reachable--observable realization of the returned kernels.
The kernels themselves are recursively recovered from the compressed powers
by \Cref{thm:pre-renewal-visible-recovery}.

If $\widetilde T$ and $T_0$ are contractions, then
\[
 \boxed{\|X_n-T_0^n\|
 \le n\|A-T_0\|+
 \sum_{k=0}^{n-2}(n-1-k)\|BD^kC\|.}
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Block multiplication groups every old-to-old path according to its last
external excursion, giving the convolution equation; summing formal series
gives the Schur resolvent.  Equality at $n=1$ gives $A=T_0$.  Once
$K_0,\ldots,K_{r-1}$ vanish, the first possible additional term in
$X_{r+2}$ is $K_r$, so induction gives the exact criterion.  Cayley--Hamilton
reduces the infinite list to the first $\dim\mathcal E$ powers.  Standard
reachable/observable realization theory identifies the stabilized Hankel rank
with the external reachable subspace modulo its future-unobservable part.

For the norm estimate, put $e_n=\|X_n-T_0^n\|$.  Contractivity and the
convolution equation give
\[
 e_{n+1}\le e_n+\|A-T_0\|+\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}\|BD^kC\|.
\]
Iterating from $e_0=0$ and reversing the order of summation yields the displayed
bound.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Source-minimal retained-tail derivative]
\label{cor:GT-returned-tail-derivative}
For a retained-plus-tail linearization
$\begin{psmallmatrix}A&B\\C&D\end{psmallmatrix}$ with $\|D\|<1$, the exact
reduced derivative on the invariant tail graph is
\[
 \boxed{
 A+B(I-D)^{-1}C
 =A+\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}BD^nC.}
 \tag{RT.1}
\]
It depends only on the reachable--observable returned quotient already
identified in \Cref{thm:universal-feedback-memory}.  The stabilized Hankel rank
of $[BD^{i+j}C]$ is the exact minimum tail dimension relevant to this retained
linear response.
\end{corollary}

\begin{theorem}[Associativity of invariant-tail elimination]
\label{thm:GT-staged-tail-elimination}
Let the tail split as $R=R_1\oplus R_2$, write
\[
 B=(B_1\ B_2),\quad C=\binom{C_1}{C_2},\quad
 D=\begin{pmatrix}D_{11}&D_{12}\\D_{21}&D_{22}\end{pmatrix},
\]
and assume $\|D\|<1$.  Put $R_2^0=(I-D_{22})^{-1}$ and
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \widetilde A&=A+B_2R_2^0C_2,&
 \widetilde B&=B_1+B_2R_2^0D_{21},\\
 \widetilde C&=C_1+D_{12}R_2^0C_2,&
 \widetilde D&=D_{11}+D_{12}R_2^0D_{21}.
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{RT.2}
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{
 A+B(I-D)^{-1}C
 =\widetilde A+\widetilde B(I-\widetilde D)^{-1}\widetilde C.}
 \tag{RT.3}
\]
Thus exact elimination of finitely many tail strata is order independent.  A
stratum with no direct retained entrance can still be indispensable through a
path entering it from another tail stratum and returning to the head.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Solve the $R_2$ component of the invariant-tail equation
$r=Cx+Dr$ and substitute it into the $R_1$ component.  The resulting system is
\textup{(RT.2)}, and uniqueness of the full solution gives \textup{(RT.3)}.
Repeated elimination is block Gaussian elimination of the same invertible
system.
\end{proof}

\begin{countertheorem}[Zero aggregate self-energy is not no return]
\label{cth:GT-return-cancellation}
The equality $B(I-D)^{-1}C=0$ does not imply that the returned quotient
vanishes.  There are finite stable packets with nonzero returned words which
cancel in the aggregate sum.
\end{countertheorem}

\begin{proof}
Take a one-dimensional retained space, a two-dimensional tail,
$0<t<1$, and
\[
 C=\binom10,\qquad
 D=\begin{pmatrix}0&0\\t&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad
 B=\begin{pmatrix}1&-t^{-1}\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Then $BD^0C=1$, $BDC=-1$, and $BD^nC=0$ for $n\ge2$.  The aggregate correction
vanishes, while the returned Hankel sequence has positive rank.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[Scope of the returned quotient]
A tail direction absent from the returned quotient is silent only for the
declared linear retained response at the chosen point.  It may still affect
higher nonlinear jets, another observable, reflection positivity, global
stability, or a different boundary row.  The quotient is source minimal for
one response problem; it is not a license to delete the full physical shell
law.
\end{firewall}

\begin{theorem}[Connected residual under exact factorization]
\label{thm:connected-residual-factorization}
Suppose a parameterized operational transfer and state factor exactly as
\[
 T_{\boldsymbol\theta}=\bigotimes_{c\in\mathcal C}T_{c,\theta_c},
 \qquad
 \Omega_{\boldsymbol\theta}=\bigotimes_{c\in\mathcal C}
 \Omega_{c,\theta_c},
\]
and a centered source is supported in one component $c_0$.  Then every mixed
Taylor coefficient of its vacuum-relative future residual vanishes whenever
the differentiated components contain a connected component disjoint from
$c_0$.  Thus nonzero coefficients are supported on connected interaction
clusters meeting the source.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Split the differentiated components into the component $A$ containing $c_0$
and a disjoint union $B$.  Exact tensor factorization makes the normalized
vacuum-relative source residual equal to its $A$-residual tensored with the
identity on $B$; it is therefore independent of every parameter in $B$.
Every mixed derivative using a parameter from $B$ vanishes.
\end{proof}


\subsection{Infinite-regulator feedback, rational memory, and delay-mass escape}
\label{sec:feedback-limit-classification}

For each cutoff, let
\[
 K_{k,n}=B_nD_n^kC_n
\]
be the returned-feedback kernel of the old visible carrier.  Pointwise
convergence in the delay variable does not control the total memory: mass may
move to later delays while every fixed coefficient tends to zero.

\begin{theorem}[Exact operator-valued \texorpdfstring{$\ell^1$}{l1} feedback limit]
\label{thm:feedback-l1-limit}
Assume $K_{k,n}\to K_k$ in operator norm for every fixed $k$.  Then
\[
 \sum_{k\ge0}\|K_{k,n}-K_k\|\longrightarrow0
\]
if and only if
\[
 \boxed{
 \lim_{R\to\infty}\sup_n\sum_{k\ge R}\|K_{k,n}\|=0.}
\]
On this branch $K\in\ell^1$, and if $A_n\to A$, the retained responses satisfy
the limiting Volterra recursion
\[
 \boxed{
 X_{m+1}=AX_m+\sum_{j=0}^{m-1}K_{m-1-j}X_j,
 \qquad X_0=I.}
\]
If
\[
 q:=\sup_n\|A_n\|+\sup_n\sum_k\|K_{k,n}\|<1,
\]
the response generating functions
\[
 \mathscr X_n(z)
 =[I-zA_n-z^2\mathscr K_n(z)]^{-1}
\]
converge uniformly on $|z|\le1$, with
\[
 \sup_{|z|\le1}\|\mathscr X_n(z)-\mathscr X(z)\|
 \le\frac{\|A_n-A\|+\|K_n-K\|_{\ell^1}}{(1-q)^2}.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The forward implication gives uniform tail control by splitting the tail of
$K_{\cdot,n}$ into the tail of $K$ and the $\ell^1$ difference.  Conversely,
choose $R$ with uniformly small tails; convergence of the finitely many
coefficients below $R$ gives convergence of the heads, proving $\ell^1$
convergence.  Passing to the limit in the finite convolution gives the Volterra
recursion.  On the unit disk,
$\|zA_n+z^2\mathscr K_n(z)\|\le q$, so the inverses are bounded by
$(1-q)^{-1}$.  The resolvent identity gives the displayed estimate.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Operator-valued Hankel realization]
\label{thm:feedback-Hankel-realization}
For a kernel $K=(K_k)_{k\ge0}$ define
\[
 \mathbb H_{p,q}(K)=[K_{i+j}]_{0\le i<p,\ 0\le j<q},
 \qquad
 r_{\rm fb}(K)=\sup_{p,q}\rank\mathbb H_{p,q}(K).
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{
 r_{\rm fb}(K)=r<\infty
 \iff
 K_k=BD^kC}
\]
for a reachable and observable $r$-dimensional linear realization.  Every
realization has dimension at least $r$, minimal realizations are uniquely
similar, and
\[
 \mathscr K(z)=B(I-zD)^{-1}C
\]
is rational.  For a minimal finite realization,
\[
 (K_k)\in\ell^1\iff\rho(D)<1.
\]
Thus finite memory dimension and temporal summability are independent axes.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
If $K_k=BD^kC$, the block Hankel factors as an observability matrix times a
controllability matrix and has rank at most the state dimension.  Conversely,
finite stabilized Hankel rank identifies the quotient of finite past columns
by equality against all future rows; the shift of a column descends to a
well-defined state transition $D$, while the zeroth row and column define
$B$ and $C$.  Reachability and observability are built into the quotient and
its dimension is the stabilized rank.  The standard reachable--observable
argument gives unique similarity.  The rational formula is the geometric
series.  In finite dimension, $BD^kC$ is summable on the minimal realization
exactly when every visible eigenvalue of $D$ lies strictly inside the unit disk;
minimality makes every eigenvalue visible.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Corrected feedback-memory classification]
\label{thm:feedback-limit-classification}
Every limiting feedback kernel belongs to exactly one row and one column of
\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c}
 & K\in\ell^1 & K\notin\ell^1\\ \hline
r_{\rm fb}(K)<\infty
 &\text{stable rational memory}
 &\text{persistent rational memory}\\
r_{\rm fb}(K)=\infty
 &\text{infinite-dimensional short memory}
 &\text{infinite-dimensional long memory}.
\end{array}
\]
All four branches occur.  Uniformly bounded finite-stage Hankel ranks imply a
finite-dimensional limiting realization under fixed-delay convergence, but do
not by themselves give one transition matrix reusable at every cutoff.
A strict realization arrow or one common annihilating recurrence is sufficient
for such reusable memory.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The table is the Cartesian product of the two independent properties in
\Cref{thm:feedback-l1-limit,thm:feedback-Hankel-realization}.  The examples
$2^{-k}$, $1$, $1/(k+1)!$, and $1/(k+1)$ realize the four entries; the last two
have nonrational generating functions and hence infinite Hankel rank.  Every
finite Hankel minor passes to the pointwise limit, so a uniform rank bound
passes to the limit.  However the rank-one family $K_{k,n}=\lambda_n^k$ with
infinitely many distinct $\lambda_n$ cannot be realized by one fixed finite
matrix, since its transfer functions have infinitely many distinct poles.
Strict realization intertwiners give a finite direct-limit carrier, while a
common recurrence gives the usual companion realization.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Temporal-tail and rank-growth witnesses]
\label{thm:feedback-witnesses}
If the uniform $\ell^1$ tail condition fails, there are cutoffs $n_j$, delay
intervals $I_j$ escaping to infinity, and $\varepsilon>0$ such that
\[
 \sum_{k\in I_j}\|K_{k,n_j}\|\ge\varepsilon.
\]
After a subsequence, either:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(T\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item an atomic delayed route survives:
      $\|K_{k_j,n_j}\|\ge\eta>0$ for some $k_j\to\infty$; or
\item the escape is diffuse:
      $\sup_{k\in I_j}\|K_{k,n_j}\|\to0$ while $|I_j|\to\infty$.
\end{enumerate}
In finite input dimension, one normalized input vector detects a fixed fraction
of every diffuse packet.

If no memory of dimension $M$ represents the family, some finite feedback
Hankel block satisfies
\[
 \boxed{\sigma_{M+1}(\mathbb H_{p,q}(K_n))>0.}
\]
Its left and right singular vectors are a finite delayed-source experiment
excluding $M$ recurrent coordinates.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Failure of uniform tail tightness gives the escaping finite intervals.  If the
largest coefficient on a subsequence has a positive lower bound, choose its
maximizing delay; otherwise the maxima vanish and the fixed total mass forces
the interval lengths to diverge.  Averaging over an orthonormal input basis
shows that one basis direction captures at least the reciprocal input-dimension
fraction of the sum.  The Hankel statement is the Eckart--Young rank criterion:
a realization of dimension $M$ makes every block rank at most $M$, while a
positive $(M+1)$st singular value gives the explicit separating bilinear
combination.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Spatiotemporal feedback influence]
\label{thm:spatiotemporal-feedback}
For the operational atom graph define
\[
 \|L\|_\mu
 :=\sup_i\sum_j e^{\mu d(i,j)}\|Q_jLQ_i\|,
 \qquad
 \kappa_{\mu,\eta}(K)
 :=\sum_{k\ge0}e^{\eta k}\|K_k\|_\mu.
\]
If
\[
 q_{\mu,\eta}
 :=e^\eta\|A\|_\mu
 +e^{2\eta}\kappa_{\mu,\eta}(K)<1,
\]
then the Volterra response satisfies
\[
 \boxed{
 \|Q_jX_mQ_i\|
 \le
 \frac{e^{-\mu d(i,j)}e^{-\eta m}}{1-q_{\mu,\eta}}.}
\]
Long memory and spatial nonlocality remain independent: a kernel may be
nonsummable and on-site, or delay zero and spatially nonlocal.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The weighted influence norm is submultiplicative by the triangle inequality for
the graph distance.  Multiply the Volterra recursion by the temporal weight
$e^{\eta m}$ and take the weighted spatial norm.  The resulting scalar
convolution is dominated by a geometric series with ratio
$q_{\mu,\eta}$.  Removing the spatial and temporal weights gives the estimate.
The two independence examples are immediate from kernels of the form
$K_k=a_kI$ and $K_0=L_{\rm nonlocal}$, respectively.
\end{proof}


% =============================================================================
\subsection{Hodge-screen reduction and canonical field completion of loaded feedback}
\label{sec:Hodge-loaded-feedback}
% =============================================================================

The abstract feedback classification distinguishes delay tails and realization
rank.  On the positive spatial branch, the Hodge screen gives a stronger
conclusion: low loaded modes form a uniformly finite physical carrier at every
fixed resolution, while high modes become a small local correction plus a
compact memory tail.

\begin{theorem}[Fast loaded feedback collapses to a local generator]
\label{thm:fast-feedback-collapse}
Let the compressed physical-step responses satisfy
\[
 X_{0,h}=I,
 \qquad
 X_{n+1,h}=A_hX_{n,h}
 +\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}K_{k,h}X_{n-1-k,h}.
\]
Assume
\[
 \frac{A_h-I}{h}\longrightarrow G,
\]
and suppose there are operators $(R_k)_{k\ge0}$ such that
\[
 \sum_{k\ge0}(k+1)\|R_k\|<\infty,
 \qquad
 \frac1h\sum_{k\ge0}(k+1)\|K_{k,h}-hR_k\|\longrightarrow0.
\]
Then, with $R=\sum_kR_k$,
\[
 \boxed{
 \sup_{0\le nh\le T}
 \|X_{n,h}-e^{nh(G+R)}\|\longrightarrow0}
\]
for every $T<\infty$.  In particular, feedback supported on $O(1)$ raw steps
has vanishing physical delay and renormalizes the local generator rather than
producing a continuum memory kernel.

If $K_{k,h}=B_hD_h^kC_h$, $D_h\to D_0$,
$\|D_h^k\|\le Cr^k$ with $r<1$, and
$h^{-1/2}B_h\to B$, $h^{-1/2}C_h\to C$, then
\[
 \boxed{R=B(I-D_0)^{-1}C.}
\]
If instead $\|B_h\|\|C_h\|=o(h)$, the fast feedback disappears at generator
scale.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The assumptions imply uniform bounds
$\|A_h\|\le1+Ch$ and $\sum_k\|K_{k,h}\|\le Ch$.  Discrete Gronwall therefore
gives a uniform bound on $X_{n,h}$ for $nh\le T$ and, from the recursion,
$\|X_{n+1,h}-X_{n,h}\|=O(h)$.  Rewrite the recursion as
\[
 X_{n+1,h}=X_{n,h}+h(G+R)X_{n,h}+hE_{n,h}.
\]
The accumulated error from $(A_h-I)/h-G$ tends to zero.  The kernel
approximation contributes at most
$T h^{-1}\sum_k(k+1)\|K_{k,h}-hR_k\|$.  Replacing
$X_{n-1-k,h}$ by $X_{n,h}$ costs
$O(h\sum_k(k+1)\|R_k\|)$ per unit physical time, and the missing initial tail
has total size
$O(h\sum_k(k+1)\|R_k\|)$.  Thus this is a perturbed Euler scheme for
$\dot X=(G+R)X$ with vanishing integrated error.

In the geometric-decay specialization,
$h^{-1}K_{k,h}\to BD_0^kC$ and dominated convergence holds with the weight
$k+1$.  Summation gives the resolvent correction.  The little-$o$ product
bound makes the normalized kernel mass vanish.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Canonical Markovian completion of finite physical-time memory]
\label{thm:continuum-memory-completion}
Let
\[
 M(t)=Be^{tH}C
\]
be a finite-dimensional physical-time feedback kernel.  The Volterra equation
\[
 \dot x(t)=Gx(t)+\int_0^tM(t-s)x(s)\,\dd s,
 \qquad x(0)=x_0,
\]
is equivalent to the local system
\[
 \boxed{
 \frac{\dd}{\dd t}\binom{x}{y}
 =\begin{pmatrix}G&B\\C&H\end{pmatrix}\binom{x}{y},
 \qquad \binom{x(0)}{y(0)}=\binom{x_0}{0}.}
\]
The source-reachable quotient
\[
 \mathcal F_{\rm mem}
 =\frac{\Span\{H^nCx:n\ge0\}}
 {\{e:BH^ne=0\text{ for every }n\ge0\}}
\]
is the unique minimal auxiliary carrier.  If
\[
 \mathsf H_{p,q}^{\rm mem}=[BH^{i+j}C]_{0\le i<p,\,0\le j<q},
\]
then, for sufficiently large $p,q$,
\[
 \boxed{
 \rank\mathsf H_{p,q}^{\rm mem}=\dim\mathcal F_{\rm mem}.}
\]
Thus the stabilized feedback-Hankel rank is the exact minimum number of
continuum fields needed to Markovianize a finite persistent kernel.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Set
$y(t)=\int_0^te^{(t-s)H}Cx(s)\,\dd s$.  Differentiation gives
$\dot y=Hy+Cx$ and the first equation becomes $\dot x=Gx+By$; variation of
constants proves the converse.  The reachable space and its future-unobservable
subspace are $H$-invariant, so the maps descend to a reachable and observable
realization.  The Hankel block factors as its finite observability matrix times
its finite controllability matrix.  Reachability and observability make these
maps surjective and injective after at most $\dim\mathcal F_{\rm mem}$ rank
changes.  Standard minimal-realization uniqueness gives the final assertion.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Hodge-dominated loaded transient packet]
\label{def:Hodge-loaded-transient}
Let $H_X=H_X^*\succeq\lambda_{\rm tr}I$ act on a loaded transient carrier
$\mathcal E_X$ after every protected zero mode and already-declared persistent
field has been separated.  Let
\[
 \mathsf B_X:\mathcal E_X\to\mathcal H_{0,X},
 \qquad
 \mathsf C_X:\mathcal H_{0,X}\to\mathcal E_X
\]
obey $\|\mathsf B_X\|\le b_*$ and $\|\mathsf C_X\|\le c_*$.  Assume
\[
 \boxed{H_X\succeq c_H\Delta_X^{\rm sp}-C_HI}
\]
with $c_H>0$, where $\Delta_X^{\rm sp}$ satisfies the counting law of
\Cref{thm:operational-Sobolev-Weyl}.  Put
\[
 M_X(t)=\mathsf B_Xe^{-tH_X}\mathsf C_X,
 \qquad
 \Sigma_X(z)=\mathsf B_X(z+H_X)^{-1}\mathsf C_X.
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Hodge-screen spectral reduction of loaded memory]
\label{thm:Hodge-feedback-tail}
Let $P_{X,R}=\one_{[\lambda_{\rm tr},R]}(H_X)$ and
$Q_{X,R}=I-P_{X,R}$.  Under
\Cref{def:Hodge-loaded-transient},
\[
 \boxed{
 \rank P_{X,R}
 \le N_X\!\left(\frac{R+C_H}{c_H}\right)
 \le C_{\rm W,H}(1+R^{3/2})}
\]
for a cutoff-independent constant $C_{\rm W,H}$.  The high-energy memory
satisfies
\[
 \boxed{
 \|\mathsf B_Xe^{-tH_X}Q_{X,R}\mathsf C_X\|
 \le b_*c_*e^{-Rt},}
\]
\[
 \boxed{
 \int_0^\infty\|M_{X,>R}(t)\|\,\dd t
 \le\frac{b_*c_*}{R},
 \qquad
 \int_0^\infty t\|M_{X,>R}(t)\|\,\dd t
 \le\frac{b_*c_*}{R^2}.}
\]
For $\operatorname{Re}z\ge0$,
\[
 \boxed{
 \Sigma_X(z)
 =\Sigma_{X,\le R}(z)+\mathcal R_{X,>R}
  +\mathcal E_{X,>R}(z),}
\]
where
\[
 \mathcal R_{X,>R}
 =\mathsf B_XH_X^{-1}Q_{X,R}\mathsf C_X,
\]
\[
 \boxed{
 \|\mathcal R_{X,>R}\|\le\frac{b_*c_*}{R},
 \qquad
 \|\mathcal E_{X,>R}(z)\|
 \le\frac{|z|b_*c_*}{R^2}.}
\]
Thus high loaded modes contribute a small time-local Feshbach correction and a
smaller frequency-dependent remainder.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
If $u\in P_{X,R}\mathcal E_X$, then
$\langle u,H_Xu\rangle\le R\|u\|^2$.  Hodge domination gives
$\langle u,\Delta_X^{\rm sp}u\rangle\le(R+C_H)c_H^{-1}\|u\|^2$.
The min--max principle bounds the dimension of this subspace by the spatial
counting function, and \Cref{thm:operational-Sobolev-Weyl} gives the
$R^{3/2}$ law.

On $Q_{X,R}\mathcal E_X$, functional calculus gives
$\|e^{-tH_X}Q_{X,R}\|\le e^{-Rt}$; multiplication by the two couplings and
integration give the time-domain estimates.  Split the resolvent with
$P_{X,R}+Q_{X,R}$ and use
\[
 (z+H_X)^{-1}-H_X^{-1}
 =-z(z+H_X)^{-1}H_X^{-1}
\]
on the high-energy range.  Both inverse factors have norm at most $R^{-1}$,
which gives the Feshbach estimates.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Feedback-Hankel compactness and the dimension-three decay law]
\label{thm:feedback-Hankel-Weyl}
Define
\[
 (\mathfrak H_Xf)(t)
 =\int_0^\infty M_X(t+s)f(s)\,\dd s
\]
on $L^2(\R_+;\mathcal H_{0,X})$.  The low-energy truncation has rank at most
$\rank P_{X,R}$ and
\[
 \boxed{
 \|\mathfrak H_X-\mathfrak H_{X,\le R}\|
 \le\frac{b_*c_*}{2R}.}
\]
Consequently every $\mathfrak H_X$ is compact and, uniformly in the cutoff,
\[
 \boxed{s_n(\mathfrak H_X)\le C_{\rm fb}n^{-2/3}}
\]
for all sufficiently large $n$.

For every frequency window $|z|\le Z$, $\operatorname{Re}z\ge0$, and every
$\varepsilon>0$, choosing
$R=(Zb_*c_*/\varepsilon)^{1/2}$ gives an approximation by the finite
Markovian carrier $P_{X,R}\mathcal E_X$ plus the local correction
$\mathcal R_{X,>R}$, with error at most $\varepsilon$ and field count
\[
 \boxed{
 N_{\rm aux}(Z,\varepsilon)
 \le C'\left[1+
 \left(\frac{Zb_*c_*}{\varepsilon}\right)^{3/4}\right].}
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The low-energy Hankel operator factors through $P_{X,R}\mathcal E_X$.
For the high-energy part, its controllability and observability factors have
norms at most $c_*/\sqrt{2R}$ and $b_*/\sqrt{2R}$ by Cauchy--Schwarz and the
spectral exponential bound.  Their product gives the approximation estimate.
Choose $R\asymp n^{2/3}$ in the counting law of
\Cref{thm:Hodge-feedback-tail} to obtain the singular-value decay.  The
finite-frequency statement is the Feshbach remainder estimate with the
specified $R$, and substitution in the $R^{3/2}$ counting law gives the field
count.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[No amorphous loaded-memory branch on the positive spatial sector]
\label{cor:finite-resolution-memory}
Under \Cref{def:Hodge-loaded-transient}, every loaded memory on a fixed compact
region has the exhaustive finite-resolution profile
\[
 \boxed{
 \text{declared physical low modes}
 \;\oplus\;
 \text{canonical finite field innovations}
 \;\oplus\;
 \text{a vanishing high-energy tail}.}
\]
The source and dynamic-containment residuals determine whether each low mode is
already part of the declared connection or matter carrier.  A fixed-resolution
growing-rank or noncompact-memory obstruction can persist only if spatial
low-energy counting, the transient floor, the physical coupling bounds, or
cutoff compactness fails.
\end{corollary}

\begin{firewall}[A local Feshbach correction is not automatically a counterterm]
The operator $\mathcal R_{X,>R}$ is local in physical time, but it is an
admissible action counterterm only after it passes the locality, symmetry,
exactness, common-action, and cutoff-transport tests of the spacetime loading.
High energy alone is also insufficient when the physical couplings grow with
the energy scale.
\end{firewall}

\subsection{Uniform gaps, compactness, and continuum certification}
\label{sec:uniform-continuum-certification}

\begin{theorem}[State compactness and spectral tightness]
\label{thm:state-compactness-tightness}
Let $\mathcal A_{\rm ql}$ be a separable unital quasilocal $C^*$-algebra.
Every sequence of states has a weak-$*$ convergent subsequence.  If the
restrictions converge on a norm-dense local $*$-subalgebra, the full sequence
converges to the unique extension.

For self-adjoint observables $F_X$ affiliated with the finite-stage
representations, a uniform $p$-moment bound
\[
 \sup_X\omega_X(|F_X|^p)\le C_p<\infty
\]
implies the spectral tightness estimate
\[
 \boxed{\omega_X(\mathbf1_{\{|F_X|>R\}})
 \le C_pR^{-p}.}
\]
Bounded-state compactness is automatic; tightness of unbounded continuum fields
is an additional moment certificate.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The state space is weak-$*$ compact by Banach--Alaoglu and metrizable on bounded
sets because the algebra is separable, giving a subsequence.  Pointwise
convergence on a norm-dense subalgebra and uniform norm one determine a unique
continuous extension.  On the spectral subspace $|F_X|>R$ one has
$|F_X|^p\ge R^p$, so functional calculus and positivity give the Markov bound.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Universal coercive continuum handoff]
\label{thm:universal-coercive-continuum}
Let compatible positive contractions $T_X$ act in compatible physical GNS
spaces, with fixed-space projections $E_X$ and source-saturated transient
spaces.  Suppose either:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(H\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item source-native heads have uniform bounds $a_X\le a<1$,
      $d_X\le d<1$, and leakage $b_X\le b$ with
      $b^2<(1-a)(1-d)$; or
\item a predeclared grading has weighted influence constants
      $\kappa_{w,X}\le q<1$.
\end{enumerate}
Then
\[
 \sup_X\|(I-E_X)T_X(I-E_X)\|\le q_*<1,
\]
where in branch~\textup{(H1)} one may take
\[
 q_*=\frac{a+d+\sqrt{(a-d)^2+4b^2}}2.
\]
Consequently the direct-limit transfer has the same noncollapsing contraction
and a gap at least $-\tau^{-1}\log q_*$ at physical time $\tau$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Source saturation and \Cref{thm:universal-Hankel-exhaustion} identify the full
transient norm with the supremum over source heads.  Branch~\textup{(H1)} is
\Cref{thm:sharp-positive-head-tail}, while branch~\textup{(H2)} is the weighted
Schur estimate of \Cref{thm:weighted-source-influence}.  The uniform-gap limit
theorem below transports the common bound to the Hilbert direct limit, and
spectral calculus gives the Hamiltonian gap.
\end{proof}


\subsection{Field tightness, triviality, and the complete limit alternative}
\label{sec:complete-limit-alternative}

\begin{definition}[Field-tightness profile]
\label{def:field-tightness-profile}
For a self-adjoint regulated field $F_n$ in the state $\omega_n$, define
\[
 \Theta_F(R)
 :=\sup_n\omega_n(\mathbf1_{\{|F_n|>R\}}),
 \qquad
 \Xi_F(R)
 :=\sup_n\omega_n\!\left(\frac{F_n^2}{F_n^2+R^2}\right).
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Exact field-tightness and mass-escape alternative]
\label{thm:field-tightness-alternative}
One has
\[
 \boxed{
 \Theta_F(R)\longrightarrow0
 \iff
 \Xi_F(R)\longrightarrow0.}
\]
If the condition fails, there are cutoffs $n_j$, radii $R_j\to\infty$, and
$\varepsilon>0$ such that
\[
 \boxed{
 \omega_{n_j}(\mathbf1_{\{|F_{n_j}|>R_j\}})\ge\varepsilon.}
\]
Thus field nontightness always returns a spectral projection carrying positive
mass to arbitrarily large values.  A uniform positive moment is sufficient for
tightness but is not necessary.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
For $|x|>R$, $x^2/(x^2+R^2)\ge1/2$, while for every $0<M<R$,
\[
 \frac{x^2}{x^2+R^2}
 \le\mathbf1_{\{|x|>M\}}+\frac{M^2}{R^2}.
\]
Functional calculus and expectation give both implications after first sending
$R\to\infty$ and then $M\to\infty$.  Failure of uniform tightness is exactly
the displayed sequence.  Markov's inequality proves the moment sufficient
condition.  Tight distributions with increasingly rare large tails show that
no fixed positive moment bound is necessary.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Source leakage: persistence, splitting, or escape]
\label{thm:source-leakage-limit-alternative}
Let $y_n$ be normalized source-leakage vectors transported to a common Hilbert
carrier.  After passing to a subsequence,
$y_n\rightharpoonup y$, and
\[
 \boxed{\|y_n-y\|^2\longrightarrow1-\|y\|^2.}
\]
Hence the missing source either persists strongly $(\|y\|=1)$, splits into a
persistent and an escaping component $(0<\|y\|<1)$, or escapes every compact
source head $(y=0)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Weak convergence gives
$\langle y_n,y\rangle\to\|y\|^2$.  Expanding
$\|y_n-y\|^2$ and using $\|y_n\|=1$ gives the formula.  The three cases are
exhaustive.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Determining variances and exact operational triviality]
\label{thm:operational-triviality}
Let $\mathscr D$ be a self-adjoint family generating a unital $C^*$-algebra
$\mathcal A$, and let $\omega$ be a state.  Put
\[
 \nu_\omega(a)=\omega(a^2)-\omega(a)^2.
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{
 \nu_\omega(a)=0\ \forall a\in\mathscr D
 \iff
 \dim\mathcal H_\omega=1
 \iff
 \omega\text{ is a character of }\mathcal A.}
\]
If a finite-dimensional selected central component admits no character, then
for every fixed finite self-adjoint generating frame $\mathscr D$ there is a
uniform margin
\[
 \inf_{\omega}\max_{a\in\mathscr D}\nu_\omega(a)>0.
\]
A nondetermining panel cannot certify triviality.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
In the GNS representation,
\[
 \nu_\omega(a)
 =\|(\pi_\omega(a)-\omega(a)I)\Omega_\omega\|^2.
\]
Zero variance makes every generator act scalarly on the cyclic vector.  The
same is then true for every noncommutative polynomial in the generators and,
by norm density, for all of $\mathcal A$.  Cyclicity makes the GNS space one
dimensional and the state multiplicative.  The converse is immediate.  On a
finite character-free component, the continuous function
$\omega\mapsto\max_{a\in\mathscr D}\nu_\omega(a)$ is positive on the compact
state space and therefore has a positive minimum.  If the panel does not
generate the algebra, it may be scalar on the cyclic vector while an orthogonal
factor remains nontrivial.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Complete Grand-Tensor audit profile]
\label{def:complete-GT-profile}
For an audit-ready countably cofinal regulator family, define
\[
 \mathfrak P_{\Grand}
 =(
 \mathfrak P_{\rm cut},
 \mathfrak P_{\rm state},
 \mathfrak P_{\rm ren},
 \mathfrak P_{\rm src},
 \mathfrak P_{\rm form},
 \mathfrak P_{\rm field},
 \mathfrak P_{\rm loc},
 \mathfrak P_{\rm mem},
 \mathfrak P_{\rm coer},
 \mathfrak P_{\rm nontriv}).
\]
The coordinates are respectively the cutoff innovations, projective state
set, renormalization/metric profile, source saturation and leakage, Mosco and
graph-domain profile, field-tightness profile, operational hypergraph and
influence profile, feedback-memory profile, gap/soft-mode profile, and
determining-variance profile.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Universal Grand-Tensor limit and obstruction alternative]
\label{thm:GT-universal-limit-alternative}
Every countably cofinal audit-ready operational regulator family admits a
cofinal subnet on which its complete profile is defined.  The following
nonexclusive branches exhaust the possibilities.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(U\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item \emph{Canonical controlled continuum}: the projective state is unique,
      the renormalization is fixed modulo declared compact gauge, sources and
      forms converge, fields are tight and nontrivial, locality or weighted
      memory is controlled, and the coercive floor remains positive.
