new future-readable coordinate.  For the last claim, the orbit of one occurring
unoriented edge under a group transitive on $\binom X2$ is the complete set of
unordered pairs.  Reversal supplies both orientations.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Cut--cycle decomposition of a complete relational cell]
\label{thm:dimension-cut-cycle}
Let $X=\{1,\ldots,N\}$, let
$u_0=N^{-1/2}\one_N$, and write
$\R^N=\R u_0\oplus W_N$.  Identify the signed edge space of $K_N$ with
$\Lambda^2\R^N$ by $e_i\wedge e_j\leftrightarrow[i\to j]$.  Then
\[
 \boxed{
 C_1(K_N)
 =u_0\wedge W_N\oplus\Lambda^2W_N,}
 \tag{DS.1}
\]
orthogonally, and
\[
 \boxed{
 \partial(u_0\wedge w)=\sqrt N\,w,
 \qquad
 \Ker\partial=\Lambda^2W_N.}
 \tag{DS.2}
\]
Consequently
\[
 \boxed{
 \dim\Ran\partial=N-1,
 \qquad
 \dim\Ker\partial=\binom{N-1}{2}.}
 \tag{DS.3}
\]
The first summand is the endpoint/cut source and the second is the complete
cycle/interference source.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The exterior-square decomposition follows from
$\R^N=\R u_0\oplus W_N$.  For $x,y\in\R^N$, direct expansion of
$\partial(e_i\wedge e_j)=e_j-e_i$ gives
\[
 \partial(x\wedge y)
 =\Bigl(\sum_i x_i\Bigr)y-\Bigl(\sum_i y_i\Bigr)x.
\]
Taking $x=u_0$, $y=w\in W_N$ gives the first identity in
\textup{(DS.2)}, while two vectors in $W_N$ have zero coordinate sum and hence
zero boundary.  The dimension formulas follow.
\end{proof}

\begin{countertheorem}[Metric tomography alone does not select the dimension]
\label{cth:dimension-metric-count}
For every $N\ge2$, the rank-one root tensors of the complete simplex give an
isomorphism
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal T_N:\R^{\binom N2}\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }
 \operatorname{Sym}(W_N),
 \qquad
 (a_{ij})\longmapsto
 \sum_{i<j}a_{ij}\rho_{ij}\rho_{ij}^{\mathsf T},}
 \tag{DS.4}
\]
where $\rho_{ij}=e_j-e_i$.  Hence the equality
\[
 \binom N2=\dim\operatorname{Sym}(W_N)
\]
holds in every simplex dimension and does not by itself distinguish $K_4$.
\end{countertheorem}

\begin{proof}
The dimensions agree because $\dim W_N=N-1$.  If the tensor in
\textup{(DS.4)} vanishes on $W_N$, its extension to $\R^N$ is a weighted graph
Laplacian which also annihilates $\one_N$, and therefore vanishes identically.
Its off-diagonal $(i,j)$ entry is $-a_{ij}$, so all coefficients vanish.  Thus
$\mathcal T_N$ is injective and hence bijective.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Compiler-minimal complete-cell selector]
\label{thm:dimension-K4-selector}
Assume the future-minimal relation cell satisfies:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(D\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item the one-source/one-target, reversal and pair-homogeneity hypotheses of
      \Cref{thm:dimension-pairwise-completion};
\item the temporal--spatial modular coefficient space is
      $\R t\oplus W_N$ and carries a nondegenerate alternating form;
\item the endpoint and complete signed-edge source Grams are faithful, and the
      cycle source is nonzero;
\item among conservative operational completions satisfying the preceding
      queries, the future-readable source innovation is minimal.
\end{enumerate}
Then
\[
 \boxed{N=4,
 \qquad G_{\rm rel}=K_4,
 \qquad W_{\rm sp}=W_4\cong\R^3.}
 \tag{DS.5}
\]
More precisely, the faithful endpoint and edge ranks are
\[
 r_0(N)=N-1,
 \qquad
 r_1(N)=\binom N2.
\]
Nondegeneracy of the alternating form forces $N$ even, and nonzero
interference excludes $N=2$.  Both source ranks are then uniquely minimized at
$N=4$.

Independently, for the standard $S_N$-module $W_N$,
\[
 \boxed{
 \Hom_{S_N}
 \bigl(\Lambda^2W_N,\,W_N\otimes\operatorname{sgn}\bigr)
 =\begin{cases}
   \R,&N=4,\\
   0,&N\ne4,
  \end{cases}}
 \tag{DS.6}
\]
on the nontrivial simplex branch.  Thus $K_4$ is the unique complete cell for
which the entire cycle representation is one oriented spatial copy rather
than an additional inequivalent geometric source.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The alternating space has dimension
$1+\dim W_N=N$, and a nondegenerate alternating form has even dimension.
Since $\Lambda^2W_N\ne0$, one has $N-1\ge2$; together these conditions give
$N\ge4$ even.  The two displayed faithful source ranks are strictly increasing
on that set, so the universal source-innovation minimum is attained uniquely at
$N=4$.

For the representation statement, after complexification
$W_N\cong S^{(N-1,1)}$,
\[
 \Lambda^2W_N\cong S^{(N-2,1,1)},
 \qquad
 W_N\otimes\operatorname{sgn}\cong S^{(2,1^{N-2})}.
\]
These irreducible Specht modules are isomorphic exactly when their Young
diagrams agree, which occurs at $N=4$.  The real intertwiner is then unique up
to scale and is the oriented three-dimensional Hodge map.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Selection beyond the complete-graph ansatz]
\label{cor:dimension-regular-graph}
Let $G$ be a connected simple $k$-regular relation graph on $v$ endpoints.  If
its complete endpoint and cycle sources are faithful and have equal rank, then
\[
 v-1=\frac{kv}{2}-v+1,
 \qquad\text{hence}\qquad
 (4-k)v=4.
\]
Apart from the one-point graph, the unique solution is
\[
 \boxed{v=4,
 \qquad k=3,
 \qquad G\cong K_4.}
\]
Thus $K_4$ is the unique nontrivial connected regular simple relation graph with
exact endpoint--interference balance.  Arbitrary higher-arity regular designs
are outside this theorem because they change the primitive boundary type.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
For a connected graph the cut rank is $v-1$ and the cycle rank is
$|E|-v+1$.  Regularity gives $|E|=kv/2$.  Solving the displayed Diophantine
equation under $v\ge2$ and $0\le k\le v-1$ gives $v=4$, $k=3$; the only simple
three-regular graph on four vertices is complete.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[The locked Store supplies the faithful local $K_4$ source]
\label{thm:dimension-locked-K4-source}
Fix one accepted type and let $P^-$ be the six-dimensional reversal-odd
coefficient space of the twelve ordered roots
$\rho_{ij}=e_j-e_i$.  Write its coefficients as
$d_{ij}=-d_{ji}$ and define
\[
 B:P^-\longrightarrow W_0,
 \qquad
 B(d)=\sum_{i<j}d_{ij}\rho_{ij},
 \qquad
 W_0=\one_4^\perp.
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{BB^*=4I_{W_0},
 \qquad
 P^-=\Ran B^*\oplus\Ker B.}
 \tag{DS.7}
\]
For the intrinsic accepted contrast metric of
\Cref{cor:locked-opportunity-contrast-spectrum}, let
$S_-:P^-\to\mathcal H_{\rm acc}$ be the source synthesis.  Then
\[
 S_-^*S_-=\vartheta I_{P^-},
\]
and the endpoint and loop syntheses
\[
 S_{\rm end}=S_-B^*,
 \qquad
 S_{\rm loop}=S_-|_{\Ker B}
\]
obey
\[
 \boxed{
 S_{\rm end}^*S_{\rm end}=4\vartheta I_3,
 \qquad
 S_{\rm loop}^*S_{\rm loop}=\vartheta I_3,
 \qquad
 S_{\rm end}^*S_{\rm loop}=0.}
 \tag{DS.8}
\]
Thus the selected Store already contains one faithful endpoint triplet and one
faithful, orthogonal loop triplet; a nonfaithful cycle quotient is not hidden in
the supplied local packet.  Under another faithful physical future metric the
two scalar weights may change, but the ranks, orthogonal representation split,
and positive margins remain.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The operator $BB^*$ is the Laplacian of $K_4$ restricted to the zero-sum
subspace, hence equals $4I_{W_0}$.  This makes $B^*/2$ an isometric embedding
and gives the orthogonal range--kernel decomposition.  The accepted coefficient
metric is $\vartheta I$ on every contrast orthogonal to the uniform accepted
direction.  Conjugating that metric by $B^*$ gives the endpoint Gram, while
restriction to the kernel gives the loop Gram; scalarity makes the two source
ranges orthogonal.  Positive congruence by a faithful future metric preserves
both ranks and their representation-theoretic separation.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Minimal recurrent-root experiment and the historical boundary]
\label{thm:dimension-recurrent-root-table}
Let $S$ be the future-minimal source record of a claimed recurrent spatial
port, let $\alpha$ be the locked root, and let $S'$ be the source at the next
accepted cut.  For each accepted type $r\in\{c,\ell\}$ put
\[
 \boxed{
 J_r(s,\alpha,s')
 :=\Pr(S_n=s,\alpha_n=\alpha,S_{n+1}=s'\mid R_n=r).}
 \tag{DS.9}
\]
If the source marginal
$\mu_r(s)=\sum_{\alpha,s'}J_r(s,\alpha,s')$ is faithful, then
\[
 \boxed{
 P_{r,\alpha}(s,s')
 =\mu_r(s)^{-1}J_r(s,\alpha,s')}
 \tag{DS.10}
\]
reconstructs the complete recurrent root kernel.  The table is row minimal:
any quotient identifying two distinct $J_r$ with the same faithful source
marginal fails to determine at least one recurrent row.  Pairwise marginals do
not suffice in general.

When the root label determines the accepted target $t(\alpha)$, the target slip
is already
\[
 \boxed{
 \delta_r^{\rm slip}
 =\sum_{s,\alpha,s'}J_r(s,\alpha,s')
  \mathbf1_{s'\ne t(\alpha)}.}
 \tag{DS.11}
\]
Under diagonal $S_4$ covariance the target-to-next-source bridge has the unique
form
\[
 B_r=(1-3b_r)I_4+b_r(\one\one^{\mathsf T}-I_4),
 \qquad
 b_r=\delta_r^{\rm slip}/3.
\]
The direct target is sharply copied exactly at $b_r=0$; at $b_r>0$ its overlap
graph is connected and has no nonconstant target-only sharp factor.

The larger commutant-reduced terminal-output/next-source assemblage remains
necessary only for the stronger claim that hidden old output carries an
additional sharp or statistical recurrent state.  It is not required to
reconstruct the geometric recurrent kernel itself.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Summing $J_r$ over $\alpha,s'$ gives $\mu_r$, and faithfulness permits the
rowwise division in \textup{(DS.10)}.  If two distinct joint tables with the
same source marginal were identified, their normalized kernels would differ on
one row, proving minimality.  The standard parity construction on three binary
variables gives two joint laws with identical one- and two-variable marginals
and different triple support, proving the pairwise-marginal claim.
Equation \textup{(DS.11)} is a marginal of the same table.  Diagonal $S_4$
covariance has only diagonal and off-diagonal orbits on $X\times X$, which gives
the displayed bridge.  If $b_r>0$, every distinct target pair is joined in the
positive-support graph; if $b_r=0$, the bridge is the identity.  The last
statement is the distinction between recurrent-kernel sufficiency and the
historical overlap quotient of \Cref{thm:minimal-record} and
\Cref{thm:joint-source-short}.
\end{proof}

\begin{construction}[Minimum active carry--exchange instrument]
\label{con:dimension-active-exchange}
On $X=\{1,2,3,4\}$ let
\[
 s=(12),
 \qquad
 r=(1234),
 \qquad
 \mathcal G_0=\{s,r,r^{-1}\}.
\]
After a target endpoint $t$ is written, draw
$g\in\mathcal G_0$ with positive probabilities and equal probabilities on
$r,r^{-1}$, retain $g$ through the next source cut, and write
\[
 \boxed{(g,s'),
 \qquad s'=gt.}
 \tag{DS.12}
\]
The control is discarded after that cut.
\end{construction}

\begin{theorem}[Minimum active recurrent tetrahedral port]
\label{thm:dimension-active-exchange}
The construction in \textup{(DS.12)} has the following properties.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(A\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item the previous target is recovered sharply from the next-source record by
      $t=g^{-1}s'$;
\item $\langle s,r\rangle=S_4$, so the executable operation is transitive on
      unordered endpoint pairs;
\item inverse pairing makes the endpoint marginal reciprocal;
\item forgetting the added port and its one-cut control leaves every old renewal
      cylinder unchanged;
\item the persistent hardware cost is exactly the three contrasts of a four-point
      endpoint register, and the only additional one-step memory is one transient
      trit.
\end{enumerate}
For the uniform three-outcome law the endpoint and unordered-pair Poincar\'e gaps
are respectively
\[
 \boxed{\gamma_1=\frac23,
 \qquad
 \gamma_2=1-\frac1{\sqrt3}.}
 \tag{DS.13}
\]
No endpoint-only kernel can give both identity target carry and nontrivial pair
exchange; retaining the control for one cut is load bearing.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The recovery formula is deterministic.  A transposition and a four-cycle
generate $S_4$, and the symmetric use of $r,r^{-1}$ gives reciprocity.  The
instrument acts only on a conservative product port after the old accepted
writer, so partial trace recovers every old word.  Four sharp points have three
centred contrasts.  Direct diagonalization of
$(U_s+U_r+U_{r^{-1}})/3$ gives endpoint spectrum
\[
 1,\quad\frac13,\quad\frac{-1+\sqrt2}{3},\quad
 \frac{-1-\sqrt2}{3},
\]
and its action on the six unordered pairs has spectrum
\[
 1,\quad\frac13,\quad\frac1{\sqrt3},\quad-\frac1{\sqrt3},\quad
 \frac{-1+\sqrt2}{3},\quad\frac{-1-\sqrt2}{3},
\]
which proves \textup{(DS.13)}.  If an endpoint-only bridge carries the target
identically, it is the identity kernel and its induced pair action has zero gap.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Cofinal stability and the selected spacetime dimension]
\label{cor:dimension-cofinal-3plus1}
Apply the minimal-readable-record and joint-source compilers to the endpoint,
signed-edge, pair-exchange, source-loss, and extra-writer queries.  On a cofinal
system with summably correctable mixed-Gram defects, suppose the corrected
endpoint and edge source operators have separated threshold ranks three and
six, the pair gap has a positive lower margin, and the source-loss and
extra-writer tails vanish.  Then these properties persist on the canonical
limit quotient, which is terminal among all cofinal sufficient factors, and
its local relation cell is $K_4$.

The selected spatial module is therefore
$W_4\cong\R^3$.  Together with the independently reconstructed one-dimensional
physical clock, the compiler-minimal active branch has
\[
 \boxed{1\text{ temporal}+3\text{ spatial dimensions}.}
 \tag{DS.14}
\]
The number four refers to the vertices of one local relational simplex, not to
the number of sites in the global spatial regulator.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The future-query quotient is the universal quotient of
\Cref{thm:minimal-record}.  Summable positive mixed-Gram correction and the
joint-source direct limit are
\Cref{thm:summable-mixed-Gram-correction,thm:joint-source-inductive-limit}.
Spectral separation preserves the endpoint and edge threshold ranks and the
positive pair gap.  The zero loss and writer tails leave the complexity profile
$(3,6,1,0,0)$, so \Cref{thm:dimension-K4-selector} identifies the limit cell.
The clock contributes the independent temporal direction.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Higher-dimensional cross-product boundary]
\label{thm:dimension-G2-boundary}
Suppose one abandons faithful retention of the complete cycle source and seeks a
metric vector cross product
\[
 \times:\Lambda^2W\longrightarrow W,
 \qquad
 \|x\times y\|^2
 =\|x\|^2\|y\|^2-\langle x,y\rangle^2.
\]
Then $\dim W\in\{0,1,3,7\}$.  With nonzero two-vector interference, only
$d=3$ and $d=7$ remain.  At $d=7$ the quotient has
\[
 \boxed{\dim\Ker(\times)=21-7=14,}
 \tag{DS.15}
\]
and requires a protected positive stable three-form with stabilizer $G_2$.
If the faithful cycle Gram satisfies $G_{\rm cyc}\succeq\lambda_*I$, the lost
source obeys
\[
 \boxed{
 \operatorname{Tr}
 \bigl(P_{\Ker\times}G_{\rm cyc}P_{\Ker\times}\bigr)
 \ge14\lambda_*.}
 \tag{DS.16}
\]
Thus degree-eight $G_2$ packets are coherent enriched theories, but they are not
compiler-minimal competitors to the faithful $K_4$ branch.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The multiplication
$(a,x)(b,y)=(ab-\langle x,y\rangle,ay+bx+x\times y)$ is a real normed division
algebra precisely when the displayed cross-product identities hold.  Hurwitz's
theorem gives dimensions $1,2,4,8$ for that algebra and hence
$d=0,1,3,7$ for $W$.  Rank--nullity gives \textup{(DS.15)}.  The trace bound is
the compression of the positive source floor to a fourteen-dimensional
subspace.  A positive seven-dimensional cross product is equivalently a stable
positive three-form, whose stabilizer is $G_2$.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[Exact scope of dimension selection]
\label{fire:dimension-selection-scope}
The conclusion \textup{(DS.14)} is a theorem for the future-minimal,
one-source/one-target, reciprocal, pair-homogeneous, faithful and
compiler-minimal relational branch.  It is not a theorem that every conceivable
higher-arity, relation-coloured, nonfaithful, or deliberately enriched loading
has three spatial dimensions.  The bare coarse renewal law alone also does not
count hidden unread atoms.  On the concrete selected Store, local $A_3$ labels,
reversal and faithful endpoint/loop sources are already verified; historical
recurrent persistence still requires the two tables in \textup{(DS.9)}, while
the active completion of \Cref{thm:dimension-active-exchange} is unconditional
and conservative.
\end{firewall}


\begin{definition}[Reduced spacetime loading packet]
\label{def:spacetime-loading-packet}
At cutoff $X$, a spacetime loading packet consists of the following selected
universal histories and genuinely physical data in one future-null-completed
source realization.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(S\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item The universal records for every claimed causal order, clock tick,
      temporal/spatial branch, face, boundary, orientation, endpoint, and
      plaquette-traversal label.
\item The dimension-selected recurrent relation port of
      \Cref{sec:dimension-selected-spatial-cell}.  Historically it is supplied by
      the two direct recurrent root tables of
      \Cref{thm:dimension-recurrent-root-table}; on the active branch it is the
      conservative four-point endpoint register and one-cut exchange control of
      \Cref{thm:dimension-active-exchange}.  This item fixes the local spatial
      coefficient module $W_4$ but does not supply a global atlas or metric.
\item One of two finite kinematic entrances:
      \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(S3\alph*)},leftmargin=3em]
      \item the source-native Store branch of
            \Cref{thm:SMST-store-native-route,thm:SMST-monoidal-CAR}, with two
            protected parity cells for the external Clifford factor; or
      \item two independently verified physical Pauli-clock copies as a
            fallback loading.
      \end{enumerate}
\item A faithful physical future metric on the derived spatial Clifford-frame
      source.  Independent clock and geometry source maps, their calibrated
      cross Gram, and the common-action residuals are required only when the
      stronger semantic clock--geometry identity is claimed.
\item Actual ordered cell-transfer and coframe/endpoint histories.  Connection,
      curvature, strain, and finite Cartan translation are derived from these
      histories by \Cref{thm:SMST-frame-transport}; they are inserted separately
      only on a fallback branch where the underlying transport is independently
      sourced.
\item One of two normal entrances whenever HDA is claimed:
      \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(S6\alph*)},leftmargin=3em]
      \item the generator-native normal projection of
            \Cref{thm:SMST-generator-projections}, together with the actual
            endpoint writer and its one-body provenance residual; or
      \item independently loaded normal-density and endpoint-flow histories.
      \end{enumerate}
\item A jointly minimal pressure--action--temporal packet, same-history
      neighboring transport, uniform generator and source-frame margins, and
      actual spatial and mixed face histories for finite ADM/Cartan statements.
      These quantitative inputs may be supplied directly or through the
      regenerative complete-observability packet of
      \Cref{def:renewal-regenerative-packet,thm:renewal-finite-type-closure}.
      Whenever HDA is claimed, retain the two orderings and calibrated phases of
      normal histories, the cell-local normal densities, the endpoint-flow
      action, and the complete reducing source carrier.  A localized
      chronological action and one compatible regulator sequence are required
      for Palatini or Einstein--matter conclusions.  Compact positive screens,
      state tightness, and the $p>4$ face packet may be derived by the
      regenerative branch; potential-force, counterterm-derivative,
      variational stationarity, and infinitesimal coherent Ward data remain
      independent.
\end{enumerate}
The universal records in item~\textup{(S1)} require no readmission.  The local
spatial rank in item~\textup{(S2)} is a compiler output rather than a chosen
number of axes; a global endpoint set, period law, atlas, metric and action
remain separate physical data.  On the source-native branches, the Clifford
axes, determinant volume, connection, curvature, Cartan translation, and
normal candidate are outputs rather than loading hypotheses.  A physical
metric, actual transport, action, and regulator control are not created by the
structural Grand Tensor.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Depth-two external Lorentzian Clifford cell]
\label{thm:external-Clifford}
Let $A,B$ be either two Store-native parity cells from
\Cref{thm:SMST-store-native-route} or the two verified fallback Pauli-clock
copies of \Cref{def:spacetime-loading-packet}.  On the compiler-minimal branch
of \Cref{cor:dimension-cofinal-3plus1}, identify the three spatial axes below
with an orthonormal frame of the selected module $W_4$.  Define
\[
 \gamma^0=-iX_A\otimes I_B,
 \qquad
 \gamma^1=Z_A\otimes Z_B,
 \qquad
 \gamma^2=Z_A\otimes Y_B,
 \qquad
 \gamma^3=Y_A\otimes I_B.
\]
Then
\[
 (\gamma^0)^2=-I,
 \qquad
 (\gamma^i)^2=I,
 \qquad
 \gamma^\mu\gamma^\nu+\gamma^\nu\gamma^\mu=0
 \quad(\mu\ne\nu),
\]
and
\[
 \boxed{C^*_{\C}(\gamma^0,\gamma^1,\gamma^2,\gamma^3)
 =M_4(\C)\cong\Cl_{1,3}(\C).}
\]
The three spatial involutions admit a six-outcome direction Read with labels
$\pm e_i$ and state-independent second moment $I_3/3$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Every mixed product contains exactly one local Pauli anticommutation, proving
the Clifford relations.  The generators contain $X_A\otimes I$ and
$Y_A\otimes I$, hence $Z_A\otimes I$.  Multiplication by $\gamma^1$ and
$\gamma^2$ then gives $I\otimes Z_B$ and $I\otimes Y_B$, hence
$I\otimes X_B$.  Thus both local matrix factors are generated and the total
algebra is $M_2(\C)\otimes M_2(\C)=M_4(\C)$.  Choosing one spatial involution
with probability $1/3$ and measuring its two spectral projections gives the
stated second moment after summing over the three axes.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Dimension-selected Clifford core]
The parity argument for the symplectic label space is now one component of the
stronger selector in \Cref{thm:dimension-K4-selector}: one temporal label makes
$N=\dim(\R t\oplus W_N)$ even, nonzero interference removes $N=2$, and
future-readable source minimality chooses $N=4$.  The three spatial Clifford
axes therefore realize the already selected $W_4$, rather than selecting the
number three by themselves.  The theorem does not exclude a commuting internal
complement or a deliberately enriched higher-dimensional loading; those are
separated by \Cref{fire:dimension-selection-scope}.
\end{remark}

\subsubsection{Locked grading on the external Clifford cell}
\label{sec:SMST-Clifford-matter-audit}

Put
\[
 \sigma_0:=i\gamma^0=X_A\otimes I_B,
 \qquad
 \sigma_i:=\gamma^i\quad(1\le i\le3),
\]
so that the $\sigma_\mu$ are self-adjoint anticommuting involutions.  Their
intrinsic chirality word is
\[
 \boxed{
 \Gamma_{\rm Cl}
 :=\sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_2\sigma_3
 =Z_A\otimes X_B.}
\]
It is a self-adjoint involution and anticommutes with every $\sigma_\mu$.
Every finite representation of the Clifford matrix algebra has the form
\[
 \mathcal H\cong\C^4\otimes M,
 \qquad
 \mathcal N:=C^*(\sigma_0,\ldots,\sigma_3)
 =M_4(\C)\otimes I_M,
 \qquad
 \mathcal N'=I_4\otimes\mathcal B(M),
\]
uniquely up to a unitary on the multiplicity space $M$.

\begin{theorem}[One-scalar Clifford-twirl matter audit]
\label{thm:SMST-Clifford-twirl-matter}
Let $J=J^*=J^{-1}$ be the protected pre-central grading represented on the
same faithful carrier as the external Clifford packet, and put
\[
 P_\pm=\frac12(I\pm J),
 \qquad D=\dim_\C\mathcal H.
\]
Define
\[
 \eta_\mu:=\|P_-\sigma_\mu P_+\|_{\HS}^2,
 \qquad
 p_\mu:=\frac{2\eta_\mu}{D},
 \qquad
 p_{\rm Cl}:=\frac14\sum_{\mu=0}^{3}p_\mu,
\]
and the Clifford twirl
\[
 \mathscr T_{\rm Cl}(X)
 :=\frac14\sum_{\mu=0}^{3}\sigma_\mu X\sigma_\mu.
\]
Then, for
\[
 c_\mu:=D^{-1}\Tr(J\sigma_\mu J\sigma_\mu),
\]
one has
\[
 \boxed{
 \eta_\mu=\frac D4(1-c_\mu),
 \qquad p_\mu=\frac12(1-c_\mu),}
\]
and the complete Clifford occurrence mass is
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathfrak m_{\rm Cl}(J)
 :=\sum_{\mu=0}^{3}\eta_\mu
 =D-\langle J,\mathscr T_{\rm Cl}(J)\rangle_{\HS}
 =2Dp_{\rm Cl}.}
\]
Consequently the following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(M\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item $p_{\rm Cl}>0$;
\item $\mathfrak m_{\rm Cl}(J)>0$;
\item $P_-\sigma_\mu P_+\ne0$ for at least one $\mu$;
\item $J\notin\mathcal N'$;
\item the common finite packet contains a nonzero protected
      grading-changing matter route.
\end{enumerate}
The exact no-matter branch is
\[
 \boxed{p_{\rm Cl}=0
 \iff J=I_4\otimes J_M}
\]
for a self-adjoint unitary $J_M$ on $M$.  The exact intrinsic-chirality branch
is
\[
 \boxed{p_{\rm Cl}=1
 \iff J=\Gamma_{\rm Cl}\otimes V}
\]
for a self-adjoint unitary $V$ on $M$.

The two finite grading-automorphism residuals
\[
 \Delta_{\rm triv}^{\rm Cl}
 :=\sum_{\mu=0}^{3}\|J\sigma_\mu J-\sigma_\mu\|_{\HS}^2,
 \qquad
 \Delta_{\rm chir}^{\rm Cl}
 :=\sum_{\mu=0}^{3}\|J\sigma_\mu J+\sigma_\mu\|_{\HS}^2
\]
satisfy
\[
 \boxed{
 \Delta_{\rm triv}^{\rm Cl}=16Dp_{\rm Cl},
 \qquad
 \Delta_{\rm chir}^{\rm Cl}=16D(1-p_{\rm Cl}),
 \qquad
 \Delta_{\rm triv}^{\rm Cl}+\Delta_{\rm chir}^{\rm Cl}=16D.}
\]
Finally, if $\mathbb E_{\mathcal N'}$ is the trace-preserving expectation onto
the normal multiplicity commutant and
\[
 \Omega_{\rm Cl}
 :=\|J-\mathbb E_{\mathcal N'}J\|_{\HS}^2,
\]
then
\[
 \boxed{Dp_{\rm Cl}\le\Omega_{\rm Cl}\le4Dp_{\rm Cl}.}
\]
Writing $\rho_\pm=\Tr_{\C^4}P_\pm$, the same residual has the exact branch
form
\[
 \boxed{\Omega_{\rm Cl}=\Tr_M(\rho_+\rho_-).}
\]
Thus a positive overlap of the two locked-sign branches on one normal
multiplicity direction is precisely the obstruction to a separated grading.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
For one axis,
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \eta_\mu
 &=\Tr(P_+\sigma_\mu P_-\sigma_\mu P_+)\\
 &=\frac14\Tr\bigl[(I+J)\sigma_\mu(I-J)\sigma_\mu\bigr]\\
 &=\frac14\bigl[D-\Tr(J\sigma_\mu J\sigma_\mu)\bigr],
 \end{aligned}
\]
because $\Tr J=\Tr(\sigma_\mu J\sigma_\mu)$.  This gives the axis identities;
averaging and summing give the twirl and occurrence formulas.

If all $\eta_\mu$ vanish, both off-diagonal corners of every self-adjoint
$\sigma_\mu$ vanish, so $[J,\sigma_\mu]=0$ for all $\mu$ and
$J\in\mathcal N'$.  The converse is immediate.  The finite representation of
$M_4(\C)$ then gives $J=I_4\otimes J_M$.  If $p_{\rm Cl}=1$, every
$p_\mu=1$, hence $J\sigma_\mu J=-\sigma_\mu$ for all $\mu$.  Since
$\Gamma_{\rm Cl}$ has the same anticommutation relations,
$\Gamma_{\rm Cl}J$ commutes with $\mathcal N$ and equals $I_4\otimes V$;
$J$ commutes with $\Gamma_{\rm Cl}$, so $V$ is a self-adjoint unitary.  The
converse follows by substitution.

Direct expansion gives
\[
 \|J\sigma J-\sigma\|_{\HS}^2=2D(1-c),
 \qquad
 \|J\sigma J+\sigma\|_{\HS}^2=2D(1+c),
\]
which proves the residual identities.  Expanding an arbitrary operator in the
Clifford monomial basis shows that the commutator Laplacian
$X\mapsto\sum_\mu[\sigma_\mu,[\sigma_\mu,X]]$ has kernel $\mathcal N'$ and
positive eigenvalues between $4$ and $16$.  Hence
$4\Omega_{\rm Cl}\le\Delta_{\rm triv}^{\rm Cl}\le16\Omega_{\rm Cl}$,
which gives the two-sided bound.

Finally
$\mathbb E_{\mathcal N'}(J)=\frac14I_4\otimes\Tr_{\C^4}J$.  Put
$T_J=\frac14\Tr_{\C^4}J$.  Then
$\rho_\pm=2(I_M\pm T_J)$ and
\[
 \Omega_{\rm Cl}=4\Tr_M(I_M-T_J^2)
 =\Tr_M(\rho_+\rho_-).
\]
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Accepted-response pressure export of the Clifford matter mass]
\label{cor:SMST-Clifford-pressure-matter}
Assume, in addition, that the locked sign can be prepared and read before and
after an executable Clifford axis.  Prepare the maximally mixed state on the
common carrier---equivalently, choose the initial sign with law $d_\pm/D$ and
the maximally mixed state within that fibre---and choose the four axes uniformly
after an accepted completed-private opportunity.  Let
$F=\one_{\{\text{final sign}\ne\text{initial sign}\}}$.  The accepted-count
pressure is
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal P_{\#,\rm flip}(q)
 =\log\!\left(
 1-\vartheta
 +\vartheta[(1-p_{\rm Cl})+p_{\rm Cl}e^{-q}]
 \right),}
\]
so
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal P_{\#,\rm flip}'(0)=-\vartheta p_{\rm Cl},
 \qquad
 \mathfrak m_{\rm Cl}(J)
 =-\frac{2D}{\vartheta}\mathcal P_{\#,\rm flip}'(0).}
\]
For raw physical time,
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal P_{t,\rm flip}'(0)
 =-\frac{4\vartheta}{11}p_{\rm Cl},
 \qquad
 \mathfrak m_{\rm Cl}(J)
 =-\frac{11D}{2\vartheta}\mathcal P_{t,\rm flip}'(0).}
\]
If $d_\pm=\rank P_\pm$, the binary difference-reward Hessian has generalized
gap
\[
 \boxed{
 \sigma_{\#,\rm Cl}
 =\frac{\vartheta D^2}{d_+d_-}p_{\rm Cl},
 \qquad
 \sigma_{t,\rm Cl}=\frac4{11}\sigma_{\#,\rm Cl}.}
\]
Thus the mixed word norm, action--grading residual, sign-flip probability,
pressure slope, and binary pressure gap are exact coordinates of the same
finite occurrence statement.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
At one opportunity the tilted total likelihood is
$1-\vartheta+\vartheta\mathbb E(e^{-qF})$, which gives the count pressure and
its derivative.  The raw-time slope is the mean reward divided by the mean
accepted-response duration $11/(4\vartheta)$ from
\Cref{thm:accepted-response-renewal}.  For the difference reward
$R=e_\tau-e_\epsilon$, stationarity gives $\mathbb ER=0$ and
\[
 \langle x,\mathbb H_{\#,\rm Cl}x\rangle
 =\vartheta p_{\rm Cl}|x_+-x_-|^2.
\]
Since the stationary sign law is $(d_+/D,d_-/D)$, its variance form is
$(d_+d_-/D^2)|x_+-x_-|^2$, proving the gap formulas.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Spatial localization of the Clifford occurrence]
\label{cor:SMST-Clifford-spatial-route}
Put
\[
 p_t=p_0,
 \qquad
 p_s=\frac13\sum_{i=1}^{3}p_i,
 \qquad
 p_{\rm Cl}=\frac14(p_t+3p_s).
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{
 p_s\ge\max\left\{0,\frac{4p_{\rm Cl}-1}{3}\right\}.}
\]
Consequently $p_s>0$ is the direct finite certificate for a spatial
edge-provenance matter route, while the uniform scalar alone implies such a
route whenever $p_{\rm Cl}>1/4$.  Under exact tetrahedral covariance the three
spatial masses are equal.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The identity follows from the definitions.  Since $0\le p_t\le1$, eliminating
$p_t$ gives the lower bound.  Tetrahedral covariance makes the three spatial
axis blocks unitarily conjugate.
\end{proof}

\begin{countertheorem}[Separate normal and sign marginals do not decide matter]
\label{cth:SMST-Clifford-marginals}
On $\C^4\otimes\C^2$, the gradings
\[
 J_{\rm chir}=\Gamma_{\rm Cl}\otimes I_2,
 \qquad
 J_{\rm sep}=I_4\otimes X
\]
have the same two sign-fibre dimensions and the same marginal external
Clifford packet.  Nevertheless
\[
 \boxed{p_{\rm Cl}(J_{\rm chir})=1,
 \qquad p_{\rm Cl}(J_{\rm sep})=0.}
\]
Therefore sign fairness, Clifford reconstruction, and their separate source
Grams do not determine the relative grading action.  The same-history mixed
word Gram, a common differentiated-response table, or the executable
sign-after-Clifford panel is information-theoretically necessary.
\end{countertheorem}

\begin{proof}
Intrinsic chirality anticommutes with all four axes, whereas an operator acting
only on the multiplicity factor commutes with them.  Both involutions have
four positive and four negative eigenvalues.  The claimed values follow from
\Cref{thm:SMST-Clifford-twirl-matter}.
\end{proof}


\begin{theorem}[One positive sign branch determines the normal-assisted matter margin]
\label{thm:SMST-one-branch-purity}
Let the saturated normal carrier factor as
\[
 \mathcal H=H_{\rm N}\otimes M,
 \qquad d_{\rm N}=\dim H_{\rm N},
\]
and let $J=J^*=J^{-1}$ be the locked grading with
$P_+=(I+J)/2$.  Define the normalized conditional sign effect
\[
 \boxed{
 E_+=\frac1{d_{\rm N}}\Tr_{H_{\rm N}}P_+,
 \qquad T=2E_+-I_M.}
\]
Then $0\preceq E_+\preceq I$ and the exact branch-overlap matter margin is
\[
 \boxed{
 \Omega_{\rm br}
 =4d_{\rm N}\Tr_M(E_+-E_+^2)
 =d_{\rm N}\Tr_M(I-T^2).}
\]
The following are equivalent:
\[
 \boxed{
 \Omega_{\rm br}=0
 \iff E_+\text{ is a projection}
 \iff T^2=I_M
 \iff J=I_{H_{\rm N}}\otimes T.}
\]
Thus matter occurrence is exactly the failure of the sharp sign to remain
sharp after the normal factor is forgotten.

If $W_{\rm N}$ is the first saturated normal-word synthesis and
\[
 G_{\rm N}=W_{\rm N}^*W_{\rm N},
 \qquad G_+^{\rm N}=W_{\rm N}^*P_+W_{\rm N},
\]
then
\[
 \boxed{
 P_+=(W_{\rm N}^\dagger)^*G_+^{\rm N}W_{\rm N}^\dagger.}
\]
Hence the total normal Gram and one positive sign-branch Gram reconstruct the
complete margin; the negative branch is redundant.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The partial trace gives
$E_+=(I+T)/2$, where $T=d_{\rm N}^{-1}\Tr_{H_{\rm N}}J$ is a self-adjoint
contraction.  Expanding $E_+(I-E_+)$ gives $(I-T^2)/4$, proving the formula.
A positive contraction has $E_+(I-E_+)=0$ exactly when its spectrum lies in
$\{0,1\}$, which is the projection condition.  Equality in the Hilbert--Schmidt
contractivity of the conditional expectation onto
$I_{H_{\rm N}}\otimes\mathcal B(M)$ is equivalent to $J$ lying in that
subalgebra, giving the separated form.  The last formula is the
Moore--Penrose reconstruction of an inserted operator from a saturated Gram.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Exact $S_4$ exceptional three-matrix panel]
\label{thm:SMST-exceptional-three-matrix}
Assume the residual normal multiplicity has the $S_4$ decomposition
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 M\cong{}&[4]\otimes\C^{m_1}
 \oplus[1^4]\otimes\C^{m_{\rm sgn}}
 \oplus[31]\otimes\C^{m_{31}}\\
 &\oplus[211]\otimes\C^{m_{211}}
 \oplus[22]\otimes\C^{m_{22}},
 \end{aligned}
\]
and that $T=2E_+-I$ is orientation covariant:
$V_gTV_g^*=\operatorname{sgn}(g)T$.  Then, up to unitary multiplicity-frame
changes, $T$ is determined by exactly three contractions
\[
 \boxed{
 A_1:\C^{m_1}\to\C^{m_{\rm sgn}},
 \qquad
 A_3:\C^{m_{31}}\to\C^{m_{211}},
 \qquad
 A_2=A_2^*\in M_{m_{22}}(\C).}
\]
In twist-adapted frames the two paired blocks are the self-adjoint dilations of
$A_1$ and $I_3\otimes A_3$, while the self-twist block is
$C_{22}\otimes A_2$ for a fixed self-adjoint sign-twist intertwiner $C_{22}$.
The exact exceptional contribution is
\[
 \boxed{
 \begin{aligned}
 \Omega_{\rm exc}=d_{\rm N}\Bigl[&
 m_1+m_{\rm sgn}-2\|A_1\|_{\rm HS}^2\\
 &+3\bigl(m_{31}+m_{211}-2\|A_3\|_{\rm HS}^2\bigr)\\
 &+2\bigl(m_{22}-\Tr A_2^2\bigr)\Bigr].
 \end{aligned}}
\]
It vanishes exactly when
\[
 m_1=m_{\rm sgn},\qquad m_{31}=m_{211},
\]
$A_1,A_3$ are unitary, and $A_2^2=I$.  On this zero branch the formula
reconstructs the complete separated multiplicity grading rather than leaving
an unclassified obstruction.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Orientation covariance maps each irreducible isotype only to its sign twist.
Schur's lemma therefore permits blocks only between $[4]$ and $[1^4]$, between
$[31]$ and $[211]$, and within the self-twist $[22]$ isotype.  Factoring the
unique irreducible intertwiner leaves precisely the three multiplicity
matrices.  Squaring the paired self-adjoint dilations gives
$A_j^*A_j$ and $A_jA_j^*$, while the self-twist square is $I_{[22]}\otimes
A_2^2$.  Substitution in
$\Omega_{\rm br}=d_{\rm N}\Tr(I-T^2)$ gives the displayed formula.  Every term
is nonnegative, and simultaneous vanishing is exactly the stated unitary and
multiplicity-balance condition.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[Word-Gram and executable Clifford interfaces]
The quantities $\eta_\mu$ are ordinary same-history word norms once the locked
grading and Clifford axes lie on one faithful carrier; no laboratory pulse or
coherent eraser is required to define them.  Their Markov-kernel and renewal-
pressure interpretation is stronger: it requires physical preparation of a
sign branch, an executable Clifford involution or equivalent reversible
history, and a terminal sign Read.  If those operations are absent, the
correct interface is the mixed word-Gram residual, not an invented transition
experiment.
\end{firewall}


\begin{theorem}[Intrinsic frame volume and DeWitt inverse]
\label{thm:DeWitt}
Let $E:\C^3\to\mathcal H$ be the future-visible spatial frame source generated
by the three spatial Clifford histories, and let a faithful physical future
metric induce
\[
 q=E^*E\in\operatorname{Sym}_3^+.
\]
Then the squared norm of the exterior frame is the Gram determinant,
\[
 \boxed{
 \norm{\bigwedge^3E(e_1\wedge e_2\wedge e_3)}^2=\det q.}
\]
Consequently determinant volume is an intrinsic word-Gram readout once the
physical metric and frame are present; no independent determinant-volume writer
is required on this branch.  The normalized negative Hessian of this determinant
response is
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathfrak B_q(h,k)=\Tr(q^{-1}h\,q^{-1}k)
 -\Tr(q^{-1}h)\Tr(q^{-1}k),}
\]
has five positive traceless directions and one negative trace direction, and
its cotangent inverse is
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathfrak B_q^{-1}(P,Q)=\Tr(PQ)-\frac12\Tr(P)\Tr(Q).}
\]
The coefficient $1/2$ is independent of the overall physical stiffness of the
metric response.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The Gram determinant identity for exterior products gives
$\norm{\bigwedge^3E}^2=\det(E^*E)$.  For $X=q^{-1}h$ and $Y=q^{-1}k$,
\[
 D^2\det(q)[h,k]=\det(q)\bigl(\Tr X\Tr Y-\Tr(XY)\bigr).
\]
Negating and normalizing gives $\mathfrak B_q$.  Writing
$X=X_0+xI$ with $\Tr X_0=0$ yields
$\mathfrak B_q(X,X)=\Tr(X_0^2)-6x^2$, hence signature $(5,1)$.
The form is the trace pairing on the traceless block and $-2$ times that
pairing on the scalar block, so its inverse has scalar coefficient $-1/2$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Actual transport derives finite connection, curvature, and Cartan translation]
\label{thm:SMST-frame-transport}
For neighboring cells $x,y$, let $E_x,E_y$ be the intrinsic frame sources,
$q_x=E_x^*E_x$, and $\widehat E_x=E_xq_x^{-1/2}$.  Let
$T_e:\mathcal H_x\to\mathcal H_y$ be an actual ordered transport history and
put
\[
 A_e=\widehat E_y^*T_e\widehat E_x,
 \qquad
 \mathbb V_e=\widehat E_x^*T_e^*(I-\widehat E_y\widehat E_y^*)
              T_e\widehat E_x\succeq0.
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{
 \widehat E_x^*T_e^*T_e\widehat E_x=A_e^*A_e+\mathbb V_e,}
\]
and $\mathbb V_e=0$ exactly when the actual transport closes on the spatial
frame.  On that branch, if $A_e$ is invertible, its polar decomposition
$A_e=U_eP_e$ gives the unique unitary finite frame connection $U_e$ and positive
strain $P_e$.  Ordered products of the $U_e$ give gauge-covariant loop
holonomies; whenever $-1$ is absent from a loop spectrum, the principal
logarithm gives its finite curvature.  If the separately tested real-structure
and orientation residuals vanish, then $U_e\in\SO(3)$.

If an actual endpoint/coframe history $d_e$ obeys
$(I-\widehat E_y\widehat E_y^*)d_e=0$, set
$\xi_e=\widehat E_y^*d_e$ and
\[
 \mathbf G_e=\begin{pmatrix}U_e&\xi_e\\0&1\end{pmatrix}.
\]
On the real orientation-preserving branch this is an
$\SO(3)\ltimes\R^3$ link.  For every protected face, the translation part of
the ordered product $\mathbf G_f$ is the finite Cartan/torsion residual.  Thus
connection, curvature, and torsion are derived from actual transport and
coframe words, not loaded independently.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Insert $I=\widehat E_y\widehat E_y^*+
(I-\widehat E_y\widehat E_y^*)$ between $T_e^*$ and $T_e$ and compress by
$\widehat E_x$ to obtain the decomposition.  The second summand is the Gram of
$(I-\widehat E_y\widehat E_y^*)T_e\widehat E_x$, proving positivity and the
closure criterion.  Polar decomposition gives the unique unitary factor of an
invertible $A_e$, with the usual endpoint gauge covariance.  Multiplication of
links gives loop holonomy and the logarithm is finite functional calculus.
The coframe condition gives $d_e=\widehat E_y\xi_e$.  On the verified
real orientation-preserving branch, multiplication in
$\SO(3)\ltimes\R^3$ shows that the accumulated translation is exactly the
failure of affine closure around the face; before that test the same formula is
a unitary affine transport identity.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Clock--geometry source audit]
\label{thm:SMST-clock-geometry-audit}
Put
\[
 A=S_{\rm clk}^*S_{\rm clk},\qquad
 B=S_{\rm clk}^*S_{\rm geo},\qquad
 D=S_{\rm geo}^*S_{\rm geo}.
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathbb G_{{\rm geo}\mid{\rm clk}}
 :=D-B^*A^\dagger B
 =S_{\rm geo}^*(I-P_{\rm clk})S_{\rm geo}\succeq0,}
\]
where $P_{\rm clk}=S_{\rm clk}A^\dagger S_{\rm clk}^*$ projects onto
$\Ran S_{\rm clk}$.  Moreover,
\[
 \mathbb G_{{\rm geo}\mid{\rm clk}}=0
 \iff \Ran S_{\rm geo}\subseteq\Ran S_{\rm clk},
\]
and the rank of this residual is the increase of the joint source rank over
the clock-source rank.  If $A,D\succ0$, then
$\mathcal C_{\rm cg}=A^{-1/2}BD^{-1/2}$ is a contraction and
\[
 \boxed{
 D^{-1/2}\mathbb G_{{\rm geo}\mid{\rm clk}}D^{-1/2}
 =I-\mathcal C_{\rm cg}^*\mathcal C_{\rm cg}.}
\]
The complete cross Gram $B$ is reconstructed from the two physical amplitudes
$\|S_{\rm clk}v+S_{\rm geo}w\|^2$ and
$\|S_{\rm clk}v+iS_{\rm geo}w\|^2$ together with the marginal Grams.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The Moore--Penrose expression for the orthogonal projection onto
$\Ran S_{\rm clk}$ is $P_{\rm clk}=S_{\rm clk}A^\dagger S_{\rm clk}^*$.
Substitution gives the Schur identity and positivity; vanishing is exactly
range inclusion.  The rank formula is the standard Gram-rank increment.  The
normalized source maps $S_{\rm clk}A^{-1/2}$ and
$S_{\rm geo}D^{-1/2}$ are isometries, whose cross product is
$\mathcal C_{\rm cg}$, proving the contraction identity.  Finally, for
$a=S_{\rm clk}v$ and $b=S_{\rm geo}w$,
\[
 \langle a,b\rangle
 =\frac12\left[
 \|a+b\|^2-\|a\|^2-\|b\|^2
 -i\bigl(\|a+ib\|^2-\|a\|^2-\|b\|^2\bigr)
 \right],
\]
which reconstructs every matrix element of $B$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Cross-Hankel chronology alternative]
\label{thm:SMST-cross-Hankel}
Let $T$ be the common positive future transfer and define
\[
 \mathcal V_r^a(x_0,\ldots,x_r)=\sum_{j=0}^rT^jS_ax_j,
 \qquad a\in\{{\rm clk},{\rm geo}\}.
\]
If $\mathbb H_r^{ab}=(\mathcal V_r^a)^*\mathcal V_r^b$, then
\[
 \boxed{
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathbb G_r^{{\rm geo}\mid{\rm clk}}
 ={}&\mathbb H_r^{{\rm geo},{\rm geo}}
 -(\mathbb H_r^{{\rm clk},{\rm geo}})^*
  (\mathbb H_r^{{\rm clk},{\rm clk}})^\dagger
  \mathbb H_r^{{\rm clk},{\rm geo}}\\
 ={}&(\mathcal V_r^{\rm geo})^*(I-\Pi_r^{\rm clk})
     \mathcal V_r^{\rm geo}\succeq0.
 \end{aligned}}
\]
Its rank is the number of geometry-history directions not contained in the
clock packet through depth $r$.  If the first vanishing occurs at depth $d$,
then
\[
 \boxed{S_{\rm geo}=\sum_{n=0}^dT^nS_{\rm clk}R_n,}
\]
with minimum-norm coefficients determined by the Moore--Penrose inverse of the
clock Hankel Gram.  The case $d=0$ is local source inclusion; $d>0$ is a
measurable chronology filter and is not a local common-action identity.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The joint history matrix is the Gram of
$(\mathcal V_r^{\rm clk},\mathcal V_r^{\rm geo})$.  Its generalized Schur
complement is the Gram after orthogonal projection away from the clock-history
range.  Vanishing is therefore range inclusion.  Solving this inclusion by
least squares gives the displayed coefficient maps and the minimal closure
depth.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Source-native common-action criterion]
\label{thm:SMST-common-action}
Assume the clock and geometry source maps are loaded in one physical quotient,
their source Grams are nonsingular on $\C u\oplus V_5$, their cross Gram is
physically reconstructed, and the following residuals vanish:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(C\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item the source Schur residual of \Cref{thm:SMST-clock-geometry-audit};
\item the relative amplitudes and phases on the multiplicity-free homogeneous
      and shape modules;
\item the cross-Hankel chronology degree beyond zero;
\item the persistent-transfer, frequency-mixing, and depth-two semantic-clock
      residuals of the loaded score instrument.
\end{enumerate}
Then $S_{\rm geo}=S_{\rm clk}$ as physical source maps.  Consequently all
future moments and analytic control derivatives agree, and one scalar
$\chi>0$ multiplies the gravitational kinetic parent and curvature response.
The Hamiltonian coefficients are reciprocal:
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal H_{\rm g}
 =\frac{\chi^{-1}}{\sqrt q}
  \left(\pi^{ab}\pi_{ab}-\frac12\pi^2\right)
 -\chi\sqrt q\,R+\Lambda_H\sqrt q,
 \qquad ab=1.}
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Zero Schur residual gives source-range inclusion.  Multiplicity-free frame
covariance makes the source comparison scalar on the homogeneous and shape
modules; zero amplitude and phase defects make both scalars equal to one.
Zero chronology degree excludes a nonconstant future filter, while the score
residuals exclude hidden state-update memory and central semantic splitting.
Thus the two loaded source maps coincide.  The determinant Hessian theorem
gives the DeWitt coefficient $1/2$.  The Legendre transform of a Lagrangian
quadratic form multiplied by $\chi$ has kinetic coefficient $\chi^{-1}$,
whereas its curvature descendant retains $\chi$, proving reciprocity.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Finite external spacetime loading]
\label{def:external-spacetime-loading}
The finite external spacetime loading is generated by the selected universal
causal/face/orientation records together with one verified branch of
\Cref{def:spacetime-loading-packet}.  Its external algebra is
\[
 \boxed{\mathcal A_{{\rm ext},X}:=
 C^*(\gamma^0,\gamma^1,\gamma^2,\gamma^3)\cong M_4(\C).}
\]
On the Store-native branch the Pauli cells are obtained from the calibrated
Store route, the determinant volume and DeWitt inverse from the physical frame
Gram, and finite connection/curvature/Cartan translation from actual transport
and coframe histories.  On a fallback branch the corresponding physical panels
must be supplied explicitly.  Clock--geometry common action, pressure/action,
HDA, Palatini, and continuum statements retain their separately displayed
certificates.
\end{definition}

% =============================================================================
\subsection{The Standard-Model loading: typed incidence, generation attachment,
and finite-Dirac reconstruction}
\label{sec:SM-sector}
% =============================================================================

The Standard-Model branch has four logically distinct layers.  First, the
revision fibre and Store-derived weak fibre reconstruct the representation
skeleton; anomaly freedom fixes the central weight ratio and the quotient group.
Second, the protected record retains pre-central type, branch, source/target,
revision, chronology, routing, and tetrahedral facts, but a label cannot create a
missing cross-support coefficient.  Third, matter may enter source natively
through the odd block of a calibrated Store generator, through an independently
measured cross-support generator, or through the protected score-square fallback.
On the source-native branch, strict graded monoidal composition derives the weak
CAR writer and incidence rows, and the relative homogeneous $K_4$ record derives
the generation factor.  Fourth, one calibrated full-cell generator can replace
separately loaded finite-residue matrices; common-Hodge and marked-panel
reconstruction remain rigorous fallbacks.  Numerical source values and continuum
dynamics are not supplied by these structural reductions.


% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
\subsubsection{Geometry-shorted active residual and a source-minimal structural SM realization}
\label{sec:SM-active-residual-realization}
% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

The finite-Heisenberg and source-native theorems below remain the appropriate
historical and representation-independent reconstruction tools.  On the
explicit active branch, the completed spacetime packet makes a stronger
realization available directly from the accepted Store contrasts.  The
construction is inserted here because it allocates the internal factors before
the general finite SM loading is formulated.

Let $\Phi$ be the twelve oriented $A_3$ roots and
$P=\R^{\Phi}$.  Let $\mathscr T=\{c,\ell\}$ be the two accepted types and put
\[
 t_0=2^{-1/2}(\mathbf e_c+\mathbf e_\ell),
 \qquad
 t_1=2^{-1/2}(\mathbf e_c-\mathbf e_\ell),
\]
\[
 P_0=\left\{f\in P:\sum_{\alpha\in\Phi}f(\alpha)=0\right\}.
\]
After removal of the overall accepted mean, the coefficient space is
\[
 \boxed{
 E_{\rm acc}^0
 =(P_0\otimes t_0)
 \oplus(\R\one_\Phi\otimes t_1)
 \oplus(P_0\otimes t_1).}
 \tag{SM.0a}
\]
The three summands have dimensions $11,1,11$.

\begin{theorem}[Exact geometry short of the accepted Store source]
\label{thm:SM-active-residual-short}
Let $S_{\rm acc}:E_{\rm acc}^0\to\mathcal H_{\rm acc}$ be the accepted source
synthesis.  On the locked opportunity branch,
\[
 \boxed{S_{\rm acc}^*S_{\rm acc}=\vartheta I_{E_{\rm acc}^0}.}
 \tag{SM.0b}
\]
Allocate
\[
 E_{\rm ST}^{\rm cat}:=P_0\otimes t_0,
 \qquad
 E_{\rm int}^{\rm cat}
 :=(\R\one_\Phi\otimes t_1)\oplus(P_0\otimes t_1).
 \tag{SM.0c}
\]
On the explicit active spacetime completion, all additional waiting-time,
speed, bracket, shift, and geometric-circulation source directions lie in the
independently adjoined relational port.  Simultaneous shorting by the complete
spacetime source therefore leaves
\[
 \boxed{G_{\rm int\mid ST}=\vartheta I_{12}.}
 \tag{SM.0d}
\]
On an arbitrary historical common carrier the corresponding formula is
\[
 \boxed{
 G_{\rm int\mid ST}
 =\vartheta I_{12}-C_{\rm ext}^*D_{\rm ext}^{\dagger}C_{\rm ext}\succeq0,}
 \tag{SM.0e}
\]
where $D_{\rm ext}$ is the Gram of the additional geometric source after the
categorical geometry copy has been removed and $C_{\rm ext}$ is its mixed
block with $E_{\rm int}^{\rm cat}$.  Thus \textup{(SM.0d)} is historical
exactly when $C_{\rm ext}=0$.

Let root reversal act by $\iota(i,j)=(j,i)$.  As a representation of
$S_4\times\langle\iota\rangle$, the residual is multiplicity free:
\[
 \boxed{
 E_{\rm int}^{\rm cat}\otimes\C
 \cong
 \C_{\rm type}^{+}
 \oplus W_+
 \oplus(V_2)_+
 \oplus W_-
 \oplus(W\otimes\operatorname{sgn})_-.}
 \tag{SM.0f}
\]
The odd standard block $W_-$ is the endpoint quotient of
\Cref{thm:dimension-locked-K4-source}; the odd sign-twisted block is its
orthogonal loop kernel.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Equation \textup{(SM.0b)} is the accepted contrast statement of
\Cref{thm:locked-incidence-profile}.  The decomposition
\textup{(SM.0a)} is orthogonal for this scalar metric.  On the active
conservative product carrier, the additional spacetime scores are orthogonal
to the accepted categorical source, so the Anderson--Trapp short deletes only
$P_0\otimes t_0$ and gives \textup{(SM.0d)}.  On a shared historical carrier,
shorting the residual by the remaining geometric source gives the Schur
formula \textup{(SM.0e)}.

For the permutation representation on ordered roots,
$P^+\cong\mathbf1\oplus W\oplus V_2$ and
$P^-\cong W\oplus(W\otimes\operatorname{sgn})$.  Removing the root mean from
$P^+$ and adjoining the scalar type contrast gives \textup{(SM.0f)}.  The
endpoint/loop identification is \Cref{thm:dimension-locked-K4-source}.
\end{proof}

Let
\[
 \mathcal K_{\rm res}
 =\C_{\rm type}\oplus C\oplus W_2\oplus G\oplus P_{\rm loop}
 \tag{SM.0g}
\]
be the source-minimal complex carrier of \textup{(SM.0f)}, with dimensions
$1,3,2,3,3$.  Here $C=W_+$, $W_2=(V_2)_+$,
$G=W_-$, and $P_{\rm loop}=(W\otimes\operatorname{sgn})_-$.  Let
$s=(12)$, $r=(1234)$, and let $R_\iota$ implement root reversal.

\begin{theorem}[Two-control reconstruction of the internal matrix factors]
\label{thm:SM-active-residual-algebra}
Suppose the two tetrahedral relabelings $U_s,U_r$ are executable on
$\mathcal K_{\rm res}$.  Then
\[
 \boxed{
 C^*(U_s,U_r,R_\iota)
 \cong
 \C
 \oplus M_3(\C)_C
 \oplus M_2(\C)_{W_2}
 \oplus M_3(\C)_G
 \oplus M_3(\C)_{P_{\rm loop}}.}
 \tag{SM.0h}
\]
In particular, the reversal-even internal corner is
\[
 \boxed{M_3(\C)_C\oplus M_2(\C)_{W_2}.}
 \tag{SM.0i}
\]
One unitary control cannot generate either noncommutative matrix block; hence
two noncommuting tetrahedral controls are minimal on this active realization.
Moreover
\[
 \det\rho_C(g)=\det\rho_{W_2}(g)=\operatorname{sgn}(g),
 \tag{SM.0j}
\]
so $\det C\otimes\det W_2$ is a trivial $S_4$ line.  Any nonzero unit
trivialization has stabilizer
$S(U(3)\times U(2))$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The permutations $s,r$ generate $S_4$.  The five summands in
\textup{(SM.0f)} are irreducible and pairwise inequivalent for
$S_4\times\langle\iota\rangle$; reversal separates the two standard copies.
Their commutant is therefore scalar on each summand.  The finite bicommutant
theorem gives the full matrix algebra on every irreducible block, proving
\textup{(SM.0h)}.  A $C^*$-algebra generated by one unitary is commutative,
which proves minimality.  The determinant of the standard representation is
the sign character.  The two-dimensional representation factors through
$S_4/V_4\cong S_3$ and has the same determinant character.  Their product is
therefore trivial, and \Cref{thm:SM-group} identifies its unitary stabilizer.
\end{proof}

For the six unoriented edges of $K_4$, let
$u_e=(e_j-e_i)/\sqrt2\in G$ and $P_e=u_eu_e^*$.  Then
\[
 \boxed{\sum_{e\in E(K_4)}P_e=2I_G.}
 \tag{SM.0k}
\]
Let $h_0\in W_2$ be a unit vector.  The four canonical incidence maps generated
by \Cref{thm:SMST-monoidal-CAR} and \Cref{thm:SM-generation} combine into one
normalized grading-odd operator
\[
 D_0:\mathcal H_R^{(1)}\longrightarrow\mathcal H_L^{(1)},
 \qquad D_0^*D_0=D_0D_0^*=I.
 \tag{SM.0l}
\]
Define $B_e=P_e\otimes D_0$ on the generation--chiral carrier.

\begin{theorem}[Unconditional active finite structural Standard Model]
\label{thm:SM-active-SM-I}
Adjoin to the source-minimal residual carrier the executable controls
$U_s,U_r$ and one nonzero representative of the grading-odd root seed $B_e$;
retain the complete $S_4$ orbit and the protected root/reversal records.  Then,
at every finite cutoff:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(S\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item the internal matrix factors are $M_3(\C)$ and $M_2(\C)$ by
      \Cref{thm:SM-active-residual-algebra};
\item the invariant determinant line gives
      \[
       \boxed{G_{\rm SM}=S(U(3)\times U(2))
       \cong\frac{SU(3)\times SU(2)\times U(1)}{\mathbb Z_6};}
       \tag{SM.0m}
      \]
\item anomaly freedom gives, up to simultaneous orientation,
      \[
       \boxed{6Y:(Q,u,d,L,e,\nu,H)
       =(1,4,-2,-3,-6,0,3);}
       \tag{SM.0n}
      \]
\item the odd root orbit is tight:
      \[
       \boxed{
       \sum_eB_e^*B_e=2I,
       \qquad
       \sum_eB_eB_e^*=2I,
       \qquad
       I_G\otimes D_0=\frac12\sum_eB_e;}
       \tag{SM.0o}
      \]
      hence the complete odd full-cell generator lies in the one-seed orbit
      span and the odd-exhaustion and finite-Dirac relation residuals vanish;
\item the only matter multiplicity carrier is the endpoint quotient
      $G\cong\C^3$; the orthogonal block $P_{\rm loop}$ remains loop
      provenance.  Thus the future-visible structural generation number is
      exactly three;
\item with total grading
      $J=\Gamma_{\rm Cl}\otimes\Gamma_F$, every external Clifford axis flips
      $J$, so the normalized Clifford occurrence scalar is
      \[
       \boxed{p_{\rm Cl}=1;}
       \tag{SM.0p}
      \]
\item the packet contains one weak Higgs doublet and one nonzero finite Dirac
      operator.  The five numerical residue matrices are typed contractions
      of this one operator in the common generation frame.
\end{enumerate}
The construction is a conservative active completion of the relational Grand
Tensor.  Historical occurrence in the old Store is equivalent to membership
of the two relabeling controls and one odd seed in the old source-minimal word
algebra; failure returns their exact orthogonal innovation rank.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Items~\textup{(S1)--(S3)} are
\Cref{thm:SM-active-residual-algebra,thm:SM-group,thm:SM-anomaly-forced-weights}.
The complete-graph tight-frame identity gives \textup{(SM.0k)}, and tensoring
with the normalized incidence operator gives \textup{(SM.0o)}.  Hence the
full odd operator is in the protected orbit span, so no additional odd source
is present.  By \Cref{thm:SMST-record-native-generations}, the endpoint and
loop triplets are faithful and orthogonal; only the endpoint quotient is
inserted in the fermion carrier, proving the generation statement.  Since the
external Clifford chirality anticommutes with every Clifford axis,
$J\sigma_\mu J\sigma_\mu=-I$ and the Clifford-twirl formula gives
$p_{\rm Cl}=1$.  The CAR/incidence and finite-Dirac conclusions are
\Cref{thm:SMST-monoidal-CAR,thm:SMST-generator-projections}.  Conservativity is
implemented by adjoining the source-minimal residual controls and seed as
future-readable words and forgetting them at the old interface.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[Active realization versus historical identification]
\label{fire:SM-active-historical}
The theorem proves a finite structural Standard Model for the explicitly
completed active primitive.  It does not infer executable relabelings or the
odd root seed from the accepted source Gram alone.  A historical claim about
the old Store must evaluate the corresponding word-membership and mixed
Clifford rows.  Numerical couplings, masses, flavour matrices, running, and the
fermion measure are not consequences of the structural packet.
\end{firewall}


\begin{theorem}[Finite-Heisenberg revision and no-hiding packet]
\label{thm:SM-qutrit-packet}
Let $H_3=\mathbb F_3^2$ and let unitaries $R_a$ satisfy
\[
 R_aR_bR_a^*R_b^*=\omega^{[a,b]}I,
 \qquad \omega=e^{2\pi i/3},
\]
for a nondegenerate alternating form $[\cdot,\cdot]$ on $H_3$.  Then
\[
 \boxed{C^*(R_a:a\in H_3)\cong M_3(\C).}
\]
The uniform revision twirl is exact qutrit erasure,
\[
 \frac19\sum_aR_aAR_a^*=\Tr(A)\frac{I_3}{3},
\]
and its minimal Stinespring environment has dimension nine and factors,
canonically up to a unitary, as
$\C^3_{\rm key}\otimes\C^3_{\rm rec}$.  The relative-revision operators
$\overline{R_a}\otimes R_a$ form an ordinary representation whose Fourier
projections are the rank-one Bell pointer.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
For $a\ne0$, choose $c$ with $[c,a]\ne0$.  Conjugation by $R_c$ multiplies
$R_a$ by a nontrivial cubic root, so $\Tr R_a=0$.  Hence the nine $R_a$ are
Hilbert--Schmidt orthogonal and span a nine-dimensional simple complex
$C^*$-algebra, necessarily $M_3(\C)$.  The twirl commutes with this full matrix
algebra and is therefore scalar; trace preservation fixes the scalar to
$\Tr(A)/3$.  The nine orthogonal Kraus operators give Choi rank nine, so the
minimal environment has dimension nine.  The standard minimal erasure
isometry sends $\psi$ to a maximally entangled key state tensored with
$\psi$ in the record factor, proving the factorization.  Complex conjugation
cancels the projective cocycle in
$\overline{R_a}\otimes R_a$; Fourier inversion on $H_3$ gives the Bell
projections.
\end{proof}

Let $C$ and $W$ be Hermitian spaces of dimensions three and two.

\begin{definition}[Standard-Model determinant seed]
A Standard-Model determinant seed is
$\mathfrak S_{\rm SM}=(C,W,\tau)$ with a unitary isomorphism
\[
 \tau:\det C\otimes\det W\xrightarrow{\sim}\C.
\]
Only the determinant line and its stabilizer are physical in the finite group
reconstruction: replacing $\tau$ by $e^{i\theta}\tau$ changes neither the
stabilizer nor any completely positive incidence branch.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Automorphism reconstruction of the global gauge group]
\label{thm:SM-group}
The unitary tensor automorphism group of the determinant seed is
\[
 \boxed{
 \Aut_{\rm U}(C,W,\tau)=S(\U(3)\times\U(2))
 \cong\frac{\SU(3)\times\SU(2)\times\U(1)}{\Z_6}.}
\]
An explicit quotient map is
$\Phi(g_3,g_2,z)=(z^{-2}g_3,z^3g_2)$, with kernel
$\{(z^2I_3,z^{-3}I_2,z):z^6=1\}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
A pair $(A,B)\in\U(C)\times\U(W)$ preserves $\tau$ exactly when
$\det(A)\det(B)=1$, giving $S(\U(3)\times\U(2))$.  The displayed map has
image in this subgroup.  Given $(A,B)$ there, choose $z^6=\det B$ and put
$g_3=z^2A$, $g_2=z^{-3}B$; these are special unitary and map to $(A,B)$.
The kernel is the displayed order-six central subgroup.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Anomaly-forced central weights]
\label{thm:SM-anomaly-forced-weights}
Let the central infinitesimal action on $C\oplus W$ be
$iaI_C\oplus ibI_W$.  On the tensor types
\[
 Q=C\otimes W,\quad u=\Lambda^2C^*,\quad d=C,
 \quad L=W^*,\quad e=\Lambda^2W^*,\quad H=W,
\]
the corresponding weights are
\[
 (a+b,-2a,a,-b,-2b,b).
\]
After replacing right-handed matter by left-handed conjugates, all local mixed,
cubic, and gravitational anomalies vanish exactly when
\[
 \boxed{3a+2b=0.}
\]
Up to reversal of the $U(1)$ orientation, the primitive integral solution is
$(a,b)=(-2,3)$ and therefore
\[
 \boxed{y=6Y:\quad (Q,u,d,L,e,H)=(1,4,-2,-3,-6,3).}
\]
Thus the finite hypercharge table is fixed by the dimensions $(3,2)$, the
tensor type packet, and anomaly freedom; it is not an independent loading
parameter.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Direct trace over the left-handed chiral packet gives
\[
 \mathcal A_{\SU(3)^2Y}=\mathcal A_{\SU(2)^2Y}
 =\frac12(3a+2b),
 \qquad
 \mathcal A_{{\rm grav}^2Y}=3(3a+2b),
\]
and
\[
 \mathcal A_{Y^3}=3(3a+2b)(3a^2+2b^2).
\]
The pure colour anomaly cancels as $2-1-1$, and four weak doublets remove the
Witten anomaly.  Since $3a^2+2b^2>0$ for a nontrivial action, simultaneous
vanishing is equivalent to $3a+2b=0$.  The coprime integral solution is
$(-2,3)$ up to sign, and substitution gives the displayed weights.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Renewal-admissible finite real algebra]
\label{thm:SM-finite-real-algebra}
Assume a charged finite real geometry has at most three charged central
summands and total non-scalar real algebra dimension at most $22$.  Assume it
contains an independent complex scalar factor, a quaternionic factor carrying
a minimal pseudoreal weak doublet, and a genuinely complex faithful colour
factor of rank at least three.  Then, up to permutation of summands,
\[
 \boxed{\mathcal A_F^{\rm ch}\cong
 \C\oplus\mathbb H\oplus M_3(\C).}
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The quaternionic factor has real dimension $4$.  A genuinely complex matrix
factor of rank at least three has real dimension at least
$2\cdot3^2=18$.  These two factors already exhaust the non-scalar dimension
bound $22$.  The independent scalar channel contributes no non-scalar
dimension.  Replacing $M_3(\C)$ by a smaller complex matrix algebra violates
the colour-rank hypothesis; omitting $\mathbb H$ violates pseudoreal weak type;
omitting $\C$ removes the independent scalar channel; and adding another
non-scalar factor exceeds the bound.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Central descent selector]
\label{thm:SM-selector}
An irreducible $\SU(3)\times\SU(2)\times\U(1)$ representation with colour
triality $t\in\Z/3$, weak parity $s\in\Z/2$, and integer charge $y=6Y$
descends to the quotient in \Cref{thm:SM-group} exactly when
\[
 \boxed{2t+3s+y\equiv0\pmod6.}
\]
Its indicator is the finite Fourier projector
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathbf1_{2t+3s+y\equiv0\ (6)}
 =\frac16\sum_{k=0}^5
 \exp\!\left(\frac{2\pi ik}{6}(2t+3s+y)\right).}
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
A generator of the quotient kernel acts by
$\exp(2\pi i(2t+3s+y)/6)$.  Triviality gives the congruence, and character
orthogonality on $\Z/6\Z$ gives the indicator.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Tensor generation of one chiral matter packet]
\label{thm:SM-generation}
Define
\[
 Q=C\otimes W,
 \quad u=\Lambda^2C^*,
 \quad d=C,
 \quad L=W^*,
 \quad e=\Lambda^2W^*,
 \quad H=W.
\]
Their $(\SU(3),\SU(2))_y$ labels are
\[
\begin{array}{c|c}
 Q&(\mathbf3,\mathbf2)_1\\
 u&(\mathbf3,\mathbf1)_4\\
 d&(\mathbf3,\mathbf1)_{-2}\\
 L&(\mathbf1,\mathbf2)_{-3}\\
 e&(\mathbf1,\mathbf1)_{-6}\\
 H&(\mathbf1,\mathbf2)_3.
\end{array}
\]
The seed supplies one-dimensional intertwiner spaces for
$Q\otimes H\to u$, $Q\otimes H^*\to d$, and $L\otimes H^*\to e$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
By \Cref{thm:SM-anomaly-forced-weights}, the primitive central weights are
$C\sim(\mathbf3,\mathbf1)_{-2}$ and
$W\sim(\mathbf1,\mathbf2)_3$.  Tensor products add charge, and
$\Lambda^2\overline{\mathbf3}\cong\mathbf3$.  Evaluation gives the down
channel, exterior multiplication gives the lepton channel, and the determinant
seed identifies the up channel.  Each target irreducible occurs once, so the
intertwiner space is one dimensional by Schur's lemma.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Anomaly cancellation of the generated packet]
\label{thm:SM-anomaly}
After replacing right-handed fields by left-handed conjugates, the packet
$Q\oplus u^c\oplus d^c\oplus L\oplus e^c$ has vanishing local gauge and mixed
gravity anomalies and no Witten $\SU(2)$ anomaly.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
With quadratic index $1/2$ for defining representations, the anomaly
coefficients are
\[
 2-1-1=0,
\]
\[
 2(1)\frac12+(-4)\frac12+(2)\frac12=0,
 \qquad
 3(1)\frac12+(-3)\frac12=0,
\]
\[
 6(1)^3+3(-4)^3+3(2)^3+2(-3)^3+6^3=0,
\]
and
\[
 6(1)+3(-4)+3(2)+2(-3)+6=0.
\]
There are four weak doublets after colour multiplicity is included, so the
global $\SU(2)$ anomaly also vanishes.
\end{proof}

\begin{countertheorem}[Gauge data do not determine generation number]
\label{cth:generation-number}
For every $g\ge1$, tensor the anomaly-free one-generation matter packet by a
trivial multiplicity space $F_g\cong\C^g$.  The gauge types, central descent
law, incidence slots, and anomaly cancellation remain unchanged, while the
generation number is $g$.
\end{countertheorem}

\begin{proof}
Tensoring by a trivial representation changes no irreducible gauge type and
multiplies each local anomaly coefficient by $g$, so zero remains zero.  The
number of weak doublets becomes $4g$ and remains even.  The multiplicity space
lies in the commutant and is therefore invisible to the associative gauge
relations alone.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Incidence-before-interference firewall]
\label{thm:SM-incidence-firewall}
Let $P_R,P_L$ be two typed supports.  If every primitive coefficient $K_a$
satisfies $P_LK_aP_R=0$, then every finite coefficient obtained from the
$K_a$ by sums, products, adjoints, ancillary matrix coefficients, coherent
order control, postselection, environment measurement, or norm limits also
has zero $P_R\to P_L$ block.  In particular, no character, Maslov, Walsh, or
relative-history compression can create a grading-changing occurrence that is
absent from the primitive coefficient algebra.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The coefficients preserving the support decomposition form a unital
$C^*$-algebra.  It is closed under sums, products, adjoints, tensoring with
ancillas, taking ancillary matrix coefficients, and norm limits.  Every listed
network operation remains in this algebra.  Character and Walsh compressions
are finite linear combinations, so their cross block also vanishes.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Common-row top-Walsh occurrence reconstruction]
\label{thm:SM-top-Walsh}
Let $X_j^2=\delta_jI$ with $\delta_j>0$, put
$N_j=\delta_j^{-1/2}X_j$, and let one typed occurrence row be
$\mathcal C:Q_0\to Y$.  For $\varepsilon\in\{\pm1\}^m$ define
\[
 K_\varepsilon(\mathbf t)=\mathcal C
 e^{-i\varepsilon_1t_1X_1}\cdots e^{-i\varepsilon_mt_mX_m}.
\]
For $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}$ let
$\chi_S(\varepsilon)=\prod_{j\in S}\varepsilon_j$ and
$K_S=2^{-m/2}\sum_\varepsilon\chi_S(\varepsilon)K_\varepsilon$.  Then
\[
 \boxed{
 K_S(\mathbf t)=2^{m/2}
 \prod_{j\notin S}\cos(\sqrt{\delta_j}t_j)
 \prod_{j\in S}[-i\sin(\sqrt{\delta_j}t_j)]
 \mathcal C N_S,}
\]
with the $N_j$ kept in their displayed order.  At quarter dwells
$t_j=(2k_j+1)\pi/(2\sqrt{\delta_j})$, every proper Walsh column vanishes and
the top column is a nonzero scalar times $\mathcal C N_1\cdots N_m$.
Consequently, when the ordered product is unitary, the top column reconstructs
$\mathcal C$ and has the same rank.  The conclusion requires the physical
common-row residual to vanish; equal resolved branch effects alone do not
supply that relation.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Use
$e^{-i\varepsilon_jt_jX_j}=\cos(\sqrt{\delta_j}t_j)I
-i\varepsilon_j\sin(\sqrt{\delta_j}t_j)N_j$ and expand the ordered product.
Walsh orthogonality kills every monomial whose sign set differs from $S$.
At quarter dwell every cosine is zero, so only the full sign set survives.
If the ordered product is unitary, right multiplication by its adjoint recovers
the occurrence row.  Without one common terminal row, branch-dependent phases
can preserve every resolved effect while changing the top Walsh column, so the
common-row certificate is necessary.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Principal matter-module theorem]
\label{thm:SM-principal-module}
Let $Q_0\cong\C^2$ and let $C_0:Q_0\to Y$ be a nonzero loaded occurrence row
with
\[
 C_0^*C_0=\kappa I_{Q_0},\qquad \kappa>0.
\]
Then
\[
 \mathcal J_{C_0}:M_2(\C)\to\operatorname{Hom}(Q_0,Y),
 \qquad \mathcal J_{C_0}(X)=\kappa^{-1/2}C_0X,
\]
is an isometric faithful right $M_2(\C)$ module map:
\[
 \boxed{\mathcal J_{C_0}(X)^*\mathcal J_{C_0}(Y)=X^*Y.}
\]
The Choi or Stinespring rank of the complete occurrence column is environment
memory and is not a generation count.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The identity is
$\kappa^{-1}X^*C_0^*C_0Y=X^*Y$.  Hence the range is one standard faithful
right module.  Replacing $C_0$ by a minimal Stinespring column changes only the
environment basis; its rank is therefore an implementation dimension and does
not change the source-side module.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Source-derived commutator--Hodge generation carrier]
\label{thm:SM-commutator-Hodge}
Let $W_0=\mathbf1^\perp\subset\R^4$ and let
$F:W_0\to\operatorname{Herm}_0(M_2(\C))$ be a tetrahedrally covariant writer
with
\[
 \tau_2(F(x)F(y))=\lambda\langle x,y\rangle,
 \qquad \lambda>0.
\]
Under $H^1(K_4;\R)\cong\bigwedge^2W_0$, define
\[
 \mathcal C_F(x\wedge y)=-\frac i2[F(x),F(y)].
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{
 \tau_2(\mathcal C_F(\xi)\mathcal C_F(\eta))
 =\lambda^2\langle\xi,\eta\rangle,}
\]
so $\lambda^{-1}\mathcal C_F$ is an orthogonal isomorphism
\[
 \boxed{H^1(K_4;\R)\cong\operatorname{Herm}_0(M_2(\C)).}
\]
Composing with the occurrence row of \Cref{thm:SM-principal-module} produces
six physical commutator-edge histories spanning one source-derived
three-dimensional generation carrier.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Choose an orthogonal coordinate map $O:W_0\to\R^3$ with
$F(x)=\sqrt\lambda\,Ox\cdot\sigma$.  The Pauli identity gives
$-\frac i2[F(x),F(y)]=\lambda(Ox\times Oy)\cdot\sigma$.  The cross-product
inner product is the exterior-square inner product, proving the metric formula
and bijectivity.  Multiplication on the left by $C_0/\sqrt\kappa$ preserves
that Gram and therefore transports the carrier into the physical occurrence
space.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Copy--deformation separation and multiplicity saturation]
\label{thm:SM-multiplicity-saturation}
Let the complete future-cyclic carrier support the faithful right
$M_2(\C)$ action of \Cref{thm:SM-principal-module}.  Suppose the future
transfer $T$ commutes with that action; equivalently, its writer--Casimir
commutator Gram vanishes.  Then, up to a multiplicity-space unitary,
\[
 \mathcal K=\mathcal M\otimes\C^2,
 \qquad T=A\otimes I_2,
 \qquad S=B\otimes I_2.
\]
For
\[
 \mathbb G_{{\rm mult},n}
 =\bigl[B^*A^{*i}A^jB\bigr]_{0\le i,j<n},
\]
the matter and generation Grams factor as
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathbb G_{{\rm mat},n}=\mathbb G_{{\rm mult},n}\otimes I_2,
 \qquad
 \mathbb G_{{\rm gen},n}=\mathbb G_{{\rm mult},n}\otimes I_3.}
\]
If $g_n$ and $h_n$ are the cross and next-layer blocks, then
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathfrak L_{{\rm mult},n}
 =h_n-g_n^*\mathbb G_{{\rm mult},n}^\dagger g_n\succeq0}
\]
has rank equal to the next multiplicity-rank increment.  The minimal
future-visible realization has exactly one generation copy precisely when,
for some $n$,
\[
 \boxed{\rank\mathbb G_{{\rm mult},n}=1,
 \qquad \mathfrak L_{{\rm mult},n}=0.}
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Every finite unital representation of $M_2(\C)$ is a direct sum of defining
representations, giving $\mathcal K\cong\mathcal M\otimes\C^2$.  Its
commutant is $\End(\mathcal M)\otimes I_2$, so the zero deformation condition
gives $T=A\otimes I_2$ and module naturality gives $S=B\otimes I_2$.
The displayed matrices are Grams of the Krylov columns $A^jB$ tensored with
the identity on the matter or Hodge carrier.  The generalized Schur complement
is the Gram of the orthogonal part of the next column, proving the rank and
saturation statements.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Marked bi-Hankel reconstruction of the finite Dirac operator]
\label{thm:SM-marked-Dirac}
Let $S$ be the common source synthesis, $M$ the reconstructed future transfer,
and assume the ordinary block Hankel Gram
\[
 \mathbb H_d=[S^*M^{i+j}S]_{0\le i,j\le d}
\]
is flat.  Let
\[
 \mathbb N_d=[S^*M^iDM^jS]_{0\le i,j\le d}
\]
be an independently measured one-insertion panel and put
$P_{\mathbb H}=\mathbb H_d\mathbb H_d^\dagger$.  If
\[
 \Delta_{\rm null}^D
 =\|(I-P_{\mathbb H})\mathbb N_d\|_{\HS}^2
 +\|\mathbb N_d(I-P_{\mathbb H})\|_{\HS}^2=0,
\]
then for every full-row-rank Gram factorization $\mathbb H_d=R_d^*R_d$,
\[
 \boxed{D_{R_d}=(R_d^\dagger)^*\mathbb N_dR_d^\dagger}
\]
is the unique packet operator with $\mathbb N_d=R_d^*D_{R_d}R_d$.
Different Gram factors conjugate $D_{R_d}$ by the same packet unitary.  After
self-adjointness, grading, reality, order, one-leg, generation, slot, and
Majorana tests, this one operator exports
\[
 \boxed{Y_u,Y_d,Y_e,Y_\nu,M_R}
\]
in one common physical generation frame.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The same-null condition says that the sesquilinear form encoded by
$\mathbb N_d$ descends to the quotient determined by $\mathbb H_d$.  The
Moore--Penrose formula is the unique representing operator on the row space.
Two full-row-rank Gram factors differ by one unitary, so the reconstructed
operator transforms by that same unitary.  All support, type, and slot
projections are reconstructed on the same packet; therefore every Yukawa block
is obtained by one common orthogonal compression and all blocks share the same
generation gauge.  The Majorana block transforms by congruence because it is a
symmetric singlet form.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Exact no-matter obstruction for the displayed six-state source]
\label{thm:SM-six-state-no-matter}
Suppose every primitive system-bearing coefficient of a source commutes with a
common central-support and grading refinement.  Then every finite or
norm-convergent network formed from those coefficients by serial or parallel
composition, coherent order control, ancillas, feedback, postselection,
environment measurement, and chronological limits is support preserving.
Consequently every grading-changing Maslov/Walsh coefficient and every marked
finite-Dirac block is zero.  In particular, for the displayed six-state source,
\[
 \boxed{K_\mu=0,\qquad Q_\mu=0,\qquad D_F=0.}
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The block-preserving coefficients form a unital $C^*$-algebra closed under all
listed operations and norm limits.  Every effective coefficient therefore has
zero cross-support block.  Finite character compression and the marked-panel
reconstruction are linear or quotient operations on those coefficients and
cannot create an absent block.
\end{proof}

\subsubsection{Generator-native occurrence and typed Radon--Nikodym geometry}
\label{sec:SM-generator-native-occurrence}

The incidence firewall says that a stationary grading-even source cannot create
matter.  The correct next object is therefore the cross-support first derivative
of the actual pre-release semigroup, not another stationary likelihood or a
chosen Yukawa matrix.

\begin{theorem}[Cross-support extraction from a CP generator]
\label{thm:SM-cross-support-generator}
Let $\mathcal T_{t,*}=e^{t\mathcal L_*}$ be a finite-dimensional completely
positive trace-preserving semigroup on
$\mathcal H=\mathcal H_L\oplus\mathcal H_R$.  Define
\[
 \boxed{\Phi_{L\leftarrow R}(X)
 =P_L\mathcal L_*(P_RXP_R)P_L}
\]
and similarly $\Phi_{R\leftarrow L}$.  These maps are completely positive and
are reconstructed operationally by
\[
 \boxed{\Phi_{L\leftarrow R}(X)
 =\lim_{t\downarrow0}t^{-1}P_L\mathcal T_{t,*}(P_RXP_R)P_L.}
\]
In every GKSL representation only the support-changing jump amplitudes survive:
\[
 \boxed{\Phi_{L\leftarrow R}(X)
 =\sum_\alpha(P_LV_\alpha P_R)X(P_RV_\alpha^*P_L).}
\]
The Hamiltonian and anticommutator terms vanish under this compression.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Insert the GKSL formula.  Since $P_LP_R=0$, both the commutator with the
Hamiltonian and each anticommutator term has zero $L\leftarrow R$ compression.
The remaining sum is Kraus form and hence CP.  Differentiability of the
semigroup at zero gives the operational limit.  Because the map is defined
from $\mathcal L_*$ itself, it is independent of the chosen GKSL coordinates.
\end{proof}



% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
\subsubsection{Channel-native Hamiltonian tangents and noisy coherent compilation}
\label{sec:SMST-channel-native-tangent}
% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

The principal-log branch of \Cref{thm:SMST-store-native-route} is an exact
finite-time reconstruction, but exact unitary pulses are stronger than finite
SM emergence requires.  The weaker operational datum is a two-sided physical
channel family through the identity whose first derivative is a Hamiltonian
derivation on the canonical source core.  Dissipative or leakage terms which
begin at second order may be suppressed by physical subdivision and are not
first-order matter obstructions.

Let \(M_d=M_d(\C)\), with matrix units \(E_{ab}\).  For linear maps
\(\mathcal L_1,\mathcal L_2:M_d\to M_d\), define
\[
 \boxed{
 \langle\!\langle\mathcal L_1,\mathcal L_2\rangle\!\rangle
 :=\sum_{a,b=1}^{d}
   \langle\mathcal L_1(E_{ab}),\mathcal L_2(E_{ab})\rangle_{\HS}.}
\]
Write \(\|\cdot\|_{\rm sup,HS}\) for the associated norm, using the real
Hilbert structure on Hermiticity-preserving maps.

\begin{lemma}[Exact conditioning of inner derivations]
\label{lem:SMST-inner-derivation-norm}
For \(H=H^*\),
\[
 \boxed{
 \|\operatorname{ad}_H\|_{\rm sup,HS}^2
 =2d\left\|H-\frac{\Tr H}{d}I\right\|_{\HS}^2.}
\]
Thus \(H\mapsto-i\operatorname{ad}_H\) is injective on traceless Hermitian
matrices and has smallest singular value \(\sqrt{2d}\).
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Expand
\(\sum_{a,b}\|HE_{ab}-E_{ab}H\|_{\HS}^2\).  The two diagonal sums are
\(d\Tr(H^2)\), while the two mixed sums total \(2|\Tr H|^2\).  Their
difference is the displayed expression.
\end{proof}

Choose an orthonormal basis
\((T_\alpha)_{\alpha=1}^{d^2-1}\) of the traceless Hermitian matrices and put
\(\mathcal C_\alpha=-i\operatorname{ad}_{T_\alpha}\).  Let
\[
 G^{\rm Ham}_{\alpha\beta}
 =\langle\!\langle\mathcal C_\alpha,\mathcal C_\beta\rangle\!\rangle,
 \qquad
 b_\alpha(\mathcal L)
 =\langle\!\langle\mathcal C_\alpha,\mathcal L\rangle\!\rangle.
\]

\begin{definition}[Canonical Hamiltonian tangent]
\label{def:SMST-Hamiltonian-tangent}
For a Hermiticity-preserving map \(\mathcal L:M_d\to M_d\), define
\[
 \boxed{
 H_{\mathcal L}
 =\sum_\alpha
 \bigl((G^{\rm Ham})^{-1}b(\mathcal L)\bigr)_\alpha T_\alpha,}
\]
\[
 \boxed{
 \Delta_{\rm Ham}(\mathcal L)
 =\|\mathcal L+i\operatorname{ad}_{H_{\mathcal L}}\|_{\rm sup,HS}^2.}
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Finite Hamiltonian-tangent certificate]
\label{thm:SMST-Hamiltonian-tangent-certificate}
The operator \(H_{\mathcal L}\) is the unique traceless Hermitian minimizer of
\[
 H\longmapsto\|\mathcal L+i\operatorname{ad}_H\|_{\rm sup,HS}^2.
\]
Moreover
\[
 \boxed{
 \Delta_{\rm Ham}(\mathcal L)=0
 \iff
 \mathcal L=-i\operatorname{ad}_{H_{\mathcal L}}.}
\]
On the positive branch,
\[
 \frac{\mathcal L+i\operatorname{ad}_{H_{\mathcal L}}}
