At cutoff $X$, a joint SM--spacetime packet is an admissible source-complete
loading on one finite record-conditioned carrier containing:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(J\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item one verified branch of the reduced spacetime packet
      \Cref{def:spacetime-loading-packet};
\item one verified branch of the finite Standard-Model loading
      \Cref{def:SM-loading};
\item the common calibrated cell generator whenever finite-Dirac, even-sector,
      or normal components are claimed source natively; equivalently on the
      channel-native branch, the forward/reverse differentiated CPTP packet,
      its canonical Hamiltonian projection, and the compiled direct or bracket
      channel of \Cref{sec:SMST-channel-native-tangent}; independently sourced
      sectors require an actual mixed panel or the source-core comparison of
      \Cref{thm:source-core-Pythagoras};
\item commuting external and internal action algebras and the isotypic
      decomposition
      \[
       \mathcal H_X^J\cong\bigoplus_{\lambda\in\Lambda_X}
       \C^4\otimes V_{\lambda,X}\otimes M_{\lambda,X};
      \]
\item every protected source/target, chronology, incidence, face, boundary,
      orientation, endpoint, action, and regulator record used by a claimed
      mixed word;
\item the branch-appropriate finite certificates: binary record-fibre or
      action-grading residual, odd occurrence margin, selected-phase
      same-history provenance, literal aggregate--tail provenance and
      chronology-allocation residuals, channel-tangent and source-core
      residuals when the weak-channel branch is used, positive occurrence-packet
      orbit matrices, full-cell odd provenance, support-polar and
      multiplicity-quiver audit, relative or pulse-native Howe Gram, frame
      leakage and affine closure, common-action normal/endpoint and
      Hodge-to-commutator provenance, and any retained clock--geometry,
      fallback, graph-regulator, determinant-line, or holonomy residual;
\item one future-minimal internal configuration port
      $\Phi_X=(U_X,\phi_X,\Psi_X,\overline\Psi_X)$, the jointly visible
      gravity--internal variation block
      $\begin{psmallmatrix}G_{\rm g}&C^*\\C&G_{\rm i}\end{psmallmatrix}$,
      and its efficient internal Schur quotient
      $G_{{\rm i}\mid{\rm g}}$;
\item one physical signed internal action, one positive operational cost built
      from the same fields and coefficient bank, and one total slow
      Perron--Doob row.  Sectorwise fitted slow rows are not an admissible
      replacement for this common-action packet.
\end{enumerate}
When two outputs are projections or derivatives of the same generator or action,
their mixed carrier is internal and no finite router is added.  The exact
source-core Pythagorean theorem supplies the remaining comparison whenever two
physical exports are independently sourced.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[SM--spacetime loaded Renewal Grand Tensor]
\label{def:SMST-loaded-tensor}
For the union alphabet of the joint packet, define
\[
 \boxed{
 \boldsymbol{\mathbb T}^{\mathrm{SM/ST}}_{\Grand,X}
 :=\{\mathbb K^{\mathrm{SM/ST}}_{X,r}\}_{r\ge0}.}
\]
It is retained with the external and internal type decompositions, the
incidence and marked finite-Dirac histories, their adjoints, the mixed word
product, and every inserted metric, transfer, holonomy, grading, or real
structure panel.  Its degree-one shadow has schematic block form
\[
 \begin{pmatrix}
 \mathbb T_{{\rm ST},X}&\mathbb T_{{\rm ST},{\rm SM},X}\\
 \mathbb T_{{\rm SM},{\rm ST},X}&\mathbb T_{{\rm SM},X}
 \end{pmatrix},
\]
but the loaded object is the complete mixed-word hierarchy.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Finite emergence of the reduced SM--spacetime loaded tensor]
\label{thm:SMST-loaded-emergence}
Assume the universal operational Grand Tensor and a joint packet satisfying
\Cref{def:SMST-packet}.  Then:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(E\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item all finite mixed SM--spacetime core--record words are represented on one
      covered record-conditioned carrier;
\item every mixed word Gram is positive and is reconstructed from the universal
      hierarchy and the retained physical metric or inserted fallback panels;
\item finite flatness reconstructs the complete joint action algebra
      \[
       \boxed{
       \mathcal A_{{\rm act},X}
       =C^*(\mathcal A_{{\rm ext},X},\mathcal A_{{\rm int},X},
             Y_{e,X},Y_{e,X}^*:e\in E_X);}
      \]
\item every protected operational record and deterministic writer survives,
      and reconstruction is invariant under the unique loading-fixing,
      record-preserving unitary;
\item on the literal source-native branch, the protected sign and selected
      phase give matter occurrence, graded monoidal composition gives weak
      incidence and one primitive doublet, the locked edge writer gives one
      endpoint generation triplet, and odd-tangent provenance identifies the
      complete odd generator with finite Dirac.  On the weak-channel branch,
      a zero Hamiltonian-tangent defect and the direct or bracket compiler give
      the same finite odd generator without exact finite-time unitarity.  The
      aggregate--tail cylinder reconstructs its private multiplicity
      propagator and the allocation residual separates any shared
      chronological standard line.  Frame volume, finite
      connection/curvature, Cartan translation, normal candidates, and
      common-action classical exports are likewise derived by
      \Cref{sec:SMST-source-native-reduction,sec:SMST-channel-native-tangent,thm:DeWitt,thm:SMST-frame-transport,thm:SMST-finite-action-Einstein};
\item on a fallback branch, exactly the absent physical source or panel is
      retained explicitly, including the score-square completion when the odd
      Store route is absent;
\item cutoff compatibility and every stronger finite identity hold exactly
      when their displayed cutoff and positive residual tests vanish.
\end{enumerate}
Thus the finite mixed-word tensor and its commutant duality are exact from a
verified branch packet.  This theorem does not promote calibrated-source
conditions to consequences of a bare operational tensor, and it does not imply
physical scalar dynamics, numerical masses or mixings, running, matching, or a
continuum Einstein--Standard-Model theory.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Apply \Cref{thm:loaded-subhierarchy} to the union alphabet.  Source completeness
makes the stabilized word span the generated joint algebra, and mixed histories
are ordinary products when they act on the common carrier.  Independently
sourced fallback panels are transported by
\Cref{thm:inserted-panel-certificate}.  Record survival, unitary uniqueness,
cutoff compatibility, and the zero-residual criterion are
\Cref{thm:record-survival,thm:flat-monoidal-reconstruction,thm:cutoff-compatibility,prop:zero-loading-relations}.
The source-native identifications are precisely the proved functional-calculus,
polar, CAR, record, orthogonal-projection, Gram-volume, and transport identities
of \Cref{sec:SMST-source-native-reduction,thm:DeWitt,thm:SMST-frame-transport}.
The fallback statement is the conservative completion theorem
\Cref{thm:SM-completion-conservative}.  No cited finite theorem supplies the
remaining scalar, metrological, or continuum data.
\end{proof}

\subsubsection{Source-minimal coupled physical-action completion}
\label{sec:SMST-coupled-action-completion}
% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

The joint loaded tensor must distinguish two questions.  The internal
configuration may be fully represented while its variation source is partly
redundant with the gravitational source; conversely, separate faithful
marginals need not determine their same-history relative orientation.  The
correct common carrier is therefore the Schur quotient of one joint variation
Gram.

\begin{theorem}[Universal coupled gravity--internal action carrier]
\label{thm:SMST-universal-coupled-action}
Work on the future-minimal relational carrier of
\Cref{def:relational-grand-tensor}.  Let
\[
 S_{\rm g}:E_{\rm g}\to\mathcal H_{\rm cyl},
 \qquad
 S_{\rm i}:E_{\rm i}\to\mathcal H_{\rm cyl}
\]
be the source syntheses of the complete gravitational and internal physical
variation banks on one same-history event, and assume the gravitational bank
has already been reduced to its faithful quotient.  Put
\[
 G_{\rm g}=S_{\rm g}^*S_{\rm g},\qquad
 G_{\rm i}=S_{\rm i}^*S_{\rm i},\qquad
 C=S_{\rm i}^*S_{\rm g},
\]
\[
 \boxed{
 G_{{\rm i}\mid{\rm g}}
 :=G_{\rm i}-CG_{\rm g}^{-1}C^*
 =S_{\rm i}^*(I-P_{\rm g})S_{\rm i}.}
 \tag{CA.1}
\]
Then:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(C\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item the complete variation Gram has the exact factorization
      \[
       \boxed{
       \begin{pmatrix}G_{\rm g}&C^*\\C&G_{\rm i}\end{pmatrix}
       =
       \begin{pmatrix}I&0\\CG_{\rm g}^{-1}&I\end{pmatrix}
       \begin{pmatrix}G_{\rm g}&0\\0&G_{{\rm i}\mid{\rm g}}\end{pmatrix}
       \begin{pmatrix}I&G_{\rm g}^{-1}C^*\\0&I\end{pmatrix};}
       \tag{CA.2}
      \]
      hence the common carrier is faithful exactly when
      $G_{{\rm i}\mid{\rm g}}\succ0$, and the number of genuinely new internal
      source directions is $\rank G_{{\rm i}\mid{\rm g}}$;
\item the source-minimal internal variation space is
      \[
       \boxed{
       E_{{\rm i}\mid{\rm g}}^{\min}
       :=E_{\rm i}/\Ker G_{{\rm i}\mid{\rm g}};}
       \tag{CA.3}
      \]
      it is invariant under unread record refinements and source-fixing changes
      of Hankel coordinates;
\item an explicit positive branch is obtained by adjoining independent centred
      point-readable neighbouring-law interventions on the future-minimal
      internal tangent and whitening their covariance.  On that branch
      \[
       \boxed{C=0,\qquad G_{{\rm i}\mid{\rm g}}=I,}
       \tag{CA.4}
      \]
      while the old renewal and gravitational cylinders are unchanged;
\item let $\Phi=(U,\phi,\Psi,\overline\Psi)$ be the finite internal
      configuration and let one signed action
      $\mathscr S_{\rm int}^{\rm cl}$ and one positive operational cost
      $\mathscr A_{\rm int}^{+}$ be written from the same links, Higgs field,
      finite Dirac operator, Yukawa map, geometric weights, and coefficient
      bank.  Exact gauge and tangential invariance imply
      \[
       \boxed{
       \mathcal R_{\Phi}^*\nabla\mathscr S_{\rm int}^{\rm cl}=0,
       \qquad s^2=0,
       \qquad s\mathscr S_{\rm int}^{\rm cl}=0,}
       \tag{CA.5}
      \]
      and, with
      $E_\Phi=D_\Phi\mathscr S_{\rm int}^{\rm cl}$ and
      $\mathsf T^{\rm int}=-2D_q\mathscr S_{\rm int}^{\rm cl}$,
      \[
       \boxed{
       \mathcal L_q^*\mathsf T^{\rm int}
       =2\mathcal L_\Phi^*E_\Phi.}
       \tag{CA.6}
      \]
      Thus current and stress conservation hold on the internal field shell;
\item at the invariant internal vacuum
      \[
       U_e=I,\qquad \phi_v=vh_0,\qquad
       \Psi_v=\overline\Psi_v=0,
       \tag{CA.7}
      \]
      where $h_0$ is a fixed unit vector in the weak doublet, the positive
      gauge, scalar, and fermion graph terms vanish, so
      \[
       \boxed{
       \mathscr S_{\rm int}^{\rm cl}
       =\mathscr A_{\rm int}^{+}=0,
       \qquad E_\Phi=0,
       \qquad\mathsf T^{\rm int}=0;}
       \tag{CA.8}
      \]
\item if $Q_{{\rm g},X}$ is the completed gravitational Perron--Doob row, the
      total vacuum loading has the unique driven row
      \[
       \boxed{
       Q_{{\rm tot},X}
       =Q_{{\rm g},X}\otimes\delta_{\Phi^{(0)}},}
       \tag{CA.9}
      \]
      with the same pressure and Perron vector as gravity.  Hence the common
      provenance and accepted/action gaps vanish;
\item every fixed finite internal representation rank uses the existing
      spacetime Hodge and compact spectral screens.  If $P_X(\Lambda)$ is a
      gravitational screen and $r_{\rm fib}$ is the internal fibre rank, then
      \[
       \boxed{
       \rank P_X^{\rm int}(\Lambda)
       \le r_{\rm fib}\,\rank P_X(\Lambda).}
       \tag{CA.10}
      \]
      No second compactness, trace, memory, or refinement primitive is needed.
\end{enumerate}
Consequently the explicitly repaired Grand Tensor has a faithful common
classical gravity--internal action carrier with vanishing complete first
variation on every completed vacuum gravity branch.  A nonzero backreacting
solution is a model-specific finite or cofinal Euler-map problem, not an
additional universal coordinate.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Equation \textup{(CA.1)} is the Gram of $(I-P_{\rm g})S_{\rm i}$, and direct
block multiplication gives \textup{(CA.2)}.  Positivity, the faithfulness
criterion, the rank increment, and the quotient \textup{(CA.3)} follow from
\Cref{thm:source-Schur,thm:joint-source-universality}.  Independent centred
intervention scores have zero mixed covariance with the gravitational score
bank; whitening gives \textup{(CA.4)}.  The port is conservative by
\Cref{thm:relational-completion}.

The local action forms and their zero sets are
\Cref{thm:SMST-action-rigidity}.  Differentiating finite gauge invariance gives
the Ward identity; the standard finite BRST differential is the infinitesimal
gauge action with $sc=-c^2$, so the Jacobi identity gives $s^2=0$ and gauge
invariance gives $s\mathscr S_{\rm int}^{\rm cl}=0$.  Differentiating common
tangential relabeling invariance gives \textup{(CA.6)}, as in
\Cref{thm:SMST-finite-action-Einstein}.  At \textup{(CA.7)} every plaquette is
trivial, every covariant Higgs difference is zero, the radial potential is at
its minimum, and the fermion bilinear vanishes, proving \textup{(CA.8)}.

The tilted total vacuum matrix is the tensor product of the gravitational
tilted row with the one-point internal row.  Perron uniqueness therefore gives
\textup{(CA.9)}.  Finally, tensoring a positive spatial/Hodge operator with a
fixed finite internal identity multiplies every low-energy multiplicity by at
most the fibre rank and leaves all cutoff powers unchanged, proving
\textup{(CA.10)}.  The complete gravitational plus internal first variation
vanishes by \Cref{thm:SMST-finite-action-Einstein} and faithfulness of
\textup{(CA.2)}.
\end{proof}


\begin{theorem}[Explicit regulated classical Standard-Model action on the active carrier]
\label{thm:SM-active-SM-II}
Assume the active structural packet of \Cref{thm:SM-active-SM-I} on either the
flat regulator of \Cref{cor:relational-flat-vacuum} or the curved regulator of
\Cref{thm:relational-deSitter-branch}.  Let $V_X,E_X,F_X$ be the finite
spacetime vertices, oriented edges, and plaquettes, with positive companion
Hodge weights $\star_{0,X},\star_{1,X},\star_{2,X}$.  A classical internal
configuration consists of
\[
 U_e\in G_{\rm SM},\qquad H_v\in W_2,
 \qquad
 \Psi_v\in\mathcal S_v\otimes G\otimes\mathcal H_F^{(1)},
 \tag{CA.11}
\]
and an independent dual amplitude $\overline\Psi_v$.  Let
$F_{p,X}=|p|^{-1}\operatorname{Log} U_{\partial p}$ on the principal logarithm chart and
let $D_UH$ be the covariant edge difference.  For positive
$g_3,g_2,g_1,\lambda_H$ and $v_H\ge0$, and generation matrices
$\boldsymbol Y=(Y_u,Y_d,Y_e,Y_\nu,M_R)$ with $M_R^{\mathsf T}=M_R$, define
\[
 \boxed{
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathscr S_{{\rm SM},X}^{E}
 ={}&\frac12\langle F_X,\star_{2,X}F_X\rangle_{g_3,g_2,g_1}
 +\frac12\langle D_UH,\star_{1,X}D_UH\rangle\\
 &+\sum_vm_{v,X}\lambda_H(\|H_v\|^2-v_H^2)^2\\
 &+\operatorname{Re}\langle\overline\Psi,
 \star_{0,X}\bigl(D_{{\rm sp},X}^{U}
 +\Gamma_{\rm Cl}\otimes D_F^{\boldsymbol Y}(H)\bigr)\Psi\rangle .
 \end{aligned}}
 \tag{CA.12}
\]
Here the invariant gauge metric has one coefficient on each simple or central
Lie-algebra factor.  The Lorentzian action uses the reconstructed temporal
Hodge signs.  Then:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(R\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item \textup{(CA.12)} is exactly gauge invariant and has cutoff-independent
      support radius: its terms are supported on one vertex, one edge, or one
      plaquette;
\item its Euler covectors satisfy the exact finite Ward identity
      \[
       \boxed{
       d_U^*E_U+\mathcal R_H^*E_H
       +\mathcal R_\Psi^*E_\Psi
       +\mathcal R_{\overline\Psi}^*E_{\overline\Psi}=0;}
       \tag{CA.13}
      \]
\item the standard finite ghost extension
      $sc=-c^2$, $sU=c_tU-Uc_s$, $sH=cH$, $s\Psi=c\Psi$,
      $s\bar c=B$, $sB=0$ is nilpotent and annihilates the action;
\item metric and coframe variation of the same action gives the matter stress,
      and common relabeling invariance gives
      \[
       \boxed{
       \mathcal L_q^*\mathsf T
       =2\mathcal L_U^*E_U+2\mathcal L_H^*E_H
        +2\mathcal L_\Psi^*E_\Psi
        +2\mathcal L_{\overline\Psi}^*E_{\overline\Psi};}
       \tag{CA.14}
      \]
\item every local Gibbs row built from the action increment, and the global
      Perron--Doob row on a compact configuration screen, has exactly zero
      accepted/common-action relative-entropy gap and is gauge equivariant;
\item the periodic configuration
      \[
       U_e=I,
       \qquad H_v=v_Hh_0,
       \qquad\Psi_v=\overline\Psi_v=0
       \tag{CA.15}
      \]
      is a stationary internal vacuum.  For $v_H>0$ its gauge stabilizer is
      \[
       \boxed{U(3)\cong
       (SU(3)\times U(1)_{\rm em})/\mathbb Z_3,}
       \tag{CA.16}
      \]
      the gauge-orbit mass form has rank three, and the radial Higgs Hessian is
      $8\lambda_Hv_H^2$;
\item the gauge, Higgs-gradient, potential, and fermion graph norms inherit the
      spacetime Hodge and compact screens.  No second compactness primitive is
      required.
\end{enumerate}
The coefficients in \textup{(CA.12)} remain physical parameters; changing
them does not change the V22 structural representation packet.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Plaquette holonomy transforms by conjugation, the covariant Higgs difference
transforms in the target fibre, and
$D_F^{\boldsymbol Y}(gH)=\rho_L(g)D_F^{\boldsymbol Y}(H)\rho_R(g)^{-1}$ by the
multiplicity-one incidence construction.  These identities prove gauge
invariance and locality.  Differentiation gives \textup{(CA.13)}.  The BRST
calculation is the graded Jacobi identity together with the same covariance.
Differentiating common relabeling invariance gives \textup{(CA.14)}.  The Gibbs
and Perron--Doob statements are the relative-entropy completion theorem applied
to the one common local cost.

At \textup{(CA.15)} every plaquette and covariant Higgs difference is trivial,
the quartic is at its minimum, and the fermion bilinear vanishes.  The Higgs
stabilizer inside $S(U(3)\times U(2))$ is canonically $U(3)$; its codimension is
three.  Expanding the quartic in the radial real coordinate gives the stated
Hessian.  Finally, all internal fibres have fixed finite rank and the finite
Dirac term is a bounded sitewise perturbation, so the reducing-router and Kato
estimates transfer the existing spacetime screens.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Classical SM-II continuum handoff]
\label{thm:SM-active-SM-II-continuum}
Sample a smooth $G_{\rm SM}$ connection, Higgs doublet, and classical spinor
fields on a compact physical slab by link parallel transport and vertex
restriction.  If the numerical coefficients converge, then
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathscr S_{{\rm SM},X}^{L}\longrightarrow
 \mathscr S_{\rm SM}^{L}}
 \tag{CA.17}
\]
with
\[
 \boxed{
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathscr S_{\rm SM}^{L}
 =\int_{\mathcal M}\sqrt{|g|}\,\dd^4x\,
 \bigg[&-\frac14\langle F_{\mu\nu},F^{\mu\nu}\rangle_{\boldsymbol g}
 +(D_\mu H)^\dagger D^\mu H
 -\lambda_H(\|H\|^2-v_H^2)^2\\
 &+\operatorname{Re}\,\overline\Psi
 \bigl(i\not\!D_A+\Gamma_{\rm Cl}\otimes
 D_F^{\boldsymbol Y}(H)\bigr)\Psi\bigg].
 \end{aligned}}
 \tag{CA.18}
\]
The finite Euler, Ward, BRST, current, and stress identities converge to their
classical continuum counterparts.  If the positive sector energies converge
to the energies of a weak limit, the common screens upgrade curvature and
Higgs-gradient convergence to strong local $L^2$ and Higgs convergence to
strong local $L^4$, so every quadratic current, Yukawa insertion, and stress
term passes to the limit.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
For a smooth connection,
$|p|^{-1}\operatorname{Log} U_{\partial p}=F_A(p)+O(h_X)$; covariant Taylor expansion gives
$\ell_e^{-1}(U_eH_s-H_t)=D_AH(e)+O(h_X)$; and the completed centred spacetime
Dirac with gauge links has the symbol of $\not\!D_A$ with an $O(h_X)$
graph-norm error.  The sitewise finite Dirac converges pointwise.  The Hodge
weights are the spacetime Riemann-sum weights, which proves
\textup{(CA.17)--(CA.18)}.  Exact algebraic Ward and BRST identities pass by
coefficient convergence.  The strong statement is uniform convexity of the
positive gauge and Higgs sectors on the common Hodge screens, followed by the
bundle Sobolev estimate.
\end{proof}

\begin{assessment}[SM-II boundary]
The explicitly completed active primitive now carries a regulated classical
Standard Model on the same cofinal spacetime family.  This does not construct
the Grassmann integral, determinant or Pfaffian section, its Berry curvature
or global phase, nor does it determine the numerical couplings, running,
matching, or an interacting renormalized quantum continuum.  Those questions
begin the quantum SM-III programme and do not reopen the finite structural or
classical action carrier.
\end{assessment}


\begin{firewall}[Universal interface versus physical parameter selection]
\label{fire:SMST-coupled-action-scope}
The theorem closes the universal classical loading interface.  It does not fix
numerical gauge couplings, the Higgs radius or quartic coefficient, Yukawa and
Majorana matrices, running, matching, the quantum determinant-line phase, or a
particular nonzero Einstein--matter solution.  These are physical parameters or
individual realization problems on the completed common carrier.
\end{firewall}


\begin{firewall}[A direct sum is not the joint loading]
The SM--spacetime loaded tensor is not
$\boldsymbol{\mathbb T}^{\rm ST}_{\Grand}\oplus
 \boldsymbol{\mathbb T}^{\rm SM}_{\Grand}$.  A direct sum omits incidence,
marked finite-Dirac panels, clock--matter comparisons, and alternating mixed
words.  Those data are precisely where covariant matter transport, common
source tests, and the commutant duality are defined.
\end{firewall}
\subsection{The internal SM--spacetime commutant duality}
\label{sec:SMST-duality}
% =============================================================================

The exact duality is not an equality between the spacetime Clifford algebra and
the Standard-Model gauge algebra.  A reducible typed gauge representation
cannot generally be the full commutant of the external matrix factor.  The
correct dual pair is the joint typed action algebra and the residual
multiplicity algebra.  Equivalently, on one common multiplicity fibre, the
surviving typed multiplicity algebra is the commutant of the Yukawa/incidence
polar metric--holonomy algebra.

\begin{theorem}[Factor-commutant obstruction]
\label{thm:SMST-factor-obstruction}
Let a unital copy of $M_n(\C)$ act on a finite-dimensional Hilbert space
$\mathcal H$.  Then
\[
 \mathcal H\cong\C^n\otimes\mathcal K,
 \qquad
 M_n(\C)=M_n(\C)\otimes I_{\mathcal K},
 \qquad
 M_n(\C)'=I_n\otimes\mathcal B(\mathcal K).
\]
Consequently a reducible internal algebra with nontrivial centre, or with a
nontrivial multiplicity commutant, cannot equal the full commutant of the
external factor.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Every finite-dimensional unital representation of the simple algebra
$M_n(\C)$ is a direct sum of copies of its defining representation, giving
$\mathcal H\cong\C^n\otimes\mathcal K$.  An operator commutes with every matrix
unit on the first factor exactly when it is the identity there and arbitrary
on $\mathcal K$.  The full commutant is therefore a simple matrix algebra.  A
reducible internal algebra has either more than one central block or a
non-scalar multiplicity commutant, and hence is a proper subalgebra of that
simple commutant.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[External--internal--multiplicity decomposition]
\label{thm:SMST-trinity}
Let $\mathcal A_{\rm ext}\cong M_n(\C)$ and let
$\mathcal A_{\rm int}$ be a commuting finite-dimensional unital $C^*$-algebra
on $\mathcal H$.  Then there are spaces $V_\lambda,M_\lambda$ such that
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal H\cong
 \bigoplus_{\lambda\in\Lambda}
 \C^n\otimes V_\lambda\otimes M_\lambda,}
\]
\[
 \mathcal A_{\rm int}
 =\bigoplus_\lambda
 I_n\otimes\mathcal B(V_\lambda)\otimes I_{M_\lambda}.
\]
For
$\mathcal C=C^*(\mathcal A_{\rm ext},\mathcal A_{\rm int})$ one has
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal C=
 \bigoplus_\lambda
 \mathcal B(\C^n\otimes V_\lambda)\otimes I_{M_\lambda},}
\]
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal C'=
 \bigoplus_\lambda
 I_{\C^n\otimes V_\lambda}\otimes\mathcal B(M_\lambda),
 \qquad
 \mathcal C''=\mathcal C.}
\]
Thus the residual factors $M_\lambda$, rather than the raw internal gauge
algebra, carry generation and flavour multiplicity.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Apply \Cref{thm:SMST-factor-obstruction} to write
$\mathcal H=\C^n\otimes\mathcal K$ and
$\mathcal A_{\rm int}=I_n\otimes\widetilde{\mathcal A}_{\rm int}$.  The finite
representation theorem gives
\[
 \mathcal K\cong\bigoplus_\lambda V_\lambda\otimes M_\lambda,
 \qquad
 \widetilde{\mathcal A}_{\rm int}
 =\bigoplus_\lambda\mathcal B(V_\lambda)\otimes I_{M_\lambda}.
\]
The minimal central projections of the internal algebra belong to the joint
algebra.  On each central block the two commuting full matrix factors generate
$\mathcal B(\C^n\otimes V_\lambda)$.  An operator commuting with that full
matrix algebra is the identity on the first two factors and arbitrary on
$M_\lambda$; central projections prevent off-diagonal maps between different
$\lambda$ blocks.  This gives the commutant formula.  Applying the same
calculation to the commutant gives the bicommutant identity.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Typed multiplicity graph and residual algebra]
\label{def:typed-multiplicity-graph}
For a joint packet as in \Cref{def:SMST-packet}, let
$\Gamma_X=(\Lambda_X,E_X)$ be the graph of retained incidence histories.  The
\emph{typed multiplicity algebra} is the algebra of families
\[
 R=(R_\lambda)_{\lambda\in\Lambda_X},
 \qquad R_\lambda\in\mathcal B(M_{\lambda,X}),
\]
satisfying, for every $e:\lambda\to\mu$,
\[
 \boxed{
 R_\mu F_e=F_eR_\lambda,
 \qquad
 R_\lambda F_e^*=F_e^*R_\mu.}
\]
It is represented globally by
$\bigoplus_\lambda I_{\C^4\otimes V_\lambda}\otimes R_\lambda$ and is denoted
$\mathcal M_{{\rm type},X}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Multiplicity-one incidence factorization]
\label{lem:SMST-multiplicity-factorization}
Suppose the external--internal symmetry acts trivially on
$M_\lambda,M_\mu$ and the typed carrier-intertwiner space for an edge
$e:\lambda\to\mu$ is one dimensional, spanned by a nonzero $D_e$.  Then every
equivariant loaded incidence map has a unique factorization
\[
 \boxed{Y_e=D_e\otimes F_e.}
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Triviality on the multiplicity factors gives
\[
 \Hom_{\rm typed}
 ((\C^4\otimes V_\lambda)\otimes M_\lambda,
  (\C^4\otimes V_\mu)\otimes M_\mu)
 \cong
 \Hom_{\rm typed}(\C^4\otimes V_\lambda,
                  \C^4\otimes V_\mu)
 \otimes\Hom(M_\lambda,M_\mu).
\]
The first factor is the line $\C D_e$, proving existence and uniqueness of
$F_e$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Exact edge-commutant reconstruction]
\label{thm:SMST-edge-commutant}
For the joint action algebra
$\mathcal A_{\rm act}=C^*(\mathcal A_{\rm ext},\mathcal A_{\rm int},
Y_e,Y_e^*:e\in E)$,
\[
 \boxed{\mathcal A_{\rm act}'=\mathcal M_{\rm type}.}
\]
In particular, if the incidence graph is connected and every $F_e$ is
invertible, all multiplicity spaces have one common dimension $g$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
By \Cref{thm:SMST-trinity}, an operator commuting with the external and
internal algebras has the form
$X=\bigoplus_\lambda I_{\C^4\otimes V_\lambda}\otimes R_\lambda$.
For $Y_e=D_e\otimes F_e$,
\[
 XY_e-Y_eX
 =D_e\otimes(R_\mu F_e-F_eR_\lambda),
\]
and the commutator with $Y_e^*$ is
\[
 D_e^*\otimes(R_\lambda F_e^*-F_e^*R_\mu).
\]
Because $D_e\ne0$, each tensor product vanishes exactly when its multiplicity
factor vanishes.  Thus the commutant equations are precisely those in
\Cref{def:typed-multiplicity-graph}.  If $F_e$ is invertible, its two endpoint
spaces have equal dimension; connectedness propagates this equality through
the graph.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Singular polar-edge equivalence]
\label{lem:SMST-polar-edge}
Let $F:E\to H$ have polar decomposition $F=UP$, where
$P=(F^*F)^{1/2}$, $p=U^*U=\supp P$, and
$q=UU^*=\supp(FF^*)$.  For $R_E\in\mathcal B(E)$ and
$R_H\in\mathcal B(H)$, the equations
\[
 R_HF=FR_E,
 \qquad
 R_EF^*=F^*R_H
\]
are equivalent to
\[
 \boxed{
 [R_E,P^2]=0,
 \qquad
 R_HU=UR_E,
 \qquad
 R_EU^*=U^*R_H.}
\]
On either branch,
\[
 [R_E,p]=0,
 \qquad [R_H,q]=0,
 \qquad [R_H,UP^2U^*]=0.
\]
No invertibility or equality of the source and target dimensions is required.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
The two incidence equations imply
\[
 F^*R_HF=F^*FR_E=R_EF^*F,
\]
so $[R_E,P^2]=0$; the target-side calculation gives
$[R_H,FF^*]=0$.  Functional calculus gives commutation with $p$ and $q$.
Writing the first incidence equation as
$R_HUP=UR_EP$ and multiplying by $P^\dagger$ gives
$R_HU=UR_E$ on the supported source; both sides vanish on its orthogonal
complement.  The adjoint equation gives the reverse transport identity.
Conversely, functional calculus gives $[R_E,P]=0$, and the three displayed
conditions directly recover the two incidence equations.  Conjugating the
metric commutator by $U$ gives the final target identity.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Support-polar multiplicity action algebra]
\label{def:SMST-support-polar-algebra}
On the total multiplicity carrier
\[
 \mathscr M_X=\bigoplus_{\lambda\in\Lambda_X}M_{\lambda,X},
\]
let $Z_\lambda$ be the vertex projections.  For each incidence map
$F_e:M_{s(e),X}\to M_{t(e),X}$ write
$F_e=U_e(F_e^*F_e)^{1/2}$ and define
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal O_{F,X}^{\rm sup}
 :=C^*(Z_\lambda,F_e^*F_e,U_e,U_e^*: \lambda,e)
 \subseteq\mathcal B(\mathscr M_X).}
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Exact support-polar commutant]
\label{thm:SMST-support-polar-commutant}
For arbitrary rectangular, singular, rank-deficient, or zero incidence maps,
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal M_{{\rm type},X}
 =\bigl(\mathcal O_{F,X}^{\rm sup}\bigr)',
 \qquad
 \mathcal O_{F,X}^{\rm sup}
 =\mathcal M_{{\rm type},X}'.}
\]
Moreover,
\[
 \boxed{
 C^*(Z_\lambda,F_e,F_e^*: \lambda,e)
 =\mathcal O_{F,X}^{\rm sup}.}
\]
Thus support projections, positive support metrics, and polar partial
isometries add no finite loading; they are exact functional-calculus outputs of
the original incidence maps.  A zero singular value remains an explicit
support boundary rather than being completed by an inverse residue map.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Commutation with the vertex projections makes an operator block diagonal.
Commutation with $F_e^*F_e$, $U_e$, and $U_e^*$ is exactly the three-condition
form of \Cref{lem:SMST-polar-edge}, hence exactly the two incidence
intertwining equations defining $\mathcal M_{{\rm type},X}$.  The reverse
commutant equality is finite bicommutant closure.

For the algebra identity, $F_e^*F_e$ belongs to the incidence algebra.  On its
finite spectrum, interpolate the function $g(0)=0$ and
$g(t)=t^{-1/2}$ for $t>0$ by a polynomial.  Then
$U_e=F_eg(F_e^*F_e)$ belongs to the incidence algebra.  Conversely
$F_e=U_e(F_e^*F_e)^{1/2}$, proving equality.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Residue support algebra and multiplicity quiver]
\label{def:SMST-multiplicity-quiver}
Put
\[
 p_e=\supp(F_e^*F_e),
 \qquad q_e=\supp(F_eF_e^*),
 \qquad
 \mathcal S_{F,X}=C^*(Z_\lambda,p_e,q_e: \lambda,e).
\]
Its canonical central multiplicity decomposition is
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathscr M_X\cong\bigoplus_{a\in\mathfrak A_X}V_{a,X}\otimes N_{a,X},}
\]
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal S_{F,X}
 =\bigoplus_a\mathcal B(V_{a,X})\otimes I_{N_{a,X}},
 \qquad
 \mathcal S_{F,X}'
 =\bigoplus_a I_{V_{a,X}}\otimes\mathcal B(N_{a,X}).}
\]
Let $\bm T_X$ be any finite $*$-closed family of further reconstructed
support metrics, polar arrows, cycle products, or action generators.  For a
block
$T_{ba}:V_a\otimes N_a\to V_b\otimes N_b$, define its basis-free multiplicity
slice space by
\[
 \mathfrak B_{ba}(T)
 :=\{(\varphi\otimes\id)(T_{ba}):
       \varphi\in\mathcal B(V_a,V_b)^*\}
 \subseteq\mathcal B(N_a,N_b).
\]
The multiplicity quiver $\mathfrak Q_{F,X}(\bm T_X)$ has vertex spaces $N_a$
and arrow spaces
$\mathfrak B_{ba}=\Span_{T\in\bm T_X}\mathfrak B_{ba}(T)$.  Its endomorphism
algebra is
\[
 \boxed{
 \End\mathfrak Q_{F,X}
 =\{(X_a)_a:X_bB=BX_a
   \text{ for every }B\in\mathfrak B_{ba}\}.}
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Noncommuting-support multiplicity-quiver theorem]
\label{thm:SMST-quiver-commutant}
For the packet of \Cref{def:SMST-multiplicity-quiver},
\[
 \boxed{
 C^*(\mathcal S_{F,X},\bm T_X)'
 \cong\End\mathfrak Q_{F,X}.}
\]
If
$(T_j)_{ba}=\sum_\alpha E_\alpha^{ba}\otimes B_{j,\alpha}^{ba}$ in a
Hilbert--Schmidt orthonormal basis of $\mathcal B(V_a,V_b)$, then the
restriction of the ambient commutator form to $\mathcal S_{F,X}'$ is
\[
 \boxed{
 q_{\bm T_X}[(X_a)]
 =\frac1{\dim\mathscr M_X}
   \sum_{j,b,a,\alpha}
   \|B_{j,\alpha}^{ba}X_a-X_bB_{j,\alpha}^{ba}\|_{\HS}^2.}
\]
Its kernel is exactly $\End\mathfrak Q_{F,X}$.  Hence the first positive
quiver eigenvalue is a finite coercive certificate for the absence of
additional flavour/generation endomorphisms.  The construction is unique up
to permutation of central blocks and vertexwise unitary gauge.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
An operator commuting with $\mathcal S_{F,X}$ has the form
$\bigoplus_aI_{V_a}\otimes X_a$.  Expanding one block of each $T_j$ gives
\[
 (I\otimes X_b)(T_j)_{ba}-(T_j)_{ba}(I\otimes X_a)
 =\sum_\alpha E_\alpha^{ba}\otimes
   (X_bB_{j,\alpha}^{ba}-B_{j,\alpha}^{ba}X_a).
\]
Linear independence proves the quiver intertwining equations.  Orthogonality
of the $E_\alpha^{ba}$ gives the displayed positive form and its kernel.
Finite-dimensional representation uniqueness gives the stated gauge
independence.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Polar metric--holonomy commutant theorem]
\label{thm:SMST-polar-holonomy}
Assume the typed multiplicity graph is connected, every multiplicity space has
common dimension $g$, and each edge transport is invertible.  Write
\[
 F_e=U_eP_e,
 \qquad U_e\in U(g),
 \qquad P_e\succ0.
\]
Choose a root $o$ and a spanning tree.  Let
$Q_\lambda:M_o\to M_\lambda$ be the ordered product of the unitary factors
along the tree path, using $U_e^*$ for a reversed edge.  For
$e:\lambda\to\mu$ define on the root fibre
\[
 K_e:=Q_\lambda^*P_e^2Q_\lambda,
 \qquad
 W_e:=Q_\mu^*U_eQ_\lambda,
\]
and put
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal O_{F,X}:=C^*(K_e,W_e:e\in E_X)\subseteq M_g(\C).}
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal M_{{\rm type},X}\cong\mathcal O_{F,X}',}
\]
where $R\in\mathcal O_{F,X}'$ corresponds to the parallel family
\[
 \boxed{R_\lambda=Q_\lambda RQ_\lambda^*.}
\]
Consequently
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal O_{F,X}'=\mathcal M_{{\rm type},X}^{(o)},
 \qquad
 (\mathcal M_{{\rm type},X}^{(o)})'=\mathcal O_{F,X},}
\]
on the root multiplicity fibre.  Thus the typed multiplicity algebra and the
Yukawa/incidence polar metric--holonomy algebra reconstruct one another by a
finite commutant calculation.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
By \Cref{thm:SMST-edge-commutant,lem:SMST-polar-edge}, a residual family
satisfies on every edge
\[
 [R_\lambda,P_e^2]=0,
 \qquad R_\mu=U_eR_\lambda U_e^*.
\]
Along the chosen spanning tree, the second relation forces
$R_\lambda=Q_\lambda RQ_\lambda^*$ from the root value $R=R_o$.  The metric
condition becomes
\[
 [R,Q_\lambda^*P_e^2Q_\lambda]=[R,K_e]=0.
\]
For a non-tree edge, consistency between the tree transport and the direct
unitary edge transport is equivalent to
\[
 [R,Q_\mu^*U_eQ_\lambda]=[R,W_e]=0.
\]
Hence a residual family is determined exactly by one root operator commuting
with every generator of $\mathcal O_{F,X}$.  Conversely any such root operator
defines a family satisfying all edge and adjoint-edge equations.  These maps
are inverse unital $*$-homomorphisms.  Finally, every finite-dimensional unital
$C^*$-algebra equals its bicommutant, so
$(\mathcal O_{F,X}')'=\mathcal O_{F,X}$.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Flat and irreducible limits]
\label{cor:SMST-polar-extremes}
Under \Cref{thm:SMST-polar-holonomy}:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.8em]
\item $\mathcal M_{{\rm type},X}^{(o)}=M_g(\C)$ exactly when every generator
      $K_e,W_e$ is scalar;
\item $\mathcal M_{{\rm type},X}^{(o)}=\C I$ exactly when
      $\mathcal O_{F,X}=M_g(\C)$;
\item if all $F_e$ are unitary, then $K_e=I$ and the obstruction reduces to
      relative-cycle unitary holonomy;
\item even on a tree, a non-scalar positive polar metric can reduce the
      residual multiplicity algebra.
\end{enumerate}
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The commutant of a set is all of $M_g(\C)$ exactly when the set is contained in
the centre.  A finite unital algebra has scalar commutant exactly when it is
$M_g(\C)$.  If $F_e$ is unitary, $P_e=I$.  The final statement follows because
$K_e$ remains among the generators even when there are no cycle holonomies.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[SM--spacetime loaded Howe duality]
\label{thm:SMST-main-duality}
For every source-complete joint packet, without an invertibility assumption on
the residue maps,
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal A_{{\rm act},X}'=\mathcal M_{{\rm type},X},
 \qquad
 \mathcal M_{{\rm type},X}'=\mathcal A_{{\rm act},X}.}
\]
On the total multiplicity carrier,
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal M_{{\rm type},X}
 =\bigl(\mathcal O_{F,X}^{\rm sup}\bigr)',
 \qquad
 \mathcal O_{F,X}^{\rm sup}
 =\mathcal M_{{\rm type},X}'.}
\]
If the residue support projections are noncommuting, their canonical central
decomposition gives instead the equivalent finite realization
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal M_{{\rm type},X}
 \cong\End\mathfrak Q_{F,X}.}
\]
On the connected invertible branch of
\Cref{thm:SMST-polar-holonomy}, choosing one root multiplicity fibre gives
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal M_{{\rm type},X}^{(o)}=\mathcal O_{F,X}',
 \qquad
 \mathcal O_{F,X}=(\mathcal M_{{\rm type},X}^{(o)})'.}
\]
Hence the strongest exact finite duality is not
$\mathcal A_{\rm spacetime}=\mathcal A_{\rm gauge}$, but the mutual commutant
pair
\[
 \boxed{
 \text{joint typed spacetime--gauge--incidence action}
 \quad\longleftrightarrow\quad
 \text{residual typed gauge--matter multiplicity}.}
\]
The support-polar algebra, multiplicity quiver, and invertible root-fibre
metric--holonomy algebra are three canonical presentations of this same dual
pair on their respective branches.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The first equality is \Cref{thm:SMST-edge-commutant}; finite bicommutant closure
gives the reverse equality.  The support-polar presentation is
\Cref{thm:SMST-support-polar-commutant}, and the noncommuting-support
presentation is \Cref{thm:SMST-quiver-commutant}.  The rooted invertible
presentation is \Cref{thm:SMST-polar-holonomy}.  Every generator and support
projection is reconstructed at saturated Grand-Tensor depth by
\Cref{thm:SMST-loaded-emergence,thm:SMST-support-polar-commutant}; no target
basis or inverse residue slot is inserted.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Commutant Laplacian]
\label{def:SMST-commutant-Laplacian}
Let $c_1,\ldots,c_s$ span a unital $*$-algebra
$\mathcal C\subseteq\mathcal B(\mathcal H)$.  On Hilbert--Schmidt operator
space define
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathscr L_{\mathcal C}
 :=\sum_{j=1}^s\operatorname{ad}_{c_j}^*
                    \operatorname{ad}_{c_j},
 \qquad
 \operatorname{ad}_{c}(X)=[c,X].}
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Terminating and stable commutant audit]
\label{thm:SMST-commutant-audit}
The commutant Laplacian is positive and
\[
 \boxed{\Ker\mathscr L_{\mathcal C}=\mathcal C'.}
\]
Let $P_{\mathcal C'}$ be Hilbert--Schmidt projection onto the commutant and let
$\lambda_{\mathcal C}>0$ be the least positive eigenvalue of
$\mathscr L_{\mathcal C}$.  Then
\[
 \boxed{
 \norm{X-P_{\mathcal C'}X}_{\HS}^2
 \le\lambda_{\mathcal C}^{-1}
 \sum_{j=1}^s\norm{[c_j,X]}_{\HS}^2.}
\]
Thus the zero eigenspace reconstructs the exact multiplicity algebra and the
first positive eigenvalue is a quantitative rigidity margin.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
For the Hilbert--Schmidt inner product,
$\operatorname{ad}_{c}^*=\operatorname{ad}_{c^*}$.  Therefore
\[
 \ip{X}{\mathscr L_{\mathcal C}X}_{\HS}
 =\sum_j\norm{[c_j,X]}_{\HS}^2\ge0.
\]
The quadratic form vanishes exactly when $X$ commutes with every generator and
hence with $\mathcal C$.  On $(\mathcal C')^\perp$, the positive operator is
bounded below by its least positive eigenvalue.  Apply that bound to
$X-P_{\mathcal C'}X$; the commutant component contributes zero to every
commutator.
\end{proof}


\begin{definition}[Relative Howe Gram]
\label{def:SMST-relative-Howe-Gram}
Let $\mathcal M\subseteq\mathcal B(\mathcal H)$ be a proposed protected
multiplicity algebra satisfying $\mathcal M\subseteq C^*(\bm c)'$, and let
$E_1,\ldots,E_r$ be a Hilbert--Schmidt orthonormal basis of
$\mathcal M^\perp$.  Define
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathbb G_{\rm Howe}(\bm c\mid\mathcal M)_{ab}
 :=\sum_j\langle[c_j,E_a],[c_j,E_b]\rangle_{\HS}.}
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Finite positive certificate for the exact multiplicity algebra]
\label{thm:SMST-relative-Howe-certificate}
Under \Cref{def:SMST-relative-Howe-Gram},
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathbb G_{\rm Howe}(\bm c\mid\mathcal M)\succ0
 \iff C^*(\bm c)'=\mathcal M.}
\]
On this branch its least eigenvalue is the first positive eigenvalue of the
commutant Laplacian.  Thus exactness of the desired flavour/generation algebra
and its finite rigidity margin are one positive Gram test reconstructed from
commutator words.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The displayed Gram is the matrix of
$\mathscr L_{C^*(\bm c)}$ restricted to $\mathcal M^\perp$.  Since
$\mathcal M$ is already contained in the kernel, the restriction is positive
definite exactly when no further kernel vector exists.  Its least eigenvalue
is then the first positive commutant-Laplacian eigenvalue.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Finite-anchor locking of the Howe commutant]
\label{thm:SMST-finite-anchor-Howe}
After transporting a cutoff family to one common finite screened carrier, let
$\bm c_X=(c_{1,X},\ldots,c_{s,X})$ and let a fixed protected algebra
$\mathcal M$ commute with every tuple.  Put
\[
 C_X=\left(\sum_j\|c_{j,X}\|_{\op}^2\right)^{1/2},
 \qquad
 \varepsilon_{X,Y}
 =\left(\sum_j\|c_{j,X}-c_{j,Y}\|_{\op}^2\right)^{1/2}.
\]
Suppose that at one cutoff $X_0$,
\[
 \mathbb G_{\rm Howe}(\bm c_{X_0}\mid\mathcal M)
 \succeq\gamma_0I,
 \qquad \gamma_0>0,
\]
and that, for every later $X$,
\[
 \boxed{
 4(C_X+C_{X_0})\varepsilon_{X,X_0}<\gamma_0.}
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{
 C^*(\bm c_X)'=\mathcal M,
 \qquad
 \lambda_{\min}^+(\mathscr L_{C^*(\bm c_X)})
 \ge\gamma_0-4(C_X+C_{X_0})\varepsilon_{X,X_0}.}
\]
In particular, a uniform bound $C_X\le C_*$ and the summable tail condition
\[
 \sum_{n\ge X_0}\varepsilon_{n+1,n}<\frac{\gamma_0}{8C_*}
\]
lock the exact commutant and a common positive gap at every later cutoff.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
For the commutator derivations,
\[
 \|\partial_{\bm c_X}-\partial_{\bm c_Y}\|_{2\to2}
 \le2\varepsilon_{X,Y},
 \qquad
 \|\partial_{\bm c_X}\|_{2\to2}\le2C_X.
\]
Using $A^*A-B^*B=A^*(A-B)+(A^*-B^*)B$ gives
\[
 \|\mathscr L_X-\mathscr L_Y\|
 \le4(C_X+C_Y)\varepsilon_{X,Y}.
\]
On $\mathcal M^\perp$, the anchor Laplacian is at least $\gamma_0I$.
The perturbation inequality gives the displayed later lower bound.  A later
commutant vector has zero energy and must therefore lie in $\mathcal M$; the
reverse inclusion is protected.  The summable statement follows by
telescoping the tuple increments.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Coercive continuum Howe duality]
\label{thm:SMST-continuum-Howe}
Let $\mathscr L_X$ be the commutant Laplacians of a cutoff family of screened
support-polar or multiplicity-quiver generators.  Assume:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(H\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item their closed forms converge in the Grand-Tensor Mosco sense;
\item the common graph-screen profile is compact, so the embedded resolvents
      converge in norm and isolated eigenvalues converge with multiplicity;
\item protected multiplicity projections $P_{\mathcal M_X}$ have one fixed
      finite rank, lie in $\Ker\mathscr L_X$, and converge in norm to
      $P_{\mathcal M_\infty}$;
\item the limiting action has no additional commutant:
      $\Ker\mathscr L_\infty=\mathcal M_\infty$.
\end{enumerate}
Then, for every sufficiently large cutoff,
\[
 \boxed{
 \Ker\mathscr L_X=\mathcal M_X,
 \qquad
 C^*(\bm c_X)'=\mathcal M_X,}
\]
the commutant projections converge in norm, and
\[
 \boxed{
 \lambda_{\min}^+(\mathscr L_X)
 \longrightarrow\lambda_{\min}^+(\mathscr L_\infty)>0.}
\]
Consequently there is $\gamma_*>0$ such that
\[
 \boxed{
 \sum_j\|[c_{j,X},A]\|_{\HS}^2
 \ge\gamma_*\|(I-P_{\mathcal M_X})A\|_{\HS}^2}
\]
for every sufficiently large $X$.  No bounded sequence of unprotected flavour
transformations can escape every finite screen while its commutators tend to
zero.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The compact-screen hypothesis and \Cref{thm:compact-screen-alternative} give
norm-resolvent convergence and convergence of the ordered low eigenvalues with
multiplicity.  The limiting kernel has the protected finite rank, and the next
eigenvalue is strictly positive.  An additional finite-cutoff zero eigenvalue
along a cofinal subsequence would force the next limiting eigenvalue to be
zero, a contradiction.  Hence the finite kernel eventually equals the
protected kernel, and convergence of the first positive eigenvalue gives the
uniform estimate.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Canonical full-cell orbit and Hodge-to-commutator transfer]
\label{thm:SMST-orbit-Hodge-transfer}
Let $\bm G=(G_1,\ldots,G_m)$ be the reconstructed common full-cell tuple and
let $\mathfrak T$ be the typed Hilbert--Schmidt perturbation space.  The
canonical conjugation-orbit source is
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal J_{\bm G}(A)=([G_1,A],\ldots,[G_m,A]),
 \qquad
 \Ker\mathcal J_{\bm G}=C^*(\bm G)'\cap\mathfrak T.}
\]
If an action tuple is an equivariant finite export
$\bm c=\Phi(\bm G)$, then differentiation of
$\Phi(U\bm GU^*)=U\Phi(\bm G)U^*$ gives a unique source-minimal orbit
derivative satisfying
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal J_{\bm c}
 =D_{\rm orb}\Phi_{\bm G}\,\mathcal J_{\bm G}.}
\]
In particular, if $\bm c\subseteq C^*(\bm G)$,
$\mathcal M\subseteq C^*(\bm G)'$, and
$C^*(\bm c)'=\mathcal M$, then
\[
 \boxed{C^*(\bm G)'=\mathcal M.}
\]

On the unprotected operator space
$\mathfrak K=(I-P_\mathcal M)\mathfrak T$, put
$J=\mathcal J_{\bm G}|_{\mathfrak K}$.  Let $D^{\rm sh}$ be the shorted
renewal Hodge/current differential and let
$\partial_{\bm c}$ be the action commutator derivation.  Define
\[
 \mathbb H=J^*(D^{\rm sh})^*D^{\rm sh}J,
 \qquad
 \mathbb C=\partial_{\bm c}^*\partial_{\bm c},
 \qquad
 \mathbb R=R^2.
\]
If, for constants $C_0>0$, $\alpha,\Lambda,\varepsilon\ge0$,
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathbb R\preceq C_0\mathbb H+\alpha I,
 \qquad
 \mathbb H\preceq\Lambda\mathbb C+\varepsilon^2\mathbb R,
 \qquad
 C_0\varepsilon^2<1,}
\]
then
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathbb R
 \preceq
 \frac{C_0\Lambda}{1-C_0\varepsilon^2}\mathbb C
 +\frac{\alpha}{1-C_0\varepsilon^2}I.}
\]
When $R=(I+L)^{s/2}$ for the compact-resolvent regularity anchor of the renewal
Hodge packet, this is the two-sided Hodge--Morrey estimate needed for the
compact commutator screens in \Cref{thm:SMST-continuum-Howe}.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The orbit-kernel identity is the definition of simultaneous commutation.
Differentiating the equivariance identity along $U(t)=e^{-tA}$ gives the chain
rule.  Since $\bm c\subseteq C^*(\bm G)$,
$C^*(\bm G)'\subseteq C^*(\bm c)'=\mathcal M$, while the protected inclusion
gives the reverse containment.

For the form estimate, substitute
$\mathbb H\preceq\Lambda\mathbb C+\varepsilon^2\mathbb R$ into
$\mathbb R\preceq C_0\mathbb H+\alpha I$, move
$C_0\varepsilon^2\mathbb R$ to the left, and divide by the positive scalar
$1-C_0\varepsilon^2$.  The final screen statement is the spectral-tail estimate
of the compact Hodge anchor applied to this domination and to its adjoint.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Reducing coherent source closure]
\label{thm:SMST-reducing-coherent-closure}
Let $V:E\to H$ be an isometry whose range reduces a bounded coherent generator
$A$, and put $a=V^*AV$.  For $t>0$, define
\[
 B_C=AV,
 \qquad
 B_H=\frac{e^{tA}-e^{-tA}}{2t}V,
 \qquad
 \psi_t(z)=\sum_{k\ge0}\frac{t^{2k}z^{2k}}{(2k+1)!}.
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{
 B_H=B_CW_t,
 \qquad W_t=\psi_t(a),}
\]
so the source Schur mismatch of $B_H$ relative to $B_C$ vanishes exactly.  If
$a$ is normal and $\|a\|\le M$, then, with $c=B_C^*B_C$,
\[
 \boxed{
 (B_H-B_C)^*(B_H-B_C)
 =(W_t-I)^*c(W_t-I)
 \preceq\frac{t^4M^4e^{2tM}}{36}\,c.}
\]
For physical step $\tau=2t$,
\[
 \boxed{\tau^{-1}\log W_t\longrightarrow0.}
\]
Thus a saturated reducing full-cell carrier together with the deterministic
same-history writer of \Cref{thm:SMST-reversal-writer} closes the Hodge/action
source comparison at every cutoff and leaves no additional continuum relative
connection.

More generally, if $R_A=AV-Va$ and
$E_{\rm pol}=B_H-(e^{tA}-e^{-tA})(2t)^{-1}V$, then for a positive regularity
form $r$,
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathbb S_{H\mid C}
 \preceq
 \left[
 \left(e^{tM}+\frac{\sinh(tM)}{tM}\right)
 \|R_Ar^{-1/2}\|
 +\|E_{\rm pol}r^{-1/2}\|
 \right]^2r.}
\]
Hence source-core and same-history defects of order $o(\tau)$ give the dense
Schur scale $o(\tau^2)r$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Reduction gives $A^nV=Va^n$ and hence
$e^{sA}V=Ve^{sa}$ by entire functional calculus.  Since
$(e^{ta}-e^{-ta})/(2t)=a\psi_t(a)$,
\[
 B_H=Va\psi_t(a)=AV\psi_t(a)=B_CW_t.
\]
The Schur residual is the squared orthogonal distance from $B_H$ to
$\Ran B_C$, so it vanishes.  Normality makes $c=a^*a$ commute with $W_t$.
The series estimate
\[
 \|W_t-I\|
 \le\frac{t^2M^2e^{tM}}6
\]
gives the graph bound.  The principal logarithm satisfies
$\|\log W_t\|=O(t^2)$, proving the physical-time limit.

For the approximate statement, Duhamel's formula gives
\[
 \|e^{sA}V-Ve^{sa}\|\le |s|e^{|s|M}\|R_A\|.
\]
Taking the centred difference and using
$\|\psi_t(a)\|\le\sinh(tM)/(tM)$ yields the displayed source error.  Evaluating
the Schur variational formula at $W_t$ gives the positive form bound.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Coercive SM--spacetime multiplicity closure]
\label{thm:SMST-coercive-multiplicity-closure}
Consider one cofinal joint SM--spacetime regulator family.  Assume:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(C\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item the finite source-native matter, CAR/incidence, endpoint-generation, and
      finite-Dirac packet of \Cref{thm:SM-GT};
\item the exact support-polar or multiplicity-quiver realization of
      $\mathcal M_{{\rm type},X}$ and either the finite-anchor hypothesis of
      \Cref{thm:SMST-finite-anchor-Howe} or the Mosco/compact-screen hypotheses
      of \Cref{thm:SMST-continuum-Howe};
\item the binary record or action-grading certificate of
      \Cref{thm:SMST-record-grading-rigidity,thm:SMST-grading-commutant};
\item saturated full-cell reduction and the deterministic same-history writer,
      or their $o(\tau_X)$ quantitative residual versions;
\item the Hodge-to-commutator transfer packet of
      \Cref{thm:SMST-orbit-Hodge-transfer} with uniform constants;
\item a regulator-uniform lower bound on the positive rank-three endpoint
      generation-source Gram.
\end{enumerate}
Then, for all sufficiently late cutoffs,
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal A_{{\rm act},X}'=\mathcal M_{{\rm type},X},
 \qquad
 \inf_X\lambda_{\min}^+(\mathscr L_{\mathcal A_{{\rm act},X}})>0,}
\]
the commutant projections and multiplicity-quiver algebra are regulator
stable, the compact commutator screens are uniformly exhausted, and the
rank-three generation source cannot collapse.  On the exact deterministic
writer and reducing coherent branch,
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathbb S_{H\mid C,X}=0,
 \qquad
 \tau_X^{-1}\log W_{0,X}\to0.}
\]
Thus no additional multiplicity direction or relative connection survives the
continuum handoff.  The theorem does not determine the numerical residue
matrices, flavour breaking, scalar/gauge coefficients, running, matching, or
quantum determinant/Pfaffian phase.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The finite commutant is the support-polar or quiver commutant by
\Cref{thm:SMST-main-duality}.  Its exactness and uniform gap follow from
\Cref{thm:SMST-finite-anchor-Howe} or
\Cref{thm:SMST-continuum-Howe}.  The record theorems identify the grading and
same-history sources without an inserted router; full-cell flatness supplies
exact reduction as in \Cref{thm:SMST-generator-projections}.  The Hodge
transfer theorem gives the compact commutator screen, and
\Cref{thm:SMST-reducing-coherent-closure} gives the exact Schur and connection
statements.  The generation-source lower bound preserves its rank and positive
variance under the cutoff embeddings.  The final limitations are outside the
hypotheses and remain independent physical data.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Canonical one-generation incidence audit]
\label{thm:SMST-one-generation-audit}
On the five typed modules
\[
 \mathcal F_{15}=Q\oplus u\oplus d\oplus L\oplus e
\]
of \Cref{thm:SM-generation}, the gauge-generated algebra and commutant are
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal A_{\rm gauge}
 =M_6(\C)\oplus M_3(\C)\oplus M_3(\C)
  \oplus M_2(\C)\oplus\C,
 \qquad
 \mathcal A_{\rm gauge}'\cong\C^5.}
\]
If the three incidence histories
$Q\leftrightarrow u$, $Q\leftrightarrow d$, and
$L\leftrightarrow e$ are nonzero after contraction with their loaded Higgs
source, then
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal A_{\rm gauge+inc}
 =M_{12}(\C)\oplus M_3(\C),
 \qquad
 \mathcal A_{\rm gauge+inc}'\cong\C^2.}
\]
The two residual central directions are the quark and lepton components.  If a
neutral singlet and a nonzero $L$--neutral incidence are added, the second
matrix block becomes $M_4(\C)$ while the residual remains $\C^2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The five gauge modules are irreducible and pairwise inequivalent, so Schur's
lemma and the finite bicommutant theorem give the first algebra and its
five-dimensional scalar-block commutant.  A nonzero block between two full
matrix summands generates every cross map between them: if
$Y:V_s\to V_r$ is nonzero, choose $u,v$ with
$\langle u,Yv\rangle\ne0$; multiplying by endpoint rank-one matrices produces
any rank-one map $V_s\to V_r$.  Products and adjoints therefore generate the
full matrix algebra on each connected component of the incidence graph.  The
three edges have components
$\{Q,u,d\}$ and $\{L,e\}$, of dimensions $12$ and $3$, giving the displayed
algebra and a scalar on each component.  Adding one neutral vertex connected
to $L$ changes only the dimension of the lepton component.
\end{proof}

\begin{assessment}[Reader-level summary of the finite and coercive duality]
The universal Grand Tensor supplies the positive history carrier and the
finite reconstruction calculus.  The SM--spacetime loading supplies the actual
Clifford, gauge-type, incidence, support, and transport histories.  Once these
histories are on one source-minimal carrier, the finite duality is terminating:
compute the joint action algebra and its commutant.  Singular residues are
handled by the support-polar algebra, noncommuting supports by the canonical
multiplicity quiver, and the connected invertible branch by one rooted polar
metric--holonomy algebra.  The relative Howe Gram tests in one positive matrix
whether the proposed generation/flavour algebra is the complete commutant.  A
finite anchor plus a controlled tail, or Mosco convergence plus a compact
commutator screen, upgrades the same finite duality to a regulator-uniform
coercive statement.
\end{assessment}


% =============================================================================
\subsection{Spacetime dynamics and the continuum handoff inside the loaded tensor}
\label{sec:spacetime-sector}
% =============================================================================

The finite commutant duality is independent of the continuum handoff.  The
latter is a layered conditional theorem whose hypotheses are histories and
quantitative residuals inside the same loaded tensor.

\begin{theorem}[Structured spacetime source-frame noncollapse]
\label{thm:SMST-spacetime-frame}
Let the intended one-cell spacetime source at cutoff $h$ decompose orthogonally
into finitely many equivariant positive blocks $A_{\lambda,h}\succeq0$.  Assume
that every block declared to survive has
\[
 \lambda_{\min}^{+}(A_{\lambda,h})\ge c_*>0
\]
with one constant independent of $h$.  Then the one-cell source synthesis has
frame lower bound $c_*$ on the intended support.  Its threefold determinant
source has frame lower bound $c_*^3$.  Conversely, if an intended positive
eigenvalue tends to zero, a corresponding normalized eigenvector is an explicit
collapsing source direction, so finite source saturation need not survive the
regulator limit.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The equivariant block decomposition is orthogonal.  If
$x=\bigoplus_\lambda x_\lambda$ belongs to the intended supported coefficient
space, then
\[
 \sum_\lambda\langle x_\lambda,A_{\lambda,h}x_\lambda\rangle
 \ge c_*\sum_\lambda\|x_\lambda\|^2=c_*\|x\|^2.
\]
This is exactly the lower frame inequality.  Tensoring the inequality three
times gives $A_h^{\otimes3}\succeq c_*^3I$ on the tensor support, and restriction
to the alternating determinant line preserves the same lower bound.  If
$A_{\lambda,h}v_h=\varepsilon_hv_h$ with $\|v_h\|=1$ and
$\varepsilon_h\downarrow0$, then the physical source norm of $v_h$ is
$\varepsilon_h^{1/2}\to0$, which is the asserted explicit collapse.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Pressure-adapted coherent ADM packet]
\label{thm:SMST-ADM-Cartan}
Let a regulator family carry, on each compact source phase:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(P\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item an irreducible positive renewal-pressure transfer with root $\beta_h>0$,
      positive directional depths $\ell_{\mu,h}$, and physical scale
      $h_{{\rm P},h}=c_*/\beta_h$;
\item one finite-coefficient or uniquely generated jointly minimal coherent
      history kernel containing the pressure branches, the marked temporal
      branch, the three spatial generator branches, and their retained tangent
      histories;
\item exact neighboring covariance of that complete kernel under the actual
      physical links, or a same-history covariance defect tending to zero in
      the stated local $L^p$ topology;
\item a uniform completely bounded generator bound
      $\|\mathcal B_{\mu,h}\|_{\rm cb}\le M$ and near-identity links
      $\|\Phi_{e,h}-I\|_{\rm cb}\le hM$;
\item the complete-source frame floor of
      \Cref{thm:SMST-spacetime-frame}, horizontal gauge, and either uniform
      discrete Hodge--Sobolev constants on compact regulator patches or the
      finite-type weighted inverse packet of
      \Cref{thm:renewal-finite-type-closure}.
\end{enumerate}
Then:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.8em]
\item the physical lapse is
      \[
       \boxed{\mathcal N_h=\beta_h\ell_{0,h}},
      \]
      and has positive upper and lower bounds on every compact pressure phase;
\item one environment unitary transports all pressure, temporal, and spatial
      Radon--Nikodym coordinates and their retained generator histories across
      each neighboring link;
\item after a common frame identification,
      \[
       \boxed{
       h^{-1}\|\mathcal B_{\mu,h}(y)-\mathcal B_{\mu,h}(x)\|_{\rm cb}
       \le C M^2+o(1)};
      \]
\item every actual spatial or mixed chronological face satisfies
      \[
       \boxed{
       \left\|-h^{-2}\operatorname{Log}\mathscr H_{\mu\nu,h}\right\|
       \le C\bigl(M^2+\mathfrak V_{\mu\nu,h}\bigr),}
      \]
      where $\mathfrak V_{\mu\nu,h}$ is the calibrated same-history transport
      residual for that face;
\item if the face packet is uniformly bounded in local $L^p$ for some $p>4$,
      either directly or by the regenerative finite-type graph estimate of
      \Cref{thm:SMST-regenerative-ADM}, then the horizontal connection is
      uniformly bounded in $W^{1,p}_{\rm loc}$ and the reconstructed ADM
      response metric is bounded in $C^{0,\alpha}_{\rm loc}$ for every
      $\alpha<1-4/p$.
\end{enumerate}
No smooth continuum connection is inserted before these estimates.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
A directional history of depth $\ell_{\mu,h}$ has physical duration
$\tau_{\mu,h}=c_*\ell_{\mu,h}$.  Dividing the temporal duration by the intrinsic
pressure scale gives
\[
 \frac{\tau_{0,h}}{h_{{\rm P},h}}=\beta_h\ell_{0,h}=\mathcal N_h.
\]
Compactness of the chosen positive Perron phase gives the two-sided lapse
bounds.

Two source-minimal realizations of the same complete coherent kernel are
related by one source-fixing unitary.  Applying minimal-realization uniqueness
to neighboring cells therefore gives one unitary independent of the history
label.  Differentiating the coherent intertwining identity transports every
retained tangent generator, proving item~\textup{(ii)}.

Write the exact transported generator relation in a common coefficient frame
as
\[
 \mathcal B_y(v)=\Phi_e\mathcal B_x(Q_e^{-1}v)\Phi_e^{-1}+R_e(v),
 \qquad \|R_e\|_{\rm cb}=o(h).
\]
Near identity, $\|Q_e^{-1}-I\|\le ChM$, while conjugation by $\Phi_e$ changes an
operator of norm at most $M$ by at most $2hM^2+O(h^2M^3)$.  Subtraction and
division by $h$ give item~\textup{(iii)}.

Let $W_\mu$ be the actual edge propagator, written on a unit parameter interval
as $\partial_sW_\mu=-h\mathcal B_\mu(s)W_\mu$.  Variation of constants gives
\[
 \|W_B(1)-W_C(1)\|
 \le h e^{2hM}\int_0^1\|B(s)-C(s)\|\,\dd s.
\]
Compare the actual face product with the same-base commutator face.  The
Baker--Campbell--Hausdorff remainder is $O(h^2M^2)$, and the preceding estimate
controls the base-transport error by $h^2\mathfrak V_{\mu\nu,h}$.  The principal
logarithm is defined for all sufficiently small $h$, giving item~\textup{(iv)}.

Finally, horizontal gauge removes the discrete exact component.  The uniform
Hodge estimate controls the full first difference of the connection by its
exterior derivative, codifferential, and zeroth-order norm.  The face bound
controls the exterior derivative, while the frame floor controls conversion
between source and coefficient norms.  The uniform discrete Sobolev estimate
therefore gives a $W^{1,p}$ bound.  In four dimensions, Morrey embedding yields
$C^{0,\alpha}$ for every $\alpha<1-4/p$, proving item~\textup{(v)}.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Regenerative derivation of the ADM regularity packet]
\label{thm:SMST-regenerative-ADM}
Assume the pressure-adapted histories of \Cref{thm:SMST-ADM-Cartan} and set
$\tau_h=c_*\ell_{0,h}$.  Suppose that, on a fixed compact pressure region:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(R\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item the horizontal current/outgoing source and actual face families form a
      finite physical type atlas with a positive type-mass floor;
\item their prototype source Grams have a common positive floor and their
      normalized Ward--graph and face-composition matrices have bounded
      integrated quadratic energy and controlled type-covariance residuals;
\item the protected-horizontal Hodge packet satisfies either direct $L^{p_0}$
      and $L^p$ conorm bounds for some
      $4p/(p+2)\le p_0<4<p$, or the weighted inverse branch of
      \Cref{thm:renewal-finite-type-closure};
\item the generator source is uniformly bounded and its projection outside the
      horizontal source frame is uniformly controlled.
\end{enumerate}
Then the source-frame floor converts the generator-source bound into a uniform
connection-coefficient bound.  The finite type-mass theorem converts the
quadratic Ward--graph and face energies into local amplitude caps and hence
into every finite $L^r$ bound.  In particular the actual chronological faces
are uniformly bounded in local $L^p$ for the displayed $p>4$.  The horizontal
Hodge estimate gives a uniform $W^{1,p}_{\rm loc}$ connection, and the coframe
and metric are precompact in $C^{0,\alpha}_{\rm loc}$ for every
$\alpha<1-4/p$.

If the same protected-soft Hodge form dominates a compact-resolvent anchor,
the finite-rank screen and its uniformly exhausted tails follow from
\Cref{thm:renewal-shorted-Hodge}.  Thus on this branch the separate local
amplitude, $p>4$ face, Hodge-conorm, and compact-screen hypotheses are outputs
of one finite-type regenerative packet.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The local source-frame estimate is the least-eigenvalue inequality applied to
the coefficient synthesis.  The first conclusion of
\Cref{thm:renewal-finite-type-closure} gives the local Ward--graph and face
caps from their integrated energies, and interpolation gives their finite
$L^r$ bounds.  The coherent plaquette comparison in
\Cref{thm:SMST-ADM-Cartan} transfers the spatial and mixed edge defects to the
actual faces.  The direct conorm branch is the finite Hodge estimate; on the
weighted inverse branch it follows from the final assertion of
\Cref{thm:renewal-finite-type-closure}.  Sobolev--Morrey embedding gives the
coefficient compactness.  The screen statement is
\Cref{thm:renewal-shorted-Hodge}.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[Pressure data alone do not control curvature]
A bounded scalar pressure packet and bounded one-edge generator norms do not
control transverse generator oscillation.  Alternating neighboring generators
may have identical scalar pressure data while the normalized spatial or mixed
face curvature grows like $h^{-1}$.  The jointly coherent same-history
transport and its residual in \Cref{thm:SMST-ADM-Cartan} are therefore
load-bearing.
\end{firewall}

\begin{theorem}[Endpoint shift and Cartan closure]
\label{thm:SMST-shift-Cartan}
Assume \Cref{thm:SMST-ADM-Cartan}.  Let the retained temporal endpoint source
decompose under spatial rotations into a scalar normal line, vector endpoint
lines, and an orthogonal residual.  Let $G_h=E_h^{\mathsf T}E_h$ be the spatial
metric and let $\mathscr P_{\beta,h}$ pull the later metric back by the actual
endpoint map.  Then:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.8em]
\item the vector-isotypic Gram is $I_3\otimes C_h$, and $\rank C_h$ is the
      number of independent physical shift ports;
\item rank zero makes the shift future null, while rank one reconstructs one
      shift $\beta_h$; if endpoint relabelings are future null, a local inverse
      flow removes $\beta_h$ without changing the physical quotient;
\item the finite extrinsic response
      \[
       K_h=\frac{\mathscr P_{\beta,h}G_h(t+h)-G_h(t)}
                   {2h\mathcal N_h}
      \]
      converges, whenever the displayed difference converges, to
      \[
       K=\frac1{2\mathcal N}
       (\partial_0G-\mathcal L_\beta G);
      \]
\item for the time-gauge coframe
      \[
       e^0=\mathcal N\,\dd t,
       \qquad e^a=E^a{}_i(\dd x^i+\beta^i\dd t),
      \]
      the complete mixed torsion is
      \[
       \boxed{
       T^a{}_{0i}=\left[(\partial_0-\mathcal L_\beta)E
       +(\omega_0-\beta^j\omega_j)E
       -\mathcal N E^{-\mathsf T}K\right]^a{}_i;}
      \]
\item the unique Cartan-compatible temporal rotation is
      \[
       \boxed{
       \omega_0^{\rm C}=\beta^j\omega_j
       +\mathcal N E^{-\mathsf T}KE^{-1}
       -(\partial_0-\mathcal L_\beta)EE^{-1},}
      \]
      and, after spatial torsion vanishes,
      \[
       \boxed{T=0\iff\omega_0=\omega_0^{\rm C}.}
      \]
\end{enumerate}
If the physical and Cartan temporal-rotation sources have the same
multiplicity-one adjoint range and preserve one nonzero ordered
$\mathfrak{so}(3)$ bracket, they are equal; the resulting connection is
Levi--Civita.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Rotation covariance makes the vector source an isotypic tensor product of the
standard real three-dimensional representation with a multiplicity space.
The real Schur lemma therefore gives $I_3\otimes C_h$, and its multiplicity rank
counts the independent vector ports.  Under a time-dependent spatial
relabeling $y=\phi_t(x)$ the shift transforms as
\[
 \widetilde\beta=D\phi_t\,\beta-\partial_t\phi_t.
\]
Solving $\partial_t\psi_t=-\beta(t,\psi_t)$ gives a local zero-shift chart when
that relabeling is physically null.  Pullback of the later metric by the actual
endpoint map and first-order expansion give the formula for $K$.

Insert the displayed coframe into Cartan's first structure equation
$T^I=\dd e^I+\Omega^I{}_J\wedge e^J$.  The spatial boost part is fixed by $K$
and $\dd\log\mathcal N$.  Collecting the $\dd t\wedge\dd x^i$ coefficients
gives the mixed-torsion matrix in item~\textup{(iv)}.  Solving that equation for
$\omega_0$ gives $\omega_0^{\rm C}$.  Its symmetric part vanishes because $K$
is defined by the symmetric metric derivative, hence
$\omega_0^{\rm C}\in\mathfrak{so}(3)$.  Once spatial torsion is zero, every
remaining torsion component is $(\omega_0-\omega_0^{\rm C})E$, proving the
equivalence.

On one adjoint source copy, equivariance makes the two source maps scalar
multiples: $S_{\rm C}=\lambda S_{\rm phys}$.  Preservation of one nonzero
relation $[J_1,J_2]=J_3$ gives $\lambda^2=\lambda$.  Nonzero source rank excludes
$\lambda=0$, so $\lambda=1$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Rigidity of the local one-doublet and minimal gauge actions]
\label{thm:SMST-action-rigidity}
Let $W_x\cong\C^2$ be the source-native weak fibres and
$U_e^W:W_x\to W_y$ the actual unitary weak transport on an oriented edge
$e:x\to y$.

\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(A\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item Let $Q_e$ be a real quadratic edge action which is locally weak-gauge
      covariant, nonnegative, and whose zero set is exactly
      $\phi_y=U_e^W\phi_x$.  Then for a unique $w_e>0$,
      \[
       \boxed{Q_e(\phi_x,\phi_y)
       =w_e\|U_e^W\phi_x-\phi_y\|^2.}
      \]
\item Let $V_x$ be weak-$U(2)$ invariant, nonnegative, polynomial of total
      degree at most four, and zero exactly on the microscopic source sphere
      $\|\phi\|=\rho_x>0$.  Then for a unique $\lambda_x>0$,
      \[
       \boxed{V_x(\phi)
       =\lambda_x(\|\phi\|^2-\rho_x^2)^2.}
      \]
\item Let a face action on $U_f\in U(n)$ be affine in the fundamental character
      and its conjugate, invariant under conjugation and reversal, nonnegative,
      and zero exactly at $U_f=I$.  Then for a unique $w_f>0$,
      \[
       \boxed{S_f(U_f)
       =w_f\bigl(n-\operatorname{Re}\Tr U_f\bigr)
       =\frac{w_f}{2}\|I-U_f\|_{\HS}^2.}
      \]
      Its Hessian at the identity is the physical invariant current metric
      $w_f\operatorname{Re}\Tr(XY)$.
\end{enumerate}
Consequently, on this local branch the scalar and minimal plaquette actions are
fixed by the actual links, source radius, and one positive coefficient per edge,
site, or gauge factor.  Higher-order, nonlocal, or higher-character terms are
not excluded and must be retained when their action residuals are nonzero.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Conjugate the edge variables by the actual transport and write the most general
simultaneously $U(2)$-invariant real quadratic form as
$a\|x\|^2+b\|y\|^2-2\operatorname{Re}(c\langle x,y\rangle)$.  Vanishing on
$x=y$ gives $a+b=2\operatorname{Re}c$ and vanishing of the imaginary cross
part.  Positivity and the requirement that the kernel be precisely the diagonal
force $a=b=c=w_e>0$.

A continuous $U(2)$-invariant polynomial depends only on
$s=\|\phi\|^2$.  Degree at most four gives $as^2+bs+c$.  Nonnegativity and a
complete zero set at $s=\rho_x^2$ make this polynomial a positive multiple of
$(s-\rho_x^2)^2$.  Finally, the assumed character branch has the form
$a-b\operatorname{Re}\Tr U$.  Vanishing at $I$, nonnegativity, and uniqueness
of the zero give $a=bn$ and $b=w_f>0$.  Expanding
$e^{i(sX+tY)}$ to second order gives the current metric.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Typed matter closure and finite Legendre reciprocity]
\label{thm:SMST-matter-Legendre}
Let $\mathscr L(z,v)$ be a finite matter Lagrangian with symmetric positive
velocity Hessian $\mathbb K=D_v^2\mathscr L\succ0$, and let
\[
 p=D_v\mathscr L(z,v),\qquad
 \mathscr H(z,p)=\langle p,v(z,p)\rangle-\mathscr L(z,v(z,p)).
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{D_p\mathscr H=v,\qquad D_z\mathscr H=-D_z\mathscr L,
 \qquad D_p^2\mathscr H=\mathbb K^{-1}.}
\]
Thus Lagrangian and Hamiltonian metric derivatives define the same stress
covector.

For typed matter sectors $r$, suppose the finite normal density has momentum
coefficient $a_r>0$ and transported spatial-gradient coefficient $b_r>0$.
Then the exact lapse-antisymmetrized matter bracket is
\[
 \boxed{
 -i[H_{{\rm m},h}[N],H_{{\rm m},h}[M]]
 =\sum_r a_rb_r\,D_{r,h}
 \!\left[\mathsf Q_{r,h}(N\dd_hM-M\dd_hN)\right],}
\]
where $\mathsf Q_{r,h}$ is the measured conductance second-moment tensor.  If
\[
 \mathcal K_{xy}^{\rm gm}=-iP[t_{{\rm g},x},h_{{\rm m},y}]P,
\]
the complete gravity--matter cross anomaly is
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal X_h^{\rm gm}(N,M)
 =\sum_{x<y}(N_xM_y-N_yM_x)
 (\mathcal K_{xy}^{\rm gm}-\mathcal K_{yx}^{\rm gm}).}
\]
Consequently, conductance matching $\mathsf Q_{r,h}=G_h^{-1}$, symmetry of the
cross kernel, and positivity of a determining species-current Gram imply total
HDA closure exactly when
\[
 \boxed{a_rb_r=1\qquad\text{for every loaded species }r.}
\]
If one positive amplitude multiplies the whole Hamiltonian sector,
$a_r=b_r=\lambda_r$, then $\lambda_r=1$.  If instead one Lagrangian sector has
action stiffness $\eta_r>0$, its Legendre descendants are
\[
 \boxed{a_r=\eta_r^{-1},\qquad b_r=\eta_r,}
\]
so HDA closure does not determine $\eta_r$.

More generally, for a cutoff family of measured kinetic Hessians $\mathbb K_h$
and independently measured Hamiltonian Hessians $\mathbb A_h$, a uniform least
singular-value margin for $\mathbb K_h$, a vanishing mixed-block residual, and
\[
 \boxed{
 \Delta_{\rm Leg,h}
 :=\|\mathbb A_h\mathbb K_h-I\|_{\HS}^2
  +\|\mathbb K_h\mathbb A_h-I\|_{\HS}^2}
\]
are respectively the exact certificates for uniform Legendre invertibility,
absence of unintended metric--matter kinetic mixing, and reciprocal Hessians.
For quadratic fermions,
$[\dd\Gamma(A),\dd\Gamma(B)]=\dd\Gamma([A,B])$, so the many-body bracket is the
CAR lift of the one-particle bracket.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Differentiate the Legendre identity at fixed $p$.  The terms involving
$D_zv$ or $D_pv$ cancel because $p=D_v\mathscr L$, giving the first two
envelope formulas.  Differentiating $p=D_v\mathscr L$ with respect to $p$
gives $D_pv=\mathbb K^{-1}$ and therefore the inverse-Hessian identity.

In the lapse antisymmetrization, momentum--momentum and multiplication--
multiplication terms commute.  A local potential contributes the coefficient
$N_xM_x-M_xN_x=0$.  Only momentum--gradient commutators remain.  On an oriented
edge they give the transported symmetrized current multiplied by
$a_rb_r(N_xM_y-M_xN_y)$.  Summation over edges gives the displayed matter
bracket and identifies $\mathsf Q_{r,h}$.

Expanding the two mixed smeared Hamiltonians and pairing the terms indexed by
$(x,y)$ and $(y,x)$ gives the cross-anomaly formula.  After conductance matching
and cross-kernel symmetry, subtracting the physical unweighted total
diffeomorphism source leaves
\[
 \sum_r(a_rb_r-1)D_{r,h}(v)=0.
\]
Let $c_r=a_rb_r-1$.  On a determining family of currents its squared physical
norm is $c^*G_{\rm sp}c$.  Positivity of the species-current Gram makes this zero
only for $c=0$, proving $a_rb_r=1$.  The two specializations are immediate; the
second is the usual inversion of a Lagrangian quadratic coefficient under the
Legendre transform.

The reciprocity residual is a sum of squares and vanishes exactly when
$\mathbb A_h$ is both a left and right inverse of $\mathbb K_h$.  A uniform
least singular value bounds $\|\mathbb K_h^{-1}\|$; inverse convergence follows
from
\[
 \mathbb K_h^{-1}-\mathbb K^{-1}
 =\mathbb K_h^{-1}(\mathbb K-\mathbb K_h)\mathbb K^{-1}.
\]
Finally, the CAR identity follows by direct computation on matrix units
$c_i^*c_j$ and linearity.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Action-derived scalar current]
For the local scalar action of \Cref{thm:SMST-action-rigidity}, let $K_x>0$ be
the transported kinetic metric and let $p_x$ be the canonical momentum.  Then
\[
 \{H(N),H(M)\}=D_{\rm sc}(\omega(N,M)),
 \qquad \omega(N,M)_{(x,y)}=N_xM_y-M_xN_y,
\]
with edge current
\[
 \boxed{
 J_e^{\rm sc}=\frac{w_e}{2}\left\langle
 \phi_y-U_e\phi_x,\ U_ep_x+p_y\right\rangle.}
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The inverse kinetic metric in the Hamiltonian cancels the transported kinetic
metric in the gradient energy.  Collecting both orientations of each edge gives
the displayed current; the local potential cancels by lapse antisymmetry.
\end{proof}


\begin{theorem}[Shared-edge normal current, reduction, and commutant]
\label{thm:shared-edge-normal-current}
Let a finite one-skeleton carry one extracted Pauli factor per edge, with
cross-edge factors commuting.  For an oriented edge $e=(x,y)$ choose the
endpoint axes $A_{e,x}=X_e$ and $A_{e,y}=Y_e$, and define
\[
 n_{x,h}=\sum_{e\ni x}\lambda_{e,x,h}A_{e,x},
 \qquad
 H_h[N]=\sum_xN_xn_{x,h}.
\]
Then nonadjacent vertex densities commute.  On $e=(x,y)$,
\[
 \boxed{
 j_{e,h}:=-ih[n_{x,h},n_{y,h}]
 =2h\lambda_{e,x,h}\lambda_{e,y,h}Z_e.}
\]
Consequently
\[
 \boxed{
 -i[H_h[N],H_h[M]]
 =\sum_{e=(x,y)}
 (N_x\nabla_eM-M_x\nabla_eN)j_{e,h}.}
\]
With the product normalized trace, distinct edge currents are orthogonal and
have squared norms
$4h^2|\lambda_{e,x,h}\lambda_{e,y,h}|^2$.

If all incidence coefficients are nonzero, the algebra generated by the
vertex normal densities contains the complete Pauli factor on every edge.  On
the minimal parallel-edge carrier it is the full tensor product and has scalar
commutant.  The carrier is reducing for the normal-history algebra.

A regulator-uniform nonzero current requires an unbounded normal scale.  More
precisely, if
$|2h\lambda_{e,x,h}\lambda_{e,y,h}|\ge\kappa_*>0$, then
\[
 \max\{|\lambda_{e,x,h}|,|\lambda_{e,y,h}|\}
 \ge\sqrt{\kappa_*/(2h)}.
\]
Under a bounded endpoint-loading ratio, both coefficients are of order
$h^{-1/2}$; the continuum passage must therefore use the quadratic-form and
ordered-product-core theory of Part~I-B.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Only a shared edge factor can contribute to the commutator of two different
vertex densities.  The Pauli identity $[X_e,Y_e]=2iZ_e$ gives the current and,
after pairing both orientations, the smeared bracket.  Product-trace
orthogonality follows because distinct currents are traceless operators on
distinct tensor factors.

Since $j_{e,h}$ is a nonzero scalar multiple of $Z_e$, the normal algebra
contains $Z_e$.  Commuting it with the endpoint density at $x$ recovers $Y_e$,
and commuting it with the endpoint density at $y$ recovers $X_e$.  Hence it
contains every edge $M_2(\C)$; on the minimal tensor-product carrier their
joint commutant is scalar.  Reduction follows because the full generated
matrix algebra leaves no exterior source-cyclic direction.  The scaling bound
is the arithmetic--geometric inequality applied to
$2h|\lambda_{e,x,h}\lambda_{e,y,h}|\ge\kappa_*$.  A bounded ratio makes the
two factors comparable.
\end{proof}

\begin{assessment}[What the shared-edge packet discharges]
On this branch the Store--score compiler supplies coherent access to the two
ordered normal words, while
\Cref{thm:shared-edge-normal-current} supplies off-edge locality, the finite
current frame, a reducing minimal carrier, and the scalar normal commutant.
The remaining HDA content is the same-history identity of this current with the
metric/tangential endpoint source, its absolute unit normalization, a physical
differentiable endpoint-flow action, and the common unbounded form/domain
limit.
\end{assessment}

\begin{theorem}[Complete finite coherent vacuum HDA]
\label{thm:finite-HDA}
