Let $H_h[N]$ and $D_h[v]$ be self-adjoint normal and tangential generators on
one finite physical carrier.  Assume:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(H\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item the two ordered normal histories lie in one covered Store--score target,
      and the calibrated phases $1$ and $i$ reconstruct their complex cross
      kernel; the settings $-1$ and $-i$ are consistency checks;
\item $H_h[N]=\sum_xN_xn_{x,h}$ and
      $[n_{x,h},n_{y,h}]=0$ outside the declared one-link neighborhood;
\item the normalized edge-current source is same-history identical with the
      endpoint commutator of two unit-normal deformations and has exactly one
      physical tangential vector copy;
\item the carrier is the complete reducing source-cyclic carrier of the retained
      normal and tangential history algebra;
\item physical endpoint relabelings form a finite Lie group acting on scalar
      lapse labels, and the complete coherent normal histories transform by that
      semidirect action;
\item either the coherent relabeling histories form a strict representation, or
      the normal-history commutant is scalar and $D_h[v]$ is canonically
      centered.
\end{enumerate}
Then
\begin{align}
 -i[D_h[v],D_h[w]]&=D_h[[v,w]_h],\\
 -i[D_h[v],H_h[N]]&=H_h[\ell_h(v)N],\\
 -i[H_h[N],H_h[M]]
 &=D_h\!\left[G_h^{-1}(N\dd_hM-M\dd_hN)\right].
\end{align}
All interface or Feshbach terms vanish on the reducing carrier.  Under
consistent label, source, and metric convergence, the identities pass to the
continuum vacuum hypersurface-deformation algebra.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Expand the local normal densities.  Off-neighbor commutativity leaves only
oriented edges:
\[
 -i[H_h[N],H_h[M]]
 =\sum_{e=(x,y)}(N_xM_y-M_xN_y)(-i[n_{x,h},n_{y,h}]).
\]
Writing $j_{e,h}=-ih[n_{x,h},n_{y,h}]$, the coefficient is
$N_x\nabla_eM-M_x\nabla_eN$.  For a spacelike embedding $X$ with unit normal
$n$, differentiation of $g(n,n)=-1$ and $g(n,\partial_iX)=0$ under
$\delta_NX=Nn$ gives
\[
 \delta_Nn=G^{-1}\dd N,
 \qquad
 [\delta_N,\delta_M]_{\rm ord}X
 =G^{-1}(N\dd M-M\dd N).
\]
The same-history endpoint identity transfers this unit coefficient to the
physical edge current.  The one-copy condition removes every orthogonal vector
port, proving the $HH$ bracket.

Let $R_h(g)=e^{-isD_h[v]}$ implement endpoint flow and
$U_h(N,t)=e^{-itH_h[N]}$.  Semidirect naturality is
\[
 R_h(g)U_h(N,t)R_h(g)^{-1}=U_h(\rho_h(g)N,t).
\]
Differentiate first in $t$ and then at $g=e^{sv}$ to obtain the $DH$ bracket
with unit amplitude.

Set
\[
 Z(v,w)=-i[D_h[v],D_h[w]]-D_h[[v,w]_h].
\]
The operator Jacobi identity, the $DH$ relation, and
$[\ell_h(v),\ell_h(w)]=\ell_h([v,w]_h)$ imply
$[Z(v,w),H_h[N]]=0$ for every retained lapse.  Under the scalar-commutant branch,
$Z(v,w)$ is scalar; canonical centering makes it traceless and hence zero.  In
the strict group-law branch, direct differentiation of the representation law
gives the same conclusion.

Finally, if $P$ is the reducing source projection and $Q=I-P$, then
$QH_h[N]P=QD_h[v]P=0$.  Every Schur/Feshbach cross term such as
$PAQBP-PBQAP$ therefore vanishes.  Convergence of the finite labels and source
forms passes the three identities to the limit on a common core.
\end{proof}

\begin{assessment}[Why the HDA coefficient is not fitted]
The coefficient one in the $HH$ bracket is the measured coefficient of the
unit-normal endpoint commutator, not an inserted continuum structure function.
The canonical Store--score compiler supplies ordered-history coherence once the
normal generators occur.  On the shared-edge branch,
\Cref{thm:shared-edge-normal-current} additionally supplies off-edge locality,
a reducing carrier, and a scalar finite commutant.  The remaining content is
the physical current--geometry source identity, its absolute normalization,
semidirect endpoint flow, and the regulator-uniform unbounded-domain limit.
\end{assessment}

\begin{corollary}[Common-action provenance discharges the normal--endpoint comparison]
Let $h_x^{\rm act}$ be the action-derived normal generator, $n_x$ the
generator-native normal candidate, $a_x$ the protected affine endpoint writer,
and $V_{\rm aff}$ a whitened source-minimal synthesis.  Define
\[
 \Delta_{\rm act\to nor}=\sum_x\|n_x-h_x^{\rm act}\|_{\HS}^2,
 \qquad
 \Delta_{\rm act\to end}
 =\sum_x\|h_x^{\rm act}V_{\rm aff}-V_{\rm aff}a_x\|_{\HS}^2.
\]
Then, for $R_x=n_xV_{\rm aff}-V_{\rm aff}a_x$,
\[
 \boxed{
 \sum_x\|R_x\|_{\HS}^2
 \le2\Delta_{\rm act\to nor}+2\Delta_{\rm act\to end}.}
\]
Thus zero provenance residuals identify the generator-native normal and the
endpoint writer as restrictions of one Hamiltonian flow.  Together with the
phase, locality, cyclicity, and semidirect hypotheses of
\Cref{thm:finite-HDA}, this verifies the endpoint-source premise without an
independent one-particle HDA assumption.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Insert and subtract $h_x^{\rm act}V_{\rm aff}$ and use
$\|u+v\|^2\le2\|u\|^2+2\|v\|^2$, then sum over $x$.  If both residuals vanish,
$n_xV_{\rm aff}=V_{\rm aff}a_x$ and both are equal to the action-derived
restriction.  No cancellation between unrelated mismatches is used.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Common-action Ward, BRST, stress, and finite Einstein residual]
\label{thm:SMST-finite-action-Einstein}
Let
\[
 \mathscr S_{\rm tot}(q,\Phi)
 =\mathscr S_g(q)+\mathscr S_{\rm mat}(q,\Phi)
\]
be one finite action on the joint loaded carrier.  Define
\[
 E_\Phi=D_\Phi\mathscr S_{\rm mat},
 \qquad
 \mathsf T=-2D_q\mathscr S_{\rm mat},
\]
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal E_q^{\rm tot}
 =2D_q\mathscr S_{\rm tot}
 =2D_q\mathscr S_g-\mathsf T.}
\]
Then:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(F\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item exact finite gauge invariance gives the Ward identity
      \[
       \boxed{\operatorname{Div}_UJ+
       \mathcal R_{\rm mat,\Phi}^*E_\Phi=0;}
      \]
      on matter shell the current is conserved;
\item the standard finite BRST differential on ghosts, links, scalar fields,
      and every covariant finite-Dirac carrier is nilpotent and annihilates the
      classical action;
\item common tangential relabeling invariance gives
      \[
       \boxed{\mathcal L_q^*\mathsf T
       =2\mathcal L_\Phi^*E_\Phi,}
      \]
      and therefore tangential stress conservation on matter shell;
\item for any faithful metric $G_{\mathcal Q}$ on geometric variations,
      \[
       \boxed{
       \Delta_{\rm Ein}^{\rm fin}
       :=\langle\mathcal E_q^{\rm tot},
       G_{\mathcal Q}^{-1}\mathcal E_q^{\rm tot}\rangle\ge0}
      \]
      vanishes exactly when the finite total action is metrically stationary,
      equivalently $2D_q\mathscr S_g=\mathsf T$.
\end{enumerate}
No external stress router is required on the common-action branch.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Differentiate gauge invariance and integrate the link variations by the finite
incidence adjoint to obtain the Ward identity.  The BRST rules are the
infinitesimal gauge action with $sc=-c^2$; the Jacobi identity and covariance
give $s^2=0$, and gauge invariance gives $s\mathscr S_{\rm tot}=0$.
Differentiating tangential invariance in the same way gives the stress identity.
The final statement follows from positivity and faithfulness of
$G_{\mathcal Q}^{-1}$.
\end{proof}



% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
\subsubsection{Protected cycle rewards, renewal pressure, and common-action exactness}
\label{sec:renewal-action-pressure}
% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

The normalized score of a probability law is centered and therefore does not,
by itself, contain the affine first variation of an action.  On a marked
renewal cycle that affine coordinate is recovered from the physical duration
and the renewal-pressure normalization.  The complete action sectors must be
placed on the same resolved reward record; proportionality to the accepted
count is neither required nor expected.

\begin{definition}[Protected vector cycle-reward packet]
\label{def:protected-cycle-reward}
Let $(\Omega_X,p_X)$ be a finite faithful marked first-return law, let
$\tau_X:\Omega_X\to(0,\infty)$ be the protected physical duration, and let
$E_X$ be a finite real variation space.  A protected cycle-reward synthesis is
\[
 G_X:E_X\longrightarrow L^2(\Omega_X,p_X),
 \qquad v\longmapsto g_{v,X},
\]
whose values are actual Reads or fixed functions of protected record
coordinates.  Define
\[
 \mathcal L_X(q,r)
 =\mathbb E_X[e^{-g_{q,X}-r\tau_X}],
 \qquad
 \bar\tau_X=\mathbb E_X\tau_X,
 \qquad
 T_Xc=c\tau_X.
\]
The minimal reward record identifies precisely those cycle records with equal
$(g_X,\tau_X)$ values.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Table-derived reward pressure and complete action-slope reconstruction]
\label{thm:reward-pressure-reconstruction}
For every packet of \Cref{def:protected-cycle-reward}, the complete Laplace
transform $\mathcal L_X$ and all of its finite derivatives are reconstructed
from the marked-cycle table; no additional tilted experiment is needed for
this finite calculation.  There is a unique analytic pressure
$\mathcal P_X$ near the origin such that
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal P_X(0)=0,
 \qquad
 \mathcal L_X(q,\mathcal P_X(q))=1.}
\]
Let
\[
 p_{X,q}(\omega)
 =p_X(\omega)e^{-g_{q,X}(\omega)-\mathcal P_X(q)\tau_X(\omega)}
\]
and let $S_Xv=D\log p_{X,q}|_{q=0}[v]$.  Writing
$\pi_X=D\mathcal P_X(0)$ and
$\gamma_X=G_X^*\one$, one has
\[
 \boxed{
 \pi_X(v)=-\frac{\gamma_X(v)}{\bar\tau_X},}
\]
\[
 \boxed{
 S_Xv=-G_Xv-\pi_X(v)\tau_X,
 \qquad
 G_X=-S_X-T_X\pi_X.}
\]
Thus renewal pressure reconstructs the affine action anchor and, together with
the normalized score and duration writer, the complete uncentered physical
cycle-action slope.

The covariance rank satisfies
\[
 \boxed{
 \rank\operatorname{Cov}_{p_X}(g_X)
 =\dim\operatorname{Aff}\{g_X(\omega):\omega\in\Omega_X\}.}
\]
It is the exact number of independent fluctuating action directions present on
the resolved cycle record.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The transform is the finite sum of known probabilities times known protected
writer values; differentiating under the finite sum reconstructs every mixed
moment.  At the origin,
$\mathcal L_X(0,0)=1$ and
$\partial_r\mathcal L_X(0,0)=-\bar\tau_X<0$, so the analytic
implicit-function theorem gives the pressure root.  Differentiation of its
normalization in direction $v$ gives
\[
 0=-\mathbb E_Xg_{v,X}-\pi_X(v)\bar\tau_X,
\]
which proves the pressure-gradient identity.  Differentiating the normalized
law gives the score formula and hence the synthesis reconstruction.

For the rank statement, the quadratic form of the reward covariance on $v$ is
\[
 \mathbb E_X|\langle v,g_X-\mathbb E_Xg_X\rangle|^2.
\]
Faithfulness makes this zero exactly when $\langle v,g_X\rangle$ is constant
on the finite support.  The orthogonal complement of this kernel is the span of
all reward differences, whose dimension is the affine dimension of the reward
image.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Pressure-jet reconstruction of the complete mixed action Gram]
\label{thm:reward-pressure-jet}
In the setting of \Cref{thm:reward-pressure-reconstruction}, put
\[
 \bar\tau_X(q)=\mathbb E_{X,q}\tau_X,
 \qquad
 \delta_X=D\bar\tau_X(0),
 \qquad
 m_{2,X}=\mathbb E_X\tau_X^2.
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{
 D^2\mathcal P_X(0)=\bar\tau_X^{-1}S_X^*S_X\succeq0,}
\]
\[
 \boxed{\delta_X=T_X^*S_X,}
\]
and
\[
 \boxed{
 G_X^*G_X
 =\bar\tau_XD^2\mathcal P_X(0)
 +\delta_X^*\pi_X+\pi_X^*\delta_X
 +m_{2,X}\pi_X^*\pi_X.}
\]
Consequently, if
\[
 E_X=E_{g,X}\oplus E_{{\rm mat},X}\oplus E_{{\rm gauge},X}
 \oplus E_{{\rm pot},X}\oplus E_{{\rm ct},X}\oplus E_{{\rm bdry},X}
\]
and every sector reward is represented on the same marked cycle record, one
pressure surface reconstructs every marginal and mixed action block.  No
independent relative action router remains.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Differentiate
$\mathcal L_X(q,\mathcal P_X(q))=1$ twice.  Linearity of $q\mapsto g_{q,X}$
gives
\[
 0=\mathbb E_X\!
 \left[(g_u+\pi_X(u)\tau_X)(g_v+\pi_X(v)\tau_X)
 -D^2\mathcal P_X(0)[u,v]\tau_X\right].
\]
The first factors are $-S_Xu$ and $-S_Xv$, proving the Hessian identity.
Differentiating $\bar\tau_X(q)$ gives
$\delta_X(v)=\mathbb E_X[\tau_XS_Xv]=T_X^*S_Xv$.  Finally expand
$G_X=-S_X-T_X\pi_X$ and substitute
$S_X^*S_X=\bar\tau_XD^2\mathcal P_X(0)$,
$T_X^*S_X=\delta_X$, and $T_X^*T_X=m_{2,X}$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Protected Palatini--Cartan--Holst graph writer]
\label{thm:SMST-PCH-graph-writer}
Assume the finite protected field tuple contains the coframe, Cartan
connection, incidence, oriented normals, physical duration, boundary data, and
the already reconstructed coefficients on one nondegenerate logarithm branch.
Then the complete Palatini--Cartan--Holst bulk plus boundary functional
\[
 \boxed{g_{\rm PCH}=S_{\rm bulk}+S_{\partial}}
\]
is a deterministic real-analytic function of that tuple.  Appending the graph
coordinate
\[
 \Theta\longmapsto(\Theta,g_{\rm PCH}(\Theta))
\]
is an exactly conservative one-way writer: discarding the new coordinate
recovers every old probability and payload map, and the generated record
algebra is canonically isomorphic to the old one.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
All contractions, wedge products, incidence sums, boundary restrictions, and
matrix functions entering the finite action are fixed functions of the
protected tuple on the selected branch.  The graph map is injective and its
projection to the first coordinate is its inverse.  Summing over the appended
coordinate therefore recovers the old cylinder exactly, and every function of
the new coordinate already belongs to the old finite record algebra.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Writer-native Hodge and reward closure]
\label{thm:SMST-PCH-writer-closure}
Let
\[
 C^0\xrightarrow{d_0}C^1\xrightarrow{d_1}C^2,
 \qquad d_1d_0=0,
\]
be the protected finite variation complex, and let
\(\Sigma_{\rm PCH}:V_{\rm Ein}\to C^0\) be the directional first variation of
\(g_{\rm PCH}\).  Put
\[
 \boxed{A_{\rm PCH}=d_0\Sigma_{\rm PCH}.}
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{
 A_{\rm PCH}^*(I-d_0d_0^\dagger)A_{\rm PCH}=0,}
\]
\[
 \boxed{d_1A_{\rm PCH}=0,
 \qquad H^*A_{\rm PCH}=0,}
\]
where \(H\) synthesizes the harmonic one-cochains.  Hence every period, curl,
and harmonic residual of the differentiated writer vanishes.

If the same deterministic function \(g_{\rm PCH}\) is inserted as the
protected gravitational reward in the renewal-pressure packet and the same
nuisance sources are shorted from the pressure and Palatini--Holst--volume
columns, the pressure reconstruction returns that reward exactly and its
shorted source lies in the Palatini--Holst--volume source range.  The
corresponding Palatini Schur residual is therefore zero.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
By construction \(A_{\rm PCH}\subseteq\Ran d_0\), so the orthogonal projection
onto the exact range fixes it.  The relation \(d_1d_0=0\) gives the curl
identity, and the harmonic space is orthogonal to \(\Ran d_0\).  Renewal
pressure reconstructs the complete uncentered reward uniquely from its
protected score and duration; inserting \(g_{\rm PCH}\) therefore returns the
same function.  Orthogonal nuisance shorting is linear, so the shorted reward
remains the same fixed coefficient combination of the shorted physical action
columns, and its Schur innovation vanishes.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[Deterministic action provenance is not dynamical stationarity]
The preceding writer theorem proves that the proposed finite action is
non-arbitrary and that its formal Hodge and reward provenance close.  It does
not prove that the observed accepted transition is Gibbs, Bregman proximal, or
generated by that action.  The same-history accepted/common-action likelihood
test and the reference-measure Ward tests remain independent.
\end{firewall}

\begin{firewall}[Accepted count versus physical action]
\label{fire:count-action-residual}
The accepted-count source is the constant line in the accepted-cycle record.
For a physical action synthesis $G_X$, its count-short residual is
\[
 G_X^*(I-P_{\one})G_X
 =G_X^*G_X-(G_X^*\one)(G_X^*\one)^*\succeq0.
\]
It vanishes only when every action slope is cyclewise constant.  The accepted
count therefore calibrates the affine action component; its orthogonal
residual is generally genuine physical fluctuation and must not be forced to
zero.
\end{firewall}

\begin{theorem}[Finite common-action exactness]
\label{thm:common-action-exactness}
Let $\mathscr V_X$ be the finite protected variation complex: vertices are
finite physical configurations, oriented edges are primitive geometric or
matter variations, and $2$-cells encode commuting-variation or declared
relation loops.  Let $\alpha_X\in C^1(\mathscr V_X;\R)$ be the protected
cycle-action increment.  There is a scalar common action
$\mathscr S_X$ with
\[
 \boxed{\alpha_X=d_0\mathscr S_X}
\]
if and only if
\[
 \boxed{d_1\alpha_X=0}
\]
on every $2$-cell and all periods of $\alpha_X$ on one integral basis of
$H_1(\mathscr V_X;\Z)$ vanish.  After fixing one action anchor,
$\mathscr S_X$ is unique and is reconstructed by path integration.

If $P_{\rm ex}$, $P_{\rm har}$, and $P_{\rm coex}$ are the finite Hodge
projections on $C^1$ and $\sigma_{\rm coex}>0$ is the least singular value of
$d_1$ on the coexact range, then
\[
 \boxed{
 \operatorname{dist}(\alpha_X,\Ran d_0)^2
 \le\|P_{\rm har}\alpha_X\|^2
 +\sigma_{\rm coex}^{-2}\|d_1\alpha_X\|^2.}
\]
Thus face-curl and period Grams give a quantitative obstruction to one common
scalar action.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
If $\alpha_X=d_0\mathscr S_X$, telescoping gives zero face sums and zero
periods.  Conversely fix a base configuration and define $\mathscr S_X(q)$ by
summing $\alpha_X$ along a path from the base to $q$.  Face closure makes the
sum invariant under elementary relation moves and the period conditions make
it invariant under the remaining homology class.  This gives a well-defined
primitive.  Anchoring removes the additive constant.

The finite Hodge decomposition is
$C^1=\Ran d_0\oplus\mathcal H^1\oplus\Ran d_1^*$.  The distance to the exact
range is the squared norm of the harmonic and coexact components.  On the
coexact range,
$\|d_1\beta\|\ge\sigma_{\rm coex}\|\beta\|$, which yields the estimate.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Potential and counterterm exactness]
\label{thm:potential-counterterm-exactness}
Let $r_y(\phi)>0$ be a protected conditional Radon--Nikodym coordinate on a
finite field-configuration record.  Then
\[
 \boxed{V_y(\phi)=-\log r_y(\phi)}
\]
is a protected potential writer and the primitive field-move force
\[
 f_y(\phi\to\phi')
 =-\log\frac{r_y(\phi')}{r_y(\phi)}
\]
satisfies
\[
 \boxed{f_y=d_0V_y.}
\]
Thus all field-space curls and periods vanish identically.  Conditional
likelihood ratios determine the matter Euler force; an additive function of
the external geometry remains invisible to that conditional law and is fixed
by the pressure/partition anchor.

Likewise, a proposed local counterterm derivative
$c_X\in C^1(\mathscr V_X;\R)$ is the derivative of a scalar counterterm action
if and only if
\[
 \boxed{d_1c_X=0}
\]
and its periods vanish.  Given a predeclared allowed counterterm synthesis
$C_X:F_X\to\mathcal H_X$ and a raw action source
$R_X:E_X\to\mathcal H_X$, the irreducible residual after optimal allowed
cancellation is
\[
 \boxed{
 R_X^*(I-P_{C_X})R_X
 =R_X^*R_X-R_X^*C_X(C_X^*C_X)^\dagger C_X^*R_X.}
\]
A nonzero exactness or Schur residual is a genuine anomaly or additional force
source rather than a removable scheme choice.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The potential identity is the logarithm of a ratio and therefore telescopes on
every path.  Strict positivity and finite functional calculus place $V_y$ in
the same protected classical algebra.  Multiplication of $r_y$ by a positive
factor depending only on $y$ shifts $V_y$ by an external additive function,
leaving all field differences unchanged.

The counterterm exactness criterion is
\Cref{thm:common-action-exactness} applied to $c_X$.  For the cancellation
formula, write
$R_X=P_{C_X}R_X+(I-P_{C_X})R_X$.  For any coefficient router $K$,
\[
 R_X+C_XK=(I-P_{C_X})R_X
 +C_X\bigl(K+(C_X^*C_X)^\dagger C_X^*R_X\bigr),
\]
and the two terms are orthogonal.  Minimizing the Gram over $K$ leaves exactly
the displayed Schur residual.
\end{proof}


% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
\subsubsection{Accepted determining-field quotient and same-history action consistency}
\label{sec:accepted-action-consistency}
% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

The accepted-response clock determines when an update occurs, but it does not
by itself determine the updated physical field.  The correct field state and
action comparison are reconstructed from the complete accepted cylinder rather
than selected after the fact.

\begin{definition}[Minimal determining-field quotient and accepted kernel]
\label{def:minimal-determining-field}
Let $\widetilde\Theta_X$ be the finite generated ledger carrying the declared
coframe, connection, matter, gauge, boundary, metric, common-action, reward,
duration, and resolved accepted-branch coordinates.  Two ledger values are
future equivalent, $x\sim_{{\rm fld},X}y$, when every admitted future word and
every one of these determining coordinates has the same value from $x$ and
$y$, including all branch-domain indicators.  Put
\[
 \boxed{
 \Theta_{{\rm fld},X}^{\min}
 :=\widetilde\Theta_X/\!\sim_{{\rm fld},X}.}
\]
For the set $\mathscr A_{{\rm acc},X}$ of resolved accepted subbranches, define
on the positive-acceptance domain
\[
 \boxed{
 K_X^{\rm acc}(\theta'\mid\theta)
 :=\frac{1}{p_{{\rm acc},X}(\theta)}
   \sum_{\substack{a\in\mathscr A_{{\rm acc},X}:\\
        u_a^{\min}(\theta)=\theta'}}p_{a,X}(\theta).}
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Terminating determining-field and accepted-kernel compiler]
\label{thm:determining-field-compiler}
The quotient of \Cref{def:minimal-determining-field} is the unique coarsest
finite record through which every selected determining-field future and every
primitive update factors.  A partition refinement beginning with the immediate
coordinates and branch domains stabilizes after at most
$|\widetilde\Theta_X|-1$ strict rounds.  The kernel $K_X^{\rm acc}$ is well
defined, table native, and is the unique accepted transition reproducing all
selected post-accepted field futures.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Future equality is a typed right congruence: if $x\sim_{{\rm fld},X}y$, then
for every primitive branch $a$ and continuation $w$,
$d(u_wu_a(x))=d(u_{wa}(x))=d(u_{wa}(y))=d(u_wu_a(y))$.  Hence every update
descends.  At each refinement round split two states whenever an immediate
coordinate differs or one primitive update reaches different blocks.  The
$k$th partition identifies exactly the states not separated by a future of
length at most $k$; each strict refinement increases the number of blocks, so
termination is finite.  The stable quotient has the stated universal property.
The accepted branch probabilities and target quotient classes are constant on
its fibres, which makes the displayed kernel well defined.  Summing the
resolved branches whose target lies in a prescribed quotient class gives the
probability of that post-accepted Read, proving uniqueness.
\end{proof}


\begin{definition}[Stationary accepted joint table and residuals]
\label{def:accepted-joint-table}
Let
\[
 J_{xy}=\Pr(X_0=x,X_1=y\mid\mathrm{acc})
\]
be a finite stationary accepted initial--terminal table with faithful marginal
$\mu$, and put $D_\mu=\operatorname{diag}(\mu)$.  Define
\[
 \Delta_{\rm marg}
 =\|J\one-\mu\|_2^2+\|J^*\one-\mu\|_2^2,
\]
\[
 \Delta_{\rm rev}=\|J-J^*\|_{\rm HS}^2,
 \qquad
 \Delta_{\rm idem}=\|JD_\mu^{-1}J-J\|_{\rm HS}^2.
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Accepted-table reconstruction of a Gibbs partition projection]
\label{thm:accepted-joint-table}
The three residuals of \Cref{def:accepted-joint-table} vanish if and only if
\[
 R=D_\mu^{-1}J
\]
is a stochastic, $\mu$-reversible, idempotent Markov kernel.  On that branch
there is a unique partition $\mathscr P$ of the accepted field space such that
\[
 \boxed{
 R_{xy}=\one_{\{C(x)=C(y)\}}
 \frac{\mu_y}{\mu(C(x))},
 \qquad
 J_{xy}=\one_{\{C(x)=C(y)\}}
 \frac{\mu_x\mu_y}{\mu(C(x))}.}
\]
The blocks are the connected components of the support graph $J_{xy}>0$.
The same table reconstructs the stationary free action
\[
 \boxed{\mathcal F_J(x)=-\log\mu_x}
\]
up to an additive constant and, on every supported transition,
\[
 \boxed{
 \log\frac{R_{xy}}{R_{yx}}
 +\mathcal F_J(y)-\mathcal F_J(x)=0.}
\]
Thus a separate free-action-increment column is redundant on the reversible
accepted branch.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The marginal residual makes $R$ stochastic and stationary for $\mu$.
Symmetry of $J=D_\mu R$ is detailed balance, and the idempotency residual is
exactly $R^2-R$ after multiplication by $D_\mu$.  A reversible idempotent
kernel is an orthogonal projection in $L^2(\mu)$ which is also positive and
unital.  Its range is therefore a finite function algebra, hence the functions
constant on the blocks of a unique partition.  Orthogonal projection onto that
algebra is conditional expectation, giving the displayed rows.  The support
components recover the blocks because every row is strictly positive on its
own block.  Finally detailed balance gives the logarithmic free-action
identity.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Finite affinity Hodge compiler]
\label{thm:accepted-affinity-Hodge}
For a general bidirected accepted support graph, define the edge affinity
\[
 \ell_{xy}=\log\frac{R_{xy}}{R_{yx}}.
\]
Let $B$ be an oriented incidence matrix and put
\[
 P_{\rm cut}=B^*(BB^*)^\dagger B,
 \qquad P_{\rm cyc}=I-P_{\rm cut}.
\]
Then the following are equivalent:
\[
 \boxed{\ell=-B^*\mathcal F\text{ for some scalar }\mathcal F,}
\]
\[
 \boxed{P_{\rm cyc}\ell=0,}
\]
and vanishing of every cycle affinity.  The canonical least-squares free action
is
\[
 \boxed{\mathcal F_*=-(BB^*)^\dagger B\ell,}
\]
and
\[
 \boxed{
 \inf_{\mathcal F}\|\ell+B^*\mathcal F\|_2^2
 =\|P_{\rm cyc}\ell\|_2^2.}
\]
A spanning forest reconstructs the candidate potential and one period on each
fundamental cycle completes the audit.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The orthogonal decomposition of edge cochains is
$\C^E=\Ran B^*\oplus\Ker B$.  Projection onto the first summand gives the
Moore--Penrose solution and projection onto the second gives the minimum
residual.  An edge cochain lies in $\Ran B^*$ exactly when all of its cycle
periods vanish.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Protected Reads surviving an accepted projection]
\label{thm:accepted-projection-read-survival}
Let $R_{\mathscr P}$ be the conditional expectation associated with an
accepted partition $\mathscr P$, and let $G$ be a protected physical Read.
Then $R_{\mathscr P}$ preserves every function of $G$ if and only if every
partition block is contained in one fibre of $G$.  If the retained Reads
separate all field configurations, the only preserving idempotent accepted
kernel is the identity.

For the count projection $R_K$ on $M$ exchangeable renewal cells,
\[
 \boxed{R_K\varphi_i=\frac1M\sum_{j=1}^{M}\varphi_j,}
 \qquad
 \boxed{\|(I-R_K)\varphi_i\|_2^2=1-\frac1M.}
\]
Every nonconstant spatial Fourier mode $\Phi_k$ satisfies
\[
 \boxed{R_K\Phi_k=0.}
\]
Hence count equilibration can preserve a local spacetime field only when it
acts on a separate microscopic factor:
\[
 \mathsf X=\mathsf X_{\rm geom}\times\mathsf X_{\rm micro},
 \qquad R=I_{\rm geom}\otimes R_{\rm mix},
\]
up to source-minimal equivalence.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Conditional expectation fixes a function exactly when it is measurable with
respect to the partition algebra.  This is equivalent to constancy on each
partition block and proves the first claim.  Exchangeability gives
$\mathbb E[\varphi_i\mid K]=M^{-1}\sum_j\varphi_j$; orthogonality and unit
variance give the norm formula.  A nonconstant Fourier coefficient sums to
zero and is orthogonal to every function of the count, proving its
annihilation.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Exact first-chaos spectrum and projection--persistence tradeoff]
\label{thm:projection-persistence-tradeoff}
For the unmodulated flip--interchange regulator on the three-torus,
\[
 \mathcal L_N^0\Phi_N(c)
 =\Phi_N\left(\kappa_NN^2\Delta_Nc-\frac{22\lambda_N}{15}c\right).
\]
A Fourier mode $e_{k,N}$ has decay rate
\[
 \boxed{
 \Lambda_{k,N}=\frac{22\lambda_N}{15}
 +4\kappa_NN^2\sum_{j=1}^{3}\sin^2\frac{\pi k_j}{N}.}
\]
Put
\[
 q_N=4\frac{\kappa_N}{\lambda_N}N^2\sin^2\frac\pi N.
\]
For the actual completed-private dwell, the operator-norm error of pure
interchange relative to the count projection obeys
\[
 \boxed{
 \varepsilon_N^{\rm proj}\ge
 E(q_N):=\frac{8/15}{(q_N+4/5)(q_N+2/3)}.}
\]
The renewal-clock persistence of the first nonconstant spatial mode is
\[
 \boxed{A_N(s)=\exp\left[-s\left(\frac{22}{15}+q_N\right)\right].}
\]
If $0<\varepsilon_N^{\rm proj}\le\varepsilon\le1$, then
\[
 \boxed{
 q_N\ge\frac{\sqrt{1+120/\varepsilon}-11}{15},}
\]
and therefore
\[
 \boxed{
 A_N(s)\le
 \exp\left[-\frac{s}{15}
 \left(11+\sqrt{1+120/\varepsilon}\right)\right].}
\]
In particular, projection accuracy tending to zero and persistence of one
nonconstant spatial mode for a positive renewal time are incompatible.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The first-chaos generator follows by combining the local renewal eigenvalue
$-22\lambda_N/15$ with the discrete exchange Laplacian.  The completed-private
dwell has generating function
$8z^2/[(5-z)(3-z)]$; applying spectral calculus to the slowest nonconstant
interchange eigenvalue gives $E(q_N)$.  The persistence formula is the same
first-chaos eigenvalue expressed in renewal time.  Solving
$E(q_N)\le\varepsilon$ for $q_N\ge0$ and substituting it in $A_N(s)$ gives the
last two inequalities.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Singular two-clock limit]
\label{thm:renewal-interchange-two-clock}
Assume $\kappa_N/\lambda_N\to\infty$.  For every smooth test profile $f$:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.8em]
\item on the fast clock $t=\sigma/\kappa_N$,
      \[
       \boxed{
       e^{(\sigma/\kappa_N)\mathcal L_N^0}\Phi_N(f)
       \longrightarrow\Phi_N(e^{\sigma\Delta}f);}
      \]
\item on the slow renewal clock $t=s/\lambda_N$, $s>0$,
      \[
       \boxed{
       e^{(s/\lambda_N)\mathcal L_N^0}\Phi_N(f)
       \longrightarrow e^{-22s/15}\Phi_N(\overline f).}
      \]
\end{enumerate}
Thus the count projection is a fast nuisance reduction followed by a slow
scalar count relaxation.  It is not a local reaction--diffusion evolution on
the same slow clock.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Use the exact Fourier spectrum of
\Cref{thm:projection-persistence-tradeoff}.  On the fast clock the reaction
factor tends to one and each fixed Fourier exchange factor tends to the heat
multiplier.  On the slow clock every nonzero spatial mode has exponent
$-s(\kappa_N/\lambda_N)4\pi^2|k|^2+o(1)$ and vanishes, while the zero mode
retains the reaction multiplier $e^{-22s/15}$.
\end{proof}

\begin{assessment}[Free action and the accepted-field boundary]
The accepted stationary table reconstructs its own free-action cochain.  A
Palatini, matter, counterterm, or reference writer enters only through a
same-history comparison with that cochain.  Stationarity of the accepted free
law is therefore weaker than vanishing first variation of an independently
loaded Einstein action.  Likewise, an idempotent count projection and a local
spacetime evolution are different clock-level objects unless the projection
acts only on a protected microscopic factor.
\end{assessment}

Let $\Theta\subset\R^d$ be one compact determining-field chart.  Let
$\Psi\in C^2(\Theta)$ be the operational Fisher potential,
$G(\theta)=\nabla^2\Psi(\theta)$, and assume
\[
 mI\preceq G(\theta)\preceq MI.
\]
Let the reconstructed common action $\mathcal A\in C^2(\Theta)$ satisfy
\[
 -\lambda G(\theta)\preceq D^2\mathcal A(\theta)
 \preceq L G(\theta),
 \qquad \eta\lambda<1.
\]
For
\[
 D_\Psi(y,\theta)
 =\Psi(y)-\Psi(\theta)
  -\langle\nabla\Psi(\theta),y-\theta\rangle,
\]
define
\[
 \Phi_\theta(y)=\mathcal A(y)+\eta^{-1}D_\Psi(y,\theta),
 \qquad y_\theta^*=\arg\min_y\Phi_\theta(y).
\]

\begin{definition}[Accepted Fisher--Bregman action gap]
\label{def:accepted-action-gap}
For one observed accepted transition $\theta\to y$, put
\[
 \boxed{
 \Delta_\Psi(\theta,y)
 :=\Phi_\theta(y)-\Phi_\theta(y_\theta^*)\ge0.}
\]
If the complete feedback kernel is
$K=(1-\vartheta)I+\vartheta K^{\rm acc}$ with state-independent
$\vartheta>0$ and stationary law $\nu$, define
\[
 \boxed{
 \overline\Delta_\Psi
 :=\int\nu(\dd\theta)K^{\rm acc}(\dd y\mid\theta)
       \Delta_\Psi(\theta,y).}
\]
The supported stationarity form is
\[
 \mathfrak S(\theta)
 :=\nabla\mathcal A(\theta)^*G(\theta)^{-1}
   \nabla\mathcal A(\theta).
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Accepted Bregman gap forces common-action stationarity]
\label{thm:accepted-Bregman-stationarity}
Put
\[
 \Lambda_\Phi=(\eta^{-1}+L)M,
 \qquad \ell=\max\{\lambda,L\}.
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{
 \int D_\Psi(y,\theta)\,
       \nu(\dd\theta)K^{\rm acc}(\dd y\mid\theta)
 \le\eta\overline\Delta_\Psi,}
\]
\[
 \boxed{
 \int\|y-\theta\|^2\,
       \nu(\dd\theta)K^{\rm acc}(\dd y\mid\theta)
 \le\frac{2\eta}{m}\overline\Delta_\Psi,}
\]
and
\[
 \boxed{
 \int\mathfrak S(\theta)\,\nu(\dd\theta)
 \le C_{\Psi,\mathcal A,\eta}\overline\Delta_\Psi,}
\]
where
\[
 \boxed{
 C_{\Psi,\mathcal A,\eta}
 =\frac{4\Lambda_\Phi}{m}
  +\frac{4M^2(1+\eta\ell)^2}{m^2\eta}.}
\]
In particular, $\overline\Delta_\Psi=0$ forces the complete represented
common-action first variation to vanish $\nu$-almost surely.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Stationarity of $K$ and state independence of acceptance give
$\nu K^{\rm acc}=\nu$.  Since $y_\theta^*$ minimizes $\Phi_\theta$,
\[
 \mathcal A(y)-\mathcal A(\theta)
 +\eta^{-1}D_\Psi(y,\theta)
 \le\Delta_\Psi(\theta,y).
\]
Averaging cancels the action difference and proves the first estimate.  The
metric floor gives $D_\Psi(y,\theta)\ge(m/2)\|y-\theta\|^2$, proving the
second.

The KKT residual
\[
 r_\Psi(\theta,y)
 =\nabla\Psi(y)-\nabla\Psi(\theta)+\eta\nabla\mathcal A(y)
\]
satisfies
$\|r_\Psi\|^2\le2\eta^2\Lambda_\Phi\Delta_\Psi$ by smooth convexity of
$\Phi_\theta$.  Moreover
\[
 \eta\nabla\mathcal A(\theta)
 =r_\Psi-\bigl(\nabla\Psi(y)-\nabla\Psi(\theta)\bigr)
 +\eta\bigl(\nabla\mathcal A(\theta)-\nabla\mathcal A(y)\bigr).
\]
The Hessian bounds control the two differences by $M\|y-\theta\|$ and
$\ell M\|y-\theta\|$.  Squaring in the inverse Fisher metric, integrating,
and using the first two bounds gives the displayed constant.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Finite Gibbs/KL accepted-row certificate]
\label{cor:accepted-Gibbs-gap}
Let $p_\theta(y)>0$ be the pre-update reference law on a finite terminal field
record and let $c_\theta(y)$ be the independently reconstructed same-history
common-action cost.  Then
\[
 \boxed{
 q_\theta^*(y)
 =\frac{p_\theta(y)e^{-\eta c_\theta(y)}}
        {\sum_zp_\theta(z)e^{-\eta c_\theta(z)}}}
\]
is the unique entropy-proximal row, and
\[
 \boxed{
 \Delta_{{\rm Gibbs},\theta}
 :=\eta^{-1}D_{\rm KL}
   \bigl(K^{\rm acc}(\cdot\mid\theta)\Vert q_\theta^*\bigr)}
\]
is exactly the row-wise action gap.  Its stationary average is an instance of
$\overline\Delta_\Psi$ and vanishes precisely when the observed likelihood
ratio obeys the common-action Gibbs identity.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
For a probability row $q$,
\[
 \sum_yq(y)c_\theta(y)+\eta^{-1}D_{\rm KL}(q\Vert p_\theta)
 =\eta^{-1}D_{\rm KL}(q\Vert q_\theta^*)
  -\eta^{-1}\log\sum_zp_\theta(z)e^{-\eta c_\theta(z)}.
\]
Relative entropy is nonnegative and vanishes only at equality.  The
negative-entropy Fisher potential identifies this row gap with the Bregman gap
of \Cref{def:accepted-action-gap}.
\end{proof}

\begin{countertheorem}[The accepted renewal bit does not determine a field kernel]
\label{cth:accepted-bit-no-field-kernel}
Fix any state-independent acceptance probability and any two-state determining
field.  The identity accepted kernel and an arbitrary full-support reset kernel
are both idempotent and produce exactly the same acceptance/no-acceptance
record, first-acceptance law, and accepted-count pressure, while their terminal
field laws and common-action Gibbs gaps are generally different.  Hence the
locked accepted-response record alone does not determine the accepted
spacetime-field operation.
\end{countertheorem}

\begin{proof}
Let $K_0^{\rm acc}=I$ and let every row of $K_1^{\rm acc}$ equal one fixed
full-support law $\rho$.  Then $K_0^2=K_0$ and $K_1^2=K_1$.  Apply either map
only after the same state-independent accepted mark and apply the identity on
rejection.  Discarding the terminal field gives the same Bernoulli acceptance
process and all the same renewal-time statistics.  The terminal laws differ.
For a nonconstant independently fixed cost, the identity and reset rows cannot
both equal the same Gibbs comparator for every initial state, so their KL gaps
differ.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[The action cost is not fitted from the observed kernel]
The Gibbs or Bregman certificate is physical only when the terminal cost is the
common gravitational--matter--gauge--potential--counterterm--boundary action
reconstructed from the protected reward packet.  Every positive transition can
be written as a Gibbs tilt for a cost chosen afterward; such a fitted cost has
no stationarity content.
\end{firewall}


% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
\subsubsection{Derivative-free face linearization, memory shorting, and torsion control}
\label{sec:renewal-Palatini-upgrade}
% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

The localized gravitational score is evaluated after the persistent geometric
carrier has been fixed and every resolved cut-memory coordinate has been
retained.  Binary renewal divisibility then replaces an assumed derivative at
the zero face, while the connection Euler source replaces an assumed
vanishing torsion.

\begin{theorem}[Derivative-free renewal face linearization]
\label{thm:renewal-face-linearization}
Let $E$ be a finite-dimensional real normed space, let $U\subset E$ be a
balanced convex neighborhood of zero, and let $A:U\to\R$ satisfy $A(0)=0$.
Assume
\[
 \boxed{A(z)=2A(z/2)}
\]
for every $z\in U$, that $A$ is bounded on a neighborhood of zero, and that
for some $r,H>0$,
\[
 \boxed{
 |A(x+y)-A(x)-A(y)|\le H\|x\|\,\|y\|}
\]
whenever $x,y,x+y\in U$ and their norms are at most $r$.  Then $A$ is the
restriction of a unique real linear functional on $E$.

More generally, let
\[
 L_m(z)=2^mA_m(2^{-m}z)
\]
be renormalized face scores on a fixed bounded balanced set.  If
\[
 |L_{m+1}(z)-L_m(z)|\le\varepsilon_m\|z\|,
 \qquad \sum_m\varepsilon_m<\infty,
\]
\[
 |L_m(x+y)-L_m(x)-L_m(y)|
 \le\eta_m\|x\|\,\|y\|,
 \qquad \eta_m\longrightarrow0,
\]
and one $L_m$ is continuous at zero, then $L_m$ converges locally uniformly
to one continuous linear functional $L$, with
\[
 \boxed{
 |L(z)-L_m(z)|
 \le\left(\sum_{n\ge m}\varepsilon_n\right)\|z\|.}
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
For the exact branch, iterate the divisibility relation.  For all sufficiently
large $m$,
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 A(x+y)-A(x)-A(y)
 &=2^m\bigl[A(2^{-m}(x+y))-A(2^{-m}x)-A(2^{-m}y)\bigr],
 \end{aligned}
\]
whose absolute value is at most
$H2^{-m}\|x\|\,\|y\|$.  Letting $m\to\infty$ proves additivity.  An additive
map bounded on a neighborhood of zero is continuous there; rational
homogeneity and continuity then give real homogeneity.  Uniqueness follows
because $U$ contains a neighborhood of zero.

For the stable branch, telescoping gives
\[
 |L_n(z)-L_m(z)|
 \le\left(\sum_{j=m}^{n-1}\varepsilon_j\right)\|z\|,
\]
so $(L_m)$ is locally uniformly Cauchy and has the displayed tail bound.
Passing to the limit in the polarized estimate proves additivity.  The
summable transport bound transfers continuity from one $L_m$ to the limit,
and a continuous additive map on $E$ is linear.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Complete classical--quantum cut-memory short]
\label{thm:renewal-memory-cumulant}
Let a resolved finite cut-memory coordinate have faithful classical--quantum
state and linear face perturbation
\[
 \rho_{\rm cq}=\bigoplus_{\omega}p_\omega\rho_\omega,
 \qquad
 K_{\rm cq}(z)=\bigoplus_\omega K_\omega(z),
\]
where $p_\omega>0$, $\sum_\omega p_\omega=1$, and every $\rho_\omega$ is
faithful on its support.  Put
\[
 m_\omega(x)=\Tr(\rho_\omega K_\omega(x)),
 \qquad
 \bar m(x)=\sum_\omega p_\omega m_\omega(x),
\]
\[
 \widetilde K_\omega(x)
 =K_\omega(x)-m_\omega(x)I,
\]
and define the complete memory log-partition
\[
 \boxed{
 M_{\rm cq}(z)
 =\log\Tr\exp(\log\rho_{\rm cq}+K_{\rm cq}(z))-\bar m(z).}
\]
Then $M_{\rm cq}(0)=0$, $DM_{\rm cq}(0)=0$, and
\[
 \boxed{
 \begin{aligned}
 D^2M_{\rm cq}(0)[x,y]
 ={}&\sum_\omega p_\omega
 (m_\omega(x)-\bar m(x))(m_\omega(y)-\bar m(y))\\
 &+\sum_\omega p_\omega\int_0^1
 \Tr\!\left(
 \rho_\omega^s\widetilde K_\omega(x)
 \rho_\omega^{1-s}\widetilde K_\omega(y)
 \right)\dd s.
 \end{aligned}}
\]
Both summands are positive.  They vanish identically exactly when all branch
mean slopes agree and every quantum perturbation is scalar on its support.
If $A_{\rm coarse}$ is the logarithmic face score after the memory mark has
been forgotten, then
\[
 \boxed{A_{\rm sh}=A_{\rm coarse}-M_{\rm cq}}
\]
is the canonical fully memory-shorted face score.  The subtraction removes
the complete memory log-partition, not only its quadratic Taylor coefficient.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The block exponential and trace split over the classical label.  For a single
faithful block the Duhamel formula
\[
 D e^B[C]=\int_0^1e^{(1-s)B}Ce^{sB}\,\dd s
\]
gives first derivative $\Tr(\rho K(x))$ and second logarithmic derivative
\[
 \int_0^1\Tr(\rho^s\widetilde K(x)
 \rho^{1-s}\widetilde K(y))\,\dd s.
\]
Differentiating the outer finite log-sum-exp adds the covariance of the branch
means.  Diagonalizing each $\rho_\omega$ shows that every coefficient in the
Kubo--Mori quadratic form is strictly positive; hence its zero directions are
precisely the scalar perturbations.  The covariance zero criterion follows
from faithfulness of the finite classical weights.  The final identity is the
definition of the orthogonal memory removal at the level of the complete
log-partition.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Connection stationarity and the torsion alternative]
\label{thm:Palatini-torsion}
Let $e^I$ be a nondegenerate four-dimensional coframe, let $\omega^{IJ}$ be a
metric-compatible Cartan connection, and put
\[
 B^{IJ}=e^I\wedge e^J,
 \qquad T^I=De^I,
 \qquad P_{\alpha,\beta}=\alpha\star+\beta I.
\]
If $(\alpha,\beta)\ne(0,0)$, then
\[
 \boxed{
 P_{\alpha,\beta}^{-1}
 =\frac{\beta I-\alpha\star}{\alpha^2+\beta^2}.}
\]
For the Palatini--Holst action and matter spin current $\Sigma^{IJ}$, the
connection Euler equation is
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal E_\omega^{IJ}
 =-D(P_{\alpha,\beta}B)^{IJ}-\Sigma^{IJ}=0.}
\]
The Cartan map
\[
 \mathcal K_e(T)^{IJ}=T^I\wedge e^J-e^I\wedge T^J
\]
is injective.  Consequently, on the spinless branch, connection stationarity
implies $T=0$; with spin it gives the unique Einstein--Cartan torsion sourced
by $\Sigma$.  At finite cutoff, if
$\sigma_{\min}(\mathcal K_{e,X})\ge\kappa_*>0$, then
\[
 \boxed{
 \|T_X\|
 \le\kappa_*^{-1}\|P_{\alpha_X,\beta_X}^{-1}\|
 \bigl(\|\mathcal E_{\omega,X}\|+\|\Sigma_X\|\bigr).}
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The inverse formula follows from $\star^2=-I$.  Varying the connection and
integrating by parts gives the displayed Euler source, since $\star$ is
Lorentz natural and commutes with $D$.  To prove injectivity, expand
$T^I=\frac12T^I{}_{KL}e^K\wedge e^L$ in the coframe basis.  In
$T^I\wedge e^J-e^I\wedge T^J=0$, choosing $J$ distinct from $I,K,L$ first
forces $T^I{}_{KL}=0$ whenever $K,L\ne I$.  The remaining coefficients
$t_{I,K}=T^I{}_{IK}$ obey $t_{I,K}+t_{J,K}=0$ for all distinct $I,J,K$;
using three indices different from $K$ forces all of them to vanish.  Thus
$DB=0$ implies $T=0$.  Inverting $P_{\alpha,\beta}$ and then the Cartan map
gives the finite norm estimate and the stated torsion alternatives.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[Renewal is localized, not a transparent reset of spacetime]
A complete replacement channel has superoperator rank one, whereas a nontrivial
reversible channel on $M_d(\C)$ has superoperator rank $d^2$.  Pre- and
post-processing cannot increase the rank of a replacement channel.  Therefore
a complete renewal replacement cannot be transparent inside the full
reversible spacetime history.  Every subdivision hypothesis below acts on the
relative action or residual-multiplicity carrier while the persistent geometric
algebra is fixed pointwise.
\end{firewall}

\begin{theorem}[Localized renewal--Palatini insertion]
\label{thm:Palatini}
Let $Z_X$ be the integrated Cartan-completed chronological face coordinate on
a compact spacetime cylinder.  Assume:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(E\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item after the complete classical--quantum correction of
      \Cref{thm:renewal-memory-cumulant} has been subtracted, the protected
      binary face subdivision satisfies either the exact or the summably
      stable hypotheses of \Cref{thm:renewal-face-linearization};
\item the resulting linear face score is real and Lorentz natural, its
      commutators with the complete typed internal action vanish in the limit,
      and the residual typed-history commutant on the selected face carrier is
      scalar;
\item determinant coframe volume is represented, the Palatini--Holst
      coefficient pair is uniformly nonzero, and the connection Euler and
      matter spin-current sources satisfy the torsion alternative of
      \Cref{thm:Palatini-torsion};
\item the compact spatial packet gives
      $e_X\to e$ strongly in $L^2_{\rm loc}$ and
      $\sup_X\|e_X\|_{L^6(K)}<\infty$ on every compact $K$, while the actual
      chronological curvature satisfies
      $R_X\rightharpoonup R$ weakly in $L^p_{\rm loc}$ for some $p>3/2$.
\end{enumerate}
Then the fully memory-shorted primitive gravitational score has the unique
form
\[
 \boxed{
 \alpha L_{\rm Holst}+\beta L_{\rm Palatini}+\lambda L_{\rm vol}.}
\]
On the spinless connection-stationary branch, torsion tends to zero and, for
every compactly supported inverse-metric test $k^{\mu\nu}$, the metric first
variation converges to
\[
 \boxed{
 \chi\int_K\sqrt{-g}\,
 (G_{\mu\nu}+\Lambda g_{\mu\nu})k^{\mu\nu}.}
\]
With a nonzero represented spin current, the same hypotheses give the
corresponding controlled Einstein--Cartan insertion.  No independently
discretized Einstein tensor, Frechet derivative at the zero face, or assumed
torsion-free connection is used.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The first hypothesis and \Cref{thm:renewal-face-linearization} give one unique
real linear primitive after the complete memory log-partition has been
removed.  Both coframe bivectors and Lorentz curvature lie in
$\Lambda^2\R^{1,3}$.  After complexification this module splits into the
nonisomorphic self-dual and anti-self-dual irreducible modules.  Schur's lemma
therefore gives
\[
 \End_{SO^+(1,3)}(\Lambda^2\R^{1,3})
 =\Span_{\R}\{I,\star\}.
\]
The scalar typed commutant excludes an additional internal tensor.  The only
alternating Lorentz-invariant four-coframe scalar is determinant volume, so
the displayed Palatini--Holst--volume classification follows.

The connection statement is \Cref{thm:Palatini-torsion}.  On the spinless
stationary branch, the first Bianchi identity makes the Holst coframe
variation locally inert, while the Palatini and determinant-volume variations
give the Einstein and cosmological insertions.

It remains to pass the product to the limit.  If $p'=p/(p-1)$, the strict
inequality $p>3/2$ gives $2p'<6$.  Interpolation between strong $L^2$ and the
uniform $L^6$ bound yields $e_X\to e$ strongly in $L^{2p'}$.  Hence
\[
 \|e_X\wedge e_X-e\wedge e\|_{L^{p'}}
 \le C(\|e_X\|_{L^{2p'}}+\|e\|_{L^{2p'}})
       \|e_X-e\|_{L^{2p'}}\longrightarrow0.
\]
Pairing this strongly convergent bivector with the weakly convergent
$L^p$ curvature passes both Palatini and Holst terms.  Strong $L^4$
convergence also passes determinant volume in $L^1$.  Contracting the coframe
Euler form with the symmetric coframe lift of $k^{\mu\nu}$ gives the displayed
metric insertion.
\end{proof}

\begin{assessment}[Higher-curvature status]
A nonzero scalar second face derivative is not automatically a primitive
higher-curvature interaction.  Unresolved cut memory produces explicit
classical or quantum cumulants even when every resolved sector is face linear.
Only the residual after polarized memory reconstruction and cumulant subtraction
is a primitive composite-face source.
\end{assessment}

\begin{theorem}[Compact positive-screen coercive upgrade]
\label{thm:SMST-positive-screen}
Fix a compact spacetime cylinder $K$ and identify all cutoff quadratic packets
with one Hilbert space $\mathcal Y_K$.  Let $Y_h\rightharpoonup Y$ weakly and let
$\mathbb A_h$ be positive operators satisfying
\[
 mI\preceq\mathbb A_h\preceq MI,
 \qquad \mathbb A_h^{-1/2}\longrightarrow\mathbb A^{-1/2}
 \quad\text{strongly},
\]
with $0<m\le M<\infty$.  Put $Z_h=\mathbb A_h^{1/2}Y_h$ and assume
$Z_h\rightharpoonup Z=\mathbb A^{1/2}Y$.

For every radius $R$, suppose there are operators $S_{h,R}$ and a compact
operator $S_R$ on $\mathcal Y_K$ such that
\[
 \|S_{h,R}-S_R\|\longrightarrow0,
 \qquad
 \lim_{R\to\infty}\sup_h\|(I-S_{h,R})Z_h\|=0,
\]
and the same tail condition holds for $Z$.  Then
\[
 \boxed{Z_h\to Z\text{ strongly},\qquad Y_h\to Y\text{ strongly in }\mathcal Y_K.}
\]
In the spacetime application
\[
 Y_h=(K_h,u_h,\nabla\phi_h),
 \qquad \mathbb A_h=|\mathbb K_h|\oplus\mathbb Q_h,
\]
so every quadratic insertion converges in $L^1(K)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
For fixed $R$, compactness of $S_R$ converts weak convergence into strong
convergence: $S_RZ_h\to S_RZ$.  Operator-norm convergence of $S_{h,R}$ gives
$S_{h,R}Z_h-S_RZ_h\to0$ because $(Z_h)$ is bounded.  Hence
$S_{h,R}Z_h\to S_RZ$ strongly.  Decompose
\[
 Z_h-Z=(I-S_{h,R})Z_h+(S_{h,R}Z_h-S_RZ)+(S_R-I)Z.
\]
Taking the limsup in $h$ and then $R\to\infty$ proves $Z_h\to Z$ strongly.
Uniform coercivity bounds $\|\mathbb A_h^{-1/2}\|\le m^{-1/2}$.  Therefore
\[
 \|Y_h-Y\|
 \le m^{-1/2}\|Z_h-Z\|
 +\|(\mathbb A_h^{-1/2}-\mathbb A^{-1/2})Z\|\longrightarrow0.
\]
For a quadratic tensor $Q(Y)=B(Y,Y)$ with bounded local coefficient $B$,
\[
 \|Q(Y_h)-Q(Y)\|_{L^1}
 \le C\|Y_h-Y\|_{L^2}
      (\|Y_h\|_{L^2}+\|Y\|_{L^2}),
\]
which gives the final claim.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Regenerative construction of the spacetime positive screen]
\label{cor:SMST-regenerative-screen}
Assume the spacetime shorted Hodge/action form is the energy $V_h$ in
\Cref{thm:renewal-Lyapunov-tightness}, and is identified with the quadratic
packet $\mathbb A_h$ by a uniformly faithful Legendre--conductance comparison.
Assume either the compact domination of \Cref{thm:renewal-shorted-Hodge} or the
spatial pressure-flow screen of \Cref{cor:renewal-spatial-positive-screen}.  Then
the fixed-radius screens and uniform tail exhaustion required in
\Cref{thm:SMST-positive-screen} hold for every bounded-action sequence and in
the stationary cycle states.  Consequently the strong local $L^2$ and
quadratic-insertion conclusions of that theorem follow without a separately
postulated screen family.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The shorted Hodge theorem gives deterministic high-energy tails for every
bounded-action vector, while the compact Lyapunov theorem gives the same tail
bound in the stationary state.  Uniform Legendre--conductance equivalence
transfers both estimates to $\mathbb A_h^{1/2}Y_h$.  The fixed spectral screens
have uniformly bounded rank and converge on each fixed compact energy window,
so \Cref{thm:SMST-positive-screen} applies.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[Weak energy bounds do not remove concentration]
Weak $L^2$ convergence and a uniform quadratic-energy bound do not imply
convergence of quadratic insertions.  An orthonormal sequence converges weakly
to zero while its squared $L^1$ norm remains one.  The compact fixed-radius
screens and uniform tail exhaustion in \Cref{thm:SMST-positive-screen} are the
mechanism excluding this defect.
\end{firewall}

\begin{theorem}[Conditional local weak Einstein--matter handoff]
\label{thm:Einstein-handoff}
Assume one regulator sequence satisfies the loaded Clifford, metric-volume,
clock--geometry, Cartan, coherent HDA, typed matter--Legendre, incidence,
finite-Dirac, and localized Palatini packets.  On every compact cylinder $K$,
assume additionally:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(V\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item the gravitational, matter, gauge, potential, counterterm, and relevant
      boundary cycle rewards are protected on one resolved first-return record;
      their table-derived renewal pressure satisfies the physical
      pressure--duration calibration, and the pressure jet of
      \Cref{thm:reward-pressure-jet} has regulator-compatible limits;
\item the complete sector action increments pass the face-curl and period tests
      of \Cref{thm:common-action-exactness}, so they are derivatives of one
      scalar common action after one physical anchor is fixed;
\item the positive-screen hypotheses of \Cref{thm:SMST-positive-screen} hold for
      the complete quadratic packet, either directly, through
      \Cref{cor:SMST-regenerative-screen}, or through the spatial pressure-flow
      branch of \Cref{cor:renewal-spatial-positive-screen};
\item the potential Radon--Nikodym and allowed counterterm sources satisfy
      \Cref{thm:potential-counterterm-exactness}, and their protected values and
      first derivatives converge on the compact field and variation screens;
\item after the declared martingale source is shorted, every fast loaded
      feedback correction of \Cref{thm:fast-feedback-collapse} and every
      retained finite low-mode completion of
      \Cref{thm:continuum-memory-completion,cor:finite-resolution-memory} is
      included in the common action; the remaining actual-cycle/action defect
      is $o(\tau_X)$ per physical step and the residual high-energy memory tail
      tends to zero on compact time windows;
\item for the direct and physically relabelled total-action source syntheses
      $F_X^{\rm dir}$ and $F_X^{\rm rel}$ at relabeling step
      $\varepsilon_X$, the positive coherent Ward Gram obeys
      \[
       \boxed{
       \mathbb W_X
       =(F_X^{\rm rel}-F_X^{\rm dir})^*
        (F_X^{\rm rel}-F_X^{\rm dir}),
       \qquad
       \|\mathbb W_X\|=o(\varepsilon_X^2);}
      \]
      and one protected metric--matter variation panel $C_X$ satisfies
      $C_X^*C_X\succeq c_*G_{E,X}$ with $c_*>0$, while its total first-variation
      residual tends to zero.
\end{enumerate}
Then, after passage to the selected cofinal subsequence, there is one limiting
common-action first variation and, for every compactly supported represented
matter variation $\psi$ and symmetric metric variation $k$, one has
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal E_{\phi}^{\rm kin}(\psi)
 +\mathcal E_{\phi}^{\rm gauge}(\psi)
 +\int_K\sqrt{-g}\,\langle F(\phi),\psi\rangle
 +\mathcal E_{\phi}^{\rm ct}(\psi)=0,}
\]
\[
 \boxed{
 \chi\int_K\sqrt{-g}\,
 (G_{\mu\nu}+\Lambda g_{\mu\nu})k^{\mu\nu}
 +\mathcal T_g^{\rm ren}(k)=0.}
\]
If the limiting metric panel is determining and
\[
 \mathcal T_g^{\rm ren}(k)
 =-\frac12\int_K\sqrt{-g}\,
 T_{\mu\nu}^{\rm ren}k^{\mu\nu},
\]
then
\[
 \boxed{
 2\chi(G_{\mu\nu}+\Lambda g_{\mu\nu})
 =T_{\mu\nu}^{\rm ren}}
\]
holds distributionally.  On the canonical scalar kinetic branch the matter
identity is
\[
 \boxed{\Box_g\phi^A-\partial_AV(\phi)=0.}
\]
The limiting Ward identity gives $\nabla^\mu T_{\mu\nu}^{\rm ren}=0$ on matter
shell.  The coefficient $2\chi$ is the physically reconstructed Palatini
normalization and is not fixed by the universal structural tensor.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The pressure normalization and \Cref{thm:reward-pressure-reconstruction}
reconstruct the complete uncentered action slope from the normalized scores
and protected duration.  The pressure jet reconstructs every marginal and
mixed action Gram, so the sector sum has one operationally fixed relative
orientation.  The curl and period conditions then integrate the finite action
increments into one scalar common action.

By \Cref{thm:SMST-positive-screen}, the metric velocity, matter normal velocity,
and matter gradient converge strongly in local $L^2$; all quadratic kinetic,
gradient, and stress insertions therefore converge in local $L^1$.  The
potential force is the exact logarithmic Radon--Nikodym derivative, while the
counterterm theorem identifies the exact local derivative and separates any
irreducible Schur residual.  Their assumed compact-screen convergence passes
the corresponding first variations.

The primitive accepted-response phase already satisfies the required
physical-time comparison by \Cref{thm:accepted-phase-feedback}.  For a loaded
regulator, \Cref{thm:fast-feedback-collapse} absorbs every vanishing-delay
kernel into the local generator, while
\Cref{thm:Hodge-feedback-tail,thm:feedback-Hankel-Weyl} reduce the remaining
Hodge-dominated memory to finitely many retained low modes and a uniformly
vanishing high-energy tail.  Once those retained modes are included in the
common action, the actual cycle and action semigroup agree on compact
physical-time windows.

For a bounded terminal score $\lambda_X$, Cauchy--Schwarz gives
\[
 \frac{|\lambda_X((F_X^{\rm rel}-F_X^{\rm dir})v)|}
 {\varepsilon_X}
 \le\|\lambda_X\|\,\|v\|
 \frac{\|\mathbb W_X\|^{1/2}}{\varepsilon_X}\longrightarrow0,
\]
so the infinitesimal coherent Ward anomaly vanishes.  If
$e_X=G_{E,X}^{-1}\gamma_X$ is the Riesz vector of the total first variation,
the determining-panel floor yields
\[
 \|e_X\|_{G_{E,X}}^2
 \le c_*^{-1}\|C_Xe_X\|^2\longrightarrow0.
\]
Thus the finite common-action first variations vanish in the limit.

Finally \Cref{thm:Palatini} supplies the gravitational insertion, while the
convergent matter, potential, gauge, and counterterm sources supply the two
remaining sector sums.  This gives the displayed weak identities.  Density of
the determining metric test panel upgrades the second identity to a
distributional tensor equation.  The limiting relabeling Ward identity is the
diffeomorphism Noether identity; substitution of the matter Euler equation
gives covariant conservation.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Unconditional global-cylinder Einstein-or-obstruction alternative]
\label{thm:global-cylinder-Einstein-alternative}
Let a specified microscopic regulator supply one complete Einstein-ready global
operational cylinder process.  At every cutoff apply:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(C\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item the local source, occurrence, endpoint-locality, $1+3$ connection,
      Hodge--Palatini, common-reward, cutoff, compact-screen, higher-integrability,
      and boundary residuals of the preceding finite theorems;
\item the endpoint coequalizer and efficient-capacity compiler of
      \Cref{def:physical-endpoint-coequalizer,thm:global-spatial-compiler};
\item the minimal determining-field and accepted-kernel compiler of
      \Cref{thm:determining-field-compiler};
\item the same-history action gap of
      \Cref{def:accepted-action-gap}, or its Gibbs/KL specialization
      \Cref{cor:accepted-Gibbs-gap}.
\end{enumerate}
Then every cofinal sequence has exactly the following certification
alternative.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(A\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item If all finite local residuals tend to zero with their declared margins,
      \[
       \boxed{\liminf_X I_X>0,\qquad
              \overline\Delta_{\Psi,X}\longrightarrow0,}
      \]
      and the cutoff, compact-screen, and boundary traces pass, then the same
      sequence has a canonical nontrivial Lorentzian $3+1$ continuum satisfying
      \[
       \boxed{
       2\chi(G_{\mu\nu}+\Lambda g_{\mu\nu})
       =T_{\mu\nu}^{\rm ren}}
      \]
      distributionally on the determining test core, together with the matter
      Euler equations, on-shell Ward conservation, and the declared non-null
      GHY--Brown--York--corner completion.
\item Otherwise the actual cylinder produces at least one explicit obstruction:
      a nonzero finite source/relation/locality/Hodge/action/boundary singular
      vector; an invalid endpoint quotient or zero efficient capacity; the
      normalized pressure cut/potential sequence of
      \Cref{thm:global-spatial-compiler}; a cutoff innovation, soft mode, or
      escaping graph/field/spectral mass; a positive accepted/action Bregman or
      likelihood-ratio row; or a nonzero determining-score or trace innovation.
\end{enumerate}
The implication is unconditional as a certification-or-obstruction theorem.
It does not assert that the marginal local renewal packet forces the positive
branch.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Finite termination and witnesses follow from the structural, source-short,
endpoint, determining-field, and action-gap compilers.  On the positive spatial
branch, \Cref{thm:global-spatial-compiler,thm:operational-Sobolev-Weyl} give
the uniform Sobolev--Poincar\'e floor and compact spatial screens.  The cutoff,
Hodge, and higher-integrability hypotheses then give the strong $L^4$
coframe/connection and weak $L^2$ curvature convergence required by the
Palatini handoff.  The accepted Bregman theorem forces the complete supported
first variation to zero, and score/variation saturation upgrades it to the
determining physical core.  Applying \Cref{thm:Einstein-handoff} and the finite
Stokes--transgression boundary theorem gives the displayed continuum equations.

If a required condition fails, finite-dimensional positivity supplies a
singular vector whenever the failure is local.  Endpoint/capacity failure is a
finite quotient witness; collapse of the cut constant gives the dual pressure
sequence; failure of descent, compactness, or coercivity gives the previously
constructed innovation, mass-escape, or soft-mode sequence; and failure of the
action comparison is the positive Bregman/KL row itself.  These alternatives
are exhaustive.
\end{proof}

\begin{assessment}[Exact unconditional spacetime status]
For the old structural shadow, the strongest universal statement remains
\[
 \boxed{
 \text{complete actual global cylinder}
 \Longrightarrow
 \text{Einstein branch or explicit physical obstruction}.}
\]
The claim that the marginal locked renewal packet alone forces the positive
branch is false: \Cref{cth:local-renewal-no-global-atlas} and
\Cref{cth:accepted-bit-no-field-kernel} exhibit the missing global and
accepted-field information.

The revised definition changes the existence question rather than invalidating
those countermodels.  The future-minimal same-history relation packet is now
part of the repaired primitive, and \Cref{cor:relational-flat-vacuum} gives an
explicit cofinal positive vacuum family for which the endpoint, fast clock,
speed measure, cut, action, and refinement data are all populated.  Hence
unconditional spacetime existence is closed for the explicitly repaired
primitive, while the old countermodels remain the lower-bound proof that this
repair cannot be deleted.  Historical terminal recurrence is only a possible
reuse of the active port and is not a premise of the revised theorem.
\end{assessment}

\begin{firewall}[Local equations do not require a global boundary theorem]
All tests in \Cref{thm:Einstein-handoff} are compactly supported in the
interior.  Boundary-supported total divergences and counterterms have zero
variation on these tests.  Failure of the global packet below does not weaken
the local equations.
\end{firewall}

\begin{theorem}[Global non-null GHY--corner completion]
\label{thm:SMST-global-boundary}
Let $\Omega$ have piecewise smooth non-null boundary faces $F$ and joints $C$.
Assume a boundary-compatible finite chronological Palatini complex with:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(B\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item exact graded Stokes and the same physical coframe and Cartan connection as
      in the bulk;
\item physical unit normals and additive oriented joint angles;
\item one boundary-aware first-variation process tensor whose bulk-to-face,
      face-to-joint, and induced-data trace maps have uniform frame floors;
\item closed canonical face and joint currents, physically attached radial
      primitives, and zero induced-data/Brown--York--corner identity residual;
\item strong induced-metric traces, weak extrinsic-curvature and angle traces,
      and tightness of boundary currents on noncompact faces.
\end{enumerate}
Then the finite global first variation converges to that of
\[
 \boxed{
 \begin{aligned}
 S_{\rm cov}^{\rm glob}={}&S_{\rm cov}^{\rm ren}
 +2\chi\sum_F\varepsilon_F\int_F\sqrt{|\gamma_F|}\,K_F\\
 &+2\chi\sum_C\int_C\sqrt{|\sigma_C|}\,\eta_C.
 \end{aligned}}
\]
The limiting non-null Dirichlet problem has the Brown--York face momentum and
the canonical corner momentum.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The Palatini connection variation is a covariant divergence plus a torsion
term.  Torsion vanishes, and exact finite Stokes sends the divergence to the
boundary current.  Its unique local primitive depending on the first normal jet
is the Cartan transgression
\[
 \chi\int_F\varepsilon_{IJKL}n^Ie^J\wedge e^K\wedge Dn^L
 =2\chi\varepsilon_F\int_F\sqrt{|\gamma|}\,K.
\]
Under oriented gluing, this normal-odd term cancels on an internal face, whereas
an independent normal-even intrinsic face term would double; hence no such
unforced term is part of the canonical gluing primitive.  Smoothing a small cap
at a joint gives $K_{\rm cap}=\dd\eta/\dd s+O(1)$, so the cap limit is
$2\chi\int_C\sqrt{|\sigma|}\eta$.  Additivity of the oriented angle makes this
the unique continuous local joint writer.

Let $T$ be the trace map and $F$ a boundary source map.  The orthogonal
factorization
\[
 F=FT^*(TT^*)^\dagger T+F(I-P_T)
\]
shows that the zero factorization residual makes the boundary and joint currents
determined by the induced traces.  Closedness makes their radial primitives
exact, and physical attachment identifies them with the admitted writers.  The
remaining induced-data source is then unique; the final zero residual identifies
it with the Brown--York, corner, and matter boundary momenta.  These currents
are linear in the weakly convergent extrinsic curvature and angle, while their
metric test coefficients converge strongly.  Tightness prevents boundary mass
from escaping to infinity, completing the limit.
\end{proof}

\subsubsection{Quantum determinant-line handoff and the corrected phase boundary}
\label{sec:SMST-quantum-handoff}

The finite classical action does not by itself choose a chiral measure phase.
The source-native finite-Dirac operator does, however, determine a canonical
gapped reference regulator and makes the remaining phase ambiguity precise.

\begin{theorem}[Canonical graph regulator from the finite-Dirac operator]
\label{thm:SMST-graph-regulator}
Let $D:E\to F$ be the source-native finite-Dirac operator and let $m>0$.  Define
\[
 H_m^+(D)=\begin{pmatrix}mI_E&D^*\\D&-mI_F\end{pmatrix},
 \qquad
 H_m^-(D)=\begin{pmatrix}-mI_E&D^*\\D&mI_F\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{
 (H_m^\pm)^2
 =\operatorname{diag}(D^*D+m^2I_E,DD^*+m^2I_F),}
\]
so both Hamiltonians have spectral gap at least $m$.  Their negative spectral
projectors
\[
 P_m^\pm=\frac12\left(I-H_m^\pm((H_m^\pm)^2)^{-1/2}\right)
\]
are finite functional-calculus outputs of $D$ and are gauge covariant.  The
relative graph line
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathscr L_m^{\rm graph}(D)
 =\det\Ran P_m^+(D)\otimes(\det\Ran P_m^-(D))^*}
\]
is canonically isomorphic to the chiral amplitude line
$(\det E)^*\otimes\det F$.

Put
\[
 R_E=(D^*D+m^2I_E)^{1/2},
 \qquad R_F=(DD^*+m^2I_F)^{1/2}.
\]
In the canonical graph frames its Berry connection is
\[
 \boxed{
 \alpha_m(D)
 =-\operatorname{Im}\Tr_E
 \left[R_E^{-1}(R_E+m)^{-1}D^*\dd D\right].}
\]
For an infinitesimal gauge generator $X=(X_E,X_F)$ its vertical moment is
\[
 \boxed{
 \mu_m^D(X)
 =i\Tr_F\!\left[X_F(I-mR_F^{-1})\right]
 -i\Tr_E\!\left[X_E(I-mR_E^{-1})\right].}
\]
The gauge cocycle of the graph section is nevertheless only the fixed-fibre
character
$\det U_F\det U_E^{-1}$.  Hence the anomaly-free finite SM packet admits a
global gauge-invariant graph measure section.  At positive $m$, ordinary
unweighted anomaly cancellation does not by itself force the connection to be
basic, because the moment is spectrally weighted.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Block multiplication gives the square identity and the gap.  Spectral
functional calculus gives the projectors and their covariance.  The negative
spaces have explicit graph isometries obtained from $R_E,R_F$; taking their
top exterior powers identifies the relative graph line with
$(\det E)^*\otimes\det F$.  Differentiating the graph frames and using
$D f(D^*D)=f(DD^*)D$ gives the connection formula.  Substitution of
$\dd D=X_FD-DX_E$ and cyclicity of trace gives the moment formula.  Exterior
powers show that the gauge action on the line is the stated determinant
character, which is trivial for the complete finite anomaly-free SM packet.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Massless full-rank and zero-mode alternatives]
\label{cor:SMST-graph-massless}
On a constant-rank branch,
\[
 \boxed{\alpha_m(D)\longrightarrow
 -\operatorname{Im}\Tr(D^\dagger\dd D)}
\]
as $m\downarrow0$.  The surviving curvature is the curvature of
\[
 \boxed{(\det\ker D)^*\otimes\det\operatorname{coker}D.}
\]
If $D$ is square and invertible, then
\[
 \boxed{\alpha_0=-\dd\arg\det D,\qquad\Omega_0=0.}
\]
Thus the full-rank massless graph connection is flat after the normalized
determinant phase is included; zero modes carry the exact remaining local
obstruction.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
On the nonzero singular support,
$R_E^{-1}(R_E+m)^{-1}D^*\to(D^*D)^\dagger D^*=D^\dagger$.
Kernel and cokernel exterior powers give the residual determinant line.  In the
invertible square case $D^\dagger=D^{-1}$ and the logarithmic determinant
identity gives the final formula.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Line-valued quantum action and covariant Einstein residual]
\label{thm:SMST-line-valued-Einstein}
Let $(\mathscr L_{\rm ph},\nabla)$ be the total phase line and let
$\mathscr Z_{\rm tot}$ be a nowhere-zero quantum amplitude section.  There is a
unique complex one-form $\Xi_{\mathscr Z}$ such that
\[
 \nabla\mathscr Z_{\rm tot}
 =\Xi_{\mathscr Z}\otimes\mathscr Z_{\rm tot}.
\]
Writing
$\mathscr Z_{\rm tot}=e^{-\mathscr S_{\mathbb R}}s_{\rm ph}$ with
$\|s_{\rm ph}\|=1$ and
$\nabla s_{\rm ph}=i\alpha_{\rm ph}\otimes s_{\rm ph}$ gives
\[
 \boxed{
 -\Xi_{\mathscr Z}
 =\dd\mathscr S_{\mathbb R}-i\alpha_{\rm ph},
 \qquad
 \dd\Xi_{\mathscr Z}=i\Omega_{\rm ph}.}
\]
Thus a globally ordinary scalar effective action exists exactly when the total
phase line has zero curvature and trivial holonomy.  Otherwise the line-valued
amplitude is intrinsic.

Let
\[
 \mathcal E_q^{\mathbb R}
 =2D_q\mathscr S_g-\mathsf T_{\rm cl}-\mathsf T_{\rm mod},
 \qquad
 \mathsf t_{\rm ph}=2\alpha_{\rm ph}|_{T_q\mathcal C}.
\]
For the faithful inverse geometric metric define
\[
 \boxed{
 \Delta_{\rm Ein,q}^{\rm cov}
 =\|\mathcal E_q^{\mathbb R}\|_{G_{\mathcal Q}^{-1}}^2
  +\|\mathsf t_{\rm ph}\|_{G_{\mathcal Q}^{-1}}^2.}
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{
 \Delta_{\rm Ein,q}^{\rm cov}=0
 \iff \mathcal E_q^{\mathbb R}=0
 \text{ and }\mathsf t_{\rm ph}=0.}
\]
A real Einstein-source mismatch cannot cancel a phase stress.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The decomposition of the covariant derivative follows from the Leibniz rule
and metric compatibility of the unit section.  Applying another covariant
derivative gives the curvature identity.  A parallel global unit section exists
exactly on the zero-curvature, trivial-holonomy branch.  The Einstein residual
is the squared norm of the real and imaginary parts of the logarithmic
covariant metric response in the real direct sum; faithfulness proves the
zero criterion and orthogonality proves noncancellation.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Correct dual-line and independent-measure criterion]
\label{thm:SMST-corrected-dual-measure}
For a finite-Dirac family $D:E\to F$, distinguish
\[
 D^c=\overline D:\overline E\to\overline F,
 \qquad
 D^\vee=\overline{D^*}=D^{\mathsf T}:\overline F\to\overline E.
\]
Their graph connections satisfy
\[
 \boxed{
 \alpha_m(D^c)=-\alpha_m(D),
 \qquad
 \alpha_m(D^\vee)=\alpha_m(D),}
\]
and the same sign table holds for curvature and vertical moment.  Hence
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathscr L_m^{\rm graph}(D^c)
 \cong(\mathscr L_m^{\rm graph}(D))^*,
 \qquad
 \mathscr L_m^{\rm graph}(D^\vee)
 \cong\mathscr L_m^{\rm graph}(D).}
\]
The finite real/Nambu completion therefore does not by itself provide a second
cancelling determinant.  Exact complex phase cancellation requires an
independently sourced Berezin factor with block operator $D\oplus\overline D$,
or another independently reconstructed line with the dual connection and
inverse holonomy.  A positive bosonic Gaussian determinant contributes only to
the real modulus and cannot cancel a complex fermionic phase.

A genuinely real/Pfaffian measure line has zero local curvature and local phase
response but may retain a global $\mathbb Z_2$ holonomy.  Its final certificate
is therefore the sign holonomy, not a complex determinant cancellation.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Complex conjugation sends every graph frame and its connection to the complex
conjugate frame, reversing the imaginary trace.  Transpose together with
source--target reversal exchanges the two graph factors and the dual in the
relative-line definition, producing a second copy of the original connection.
For the scalar family $D=se^{i\varphi}$, $D^\vee=D$ and the connection is
nonzero, which rules out transpose cancellation directly.  The Nambu
skew matrix has Pfaffian equal, up to its fixed sign, to $\det D$; it is a
rewriting of one complex determinant rather than a product with
$\det\overline D$.  An independently integrated conjugate packet tensors the
line with its dual and the evaluation section is parallel.  A positive bosonic
quadratic form has positive determinant and hence no complex phase line.  A
connection-preserving real structure forces local real unit sections to be
parallel, while parallel transport around a loop may reverse their sign.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[Finite anomaly freedom versus physical quantum phase]
Triviality of the finite SM determinant character gives a gauge-invariant
measure section; it does not determine a unique gauge-invariant phase, make the
Berry connection basic at positive graph mass, or remove a theta-like period.
Likewise, the finite real structure supplies charge-real and Majorana relations
but not an independently integrated conjugate species.  Projector provenance,
section/connection provenance, and global holonomy are separate operational
certificates.
\end{firewall}


\begin{assessment}[Logical status of the SM--spacetime loading]
Relative to the operationally complete Grand Tensor, positivity, loaded
flatness, protected-record realization, source-core comparison, the
support-polar/multiplicity-quiver reconstruction, and the finite commutant
duality are exact after one verified branch packet.  The relative Howe Gram is
an exact finite certificate for whether the proposed residual multiplicity
algebra is complete.

The literal selected-phase source-native entrance now derives more than the
older residual ledger indicated.  The whole Store need not be grading odd:
protected-sign shorting canonically exports its odd cross-support component.
The locked opportunity sign is an exactly sharp normalized Read.  Deterministic
binary record factorization identifies the pre-central grading up to orientation,
while the more general action-grading residual classifies any remaining
ambiguity inside the residual multiplicity algebra.  Two parallel Store cells
give weak CAR and incidence; the locked edge packet gives one centered
rank-three endpoint generation source; source saturation removes full-cell
leakage; and odd-tangent provenance can identify the complete odd generator
with finite Dirac and force one weak doublet.  The reversal-odd calibrated
writer theorem reduces same-history Hodge/current provenance to a deterministic
record relation or to three orthogonal positive residuals.

The external Clifford cell now gives an independent occurrence alternative.
On a common locked--Clifford carrier, one scalar $p_{\rm Cl}$ is positive
exactly when the grading fails to lie in the normal multiplicity commutant.
Its zero branch explicitly reconstructs the separated grading, its maximal
branch is intrinsic chirality, and its spatial subbank locates an edge route.
The same number is a positive mixed-word norm, a grading-automorphism residual,
and, when the relevant operations are executable, an accepted-response
pressure slope.  Separate normal and sign marginals cannot determine it.  A
covariant edge-resolved CP source further exports the endpoint generation
range with zero Schur innovation and without a Kraus-phase choice.  Minimal
structural matter therefore requires one nonzero route; positivity of every
physical residue slot remains a stronger dynamical statement.

The remaining coherent matter entrance is weaker than a perfect unitary
mixer.  A forward/reverse CPTP pair through the identity is projected
canonically onto the inner Hamiltonian derivations.  Its finite positive
tangent defect identifies any first-order dissipative component, reversal
mismatch, or source-core leakage.  On the zero branch, direct or bracket
Klein refocusing removes bounded second-order channel errors and the canonical
Hamiltonian projection of the compiled channel reconstructs the typed
occurrence and relative Howe panels.  Positive packet-orbit matrices then
decide whether every admissible odd multiplicity copy is physically reached.
Classical reversible shuffles and unsigned axis populations do not establish
this branch.

The literal aggregate--tail cylinder closes the private multiplicity
subproblem by elementary two-dimensional linear algebra.  Its orbit-polytope
statistics determine the readable provenance rank and propagator, and a
separate chronology-allocation Schur residual proves that a rank-two standard
source can share at most one coefficient line with one spacetime standard
source.  This prevents both missing provenance and cross-domain double

On the spacetime side, the pressure packet no longer serves only as a symbolic
clock.  Joint coherent transport gives quantitative generator and actual-face
bounds, while a noncollapsing source frame and discrete Hodge--Morrey estimate
give the local connection atlas.  Endpoint representation theory reconstructs
the shift and Cartan rotation.  Four-phase normal histories, local normal

overall Lagrangian stiffness as independent action data.  Compact positive

Hodge-to-commutator relative-density theorem transport this screen to the
multiplicity commutant.  On a saturated same-history reducing coherent branch
the Hodge/action Schur residual is exactly zero and the router has vanishing
physical-time logarithm; more generally the source-core and polarization

renewal--Palatini theorem plus potential, counterterm, Ward, and stationarity
packets gives the local weak Einstein--matter handoff.  The GHY/corner theorem
is a separate global completion.

Still conditional are the actual numerical residue and even-sector contents,

history residuals, noncollapse of source and positive-screen frames, regulator

\begin{firewall}[Finite reduction versus interacting continuum physics]

% =============================================================================
\subsection{Canonical accepted/action states, trajectory closure, and driven fluctuations}
