\label{sec:accepted-state-trajectory-tilt}
% =============================================================================

The determining-field quotient and the common-action comparator solve two
finite reconstruction problems but do not by themselves specify the smallest
output state required by every subsequent use.  Comparison with a retained
initial class, autonomous output reconstruction, repeated updates, complete
trajectory likelihoods, and long-time conditioned fluctuations are distinct
operational tasks.  This subsection gives the canonical finite quotient and
the exact positive residual appropriate to each task.

% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
\subsubsection{Minimum co-retention and the fine accepted/action comparison}
\label{sec:accepted-master-comparison}
% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

\begin{theorem}[Canonical minimum of a co-retained accepted tuple]
\label{thm:accepted-master-tuple}
Let \(r_j:\Omega\to\Omega_j\), \(1\le j\le m\), be finitely many protected
coordinates produced at possibly different stages of one accepted history, and
put
\[
 \tau=(r_1,\ldots,r_m):\Omega\longrightarrow\Omega_\tau:=\tau(\Omega).
\]
Then the classical algebra generated by all coordinate Reads is exactly
\[
 \boxed{\mathfrak R_\tau=\tau^*C(\Omega_\tau).}
\]
Its nonzero minimal projections are the joint-tuple indicators.  Every sharp
record through which all \(r_j\) factor maps onto \(\Omega_\tau\); hence the
minimum sharp co-retention cost is \(|\Omega_\tau|\), not the cardinality of
the ambient Cartesian product.

If a coordinate would be erased before the common terminal cut, copying it to
an append-only classical ledger immediately before erasure is conservative:
tracing the ledger recovers the original complete process, and no feedback is
created unless a later operation is explicitly given an input wire from the
copy.  With tuple projections \(p_t\), a saturated word bank \(W_\alpha\), and
insertions \(X_\lambda\), the master panel
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathbb M^{(\lambda)}_{(t,\alpha),(u,\beta)}
 =\langle p_tW_\alpha,X_\lambda p_uW_\beta\rangle}
\]
contains every finite provenance, pulse, chronological, determining-field, and
action subpanel by finite compression.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Every coordinate function is constant on a tuple fibre, so the generated
algebra is contained in \(\tau^*C(\Omega_\tau)\).  Conversely the indicator of
a tuple value is the product of its coordinate point indicators, so every
point function on \(\Omega_\tau\) is generated.  If \(r_j=f_j\circ q\), then
\(\tau=(f_1,\ldots,f_m)\circ q\), giving the universal surjection and the
cardinality bound.  A passive copy has block form
\(\oplus_\omega\rho_\omega\mapsto
 \oplus_\omega\rho_\omega\otimes|r_j(\omega)\rangle\langle r_j(\omega)|\);
partial trace is the identity, and induction gives conservativity for
sequential copies.  Finally every derived panel is obtained by applying its
coefficient synthesis and compression maps to the complete master Gram.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Fine accepted comparison datum]
\label{def:accepted-fine-comparison}
Let \(\Omega_0\) be the finite initial accepted-history support with faithful
law \(\mu_x\), let \(\mathcal U\) be the complete fine accepted output record,
and let
\[
 \kappa_x(u)=\Pr(U=u\mid X=x,\mathrm{acc})
\]
be the observed row.  Let \(q_x^*\) be the independently reconstructed
common-action comparator.  Put
\[
 \Sigma(x)=(\kappa_x,q_x^*)
\]
and define \(x\sim_{\rm cmp}x'\) when \(\Sigma(x)=\Sigma(x')\).  The quotient
is denoted
\[
 \boxed{F_{\rm cmp}:\Omega_0\twoheadrightarrow\Theta_{\rm cmp}.}
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Canonical initial comparison quotient]
\label{thm:accepted-comparison-quotient}
The actual and comparator row families factor uniquely through
\(F_{\rm cmp}\).  Every other deterministic initial record through which both
families factor maps uniquely onto \(\Theta_{\rm cmp}\).  If all admitted
future accepted cylinders are included in the signatures, finite partition
refinement reconstructs this quotient after at most \(|\Omega_0|-1\) strict
splits.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The two row families are constant on the displayed equivalence classes.  If a
second quotient identifies \(x,x'\), factorization through it forces equality
of both rows and hence \(x\sim_{\rm cmp}x'\).  This gives the universal map.
The finite refinement argument is identical to the minimal-readable-record
compiler: split a block whenever one actual or comparator future signature
differs, and terminate because the number of blocks strictly increases.
\end{proof}

Let \(F:\Omega_0\to\Theta\) be any quotient through which the comparator
factors, put
\[
 \nu_\theta=\sum_{F(x)=\theta}\mu_x,
 \qquad
 \bar\kappa_\theta
 =\nu_\theta^{-1}\sum_{F(x)=\theta}\mu_x\kappa_x,
\]
and let \(C:\mathcal U\to\mathcal Z\) be any coarse terminal Read.

\begin{theorem}[Four-term accepted/action information Pythagoras]
\label{thm:accepted-four-term-Pythagoras}
With superscript \(C\) denoting pushforward and conditional rows taken inside
\(C\)-fibres, define
\[
 \Delta_{\rm lump}^{C}
 =\sum_x\mu_x\operatorname{KL}
   (\kappa_x^{C}\|\bar\kappa_{F(x)}^{C}),
\]
\[
 \Delta_{\rm fld}^{\rm hid}
 =\sum_{x,z}\mu_x\kappa_x^C(z)
   \operatorname{KL}
   (\kappa_x(\cdot\mid z)\|\bar\kappa_{F(x)}(\cdot\mid z)),
\]
\[
 \eta\overline\Delta_{\rm act}^{C}
 =\sum_\theta\nu_\theta
   \operatorname{KL}(\bar\kappa_\theta^C\|q_\theta^{*,C}),
\]
and
\[
 \eta\overline\Delta_{\rm act}^{\rm hid}
 =\sum_{\theta,z}\nu_\theta\bar\kappa_\theta^C(z)
   \operatorname{KL}
   (\bar\kappa_\theta(\cdot\mid z)\|q_\theta^*(\cdot\mid z)).
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{
 \begin{aligned}
 \sum_x\mu_x\operatorname{KL}(\kappa_x\|q_{F(x)}^*)
 &=\Delta_{\rm lump}^{C}+\Delta_{\rm fld}^{\rm hid}\\
 &\quad+\eta\overline\Delta_{\rm act}^{C}
       +\eta\overline\Delta_{\rm act}^{\rm hid}.
 \end{aligned}}
\]
All four terms are nonnegative.  They vanish simultaneously exactly when the
fine observed and comparator rows agree on every supported coordinate.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Insert the conditional mean row \(\bar\kappa_{F(x)}\).  The standard
relative-entropy projection identity separates the field insufficiency from
the action mismatch.  Applying the relative-entropy chain rule to the map
\(C\) in each of the two terms gives the displayed four summands.  Equality is
equivalent to equality in every faithful relative entropy.
\end{proof}

% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
\subsubsection{Canonical static output records}
\label{sec:accepted-static-output-quotients}
% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

Assume first that every comparator row \(q_\theta^*\) is faithful.  Define the
complete likelihood-ratio signature
\[
 \Lambda(u)=
 \left(\frac{\kappa_\theta(u)}{q_\theta^*(u)}
 \right)_{\theta\in\Theta_{\rm cmp}}.
\]

\begin{theorem}[Canonical likelihood-ratio quotient]
\label{thm:accepted-LR-quotient}
The quotient
\[
 \boxed{
 C_{\rm LR}:\mathcal U\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal Z_{\rm LR},
 \qquad
 u\sim_{\rm LR}v\iff\Lambda(u)=\Lambda(v)}
\]
is the unique coarsest deterministic output record preserving every classwise
accepted/action relative entropy:
\[
 \boxed{
 \operatorname{KL}(\kappa_\theta\|q_\theta^*)
 =\operatorname{KL}
  (\kappa_\theta^{\rm LR}\|q_\theta^{*,\rm LR}).}
\]
Inside every quotient cell the actual and comparator conditional laws agree.
Consequently there is a class-dependent common conditional kernel \(R_\theta\)
with
\[
 \boxed{
 \kappa_\theta=\kappa_\theta^{\rm LR}R_\theta,
 \qquad
 q_\theta^*=q_\theta^{*,\rm LR}R_\theta.}
\]
Total variation is preserved, and for every bounded fine observable \(f\),
its actual/comparator expectation difference is reconstructed exactly from the
quotient rows and the common conditional mean of \(f\) in each cell.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
For one pair \((p,q)\), the KL chain rule under a deterministic map is
\[
 \operatorname{KL}(p\|q)
 =\operatorname{KL}(p^C\|q^C)
 +\sum_zp^C(z)\operatorname{KL}
   (p(\cdot\mid z)\|q(\cdot\mid z)).
\]
Equality holds exactly when \(p/q\) is constant on each fibre.  Applying this
to every comparison class proves losslessness.  Any other lossless Read must
make every component of \(\Lambda\) fibrewise constant and hence refines
\(C_{\rm LR}\).  Equality of the conditional laws gives the decoder and the
observable identity; fibrewise constancy also fixes the sign of \(p-q\) and
therefore preserves total variation.
\end{proof}

For support-exact autonomous compression, let \(\{\mu_i:i\in\mathcal I\}\)
be the complete family of actual and comparator rows, let
\(m=\sum_i\omega_i\mu_i\) be any faithful positive mixture on the union
support, and put \(c(u)=(\mu_i(u))_i\).

\begin{theorem}[Canonical finite-experiment quotient and common decoder]
\label{thm:accepted-experiment-quotient}
Define
\[
 \boxed{
 u\sim_{\rm exp}v
 \iff c(u)=a\,c(v)\text{ for some }a>0,}
\]
and let \(C_{\rm exp}:\mathcal U_+\to\mathcal Z_{\rm exp}\) be the quotient.
The equivalence is independent of the mixture weights and is characterized by
vanishing of every \(2\times2\) column minor.  The kernel
\[
 \boxed{
 R(u\mid z)
 =\one_{\{C_{\rm exp}(u)=z\}}
  \frac{m(u)}{\sum_{v:C_{\rm exp}(v)=z}m(v)}}
\]
is independent of \(i\) and reconstructs every row:
\[
 \boxed{\mu_i=\mu_i^{\rm exp}R.}
\]
This is the unique coarsest deterministic output record admitting one decoder
for the complete experiment.  It preserves every pairwise finite
\(f\)-divergence, every support singularity, and every later stochastic
channel.  In particular, if \(L\) is a later channel, then
\[
 \boxed{
 \mu_iL=\mu_i^{\rm exp}L_{\rm exp},
 \qquad
 L_{\rm exp}=RL.}
\]
The experiment quotient refines \(C_{\rm LR}\); equality holds exactly when
the comparator conditionals inside each LR cell are independent of the
comparison class.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Normalized density columns \(c(u)/m(u)\) agree exactly when the probability
columns are positively proportional; this also proves independence of the
mixture.  On one quotient cell write \(\mu_i(u)=a_i(z)m(u)\).  Summation gives
\(a_i(z)=\mu_i^{\rm exp}(z)/m^{\rm exp}(z)\), proving the common decoder.
Every other common-decoder record makes the ratio of any two experiment rows
constant inside its fibres and therefore refines the projective-column
partition.  Pairwise likelihood ratios are cellwise constant, so every
\(f\)-divergence is preserved, including singular rays.  Composition with a
later channel follows by inserting the common decoder.  The relation to
\(C_{\rm LR}\) is immediate because proportional complete columns have equal
actual/comparator ratios; equality requires the class-dependent LR decoders to
coincide.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Decoder innovation]
\label{thm:accepted-decoder-innovation}
For any proposed output compression \(C\), let
\[
 R_C(u\mid z)=\one_{\{C(u)=z\}}\frac{m(u)}{m^C(z)}
\]
and define
\[
 \boxed{
 \Delta_{\rm dec}(C)
 =\sum_i\omega_i\sum_z\mu_i^C(z)
  \operatorname{KL}(\mu_i(\cdot\mid z)\|R_C(\cdot\mid z)).}
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{
 \sum_i\omega_i\operatorname{KL}(\mu_i\|m)
 =\sum_i\omega_i\operatorname{KL}(\mu_i^C\|m^C)
  +\Delta_{\rm dec}(C).}
\]
Moreover \(\Delta_{\rm dec}(C)=0\) exactly when \(C\) refines
\(C_{\rm exp}\).  Probabilistically it is the conditional mutual information
between the experiment index and the fine output given the proposed record.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Apply the KL chain rule to each pair \((\mu_i,m)\) and average.  Zero conditional
KL makes the fine conditional law independent of \(i\), which is precisely the
common-decoder condition characterized by
\Cref{thm:accepted-experiment-quotient}.
\end{proof}

% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
\subsubsection{Future saturation, Markov retracts, and generator memory}
\label{sec:accepted-dynamic-state}
% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

Let \(\{K_a:a\in\Sigma\}\) be a finite alphabet of later stochastic update
letters on \(\mathcal U_+\), and let \(V_0\) be the span of the complete
experiment rows.  Put
\[
 V_{r+1}=V_r+\sum_{a\in\Sigma}V_rK_a.
\]

\begin{theorem}[Finite future-saturated experiment state]
\label{thm:accepted-future-quotient}
The increasing chain \(V_r\) stabilizes after at most
\(|\mathcal U_+|-\dim V_0\) strict rank increases, at
\[
 \boxed{V_\infty=\Span\{\mu_iK_w:i\in\mathcal I,
 w\in\Sigma^*\}.}
\]
Choose a positive \(m\in V_\infty\) on the union support and a basis
\(f_1,\ldots,f_d\) of \(V_\infty\).  The joint level sets of
\[
 \left(\frac{f_1(u)}{m(u)},\ldots,\frac{f_d(u)}{m(u)}\right)
\]
define a basis-independent quotient \(C_{\rm fut}\) with one decoder
\(R_{\rm fut}\) satisfying
\[
 \boxed{f=(fC_{\rm fut})R_{\rm fut}
 \qquad(f\in V_\infty).}
\]
It is the unique coarsest deterministic record reconstructing every reachable
future row.  With
\[
 K_a^{\rm fut}=R_{\rm fut}K_aC_{\rm fut},
\]
one has, for every reachable row and word,
\[
 \boxed{
 \mu_iK_w
 = (\mu_iC_{\rm fut})K_w^{\rm fut}R_{\rm fut}.}
\]
Thus \(C_{\rm exp}\preceq C_{\rm fut}\), possibly strictly.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The chain consists of subspaces of a fixed finite-dimensional row space, so it
stabilizes.  Its stable value is invariant under every \(K_a\) and contains
all word rows; the reverse inclusion follows by construction.  The projective
column argument of \Cref{thm:accepted-experiment-quotient}, applied to a basis
of this row space, gives the quotient, common decoder, and universal property.
Invariance then gives the exact word recursion.
\end{proof}

Assume now that a faithful reference law \(m\) is stationary for every
\(K_a\).  For a deterministic quotient \(C\), let \(R\) be the stationary
conditional decoder, \(E=CR\), and \(L_a=RK_aC\).

\begin{theorem}[Universal Markov retract and the stronger reset branch]
\label{thm:accepted-Markov-retract}
For one update letter the following are equivalent:
\[
 \boxed{EK_a=K_aE,}
\]
\[
 \boxed{K_aC=CL_a,
 \qquad RK_a=L_aR,}
\]
and simultaneous strong lumpability of \(K_a\) and its stationary reversal
\[
 K_a^\sharp(v,u)=\frac{m(u)K_a(u,v)}{m(v)}
\]
through the same partition.  On this branch every fine law has exact quotient
dynamics and every decoded quotient law has exact reconstructed fine dynamics.
The unique coarsest refinement of \(C_{\rm fut}\) with this property is found
by finite partition refinement using forward and reversed block transition
masses.

The stronger fibre-reset identity is
\[
 \boxed{K_a=CL_aR=EK_aE.}
\]
It requires both Markov-retract closure and erasure of all within-cell motion;
a quotient may be exactly Markov while this reset residual remains positive.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Using \(RC=I\), the two intertwining relations imply
\(EK_a=CRK_a=CL_aR=K_aCR=K_aE\).  Conversely commutation gives
\(K_aC=EK_aC=C(RK_aC)\) and similarly for the decoder.  Taking adjoints in
\(L^2(m)\) identifies decoder invariance with forward lumpability of the
reversed kernel.  Stable finite partition refinement is the standard
simultaneous bisimulation algorithm.  The reset statement is the additional
identity that the fine update factors through the decoder on both sides.
\end{proof}

Let \(L\) be a finite continuous-time Markov generator and let
\(W_0=\Span\{\mu_i\}\), \(W_{r+1}=W_r+W_rL\).

\begin{theorem}[Generator-native state closure and Mori--Zwanzig alternative]
\label{thm:accepted-generator-closure}
The Krylov chain stabilizes finitely at
\[
 \boxed{
 W_\infty=\Span\{\mu_iL^k:i,k\}
 =\Span\{\mu_ie^{tL}:i,t\ge0\}.}
\]
Its projective-column quotient \(C_L\) reconstructs every reachable continuous
future.  For a proposed quotient with decoder \(R\), projection \(E=CR\), and
coarse generator \(A=RLC\), the following are equivalent:
\[
 \boxed{EL=LE,}
\]
\[
 \boxed{LC=CA,
 \qquad RL=AR,}
\]
and simultaneous rate lumpability of \(L\) and its stationary reversal.
Then
\[
 \boxed{e^{tL}C=Ce^{tA},
 \qquad Re^{tL}=e^{tA}R.}
\]

If commutation fails, put \(Q=I-E\).  For a fine evolving row split as
\(x(t)=p(t)E\), \(y(t)=p(t)Q\), elimination of \(y\) gives
\[
 \boxed{
 \begin{aligned}
 \dot x(t)
 &=x(t)ELE+y(0)e^{tQLQ}QLE\\
 &\quad+\int_0^t x(s)
   ELQe^{(t-s)QLQ}QLE\,\dd s.
 \end{aligned}}
\]
The visible resolvent is
\[
 \boxed{
 E(zI-L)^{-1}E
 =\left[zE-ELE-ELQ(zQ-QLQ)^{-1}QLE\right]^{-1}.}
\]
Thus failure of generator closure returns an exact initial hidden term, memory
kernel, and frequency-dependent self-energy.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Finite-dimensional Krylov stabilization and the exponential power series give
the first equality.  The projective-column proof is as in
\Cref{thm:accepted-future-quotient}.  The commutator equivalence follows from
\(RC=I\) exactly as in the discrete case, and exponentiation gives the
semigroup identities.  The coupled equations for \(x,y\) follow by inserting
\(E+Q=I\) around \(L\).  Variation of constants solves the \(Q\)-equation;
substitution gives the memory equation.  Block inversion gives the resolvent
short.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Canonical finite-rate fibre refresh]
\label{cor:accepted-Poisson-refresh}
For a coarse generator \(A\), decoder \(R\), quotient \(C\), and
\(E=CR\), the operator
\[
 \boxed{L_\lambda=CAR+\lambda(E-I)}
\]
is a fine Markov generator for sufficiently large \(\lambda\), with exact
semigroup
\[
 \boxed{
 e^{tL_\lambda}=Ce^{tA}R+e^{-\lambda t}(I-E).}
\]
It preserves exact quotient dynamics while refreshing hidden fibre memory
exponentially.  A nontrivial exact fibre reset cannot hold at every
arbitrarily small positive time in a strongly continuous semigroup, because
taking \(t\downarrow0\) would force \(E=I\).
\end{corollary}

% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
\subsubsection{Trajectory likelihood and hidden entropy}
\label{sec:accepted-path-action}
% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

For a finite generator \(L\), let
\(\lambda_L(u)=\sum_{v\ne u}L(u,v)\), let \(\Theta_u\) be the occupation time
of state \(u\) on \([0,T]\), and let \(N_{uv}\) be the number of directed
\(u\to v\) jumps.

\begin{theorem}[Finite continuous-time path likelihood]
\label{thm:accepted-path-likelihood}
For two absolutely continuous finite Markov models \((p,L)\) and
\((\widetilde p,\widetilde L)\),
\[
 \boxed{
 \begin{aligned}
 \log\frac{\dd\mathbb P_{p,L}^{T}}
          {\dd\mathbb P_{\widetilde p,\widetilde L}^{T}}
 &=\log\frac{p(X_0)}{\widetilde p(X_0)}\\
 &\quad+\sum_{u\ne v}N_{uv}
       \log\frac{L(u,v)}{\widetilde L(u,v)}\\
 &\quad-\sum_u\Theta_u
       (\lambda_L(u)-\lambda_{\widetilde L}(u)).
 \end{aligned}}
\]
Hence the initial state, occupation times, and directed jump counts form a
finite sufficient trajectory record.  With
\(\Phi(a,b)=a\log(a/b)-a+b\),
\[
 \boxed{
 \begin{aligned}
 \operatorname{KL}(\mathbb P_{p,L}^{T}\|
                    \mathbb P_{\widetilde p,\widetilde L}^{T})
 &=\operatorname{KL}(p\|\widetilde p)\\
 &\quad+\int_0^T\sum_up_t(u)
       \sum_{v\ne u}\Phi(L(u,v),\widetilde L(u,v))\,\dd t.
 \end{aligned}}
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Multiply the initial density, exponential holding factors, and jump rates along
one resolved path.  Their logarithmic ratio groups exactly into the displayed
statistics.  Taking expectation uses
\(\mathbb E[N_{uv}(\dd t)]=p_t(u)L(u,v)\dd t\) and
\(\mathbb E[\Theta_u]=\int_0^Tp_t(u)\dd t\).
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Coarse path-space Pythagoras]
\label{thm:accepted-path-Pythagoras}
Suppose \(L\) and \(\widetilde L\) are strongly lumpable through the same
state record \(C\), with coarse generators \(A,\widetilde A\).  For
\(z'\ne C(u)\), define the conditional fine destination law
\[
 r^L_{u,z'}(v)
 =\frac{L(u,v)}{A(C(u),z')},
 \qquad C(v)=z',
\]
when the denominator is positive, and similarly for \(\widetilde L\).  Then
\[
 \boxed{
 \begin{aligned}
 &\operatorname{KL}(\mathbb P_{p,L}^{T}\|
                    \mathbb P_{\widetilde p,\widetilde L}^{T})\\
 &=\operatorname{KL}(\mathbb P_{pC,A}^{T}\|
                     \mathbb P_{\widetilde pC,\widetilde A}^{T})
   +\Delta_{\rm init}\\
 &\quad+\int_0^T\mathfrak d_t\,\dd t
       +\int_0^T\mathfrak i_t\,\dd t,
 \end{aligned}}
\]
where
\[
 \Delta_{\rm init}
 =\sum_zpC(z)\operatorname{KL}
   (p(\cdot\mid z)\|\widetilde p(\cdot\mid z)),
\]
\[
 \mathfrak d_t
 =\sum_up_t(u)\sum_{z'\ne C(u)}
  A(C(u),z')\operatorname{KL}
  (r^L_{u,z'}\|r^{\widetilde L}_{u,z'}),
\]
and
\[
 \mathfrak i_t
 =\sum_up_t(u)
  \sum_{\substack{v\ne u\\C(v)=C(u)}}
  \Phi(L(u,v),\widetilde L(u,v)).
\]
Thus coarse trajectory mismatch, initial hidden-fibre mismatch, fine
destination-channel mismatch, and invisible within-cell motion are four
independent nonnegative coordinates.  Vanishing of the hidden three terms is
equivalent to equality of the conditional fine path laws given the coarse
path.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Apply the initial KL chain rule.  In the path-rate integral, split destination
states by their coarse target cell.  On a visible block the elementary rate
identity
\[
 \sum_j\Phi(a_j,b_j)
 =\Phi\left(\sum_ja_j,\sum_jb_j\right)
  +\left(\sum_ja_j\right)
   \operatorname{KL}
   \left(\frac{a_j}{\sum a}\middle\|
         \frac{b_j}{\sum b}\right)
\]
separates the coarse jump rate from the fine destination law.  Internal edges
have no coarse counterpart and give \(\mathfrak i_t\).  Equality in every
conditional KL gives the common conditional path decoder.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Coarse and hidden entropy production]
\label{cor:accepted-hidden-entropy}
Let \(L^\sharp\) be the stationary reversal of \(L\), and suppose \(C\) is a
generator Markov retract.  The stationary entropy-production rate decomposes
as
\[
 \boxed{
 \sigma(L)=\sigma(A)
 +\sigma_{\rm dest}^{\rm hid}
 +\sigma_{\rm int}^{\rm hid}.}
\]
An exact coarse Markov evolution can therefore conceal irreversible fine
destination choices or within-fibre cycles.  For the refresh lift of
\Cref{cor:accepted-Poisson-refresh}, the refresh edges are reversible and both
hidden terms vanish, so \(\sigma(L_\lambda)=\sigma(A)\).
\end{corollary}

% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
\subsubsection{Tilted spectra, large deviations, and driven rare-event dynamics}
\label{sec:accepted-tilted-driven}
% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

Let \(v:\mathcal U\to\R\) be a protected state reward and
\(g(u,w)\) a protected directed jump reward.  Put
\[
 Y_T=\int_0^Tv(X_t)\,\dd t
     +\sum_{0<t\le T}g(X_{t-},X_t).
\]
For \(k\in\R\), define the finite tilted matrix
\[
 B_k(u,w)=L(u,w)e^{kg(u,w)}\quad(u\ne w),
 \qquad
 B_k(u,u)=L(u,u)+kv(u).
\]

\begin{theorem}[Finite Feynman--Kac, SCGF, and large-deviation compiler]
\label{thm:accepted-Feynman-Kac-LDP}
For every bounded terminal function \(f\),
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathbb E_p[e^{kY_T}f(X_T)]=p\,e^{TB_k}f.}
\]
If \(L\) is irreducible, the spectral bound
\[
 \boxed{\psi(k)=s(B_k)}
\]
is a simple real analytic Perron eigenvalue and
\[
 \boxed{
 \lim_{T\to\infty}T^{-1}
 \log\mathbb E_p e^{kY_T}=\psi(k).}
\]
The random variables \(Y_T/T\) satisfy the finite-state large-deviation
principle with convex good rate
\[
 \boxed{I(a)=\sup_{k\in\R}\{ka-\psi(k)\}.}
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Conditioning on the first jump gives the backward Feynman--Kac equation
\(\partial_tF_t=B_kF_t\), proving the semigroup formula.  An irreducible
Metzler matrix has a simple positive Perron eigenpair; analytic perturbation
and convexity of exponential moments give analyticity and convexity of
\(\psi\).  Perron asymptotics prove the scaled limit.  Differentiability of
\(\psi\), together with exponential tightness obtained by domination of the
jump count by a finite-rate Poisson variable, gives the finite-state
Gartner--Ellis theorem.
\end{proof}

Let \(\Gamma_*\) be the finite set of nonzero jump-reward values, put
\(V=\diag(v)\), and define
\[
 J_\gamma(u,w)=L(u,w)\one_{\{g(u,w)=\gamma\}}.
\]
Then
\[
 B_k=L+kV+\sum_{\gamma\in\Gamma_*}(e^{k\gamma}-1)J_\gamma.
\]

\begin{theorem}[Finite reward-lumpability and tilted self-energy]
\label{thm:accepted-tilted-retract}
For a quotient projection \(E=CR\), the following are equivalent:
\[
 \boxed{EB_k=B_kE\quad\text{for every }k,}
\]
and the finite coefficient identities
\[
 \boxed{
 [E,L]=[E,V]=[E,J_\gamma]=0
 \quad(\gamma\in\Gamma_*).}
\]
On this branch, with \(A_k=RB_kC\), the fine and coarse Perron exponents and
large-deviation rate functions coincide exactly.

If the coefficient identities fail, the visible tilted resolvent is
\[
 \boxed{
 E(zI-B_k)^{-1}E
 =\left[zE-EB_kE-\Sigma_k(z)\right]^{-1},}
\]
with hidden tilted self-energy
\[
 \boxed{
 \Sigma_k(z)
 =EB_kQ(zQ-QB_kQ)^{-1}QB_kE,
 \qquad Q=I-E.}
\]
The two-sided coefficient residual
\[
 \boxed{
 \Delta_{\rm tilt}^{\rm coef}
 =\sum_{T\in\{L,V,J_\gamma\}}
  (\|ETQ\|_{\HS}^2+\|QTE\|_{\HS}^2)}
\]
vanishes exactly on universal tilted closure.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The scalar functions \(1,k,e^{k\gamma}-1\) for distinct \(\gamma\) are
linearly independent, so commutation of the whole analytic family is
equivalent to commutation of its finite coefficient bank.  Exact intertwining
then carries the positive Perron vector and eigenvalue between the fine and
coarse spaces.  The rate functions are the same Legendre transform.  The
resolvent formula is the Schur complement of \(zI-B_k\) relative to
\(E\oplus Q\); the residual is precisely the sum of the two cross-block norms.
\end{proof}

Let \(r_k,\ell_k>0\) be normalized Perron vectors,
\[
 B_kr_k=\psi(k)r_k,
 \qquad
 \ell_kB_k=\psi(k)\ell_k,
 \qquad
 \ell_kr_k=1,
\]
and put \(D_k=\diag(r_k)\).

\begin{theorem}[Perron--Doob driven process and entropy-optimal control]
\label{thm:accepted-driven-process}
The operator
\[
 \boxed{
 L_k^{\rm dr}=D_k^{-1}B_kD_k-\psi(k)I}
\]
is an irreducible Markov generator with stationary law
\[
 \boxed{\pi_k(u)=\ell_k(u)r_k(u).}
\]
For every finite path,
\[
 \boxed{
 \frac{\dd\mathbb P_{p,L_k^{\rm dr}}^T}
      {\dd\mathbb P_{p,L}^T}
 =\exp(kY_T-T\psi(k))
  \frac{r_k(X_T)}{r_k(X_0)}.}
\]
The driven SCGF for an additional tilt \(q\) is
\[
 \boxed{\psi_k^{\rm dr}(q)=\psi(k+q)-\psi(k),}
\]
so its typical current and asymptotic variance are
\[
 \boxed{a_k=\psi'(k),
 \qquad \sigma_k^2=\psi''(k).}
\]

For every stationary controlled generator \(K\) with invariant law \(\nu\),
let
\[
 \mathscr H(\nu,K\|L)
 =\sum_u\nu(u)\sum_{w\ne u}\Phi(K(u,w),L(u,w))
\]
and let \(j(\nu,K)\) be the stationary rate of the protected additive reward.
Then
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathscr H(\nu,K\|L)-kj(\nu,K)+\psi(k)
 =\mathscr H(\nu,K\|L_k^{\rm dr})\ge0.}
\]
Equality holds exactly for \((\nu,K)=(\pi_k,L_k^{\rm dr})\).  Hence
\[
 \boxed{
 \psi(k)=\sup_{\nu K=0}
 \{kj(\nu,K)-\mathscr H(\nu,K\|L)\}.}
\]
At an exposed strictly convex current value \(a=\psi'(k)\),
\[
 \boxed{
 I(a)=\inf_{\substack{\nu K=0\\j(\nu,K)=a}}
 \mathscr H(\nu,K\|L)
 =ka-\psi(k),}
\]
and the unique minimizer is the driven process.  The original process
conditioned on \(Y_T/T\approx a\) and the driven process have vanishing
specific relative entropy in the limits \(T\to\infty\), followed by a
shrinking conditioning window.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The Perron equation makes every row sum of \(L_k^{\rm dr}\) zero and positivity
of \(r_k\) preserves nonnegative off-diagonal rates.  The left Perron equation
proves stationarity of \(\ell_k\odot r_k\).  Multiplying the jump-rate ratios
along a path telescopes the factors \(r_k(X_t)\), while the holding-rate
change supplies \(-T\psi(k)\), proving the path identity.  Similarity gives
\(B_q^{\rm dr,k}=D_k^{-1}B_{k+q}D_k-\psi(k)I\) and hence the shifted SCGF.

For the control identity, substitute
\[
 \log\frac{L_k^{\rm dr}(u,w)}{L(u,w)}
 =kg(u,w)+\log r_k(w)-\log r_k(u)
\]
and the corresponding escape-rate relation into the entropy-rate difference.
Stationarity of \(\nu\) cancels the coboundary in \(\log r_k\), leaving the
displayed Pythagoras.  The variational formulas follow by minimization and
Legendre duality.  Finally the path Radon--Nikodym identity differs from the
canonical exponential tilt only by bounded endpoint factors; the LDP and
strict convexity give equivalence with microcanonical conditioning in specific
relative entropy.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Exact descent of driven dynamics and regulator transfer]
\label{cor:accepted-driven-quotient-regulator}
If the tilted family closes exactly through \((C,R)\), then
\[
 r_k=C\bar r_k,
 \qquad
 \ell_k=\bar\ell_kR,
\]
and the driven generators obey
\[
 \boxed{
 L_k^{\rm dr}C=C\bar L_k^{\rm dr},
 \qquad
 RL_k^{\rm dr}=\bar L_k^{\rm dr}R.}
\]
The same decoder therefore reconstructs ordinary, tilted, and driven states.
For a fixed-dimensional cutoff family with locally uniform convergence of the
coarse tilted matrices, a uniform Perron separation margin, and a positive
lower bound on the normalized Perron vector, the coarse driven generators,
stationary laws, and finite-time semigroups converge locally uniformly in the
tilt.  Joint long-time, cutoff, and shrinking-window limits require the
corresponding uniform Perron prefactor and local large-deviation estimates.
\end{corollary}

\begin{assessment}[Hierarchy of accepted/action closure]
The canonical records and residuals above form a strict hierarchy:
\[
 \begin{gathered}
 \text{fine accepted/action row comparison}\\[0.1em]
 \Downarrow\quad C_{\rm LR}\ \text{or}\ C_{\rm exp}\\[0.1em]
 \text{static lossless compression}\\[0.1em]
 \Downarrow\quad C_{\rm fut}\\[0.1em]
 \text{reachable repeated-update autonomy}\\[0.1em]
 \Downarrow\quad [E,K_a]=0\ \text{or}\ [E,L]=0\\[0.1em]
 \text{universal Markov or generator retract}\\[0.1em]
 \Downarrow\quad\Delta_{\rm path}^{\rm hid}=0\\[0.1em]
 \text{trajectory-action sufficiency}\\[0.1em]
 \Downarrow\quad\Delta_{\rm tilt}^{\rm coef}=0\\[0.1em]
 \text{long-time fluctuation closure}\\[0.1em]
 \Downarrow\quad L_k^{\rm dr}\\[0.1em]
 \text{entropy-optimal driven dynamics}.
 \end{gathered}
\]
No arrow is automatic.  Every failure returns a finite likelihood-ratio pair,
projective-column minor, partition split, commutator block, memory kernel,
path-channel mismatch, hidden entropy current, tilted self-energy, or Perron
spectral obstruction.
\end{assessment}


\section{Arithmetic derived from the universal chronology record}
\label{sec:arithmetic-loading}
% =============================================================================

The basic finite arithmetic packet is not produced by appending an
arithmetic-specific record after the universal tensor.  The operationally
complete origin object of Part~I already retains the neutral chronological
variable generated by sequential experimentation.  Selecting the first $X$
chronological positions gives a protected pointed successor, endpoint Reads,
and deterministic writers.  Although the $*$-closure of this successor is the
full algebra $M_X(\C)$, the selective datum is the oriented chronology algebra,
not an unmarked matrix algebra.  The normalized Peano relations admit one and
only one extension of that datum, force multiplicativity, and determine the
unit-weight divisibility-incidence zeta history.  Its terminating logarithm and
inverse derive the von Mangoldt and M\"obius histories.  The exact implication
is therefore
\[
 \boxed{
 \boldsymbol{\mathbb T}^{\min,op}_{\Grand,X}
 \Longrightarrow
 \boldsymbol{\mathbb T}^{\rm ar,can}_{\Grand,X}.}
\]
No prime, character, M\"obius, Mellin, endpoint weight, or target-facing
intertwiner is inserted into the universal record.  Arithmetic semantics enter
only through the proved Peano and finite Euler relations.

\begin{countertheorem}[The record-discarded predictive core need not contain arithmetic]
\label{cth:ar-unrecorded-no-go}
For every $X\ge2$ there is a bare finite predictive core whose record-discarded
history algebra is $\C$ and therefore contains no pointed $X$-endpoint
successor corner.  Consequently
\[
 \boldsymbol{\mathbb T}^{\rm core}_{\Grand,X}
 \Longrightarrow
 \boldsymbol{\mathbb T}^{\rm ar}_{\Grand,X}
\]
is false in general.  This does not contradict the arithmetic theorem, because
``full'' in this manuscript denotes the operationally complete tensor.
\end{countertheorem}

\begin{proof}
Take one predictive type with one-dimensional state space and one primitive
letter equal to the identity channel.  Every represented core word is the
identity, so the complete record-discarded history algebra is $\C$.  Any unital
$*$-subalgebra or reducing ideal of $\C$ is again $\C$.  By contrast, an exact
pointed $X$-endpoint successor $S$ with orthogonal source lines
$\eta,S\eta,\ldots,S^{X-1}\eta$ generates the matrix units
\[
 E_{ij}=S^{i-1}(I-SS^*)(S^*)^{j-1}
 \qquad(1\le i,j\le X)
\]
and hence a copy of $M_X(\C)$.  Since $M_X(\C)$ cannot embed unitally in $\C$
for $X\ge2$, the asserted core-only implication fails.  The universal record
completion theorem supplies precisely the missing neutral chronology without
encoding arithmetic data.
\end{proof}

% =============================================================================
\subsection{Universal chronology corner and arithmetic specialization}
\label{sec:ar-record-completion}
% =============================================================================

\begin{definition}[Finite protected chronological subchain]
\label{def:ar-record-chain}
For $X\ge2$, select from the universal protocol record the chronological values
$1,\ldots,X$, their one-dimensional record sectors $H_n=\C$, and the
deterministic writers
\[
 \tau_n:n\longrightarrow n+1,
 \qquad 1\le n<X.
\]
The distinguished source record is $1$, and every record projection is a
retained terminal label Read.  This is a subchain of
$\mathfrak R_X^{\rm op}$, not a new arithmetic process.
\end{definition}

Put
\[
 \mathcal R_X:=\bigoplus_{n=1}^X\mathcal B(H_n)\cong\C^X
\]
with orthonormal basis $e_1,\ldots,e_X$.  In the canonical block record
representation let
\[
 \rho_X(\tau_n)=E_{n+1,n},
 \qquad
 P_{n,X}:=E_{nn},
\]
and define
\[
 \boxed{
 S_X^{\rm rec}:=\sum_{n=1}^{X-1}E_{n+1,n},
 \qquad
 \eta_X^{\rm rec}:=e_1,
 \qquad
 N_X^{\rm rec}:=\sum_{n=1}^X nP_{n,X}.}
\]

\begin{theorem}[Exact universal record algebra and pointed count ladder]
\label{thm:ar-record-algebra}
The selected chronological record satisfies
\[
 \boxed{
 (S_X^{\rm rec})^*S_X^{\rm rec}=I-P_{X,X},
 \qquad
 S_X^{\rm rec}(S_X^{\rm rec})^*=I-P_{1,X},}
\]
\[
 \boxed{[N_X^{\rm rec},S_X^{\rm rec}]=S_X^{\rm rec},}
 \qquad
 \boxed{(S_X^{\rm rec})^{n-1}\eta_X^{\rm rec}=e_n
 \quad(1\le n\le X),}
\]
and
\[
 \boxed{C^*(S_X^{\rm rec})=M_X(\C).}
\]
The count ladder is therefore an internal subalgebra of the universal
operational history algebra.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Multiplication of the displayed matrix units gives
\[
 (S_X^{\rm rec})^*S_X^{\rm rec}
 =\sum_{n=1}^{X-1}E_{nn}=I-P_{X,X}
\]
and
\[
 S_X^{\rm rec}(S_X^{\rm rec})^*
 =\sum_{n=2}^{X}E_{nn}=I-P_{1,X}.
\]
Moreover,
\[
 N_X^{\rm rec}E_{n+1,n}=(n+1)E_{n+1,n},
 \qquad
 E_{n+1,n}N_X^{\rm rec}=nE_{n+1,n},
\]
so summing gives the commutator identity.  The orbit identity is immediate.
Finally,
\[
 E_{11}=I-S_X^{\rm rec}(S_X^{\rm rec})^*,
 \qquad
 E_{ij}=(S_X^{\rm rec})^{i-1}E_{11}
 ((S_X^{\rm rec})^*)^{j-1}.
\]
Thus every matrix unit belongs to $C^*(S_X^{\rm rec})$, proving
$M_X(\C)\subseteq C^*(S_X^{\rm rec})$; the reverse inclusion is immediate.
Internality follows from \Cref{thm:record-survival}.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Forward chronology algebra]
\label{def:ar-forward-algebra}
The \emph{forward chronology algebra} of the protected record chain is
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal T_X^+
 :=\Span\{E_{ij}:1\le j\le i\le X\}.}
\]
Equivalently, $A\in\mathcal T_X^+$ exactly when
$\langle e_i,Ae_j\rangle=0$ for $i<j$; hence a forward history never decreases
the protected endpoint label.
\end{definition}

\begin{proposition}[Intrinsic generation of the oriented chronology algebra]
\label{prop:ar-forward-generation}
One has
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal T_X^+
 =\operatorname{alg}(S_X^{\rm rec},P_{1,X},\ldots,P_{X,X})
 =\operatorname{alg}(S_X^{\rm rec},N_X^{\rm rec}).}
\]
The algebra $\mathcal T_X^+$ is a proper unital, generally non-$*$-closed
subalgebra for $X\ge2$, while its $*$-closure is $M_X(\C)$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
The displayed span is closed under multiplication because
$E_{ij}E_{k\ell}=\delta_{jk}E_{i\ell}$ and
$i\ge j=k\ge\ell$ imply $i\ge\ell$.  Since $N_X^{\rm rec}$ has simple
spectrum $\{1,\ldots,X\}$, every $P_{j,X}$ is a Lagrange polynomial in
$N_X^{\rm rec}$.  For $i\ge j$,
\[
 E_{ij}=(S_X^{\rm rec})^{i-j}P_{j,X},
\]
so $S_X^{\rm rec}$ and $N_X^{\rm rec}$ generate all forward matrix units.
Conversely both generators are forward.  Adjoining adjoints supplies the
remaining matrix units, giving the full $*$-closure.
\end{proof}

\begin{principle}[The selective arithmetic datum]
\label{prin:ar-selective-datum}
The arithmetic loading is not selected from an unmarked copy of $M_X(\C)$.
It is derived from the structured tuple
\[
 \bigl(\eta_X^{\rm rec},S_X^{\rm rec},(P_{n,X})_{n\le X},
       \mathcal T_X^+\bigr),
\]
whose source, orientation, endpoint Reads, and deterministic writers are fixed
before arithmetic semantics.  The universal relations below have a singleton
normalized solution fibre over this tuple.
\end{principle}

\begin{definition}[Arithmetic selection of the universal chronology corner]
\label{def:ar-record-completion}
Let $\mathcal A_X^{\rm hist}$ and
$\boldsymbol{\mathbb T}^{\min,op}_{\Grand,X}$ be the operationally complete
history algebra and tensor of Part~I.  The \emph{arithmetic chronology
selection} is the pointed internal corner
\[
 \boxed{
 \bigl(C^*(S_X^{\rm rec}),\eta_X^{\rm rec},N_X^{\rm rec}\bigr)
 \subseteq\mathcal A_X^{\rm hist}.}
\]
The label is retained for compatibility with earlier versions, but no new
chronological completion is performed in the arithmetic section.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Universal chronology specialization and conservativity]
\label{thm:ar-record-completion}
The arithmetic chronology selection has the following exact properties.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(R\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item It is an internal source-complete record subalgebra of the full
      operational history algebra.
\item Its source, diagonal record Reads, and deterministic successor survive
      the future quotient and have no arithmetic coefficient in their
      definition.
\item Discarding the entire universal record recovers the record-forgetting
      predictive core statistics exactly.
\item Every record-preserving process morphism, relabelling, or source-fixing
      unitary restricts to the chronology corner, and compatible cutoff
      embeddings carry the cutoff-$X$ corner into the cutoff-$Y$ corner.
\item The construction depends only on the declared chronological positions
      and their deterministic update rule; it is defined before any arithmetic
      coefficient or predicate.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Internality and source survival are
\Cref{thm:record-survival,thm:ar-record-algebra}.  Record-discard conservativity,
functoriality, and cutoff compatibility are
\Cref{thm:operational-record-completion}.  The selected writers append only the
protocol-generated chronological label, so the construction contains no
number-theoretic coefficient.  Restricting the universal morphisms and cutoff
maps to the invariant span of the first $X$ chronological records gives the
claimed corner maps.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Exact chronology, innovation, and source margins}
\label{sec:ar-record-margins}
% =============================================================================

Let
\[
 G_{X}^{\rm chr}
 :=\bigl[\langle(S_X^{\rm rec})^{i-1}\eta_X^{\rm rec},
 (S_X^{\rm rec})^{j-1}\eta_X^{\rm rec}\rangle\bigr]_{i,j=1}^{X}.
\]
For $1\le n\le X$ put
\[
 \Pi_{X,n}:=\sum_{j=1}^{n}P_{j,X},
 \qquad
 Q_{X,n}:=P_{n,X}.
\]
The predictable-backflow residual of a chronology operator $A_X$ is
\[
 \mathfrak R_{{\rm back},X}(A_X)
 :=\sum_{n=1}^{X-1}
 \norm{\Pi_{X,n}A_XQ_{X,n}}_{\HS}^{2}
 +\norm{A_XQ_{X,X}}_{\HS}^{2}.
\]

\begin{theorem}[Identity chronology Gram, zero backflow, and unit margins]
\label{thm:ar-record-margins}
For $A_X=S_X^{\rm rec}$,
\[
 \boxed{G_X^{\rm chr}=I_X,}
 \qquad
 \boxed{\mathfrak R_{{\rm back},X}(S_X^{\rm rec})=0.}
\]
If $f_i$ is the terminal Read of record type $i$, then
\[
 \boxed{
 \bigl[\Pr(f_i\circ(S_X^{\rm rec})^{j-1}p_1)\bigr]_{i,j=1}^{X}
 =I_X.}
\]
The innovation lines are $Q_{X,n}\mathcal R_X$, every normalized innovation
edge is $E_{n+1,n}$, and every innovation norm and edge ratio is one.  For the
canonical endpoint source synthesis
\[
 R_X^{\rm rec}:\C^X\longrightarrow\mathcal R_X,
 \qquad R_X^{\rm rec}e_n=e_n,
\]
one has
\[
 \boxed{(R_X^{\rm rec})^*R_X^{\rm rec}=I_X.}
\]
Consequently the chronology, innovation, and endpoint frame lower bounds are
all exactly one, uniformly in $X$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The chronology orbit is the orthonormal basis
$e_1,\ldots,e_X$, proving the first identity.  The Read $f_i$ evaluates the
$i$th record coordinate, proving the operational identity.  Since the first
$n$ chronology vectors span
$\Span\{e_1,\ldots,e_n\}$, their successive orthogonal innovations are exactly
$\C e_n$.  The successor maps $e_n$ to $e_{n+1}$ with coefficient one, so its
innovation and polar edges are $E_{n+1,n}$.

For $n<X$,
\[
 S_X^{\rm rec}Q_{X,n}=E_{n+1,n}
\]
has range orthogonal to $\Ran\Pi_{X,n}$, while
$S_X^{\rm rec}Q_{X,X}=0$.  Every summand in the backflow residual therefore
vanishes.  Finally, $R_X^{\rm rec}$ is the identity isometry in the endpoint
basis.  All claimed lower margins are thus equal to one.
\end{proof}

% =============================================================================
\subsection{Unique natural Peano extension and coefficient-free incidence zeta}
\label{sec:ar-Peano-zeta}
% =============================================================================

For every integer $a\ge1$ use the overflow convention
$e_m=0$ for $m\notin\{1,\ldots,X\}$ and set
\[
 \boxed{
 L_{a,X}^{\rm P}
 :=\sum_{1\le b\le\lfloor X/a\rfloor}E_{ab,b},}
\]
so $L_{a,X}^{\rm P}=0$ when $a>X$.

\begin{theorem}[Universal normalized Peano extension]
\label{thm:ar-Peano-multiplication}
For each $a\ge1$, $L_{a,X}^{\rm P}$ is the unique operator on
$\mathcal R_X$ satisfying
\[
 \boxed{
 L_{a,X}^{\rm P}\eta_X^{\rm rec}
 =(S_X^{\rm rec})^{a-1}\eta_X^{\rm rec},
 \qquad
 L_{a,X}^{\rm P}S_X^{\rm rec}
 =(S_X^{\rm rec})^aL_{a,X}^{\rm P}.}
\]
It has the intrinsic chronology-word formula
\[
 \boxed{
 L_{a,X}^{\rm P}
 =\sum_{b\le X/a}
 (S_X^{\rm rec})^{ab-1}P_{1,X}
 ((S_X^{\rm rec})^*)^{b-1},}
\]
and therefore
\[
 \boxed{
 L_{a,X}^{\rm P}e_b=e_{ab},}
\]
with absorbing overflow.  Moreover,
\[
 \boxed{
 L_{a,X}^{\rm P}L_{b,X}^{\rm P}=L_{ab,X}^{\rm P},
 \qquad L_{1,X}^{\rm P}=I,
 \qquad [L_{a,X}^{\rm P},L_{b,X}^{\rm P}]=0.}
\]
Thus multiplicativity is forced by pointed successor recursion; it is not an
additional loading choice.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The displayed matrix-unit sum sends $e_b$ to $e_{ab}$ when $ab\le X$ and to
zero otherwise.  This proves the source and covariance relations.  Conversely,
if $L$ satisfies those relations, then for every $b$,
\[
 Le_b=L(S_X^{\rm rec})^{b-1}\eta_X^{\rm rec}
 =(S_X^{\rm rec})^{a(b-1)}L\eta_X^{\rm rec}
 =(S_X^{\rm rec})^{ab-1}\eta_X^{\rm rec}=e_{ab}.
\]
Hence $L=L_{a,X}^{\rm P}$.  Both
$L_{a,X}^{\rm P}L_{b,X}^{\rm P}$ and $L_{ab,X}^{\rm P}$ send $e_c$ to
$e_{abc}$, including overflow, proving multiplicativity.  The remaining
identities follow.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[No hidden edge amplitude]
\label{cor:ar-Peano-projections}
Every $L_{a,X}^{\rm P}$ is a partial isometry and
\[
 (L_{a,X}^{\rm P})^*L_{a,X}^{\rm P}
 =\sum_{b\le X/a}P_{b,X},
 \qquad
 L_{a,X}^{\rm P}(L_{a,X}^{\rm P})^*
 =\sum_{b\le X/a}P_{ab,X}.
\]
In particular, all nonzero deterministic multiplication edges have coefficient
one.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The nonzero columns and rows in the matrix-unit formula are pairwise distinct
orthonormal endpoint vectors.  Multiplying the matrix units gives the stated
initial and final projections.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Count and logarithmic-grading rigidity]
\label{thm:ar-count-rigidity}
The count history is the unique operator $D_X$ satisfying
\[
 D_X\eta_X^{\rm rec}=\eta_X^{\rm rec},
 \qquad [D_X,S_X^{\rm rec}]=S_X^{\rm rec}.
\]
Consequently $D_X=N_X^{\rm rec}$, and with
$H_X:=\log N_X^{\rm rec}$ one has
\[
 \boxed{
 N_X^{\rm rec}L_{a,X}^{\rm P}
 =aL_{a,X}^{\rm P}N_X^{\rm rec},
 \qquad
 [H_X,L_{a,X}^{\rm P}]=(\log a)L_{a,X}^{\rm P}.}
\]
Moreover, $H_X$ is the unique operator $K_X$ satisfying
$K_X\eta_X^{\rm rec}=0$ and
$[K_X,L_{a,X}^{\rm P}]=(\log a)L_{a,X}^{\rm P}$ for all $a\le X$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
If $D_X$ satisfies the first two relations, induction along the successor gives
$D_Xe_n=ne_n$, hence $D_X=N_X^{\rm rec}$.  Evaluating on $e_b$ gives
\[
 N_X^{\rm rec}L_{a,X}^{\rm P}e_b=ab\,e_{ab}
 =aL_{a,X}^{\rm P}N_X^{\rm rec}e_b
\]
and
\[
 [H_X,L_{a,X}^{\rm P}]e_b
 =(\log(ab)-\log b)e_{ab}
 =(\log a)L_{a,X}^{\rm P}e_b.
\]
For the last assertion, apply the commutator relation with $a=n$ to the anchor:
$K_Xe_n=(\log n)e_n$.  The endpoint vectors form a basis.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Naturality and protected-writer rigidity]
\label{thm:ar-Peano-naturality}
Let
$U:(\mathcal R_X,\eta_X^{\rm rec},S_X^{\rm rec})\to
(\mathcal R_X',\eta_X',S_X')$
be a source-fixing chronology unitary:
$U\eta_X^{\rm rec}=\eta_X'$ and
$US_X^{\rm rec}=S_X'U$.  Then automatically
\[
 \boxed{
 UN_X^{\rm rec}=N_X'U,
 \qquad
 UL_{a,X}^{\rm P}=L_{a,X}'U
 \quad(a\ge1).}
\]
A chronology self-isomorphism is the identity.  More generally, if a unitary
preserves every endpoint projection, every deterministic writer
$E_{n+1,n}$, and the anchor, then it is the identity.  Hence the normalized
Peano extension has no coordinate, phase, or basis-selection modulus.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The conjugate $UL_{a,X}^{\rm P}U^*$ satisfies the normalized Peano relations
for $(\eta_X',S_X')$, so uniqueness in
\Cref{thm:ar-Peano-multiplication} gives
$UL_{a,X}^{\rm P}U^*=L_{a,X}'$.  The same argument with the count relations
gives $UN_X^{\rm rec}U^*=N_X'$.  A chronology automorphism fixes
$e_n=(S_X^{\rm rec})^{n-1}\eta_X^{\rm rec}$ for every $n$.  For the final
claim, projection preservation gives $Ve_n=z_ne_n$; writer preservation gives
$z_{n+1}\overline z_n=1$, and the anchor fixes $z_1=1$.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Derived truncated multiplicative monoid and incidence zeta]
The normalized Peano histories represent the monoid
$\{1,\ldots,X\}\cup\{0\}$ with ordinary multiplication below cutoff and
absorbing overflow.  Its divisibility category has one arrow $b\to m$ exactly
when $b\mid m$.  Define
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathsf Z_X:=\sum_{a=1}^{X}L_{a,X}^{\rm P}
 =\sum_{\substack{1\le b,m\le X\\ b\mid m}}E_{m,b},
 \qquad H_X:=\log N_X^{\rm rec}.}
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Universal unit-weight characterization of the finite zeta history]
\label{thm:ar-zeta-incidence}
The operator $\mathsf Z_X$ is the unique $Z\in\mathcal T_X^+$ satisfying
\[
 \boxed{
 P_{m,X}ZP_{b,X}
 =\begin{cases}
 E_{m,b},&b\mid m,\\
 0,&b\nmid m.
 \end{cases}}
\]
Equivalently, it is the unit-coefficient linearization of every divisibility
arrow derived from Peano recursion.  It is unitriangular, so
$\mathsf Z_X-I$ is nilpotent and $\mathsf Z_X^{-1}$ and
$\log\mathsf Z_X$ are terminating polynomials.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
For fixed $b$, the summand $L_{a,X}^{\rm P}$ sends $e_b$ to $e_{ab}$.
For every multiple $m$ of $b$ there is exactly one ratio $a=m/b$, and no other
summand contributes to the $(m,b)$ matrix coefficient.  These coefficients
determine the operator uniquely.  The diagonal arrows are exactly the
$a=1$ terms; every other arrow raises the endpoint label, proving nilpotence.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Why the coefficient one is not fitted]
The coefficient is the unit of the ground field assigned uniformly to each
derived deterministic arrow.  It depends on neither the multiplier, primality,
a character, a target $L$-function, nor a measured coefficient table.  The
deformation theorem below identifies exactly what parameters would appear if
this operational normalization were relaxed.
\end{remark}

\begin{theorem}[Finite Euler logarithm, von Mangoldt commutator, and M\"obius inverse]
\label{thm:ar-finite-Euler}
The truncated multiplication histories satisfy
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathsf Z_X
 =\prod_{p\le X}(I-L_{p,X}^{\rm P})^{-1},}
\]
where each inverse is its terminating geometric series.  Moreover,
\[
 \boxed{
 \log\mathsf Z_X
 =\sum_{p^k\le X}\frac1kL_{p^k,X}^{\rm P},}
 \qquad
 \boxed{
 \mathsf Z_X^{-1}
 =\sum_{n\le X}\mu(n)L_{n,X}^{\rm P},}
\]
and
\[
 \boxed{
 [H_X,\log\mathsf Z_X]
 =\sum_{n\le X}\Lambda(n)L_{n,X}^{\rm P}.}
\]
Consequently
\[
 \boxed{
 [H_X,\log\mathsf Z_X]\eta_X^{\rm rec}
 =\sum_{n\le X}\Lambda(n)e_n,}
 \qquad
 \boxed{
 \mathsf Z_X^{-1}\eta_X^{\rm rec}
 =\sum_{n\le X}\mu(n)e_n.}
\]
The target coefficients occur only in these proved expansions; they are not
entrance data.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
For a prime $p$, $L_{p,X}^{\rm P}$ is nilpotent and
\[
 (I-L_{p,X}^{\rm P})^{-1}
 =\sum_{k\ge0,\ p^k\le X}L_{p^k,X}^{\rm P}.
\]
Unique factorization assigns exactly one surviving product term to each
$n\le X$, proving the Euler product.  All factors commute and the strictly
forward ideal is nilpotent, so the formal logarithm is an exact terminating
polynomial:
\[
 \log\mathsf Z_X
 =-\sum_p\log(I-L_{p,X}^{\rm P})
 =\sum_{p^k\le X}\frac1kL_{p^k,X}^{\rm P}.
\]
Expanding $\prod_p(I-L_{p,X}^{\rm P})$ chooses each prime at most once; the
coefficient is $(-1)^{\omega(n)}$ on squarefree $n$ and zero otherwise, hence
$\mu(n)$.  Finally
$[H_X,L_{p^k,X}^{\rm P}]=\log(p^k)L_{p^k,X}^{\rm P}$, so commuting the
Euler logarithm with $H_X$ replaces $1/k$ by $\log p$, which is exactly
$\Lambda$ on prime powers.  Apply the last two identities to the anchor.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Complete classification of fit-like scalar deformations]
\label{thm:ar-loading-deformations}
Let $M_{a,X}$ satisfy
\[
 M_{a,X}S_X^{\rm rec}=(S_X^{\rm rec})^aM_{a,X},
 \qquad
 M_{a,X}\eta_X^{\rm rec}
 =c_{a,X}(S_X^{\rm rec})^{a-1}\eta_X^{\rm rec}.
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{M_{a,X}=c_{a,X}L_{a,X}^{\rm P}.}
\]
If $M_{1,X}=I$ and
$M_{a,X}M_{b,X}=M_{ab,X}$ below cutoff, then
$c_{1,X}=1$ and $c_{ab,X}=c_{a,X}c_{b,X}$.  For a cutoff-compatible family,
the stabilized coefficients form a completely multiplicative function
$c:\N\to\C$, and the corresponding zeta history is exactly
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathsf Z_{c,X}
 :=\sum_{n\le X}c(n)L_{n,X}^{\rm P}
 =\prod_{p\le X}(I-c(p)L_{p,X}^{\rm P})^{-1}.}
\]
Conversely every relaxed, natural, multiplicative Peano loading is of this
form.  Thus the prime-local parameters $c(p)$ are the complete scalar fitting
family, and deterministic source normalization is precisely the condition
$c(p)=1$ for every prime.

Likewise, if $D_X\eta_X^{\rm rec}=\alpha\eta_X^{\rm rec}$ and
$[D_X,S_X^{\rm rec}]=\beta S_X^{\rm rec}$, then
\[
 \boxed{
 D_X=\sum_{n=1}^X(\alpha+(n-1)\beta)P_{n,X}.}
\]
The protected count normalization fixes $(\alpha,\beta)=(1,1)$, so no origin
or step-size modulus remains.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
For every endpoint basis vector,
\[
 M_{a,X}e_b
 =M_{a,X}(S_X^{\rm rec})^{b-1}\eta_X^{\rm rec}
 =(S_X^{\rm rec})^{a(b-1)}M_{a,X}\eta_X^{\rm rec}
 =c_{a,X}e_{ab},
\]
which proves the scalar classification.  Multiplicativity and the nonzero
operator $L_{ab,X}^{\rm P}$ give $c_{ab,X}=c_{a,X}c_{b,X}$.  Compatible
compression identifies the same coefficient at all larger cutoffs.  Expanding
the terminating geometric factors and using unique factorization gives the
weighted Euler product; the converse follows from the first classification.
For the count deformation, induction along the successor gives
$D_Xe_n=(\alpha+(n-1)\beta)e_n$.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Positive Peano and count residuals]
For candidate histories $A_{a,X}$ and $D_X$, put
\[
 \Delta_{a,X}^{\rm Peano}(A_{a,X})
 :=\norm{A_{a,X}\eta_X^{\rm rec}
          -(S_X^{\rm rec})^{a-1}\eta_X^{\rm rec}}^2
   +\norm{A_{a,X}S_X^{\rm rec}
          -(S_X^{\rm rec})^aA_{a,X}}_{\HS}^2,
\]
\[
 \Delta_X^{\rm count}(D_X)
 :=\norm{D_X\eta_X^{\rm rec}-\eta_X^{\rm rec}}^2
   +\norm{[D_X,S_X^{\rm rec}]-S_X^{\rm rec}}_{\HS}^2.
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Finite zero-residual and stability certificate]
\label{thm:ar-Peano-stability}
One has
\[
 \Delta_{a,X}^{\rm Peano}(A_{a,X})=0
 \iff A_{a,X}=L_{a,X}^{\rm P},
 \qquad
 \Delta_X^{\rm count}(D_X)=0
 \iff D_X=N_X^{\rm rec}.
\]
Moreover,
\[
 \boxed{
 \norm{A_{a,X}-L_{a,X}^{\rm P}}_{\HS}^2
 \le X^2\Delta_{a,X}^{\rm Peano}(A_{a,X}),}
\]
\[
 \boxed{
 \norm{D_X-N_X^{\rm rec}}_{\HS}^2
 \le X^2\Delta_X^{\rm count}(D_X).}
\]
Every residual term is a positive finite word-Gram expression in the Grand
Tensor; hence uniqueness is a terminating basis-free audit.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The zero criteria are the uniqueness statements above.  Put
$B=A_{a,X}-L_{a,X}^{\rm P}$,
$r=B\eta_X^{\rm rec}$, and
$R=BS_X^{\rm rec}-(S_X^{\rm rec})^aB$.  If $d_b=Be_b$, then
\[
 d_{b+1}=(S_X^{\rm rec})^ad_b+Re_b.
\]
Because $(S_X^{\rm rec})^a$ is a contraction,
\[
 \norm{d_b}
 \le\norm r+\sum_{j<b}\norm{Re_j}.
\]
Cauchy--Schwarz yields
$\norm{d_b}^2\le X(\norm r^2+\norm R_{\HS}^2)$; summing over $b\le X$
gives the first bound.  The count estimate is identical with
$B=D_X-N_X^{\rm rec}$ and
$R=[D_X,S_X^{\rm rec}]-S_X^{\rm rec}$.
\end{proof}

% =============================================================================
\subsection{The complete basic arithmetic packet is internal}
\label{sec:ar-derived-packet}
% =============================================================================

For $h\in\Z$ define the truncated additive shift
\[
 T_{h,X}:=\sum_{\substack{1\le n\le X\\1\le n+h\le X}}E_{n+h,n};
\]
thus $T_{h,X}=(S_X^{\rm rec})^h$ for $h\ge0$ and
$T_{h,X}=((S_X^{\rm rec})^*)^{-h}$ for $h<0$.  For
$\theta\in\R$, $\sigma,t\ge0$, and $\tau\in\R$, put
\[
 A_X(\theta):=e^{2\pi i\theta N_X^{\rm rec}},
 \qquad
 \mathcal M_X(\sigma,\tau,t)
 :=e^{-(\sigma+i\tau)H_X-tH_X^2}.
\]
For a modulus $q$ and residue $r\bmod q$, define
\[
 P_{r,q;X}:=\sum_{\substack{n\le X\\n\equiv r\ (q)}}P_{n,X}.
\]
If $\chi$ is a Dirichlet character modulo $q$, define
\[
 D_{\chi,X}:=\sum_{r\bmod q}\chi(r)P_{r,q;X}
 =\sum_{n\le X}\chi(n)P_{n,X}.
\]

The atoms of the derived truncated multiplicative monoid are exactly the
integers $p>1$ which admit no factorization $p=ab$ with $a,b>1$; these are the
usual primes.  Unique factorization therefore defines, intrinsically from the
Peano product, the diagonal depth operators
\[
 \Omega_X:=\sum_{n\le X}\Omega(n)P_{n,X},
 \qquad
 \omega_X:=\sum_{n\le X}\omega(n)P_{n,X},
\]
the squarefree projection and factor-depth projections
\[
 Q_X^{\rm sf}:=\sum_{\substack{n\le X\\\Omega(n)=\omega(n)}}P_{n,X},
 \qquad
 P_{j,X}^{\Omega}:=\sum_{\substack{n\le X\\\Omega(n)=j}}P_{n,X}.
\]
These are finite spectral projections of the commuting diagonal depth
operators.

\begin{theorem}[Internal character, affine, Mellin, and factor-depth histories]
\label{thm:ar-derived-packet}
Every operator just defined belongs to the record history algebra
$M_X(\C)$.  They satisfy
\[
 D_{\chi,X}D_{\psi,X}=D_{\chi\psi,X},
 \qquad
 D_{\chi,X}^*=D_{\overline\chi,X},
\]
\[
 A_X(\theta)e_n=e^{2\pi in\theta}e_n,
 \qquad
 \mathcal M_X(\sigma,\tau,t)e_n
 =n^{-\sigma-i\tau}e^{-t(\log n)^2}e_n,
\]
and the shifts have the exact partial-isometry boundary action
$T_{h,X}e_n=e_{n+h}$ when $1\le n+h\le X$, and zero otherwise.  The prime,
Liouville, and M\"obius diagonal histories are
\[
 P_{\mathbb P,X}=P_{1,X}^{\Omega},
 \qquad
 D_{\lambda,X}=(-1)^{\Omega_X},
 \qquad
 D_{\mu,X}=Q_X^{\rm sf}(-1)^{\Omega_X}.
\]
For every Dirichlet character $\chi$,
\[
 \boxed{
 \begin{aligned}
 v_{\chi,X}(\sigma,\tau,t,\theta)
 :={}&A_X(\theta)D_{\chi,X}\mathcal M_X(\sigma,\tau,t)
 [H_X,\log\mathsf Z_X]\eta_X^{\rm rec}\\
 ={}&\sum_{n\le X}\chi(n)\Lambda(n)n^{-\sigma-i\tau}
 e^{-t(\log n)^2}e^{2\pi in\theta}e_n.
 \end{aligned}}
\]
Hence the anchor, endpoint, residue, character, affine, logarithmic, Mellin,
heat, prime/von Mangoldt, M\"obius, Liouville, prime-only, factor-depth, and
finite-window columns are internal histories or finite functional-calculus
panels of one source-complete record corner.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
By \Cref{thm:ar-record-algebra}, every matrix unit belongs to
$M_X(\C)$, so the shifts and every finite diagonal sum belong to it.  The count
operator has simple spectrum $\{1,\ldots,X\}$; finite functional calculus
therefore gives the affine, logarithmic, Mellin, heat, and indicator operators.
The character relations hold coordinatewise.  The shift and diagonal actions
follow directly from their definitions.

The Peano product recognizes reducibility of an endpoint label: $n>1$ is an
atom exactly when no product $L_{a,X}^{\rm P}L_{b,X}^{\rm P}\eta_X^{\rm rec}$
with $a,b>1$ equals $e_n$.  This is the usual primality condition.  Repeated
factorization strictly decreases the factors and therefore terminates;
uniqueness is the ordinary uniqueness of prime factorization.  Thus
$\Omega_X$, $\omega_X$, and their spectral projections are determined by the
derived monoid, and the displayed diagonal formulas give the usual prime,
Liouville, and M\"obius values.

Finally, \Cref{thm:ar-finite-Euler} gives the coefficient $\Lambda(n)$ before
any diagonal twist is applied.  Applying the character, Mellin--heat, and
affine diagonal operators multiplies its $n$th endpoint coordinate by the
three displayed factors, proving the source expansion.
\end{proof}

% =============================================================================
\subsection{Cutoff compatibility and standard arithmetic recognition}
\label{sec:ar-record-comparison}
% =============================================================================

For $X\le Y$, let
\[
 J_{XY}^{\rm rec}:\mathcal R_X\longrightarrow\mathcal R_Y,
 \qquad J_{XY}^{\rm rec}e_n=e_n,
\]
and put $P_{XY}=J_{XY}^{\rm rec}(J_{XY}^{\rm rec})^*$ and
$\pi_{XY}(A)=(J_{XY}^{\rm rec})^*AJ_{XY}^{\rm rec}$.

\begin{theorem}[Forward arithmetic compression is a unital algebra homomorphism]
\label{thm:ar-record-cutoff}
The map
\[
 \boxed{\pi_{XY}:\mathcal T_Y^+\longrightarrow\mathcal T_X^+}
\]
is a unital algebra homomorphism.  In particular,
\[
 \boxed{
 \pi_{XY}(S_Y^{\rm rec})=S_X^{\rm rec},
 \qquad
 \pi_{XY}(N_Y^{\rm rec})=N_X^{\rm rec},
 \qquad
 \pi_{XY}(L_{a,Y}^{\rm P})=L_{a,X}^{\rm P}.}
\]
It carries $\mathsf Z_Y$, $\mathsf Z_Y^{-1}$,
$\log\mathsf Z_Y$, $[H_Y,\log\mathsf Z_Y]$, and every forward residue,
character, affine, Mellin, heat, window, and factor-depth history exactly to
its cutoff-$X$ counterpart.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Relative to
$\mathcal R_Y=J_{XY}^{\rm rec}\mathcal R_X\oplus
(J_{XY}^{\rm rec}\mathcal R_X)^\perp$, every forward operator has block form
$\begin{psmallmatrix}A_{11}&0\\A_{21}&A_{22}\end{psmallmatrix}$, because a
tail input cannot move backward into the first $X$ endpoints.  The upper-left
block of a product is therefore $A_{11}B_{11}$, proving multiplicativity of
compression.  The generator identities follow from their endpoint actions.
The remaining identities follow from finite sums, the terminating polynomial
formulas for inverse and logarithm, commutators of forward histories, and
finite diagonal functional calculus.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Absorbing-corner evaluation]
For a cutoff-$Y$ word $w=A_k\cdots A_1$ whose letters compress individually,
define
\[
 \boxed{
 \operatorname{Abs}_{XY}(w)
 :=(J_{XY}^{\rm rec})^*A_kP_{XY}A_{k-1}P_{XY}\cdots
 P_{XY}A_1J_{XY}^{\rm rec}.}
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Exact, unique, and transitive absorbing-word naturality]
\label{thm:ar-absorbing-cutoff}
For every word, including arbitrary adjoints,
\[
 \boxed{
 \operatorname{Abs}_{XY}(A_k\cdots A_1)
 =\pi_{XY}(A_k)\cdots\pi_{XY}(A_1).}
\]
This is the unique word-evaluation rule agreeing with individual letter
compression and multiplicative under concatenation.  For $X\le Y\le Z$, it is
transitive: direct cutoff from $Z$ to $X$ equals letterwise cutoff to $Y$
followed by the cutoff-$X$ word product.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Insert $P_{XY}=J_{XY}^{\rm rec}(J_{XY}^{\rm rec})^*$ between consecutive
compressed letters:
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \pi_{XY}(A_k)\cdots\pi_{XY}(A_1)
 &=(J^*A_kJ)(J^*A_{k-1}J)\cdots(J^*A_1J)\\
 &=J^*A_kP_{XY}A_{k-1}P_{XY}\cdots P_{XY}A_1J.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Any multiplicative rule agreeing on letters must equal the product on the
right.  Nested chronology inclusions compose, so individual compression from
$Z$ to $X$ is the composite of the two intermediate compressions; applying
the displayed identity at both stages proves transitivity.
\end{proof}

\begin{countertheorem}[No unital full-matrix cutoff functor over all cutoffs]
\label{cth:ar-no-unital-matrix-cutoff}
For $X,Y\ge2$, a unital $*$-homomorphism
$M_X(\C)\to M_Y(\C)$ exists if and only if $X$ divides $Y$.  Hence ordinary
cutoff inclusions $X\le Y$ cannot in general be represented by unital
$*$-homomorphisms of the full matrix closures.  The forward projective algebra
and absorbing-corner rule are therefore mathematically necessary, not an ad
hoc weakening.
\end{countertheorem}

\begin{proof}
A unital $*$-homomorphism from the simple algebra $M_X(\C)$ is injective and
makes $\C^Y$ a unital finite-dimensional $M_X(\C)$-module.  Every such module
is a direct sum of copies of the defining $X$-dimensional module, so $Y=rX$.
Conversely, when $Y=rX$, the map $A\mapsto A\otimes I_r$ is a unital
$*$-homomorphism.
\end{proof}

Let $\mathcal K_X^{\rm std}=\ell^2\{1,\ldots,X\}$ have orthonormal basis
$\varepsilon_n$, standard truncated successor $J_X^{\rm std}$, count
$N_X^{\rm std}$, and standard multiplication $L_{a,X}^{\rm std}$.

\begin{theorem}[Source-fixing monoidal comparison with standard arithmetic]
\label{thm:ar-standard-comparison}
The endpoint-label map
\[
 \boxed{
 U_X^{\rm ar}:\mathcal K_X^{\rm std}\longrightarrow\mathcal R_X,
 \qquad U_X^{\rm ar}\varepsilon_n=e_n}
\]
is the unique source-fixing unitary satisfying
\[
 U_X^{\rm ar}J_X^{\rm std}=S_X^{\rm rec}U_X^{\rm ar},
 \qquad
 U_X^{\rm ar}N_X^{\rm std}=N_X^{\rm rec}U_X^{\rm ar},
\]
\[
 U_X^{\rm ar}L_{a,X}^{\rm std}=L_{a,X}^{\rm P}U_X^{\rm ar}.
\]
It is fixed before any prime or character coefficient is formed.  It
intertwines every operator in the basic arithmetic packet, and therefore all
word Grams and all finite transfer panels of the standard and record
realizations agree.

If $S_X^{\rm std}$ is any standard source synthesis and
$S_X^{\rm can}:=U_X^{\rm ar}S_X^{\rm std}$, then, after transport to the same
carrier, the source maps are equal.  Their two mutual Schur residuals and every
stabilized transfer-panel residual vanish identically.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The endpoint-label map sends one orthonormal basis to another and is therefore
unitary and unique.  The three displayed intertwinings follow from the basis
actions.  Every basic arithmetic operator is a fixed finite algebraic or
functional-calculus expression in the source, successor, count, and Peano
multiplication histories, so all further intertwinings follow by substitution.
Unitarity preserves all word inner products and transfer panels.

After transport, $S_X^{\rm can}=U_X^{\rm ar}S_X^{\rm std}$ by definition.
Writing the common source Gram as $A$, the cross and second marginal Grams are
also $A$.  Hence
\[
 A-AA^\dagger A=0
\]
by the Moore--Penrose identity.  The reverse residual is identical, and the
transfer residuals vanish by the established intertwining.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Canonical prime explicit-formula readout and compiler routing]
\label{thm:ar-explicit-compiler-routing}
Let $\mathscr M_X$ have basis
$\delta_{\log1},\ldots,\delta_{\log X}$ and define
\[
 \mathcal E_Xe_n:=\delta_{\log n}.
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal E_XD_{\chi,X}[H_X,\log\mathsf Z_X]\eta_X^{\rm rec}
 =\sum_{n\le X}\chi(n)\Lambda(n)\delta_{\log n}.}
\]
Applying $\mathcal L_s(\delta_u)=e^{-su}$ gives
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal L_s\mathcal E_XD_{\chi,X}
 [H_X,\log\mathsf Z_X]\eta_X^{\rm rec}
 =\sum_{n\le X}\frac{\chi(n)\Lambda(n)}{n^s}.}
\]

Let $\mathcal T_X$ be a finite compiler-history bank with numerical endpoint
$n(t)$ and positive weights $a_t$.  Define the unweighted endpoint map and the canonical endpoint writer by
\[
 \boxed{
 J_X^{\rm end}e_t:=\sqrt{a_t}\,e_{n(t)},
 \qquad
 \mathcal C_X^{\rm rec}e_t:=\sqrt{a_t}\,e_{n(t)}.}
\]
Thus $\mathcal C_X^{\rm rec}=J_X^{\rm end}$.  If
\[
 A_{n,X}:=\sum_{t:n(t)=n}a_t,
\]
then
\[
 \mathcal C_X^{\rm rec}(\mathcal C_X^{\rm rec})^*
 =\sum_{n\le X}A_{n,X}P_{n,X},
 \qquad
 (\mathcal C_X^{\rm rec})^*\mathcal C_X^{\rm rec}
 =(J_X^{\rm end})^*J_X^{\rm end}.
\]
After quotienting by $\Ker J_X^{\rm end}$ there is exactly one source line per
retained endpoint; on endpoints with $A_{n,X}>0$, canonical endpoint whitening
gives identity Gram.  The intrinsic endpoint synthesis $R_X^{\rm rec}$ itself
already has Gram $I_X$.  If compiler concatenation obeys
$n(uv)=n(u)n(v)$ with overflow sent to zero, this writer descends to the Peano
product.  If an exact compiler identity collects coefficient $\Lambda(n)$,
its routed prime state equals
$[H_X,\log\mathsf Z_X]\eta_X^{\rm rec}$ on the same carrier.  Hence their
cross Grams, mutual source Schur residuals, and Peano transfer panels agree
exactly.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The first identity follows by applying the spectral writer to the source
formula of \Cref{thm:ar-finite-Euler}; the Laplace identity uses
$e^{-s\log n}=n^{-s}$.  For the compiler writer,
\[
 \mathcal C_X^{\rm rec}\sum_tc_te_t
 =\sum_{n\le X}
 \left(\sum_{t:n(t)=n}c_t\sqrt{a_t}\right)e_n,
\]
so equal endpoints coalesce.  Multiplying this formula by its adjoint gives
$\sum_nA_{n,X}P_{n,X}$, while the reverse product is
$(J_X^{\rm end})^*J_X^{\rm end}$.  Quotienting by the common kernel leaves one
coordinate for each retained endpoint, and multiplication by
$\sum_{A_{n,X}>0}A_{n,X}^{-1/2}P_{n,X}$ whitens its endpoint marginal.  For
basis histories $u,v$, multiplicativity of $n$ gives
\[
 e_{n(uv)}=L_{n(u),X}^{\rm P}e_{n(v)},
\]
with both sides zero on overflow; bilinearity proves descent.  If the compiler
coefficient is $\Lambda(n)$, both routed states are the same expansion in the
same orthonormal endpoint basis.  Equality of source maps implies the Schur and
transfer conclusions by \Cref{thm:source-Schur}.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Optional comparison with an older physical response]
\label{prop:ar-old-response}
Let $J_X^{\rm end}:\mathcal T_X\to\mathcal R_X$ be the canonical endpoint
writer and let $C_X^{\rm old}:\mathcal T_X\to\mathcal H_X^{\rm old}$ be any
independently measured older response.  Put
$P_J=(J_X^{\rm end})^\dagger J_X^{\rm end}$.  Then
\[
 \boxed{
 C_X^{\rm old}=R_X^{\rm old}J_X^{\rm end}
 +C_X^{\rm old}(I-P_J),
 \qquad
 R_X^{\rm old}:=C_X^{\rm old}(J_X^{\rm end})^\dagger.}
\]
The second term is the exact endpoint-innovation defect.  Its vanishing is
equivalent to factorization through the canonical endpoint quotient.  If it
vanishes and $(R_X^{\rm old})^*R_X^{\rm old}\succ0$, polar whitening gives a
source-fixing isometry from the canonical record source to the old response
range.  These are optional empirical conditions and are not assumptions for
the existence of the canonical arithmetic loading.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
$P_J$ is the orthogonal projection onto
$(\Ker J_X^{\rm end})^\perp$.  Hence
\[
 C_X^{\rm old}P_J
 =C_X^{\rm old}(J_X^{\rm end})^\dagger J_X^{\rm end}
 =R_X^{\rm old}J_X^{\rm end},
\]
which proves the decomposition.  The defect vanishes exactly when
$C_X^{\rm old}=R_X^{\rm old}J_X^{\rm end}$.  If the response Gram is positive
definite, then
$R_X^{\rm old}((R_X^{\rm old})^*R_X^{\rm old})^{-1/2}$ is an isometry; source
minimality gives the source-fixing comparison on its range.
\end{proof}

% =============================================================================
\subsection{Arithmetic loading packet and exact finite hierarchy}
\label{sec:arithmetic-loading-packet}
% =============================================================================

\begin{definition}[Canonical arithmetic loading from universal records]
\label{def:arithmetic-loading}
At cutoff $X$, the \emph{canonical basic arithmetic loading} is the admissible
domain loading in $\mathcal A_X^{\rm hist}$ whose selected universal histories
are
\[
 \eta_X^{\rm rec},\quad S_X^{\rm rec},\quad N_X^{\rm rec},
\]
and whose remaining basic histories are the internally derived operators
\[
 (L_{a,X}^{\rm P})_{a\le X},\quad\mathsf Z_X,
\]
together with the residue, character, affine, Mellin, heat, von Mangoldt,
M\"obius, Liouville, prime-only, factor-depth, endpoint, and window histories
of \Cref{thm:ar-derived-packet}.  No genuinely arithmetic generator is inserted
at the entrance: the arithmetic relations derive the packet from the selected
neutral chronology corner.

An \emph{enriched arithmetic loading} adjoins any finite collection of
independently constructed Smith--Gale, congruence, source-short, analytic-jet,
determinant-line, fixed-modulus, Jacobi, Kloosterman, Frobenius, Whittaker,
conductor, or spectral panels.  Every enrichment must act on the same covered
carrier or be connected to it by an explicit router, and every claimed relation
must pass the positive residual test of
\Cref{def:loaded-relation-residual}.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Arithmetic loaded Renewal Grand Tensor]
\label{def:arithmetic-loaded-tensor}
Let $W_{{\rm ar},X,r}$ synthesize all composable words of length at most $r$ in
the canonical basic packet and any declared enrichment.  Define
\[
 \boxed{
 \boldsymbol{\mathbb T}^{\rm ar}_{\Grand,X}
 :=\{\mathbb K^{{\rm ar}}_{X,r}\}_{r\ge0},
 \qquad
 \mathbb K^{{\rm ar}}_{X,r}
 :=W_{{\rm ar},X,r}^*W_{{\rm ar},X,r}.}
\]
It is retained with the endpoint types, word product, involution, and all
Fourier, Mellin, affine, factor-depth, Smith--Gale, source-short, jet,
determinant, and enriched transfer panels actually constructed.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Unique natural unconditional arithmetic loading theorem]
\label{thm:arithmetic-loading}
Let the full operational Grand Tensor exist at cutoff $X$.  Then its protected
chronology record carries the unique natural, normalized arithmetic loading
with the following exact properties.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(A\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item The chronology source, successor, endpoint Reads, deterministic writers,
      and oriented algebra $\mathcal T_X^+$ are internal.  The chronology and
      endpoint source Grams are $I_X$, predictable backflow is zero, and all
      structural source margins equal one.
\item For every $a$, the anchor and Peano covariance relations have exactly one
      solution $L_{a,X}^{\rm P}$.  They force absorbing multiplication,
      commutativity, the count history, and the logarithmic grading; none is an
      independently chosen endpoint table.
\item The finite zeta history is the unique unit-weight linearization of the
      divisibility category derived from that multiplication.  Its terminating
      inverse, logarithm, and logarithmic commutator derive the M\"obius and von
      Mangoldt histories before target coefficients are invoked.
\item Every source-fixing chronology isomorphism automatically intertwines the
      count, all multiplication histories, the zeta calculus, and the complete
      residue--character--affine--Mellin--heat--depth packet.  A source-and-writer
      fixing chronology automorphism is the identity.
\item If unit-source normalization is relaxed, every natural Peano-covariant
      alternative is $c(a)L_{a,X}^{\rm P}$.  Multiplicativity and cutoff
      compatibility make $c$ completely multiplicative and produce exactly the
      weighted Euler factors $(I-c(p)L_{p,X}^{\rm P})^{-1}$.  The protected
      deterministic normalization fixes every $c(p)=1$ and removes the entire
      scalar fitting family; count origin and step are similarly rigid.
\item The positive Peano and count residuals vanish exactly on the canonical
      histories and obey the explicit $X^2$ stability bounds of
      \Cref{thm:ar-Peano-stability}.  Hence uniqueness is a finite Grand-Tensor
      certificate rather than a target-basis identification.
\item The loaded word hierarchy is positive, reaches finite flat depth, and
      reconstructs its complete finite arithmetic history $*$-algebra up to the
      unique loading-fixing, record-preserving unitary.
\item Forward histories form an exact projective cutoff family under unital
      algebra compression.  Arbitrary adjoint words descend exactly and
      transitively by absorbing corners.  No impossible unital full-matrix
      cutoff functor is assumed.
\item The endpoint-label unitary is the unique source-fixing chronology unitary
      to the standard finite arithmetic realization and intertwines the complete
      packet; stabilized word Grams, transfer panels, and correctly matched
      source Schur residuals agree.
\item The atomic prime explicit-formula source and the canonically routed
      arithmetic compiler are readouts of this same record packet.  Discarding
      the universal record recovers the record-forgetting predictive core and
      all original intervention statistics.
\end{enumerate}
Therefore
\[
 \boxed{
 \boldsymbol{\mathbb T}^{\min,op}_{\Grand,X}
 \Longrightarrow
 \boldsymbol{\mathbb T}^{\rm ar,can}_{\Grand,X}}
\]
is unconditional relative to the operationally complete structural entrance,
and the resulting packet is not merely an internal copy in $M_X(\C)$: it is
the unique natural, normalized multiplicative extension of protected pointed
chronology.  This theorem alone implies neither PCJM12 nor a critical-line,
parity-breaking, additive-prime, or determinant-line estimate.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Internal chronology and unit margins are
\Cref{thm:ar-record-algebra,thm:ar-record-completion,thm:ar-record-margins,prop:ar-forward-generation}.  Unique Peano multiplication, count rigidity,
naturality, and the incidence-zeta calculus are
\Cref{thm:ar-Peano-multiplication,thm:ar-count-rigidity,thm:ar-Peano-naturality,thm:ar-zeta-incidence,thm:ar-finite-Euler}.
The complete deformation classification and positive finite audit are
\Cref{thm:ar-loading-deformations,thm:ar-Peano-stability}.  The remaining basic
packet is \Cref{thm:ar-derived-packet}.  Applying
\Cref{thm:loaded-subhierarchy} gives positivity, finite flatness, and monoidal
reconstruction.  Exact forward cutoff descent, arbitrary-word absorption, and
the obstruction to full-matrix functoriality are
\Cref{thm:ar-record-cutoff,thm:ar-absorbing-cutoff,cth:ar-no-unital-matrix-cutoff}.  Standard recognition is
\Cref{thm:ar-standard-comparison}; the explicit-formula and compiler statements
are \Cref{thm:ar-explicit-compiler-routing}.  Record-discard conservativity is
\Cref{thm:operational-record-completion}.  None of these arguments contains a
conjecture-specific coercive or signed estimate.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[Exact scope of unconditional arithmetic emergence]
\label{fire:arithmetic-native-loading}
The basic arithmetic tensor is unconditional on the full operational tensor,
not on the record-discarded predictive core; the latter claim is ruled out by
\Cref{cth:ar-unrecorded-no-go}.  The universal record stores chronology, not a
fitted vector with preassigned coordinates
$\chi(n)\Lambda(n)n^{-s}$.  Those coordinates arise from the unique normalized
Peano extension, its unit-weight incidence zeta, and subsequent intrinsic
diagonal actions.  The complete relaxed scalar family has been classified as
$c(a)L_{a,X}^{\rm P}$, so unit-source normalization visibly removes every
prime-local Euler-weight modulus rather than hiding it.  Identity with an
unrelated older laboratory port is an optional physical comparison governed by
\Cref{prop:ar-old-response}.  PCJM12, GRH coercivity, selector-stable signed
parity, Goldbach or twin-prime lower bounds, Frobenius--Whittaker enrichment,
and analytic--Selmer determinant-line comparison remain downstream theorems.
\end{firewall}

\subsection{Anchored, reflected, normal--anomalous arithmetic ports}
\label{sec:arithmetic-sector}

The endpoint source basis is fixed by the canonical record packet.  Let $w_X$
be finitely supported and let $a_\alpha(n)\in\C$ be the coefficients of any
finite diagonal readout on that basis, including the character--von Mangoldt,
M\"obius, factor-depth, or enriched compiler readouts constructed above.  Put
\[
 F_{\alpha,X}(s,\theta)
 :=\sum_{n\ge1}a_\alpha(n)w_X(n)n^{-s}e^{2\pi in\theta},
 \qquad (s,\theta)\in\C\times\Torus,
\]
and adjoin the anchor $F_{\star,X}=1$.  Define
\[
 (\mathcal CF)(s,\theta)=\overline{F(\bar s,\theta)},
 \qquad
 (\mathcal MF)(s,\theta)=F(1-\bar s,\theta).
\]
The involutions $\mathcal C$ and $\mathcal M$ commute.  With
$\mathfrak K=\{I,\mathcal C,\mathcal M,\mathcal M\mathcal C\}$, let
\[
 \bm\Phi_X(s,\theta)
 =\left(1,(gF_{\alpha,X}(s,\theta))_{\alpha,g}\right)^{\mathsf T},
 \qquad
 \mathbb T_X^{\rm port}(s,\theta)
 =\bm\Phi_X(s,\theta)\bm\Phi_X(s,\theta)^*.
\]

\begin{proposition}[Anchor recovery and finite port positivity]
\label{prop:ar-anchor}
For every $(s,\theta)$,
$\mathbb T_X^{\rm port}(s,\theta)\succeq0$ and has rank at most one.  Its
cross-entry with the anchor recovers every component $gF_{\alpha,X}$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
The matrix is an outer product.  Its $(g,\alpha;\star)$ entry is
$gF_{\alpha,X}\overline{1}=gF_{\alpha,X}$.
\end{proof}

For real $\sigma$, define the normal and anomalous affine marginals
\[
 \mathcal D_{\alpha\beta,X}(h;\sigma)
 :=\int_0^1F_{\alpha,X}(\sigma,\theta)
       \overline{F_{\beta,X}(\sigma,\theta)}e^{-2\pi ih\theta}\dd\theta,
\]
\[
 \mathcal H_{\alpha\beta,X}(N;\sigma)
 :=\int_0^1F_{\alpha,X}(\sigma,\theta)
       F_{\beta,X}(\sigma,\theta)e^{-2\pi iN\theta}\dd\theta.
\]
The second is a Hermitian tensor entry after pairing the second factor with its
charge-conjugate type.

\begin{theorem}[Normal and anomalous arithmetic grades]
\label{thm:prime-readouts}
For every integer $h$ and $N$,
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal D_{\alpha\beta,X}(h;\sigma)
 =\sum_{m-n=h}a_\alpha(m)\overline{a_\beta(n)}
  w_X(m)\overline{w_X(n)}(mn)^{-\sigma},}
\]
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal H_{\alpha\beta,X}(N;\sigma)
 =\sum_{m+n=N}a_\alpha(m)a_\beta(n)
  w_X(m)w_X(n)(mn)^{-\sigma}.}
\]
Thus fixed differences and fixed sums are distinct quadratic grades of one
anchored affine port family.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The sums are finite.  Expanding the normal product and integrating gives
\[
 \int_0^1e^{2\pi i(m-n-h)\theta}\dd\theta
 =\mathbf 1_{m-n=h}.
\]
The anomalous product gives
$\int_0^1e^{2\pi i(m+n-N)\theta}\dd\theta
 =\mathbf 1_{m+n=N}$.  Substitution proves both identities.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Heat--Mellin prime port]
For a Dirichlet character $\chi$, $t>0$, $\tau\in\R$, and
$\theta\in\Torus$, define
\[
 \mathcal P_\chi(t,\tau,\theta)
 :=\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{\chi(n)\Lambda(n)}{n^{1/2+i\tau}}
 e^{-t(\log n)^2}e^{2\pi in\theta}.
\]
The Gaussian factor makes the series absolutely convergent.  Its cutoff-$X$
truncation is the scalar spectral readout of the canonical record vector
$v_{\chi,X}(1/2,\tau,t,\theta)$ from
\Cref{thm:ar-derived-packet}; the displayed series is its admissible
infinite-limit model.
\end{definition}


\subsection{Cutoff-matched Gaussian prime source and horizontal growth}
\label{sec:ar-gaussian-source}

Fix $A>0$ and put
\[
 G_A(v)=\frac1{\sqrt{4\pi A}}\exp\!\left(-\frac{v^2}{4A}\right).
\]
For a Dirichlet character $\chi$, let $\delta_\chi=1$ in the principal channel
and $0$ otherwise, and define the cutoff-matched arithmetic measure
\[
 \dd\mathfrak e_{\chi,X}^{\triangle}(u)
 =\sum_{n\le X}\chi(n)\Lambda(n)\delta_{\log n}(\dd u)
