 -\delta_\chi\one_{[0,\log X]}(u)e^u\dd u.
\]
The atomic term is the canonical spectral writer of
\Cref{thm:ar-explicit-compiler-routing}; the principal-density subtraction is
a deterministic analytic background and does not reintroduce a source
admission.  Its Laplace transform is
$\mathfrak L_{\chi,X}^{\triangle}(s)
 =\int e^{-su}\dd\mathfrak e_{\chi,X}^{\triangle}(u)$, and its travelling
Gaussian port is
\[
 \mathcal G_{\chi,A,\tau;X}^{\triangle}(r)
 =e^{i\tau r}\int e^{-(1/2+i\tau)u}G_A(u-r)
   \dd\mathfrak e_{\chi,X}^{\triangle}(u).
\]

\begin{theorem}[Exact Gaussian Plancherel identity]
\label{thm:ar-Gaussian-Plancherel}
For every real $\sigma$,
\[
 \boxed{
 \begin{aligned}
 &\int_{\R}e^{-2\sigma r}
 \left|\mathcal G_{\chi,A,\tau;X}^{\triangle}(r)\right|^2\dd r\\
 &\quad=\frac{e^{2A\sigma^2}}{2\pi}
 \int_{\R}e^{-2A(t-\tau)^2}
 \left|\mathfrak L_{\chi,X}^{\triangle}
 \left(\frac12+\sigma+it\right)\right|^2\dd t.
 \end{aligned}}
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Use the Fourier convention
$\widehat f(t)=\int_{\R}f(r)e^{-itr}\dd r$, for which Plancherel has factor
$(2\pi)^{-1}$.  Since $\widehat G_A(t)=e^{-At^2}$, a change of variable
$r=u+v$ gives
\[
 \widehat{e^{-\sigma\cdot}\mathcal G}(t)
 =\exp\!\left(A(-\sigma+i(\tau-t))^2\right)
 \mathfrak L_{\chi,X}^{\triangle}
 \left(\frac12+\sigma+it\right).
\]
Take absolute values, square, and apply Plancherel.
\end{proof}

Let $\Xi(s,\chi)$ denote the completed primitive $L$-function and put
\[
 \Theta_\chi
 :=\sup_{\Xi(\rho,\chi)=0}
 \left|\Re\rho-\frac12\right|.
\]
The completed explicit formula gives a travelling-wave expansion whose
nontrivial-zero terms are
$K_{A,\tau}(\rho)e^{(\rho-1/2)r}$, with Gaussian decay in $\Im\rho$ and a
super-exponentially harmless completed background.

\begin{theorem}[Cutoff-matched horizontal scaling indicator]
\label{thm:ar-scaling-indicator}
Let
\[
 \mathscr E_{\chi,X}^{\triangle}(\sigma)
 :=\int_{\R}e^{-2\sigma r}
 |\mathcal G_{\chi,A,\tau;X}^{\triangle}(r)|^2\dd r.
\]
The standard completed explicit formula and the common cutoff of the atomic
and principal-density terms imply
\[
 \boxed{
 \limsup_{X\to\infty}
 \frac{\log^+\mathscr E_{\chi,X}^{\triangle}(\sigma)}{\log X}
 =2(\Theta_\chi-\sigma)_+.}
\]
Consequently
$\mathscr E_{\chi,X}^{\triangle}(\sigma)=X^{o(1)}$ forces
$\Theta_\chi\le\sigma$, and the estimate for every $\sigma>0$ is equivalent
to GRH for the primitive channel.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Put $U=\log X$.  Because both the atomic prime measure and the principal
comparison density are truncated at $U$, the finite port agrees with the
completed explicit-formula port, with a super-Gaussian error, throughout every
bulk interval $r\le(1-\delta)U$.

For the upper bound, the zero expansion gives, for every $\varepsilon>0$,
\[
 |\mathcal G_{\chi,A,\tau}(r)|
 \ll_{\varepsilon,A,\chi}(1+r)^C
 e^{(\Theta_\chi+\varepsilon)r}.
\]
Integrating to $U$ and treating the moving endpoint by the same Gaussian tail
bound yields
\[
 \mathscr E_{\chi,X}^{\triangle}(\sigma)
 \ll X^{2(\Theta_\chi-\sigma+\varepsilon)_+}(\log X)^C.
\]

For the lower bound, choose a zero with
$\Re\rho-1/2>\Theta_\chi-\varepsilon$.  Group zero terms with equal exponent.
The resulting almost-periodic exponential sum has positive Bohr mean square,
because the Gaussian coefficient of the chosen zero is nonzero.  On
arbitrarily long intervals its weighted energy is therefore bounded below by
a positive multiple of
$e^{2(\Theta_\chi-\sigma-2\varepsilon)r}$.  Integrate inside
$[0,(1-\delta)U]$, where finite and completed ports agree, to obtain
\[
 \limsup_{X\to\infty}
 \frac{\log^+\mathscr E_{\chi,X}^{\triangle}(\sigma)}{\log X}
 \ge2(1-\delta)(\Theta_\chi-\sigma-2\varepsilon)_+.
\]
Let $\delta,\varepsilon\downarrow0$.  Reflection symmetry gives the two-sided
horizontal displacement and the GRH equivalence.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Arithmetic source short, phase rigidity, and endpoint quotient}
\label{sec:arithmetic-source-quotient}

The unconditional endpoint source is the canonical isometry
$R_X^{\rm rec}:\C^X\to\mathcal R_X$ of
\Cref{thm:ar-record-margins}; its source Gram is exactly $I_X$.  Let
$Q_X\succeq0$ be any future, reflection, or nuisance-short operator applied to
the canonical source, or to an enriched physical response of it.  The resulting
finite source response is
\[
 \mathbb G_X^{\rm ar}=(R_X^{\rm rec})^*Q_XR_X^{\rm rec}\succeq0.
\]
For a signal--nuisance splitting write
$\mathbb G_X^{\rm ar}=\begin{psmallmatrix}A&B\\B^*&C\end{psmallmatrix}$.
The universal Schur theorem gives
\[
 \operatorname{Short}_{\rm sig}(\mathbb G_X^{\rm ar})
 =A-BC^\dagger B^*\succeq0,
\]
with its variational characterization.  Thus source existence and noncollapse
are unconditional, while any conjecture-specific coercive estimate must still
be proved on the shortened response; diagonal positivity before shorting is
insufficient.

\begin{theorem}[Endpoint phase rigidity]
\label{thm:ar-phase-rigidity}
Let $x_1,\ldots,x_r$ be squarefree positive integers and put
$u=x_1\cdots x_r$.  Then
\[
 \boxed{\prod_{j=1}^r\mu(x_j)=(-1)^{\Omega(u)}=:\lambda_{\rm L}(u).}
\]
If a Dirichlet character is present, every ordered occupied-slot history with
endpoint $u$ has the same phase $\lambda_{\rm L}(u)\chi(u)$.  Hence slot
permutations and prime-to-slot allocations within one endpoint fibre cannot
supply cancellation.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Squarefreeness gives
$\mu(x_j)=(-1)^{\omega(x_j)}$.  Prime exponents add under multiplication,
including repeated occurrence of a prime in distinct slots, so
$\sum_j\omega(x_j)=\Omega(u)$.  Complete multiplicativity of $\chi$ supplies
the character factor.  Histories in one endpoint fibre therefore carry one
common phase and add coherently.
\end{proof}

Let $\mathcal T_X$ be a finite compiler-history bank, let $n(t)$ be the
numerical endpoint of $t$, and let $a_t>0$.  For response columns $\kappa_n$
define
\[
 \mathcal C_Xe_t=\sqrt{a_t}\,\kappa_{n(t)},
 \qquad
 J_Xe_t=\sqrt{a_t}\,e_{n(t)},
 \qquad
 R_Xe_n=\kappa_n.
\]
Then $\mathcal C_X=R_XJ_X$.

\begin{theorem}[Endpoint coalescence and source-minimal quotient]
\label{thm:ar-endpoint-coalescence}
If the Gram
$[\langle\kappa_m,\kappa_n\rangle]_{m,n}$ is strictly positive definite on the
retained distinct endpoints, then
\[
 \boxed{\Ker\mathcal C_X=\Ker J_X.}
\]
The physical response quotient therefore has exactly one source coordinate per
retained numerical endpoint.  Any difference of compiler signatures which
collects to the same endpoint coefficient is future null.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Strict positivity of the endpoint Gram is equivalent to injectivity of $R_X$
on the retained endpoint span.  Since $\mathcal C_X=R_XJ_X$,
$\mathcal C_Xv=0$ is equivalent to $J_Xv=0$.  Quotienting by this common
kernel leaves the endpoint span, with one coordinate for each retained
endpoint.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Unconditional coalescence on the canonical record]
\label{cor:ar-canonical-coalescence}
For the canonical endpoint writer of
\Cref{thm:ar-explicit-compiler-routing}, $\kappa_n=e_n$ and the endpoint Gram is
$I_X$.  Hence
\[
 \Ker\mathcal C_X^{\rm rec}=\Ker J_X^{\rm end}
\]
with one noncollapsing source line per retained endpoint, without an additional
source-frame hypothesis.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The endpoint response is the identity isometry on $\mathcal R_X$, so the Gram
is $I_X$ and \Cref{thm:ar-endpoint-coalescence} applies with unit lower bound.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[Orbit ranks are computed after endpoint collection]
Ordered slot labels, dyadic signatures, promoted-prime choices, and auxiliary
Gaussian-mixture labels can be useful analytic coordinates.  They are not
independent physical source lines after
\Cref{thm:ar-endpoint-coalescence}.  The canonical record frame itself is the
identity; character-orbit ranks, innovation Grams, and any additional physical
response conditioning of the enriched pair outputs must nevertheless be
evaluated after coherent endpoint collection.
\end{firewall}

\subsection{Fixed-modulus saturated source at the conductor-three benchmark}
\label{sec:ar-fixed-modulus-source}

Let $\chi_3$ be the primitive nonprincipal character modulo $3$ and set
\[
 \sigma_0=\frac9{10},\qquad
 \delta_0=\sigma_0-\frac12=\frac25,\qquad
 H_Y=Y^{1/5+o(1)}.
\]
Put
\[
 K_0=12,\qquad
 \delta_Y=(\log\log Y)^{-1/4},\qquad
 \varepsilon_Y=\delta_Y/100,
 \qquad
 z_Y=Y^{(1+\varepsilon_Y)/12},
\]
and
\[
 M_{z_Y}^{\circ}(s)
 :=\sum_{2\le n\le z_Y}\frac{\mu(n)\chi_3(n)}{n^s}.
\]

\begin{theorem}[Fixed-order saturated arithmetic source]
\label{thm:ar-fixed-order-source}
At every fixed Mellin ordinate, the order-twelve generalized
Vaughan--Heath--Brown compiler at $\sigma_0=9/10$ has the following properties.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.8em]
\item every compiler order below $12$ is power-negligible;
\item every order-twelve component with a vacant nonunit M\"obius slot is
      power-negligible;
\item the sole power-relevant analytic symbol is
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathscr F_Y^{\rm sat}(s)
 =M_{z_Y}^{\circ}(s)^{12}
  L(s,\chi_3)^{11}\bigl(-L'(s,\chi_3)\bigr);}
\]
\item if a retained endpoint is written $n=uv$, where $u$ is the product of
      the twelve occupied M\"obius atoms and $v$ is supplied by the remaining
      $L^{11}L'$ factor, then, after a power-saving deletion,
\[
 \boxed{u>Y^{1-\delta_Y},\qquad v\le Y^{2\delta_Y}=Y^{o(1)};}
\]
\item every occupied atom lies in the shrinking top annulus
\[
 \boxed{z_Y^{1-24\delta_Y}<x_i\le z_Y\qquad(1\le i\le12).}
\]
\end{enumerate}
Thus the benchmark source has fixed compiler complexity and cannot acquire
spurious physical rank by increasing the decomposition order with $Y$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The fixed-order generalized Vaughan identity decomposes the prime logarithmic
coefficient into compiler orders at most $12$.  At an order below $12$, or at
order $12$ with one nonunit M\"obius slot vacant, the arithmetic cutoff of the
corresponding Dirichlet polynomial is at most $Y^{1-\delta_Y}$ after shrinking
the retained Gaussian endpoint window by $O(\delta_Y)$.  Moving the Mellin
contour across the resulting strip costs
\[
 Y^{O(\delta_Y^{-2}/\log\log Y)}=Y^{o(1)},
\]
whereas the cutoff deficit supplies a fixed negative power of $Y$.  These
components are therefore power-negligible.  The only surviving order-twelve
term has every nonunit M\"obius slot occupied and gives the displayed symbol.

Grade the same contour estimate by the occupied product $u$.  The range
$u\le Y^{1-\delta_Y}$ is removed with the same power saving.  Since the endpoint
window has $uv=Y^{1+o(1)}$, the surviving complementary factor obeys
$v\le Y^{2\delta_Y}$.  Finally, if one atom satisfied
$x_i\le z_Y^{1-24\delta_Y}$, then
\[
 u\le z_Y^{12-24\delta_Y}
 =Y^{(1+\varepsilon_Y)(1-2\delta_Y)}<Y^{1-\delta_Y}
\]
for sufficiently large $Y$, contradicting the retained lower bound for $u$.
This proves all five assertions.  The fixed-order identity is the generalized
Vaughan identity of Heath--Brown; the complete benchmark audit and contour
localization are recorded in \cite{ArithmeticClosureV004,HeathBrown1982}.
Neither input is a zero-free-region assumption.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Microscopic transversality of nonzero near collisions]
\label{thm:ar-three-match}
Consider two retained saturated endpoints $n,n'$ with occupied atoms
$x_1,\ldots,x_{12}$ and $x'_1,\ldots,x'_{12}$.  If
\[
 0<|n-n'|\le Y^{1/5+o(1)},
\]
then at most two occupied atom occurrences can be paired by equal numerical
values.  Consequently, after any predetermined partition of the twelve slots
into four triples, at least two entire triples on each endpoint contain no atom
matching an atom of the opposite endpoint.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
If three atom occurrences matched, their common product $d$ would divide both
endpoints and hence the nonzero integer $n-n'$.  By
\Cref{thm:ar-fixed-order-source},
\[
 d>z_Y^{3(1-24\delta_Y)}=Y^{1/4-o(1)},
\]
whereas $|n-n'|\le Y^{1/5+o(1)}$, a contradiction.  At most two of four
predetermined triples can meet the at most two matched occurrences, leaving at
least two clean triples on each side.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Character duality, shifted Jacobi edge, and quotient carry}
\label{sec:ar-character-carry}

\begin{theorem}[Exact additive--multiplicative transform]
\label{thm:ar-add-mult}
Let $q$ be prime, let $A\in M_{r\times t}(\F_q)$ have columns
$a_1,\ldots,a_t$, let $b\in\F_q^r$, and let
$f_i:\F_q^\times\to\C$ be extended by zero at $0$.  With
$\widehat f_i(y)=\sum_{x\bmod q}f_i(x)e^{2\pi iyx/q}$,
\[
 \boxed{
 \sum_{\substack{x\in(\F_q^\times)^t\\Ax=b}}
 \prod_{i=1}^tf_i(x_i)
 =q^{-r}\sum_{\xi\in\F_q^r}e^{-2\pi i\xi\cdot b/q}
 \prod_{i=1}^t\widehat f_i(a_i\cdot\xi).}
\]
For a primitive multiplicative character $\chi$,
\[
 \widehat\chi(y)=
 \begin{cases}
  \tau_q(\chi)\overline{\chi(y)},&y\ne0,\\
  0,&y=0,
 \end{cases}
 \qquad |\tau_q(\chi)|=\sqrt q.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Insert additive orthogonality,
\[
 \one_{Ax=b}
 =q^{-r}\sum_{\xi\in\F_q^r}e^{2\pi i\xi\cdot(Ax-b)/q},
\]
interchange the finite sums, and factor the sum over $x$ into its $t$
coordinates.  The character formula follows by the substitution $x\mapsto
y^{-1}x$ for $y\ne0$ and the standard Gauss-sum identity; the sum at $y=0$
vanishes for a nontrivial primitive character.  Its modulus follows by the
usual orthogonality calculation
$|\tau_q(\chi)|^2=q$.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[Transform duality is not arithmetic coercivity]
The preceding theorem is a Fourier change of coordinates.  Character Parseval,
slotwise Frobenius copies, and affine Wilson orbits preserve the relevant
Hilbert norm.  A gain must enter through a signed relation, a nonzero additive
shift, a noncommuting history, or a cross-character matrix moment before the
final positive square is taken.
\end{firewall}

Let $G_q=\F_q^\times$ and
$\xi_\chi(x)=(q-1)^{-1/2}\chi(x)$.  For $h\in G_q$ define
\[
 (T_hf)(x)=\one_{G_q}(x-h)f(x-h).
\]

\begin{theorem}[Shifted Jacobi partial isometry]
\label{thm:ar-jacobi-edge}
The operator $T_h$ is a partial isometry of rank $q-2$.  In the normalized
multiplicative-character basis its matrix is
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathsf J_h(\chi,\psi)
 =\frac{\overline{\chi(h)}\psi(h)\psi(-1)}{q-1}
   J_q(\overline\chi,\psi),}
\]
where
$J_q(\alpha,\beta)=\sum_{x\bmod q}\alpha(x)\beta(1-x)$.  Hence
\[
 \boxed{\norm{\mathsf J_h}_{\op}=1,
        \qquad\rank\mathsf J_h=q-2.}
\]
The principal--principal entry is $(q-2)/(q-1)$, while every other entry has
modulus at most $\sqrt q/(q-1)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Translation maps $G_q\setminus\{-h\}$ bijectively onto
$G_q\setminus\{h\}$, so $T_h$ is a rank-$q-2$ partial isometry.  Its matrix
coefficient is
\[
 \frac1{q-1}\sum_{x\in G_q}\overline{\chi(x)}
 \one_{G_q}(x-h)\psi(x-h).
\]
With $x=-ht$ this becomes the displayed Jacobi sum.  The principal value is
the count of $q-2$ admissible residues.  If both characters and their product
are nontrivial, the standard Jacobi evaluation gives modulus $\sqrt q$; in the
degenerate nonprincipal cases the Jacobi sum has modulus at most one
\cite{Davenport}.  Division
by $q-1$ proves the entry bound.  The operator norm is one because a nonzero
partial isometry has norm one.
\end{proof}

Group the four clean triples from \Cref{thm:ar-three-match} into two
six-slot products $U,V=Y^{1/2+o(1)}$.  Choose a prime
$q=Y^{1/2+o(1)}$ with $q>H_Y$ and write
\[
 U=qa+r,\qquad V=qb+s,\qquad r,s\in G_q,
\]
where the quotient range $0\le a,b\le A_Y$ has $A_Y=Y^{o(1)}$.

\begin{theorem}[Exact base-$q$ pair-carry identity]
\label{thm:ar-pair-carry}
One has
\[
 \boxed{
 \left\lfloor\frac{UV}{q}\right\rfloor
 =qab+as+br+\left\lfloor\frac{rs}{q}\right\rfloor,}
 \qquad UV\bmod q=rs\bmod q.
\]
Thus all irreducible floor nonlinearity lies in
\[
 \kappa_q(r,s;\theta)
 :=\exp\!\left(-2\pi i\theta\left\lfloor\frac{rs}{q}\right\rfloor\right).
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Expand
$UV=(qa+r)(qb+s)=q(qab+as+br)+rs$ and apply Euclidean division to $rs$.
\end{proof}

For $f\in\ell^2(G_q)$ put
\[
 (\mathcal K_qf)(\theta,r)
 =\sum_{s\in G_q}
 \exp\!\left(-2\pi i\theta\left\lfloor\frac{rs}{q}\right\rfloor\right)f(s).
\]

\begin{theorem}[Continuous multiplication-carry Bessel bound]
\label{thm:ar-carry-Bessel}
For every prime $q$,
\[
 \boxed{
 \int_0^1\sum_{r\in G_q}|(\mathcal K_qf)(\theta,r)|^2\dd\theta
 \ll q\log(2q)\norm{f}_2^2.}
\]
The factor $q$ cannot be removed because the diagonal contribution is
$(q-1)\norm{f}_2^2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Expanding the square and integrating in $\theta$ gives the positive kernel
\[
 N_q(s,s')
 =\#\left\{r\in G_q:
 \left\lfloor\frac{rs}{q}\right\rfloor
 =\left\lfloor\frac{rs'}{q}\right\rfloor\right\}.
\]
For $s=s'$, $N_q(s,s)=q-1$.  For $d=|s-s'|\ge1$, equality of the floors
places $rs/q$ and $rs'/q$ in one unit interval, so $rd<q$ and
\[
 N_q(s,s')\le\min(q-1,q/d).
\]
Every row sum is $O(q\log q)$.  Schur's test proves the operator bound.
\end{proof}

For quotient slices $p_a,f_b\in\ell^2(G_q)$ define
\[
 \mathcal C_{q,A}[p,f](\theta)
 :=\sum_{a,b=0}^{A}\sum_{r,s\in G_q}p_a(r)f_b(s)
 e^{-2\pi i(qab+as+br+\lfloor rs/q\rfloor)\theta}.
\]

\begin{theorem}[Pair-quotient carry Bessel theorem]
\label{thm:ar-pair-quotient-Bessel}
For $A\ge1$,
\[
 \boxed{
 \begin{aligned}
 \int_0^1|\mathcal C_{q,A}[p,f](\theta)|^2\dd\theta
 \ll{}&A\log(2A)\,q\log(2q)\\
 &\times\left(\sum_a\norm{p_a}_2^2\right)
        \left(\sum_b\norm{f_b}_2^2\right).
 \end{aligned}}
\]
The same estimate holds after arbitrary unit-modulus character, Mellin,
conductor, or coherent-history twists.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
For fixed $(a,b)$ remove the outer phase $e^{-2\pi iqab\theta}$ and denote the
remaining sum by $z_{a,b}(\theta)$.  Cauchy--Schwarz in $r$ and
\Cref{thm:ar-carry-Bessel} give
\[
 \int_0^1|z_{a,b}(\theta)|^2\dd\theta
 \ll q\log(2q)\norm{p_a}_2^2\norm{f_b}_2^2.
\]
Its Fourier support is contained in an interval of length $O(Aq)$.  After the
shift by $qab$, any integer frequency belongs to at most
$O(A\log(2A))$ such intervals: for fixed $a\ge1$ the admissible values of $b$
lie in an interval of length $O(A/a+1)$, and summing in $a$ is harmonic.
Fourier Plancherel bounds the full square by this overlap multiplicity times
the sum of the slice squares.  The double sum factors.  Unit-modulus twists do
not change any norm.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Few-orbit branch and the remaining PCJM12 moment}
\label{sec:ar-PCJM}

Let $Z_L(\chi,\theta)$ and $Z_R(\chi,\theta)$ be the coherently collected,
quotient-complete endpoint transforms after
\Cref{thm:ar-endpoint-coalescence}; let $R_L,R_R$ be the dimensions of their
nonprincipal character supports.

\begin{theorem}[Few quotient-complete character orbits]
\label{thm:ar-few-orbit}
Assume $\sum_h|w_h|\le H_YY^{o(1)}$.  Then
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 &\frac1{q-1}\int_0^1
 \left|\sum_{0<|h|\le H_Y}w_h
 \left\langle
 Q_0\mathcal J_{q,h}(\theta)Q_0Z_R(\theta),Z_L(\theta)
 \right\rangle\right|\dd\theta\\
 &\qquad\ll
 H_Yq^{-1/2}\log(2q)\sqrt{R_LR_R}\,
 \norm{c_L}_2\norm{c_R}_2.
 \end{aligned}
\]
At $q=Y^{1/2+o(1)}$ the nonprincipal shifted-copy bank is therefore at the
natural square scale whenever
\[
 \boxed{\sqrt{R_LR_R}\le Y^{1/20+o(1)}.}
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Every nonexceptional entry of the carry-twisted Jacobi matrix is
$O(q^{-1/2}\log q)$.  On an $R$-dimensional character support,
$\norm{u}_1\le R^{1/2}\norm{u}_2$.  Apply this on both sides, sum the lag weights,
and use Cauchy--Schwarz in $\theta$.  Residue--quotient Plancherel cancels the
normalizing factor $(q-1)^{-1}$.  Since
$H_Yq^{-1/2}=Y^{-1/20+o(1)}$, the stated rank threshold gives the square-scale
bound.
\end{proof}

For the unrestricted source let $\mathcal C_Y^L(\chi,\theta)$ and
$\mathcal C_Y^R(\chi,\theta)$ be the actual coherently recombined pair-carry
outputs, with all conductor and relative-Mellin labels retained, and define
\[
 \mathfrak M_Y^{\rm PCJ}
 :=\frac1{q_Y-1}\int_0^1\sum_{0<|h|\le H_Y}w_Y(h)
 \left\langle
 \mathcal J_{q_Y,h}(\theta)\mathcal C_Y^R(\theta),
 \mathcal C_Y^L(\theta)
 \right\rangle\dd\theta.
\]

\begin{assumption}[Pair-carry/Jacobi matrix moment, PCJM12]
\label{ass:ar-PCJM12}
The coherently recombined benchmark source satisfies
\[
 \boxed{
 |\mathfrak M_Y^{\rm PCJ}|
 \le\norm{A}_2^2\norm{b}_2^2Y^{o(1)}.}
 \tag{PCJM12}
\]
The estimate is required before characterwise absolute values are taken.  The
Jacobi operator norm alone, or separate carry estimates followed by an
$\ell^1$ sum over characters, does not imply it.
\end{assumption}

\begin{theorem}[Present fixed-modulus coercive handoff]
\label{thm:ar-PCJM-handoff}
After the fixed-order reduction, endpoint coalescence, principal
zero-frequency short, nonunit deletion, and the controlled outer and Gaussian
tails, PCJM12 is the only additional cross-character estimate in the
conductor-three $9/10$ benchmark.  More precisely,
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathrm{PCJM12}
 \Longrightarrow
 \text{remaining Type--III current }Y^{1+o(1)}
 \Longrightarrow
 \mathscr E_{\chi_3,Y}^{\triangle}(2/5)=Y^{o(1)}.}
\]
Consequently the cutoff-matched Gaussian growth criterion yields
\[
 \boxed{L(s,\chi_3)\ne0\quad(\Re s>9/10),
 \qquad \frac1{10}\le\Re\rho\le\frac9{10}.}
\]
The conclusion is conditional on PCJM12 and is not an unconditional zero-free
strip.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The exact pair blocking in \Cref{thm:ar-pair-carry} changes neither the
arithmetic coefficient nor its phase.  The two pair outputs satisfy the
Hilbertian estimates of \Cref{thm:ar-pair-quotient-Bessel}.  After the stated
shorts and deletions, the sole remaining off-diagonal quadratic form is
$\mathfrak M_Y^{\rm PCJ}$.  PCJM12 bounds it at the diagonal scale, so the
complete finite Gaussian energy at displacement $2/5$ is subpolynomial.  The scaling theorem
\Cref{thm:ar-scaling-indicator} identifies the energy exponent with the
maximal horizontal displacement of a zero.  Hence no zero has
$\Re\rho>9/10$.  The primitive functional equation for $\chi_3$ reflects this
to $\Re\rho<1/10$.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Factor-depth loading and exact prime--semiprime separation}
\label{sec:ar-factor-depth}

\begin{lemma}[Proper-prime-power contamination]
\label{lem:ar-prime-power}
For fixed $h$, the contribution to
$\sum_{n\le X}\Lambda(n)\Lambda(n+h)$ from terms for which at least one
coordinate is a proper prime power is $O_h(X^{1/2}\log X)$.  For fixed even
$N$, the analogous contribution to
$\sum_{m+n=N}\Lambda(m)\Lambda(n)$ is $O(N^{1/2}\log N)$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
The total von Mangoldt weight of proper prime powers at most $Y$ is
\[
 \sum_{k\ge2}\sum_{p\le Y^{1/k}}\log p\ll\sqrt Y.
\]
For each exceptional coordinate the other von Mangoldt factor is
$O(\log Y)$, and either coordinate may be exceptional.
\end{proof}

Let $L_X=\log(2X)$ and define the squarefree Mellin port
\[
 \mathfrak E_{z,X}(n)
 :=\mu^2(n)\prod_{\ell\mid n}(\ell^{z/L_X}-1)
 =\sum_{j\ge1}B_{j,X}(n)z^j.
\]
For $j\ge1$ put
\[
 \Lambda_j(n)=\sum_{d\mid n}\mu(d)\left(\log\frac nd\right)^j.
\]

\begin{theorem}[Exact Mellin-degree coefficients]
\label{thm:ar-mellin-degree}
For every $j\ge1$ and $n\ge2$,
\[
 \boxed{B_{j,X}(n)=\frac{\mu^2(n)\Lambda_j(n)}{j!L_X^j}.}
\]
In particular the degree-one coefficient is the squarefree prime atom
$\mu^2(n)\Lambda(n)/L_X$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
For squarefree $n$,
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \sum_{j\ge0}\Lambda_j(n)\frac{z^j}{j!L_X^j}
 &=\sum_{d\mid n}\mu(d)
   \exp\!\left(\frac z{L_X}\log\frac nd\right)\\
 &=n^{z/L_X}\prod_{\ell\mid n}(1-\ell^{-z/L_X})
 =\prod_{\ell\mid n}(\ell^{z/L_X}-1).
 \end{aligned}
\]
Compare coefficients.  For nonsquarefree $n$, multiplication by $\mu^2(n)$
kills both sides.
\end{proof}

Define
$\mathfrak P_{\le2,X}=B_{1,X}+B_{2,X}$.

\begin{proposition}[Prime atom and squarefree-semiprime bulk]
\label{prop:ar-atom-bulk}
For $n\ge2$,
\[
 \boxed{
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathfrak P_{\le2,X}(n)
 ={}&\mu^2(n)\frac{\Lambda(n)}{L_X}
 \left(1+\frac{\log n}{2L_X}\right)\\
 &+\frac{\mu^2(n)}{2L_X^2}(\Lambda*\Lambda)(n).
 \end{aligned}}
\]
The first term is supported exactly on primes.  The second is supported exactly
on squarefree semiprimes and equals
$(\log r\log q)/L_X^2$ at $n=rq$ with distinct primes $r,q$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
The Dirichlet series identity
\[
 \Lambda_2(n)=\Lambda(n)\log n+(\Lambda*\Lambda)(n)
\]
follows from
$\zeta''/\zeta=-(-\zeta'/\zeta)'+(-\zeta'/\zeta)^2$.  Insert it into
\Cref{thm:ar-mellin-degree}.  At a prime the convolution vanishes.  At a
squarefree semiprime $rq$ it equals $2\log r\log q$; at every other squarefree
factor depth the degree-two coefficient vanishes.
\end{proof}

For $2\le n\le2X$ put $\alpha_X(n)=\log n/L_X$ and
\[
 \mathfrak J_X(n)
 :=\frac67\left(B_{1,X}(n)+B_{2,X}(n)
 -\frac{2}{\alpha_X(n)}B_{3,X}(n)\right).
\]

\begin{theorem}[Exact squarefree-semiprime cancellation]
\label{thm:ar-signed-separator}
For $2\le n\le2X$,
\[
 \mathfrak J_X(n)=
 \begin{cases}
  \dfrac67\alpha+\dfrac17\alpha^2,&n=p\text{ prime},\\[1mm]
  0,&n\text{ squarefree semiprime},\\[1mm]
  -\dfrac{12}{7\alpha_X(n)}B_{3,X}(n)<0,
      &n\text{ squarefree of factor depth }3,\\[1mm]
  0,&\text{otherwise}.
 \end{cases}
\]
Consequently
\[
 \boxed{\mathfrak J_X(n)\le\one_{\mathbb P}(n).}
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
For a prime, $B_1=\alpha$, $B_2=\alpha^2/2$, and
$B_3=\alpha^3/6$, giving the displayed positive value, at most one because
$0<\alpha\le1$.  For $n=pq$, let
$\alpha=\alpha_p+\alpha_q$.  Then
$B_2=\alpha_p\alpha_q$ and
$B_3=\frac12\alpha_p\alpha_q(\alpha_p+\alpha_q)=\alpha B_2/2$, so the
separator is zero.  At factor depth three, $B_1=B_2=0$ and $B_3>0$; at depth
at least four the first three coefficients vanish.  Nonsquarefree targets are
killed by $\mu^2$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Exact depth-one recovery on a positive $P_1\cup P_2$ carrier]
\label{thm:ar-parity-recovery}
Let $M=P_1+P_2$ be the positive mass on squarefree targets of factor depth one
or two, and let $\mathcal J=-P_1+P_2$ be its M\"obius current.  Then
\[
 \boxed{P_1=\frac12(M-\mathcal J),
        \qquad P_2=\frac12(M+\mathcal J).}
\]
Thus $M>0$ and $\mathcal J=o(M)$ imply
$P_1=(1/2+o(1))M>0$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Solve the two linear equations $M=P_1+P_2$ and
$\mathcal J=-P_1+P_2$.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[One-variable prime mass does not prove constrained prime pairs]
The canonical zeta commutator has nonzero prime and prime-power coordinates, and
the CAR filter, Mellin-degree decomposition, signed separator, and parity
identity identify the depth-one branch exactly.  These facts do not prove that
a fixed-gap or moving fixed-sum pair carrier has positive prime--prime mass.
Twin-prime and Goldbach closure still requires a selector-stable signed current,
a positive fixed-gap or fixed-sum estimate, or an equivalent contraction of the
semiprime profile.
\end{firewall}

\subsection{Common mass--prefix source and multiport control}
\label{sec:ar-mass-prefix}

Let $s_0<\cdots<s_N$ be predetermined logarithmic cell centres and let
$d_0,\ldots,d_N$ be Hilbert-valued discrepancy coefficients.  Define
\[
 M(d)=\sum_{c=0}^Nd_c,
 \qquad
 q_c(d)=\sum_{r=0}^cd_r\quad(0\le c<N),
\]
and for a translated port $T_sF(u)=F(u+s)$ put
\[
 \mathcal C_F(d)=\sum_{c=0}^Nd_c\otimes T_{s_c}F.
\]
Let $J_d(s)=q_c(d)$ on $[s_c,s_{c+1})$ and zero outside
$[s_0,s_N)$.

\begin{theorem}[Exact mass--prefix identity]
\label{thm:ar-mass-prefix}
One has
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal C_F(d)
 =M(d)\otimes T_{s_N}F
 +\sum_{c=0}^{N-1}q_c(d)\otimes
  (T_{s_c}F-T_{s_{c+1}}F).}
\]
With the unitary Fourier transform,
\[
 \boxed{
 \sum_{c=0}^Ne^{its_c}d_c
 =e^{its_N}M(d)-it\sqrt{2\pi}\,\widehat J_d(t).}
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
In the first identity, the coefficient of $T_{s_0}F$ is $q_0=d_0$; for
$1\le c<N$ it is $q_c-q_{c-1}=d_c$; and the coefficient of $T_{s_N}F$ is
$M-q_{N-1}=d_N$.  For the Fourier identity, integrate the step function:
\[
 -it\int_{s_0}^{s_N}e^{its}J_d(s)\dd s
 =\sum_{c=0}^{N-1}q_c(e^{its_c}-e^{its_{c+1}})
 =\sum_{c=0}^Ne^{its_c}d_c-e^{its_N}M(d).
\]
Insert the unitary Fourier normalization.
\end{proof}

Put
$\Lambda_F=\sup_{t\in\R}t^2|\widehat F(t)|^2$.

\begin{theorem}[Mass--flux and multiport inequalities]
\label{thm:ar-mass-flux}
If $\Lambda_F<\infty$, then
\[
 \boxed{
 \norm{\mathcal C_F(d)}
 \le\norm{F}\norm{M(d)}
 +\sqrt{2\pi\Lambda_F}\norm{J_d}_{L^2}.}
\]
If $M(d)=0$, then
\[
 \boxed{
 \norm{\mathcal C_F(d)}^2
 =2\pi\int_{\R}t^2|\widehat F(t)|^2
       \norm{\widehat J_d(t)}^2\dd t.}
\]
For a finite family $F_1,\ldots,F_R$ and weights $\lambda_r>0$,
\[
 \boxed{
 \begin{aligned}
 \left[\sum_r\lambda_r\norm{\mathcal C_{F_r}(d)}^2\right]^{1/2}
 \le{}&
 \left[\sum_r\lambda_r\norm{F_r}^2\right]^{1/2}\norm{M(d)}\\
 &+\left[2\pi\sum_r\lambda_r\Lambda_{F_r}\right]^{1/2}
 \norm{J_d}_{L^2}.
 \end{aligned}}
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Plancherel gives
\[
 \norm{\mathcal C_F(d)}^2
 =\int_{\R}|\widehat F(t)|^2
 \left\|\sum_ce^{its_c}d_c\right\|^2\dd t.
\]
Insert the Fourier boundary identity of
\Cref{thm:ar-mass-prefix}, use the triangle inequality, the definition of
$\Lambda_F$, and Plancherel for $J_d$.  If $M(d)=0$, the boundary term vanishes
and the equality is exact.  Apply the one-port inequality in the Hilbert direct
sum $\bigoplus_r\mathcal H_r$ after replacing $F_r$ by
$\sqrt{\lambda_r}F_r$ to obtain the multiport estimate.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Smallest common arithmetic source quotient]
\label{prop:ar-joint-source-quotient}
For source-to-port maps $C_r$ and $\lambda_r>0$, put
\[
 K_{\rm joint}=\sum_r\lambda_rC_r^*C_r.
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{\Ker K_{\rm joint}=\bigcap_r\Ker C_r.}
\]
The quotient by this kernel is the smallest finite source visible to every
selected arithmetic port.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
If $x\in\Ker K_{\rm joint}$, positivity gives
$0=\langle x,K_{\rm joint}x\rangle=\sum_r\lambda_r\norm{C_rx}^2$, hence
$C_rx=0$ for every $r$.  The converse is immediate.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Heat readouts, analytic jets, and exact conditional interfaces}
\label{sec:ar-readouts}

\begin{theorem}[Twin-prime heat sufficiency]
\label{thm:twin-heat}
Put
\[
 \mathcal D_2(t)
 =\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{\Lambda(n)\Lambda(n+2)}{\sqrt{n(n+2)}}
 e^{-t[(\log n)^2+(\log(n+2))^2]}.
\]
The contribution from terms for which at least one of $n,n+2$ is a proper
prime power is uniformly bounded for $0<t\le1$.  Hence
\[
 \mathcal D_2(t)\longrightarrow\infty\quad(t\downarrow0)
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 \text{infinitely many twin-prime pairs}.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
For $n=p^k$, $k\ge2$, use
$\sqrt{n(n+2)}\ge n$ and $\Lambda(n+2)\le\log(n+2)$.  The resulting majorant
is bounded by a constant multiple of
$\sum_p\sum_{k\ge2}k(\log p)^2p^{-k}<\infty$.  The case in which $n+2$ is a
proper prime power is identical.  If only finitely many genuine twin pairs
existed, their total heat contribution would also remain bounded.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Binary-Goldbach heat sufficiency]
\label{thm:Goldbach-heat}
For even $N$, put
\[
 \mathcal H_N(t)
 =\sum_{m+n=N}\frac{\Lambda(m)\Lambda(n)}{\sqrt{mn}}
 e^{-t[(\log m)^2+(\log n)^2]}.
\]
Uniformly in $t>0$, the contribution from pairs with at least one proper
prime-power summand is $O(N^{-1/4}(\log N)^2)$.  If
$\mathcal H_N(t_N)\ge c>0$ for every sufficiently large even $N$, then every
such $N$ is a sum of two primes.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
There are $O(\sqrt N)$ proper prime powers at most $N$.  For any set
$S\subset\{1,\ldots,N-1\}$ of size $K$,
\[
 \sum_{m\in S}\frac1{\sqrt{m(N-m)}}\ll\frac{\sqrt K}{\sqrt N}.
\]
Take $K=O(\sqrt N)$ and bound both von Mangoldt factors by $\log N$; heat
weights only decrease the sum.  A fixed positive lower bound eventually
exceeds the contamination and therefore forces a term with both summands
prime.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Finite analytic jet]
Let $\mathscr R_m=\C[z]/(z^m)$.  For an analytic germ $F$, let $M_m(F)$ be
multiplication by $F$ modulo $z^m$ and put
$\mathbb J_m(F)=M_m(F)^*M_m(F)$ in the monomial Hilbert structure.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Analytic rank and leading-magnitude selector]
\label{thm:analytic-jet}
If $F(z)=a_rz^r+O(z^{r+1})$ with $a_r\ne0$ and $m>r$, then
\[
 \boxed{\dim\Ker\mathbb J_m(F)=r,}
 \qquad
 \boxed{\pdet\mathbb J_m(F)=|a_r|^{2(m-r)}.}
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Write $F=z^rg$ with $g(0)=a_r\ne0$.  Multiplication by $g$ is invertible in
$\mathscr R_m$, so the kernel is
$\Span\{z^{m-r},\ldots,z^{m-1}\}$.  On its orthogonal complement, the reduced
multiplication matrix is triangular with diagonal $a_r$.  The product of its
nonzero singular values is $|a_r|^{m-r}$; squaring gives the
pseudodeterminant.
\end{proof}

\begin{assessment}[Exact unconditional/conditional boundary of arithmetic]
\label{assess:arithmetic-loading-status}
The finite basic arithmetic loading is structurally closed relative to the full
operational tensor.  The protected chronology has a unique normalized Peano
extension; multiplicativity, count, logarithmic grading, and the unit-weight
incidence zeta are forced.  M\"obius and von Mangoldt sources, residue and
character operators, affine and Mellin flows, factor-depth selectors, standard
recognition, and the explicit-formula writer are canonical functorial
consequences.  The complete scalar deformation space is the completely
multiplicative weighted family $c(a)L_{a,X}^{\rm P}$, and the deterministic
source normalization sets all $c(p)=1$.  Positive relation residuals certify
this uniqueness, forward histories form an exact projective cutoff family, and
mixed adjoint words have exact transitive absorbing descent.  Thus both
arithmetic existence and arithmetic selection are closed at finite cutoff; the
ambient fullness of $M_X(\C)$ leaves no convenient-copy ambiguity.

The anchored/reflected port tensor, normal and anomalous selectors, source
short, endpoint phase rigidity, fixed order-twelve benchmark source,
microscopic clean blocks, additive--multiplicative transform, shifted Jacobi
edge, pair-carry Bessel bounds, few-orbit branch, signed prime--semiprime
selectors, common mass--prefix source, and analytic jets remain exact finite
enrichments of that canonical source.

What remains conditional is no longer the loading.  It is one of:
(i) a conjecture-specific coercive or signed estimate such as PCJM12,
selector-stable parity, or GRH source coercivity; (ii) a genuinely enriched
Frobenius, Whittaker, or determinant-line comparison; (iii) a positive
fixed-gap or fixed-sum estimate; or (iv) the optional empirical identification
of an unrelated older laboratory response with the canonical chronology-derived
source through the innovation audit of \Cref{prop:ar-old-response}.
\end{assessment}

\begin{firewall}[No conjecture follows from unconditional loading]
The canonical source supplies nonzero prime and factor-depth coordinates, but
loading existence does not estimate the required off-diagonal currents.  Exact
transform identities, source saturation, unit record margins, low-rank
alternatives, and algebraic prime selectors therefore do not imply PCJM12, a
prime-side subpower estimate, a selector-stable M\"obius sign, a Goldbach or
twin-prime lower bound, GRH, or an analytic--Selmer determinant-line
comparison.  Those remain the named problem-specific theorems.
\end{firewall}

\section{Other loaded Grand-Tensor realizations}
\label{sec:other-loadings}
% =============================================================================

The notation $\boldsymbol{\mathbb T}^{\rm other}_{\Grand,X}$ is used for the
remaining domain-specific loadings.  Each may select neutral loop, cell, chain,
interface, regulator, or resource records from the universal operational
algebra, but must add its own physical operators and estimates.  The notation
is deliberately not a formal direct sum of all sectors.  Some sectors may
inhabit one common covered carrier and admit mixed histories; others may remain
in independently sourced ideals.  It therefore first denotes a finite
portfolio of verified loaded hierarchies, with a joint tensor constructed only
when physical routing has been proved.

\begin{definition}[Portfolio of other loadings]
\label{def:other-loading-portfolio}
Let $\mathfrak D_{{\rm other},X}$ be a finite index set of verified admissible
loadings, for example:
\[
 \mathfrak D_{{\rm other},X}
 \subseteq
 \{\mathrm{gauge},\mathrm{chain},\mathrm{Hodge},\mathrm{PDE},
   \mathrm{boundary/interface},\mathrm{resource}\}.
\]
For each $\delta\in\mathfrak D_{{\rm other},X}$ let
$\boldsymbol{\mathbb T}^{\delta}_{\Grand,X}$ be its loaded hierarchy.  Define
\[
 \boxed{
 \boldsymbol{\mathbb T}^{\rm other}_{\Grand,X}
 :=\bigl(\boldsymbol{\mathbb T}^{\delta}_{\Grand,X}
        \bigr)_{\delta\in\mathfrak D_{{\rm other},X}}.}
\]
This is a typed portfolio with the carrier, source map, word algebra, inserted
panels, and proof status retained for every component.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Joint other-sector loading]
\label{def:joint-other-loading}
Suppose a subfamily $J\subseteq\mathfrak D_{{\rm other},X}$ is routed into one
common covered carrier, all consequential multiplicity labels are retained,
and a finite alphabet of mixed words between its sectors is physically
admitted.  The union alphabet, its adjoints, and those mixed words define an
admissible loading.  Its loaded hierarchy is denoted
\[
 \boxed{
 \boldsymbol{\mathbb T}^{J}_{\Grand,X}
 =\{\mathbb K^{J}_{X,r}\}_{r\ge0}.}
\]
Without this common-router and mixed-history certificate, only the portfolio in
\Cref{def:other-loading-portfolio} is asserted and no cross-sector block is
introduced.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Emergence and compression of the other loadings]
\label{thm:other-loadings}
Every component of
$\boldsymbol{\mathbb T}^{\rm other}_{\Grand,X}$ is a canonical positive,
finite-flat, source-minimal loaded hierarchy.  If a joint loading $J$ exists,
then it is also canonical and each component $\delta\in J$ is a typed
compression of the joint word-Gram hierarchy.  More precisely, for the natural
word inclusion $I_{\delta J}^{(r)}$,
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathbb K^{\delta}_{X,r}
 =(I_{\delta J}^{(r)})^*\mathbb K^{J}_{X,r}I_{\delta J}^{(r)}.}
\]
Conversely, the separate existence of the component tensors does not determine
mixed cross kernels or a joint algebra.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Apply \Cref{thm:loaded-subhierarchy} separately to every verified loading
$\delta$.  This gives positivity, flat reconstruction, source-minimality, and
cutoff compatibility componentwise.  Under the hypotheses of
\Cref{def:joint-other-loading}, apply the same theorem to the union alphabet.
The synthesis map for a component is the joint synthesis map restricted to its
word subspace, namely
$W_{\delta,X,r}=W_{J,X,r}I_{\delta J}^{(r)}$; taking Grams proves the compression
identity.  For the converse, adjoin arbitrary relative unitaries or arbitrary
orthogonal cross blocks between two independently realized carriers.  These
changes leave both diagonal loaded hierarchies fixed while changing the mixed
word kernels.  Hence component data alone do not identify a joint loading.
\end{proof}

\begin{assessment}[What belongs to $\boldsymbol{\mathbb T}^{\rm other}$]
Gauge transfer and Wilson-loop histories, finite chain and Hodge--Dirac
complexes, viscous and nonlinear PDE insertions, boundary response and
interface systems, and resource-enriched word metrics may all be represented as
other loadings.  Their finite algebraic or positive-form identities are inherited
from the universal tensor after loading.  Continuum mass gaps, PDE regularity,
algebraic-cycle generation, and circuit lower bounds remain later
problem-specific interfaces rather than consequences of the portfolio.
\end{assessment}


\part{Millennium and major-problem interfaces}

% =============================================================================
\section{Riemann hypothesis and GRH: spectral-determinant interface}
\label{sec:RH-interface}
% =============================================================================

\begin{definition}[Finite spectral determinant]
For $A\in M_d(\C)$ and $\ell>0$, define
\[
 D_A(s):=\det(I-e^{-\ell s}A),\qquad s\in\C.
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Eigenvalue modulus--vertical-line theorem]
\label{thm:eigenvalue-zero-lines}
Let the nonzero eigenvalues of $A$ be
$\lambda_j=|\lambda_j|e^{i\theta_j}$, counted with algebraic multiplicity.
Then the zeros of $D_A$ are exactly
\[
 \boxed{
 s_{j,k}=\frac1\ell\log|\lambda_j|
 +\frac{i}{\ell}(\theta_j-2\pi k),
 \qquad k\in\Z.}
\]
Thus the real parts of the determinant zeros are the logarithmic eigenvalue
moduli divided by $\ell$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Schur triangularization gives
\[
 D_A(s)=\prod_j(1-e^{-\ell s}\lambda_j),
\]
with zero eigenvalues contributing the factor one.  A factor vanishes exactly
when $e^{-\ell s}\lambda_j=1$.  Comparing modulus and argument gives the
formula.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Critical-line/circle duality]
\label{thm:critical-line-circle}
Let $A$ be invertible and normal.  Assume its eigenvalue multiset is invariant
under $\lambda\mapsto c/\overline\lambda$ for some $c>0$, and put
$a=\ell^{-1}\log c$.  Then the zero multiset of $D_A$ is invariant under
$s\mapsto a-\overline s$.  Moreover, the following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.8em]
\item every zero of $D_A$ lies on $\Re s=a/2$;
\item every eigenvalue of $A$ lies on $|\lambda|=\sqrt c$;
\item $A^*A=cI$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The reflected eigenvalue has modulus $c/|\lambda|$, so
\Cref{thm:eigenvalue-zero-lines} sends its zero line to
\[
 \Re s=\ell^{-1}\log c-\ell^{-1}\log|\lambda|,
\]
and conjugates the corresponding imaginary coordinate.  This proves the
reflection law and the equivalence of the first two assertions.  Normality
gives a unitary diagonalization
$A=U\diag(\lambda_j)U^*$, hence
$A^*A=U\diag(|\lambda_j|^2)U^*$, proving the last equivalence.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Conditional critical-line regulator theorem]
\label{thm:conditional-RH-regulator}
Let $a\in\R$ and let $F_X$ be nonzero holomorphic functions on a domain
$\Omega\subset\C$ containing the line $\Re s=a/2$.  Suppose:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(R\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item $F_X\to F$ locally uniformly on $\Omega$, with $F\not\equiv0$;
\item $F_X=h_XD_{A_X}$, where $h_X$ is holomorphic and nowhere zero;
\item $A_X$ is normal and $A_X^*A_X=c_XI$;
\item $a_X:=\ell_X^{-1}\log c_X\to a$.
\end{enumerate}
Then every zero of $F$ in $\Omega$ lies on $\Re s=a/2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Let $U$ be either component of
$\Omega\setminus\{\Re s=a/2\}$ and let $K\Subset U$.  The distance of $K$
from the limiting line is positive.  For all sufficiently large $X$, the line
$\Re s=a_X/2$ misses $K$.  By
\Cref{thm:critical-line-circle}, $D_{A_X}$ has no zero on $K$, and neither does
$F_X$ because $h_X$ is nowhere zero.  Hurwitz's theorem applied on every
connected relatively compact subdomain of $U$ implies that the nonzero limit
$F$ is zero free there.  Exhausting both components proves the claim.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Canonical completed--Euler joint source and the remaining upper bridge}
\label{sec:GRH-joint-source-bridge}

Let $A_X,S_X,N_X$ synthesize the completed Volterra--gamma--conductor, the
Euler--OU, and the common centering/nuisance families on one operational
carrier.  When the corresponding deformations are jointly visible, their
mixed score table reconstructs the complete three-family Gram by
\Cref{thm:operational-score-export}.

\begin{theorem}[Canonical completed--Euler short]
\label{thm:GRH-completed-Euler-short}
With the notation of \Cref{thm:simultaneous-nuisance-short}, the nuisance-free
completed and Euler metrics and their cross Gram are
\[
 \widehat M_X,
 \qquad
 \widehat{\mathbb E}_X,
 \qquad
 \widehat B_X.
\]
The exact Euler source innovation is
\[
 \boxed{R_{E\mid M,X}
 =\widehat{\mathbb E}_X-
 \widehat B_X^*\widehat M_X^\dagger\widehat B_X\succeq0,}
\]
and
\[
 \boxed{\widehat{\mathbb E}_X
 =D_X^*\widehat M_XD_X+R_{E\mid M,X},
 \qquad D_X=\widehat M_X^\dagger\widehat B_X.}
\]
Thus $R_{E\mid M,X}=0$ is exactly source inclusion, not metric domination.
On $Q_X=\supp\widehat M_X$, define
\[
 \boxed{H_{E/M,X}
 =\widehat M_X^{\dagger/2}
 \widehat{\mathbb E}_X
 \widehat M_X^{\dagger/2}.}
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{\widehat{\mathbb E}_X\preceq\widehat M_X
 \iff \Ker\widehat M_X\subseteq\Ker\widehat{\mathbb E}_X
 \text{ and }\|H_{E/M,X}\|\le1.}
\]
The sharp multiplicative bridge defect is
$\eta_X^+=(\|H_{E/M,X}\|-1)_+$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The Pythagorean identity is the Gram decomposition of $\widehat S_X$ into its
orthogonal projection onto $\Ran\widehat A_X$ and its residual.  The final
order criterion and the sharp multiplicative constant are the specialization
of \Cref{thm:relative-metric-density} to
$(M,E)=(\widehat M_X,\widehat{\mathbb E}_X)$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Finite Petz--Euler sufficient certificate]
\label{thm:GRH-Petz-Euler}
Suppose the Euler algebra $\mathcal N_X^{\rm Eul}$ is a unital subalgebra of the
completed algebra $\mathcal M_X^{\rm comp}$ with faithful physical state
$\omega_X(x)=\Tr(\rho_Xx)$.  If
\[
 \rho_X^{it}\mathcal N_X^{\rm Eul}\rho_X^{-it}
 =\mathcal N_X^{\rm Eul}\qquad(t\in\R),
\]
then there is a unique $\omega_X$-preserving conditional expectation
$\mathcal P_X:\mathcal M_X^{\rm comp}\to\mathcal N_X^{\rm Eul}$.  If it maps
the completed source words to the Euler source words and preserves the common
nuisance short, then
\[
 \boxed{\widehat{\mathbb E}_X\preceq\widehat M_X}
\]
at every matrix amplification.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Finite-dimensional modular invariance is the Takesaki criterion for the unique
state-preserving conditional expectation.  Kadison--Schwarz gives
$\|\mathcal P_X(y)\|_{2,\omega_X}\le\|y\|_{2,\omega_X}$, and applying it to
every matrix of completed source-word combinations gives the complete Gram
order.  Compatibility with nuisance projection gives the shorted version.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Saturated block-first upper-bridge criterion]
\label{thm:GRH-block-first-bridge}
Assume the primitive arithmetic writer family is source saturating after all
character, parity/root-number, conductor, imprimitive, endpoint, and nuisance
records are retained.  For a finite source-Krylov head of the positive operator
$H_{E/M,X}$, let $a_X$ be the head norm,
$\nu_X$ the norm of its moment-exact leakage Gram, and $d_X$ an independently
proved tail norm.  Then
\[
 \boxed{\|H_{E/M,X}\|
 \le\frac{a_X+d_X+\sqrt{(a_X-d_X)^2+4\nu_X}}2.}
\]
In particular, $a_X<1$, $d_X<1$, and
$\nu_X<(1-a_X)(1-d_X)$ imply the exact upper bridge.  More generally a
predeclared arithmetic grading with block bounds satisfying the weighted
criterion of \Cref{thm:weighted-source-influence} also implies the bridge.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Source saturation makes the union of the primitive Krylov heads dense in the
selected source space.  The moment-exact leakage theorem identifies the
head--tail coupling norm squared with $\nu_X$.  Apply
\Cref{thm:sharp-positive-head-tail}; the weighted alternative is
\Cref{thm:weighted-source-influence}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Protected-angle formulation of the assembled hard-edge packet]
\label{cor:GRH-protected-angle-localizer}
Suppose an assembled arithmetic packet has an independently fixed predictor
projection $P_X$, residual total and phase sources
$t_{0,X}=(I-P_X)t_X$ and $p_{0,X}=(I-P_X)p_X$, and an exact readout
\[
 f_X=\mathfrak p_X+\langle t_{0,X},p_{0,X}\rangle.
\]
Then the square-root-scale angle bound
\[
 \frac{|\langle t_{0,X},p_{0,X}\rangle|}
 {\|t_{0,X}\|\,\|p_{0,X}\|}\le\eta_X
\]
is equivalent to positivity of the $2\times2$ localizer
$\mathbb L_{\eta_X}(t_X,p_X\mid P_X)$ of
\Cref{thm:GT-protected-angle}.  Consequently
\[
 \boxed{
 |f_X|\le|\mathfrak p_X|
 +\eta_X\|t_{0,X}\|\,\|p_{0,X}\|.}
\]
The predictor must be fixed from the arithmetic cylinder before $f_X$ is
examined; enlarging it adaptively is not monotone for the protected angle.
\end{corollary}

\begin{assessment}[Exact GRH boundary after joint-source reconstruction]
The relative orientation of the Euler and completed sectors is no longer an
ambiguity of the Grand Tensor once their mixed operational score panel is
retained.  The remaining theorem is quantitative: prove along one exhaustive
odd form-core diagonal that the archimedean gamma/conductor observations make
$\eta_X^+\to0$, together with the independent lower bridge.  Finite gamma
source completeness, a pointwise positive short, or source inclusion alone does
not give this uniform estimate.
\end{assessment}

\begin{firewall}[The remaining GRH theorem is quantitative]
Joint-source universality, simultaneous nuisance shorting, score export,
source innovation, the relative metric density, and the Petz--Euler sufficient
mechanism are now canonical finite theorems.  They do not prove the required
uniform inequality.  The missing statement is a source-native archimedean
observability or influence estimate which makes
$\eta_X^+\to0$ on an exhaustive odd form core, together with the separately
required lower bridge and the final compact-uniform passage.  A router chosen
by factoring the target Weil or screw matrix, finite numerical positivity, or
finite gamma totality is inadmissible and insufficient.
\end{firewall}

\subsection{Finite Weil inertia and source-resolved first-return coherence}
\label{sec:GRH-Weil-inertia-return}
% =============================================================================

A finite compression of Weil's Hermitian form supplies an upstream signed
certificate which is complementary to, rather than a replacement for, the
completed--Euler and first-return programmes.

\begin{theorem}[Typed finite Weil rank--trace certificate]
\label{thm:GRH-Weil-inertia}
Let a normalized finite test family give
\[
 \widetilde G=P+Q+E,
\]
where $P\succeq0$ is the sum of the critical-line zero columns,
$\rank P\le s$, $Q$ is the pullback of $p$ functional-equation hyperbolic
blocks of signature $(1,1)$, and $E$ is an exterior-window tail.  Then
$n_+(Q)\le p$, and, after replacing $\widetilde G$ by
$G=P+Q$ with a trace-norm tail allowance, \Cref{thm:GT-rank-trace-indefinite}
gives
\[
 \boxed{s\ge2\Tr P+4\Tr Q-4p-\|G\|_{\rm F}^2.}
 \tag{GRH.1}
\]
If, in the atom normalization,
\[
 \Tr G=N+o(N),
 \qquad
 \|G\|_{\rm F}^2
 =\left(\frac1\lambda+\frac\lambda3\right)N+o(N),
\]
then
\[
 \boxed{
 N_0^*(T,2T)
 \ge\left(2-\frac1\lambda-\frac\lambda3-o(1)\right)N(T,2T).}
 \tag{GRH.2}
\]
The same finite linear-algebra statement applies to a fixed primitive
Dirichlet character once its explicit-formula packet and functional-equation
pairing are loaded.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Each off-line functional-equation pair is a hyperbolic form; pullback does not
increase positive index.  Apply \Cref{thm:GT-rank-trace-indefinite} and then
the displayed prime-side moment asymptotics.  Tail perturbations are handled
by trace-norm and Weyl bounds.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Parallel population and causal-signed certificates]
\label{thm:GRH-parallel-signed-certificate}
Let $N_\omega$ be the source-resolved countercoherent profile of the same
functional-equation pair histories, let $\mathbb K_{{\rm pair},R}$ be their
complete cross-record kernel, and let $\mathcal P_R$ be the actual first-return
record.  Then the pair source obeys the exact decomposition
\[
 \boxed{
 N^*N
 =\mathbb I_{{\rm pair}\mid R}
 +G_{\rm dem}^{\rm pair}
 +G_{\rm open}^{\rm pair}
 +G_{\rm cyc}^{\rm pair},}
 \tag{GRH.3}
\]
with $\mathbb I_{{\rm pair}\mid R}$ given by the conditional variance formula
\textup{(SK.3)}.  The finite Weil theorem gives a population lower bound; the
first-return packet controls source-resolved phase loss, demand, open current,
and cycle holonomy.  Neither theorem constructs a canonical spectral
complement to be passed to the other.  Their physical handoff is the common
pair label and its complete mixed kernel.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Apply \Cref{thm:GT-source-record-variance} to the pair-history source and then
\Cref{thm:GT-source-word-Hodge} at the first-return grade.  The population
statement depends only on the typed compression and moments and hence remains
parallel.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[No canonical ``remaining third'']
\label{fire:GRH-no-residual-third}
A lower-bound certificate does not identify the uncertified zeros with an
off-line eigenspace.  The rank--trace slack may arise entirely from
nonorthogonality of the positive evaluation frame.  The first-return compiler
must therefore act on the actual source-tagged pair histories, not on an
adverse eigenspace selected after the population estimate.
\end{firewall}

\subsection{Integrated hard-edge packets, zero modes, and the arithmetic router}
\label{sec:GRH-integrated-zero-mode}

The completed--Euler comparison above is one source-metric formulation of the
upper bridge.  A complementary hard-edge formulation arises when the total
and phase sources are first assembled over the accepted energy region.  The
order of operations is load bearing: resolving each atomic energy and shorting
there can remove the cross-energy orientation responsible for cancellation.

\begin{theorem}[Integrated-box router and zero-mode reduction]
\label{thm:GRH-integrated-zero-mode}
Let a finite accepted energy partition have complete total--phase Grams
\[
 G_{j,X}=\begin{pmatrix}A_{j,X}&B_{j,X}\\
 \overline{B_{j,X}}&A_{j,X}\end{pmatrix}\succeq0,
 \qquad A_{j,X}>0.
\]
Set
\[
 A_X=\sum_jA_{j,X},
 \qquad B_X=\sum_jB_{j,X},
 \qquad K_X=B_X/A_X,
\]
\[
 D_X^{\rm pred}=\frac{|B_X|^2}{A_X},
 \qquad
 \kappa_X=A_X-D_X^{\rm pred}.
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{
 \sum_j\frac{|B_{j,X}|^2}{A_{j,X}}
 -\frac{|B_X|^2}{A_X}
 =\sum_jA_{j,X}\left|\frac{B_{j,X}}{A_{j,X}}-K_X\right|^2\ge0.}
\]
Thus the short of the assembled complete Gram is not the sum of the
pointwise shorts.

Suppose additionally that the assembled packet is represented on a physical
Hilbert carrier by a contraction $T_X$, an accepted total source
$A_X^{\rm src}$ with $T_X^*A_X^{\rm src}=A_X^{\rm src}$, and a phase source
$Z_X$.  Let $P_{0,X}$ project onto $\Ker(I-T_X)$.  Then the predictable mixed
energy is bounded by
\[
 \boxed{
 D_X^{\rm pred}
 \le\left\|Z_X^*P_{0,X}Z_X\right\|}
\]
after the common source normalization.  In particular, any regulator estimate
\[
 \left\|Z_X^*P_{0,X}Z_X\right\|=X^{o(1)}
\]
forces a subpower predictable-stiffness deficit.  When the arithmetic loading
identifies $B_X$ with the normalized completed Euler endpoint and
$A_X=X^{1+o(1)}$, this gives the square-root-scale upper estimate required by
the corresponding hard-edge GRH bridge.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The first identity is the scalar specialization of
\Cref{thm:GT-assembly-before-short}.  For the second statement,
\Cref{thm:GT-fixed-coboundary} shows that a fixed accepted source couples only
to $P_{0,X}Z_X$ and that its normalized prediction Gram is dominated by
$Z_X^*P_{0,X}Z_X$.  The final implication is the stated arithmetic
normalization.
\end{proof}

\begin{countertheorem}[Atomic shorting can destroy the hard-edge orientation]
\label{cth:GRH-atomic-short}
There are two energy atoms for which the protected short at each atom is zero
while the short of the assembled complete Gram is strictly positive.
\end{countertheorem}

\begin{proof}
Take total and phase columns $(1,1)^\mathsf T$ and $(1,-1)^\mathsf T$.  At
each atom the two columns are proportional, so the local protected short is
zero.  The sum of the two complete Grams is $2I_2$, whose protected short is
two.
\end{proof}

\begin{assessment}[Two admissible GRH upper-bridge routes]
The relative completed--Euler metric route and the integrated hard-router
route are complementary.  The first seeks a cutoff-uniform source metric
comparison.  The second seeks a small fixed component, an exact coboundary, or
an upstream Ward symmetry for the assembled phase source.  Neither route is
closed by pointwise positivity, a finite gap, source inclusion, or a
post-terminal permutation of already counted phase fibres.
\end{assessment}

% =============================================================================
\section{Affine-linear prime systems: local factors and connected tensor grades}
\label{sec:affine-prime-interface}
% =============================================================================

Ordinary linear Diophantine equations over $\Z$ are decided by Smith normal
form.  The open prime-valued problem begins only after affine coordinates are
required to lie in the primes.  The relevant Grand-Tensor object is therefore
not another integer-lattice solver but the all-support tensor correlation of
the von Mangoldt source after the complete local and proper-subset models have
been shorted.

\begin{definition}[Affine prime packet]
\label{def:GT-affine-prime-packet}
Let
\[
 \Psi=(\psi_1,\ldots,\psi_t),
 \qquad
 \psi_i(n)=\dot\psi_i(n)+b_i
\]
be nonconstant affine-linear forms $\Z^d\to\Z$, and let $K\subset\R^d$ be a
bounded convex body with boundary of measure zero.  Put
\[
 \mathcal P_{\Psi,K}(N)
 :=\sum_{n\in NK\cap\Z^d}\prod_{i=1}^t\Lambda(\psi_i(n)).
\]
For a prime $p$, define
\[
 \Lambda_p(a)=\frac p{p-1}\one_{a\not\equiv0\pmod p},
\]
\[
 \boxed{
 \beta_p(\Psi)
 :=\mathbb E_{n\in(\Z/p\Z)^d}
 \prod_{i=1}^t\Lambda_p(\psi_i(n)).}
\]
The packet is locally admissible when $\beta_p(\Psi)>0$ for every $p$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Exact local obstruction and Chinese-remainder assembly]
\label{thm:GT-affine-local-factors}
For every prime $p$,
\[
 \boxed{
 \beta_p(\Psi)>0
 \iff
 \exists n\in(\Z/p\Z)^d\text{ such that }
 p\nmid\prod_i\psi_i(n).}
\]
For squarefree $q$, the corresponding local density satisfies
\[
 \boxed{\beta_q(\Psi)=\prod_{p\mid q}\beta_p(\Psi).}
\]
Thus the finite singular product is an exact tensor product of local
zero-frequency densities.  Its infinite convergence and nonvanishing remain a
separate regulator certificate.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Every summand defining $\beta_p$ is nonnegative and is positive exactly when
none of the forms vanishes modulo $p$.  The Chinese remainder theorem
identifies $(\Z/q\Z)^d$ with the product of its prime-modulus factors, and
Fubini factorizes the uniform average.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Affine Fourier relation and the common source hierarchy]
\label{thm:GT-affine-Fourier}
Let $G$ be a finite abelian group, let $\widehat G$ be its character group, and
let $\psi_i(x)=L_ix+b_i$ be affine maps $G^d\to G$.  Define the dual relation
lattice
\[
 \mathcal R_\Psi
 :=\left\{(\chi_1,\ldots,\chi_t)\in\widehat G^t:
 \prod_i\chi_i(L_ix)=1\text{ for every }x\in G^d\right\}.
\]
For arbitrary functions $f_i:G\to\C$,
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathbb E_{x\in G^d}\prod_{i=1}^tf_i(\psi_i(x))
 =\frac1{|G|^t}
 \sum_{(\chi_i)\in\mathcal R_\Psi}
 \prod_{i=1}^t\widehat f_i(\chi_i)\chi_i(b_i).}
\]
Consequently degree-one Dirichlet-character sums and higher affine-prime
correlations are transforms of one von Mangoldt source, but they occupy
different tensor grades.  In particular a nontrivial character $\chi$ is
noninvariant at degree one while
$H_\chi\otimes H_{\overline\chi}$ lies in the neutral degree-two sector.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Insert Fourier inversion into every factor.  Averaging the product of the
characters over $G^d$ gives one exactly on $\mathcal R_\Psi$ and zero off it.
The final statement is the character-neutralization formula in
\Cref{thm:GT-positive-unitary-tensor-dichotomy}.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Conditional connected-uniformity bridge for affine primes]
\label{thm:GT-affine-connected-bridge}
At cutoff $N$, suppose the canonical arithmetic loading and its complete local
model give an orthogonal one-source decomposition
\[
 \lambda_N=\nu_N+r_N,
\]
where $\nu_N$ contains the constant, congruence, and local-factor source and
$r_N$ is the efficient residual.  For a degree-$t$ affine packet, perform:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(A\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item the simultaneous short by every proper-support tensor grade;
\item the source-fusion and occurrence audit of
      \Cref{thm:GT-source-fusion,thm:GT-complete-connected-sector};
\item the occurrence Feshbach reduction of
      \Cref{thm:GT-occurrence-Feshbach}.
\end{enumerate}
Let $Z_{\Psi,N}^{\rm eff}$ be the resulting all-support source, let
$L_{\Psi,N}^{\rm eff}\succeq0$ be the independently reconstructed effective
action, and let $P_{\Psi,N}^{\rm fix}$ project onto its kernel.  If the affine
relation source $A_{\Psi,N}$ is fixed by this action, if
\[
 \|A_{\Psi,N}\|^2=O_\Psi(N^d),
\]
\[
 \boxed{
 \left\|(Z_{\Psi,N}^{\rm eff})^*
 P_{\Psi,N}^{\rm fix}Z_{\Psi,N}^{\rm eff}\right\|
 =o_\Psi(N^d),}
\]
and if the singular product converges to a nonzero limit, then
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal P_{\Psi,K}(N)
 =N^d\operatorname{vol}(K)\prod_p\beta_p(\Psi)
 +o_\Psi(N^d).}
\]
The same conclusion holds simultaneously for every finite bank loaded into one
common effective action.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Expanding $(\nu_N+r_N)^{\otimes t}$ separates the local model from the
proper-subset and all-residual terms.  The first short removes every term
supported on a proper subset of slots.  Fusion and occurrence reduction replace
the remaining raw source by $Z_{\Psi,N}^{\rm eff}$.  Since the relation source
is fixed, \Cref{thm:GT-fixed-coboundary} bounds the squared connected correction
by
\[
 \|A_{\Psi,N}\|^2
 \left\|(Z_{\Psi,N}^{\rm eff})^*
 P_{\Psi,N}^{\rm fix}Z_{\Psi,N}^{\rm eff}\right\|
 =o_\Psi(N^{2d}).
\]
Hence the connected correction is $o_\Psi(N^d)$.  The surviving local term is
the finite singular product, and the assumed regulator convergence gives the
stated main term.
\end{proof}


\begin{theorem}[Neutral pair--switching incidence compiler]
\label{thm:affine-switching-incidence}
Let $N_{\rm par}$ be the complete source-resolved neutral pair synthesis before
the final parity short, and let $S_{\rm sw}$ be the actual divisor, Vaughan,
or switching-history synthesis.  With
$P_{\rm sw}=S_{\rm sw}(S_{\rm sw}^*S_{\rm sw})^\dagger S_{\rm sw}^*$, put
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathbb I_{{\rm par}\mid{\rm sw}}
 =N_{\rm par}^*(I-P_{\rm sw})N_{\rm par}\succeq0.}
 \tag{AFF.1}
\]
Its rank is the minimum missing switching or occurrence source dimension.
Only on the zero-innovation branch may the characteristic switching
connection or Hodge action be used to control the complete neutral pair
source.  After compression to one final parity line, every positive quadratic
action is a scalar multiple of the squared endpoint and supplies no new
parity mechanism.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The first statement is the source-incidence Schur Pythagoras.  On a
one-dimensional quotient every positive form is proportional to the unique
squared coordinate, proving endpoint equivalence.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[Degree-one GRH cancellation does not close neutral prime pairs]
\label{fire:GT-GRH-not-affine}
A degree-one Ward identity may annihilate every nontrivial character source
while leaving the product-one sector
$H_\chi\otimes H_{\overline\chi}$ untouched.  Twin-prime and binary-Goldbach
channels lie in such neutral quadratic sectors and may also carry a
nonmonoidal occurrence innovation.  Their closure therefore requires an
actual degree-two source fusion, proper-subset short, occurrence reduction, and
connected-uniformity estimate; it does not follow from GRH or from local
admissibility alone.
\end{firewall}


\section{Yang--Mills: transfer gaps and zero-free half-planes}
\label{sec:YM-interface}
% =============================================================================

\begin{theorem}[Mass gap--zero-free half-plane duality]
\label{thm:gap-zero-free}
Let $T_0$ be a finite normal contraction on a non-vacuum sector, let
$q=\norm{T_0}_{\op}<1$, and put
$\Delta=-\tau^{-1}\log q>0$.  For
\[
 D_{\rm rel}(s)=\det(I-e^{-\tau s}T_0)
\]
one has
\[
 \boxed{
 \sup\{\Re s:D_{\rm rel}(s)=0\}
 =\tau^{-1}\log q=-\Delta.}
\]
Consequently $D_{\rm rel}$ is zero free in $\Re s>-\Delta$.  Conversely, if
it is zero free in $\Re s>-\Delta_0$, then
$\norm{T_0}_{\op}\le e^{-\tau\Delta_0}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
For a normal matrix the operator norm equals the largest eigenvalue modulus.
Apply \Cref{thm:eigenvalue-zero-lines} with $\ell=\tau$.  The converse follows
because every nonzero eigenvalue produces a determinant zero on the vertical
line determined by its modulus.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Primitive invariant-loop saturation]
\label{thm:YM-primitive-loop-saturation}
On a finite connected lattice, retain before centering every selected global
cycle, centre-flux, and topological record.  The algebra generated by primitive
edge-current and transported plaquette writers, adjoints, finite products,
local concatenation, reflection, gauge averaging, and the retained global
cycles is dense in the selected finite-lattice gauge-invariant algebra.  If the
finite-regulator vacuum is strictly positive almost everywhere, the centered
primitive source orbit is cyclic in the selected neutral vacuum complement.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
After maximal-tree gauge reduction, defining-representation matrix
coefficients and their conjugates separate points of the compact product of
chord holonomies.  Stone--Weierstrass and gauge averaging give the full
invariant continuous algebra; Peter--Weyl gives the same statement in the
spin-network basis.  The global cycles are necessary because contractible
plaquettes are invariant under nontrivial centre one-form transformations.
Multiplication by a strictly positive vacuum is a unitary from
$L^2(|\Omega|^2d\mu)$ onto the physical Hilbert space, so density of the
function algebra gives cyclicity.  Centering then removes only the vacuum
line.
\end{proof}


\begin{theorem}[Vacuum Doob transfer as a Koopman compression]
\label{thm:YM-Doob-Koopman}
Let $0\preceq T\preceq I$ be a finite-regulator gauge-invariant transfer with
strictly positive normalized vacuum $T\Omega=\Omega$.  In a configuration
representation with reference measure $\nu$, put
\[
 d\mu=|\Omega|^2d\nu,
 \qquad
 \mathscr P f=\Omega^{-1}T(\Omega f).
\]
Then $\mathscr P$ is a self-adjoint Markov contraction on $L^2(\mu)$.  Let
$\boldsymbol\mu$ be its stationary two-sided path law, let $U$ be the path
shift on $L^2(\boldsymbol\mu)$, and let
$Jf(\omega)=f(\omega_0)$.  For every $n\ge0$,
\[
 \boxed{J^*U^nJ=\mathscr P^n,}
\]
and
\[
 \boxed{
 2(I-\mathscr P)=J^*(U-I)^*(U-I)J.}
\]
Thus the Yang--Mills transfer Dirichlet form is exactly one half of the
untwisted Koopman augmentation energy on one-slice observables.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Multiplication by $\Omega$ is unitary from $L^2(\mu)$ to the physical transfer
space, so positivity, self-adjointness, and vacuum preservation make
$\mathscr P$ a self-adjoint Markov contraction.  Stationarity gives, for
bounded $f,g$,
\[
 \langle Jf,U^nJg\rangle
 =\mathbb E[\overline{f(X_0)}g(X_n)]
 =\langle f,\mathscr P^ng\rangle.
\]
This proves the compression identity.  Expanding
$(U-I)^*(U-I)=2I-U-U^*$ and using reversibility gives the second formula.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Yang--Mills occupies the invariant/fixed-free arm]
\label{cor:YM-no-character-arm}
If $0\preceq\mathscr P\preceq I$, then its only unit-circle spectral value is
$1$.  Hence a positive self-adjoint Yang--Mills transfer cannot supply a
nontrivial predictive character.  Its protected decomposition is the vacuum
fixed sector together with the fixed-free complement on which the mass gap is
a positive augmentation floor.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The spectrum of a positive contraction is contained in $[0,1]$.  Its
intersection with the unit circle is therefore $\{1\}$.
\end{proof}


\begin{theorem}[Volume-uniform strong-electric $SU(3)$ slab gap]
\label{thm:YM-strong-electric-gap}
For the finite-volume $SU(3)$ heat-kernel/Wilson transfer, let
$\varepsilon_\kappa=\|K_\kappa-1\|_\infty$.  If
\[
 \boxed{2\varepsilon_\kappa+12\tanh\eta<1,}
\]
then in every finite periodic spatial volume and every reducing neutral
sector,
\[
 \boxed{
 \|T_{\kappa,\eta}|_{\Omega^\perp}\|
 \le
 \frac{1-12\tanh\eta-
 \sqrt{(1-12\tanh\eta)^2-4\varepsilon_\kappa^2}}
 {2\varepsilon_\kappa}<1.}
\]
The value at $\varepsilon_\kappa=0$ is understood by continuity.  In
particular,
\[
 \boxed{\kappa\ge4,
 \qquad0\le\eta\le1/18
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 \|T|_{\Omega^\perp}\|\le9/13}
\]
uniformly in the periodic spatial volume.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The pointwise heat-kernel window bounds each of the two temporal single-link
influences by $\varepsilon_\kappa$.  A link belongs to four plaquettes and each
contains three other links, so the same-slice magnetic influence row sum is at
most $12\tanh\eta$.  The space--time Dobrushin matrix therefore has row sum
$2\varepsilon_\kappa+12\tanh\eta<1$.  Coupling the future cylinder with one
changed incoming link, passing to the Perron boundary law, and using the
one-dimensional cylinder Green function gives the displayed upper root for the
Doob slab contraction.  The Doob transform is unitarily equivalent to the
positive transfer, so the same bound holds on the vacuum complement and every
reducing neutral sector.  The heat-kernel character estimate at $\kappa\ge4$
and $\tanh\eta\le\eta\le1/18$ give the stated rational bound.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Finite regulated neutral-sector mass criterion]
\label{thm:YM-regulated-criterion}
Let a positive transfer contraction have a source-head/tail decomposition
\[
 T=\begin{pmatrix}A&B\\B^*&D\end{pmatrix},
 \qquad a=\norm A,\quad b=\norm B.
\]
Assume $\norm D\le1-\mu$ with $\mu>0$, $a<1$, and
$b^2<(1-a)\mu$.  Then
\[
 \boxed{
 \norm T\le q_{\rm reg}
 :=\frac{a+1-\mu+\sqrt{(a-1+\mu)^2+4b^2}}2<1,}
\]
and if $T=e^{-\tau H}$, the non-vacuum spectral gap obeys
\[
 \boxed{\Delta_{\rm reg}\ge-\tau^{-1}\log q_{\rm reg}>0.}
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
For $x\oplus y$ with $\norm{x\oplus y}=1$, positivity and Cauchy--Schwarz give
\[
 \ip{x\oplus y}{T(x\oplus y)}
 \le a\norm x^2+2b\norm x\norm y+(1-\mu)\norm y^2.
\]
The right side is bounded by the largest eigenvalue of
$\begin{psmallmatrix}a&b\\b&1-\mu\end{psmallmatrix}$, which is
$q_{\rm reg}$.  The strict determinant inequality
$b^2<(1-a)\mu$ places that eigenvalue below one.  The transfer relation then
converts the norm bound into the displayed energy gap.
\end{proof}



\begin{theorem}[Common-time signed compression and Stieltjes return packet]
\label{thm:YM-signed-threshold-packet}
Let $J$ be the source-range isometry between adjacent cutoffs and let
$T_X,T_Y$ be positive self-adjoint contractions at one calibrated physical
time.  Put $P=JJ^*$ and
\[
 M_1=J^*T_YJ,
 \qquad M_2=J^*T_Y^2J,
 \qquad C=M_1-T_X,
\]
\[
 L=(I-P)T_YJ,
 \qquad \mathbb V=L^*L=M_2-M_1^2\succeq0.
 \tag{YM.1}
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{T_YJ-JT_X=L+JC,
 \qquad (T_YJ-JT_X)^*(T_YJ-JT_X)=\mathbb V+C^2.}
 \tag{YM.2}
\]
Writing
$T_Y=\begin{psmallmatrix}M_1&B\\B^*&D\end{psmallmatrix}$ gives
$BB^*=\mathbb V$.  If $D\preceq dI$ with $d<q$, then
\[
 \boxed{
 qI-M_1-\frac{\mathbb V}{q-d}\succeq0
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad T_Y\preceq qI.}
 \tag{YM.3}
\]
The compression mismatch $C$ is signed: negative generalized directions
increase the threshold reserve and must not be replaced by $\|C\|I$.

If the third transported moment is available, then
\[
 \mathbb W:=BDB^*
 =M_3-M_1^3-M_1\mathbb V-\mathbb VM_1,
 \tag{YM.4}
\]
and the exact return self-energy satisfies
\[
 \boxed{
 \frac{\mathbb V}{q}+\frac{\mathbb W}{q^2}
 \preceq B(qI-D)^{-1}B^*
 \preceq
 \frac{\mathbb V}{q}+\frac{\mathbb W}{q(q-d)}.}
 \tag{YM.5}
\]
Finally,
\[
 \boxed{
 \operatorname{In}(qI-T_Y)
 =\operatorname{In}(qI-D)
 +\operatorname{In}\!\bigl(qI-M_1-B(qI-D)^{-1}B^*\bigr).}
 \tag{YM.6}
\]
Thus the head Schur complement counts exactly the threshold-failing source
directions, while the moment hierarchy adaptively reconstructs the positive
return packet.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The decomposition in \textup{(YM.2)} is the orthogonal split into the old
source range and its complement.  The Schur complement of $qI-T_Y$ gives the
exact threshold; the tail bound gives \textup{(YM.3)}.  Expanding $T_Y^3$ on
the head gives \textup{(YM.4)}.  The resolvent identity and
$0\preceq D\preceq dI$ give \textup{(YM.5)}.  Equation \textup{(YM.6)} is
\Cref{thm:GT-signed-Haynsworth}.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Two-scale Yang--Mills Feshbach gap compiler]
\label{thm:YM-two-scale-Feshbach}
Let the non-vacuum positive transfer generator at one regulator admit a
physical infrared/ultraviolet decomposition
\[
 L_X=\begin{pmatrix}A_X&B_X\\B_X^*&C_X\end{pmatrix}\succeq0.
\]
Assume
\[
 C_X\succeq\gamma_{\rm UV}I,
 \qquad
 S_X^{\rm IR}:=A_X-B_XC_X^{-1}B_X^*
 \succeq\delta_{\rm IR}I,
\]
\[
 \|C_X^{-1}B_X^*\|\le\beta.
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{
 L_X\succeq
 \min\left\{
 \frac{\delta_{\rm IR}}{1+2\beta^2},
 \frac{\gamma_{\rm UV}}2
 \right\}I.}
\]
If the three constants are uniform along a reflection-positive
weak-coupling/infinite-volume regulator family and the transfer is
$T_X=e^{-\tau L_X}$ at fixed physical $\tau>0$, the corresponding transfer gap
is uniform.  Failure returns an ultraviolet soft vector, an effective
infrared soft vector, or an unbounded relaxation router.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
For $x\oplus y$, \Cref{thm:GT-effective-action} gives
\[
 \langle x\oplus y,L_X(x\oplus y)\rangle
 =\langle x,S_X^{\rm IR}x\rangle
 +\langle y+C_X^{-1}B_X^*x,
 C_X(y+C_X^{-1}B_X^*x)\rangle.
\]
Also
\[
 \|x\oplus y\|^2
 \le(1+2\beta^2)\|x\|^2
 +2\|y+C_X^{-1}B_X^*x\|^2.
\]
Combining the two lower bounds gives the displayed constant.  Exponentiation
at fixed physical time converts a generator floor into a transfer contraction.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Boundary-complete infrared handoff]
\label{cor:YM-boundary-complete-handoff}
In the setting of \Cref{thm:YM-two-scale-Feshbach}, let the infrared and
ultraviolet carriers also feed an actual boundary or sweep-comparison map
$\mathcal D_X=(D_{{\rm IR},X}\;D_{{\rm UV},X})$.  Define
\[
 E_X=D_{{\rm IR},X}-D_{{\rm UV},X}C_X^{-1}B_X^*,
 \qquad
 K_X=D_{{\rm UV},X}C_X^{-1}D_{{\rm UV},X}^*.
\]
Then the exact boundary-complete infrared action is
\[
 \boxed{
 S_X^{\rm IR}+E_X^*(I+K_X)^{-1}E_X.}
\]
In particular, a positive patch or infrared floor in $S_X^{\rm IR}$ survives
ultraviolet boundary relaxation; only the separately measured comparison
between the effective return model and the physical transfer can consume that
floor.  Shorting the ultraviolet interior before assembling the boundary
would overestimate the additional boundary cost by the positive dispersion
$E_X^*K_X(I+K_X)^{-1}E_X$.
\end{corollary}

\begin{assessment}[Weak-coupling target]
The strong-electric Dobrushin estimate proves one nonempty finite-regulator
region.  Along the weak-coupling continuum trajectory the natural common-layer
target is instead block first: construct a physical ultraviolet floor, prove a
positive occurrence-shorted infrared action, and control the relaxation
router.  Bare-link smallness is neither required by this theorem nor expected
to persist on that trajectory.
\end{assessment}


\begin{firewall}[Why the Clay Yang--Mills theorem remains open]
A finite transfer gap becomes a four-dimensional Yang--Mills mass gap only
after a gauge-invariant, reflection-positive, nontrivial continuum measure is
constructed; the physical source family is proved complete; the vacuum is
unique; and the finite gap is uniform in volume and lattice spacing and
survives the Osterwalder--Schrader reconstruction.  The Grand Tensor organizes
these certificates but does not supply them.
\end{firewall}
