\section{Navier--Stokes: the exact relative-form continuation certificate}
\label{sec:NS-interface}
% =============================================================================

Let $A=-P\Delta$ be the Stokes operator on mean-zero divergence-free fields on
$\Torus^3$, let $B(u,v)=P((u\cdot\nabla)v)$, and, for $s>5/2$, put
\[
 E_s=\frac12\norm{A^{s/2}u}_2^2,
 \qquad
 D_s=\norm{A^{(s+1)/2}u}_2^2.
\]

\begin{theorem}[Conditional Navier--Stokes continuation]
\label{thm:NS-relative-form}
Suppose that on every finite interval of smooth existence there are
$\theta\in(0,1]$ and $k\in L^1_{\rm loc}$ such that
\[
 \left|\ip{A^{s/2}B(u,u)}{A^{s/2}u}\right|
 \le(1-\theta)\nu D_s+k(t)E_s.
\]
Then, with $K(t)=\int_0^tk(r)\,\dd r$,
\[
 \boxed{
 e^{-K(t)}E_s(t)
 +\theta\nu\int_0^te^{-K(r)}D_s(r)\,\dd r
 \le E_s(0).}
\]
A global estimate of this form implies global smoothness for smooth data.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The $H^s$ energy identity is
\[
 E_s'+\nu D_s
 =-\Re\ip{A^{s/2}B(u,u)}{A^{s/2}u}.
\]
Insert the assumed relative-form estimate to obtain
$E_s'+\theta\nu D_s\le kE_s$.  Multiplication by $e^{-K(t)}$ and integration
give the boxed inequality.  Since $s>5/2$, the standard local continuation
criterion rules out finite-time breakdown while $E_s$ remains finite.
\end{proof}



\begin{theorem}[Critical source--sheet Pythagoras and the work-null sector]
\label{thm:NS-source-sheet-pythagoras}
Let $g_R=A^{-1/4}F_R$ be the critical source at one finite head and let
$v_+,v_-$ be the two orthogonal protected helical sheet writers.  Put
$D_\sigma=\|v_\sigma\|^2$ and
$j_{R,\sigma}=\operatorname{Re}\langle v_\sigma,g_R\rangle$, and let
$P_{\rm sh}$ be the real orthogonal projection onto their supported span.  Then
\[
 \boxed{
 \|g_R\|_2^2
 =\sum_{\sigma=\pm}D_\sigma^\dagger j_{R,\sigma}^2
 +\|(I-P_{\rm sh})g_R\|_2^2.}
 \tag{NS.1}
\]
The first term is the minimum critical source norm visible to the two signed
sheet works; the second is the complete work-null source.

For exact-output fibres $h_{k,\sigma}$ and state writers $v_{k,\sigma}$, put
$r_{k,\sigma}=\operatorname{Re}\langle h_{k,\sigma},v_{k,\sigma}\rangle/
\|v_{k,\sigma}\|^2$ when $v_{k,\sigma}\ne0$, and
$\zeta_{k,\sigma}=h_{k,\sigma}-r_{k,\sigma}v_{k,\sigma}$.  With the weighted
sheet mean $\overline r_\sigma$, the high--high work-null source further
splits as
\[
 \boxed{
 \sum_{\sigma=\pm}\left[
 \sum_k\|v_{k,\sigma}\|^2|r_{k,\sigma}-\overline r_\sigma|^2
 +\sum_k\|\zeta_{k,\sigma}\|^2
 +\sum_{v_{k,\sigma}=0}\|h_{k,\sigma}\|^2
 \right].}
 \tag{NS.2}
\]
These are respectively exact-output router dispersion, phase quadrature, and
first-birth source mass.  They remain independent of the visible mixed-helicity
current.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The sheet writers are orthogonal, so \textup{(NS.1)} is orthogonal projection.
For each exact output, project $h_{k,\sigma}$ onto the real writer line and
then apply the weighted variance identity to the coefficients
$r_{k,\sigma}$; the zero-writer fibres are orthogonal first-birth terms.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Mixed-helicity/work-null continuation interface]
\label{cor:NS-mixed-null-continuation}
If on a maximal smooth interval $[t_0,T)$ the minimum common mixed-helicity
source action and the complete high--high work-null source in
\textup{(NS.2)} are both integrable, then
\[
 \int_{t_0}^{T}\|A^{-1/4}F_R(t)\|_2^2\,dt<\infty,
\]
and the standard critical source continuation theorem extends the solution
when $T<\infty$.  The unresolved PDE problem is to derive these integrability
bounds from the actual reproduction law, viscosity, pressure/projector rows,
open-scale current, and boundary work.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Add the visible and work-null identities and integrate.  The resulting
critical source moment is precisely the hypothesis of the inherited
continuation criterion.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Occurrence-shorted triad action and open scale current]
\label{thm:NS-effective-scale-current}
Let $H_{3,X}$ be an actual degree-three triad carrier.  Short simultaneously by
all one- and two-slot source ranges and by every nonmonoidal occurrence sector,
and let
\[
 A_{3,X}^{\rm eff}\succeq0
\]
be the resulting positive all-residual action.  Let
\[
 D_{{\rm sc},X}:H_{3,X}^{\rm eff}\longrightarrow S_X
\]
be the physical logarithmic-scale boundary map, and put
\[
 L_{{\rm sc},X}
 :=D_{{\rm sc},X}(A_{3,X}^{\rm eff})^\dagger
 D_{{\rm sc},X}^*.
\]
For every scale source $s_X\in\Ran D_{{\rm sc},X}$ orthogonal to the harmonic
obstruction,
\[
 \boxed{
 \inf_{D_{{\rm sc},X}j=s_X}
 \langle j,A_{3,X}^{\rm eff}j\rangle
 =\langle s_X,L_{{\rm sc},X}^\dagger s_X\rangle.}
\]
The minimizer is the canonical current
\[
 \boxed{
 j_X^*=(A_{3,X}^{\rm eff})^\dagger
 D_{{\rm sc},X}^*L_{{\rm sc},X}^\dagger s_X.}
\]
If the scale carrier is an open path, this cost reduces to the cumulative-sum
formula of \Cref{thm:GT-open-current}.  Any physical estimate comparing the
right side with viscosity, elapsed physical time, or boundary work therefore
charges the critical-null scale-counterflow branch without imposing an
artificial periodic character.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
This is the weighted Thomson principle.  Minimize the positive quadratic form
under the affine constraint with Lagrange multiplier $\phi$.  The normal
equation gives
$j=(A_{3,X}^{\rm eff})^\dagger D_{{\rm sc},X}^*\phi$, and the constraint gives
$L_{{\rm sc},X}\phi=s_X$.  The minimum-norm multiplier is
$\phi=L_{{\rm sc},X}^\dagger s_X$, which yields both formulas.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Translation--helical common-action handoff]
\label{thm:NS-translation-helical-handoff}
Let $D_{\rm tr}:E_{\rm tr}\to\mathcal H$ be the physically loaded translation-
strain bank and let $D_{\rm hel}:E_{\rm hel}\to\mathcal H$ be the helical
source, both represented in one positive same-history action.  Put
\[
 P_{\rm tr}=D_{\rm tr}(D_{\rm tr}^*D_{\rm tr})^\dagger D_{\rm tr}^*,
 \qquad
 R_{\rm hel}=(I-P_{\rm tr})D_{\rm hel}.
\]
For a screened interior--boundary action $A_Z=L_Z+D_Z^*D_Z$ with closed
obstruction projection $P_0$ as in the universal open-current packet, define
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathbb O_{\rm hel}
 =R_{\rm hel}^*P_0QR_{\rm hel},}
\]
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathbb K_{\rm hel}
 =R_{\rm hel}^*(Q-P_0)A_Z^\dagger(Q-P_0)R_{\rm hel}.}
\]
Then $R_{\rm hel}=0$ is exact routing of the helical source through the
translation source.  Otherwise $\mathbb O_{\rm hel}$ is the closed helical
obstruction and $\mathbb K_{\rm hel}$ is the minimum positive
interior-plus-boundary cost of the surviving source.  For each coefficient
$c$, the corresponding source has the canonical minimum decomposition
\[
 (Q-P_0)R_{\rm hel}c=L_Z^{1/2}a_c+D_Z^*j_c,
 \qquad
 \|a_c\|^2+\|j_c\|^2
 =\langle c,\mathbb K_{\rm hel}c\rangle.
\]
A signed scalar strain trace alone does not determine any of these positive
source ranges or costs.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The first residual is the Anderson--Trapp source short by the translation
range.  Orthogonal decomposition of $QR_{\rm hel}c$ into
$P_0QR_{\rm hel}c$ and its complement gives the closed obstruction.  The
minimum interior-plus-boundary representation on the complement is the
Moore--Penrose Riesz/Thomson formula for $A_Z$, yielding the displayed cost.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[The scale boundary must remain open]
\label{fire:NS-open-scale}
The triad source is a higher-grade connected object, but its logarithmic-scale
image is an open-boundary current.  Periodicizing the scale interval can reduce
the minimum transport action by an unbounded factor
\Cref{cth:GT-periodicization}; it is therefore not a harmless character
reformulation.  The unresolved PDE estimate is the comparison of the canonical
open current with the actual viscous and physical-time budget.
\end{firewall}


\begin{firewall}[A positive Schur complement is not the nonlinear estimate]
The Grand Tensor can encode the viscous form, the nonlinear insertion, and
their Schur residual.  Positivity of the ambient response does not imply the
scale-critical inequality in \Cref{thm:NS-relative-form}; proving that
inequality from the actual three-dimensional nonlinearity is the unresolved
PDE theorem.
\end{firewall}

\section{Birch--Swinnerton--Dyer: analytic jets, complexes, and determinant lines}
\label{sec:BSD-interface}
% =============================================================================

\begin{definition}[Analytic jet complex]
For an analytic germ $F$ and $m\ge1$, define the two-term finite Hilbert
complex
\[
 \mathcal C_{\rm an}(F,m):
 \qquad 0\longrightarrow\mathscr R_m
 \xrightarrow{\,M_m(F)\,}\mathscr R_m\longrightarrow0,
 \qquad \mathscr R_m=\C[z]/(z^m).
\]
Its determinant line is
\[
 \det H^\bullet(\mathcal C_{\rm an})
 :=\det H^0(\mathcal C_{\rm an})
 \otimes\det H^1(\mathcal C_{\rm an})^{-1}.
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{proposition}[Jet cohomology]
\label{prop:jet-cohomology}
If $r=\ord_0F<m$, then
\[
 \dim H^0(\mathcal C_{\rm an})
 =\dim H^1(\mathcal C_{\rm an})=r.
\]
The product of the nonzero singular values of the differential is
$|a_r|^{m-r}$ when $F(z)=a_rz^r+O(z^{r+1})$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
The kernel statement is \Cref{thm:analytic-jet}.  Since the differential is a
square matrix, its cokernel has the same dimension as its kernel.  The
nonzero-singular-value product is the square root of the pseudodeterminant in
\Cref{thm:analytic-jet}.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Conditional analytic--Selmer determinant-line bridge]
\label{thm:BSD-determinant-bridge}
Let $E/\Q$ be an elliptic curve and let
$F_E(z)=\Lambda(E,1+z)$.  Choose $m>r_{\rm an}(E)$.  Suppose an independently
constructed finite arithmetic Hilbert complex
$\mathcal C_{\rm Sel}(E,m)$ satisfies:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(B\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item its distinguished degree-zero cohomology has dimension
      $r_{\rm alg}(E)$;
\item there is a unitary chain isomorphism
      $U:\mathcal C_{\rm an}(F_E,m)\to\mathcal C_{\rm Sel}(E,m)$;
\item the determinant-line metric and the local period, Tamagawa, torsion, and
      Tate--Shafarevich normalization are identified independently.
\end{enumerate}
Then $r_{\rm an}(E)=r_{\rm alg}(E)$, and the analytic leading-coefficient
magnitude encoded by \Cref{thm:analytic-jet} equals the corresponding
arithmetic determinant-line magnitude.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
A chain isomorphism induces isomorphisms on cohomology.  Hence the degree-zero
cohomology dimensions agree, giving rank equality by
\Cref{prop:jet-cohomology}.  A unitary chain isomorphism identifies the
orthogonal complements of the kernels and preserves every nonzero singular
value of the differential.  It therefore preserves the determinant-line norm
obtained from the product of those singular values.  The third hypothesis
identifies that abstract norm with the independently normalized arithmetic
BSD line, proving the second conclusion.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[BSD scope]
Placing an analytic jet and a Selmer object in one direct sum is not a chain
comparison.  The arithmetic complex, its local conditions, the period metric,
Tamagawa maps, torsion, and $\Sha$ contribution must be constructed without
using the desired equality.  That construction and the unitary determinant-line
comparison are the unresolved arithmetic content.
\end{firewall}

\section{Hodge conjecture: cycle observability}
\label{sec:Hodge-interface}
% =============================================================================

\begin{theorem}[Hodge cycle-observability equivalence]
\label{thm:Hodge-observability}
Let $X$ be a smooth complex projective variety and fix codimension $p$.  For
rational algebraic cycles $Z_1,\ldots,Z_m$, define
\[
 \mathcal Z_X:\C^m\longrightarrow H_{\rm Hdg}^{2p}(X;\C),
 \qquad
 c\longmapsto\sum_jc_j[Z_j].
\]
The following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.8em]
\item the classes $[Z_j]$ span the Hodge sector;
\item $\mathcal Z_X$ is surjective;
\item $\mathcal Z_X\mathcal Z_X^*$ is positive definite on the Hodge sector;
\item $\mathcal Z_X\mathcal Z_X^*\succeq c_XI$ for some $c_X>0$.
\end{enumerate}
Thus the Hodge conjecture for $(X,p)$ is equivalent to the existence of a
finite rational-cycle family satisfying these conditions.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Spanning is surjectivity.  In finite dimensions surjectivity of
$\mathcal Z_X$ is equivalent to injectivity of $\mathcal Z_X^*$.  For every
$h$,
\[
 \ip{h}{\mathcal Z_X\mathcal Z_X^*h}=\norm{\mathcal Z_X^*h}^2,
\]
so injectivity is equivalent to positive definiteness, which in finite
dimension is equivalent to a positive least eigenvalue.  A finite rational
spanning family is exactly the fixed-sector Hodge assertion.
\end{proof}


\begin{theorem}[Finite invariants commute with cohomology]
\label{thm:Hodge-invariants-cohomology}
Let a finite group $G$ act by chain maps on a finite-dimensional complex
$(C^\bullet,d)$ over $\C$.  Then
\[
 \boxed{H^k((C^\bullet)^G)\cong H^k(C^\bullet)^G.}
\]
With a $G$-invariant Hilbert structure, the Hodge Laplacian and Green operator
commute with the Reynolds projector, and
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal H^k((C^\bullet)^G)
 =\mathcal H^k(C^\bullet)\cap(C^k)^G.}
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The Reynolds projector $P_G=|G|^{-1}\sum_g g$ commutes with $d$.  It replaces
an invariant cohomology class by an invariant representative and replaces a
primitive of an invariant exact class by an invariant primitive.  With an
invariant metric it also commutes with $d^*$ and therefore with the Hodge
Laplacian and its functional calculus.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Occurrence-shorted invariant semiregularity]
\label{thm:Hodge-occurrence-short}
Let an equivariant obstruction source split into product and occurrence
components,
\[
 \mathcal O^G=\mathcal O_{\rm prod}^G\oplus\mathcal O_{\rm occ}^G,
\]
and let the invariant semiregularity Gram be
\[
 G^{\rm sr}_G
 =\begin{pmatrix}A&B\\B^*&C\end{pmatrix}\succeq0.
\]
If $C$ is faithful on $\mathcal O_{\rm occ}^G$, define
\[
 \boxed{S_G^{\rm sr}:=A-BC^{-1}B^*\succeq0.}
\]
Then the full invariant semiregularity map is injective exactly when
$S_G^{\rm sr}$ is positive definite on $\mathcal O_{\rm prod}^G$.  On failure,
$p\in\Ker S_G^{\rm sr}$ returns the explicit invariant obstruction
\[
 \boxed{p\oplus(-C^{-1}B^*p)\in\Ker G_G^{\rm sr}.}
\]
Thus induction, orbit fusion, or another categorical occurrence construction
must be shorted before positivity of the product zero-character block is used.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Apply the completed-square identity of \Cref{thm:GT-effective-action} to
$G_G^{\rm sr}$.  Its kernel is the graph of the occurrence corrector over
$\Ker S_G^{\rm sr}$, giving both equivalence and witness.
\end{proof}


\begin{firewall}[Harmonic projection is not algebraicity]
Hodge--Dirac shorting reconstructs the harmonic sector, but it does not create
rational algebraic cycles.  The open certificate is the nondegenerate loading
$\mathcal Z_X\mathcal Z_X^*\succeq c_XI$ for an independently specified
cycle family.
\end{firewall}

% =============================================================================
\section{Complexity: resource-faithful loading}
\label{sec:PvsNP-interface}
% =============================================================================

\begin{countertheorem}[Ambient record dimension does not imply a circuit lower bound]
\label{cth:ambient-dimension-complexity}
Representing all $2^n$ Boolean inputs by orthogonal vectors forces ambient
dimension at least $2^n$, but it implies no superpolynomial circuit lower
bound.
\end{countertheorem}

\begin{proof}
The standard computational basis has dimension $2^n$.  Nevertheless the
identity, parity, and many other explicit functions on that basis have circuits
of polynomial size.  Hence storage dimension alone cannot lower-bound circuit
complexity.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Conditional resource-faithful complexity bridge]
\label{thm:PvsNP-resource-bridge}
Let $L$ be an explicit NP-complete language with Boolean family $f_n$.  Suppose
an independently defined Grand-Tensor loading has a resource functional
$R_n(f)$ satisfying
\[
 \CircuitSize(f)\ge\frac{R_n(f)}{p(n)}
\]
for one polynomial $p$, and suppose $R_n(f_n)$ grows faster than every
polynomial.  Then $L\notin P/{\rm poly}$ and, in particular, $P\ne NP$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The comparison gives superpolynomial circuit size for the explicit family
$f_n$.  Every language in $P$ has polynomial-size circuit families, so $L$ is
not in $P$; the stronger conclusion $L\notin P/{\rm poly}$ follows directly
from the stated circuit lower bound.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[Algebraic duality need not preserve resources]
A source-minimal realization may be dense even when the primitive process is
sparse, and Schur elimination may create quadratic fill-in.  A complexity
duality must therefore preserve or compare gate count, locality, precision,
communication, memory, separator size, and circuit depth.  Pairwise Grams,
spectra, and exact algebraic equivalence do not supply those bounds.
\end{firewall}

\section{Poincar\'e as a solved scale-flow benchmark}
\label{sec:Poincare-interface}
% =============================================================================

\begin{proposition}[Perelman benchmark interface]
\label{prop:Poincare-benchmark}
A scale-indexed Grand Tensor can encode a geometrically defined monotone
entropy, canonical-neighbourhood data, no-collapse margins, and surgery jumps.
Perelman's Ricci-flow solution shows that such a package can close a global
geometric problem.  The encoding alone neither reproves Poincar\'e nor
transports those estimates to arithmetic, gauge, fluid, or complexity sectors.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Representing each finite-scale response and each surgery jump as a typed scalar
or operator port is formal.  Monotonicity, canonical-neighbourhood control,
noncollapsing, and summability of the surgery budget are additional geometric
theorems.  Their validity for Ricci flow proves compatibility of the
architecture, not validity in another sector.
\end{proof}

\part{Exact cross-sector dualities}

% =============================================================================
\section{Abelian constraints, characters, Smith data, and Gale variables}
\label{sec:abelian-dualities}
% =============================================================================

Let $G$ be a finite abelian group, let
$A:G^n\to G^m$ be a homomorphism, and let
$A^\vee:\widehat{G^m}\to\widehat{G^n}$ be the dual map.  For
$w:G\to\C$, use
$\widehat w(\chi)=\sum_{x\in G}w(x)\chi(x)$.

\begin{theorem}[Finite constraint--character partition duality]
\label{thm:constraint-character}
For arbitrary weights $w_1,\ldots,w_n:G\to\C$ and $b\in G^m$, define
\[
 Z_A(b;w_1,\ldots,w_n)
 =\sum_{\substack{x\in G^n\\Ax=b}}\prod_{j=1}^nw_j(x_j).
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{
 Z_A(b;w_1,\ldots,w_n)
 =\frac1{|G|^m}
 \sum_{\eta\in\widehat{G^m}}
 \eta(-b)\prod_{j=1}^n
 \widehat w_j\bigl((A^\vee\eta)_j\bigr).}
\]
Fourier inversion in $b$ reconstructs either side from the other.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Character orthogonality on $G^m$ gives
\[
 \one_{Ax=b}=\frac1{|G|^m}
 \sum_{\eta\in\widehat{G^m}}\eta(Ax-b).
\]
Since $A^\vee\eta$ is a product character on $G^n$,
$\eta(Ax)=\prod_j(A^\vee\eta)_j(x_j)$.  Insert the orthogonality identity,
exchange the finite sums, and factor the $G^n$ sum into the one-variable
Fourier transforms.  Invertibility is ordinary Fourier inversion on $G^m$.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Exact solution count]
Taking all $w_j=1$ gives
\[
 \#\{x\in G^n:Ax=b\}
 =\begin{cases}
 |\Ker A|,&b\in\Ran A,\\
 0,&b\notin\Ran A.
 \end{cases}
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Only characters in $\Ker A^\vee$, the annihilator of $\Ran A$, survive.
Orthogonality on $G^m/\Ran A$ gives the two cases, and the finite-group
rank--nullity identity supplies the factor $|\Ker A|$.
\end{proof}

Now let $A:\Z^n\to\Z^m$ have rank $r$, and write
$\Torus=\R/\Z$.

\begin{theorem}[Smith--Pontryagin constraint duality]
\label{thm:Smith-Pontryagin}
Let $d_1\mid\cdots\mid d_r$ be the nonzero Smith invariants of $A$.  Then
Pontryagin duality gives the exact sequence
\[
 \boxed{
 0\longrightarrow\widehat{\coker A}
 \longrightarrow\Torus^m
 \xrightarrow{\,A^{\mathsf T}\,}\Torus^n
 \longrightarrow\widehat{\Ker A}
 \longrightarrow0.}
\]
Moreover,
\[
 \widehat{\coker A}
 \cong\Torus^{m-r}\times\mu_{d_1}\times\cdots\times\mu_{d_r},
 \qquad
 \widehat{\Ker A}\cong\Torus^n/A^{\mathsf T}\Torus^m.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Choose unimodular $U,V$ with
$UAV=\diag(d_1,\ldots,d_r,0,\ldots,0)$.  The induced torus maps are
automorphisms, so calculate in Smith coordinates.  A character of $\Z^m$
vanishes on $A\Z^n$ exactly when its first $r$ coordinates lie in
$\mu_{d_i}$ and its remaining coordinates are arbitrary.  This identifies the
kernel of $A^{\mathsf T}$ with $\widehat{\coker A}$.  Multiplication by each
$d_i$ is surjective on $\Torus$, so the cokernel of the torus map is the
quotient $\Torus^n/A^{\mathsf T}\Torus^m$, canonically dual to $\Ker A$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Derived Smith--Gale exact sequence]
\label{thm:Smith-Gale-sequence}
Let $R_q=\Z/q\Z$, let $A_q:R_q^n\to R_q^m$ be reduction modulo $q$, put
$\mathcal L_A=\Ker(A:\Z^n\to\Z^m)$ and
$\mathcal C_A=\coker A$.  Then
\[
 \boxed{
 0\longrightarrow\mathcal L_A/q\mathcal L_A
 \xrightarrow{\rho_q}\Ker A_q
 \xrightarrow{\beta_q}\mathcal C_A[q]
 \longrightarrow0.}
\]
For $\bar x\in\Ker A_q$, choose a lift $x\in\Z^n$ and write $Ax=qy$;
then $\beta_q(\bar x)=[y]$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Replacing $x$ by $x+qz$ replaces $y$ by $y+Az$, so $[y]$ is well defined,
and $q[y]=[Ax]=0$.  If $\ell\in\mathcal L_A$ reduces to zero, write
$\ell=qz$; then $qAz=0$ in the torsion-free group $\Z^m$, so
$z\in\mathcal L_A$, proving injectivity.  If $\beta_q(\bar x)=0$, then
$y=Az$, whence $x-qz\in\mathcal L_A$ and $\bar x$ lies in the image of
$\rho_q$.  Conversely every reduced integral kernel vector maps to zero.
Finally, if $[y]\in\mathcal C_A[q]$, then $qy=Ax$ for some $x$; its reduction
lies in $\Ker A_q$ and maps to $[y]$.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Gale completeness criterion]
\label{cor:Gale-completeness}
The reduction of an integral Gale basis spans $\Ker A_q$ exactly when
$\mathcal C_A[q]=0$, equivalently when $\gcd(d_i,q)=1$ for every Smith
invariant.  It is complete for every $q$ exactly when $\coker A$ is torsion
free.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
By \Cref{thm:Smith-Gale-sequence}, the quotient of $\Ker A_q$ by the reduced
integral kernel is $\mathcal C_A[q]$.  In Smith coordinates, the $q$-torsion of
$\Z/d_i\Z$ has order $\gcd(d_i,q)$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Smith--Gale arithmetic gauge compiler]
\label{thm:Smith-Gale-compiler}
Assume $A_qx=\bar b$ is soluble, choose one solution $x_0$, an integral Gale
basis $B:\Z^{n-r}\to\mathcal L_A$, and a section
$s_q:\mathcal C_A[q]\to\Ker A_q$.  Every solution has a unique form
\[
 x=x_0+B_qy+s_q(t),
 \qquad y\in R_q^{n-r},\quad t\in\mathcal C_A[q].
\]
For arbitrary slot weights $w_j:R_q\to\C$,
\[
 \boxed{
 \sum_{A_qx=\bar b}\prod_jw_j(x_j)
 =\sum_{t\in\mathcal C_A[q]}\sum_{y\in R_q^{n-r}}
 \prod_jw_j(x_{0,j}+\mathbf b_j\!\cdot y+s_q(t)_j),}
\]
where $\mathbf b_j$ is the $j$th row of $B$.  Equivalently,
\[
 \boxed{
 \sum_{A_qx=\bar b}\prod_jw_j(x_j)
 =\frac1{|\operatorname{im}A_q^{\mathsf T}|}
 \sum_{\xi\in\operatorname{im}A_q^{\mathsf T}}
 e_q(-\xi\cdot x_0)\prod_j\widehat w_j(\xi_j).}
\]
Both formulas are independent of the chosen bases and section.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The first decomposition is the choice of a representative in each fibre of
$\beta_q$ in \Cref{thm:Smith-Gale-sequence}; its kernel is the injective image
of $B_q$.  Uniqueness follows from exactness.  For the second formula, the
annihilator of $\Ker A_q$ in the dual of $R_q^n$ is
$\operatorname{im}A_q^{\mathsf T}$.  Hence
\[
 \one_{x-x_0\in\Ker A_q}
 =\frac1{|\operatorname{im}A_q^{\mathsf T}|}
 \sum_{\xi\in\operatorname{im}A_q^{\mathsf T}}e_q(\xi\cdot(x-x_0)).
\]
Insert this identity and factor the coordinate sums.  A basis or section
change only reparametrizes the same fibre, so the total sum is unchanged.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[Smith transformations are diagnostic]
General Smith column operations mix the original slots.  They classify the
congruence kernel and its dual gauge group, but they need not preserve prime
support, positivity windows, Mellin centres, local types, or resource cost.
All weighted arithmetic formulas must ultimately be pulled back to the
original typed coordinates.
\end{firewall}

% =============================================================================
\section{Nonabelian holonomy, spin networks, and Tannaka reconstruction}
\label{sec:nonabelian-dualities}
% =============================================================================

Let $G$ be a finite group and let $\Gamma=(V,E)$ be a finite oriented graph.
The gauge group $G^V$ acts on $G^E$ by
\[
 (h\cdot g)_e=h_{t(e)}g_eh_{s(e)}^{-1}.
\]


\begin{theorem}[Physical point/fibre connection and magnetic-loop alternative]
\label{thm:GT-point-fibre-holonomy}
Let $K=K^*\succ0$ act on a carrier with an independently readable point
projection
$\mathcal H=\bigoplus_{i\in V}\mathcal H_i$.  On an equal-rank supported edge,
write
\[
 -K_{ji}=V_{j\leftarrow i}A_{j\leftarrow i},
 \qquad V_{j\leftarrow i}\in U(r),
 \qquad A_{j\leftarrow i}\succ0.
\]
The block-local gauge acts by
$V_{j\leftarrow i}\mapsto G_j^*V_{j\leftarrow i}G_i$, and the cycle products
\[
 \boxed{\mathcal W_K(C)=\prod_{e\in C}V_e}
 \tag{HOL.1}
\]
are defined up to conjugacy.  A common block gauge makes every edge transport
the identity if and only if every fundamental-cycle holonomy is $I_r$.

For $\Lambda\ge\lambda_{\max}(K)$, put
$P_\Lambda=I-\Lambda^{-1}K$.  Then
\[
 \boxed{
 \log\det K
 =n\log\Lambda-
 \sum_{m\ge1}\frac1m\Tr(P_\Lambda^m),}
 \tag{HOL.2}
\]
and every trace is a convergent sum of closed-walk amplitudes carrying the
point/fibre holonomy.  On the flat rank-one branch these amplitudes can be
gauged nonnegative; on a nonflat branch they remain signed or complex magnetic
amplitudes.  Even block flatness does not scalarize the positive polar factors
$A_{j\leftarrow i}$; that requires a rank-one point Read or an independently
physical common fibre writer.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Spanning-tree gauge fixing proves the flatness criterion.  The spectrum of
$P_\Lambda$ lies in $[0,1)$, so functional calculus gives \textup{(HOL.2)};
matrix multiplication gives the closed-walk expansion.  Entrywise
nonnegativity is exactly the scalar cycle-sign criterion.  The final statement
follows because positive polar factors are unaffected by trivialization of the
unitary connection.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[Point algebra and source overlap are prior data]
A positive matrix is diagonal in some basis, so path positivity is vacuous
until a physical point/fibre algebra is fixed.  Conversely, the source-overlap
atlas of \Cref{thm:GT-source-overlap-flatness} does not determine the kinetic
connection.  Point Reads, coherent block tomography, and kinetic transport
are separate physical inputs.
\end{firewall}

\begin{theorem}[Finite holonomy--spin-network decomposition]
\label{thm:spin-network}
The gauge-invariant Hilbert space $L^2(G^E)^{G^V}$ has an orthonormal basis
indexed by:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.8em]
\item an irreducible unitary representation $\pi_e$ on each edge;
\item at every vertex $v$, an orthonormal basis element of the invariant space
\[
 \operatorname{Inv}_G\!\left(
 \bigotimes_{e:t(e)=v}V_{\pi_e}
 \otimes
 \bigotimes_{e:s(e)=v}V_{\pi_e}^*
 \right).
\]
The corresponding basis functions are obtained by contracting all edge matrix
coefficients with the chosen vertex intertwiners.  Thus full matrix holonomy
histories and spin-network coefficients are related by a unitary transform.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Finite Peter--Weyl theory gives the unitary bimodule decomposition
\[
 L^2(G)\cong\bigoplus_{\pi\in\widehat G}V_\pi\otimes V_\pi^*.
\]
Tensoring over edges decomposes $L^2(G^E)$ into edge-representation blocks.
At a vertex, the gauge action is the tensor product of the defining action on
incoming representation factors and the dual action on outgoing factors.
Orthogonal projection onto $G^V$ invariants therefore replaces each vertex
factor by its invariant subspace.  Choosing orthonormal bases in those finite
invariant spaces and contracting the representation indices yields an
orthonormal basis.  Completeness follows because the Peter--Weyl decomposition
is complete before projection and orthogonal projection preserves the direct
sum of all invariant blocks.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Closed spin networks separate gauge orbits]
The complete family of spin-network coefficients determines a gauge-invariant
function on $G^E$, and hence separates distinct gauge orbits in the finite
configuration space.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The spin networks are an orthonormal basis of all gauge-invariant functions.
If two orbits had identical values for every basis function, every invariant
function would agree on them.  The indicator of either finite orbit is
invariant, giving a contradiction.
\end{proof}

Let $\omega_G:\Rep(G)\to\operatorname{Hilb}_{\rm fd}$ be the forgetful fibre
functor.

\begin{theorem}[Self-contained finite Tannaka theorem]
\label{thm:finite-Tannaka}
The map
\[
 \boxed{
 G\longrightarrow\Aut^\otimes(\omega_G),
 \qquad g\longmapsto(\rho_V(g))_{V\in\Rep(G)}}
\]
is an isomorphism.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The displayed family is natural and monoidal, and the left regular
representation makes the map injective.  For surjectivity, let
$\eta\in\Aut^\otimes(\omega_G)$ and consider
$\mathcal O(G)=\C^G$ with its left regular action.  Pointwise multiplication
and the unit are intertwiners, so naturality and monoidality make
$\eta_{\mathcal O(G)}$ a unital algebra automorphism of $\C^G$.  It therefore
permutes the primitive idempotents $\delta_x$; write
$\eta\delta_x=\delta_{\sigma(x)}$.  Right translations are intertwiners for
the left regular action, so naturality gives
$\sigma(xh^{-1})=\sigma(x)h^{-1}$.  Hence $\sigma(x)=gx$ for the fixed element
$g=\sigma(e)$.

For any representation $(V,\rho)$ and $\ell\in V^*$, the matrix-coefficient
map
\[
 j_\ell(v)(x)=\ell(\rho(x^{-1})v)
\]
is equivariant.  Naturality gives
$j_\ell(\eta_Vv)=\lambda(g)j_\ell(v)=j_\ell(\rho(g)v)$.  Evaluation at the
identity and variation of $\ell$ yield $\eta_V=\rho(g)$.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Fibre-functor-preserving duality determines the symmetry]
\label{cor:Tannaka-group-iso}
If finite groups $G,H$ admit a symmetric monoidal equivalence
$F:\Rep(G)\to\Rep(H)$ together with a monoidal natural unitary
$\omega_HF\cong\omega_G$, then $G\cong H$.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The equivalence and fibre-functor identification conjugate
$\Aut^\otimes(\omega_G)$ onto $\Aut^\otimes(\omega_H)$.  Apply
\Cref{thm:finite-Tannaka}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Frobenius as tensor holonomy]
Whenever an unramified arithmetic packet assigns to every object of a finite
rigid representation category a natural multiplicative operator compatible
with tensor products, duals, and the fibre functor, that packet is one tensor
automorphism and hence one reconstructed holonomy element of the Tannaka
group.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The compatibility assumptions are precisely the definition of a tensor
automorphism.  Apply \Cref{thm:finite-Tannaka} to a finite group, or the same
reconstruction argument in the finite rigid tensor subcategory generated by
the packet.
\end{proof}

\begin{countertheorem}[Representation dimensions are not a symmetry duality]
The multiset of irreducible representation dimensions does not determine the
symmetry group.
\end{countertheorem}

\begin{proof}
Both $\Z/4\Z$ and $(\Z/2\Z)^2$ have four one-dimensional irreducible
representations, but only the first has an element of order four.
\end{proof}

% =============================================================================
\section{Chain, Hodge--Dirac, and determinant-line duality}
\label{sec:chain-dualities}
% =============================================================================

Let $C_\bullet$ be a bounded chain complex of finitely generated free abelian
groups and put $C^k_{\Torus}=\Hom(C_k,\Torus)$ with
$\delta^k\phi=\phi\circ\partial_{k+1}$.

\begin{theorem}[Cycle--flat-connection Pontryagin duality]
\label{thm:chain-Pontryagin}
There is a canonical isomorphism
\[
 \boxed{
 H^k(C^\bullet_{\Torus},\delta)
 \cong\Hom(H_k(C_\bullet),\Torus).}
\]
If
$H_k\cong\Z^{b_k}\oplus\bigoplus_j\Z/d_{k,j}\Z$, then
\[
 H^k(C^\bullet_{\Torus})
 \cong\Torus^{b_k}\times\prod_j\mu_{d_{k,j}}.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The circle group $\Torus$ is divisible and hence injective in the category of
abelian groups.  Applying $\Hom(-,\Torus)$ to the short exact cycle/boundary
sequences is therefore exact.  The universal-coefficient extension term
vanishes, leaving
$H^k\cong\Hom(H_k,\Torus)$.  Dualizing the displayed decomposition of $H_k$
gives the final formula.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Unitary chain equivalence transports Hodge--Dirac data]
\label{thm:Hodge-Dirac-transport}
Let $(C^\bullet,d)$ and $(C'^\bullet,d')$ be finite Hilbert complexes, and let
$U_k:C^k\to C'^k$ be unitaries satisfying
$U_{k+1}d_k=d'_kU_k$.  Then
\[
 U_k\Delta_k=\Delta'_kU_k,
 \qquad
 \Delta_k=d_{k-1}d_{k-1}^*+d_k^*d_k.
\]
Consequently $U$ identifies harmonic spaces, cohomology, Hodge decompositions,
nonzero singular values, analytic torsion products, and determinant-line
metrics.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Taking adjoints of the chain relation gives
$U_kd_{k-1}^*=d_{k-1}'{}^*U_{k-1}$ and
$U_kd_k^*=d_k'{}^*U_{k+1}$.  Substitution yields the Laplacian intertwining.
Its kernel is the harmonic space, canonically isomorphic to cohomology.  A
unitary intertwiner preserves orthogonal ranges, singular values, and the
products and exterior powers from which torsion and determinant-line metrics
are constructed.
\end{proof}

\begin{countertheorem}[Cohomology rank does not determine the determinant line]
\label{cth:cohomology-rank-not-determinant}
Two finite complexes may have equal cohomology dimensions and unequal
nonzero-singular-value products.
\end{countertheorem}

\begin{proof}
For $c>0$, consider the two-term complex
$0\to\C\xrightarrow{c}\C\to0$.  Its cohomology vanishes for every $c$, but
the unique nonzero singular value is $c$.  Choosing different $c$ changes the
determinant-line metric and torsion while preserving cohomology rank.
\end{proof}

% =============================================================================
\section{Commutants, common action, and Legendre reciprocity}
\label{sec:commutant-action-dualities}
% =============================================================================

\begin{theorem}[Finite commutant decomposition]
\label{thm:commutant-decomposition}
Let $\mathcal A\subseteq\mathcal B(\mathcal H)$ be a finite-dimensional unital
$C^*$-algebra.  There is a unitary decomposition
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal H\cong\bigoplus_{\lambda=1}^r
 \C^{n_\lambda}\otimes\C^{m_\lambda}}
\]
such that
\[
 \mathcal A\cong\bigoplus_\lambda M_{n_\lambda}(\C)\otimes I_{m_\lambda},
 \qquad
 \mathcal A'\cong\bigoplus_\lambda I_{n_\lambda}\otimes M_{m_\lambda}(\C).
\]
In particular, $\mathcal A$ and $\mathcal A'$ are mutual commutants.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Decompose the abstract finite-dimensional algebra into simple matrix blocks.
Its minimal central projections decompose $\mathcal H$ into invariant
summands.  Every unital representation of $M_n(\C)$ is a direct sum of copies
of its defining representation, giving the displayed tensor factors.  A block
operator commutes with all matrix units on the first factor exactly when it is
identity there and arbitrary on the multiplicity factor.  Applying the same
calculation twice gives mutual commutants.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Finite Howe dual pair]
Two unital subalgebras $\mathcal A,\mathcal B\subseteq\mathcal B(\mathcal H)$
form a finite Howe dual pair when
$\mathcal A'=\mathcal B$ and $\mathcal B'=\mathcal A$.
\end{definition}

\begin{proposition}[Terminating commutant audit]
\label{prop:commutant-audit}
For finite generating sets $\{A_i\}$ and $\{B_j\}$, the Howe-pair assertion is
decidable by finite linear algebra: solve
$[X,A_i]=0$ and $[X,B_j]=0$, compare the resulting dimensions with
$\dim\operatorname{alg}(B_j)$ and $\dim\operatorname{alg}(A_i)$, and verify
the inclusions.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Each commutator equation is a homogeneous linear system in the matrix entries
of $X$.  Hence both commutants and both generated finite algebras are computed
in finitely many linear-algebra steps.  An inclusion between finite-dimensional
subspaces plus equality of dimensions is equality.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Common-action Legendre reciprocity]
\label{thm:common-action-Legendre}
Let $B$ be a nondegenerate symmetric quadratic form and let
\[
 L_\chi(q,v)=\frac\chi2B(v,v)-\chi V(q),
 \qquad \chi>0.
\]
Its Legendre transform is
\[
 \boxed{
 H_\chi(q,p)=\frac1{2\chi}B^{-1}(p,p)+\chi V(q).}
\]
Thus one common Lagrangian action coefficient produces reciprocal Hamiltonian
coefficients $a=\chi^{-1}$ and $b=\chi$, with $ab=1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The momentum is $p=\chi Bv$, so
$v=\chi^{-1}B^{-1}p$.  Substitution in
$H=p(v)-L_\chi$ gives the displayed formula.
\end{proof}

\begin{countertheorem}[A second scalar coupling need not create a branch record]
Unequal effective coefficients do not by themselves imply a nontrivial
retained discriminator.
\end{countertheorem}

\begin{proof}
On a one-dimensional action environment every self-adjoint operator is scalar.
Nevertheless two independent action coordinates
$\alpha K+\beta V$ may have $\alpha\ne\beta$.  Thus coefficient inequality can
exist without a non-scalar branch record.
\end{proof}

% =============================================================================
\section{Cycle--flavour and pointed tetrahedral source duality}
\label{sec:cycle-flavour-duality}
% =============================================================================

Let $\Gamma=(V,E)$ be a finite connected graph with incidence map
$\partial:\C^E\to\C^V$.

\begin{theorem}[Exact harmonic cycle projector]
\label{thm:cycle-projector}
The orthogonal projection onto $H_1(\Gamma;\C)=\Ker\partial$ is
\[
 \boxed{
 \Pi_{\rm cyc}=I_E-\partial^*(\partial\partial^*)^\dagger\partial.}
\]
Moreover,
$\dim H_1(\Gamma;\C)=|E|-|V|+1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
For every matrix $M$, the projection onto $\Ker M$ is
$I-M^*(MM^*)^\dagger M$.  A connected graph incidence matrix has rank
$|V|-1$, so rank--nullity gives the dimension formula.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[The $K_4$ cycle carrier]
\label{cor:K4-cycle}
$H_1(K_4;\C)$ has dimension $6-4+1=3$.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The complete graph $K_4$ has four vertices, six edges, and is connected.
Apply \Cref{thm:cycle-projector}.
\end{proof}

\subsection{A renewal-native route to tetrahedral modules}
\label{sec:renewal-native-tetrahedral-modules}

The graph-theoretic cycle carrier above may arise either from a physically
loaded one-cycle edge writer or from the chronology of a more austere renewal
record.  The following theorem states the precise finite hypotheses under
which the latter route is available.

\begin{definition}[Sourcewise-uniform renewal atom packet]
\label{def:uniform-renewal-atoms}
A sourcewise-uniform atomic refinement of the concrete two-state renewal has:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(A\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item one nonwriting $H\to H$ atom and one nonwriting $P\to P$ atom;
\item equal probability for all nonzero atoms with the same source phase;
\item individually point-readable remaining $H\to P$ opportunity atoms and
      the two point-readable completed endpoint atoms;
\item no unread parallel atom beneath these point records; and
\item stationary reset of the atom selector with no feedback from older
      provenance.
\end{enumerate}
The opportunity set is denoted $\Omega$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Atomic opportunity rigidity and relative source]
\label{thm:atomic-opportunity-rigidity}
Every packet of \Cref{def:uniform-renewal-atoms} has
\[
 \boxed{|\Omega|=4,}
\]
with source-$H$ atom weight $1/5$ and source-$P$ atom weight $1/3$.  The
opportunity label of each completed cycle is uniform on $\Omega$ and iid across
cycles, while the completed endpoint is an independent fair bit.

For the centered point contrasts
$X_i=\one_{\{O=i\}}-1/4$, the Gram is
\[
 \boxed{
 G_\Omega=\frac14P_{\rm rel},
 \qquad
 P_{\rm rel}=I-\frac14\mathbf1\mathbf1^*.}
\]
Thus
\[
 \boxed{\rank G_\Omega=3,\qquad
 \lambda_{\min}^+(G_\Omega)=\frac14.}
\]
Under the abstract relabelling action of $S_4$, the relative carrier
$V_{\rm rel}=\mathbf1^\perp$ is the irreducible standard three-dimensional
module and
\[
 \det(\sigma|_{V_{\rm rel}})=\operatorname{sgn}(\sigma).
\]
The full $S_4$ action is physical only when the complete future table is
covariant under these relabellings.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The unique $H\to H$ atom has mass $1/5$, so sourcewise uniformity gives
opportunity atom mass $1/5$.  Their total mass is $4/5$, forcing four atoms.
Likewise the $P\to P$ atom has mass $1/3$ and the completed mass $2/3$ gives
two endpoint atoms.  Geometric summation of the equal departure and completion
atoms makes the opportunity label uniform, the endpoint fair, and both
independent of the numbers of survivor loops; reset gives iid cycles.

The covariance calculation
$\mathbb E(X_iX_j)=\delta_{ij}/4-1/16$ gives the Gram.  Its range is
$\mathbf1^\perp$.  Any nonzero invariant subspace containing a vector with two
unequal coordinates contains one difference $e_i-e_j$ and hence all such
differences, proving irreducibility.  The determinant of the full permutation
module is the sign and the constant line has determinant one.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Ordered two-cycle source gives $H_1(K_4)$]
\label{thm:ordered-opportunity-cycle-source}
Condition on two successive opportunity values being distinct and retain their
order.  The twelve ordered pairs are uniform.  On the antisymmetric ordered-
pair space $\mathcal D^-$ define
\[
 \partial_-(e_i\wedge e_j)=e_j-e_i.
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{
 0\longrightarrow H_1(K_4;\C)
 \longrightarrow\mathcal D^-
 \xrightarrow{\ \partial_-\ }V_{\rm rel}
 \longrightarrow0,}
\]
with
\[
 \boxed{
 H_1(K_4;\C)=\Ker\partial_-=\Lambda^2V_{\rm rel}
 \cong V_{\rm rel}\otimes\Lambda^3V_{\rm rel}.}
\]
The cycle projector and conditional source Gram are
\[
 \boxed{
 P_{\rm cyc}=I-\frac14\partial_-^*\partial_-,
 \qquad
 G_{\rm cyc}=\frac1{12}P_{\rm cyc}.}
\]
Thus the protected order of two renewal cycles produces a canonical
three-dimensional $H_1(K_4)$ source with the necessary orientation twist and
positive margin $1/12$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The antisymmetric ordered-pair space is
$\Lambda^2(\C\mathbf1\oplus V_{\rm rel})
=(\mathbf1\wedge V_{\rm rel})\oplus\Lambda^2V_{\rm rel}$.
The incidence map is onto $V_{\rm rel}$ and vanishes on the second summand, so
its kernel is the three-dimensional exterior square.  Moreover
$\partial_-\partial_-^*=4P_{\rm rel}$, the Laplacian identity for $K_4$,
which gives the projector.  Uniformity of the twelve ordered pairs gives
$I/12$ on the antisymmetric zero-sum space, and compression gives the source
Gram.  Contraction with the determinant line gives the orientation-twisted
identification.
\end{proof}

\begin{countertheorem}[One opportunity value does not determine one local edge]
\label{cth:vertex-no-local-edge}
There is no deterministic $S_4$-equivariant map
$\Omega\to\binom{\Omega}{2}$.  A local edge incident to a given opportunity
vertex requires a further three-valued conditional coordinate.
\end{countertheorem}

\begin{proof}
The stabilizer $S_3$ of one vertex fixes no individual edge of $K_4$, whereas
equivariance would require the image edge of that vertex to be fixed by its
stabilizer.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Matching-axis half-edges and the exact two-standard plane]
\label{thm:matching-axis-half-edge}
Let $\mathscr M$ be the three perfect matchings of $K_4$.  For every
$(i,m)\in\Omega\times\mathscr M$, let $j(i,m)$ be the vertex matched with $i$
and let $\varepsilon(i,m)=\{i,j(i,m)\}$.  Then
\[
 \boxed{(i,m)\longmapsto(i,\varepsilon(i,m))}
\]
is an $S_4$-equivariant bijection from $\Omega\times\mathscr M$ to the twelve
half-edges.  For the uniform point law,
\[
 \boxed{
 L^2(\Omega\times\mathscr M)
 \cong[4]\oplus2[31]\oplus[22]\oplus[211].}
\]
On the standard coefficient space $W_0=\one_4^\perp$, define
\[
 (S_{\rm ent}x)(i,m)=x_i,
 \qquad
 (S_{\rm lock}x)(i,m)=x_i+x_{j(i,m)}.
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{S_{\rm ent}^*S_{\rm ent}=\frac14I_{W_0},\qquad
 S_{\rm lock}^*S_{\rm lock}=\frac13I_{W_0},\qquad
 S_{\rm ent}^*S_{\rm lock}=\frac16I_{W_0}.}
\]
The conditional matching-axis source
\[
 \boxed{S_{\rm ax}:=S_{\rm lock}-\frac23S_{\rm ent}}
\]
is orthogonal to the entry source and satisfies
\[
 \boxed{S_{\rm ax}^*S_{\rm ax}=\frac29I_{W_0}.}
\]
After normalization,
\[
 E_0=2S_{\rm ent},\qquad
 A_0=\frac3{\sqrt2}S_{\rm ax},\qquad
 L_0=\sqrt3S_{\rm lock},
\]
one has
\[
 \boxed{E_0^*E_0=A_0^*A_0=I,
 \qquad E_0^*A_0=0,}
\]
and
\[
 \boxed{L_0=\frac1{\sqrt3}E_0+\sqrt{\frac23}\,A_0.}
\]
Thus entry provenance occupies one standard copy, the conditional matching
axis occupies a second orthogonal copy, and the locked-edge source is their
fixed combination.  The full conditional point-Read innovation over the
vertex record has rank eight and all positive eigenvalues $1/12$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
A perfect matching contains exactly one edge incident to a specified vertex,
and every half-edge determines the unique matching containing its edge and
the disjoint complementary edge.  This proves the equivariant bijection.
Induction from the vertex stabilizer, or the character table of $S_4$, gives
the displayed twelve-dimensional decomposition.

For $x,y\in W_0$, averaging over the twelve pairs gives
\[
 \mathbb E[\overline{x_i}y_i]=\frac14\langle x,y\rangle.
\]
For fixed $i$, each $j\ne i$ occurs once among the three matchings; using
$\sum_jx_j=\sum_jy_j=0$ gives
\[
 \mathbb E[\overline{x_i}(y_i+y_j)]=\frac16\langle x,y\rangle,
\]
and expansion of the two endpoint terms gives
$S_{\rm lock}^*S_{\rm lock}=I/3$.  Subtracting the projection coefficient
$2/3$ gives orthogonality and the Gram $2I/9$.  The normalized decomposition
follows by substitution.  Finally, each of the four vertex fibres is a
uniform three-point simplex of mass $1/4$, whose centered covariance has two
eigenvalues $1/12$; summing the fibres gives rank eight.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Classical opportunity--edge source obstruction]
\label{thm:classical-entry-edge-obstruction}
Let $O$ be a uniform opportunity vertex and $E$ a uniform edge of $K_4$ in one
diagonally $S_4$-invariant classical point law.  Put
\[
 t=\Pr(O\in E).
\]
The complete joint law is
\[
 \Pr(O=i,E=e)=
 \begin{cases}
 t/12,&i\in e,\\
 (1-t)/12,&i\notin e.
 \end{cases}
\]
For the standard entry and edge sources,
\[
 \boxed{S_O^*S_O=\frac14I,
 \qquad S_E^*S_E=\frac13I,
 \qquad S_O^*S_E=\frac{2t-1}{6}I.}
\]
After normalization their cross transport is
\[
 \boxed{\rho_tI,
 \qquad \rho_t=\frac{2t-1}{\sqrt3},
 \qquad |\rho_t|\le\frac1{\sqrt3}.}
\]
Hence both normalized Schur residuals obey
\[
 \boxed{I-\rho_t^2I\succeq\frac23I.}
\]
No classical invariant opportunity--edge point record can therefore make the
entry and locked-edge triplets one normalized physical source.  The
matching-axis branch has $t=1$ and attains the maximal classical correlation,
but still retains the orthogonal axis copy of
\Cref{thm:matching-axis-half-edge}.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
There are twelve incident and twelve nonincident vertex--edge pairs, and
invariance is transitive on each orbit, which gives the joint law.  Direct
averaging of $x_O$ and $x_i+x_j$ for $E=\{i,j\}$ gives the three scalar Gram
blocks.  Whitening gives $\rho_t$, whose bound follows from $0\le t\le1$.
The Schur residual is $I-\rho_t^2I$.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[Chronological cycle source versus local edge writer]
\label{fire:chronological-vs-local-k4}
The source of \Cref{thm:ordered-opportunity-cycle-source} is a two-cycle
history source.  The half-edge of
\Cref{thm:matching-axis-half-edge} is a one-stage local point record.  Neither
is automatically identical to the locked edge/order/charge writer of the
SM--spacetime loading.  Their identification requires one common physical
carrier, the mixed source Gram, the incidence and chronology relations, and
vanishing mutual Schur or cross-Hankel residuals.  Cardinality six or dimension
three alone is not a source-identity theorem.
\end{firewall}

\begin{theorem}[Finite cycle--flavour source duality]
\label{thm:cycle-flavour}
Let $(M_{\rm flav},T_{\rm flav},S_{\rm flav})$ and
$(H_1(\Gamma;\C),T_{\rm cyc},S_{\rm cyc})$ be finite source-minimal positive
transfer realizations whose Krylov packets stabilize at depth $r$.  If
\[
 S_{\rm flav}^*T_{\rm flav}^nS_{\rm flav}
 =S_{\rm cyc}^*T_{\rm cyc}^nS_{\rm cyc}
 \qquad(0\le n\le2r+1),
\]
then there is a unique source-fixing unitary $U$ with
\[
 US_{\rm flav}=S_{\rm cyc},
 \qquad UT_{\rm flav}=T_{\rm cyc}U.
\]
In particular,
$\dim M_{\rm flav}=b_1(\Gamma)$.  For $\Gamma=K_4$, the comparison implies
three loaded flavour copies.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
On stabilized Krylov sums define
\[
 U\left(\sum_{j=0}^rT_{\rm flav}^jS_{\rm flav}x_j\right)
 =\sum_{j=0}^rT_{\rm cyc}^jS_{\rm cyc}x_j.
\]
The moments through order $2r$ make the two Krylov Grams identical, hence the
map is well defined and isometric.  Stabilization and the order-$2r+1$
moments give the transfer intertwining.  Source minimality makes the map onto
and unique.  Equality of dimensions and \Cref{cor:K4-cycle} give the final
claim.
\end{proof}

\begin{countertheorem}[Dimension coincidence is not cycle--flavour duality]
Two three-dimensional carriers need not be source-dual.
\end{countertheorem}

\begin{proof}
Take identity sources and transfers
$\diag(0,1/2,3/4)$ and $\diag(0,1/3,2/3)$.  Their spectra differ, so no unitary
intertwines them.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Five-parameter pointed tetrahedral Gram]
\label{thm:five-parameter-tetrahedral}
Let a unitary $S_4$ representation act on $\mathcal H$, and let
$\Xi=(\xi_t,\xi_1,\xi_2,\xi_3,\xi_4)$ satisfy
$U_g\xi_t=\xi_t$ and $U_g\xi_i=\xi_{g(i)}$.  Then
\[
 G_\Xi=
 \begin{pmatrix}
 a&b&b&b&b\\
 \bar b&c&d&d&d\\
 \bar b&d&c&d&d\\
 \bar b&d&d&c&d\\
 \bar b&d&d&d&c
 \end{pmatrix},
 \qquad a,c,d\in\R,\ b\in\C.
\]
Thus the complete Hermitian source Gram has five real parameters.  It is
positive exactly when $c-d\ge0$ and
$\begin{psmallmatrix}a&2b\\2\bar b&c+3d\end{psmallmatrix}\succeq0$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The diagonal action of $S_4$ on ordered pairs of labels has the five orbits
$(t,t)$, $(t,i)$, $(i,t)$, $(i,i)$, and $(i,j)$ with $i\ne j$.  Invariance
therefore forces the displayed form, and Hermiticity imposes the stated
reality conditions.  The four-point permutation module splits as the average
line plus the three-dimensional augmentation module.  On the latter the Gram
acts by $c-d$; on the two trivial copies spanned by $e_t$ and the normalized
average it acts by the displayed $2\times2$ matrix.  Positivity is therefore
equivalent to positivity on those orthogonal isotypic blocks.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Terminating arithmetic--renewal source test]
Two pointed tetrahedral source families are related by a label-fixing isometry
exactly when their five Gram parameters agree.  If they are cyclic under
transfers of dimension at most $N$, equality of the five orbit panels
$\ip{T^r\xi_a}{T^s\xi_b}$ for $0\le r,s\le N$ yields a unique
source-fixing transfer intertwiner.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Equality of Grams defines the label-fixing isometry on linear combinations and
makes it well defined.  The transfer statement is the same finite Krylov Gram
construction as in \Cref{thm:cycle-flavour}, with the $S_4$ symmetry reducing
each inserted Gram to five orbit entries.
\end{proof}


% =============================================================================
\section{Common Schur innovations in the prime and GRH branches}
\label{sec:innovation-duality}
% =============================================================================

\begin{theorem}[Exact source-innovation short]
\label{thm:source-innovation}
Let $S_0:\mathcal P_0\to\mathcal H$ and
$S_1:\mathcal P_1\to\mathcal H$ be finite source maps, and put
\[
 A=S_0^*S_0,\qquad B=S_0^*S_1,\qquad D=S_1^*S_1.
\]
If $P_0=S_0A^\dagger S_0^*$ is the orthogonal projection onto
$\Ran S_0$, then
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathbb V_{1\mid0}
 :=D-B^*A^\dagger B
 =S_1^*(I-P_0)S_1\succeq0.}
\]
Its rank is the dimension of the part of $\Ran S_1$ not contained in
$\Ran S_0$, and every nonzero eigenvector reconstructs an explicit missing
source direction.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The Moore--Penrose formula for the projection onto $\Ran S_0$ is
$P_0=S_0(S_0^*S_0)^\dagger S_0^*$.  Substitution gives the identity.
Positivity is immediate.  The rank equals that of $(I-P_0)S_1$, whose range is
the orthogonal innovation space.  Applying $(I-P_0)S_1$ to a nonzero spectral
vector produces the corresponding direction.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[One complex orbit has real rank at most two]
\label{lem:one-complex-orbit-rank}
Let $v\in\C^d$.  The real span of the orbit pair $\{v,\bar v\}$ has dimension
at most two.  Hence no source requiring three independent real innovation
directions can be generated by one complex character--Mellin orbit and its
conjugate.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Write $v=x+iy$ with $x,y\in\R^d$.  Then
$v=x+iy$ and $\bar v=x-iy$ lie in the complexification of
$\Span_\R\{x,y\}$, whose real dimension is at most two.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Opposite innovation objectives]
\label{prop:opposite-innovation}
The same positive short in \Cref{thm:source-innovation} supports two logically
opposite proof objectives.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.8em]
\item A source-completion theorem seeks a small innovation rank or a structural
      description of every nonzero innovation; in particular,
      \Cref{lem:one-complex-orbit-rank} excludes a rank-three counterstate from
      one complex orbit.
\item A cancellation or coercivity theorem seeks an upper bound for the
      innovation energy, such as
      $\Tr\mathbb V_{1\mid0}$ or
      $\ip{x}{\mathbb V_{1\mid0}x}$.
\end{enumerate}
Neither objective implies the other without additional information.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
The rank and energy are independent spectral statistics of one positive
operator.  For example, $\varepsilon I_N$ has full rank and arbitrarily small
trace for small $\varepsilon$, whereas a rank-one projection has minimal
nonzero rank and unit energy.  The one-orbit conclusion follows from
\Cref{lem:one-complex-orbit-rank}.
\end{proof}

\begin{assessment}[Prime versus GRH use of the same theorem]
In the centered prime-tuple programme, low common resonance rank is a closure
mechanism: a true all-prime counterstate must introduce a third real direction
and therefore at least a second inequivalent character--Mellin orbit.  In the
centered GRH compiler, the predictable source is first shorted away and the
target is instead a uniform upper bound for the remaining innovation energy.
The shared object is the Schur short; the required inequalities point in
opposite directions.
\end{assessment}

% =============================================================================
\section{Interface Schur gluing, scattering feedback, and spectral shift}
\label{sec:interface-duality}
% =============================================================================

Let $\mathcal E_1,\mathcal E_2$ be exterior port spaces and $\mathcal I$ a
common interface.  Suppose
\[
 \Lambda_j(z)=
 \begin{pmatrix}A_j(z)&K_j(z)\\L_j(z)&H_j(z)\end{pmatrix}
 \quad\text{on }\mathcal E_j\oplus\mathcal I,
 \qquad L_j(z)=K_j(\bar z)^*.
\]
Gluing imposes equality of interface values and conservation of outward
interface current.

\begin{theorem}[Exact matrix interface gluing]
\label{thm:interface-gluing}
Assume $H=H_1+H_2$ is invertible and put
\[
 A=\begin{pmatrix}A_1&0\\0&A_2\end{pmatrix},
 \qquad K=\binom{K_1}{K_2},
 \qquad L=\begin{pmatrix}L_1&L_2\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Then the glued exterior response is
\[
 \boxed{\Lambda_{1\#2}=A-KH^{-1}L.}
\]
For exterior value $(x_1,x_2)$, the interface value is
\[
 \boxed{u=-H^{-1}(L_1x_1+L_2x_2).}
\]
Moreover,
\[
 \boxed{
 \det\begin{pmatrix}
 A_1&0&K_1\\0&A_2&K_2\\L_1&L_2&H_1+H_2
 \end{pmatrix}
 =\det(H_1+H_2)\det\Lambda_{1\#2}.}
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The interface responses are $g_j=L_jx_j+H_ju$.  Current conservation
$g_1+g_2=0$ gives the formula for $u$.  Substitution into
$f_j=A_jx_j+K_ju$ yields the Schur formula.  The determinant identity is the
Schur determinant formula with respect to the interface block.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Herglotz closure under conservative gluing]
\label{thm:Herglotz-gluing}
If $\Lambda_1$ and $\Lambda_2$ are strict matrix Herglotz functions, then
$H_1(z)+H_2(z)$ is invertible for $\im z>0$ and
$\Lambda_{1\#2}$ is strict Herglotz.  More precisely, if $u$ is the solved
interface value, then
\[
 \boxed{
 \ip{x}{\im\Lambda_{1\#2}(z)x}
 =\sum_{j=1}^2
 \ip{(x_j,u)}{\im\Lambda_j(z)(x_j,u)}.}
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The interface block of a strict Herglotz function has positive-definite
imaginary part, so $\im(H_1+H_2)\succ0$ and the sum is invertible.  The total
boundary work is
\[
 \sum_j\ip{(x_j,u)}{\Lambda_j(x_j,u)}
 =\sum_j\ip{x_j}{f_j}+\ip{u}{g_1+g_2}
 =\ip{x}{\Lambda_{1\#2}x}.
\]
The interface term vanishes by conservation.  Taking imaginary parts proves
the identity and strict positivity.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Associative interface elimination]
\label{thm:Schur-associativity}
Let a finite response be split into exterior space $\mathcal E$ and internal
space $\mathcal I_1\oplus\mathcal I_2$.  Whenever all displayed Schur
complements exist,
\[
 \boxed{
 \bigl(L/L_{I_1I_1}\bigr)
 /\bigl(L/L_{I_1I_1}\bigr)_{I_2I_2}
 =L/L_{II}.}
\]
Hence a finite network response is independent of the order in which internal
interfaces are eliminated.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Block Gaussian elimination first on $\mathcal I_1$ and then on
$\mathcal I_2$ has the same exterior diagonal block as direct elimination on
$\mathcal I_1\oplus\mathcal I_2$.  Equivalently, both sides are obtained by
solving the same internal Euler equation and inserting its unique solution
into the quadratic form.
\end{proof}

For a self-adjoint real-axis response, define the Cayley scattering matrix
\[
 \mathcal S=(\Lambda-iI)(\Lambda+iI)^{-1}.
\]

\begin{theorem}[Schur response--Redheffer scattering equivalence]
\label{thm:Schur-Redheffer}
Under the wave coordinates
$a=2^{-1/2}(j+iu)$ and $b=2^{-1/2}(j-iu)$, the response law
$j=\Lambda u$ is equivalent to $b=\mathcal Sa$.  Conservative interface
gluing becomes the signed feedback relation
$a_2=-b_1$, $b_2=-a_1$.  Eliminating the internal waves gives the Redheffer
star product.  If the component scattering matrices are contractions
(respectively unitaries), their well-posed star product is a contraction
(respectively a unitary), and the product is associative whenever all
intermediate feedback problems are well posed.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Solving
$a=(\Lambda+iI)u/\sqrt2$ and substituting in $b$ gives the Cayley formula.
At a common interface, equality of $u$ and reversal of outward current give
the signed feedback equations.  Both the Schur response and Redheffer
scattering formulas are obtained by eliminating those same internal variables
through an invertible linear change of coordinates, so the exterior maps
coincide.

For contractive components, add their two input--output energy inequalities.
The internal incoming and outgoing norms cancel under feedback, leaving the
exterior contractive inequality.  For unitary components the inequalities are
equalities; the same argument for the adjoint gives surjectivity.  Either
parenthesization of a multiple star product solves the same finite linear
system, so uniqueness gives associativity.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Matrix continued fraction and layer stripping]
\label{thm:matrix-continued-fraction}
Let
\[
 \mathbb J=
 \begin{pmatrix}
 C_0&B_0^*&0&\cdots&0\\
 B_0&C_1&B_1^*&\ddots&\vdots\\
 0&B_1&C_2&\ddots&0\\
 \vdots&\ddots&\ddots&\ddots&B_{m-1}^*\\
 0&\cdots&0&B_{m-1}&C_m
 \end{pmatrix}
\]
be a finite self-adjoint block Jacobi chain, and let $\Lambda_k(z)$ be the
response of the tail beginning at layer $k$.  Then
\[
 \Lambda_m(z)=zI-C_m,
 \qquad
 \boxed{
 \Lambda_k(z)=zI-C_k-B_k^*\Lambda_{k+1}(z)^{-1}B_k.}
\]
If every $B_k$ is square and invertible, then
\[
 \boxed{
 \Lambda_{k+1}(z)
 =-B_k(\Lambda_k(z)-zI+C_k)^{-1}B_k^*.}
\]
In the positive gauge $B_k\succ0$, the complete response $\Lambda_0$ uniquely
reconstructs every layer.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Treat the tail beginning at $k+1$ as the hidden interior of layer $k$ and
apply the Schur formula.  Rearranging gives the reverse recursion when $B_k$
is invertible.  At high imaginary energy,
\[
 \Lambda_k(z)=zI-C_k-z^{-1}B_k^*B_k+O(z^{-2}).
\]
Thus the constant and $z^{-1}$ coefficients recover $C_k$ and $B_k^*B_k$.
The positive square root fixes $B_k$, after which layer stripping reconstructs
$\Lambda_{k+1}$; induction recovers all layers.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Boundary spectral-shift identity]
\label{thm:boundary-spectral-shift}
Let $\mathbb A_0,\mathbb A_1$ have one common interior and two boundary loads,
and let $\Lambda_0,\Lambda_1$ be their responses.  Then
\[
 \mathcal D_{10}(z)
 :=\frac{\det(\mathbb A_1-zI)}{\det(\mathbb A_0-zI)}
 =\frac{\det\Lambda_1(z)}{\det\Lambda_0(z)}
\]
and, away from the spectra,
\[
 \boxed{
 \frac{\dd}{\dd z}\log\mathcal D_{10}(z)
 =-\Tr\bigl[(\mathbb A_1-zI)^{-1}-(\mathbb A_0-zI)^{-1}\bigr].}
\]
For a contour domain $\Omega$ avoiding both spectra,
\[
 \boxed{
 N_\Omega(\mathbb A_1)-N_\Omega(\mathbb A_0)
 =\frac1{2\pi i}\int_{\partial\Omega}
 \frac{\dd}{\dd z}\log\mathcal D_{10}(z)\,\dd z.}
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The determinant ratio is the Schur determinant identity applied to the common
interior.  Jacobi's formula gives
$\frac{\dd}{\dd z}\log\det(\mathbb A_j-zI)
=-\Tr(\mathbb A_j-zI)^{-1}$; subtract.  The contour formula is the argument
principle, with zeros and poles of the ratio counting the two spectra.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Positive Wigner--Smith boundary Gram]
\label{thm:positive-delay}
On a real pole-free interval, assume $\Lambda(x)=\Lambda(x)^*$ and
$\Lambda'(x)\succ0$.  For
$\mathcal S(x)=(\Lambda(x)-iI)(\Lambda(x)+iI)^{-1}$, put
$\mathcal Q_{\mathcal S}=-i\mathcal S^*\mathcal S'$.  Then
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal Q_{\mathcal S}(x)
 =2(\Lambda+iI)^{-*}\Lambda'(x)(\Lambda+iI)^{-1}\succ0,}
\]
and
\[
 \frac{\dd}{\dd x}\arg\det\mathcal S(x)
 =\Tr\mathcal Q_{\mathcal S}(x)>0.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Differentiate the Cayley transform to obtain
$\mathcal S'=2i(\Lambda+iI)^{-1}\Lambda'(\Lambda+iI)^{-1}$.  Since
$\mathcal S^*=(\Lambda-iI)^{-1}(\Lambda+iI)$ on the real axis, multiplication
gives the positive congruence.  Finally,
$\frac{\dd}{\dd x}\log\det\mathcal S
=\Tr(\mathcal S^*\mathcal S')=i\Tr\mathcal Q_{\mathcal S}$.
\end{proof}

\begin{countertheorem}[Local spectra do not determine gluing]
\label{cth:relative-interface-frame}
Complete spectra of the component interface blocks do not determine the glued
response without their relative interface frame.
\end{countertheorem}

\begin{proof}
On $\C^2$, put
$H_1=\diag(2,1)$ and take either
$H_2=\diag(2,1)$ or $H_2'=\diag(1,2)$.  The latter two have identical spectra,
but
$H_1+H_2=\diag(4,2)$ whereas $H_1+H_2'=3I$.  With exterior coupling $K=I$,
the Schur corrections are $\diag(1/4,1/2)$ and $I/3$, respectively.
\end{proof}

\begin{countertheorem}[Schur elimination can create quadratic fill-in]
\label{cth:Schur-fill-in}
A primitive system with $n$ boundary--interior couplings can have a Schur
response with $n^2$ nonzero entries.
\end{countertheorem}

\begin{proof}
Let one hidden scalar node of energy $d$ couple to all $n$ boundary ports by
$b=(b_1,\ldots,b_n)^{\mathsf T}$ with every $b_j\ne0$.  Its self-energy is
$bb^*/(d-z)$, whose every entry $b_i\bar b_j/(d-z)$ is nonzero.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Interface and network coercivity]
\label{thm:interface-coercivity}
At a real pole-free point let
$\Lambda=A-KH^{-1}K^*$.  If
\[
 s_{\min}(A)\ge\delta_A>0,
 \qquad s_{\min}(H)\ge\delta_I>0,
 \qquad \norm K\le\kappa,
\]
then
\[
 \boxed{s_{\min}(\Lambda)\ge\delta_A-\kappa^2/\delta_I.}
\]
More generally, for a final exterior/interior split
$\mathbb A=\begin{psmallmatrix}C&B^*\\B&D\end{psmallmatrix}$, if
\[
 \norm{(D-zI)^{-1}}\le M_D,
 \qquad \norm B\le M_B,
 \qquad s_{\min}(\Lambda(z))\ge\delta_E>0,
\]
then
\[
 \boxed{
 \norm{(\mathbb A-zI)^{-1}}
 \le M_D+\frac{1+M_D^2M_B^2}{\delta_E}.}
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The Schur perturbation obeys
$\norm{KH^{-1}K^*}\le\kappa^2/\delta_I$; the minimum-singular-value
perturbation inequality proves the first bound.  For the second, the solution
operator from exterior data to the full vector is
$\gamma(z)x=(x,-(D-zI)^{-1}Bx)$, so
$\norm\gamma(z)^2\le1+M_D^2M_B^2$.  The block resolvent formula is the direct
interior resolvent plus
$\gamma(z)\Lambda(z)^{-1}\gamma(\bar z)^*$; taking norms gives the result.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Integrated interface duality]
\label{thm:integrated-interface-duality}
For finite source-minimal self-adjoint boundary systems, the following are
coordinate presentations of one interface object:
\[
 \begin{gathered}
 \text{interface gluing}
 \ \Updownarrow\ 
 \text{matrix Schur response}
 \ \Updownarrow\ 
 \text{signed Redheffer feedback}\\[0.25em]
 \Updownarrow\\[-0.1em]
 \text{matrix continued fractions and layer stripping}\\[0.25em]
 \Updownarrow\\[-0.1em]
 \text{determinant ratios, spectral shift, and positive delay}.
 \end{gathered}
\]
The complete matrix response is required for relative-frame gluing and source
loading; determinant functions are scalar shadows.  Exact interface duality
is not automatically resource faithful.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The equivalences and closure statements are
\Cref{thm:interface-gluing,thm:Herglotz-gluing,thm:Schur-associativity,thm:Schur-Redheffer,thm:matrix-continued-fraction,thm:boundary-spectral-shift,thm:positive-delay}.  The necessity of the matrix
frame and the resource boundary are
\Cref{cth:relative-interface-frame,cth:Schur-fill-in}.
\end{proof}

\section{Integrated Grand-Tensor theorem}
\label{sec:integrated-grand-tensor}
% =============================================================================

\begin{theorem}[Integrated Renewal Grand-Tensor theorem]
\label{thm:integrated-grand-tensor}
The programme assembled in this manuscript has the following rigorous logical
form.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(G\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item A complete finite intervention table reconstructs its positive causal
      combs.  The generated ledger is reduced by the unique minimal
      future-readable congruence before record writers are completed.  Unread
      refinements do not enlarge the intrinsic tensor, while every genuinely
      point-readable record and every nonzero writer survives.
\item The record-conditioned Hankel quotient is the unique minimal linear
      predictor and directly determines the executable forward algebra.  At
      unbounded horizon, finite linear memory is equivalent to finite total
      Hankel rank; finite recurrent CP memory, finite full-record storage, and
      bounded physical action are separate compactness, cardinality, and module
      questions.
\item The reconstructed comb determines the canonical square-root
      support-minimal sequential CP class, unique up to record-intertwining
      memory unitaries.  The structural $C^*$-history algebra is independent of
      CP frames, Kraus and purification coordinates, and the support-minimal
      representative, but not of arbitrary unreduced positive factorizations.
\item The contextual future radical gives the unique minimal context-preserving
      separated history envelope.  The normalized regular trace gives the
      intrinsic positive word hierarchy; finite dimensionality forces flatness
      and reconstructs the unit, involution, multiplication, minimal record,
      conditional predictive algebras, and every represented mixed history.
\item Every faithful physical future metric is a positive congruence of the
      intrinsic hierarchy and preserves all word relations and monoidal
      structure.  Direct fringes remain optional measured contraction panels,
      and every common mathematical path dilation retains its path labels until
      an operational future-nullity theorem removes them.
\item Prefix-exact cutoffs have canonical polar support maps and a strict
      absorbing-corner history functor.  Part~I-B constructs their AF,
      quasilocal, compatible-state, GNS, joint-source, and finite-memory limit
      objects and defines a nontrivial physical continuum realization.  It also
      reconstructs the primitive score Fisher geometry, its conditional
      information action, the exact mean/noise short, and covariant information
      forms with explicit resolvent-continuum branches.  Part~I-C supplies source
      saturation, exact Hankel leakage, efficient connected-score shorts,
      support-order exhaustion, relative metric, operational router and
      holonomy, locality, feedback, tightness, head--tail, influence, and
      uniform-gap certificates.  Uncornered letters, contextual quotients,
      trace isometry, and the truth of the actual physical continuum hypotheses
      remain separate tests.
\item The renewal-native source is exactly the minimal two-state active chain
      of \Cref{thm:two-state-active-renewal}.  It has the displayed completed-
      private law, active rank two, stationary metric condition number $6/5$,
      contraction $7/15$, flux $4/11$, fresh endpoint, and zero private-to-active
      routing.  The completed boundary is the first rank-one predictive reset.
      Every finite lift has a canonical returned-feedback quotient, reconstructed
      from visible powers or the resolved word series; exact renewal makes this
      quotient zero.  The remaining source-reachable lifts are one-way
      provenance extensions, whose passive Read interface has a canonical

Axis populations or a classical reversible shuffle do not replace this
coherent derivative panel.

Independently evaluate
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathbb P_{\rm span},\qquad
 \mathbb P_{\rm parity},\qquad
 \mathbb P_{\rm norm}}
\]
for the Hodge/current writer unless the deterministic reversal-odd and
duration-calibrated writer relations are already verified.  Then compute
\[
 \boxed{
 \eta_Z(G),\qquad
 \Delta_{\rm slot}^{\sigma},\qquad
 \Delta_{\rm prov,F}^{\rm odd},}
\]
the occurrence-packet orbit matrices
\(B_{\eta,\lambda}^{\rm occ}\), and either the generator or finite-pulse
relative Howe Gram.  A nonzero matter margin establishes occurrence;
positive orbit matrices eliminate missing admissible odd copies; vanishing
odd-tangent provenance identifies the complete odd generator with finite
Dirac; and a positive Howe gap fixes the exact multiplicity commutant.  No
fitted Yukawa operator, projected Lindblad dissipator, or postselected
quadrature may select the result.
\end{openproblem}



\begin{openproblem}[Literal locked-cylinder provenance and invariant source allocation]

\[

 \ E_c^{(1)},\ A_c^{(1)},\ D_c^{(1)}}
\]
and verify the aggregate, tail, and complement orbit-polytope inequalities.

\[

 P_{\rm priv}=G_A^\dagger C_{AT},
\]
while the matching rows reconstruct
\[

\]
Evaluate the standard and doublet Schur residuals, the metric contractivity
conditions, and the finite tail recurrences.  Their direct sum is the complete
readable trace-free private propagator.

Co-retain the actual chronological endpoint writer and the independently
reconstructed common-action derivative source.  Form
\[

 =D_{\rm end}^*D_{\rm end}

\]
and the finite invariant observability Gram
\[

 =\sum_{n=0}^{d-1}(P_{\rm priv}^n)^*
  \mathsf R_{\rm sel}P_{\rm priv}^n.}
\]
Its kernel gives the canonical rank-zero, rank-one, or rank-two Einstein
standard source.  On the rank-one branch compute the residual
SM/provenance quotient and the feed residual distinguishing an autonomous
direct sum from a triangular extension.  The same marginals realize all
ranks, positive Schur obstructions, and contractivity failures, so the actual
same-history counts cannot be replaced by another marginal theorem.
\end{openproblem}

\begin{openproblem}[Coercive multiplicity-quiver audit]
From the actual residue maps construct their support-polar algebra, residue
support algebra, and canonical multiplicity quiver.  Compute one relative Howe
Gram on the protected multiplicity complement and certify a positive lower
bound.  Then prove either a summable support-polar generator tail from that
finite anchor or the Mosco/compact-screen hypotheses of
\Cref{thm:SMST-continuum-Howe}.  Finally evaluate the Hodge-to-commutator kernel
leakage and relative-density panel of

SM--spacetime Howe pair persists with a regulator-uniform gap; a zero or
collapsing eigenvalue is an explicit additional flavour symmetry, missing
support direction, or escaping multiplicity mode rather than a permission to
quotient it away.

\]
and compute their slot strengths, ranks, tetrahedral-breaking components,

normal, and mixed provenance sectors.  The generation carrier and allowed

label, terminal field, and independently evaluated action increment and test

ratio, and their mixed source Grams.  These rows decide how much of the active

\]
from independently protected action Hessians, masses, and mixing observables,

measure of the regulated Dirac family, its determinant or Pfaffian line,
Berry connection, zero-mode section, BRST/gauge cocycle, and global holonomy.
Only after this line bundle is trivialized or physically sectioned should one
address counterterms, running, matching, and the interacting quantum
continuum.  None of these numerical or measure-level problems reopens the

\begin{openproblem}[Accepted state, trajectory, fluctuation, and driven-process evaluation]

common-action output experiment matrix and every later update kernel used by

projective experiment quotients, then run finite future saturation and the
simultaneous forward/reverse lumpability refinement.  For a continuous-time

Perron--Doob driven generator.  These increasingly strong tests decide,
respectively, one-time action agreement, autonomous repeated dynamics,
trajectory likelihood sufficiency, hidden entropy production, long-time
fluctuation closure, and the physical dynamics realizing a rare event.  None
may be replaced by the acceptance bit or by a static Gibbs partition alone.
\end{openproblem}

Construct the actual regulator Hamiltonian and compare it with the canonical
graph regulator.  Compute the graph Berry moment and curvature, the
actual--graph section-provenance one-form, zero-mode determinant line, and a
protected holonomy basis.  Test any proposed phase cancellation by the
independent-measure, operator-conjugacy, mixing, connection, and inverse-

structure or a positive bosonic Gaussian is not a substitute for this test.

regulator families, convergence of the real stress and phase connection,

\begin{openproblem}[Analytic--Selmer layer stripping]
Build an independently defined layered Selmer complex whose local conditions
admit matrix Schur responses or a block-Jacobi chain.  Compare its continued
fraction, harmonic kernel, determinant-line spectral shift, period metric,
Tamagawa factors, torsion, and $\Sha$ term with the analytic jet complex.
\end{openproblem}

\begin{openproblem}[Uniform Yang--Mills ultraviolet/infrared interface and continuum coercivity]
On the vacuum Doob carrier of \Cref{thm:YM-Doob-Koopman}, choose a physical
block decomposition before diagonalization.  Prove a regulator-uniform
ultraviolet floor for the occurrence block, positivity of the effective
infrared Feshbach short, and a uniform bound on the relaxation router as in
\Cref{thm:YM-two-scale-Feshbach}.  Then establish reflection positivity,
continuum compactness, vacuum uniqueness, nontriviality, and persistence of the
same positive mass under Osterwalder--Schrader reconstruction.  Bare-link
Dobrushin smallness is a sufficient finite-region tool, not the definition of
the weak-coupling continuum certificate.
\end{openproblem}

\begin{openproblem}[Scale-critical Navier--Stokes connected action and open-current comparison]
Reconstruct the actual degree-three triad response panel, short all one- and
two-slot sources and every nonmonoidal occurrence direction, and obtain the
positive effective triad action of \Cref{thm:NS-effective-scale-current}.
Transport its all-residual source through the physical logarithmic-scale
boundary and compare the resulting minimum open current with viscosity,
elapsed physical time, or boundary work.  Use this comparison to derive the
relative form in \Cref{thm:NS-relative-form} with an integrable coefficient.
The estimate must be scale compatible, must retain the open scale endpoints,
and cannot be defined by subtracting the desired dissipation after the fact.
\end{openproblem}

\begin{openproblem}[Hodge cycle loading and equivariant occurrence short]
For each projective variety and codimension, construct an independently
controlled finite rational-cycle family and prove the positive frame bound in
\Cref{thm:Hodge-observability}.  On an equivariant categorical route, first
construct the gluable object and its actual finite-order action, then compute
the zero-character obstruction complex and the occurrence-shorted
semiregularity Gram of \Cref{thm:Hodge-occurrence-short}.  Harmonic shorting,
determinant-line data, and positivity of a product block may guide the search
but do not imply algebraicity or eliminate new obstruction directions created
by induction or orbit fusion.
\end{openproblem}

\begin{openproblem}[Actual multi-sector interface atlas]
Construct finite arithmetic, gauge, Hodge, PDE, and Selmer regions with common
typed boundary ports.  Export their complete matrix responses, verify
conservative gluing and relative interface frames, and prove regulator-uniform
interface and exterior coercivity.  Local determinant nonvanishing is not a
substitute.
\end{openproblem}

\begin{openproblem}[Resource-enriched Grand-Tensor duality]
Select the universal gate, word-length, parallel-layer, communication, memory,
precision, and branching records and augment the monoidal Grand Tensor with a
certified resource metric controlling locality, sparsity, precision, separator
size, communication, memory, and parallel depth.  Prove comparison inequalities
with standard circuit or proof-complexity measures and establish a
superpolynomial loading for an explicit NP-complete family.
\end{openproblem}
